dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-esta.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Jumeirah Golf Estates Middle Years Programme students work from the criterion that is actually weak, not from the subject as a whole. You see the subject group, the year and the weekly availability before the free trial lesson.

intro.heading: The report that triggers the search, and what it is really telling you
paragraphs: Most Jumeirah Golf Estates families who go looking for a Middle Years Programme tutor do it within a week of a report arriving. The report shows numbers that look like marks and behave like something else entirely: a 6 in one column, a 3 in another, a subject grade of 4, and no sentence explaining how those relate. The instinct is to conclude the child is weak at the subject. Usually the report is saying something far more specific and far more fixable.

Each Middle Years Programme subject is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, and each criterion is scored on a published band running up to 8. The teacher writes task-specific clarifications describing what that criterion means for the particular piece of work. The four criterion scores add to a maximum of 32 and are then converted to a subject grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. So the numbers on the report are criterion scores, not percentages, and the pattern across them is the diagnosis.

A student scoring consistently well on the knowing-and-understanding criterion and badly on the one asking for critical thinking or evaluation does not have a knowledge problem. They are writing what they know instead of what the criterion asked for, usually because nobody has ever translated the criterion language, which is written for teachers rather than for thirteen-year-olds. That is a reading-the-task problem, and it moves in a handful of sessions.

Which is the second thing this page argues. Middle Years Programme tuition should be short and it should end. A standing weekly slot through Years 7 to 9 is rarely the right answer, and it is the most common way money gets spent in this part of the market without anything measurable happening. Four to six sessions working from the student's own returned tasks, aimed at one criterion, is the purchase that works.

There is one caveat worth hearing before you buy anything at all. In Years 7 to 9 criterion scores swing between tasks, because each task assesses different criteria against different clarifications, and a single low number is frequently noise rather than signal. Wait for a pattern: the same criterion weak across two reporting cycles, or the same letter weak across several unrelated subjects. From Year 10 the calculation changes, because the profile begins to influence which Diploma courses are offered at sixteen.

IB Gram teaches Jumeirah Golf Estates students one-to-one over live video at a fixed time in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The practical gain here is scheduling, because in this community the afternoon runs long and a Middle Years Programme student is rarely ready to work before six.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-esta.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme spans five years and three quite different phases, and a Jumeirah Golf Estates parent's questions should change as the student moves through them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Years 1 to 3
programmes.description: The settling-in phase, with eight subject groups and interdisciplinary units. Assessment is formative as much as summative and the criterion scores move around a lot, which is normal and not usually a signal to buy anything. The genuinely useful interventions at this stage are narrow: written fluency in English for a child who has arrived from another language of instruction, or number facts that have never been secured.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai private schools also run Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the Middle Years Programme under KHDA requirements, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. That is real timetable load the programme brochure does not show, and it is worth accounting for before adding a weekly tuition commitment in Year 7.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: The consequential phase. Subject choices narrow, extended and standard mathematics streams often separate, the Personal Project arrives in Year 5, and the criterion scores start to predict which Diploma courses will be offered at 16. This is where targeted criteria coaching earns its keep, because a student who cannot yet write to criterion D will meet the same demand again in every Diploma internal assessment.
programmes.countryNote: Schools around Jumeirah Golf Estates split between the Middle Years Programme and Cambridge IGCSE at this age, so neighbours in the same street can be on completely different assessment models. If your family may move campuses within Dubai, the transferable gap is extended writing and independent research rather than subject content.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent project with a supervisor, assessed against its own criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and reporting. It is the first genuinely independent piece of work most students attempt and the best possible rehearsal for the Extended Essay. Support is supervision-style: scoping the goal so it is achievable, keeping the process journal honestly, and holding the student to their own timeline.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah Golf Estates students frequently choose Personal Project goals that are too large, often involving an event or a build that depends on other people. Scoping it down in the first week is the single most valuable conversation available, and it must happen before the process journal is three months old.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-esta.subjectsIntro: The Middle Years Programme uses eight subject groups, and each one has its own four criteria with its own vocabulary. Knowing which criterion a subject's letter D actually refers to is most of the work.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · standard and extended streams
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students who are quick at calculation often score poorly on the investigating-patterns criterion, because it asks for a general rule to be found and justified rather than for an answer.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · biology, chemistry and physics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The design criterion is where marks concentrate and where students lose them, usually by writing a method with no stated controlled variable.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · English and other first languages
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. A student can write beautifully and still lose the analysing criterion for describing what a text says rather than how it achieves its effect, which is the commonest pattern in this subject.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · phases 1 to 6
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed by phase rather than by year group. Phase placement matters enormously: a student assessed above their actual phase appears to be failing when they are simply in the wrong band, which is worth checking before buying anything.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · history, geography, economics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. The thinking-critically criterion asks for evaluation of sources and perspectives, and students answer it with more description, which is the single most coachable error in the programme.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · product and digital design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Students who build competently lose marks on documentation, because the criteria sit as much in the recorded design process as in the finished product.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · visual, music, drama
subjects.description: Investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. The developmental workbook or process journal carries real weight, and talented performers routinely underscore because the process was never recorded as it happened.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on and improving performance. Sporty students in this community are often surprised by their grade, because two of the four criteria are written rather than physical.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Research, communication, thinking, social and self-management skills, assessed indirectly through every subject's criteria. When a report shows the same weak criterion across four unrelated subjects, this is usually what is being measured rather than any subject knowledge.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units combining two subject groups, assessed on disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection. Students treat them as double homework rather than as a distinct task type, which is why the marks come back lower than either parent subject.

sections.heading: How to read a Middle Years Programme report
paragraphs: Take the report apart in the order the programme builds it. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D. Each criterion is scored against a published band running up to 8, based on the descriptors the teacher applied to that specific task. The four scores sum to a maximum of 32, and that total converts to a subject grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. Confirm the exact boundaries with your child's school, because schools publish them and they are the only version that matters for your report.

What this means practically is that the subject grade is the least informative number on the page. A 4 can be produced by four mediocre criterion scores or by two strong ones and two weak ones, and those are completely different situations requiring completely different responses. The first may be a content problem. The second is almost always a task-reading problem, and it is the cheaper of the two to fix by a wide margin.

So read across rather than down. If the same criterion letter is weak in three or four unrelated subjects, you are not looking at four subject problems; you are looking at one skill the student has never been taught, usually critical thinking, evaluation or structured communication. If a single subject has a uniformly low profile while the others are fine, that is genuinely subject-specific.

Then read the task-specific clarifications, which are the documents the teacher writes to say what each criterion means for a particular task. They are the most useful and least read papers in the whole programme. A student who reads the clarification before starting, rather than the question, scores better immediately — and that habit, not the subject content, is what a good Middle Years tutor is actually teaching.

sections.heading: What the four criteria actually ask for, subject by subject
paragraphs: The letters mean different things in different subject groups, which is the detail that confuses parents and sometimes tutors. In Mathematics, criterion B is investigating patterns, which asks a student to find and justify a general rule rather than to compute. In Sciences, criterion B is inquiring and designing, which asks for a method with controlled variables named. In Language and literature, criterion A is analysing, which asks how a text achieves its effect, not what it says.

That variation has a direct consequence for hiring. A tutor who says they know the Middle Years Programme should be able to tell you what criterion D is in your child's specific subject and what a strong response to it looks like. In Individuals and societies it is thinking critically, which wants evaluation of sources and perspectives. In Design it is evaluating, which wants the solution tested against the specification the student wrote themselves. In Physical and health education it is reflecting on and improving performance, which is written work rather than sport.

The commonest error across all eight subject groups is the same, however: a student answers the question in front of them rather than the criterion the task is assessing. Description where evaluation was wanted, content where method was wanted, performance where reflection was wanted. Once a student understands that the criterion is the question, scores move quickly and across several subjects at once.

That is also why the right block is short. This is a transferable skill rather than a body of content. A student who learns to unpack a task against its clarification in Year 9 does not need to learn it again in Year 10, and will arrive at the Diploma's internal assessments already able to do the thing most students meet for the first time in Year 12.

sections.heading: When a session can actually happen here
paragraphs: Middle Years students are younger than Diploma students and they tire earlier, which makes timing more rather than less important. Work the arithmetic for this community: campus finish between 2.45pm and 3.30pm, ten to twenty minutes of gate queue at Jumeirah Park or on the Sports City side, and twelve to thirty-five minutes of driving depending on whether the school is in Al Barsha South or out towards Al Sufouh.

That puts most Middle Years children home between 4.00pm and 4.40pm. They then need food and a genuine break — more than a Diploma student does, not less — and many of them leave again for academies in Dubai Sports City between four and six. The window parents instinctively suggest, four o'clock, is almost always the worst available hour.

In practice, sessions for this age group work between 6pm and 7.30pm on weekdays, kept to sixty minutes rather than ninety. A thirteen-year-old at the end of a long Dubai school day produces more in a focused hour than in a stretched ninety minutes, and the shorter session is also easier to protect in the family calendar, which matters because consistency is what makes a short block work.

Weekend mornings are the most underused slot in this community and the right one for Personal Project work, which needs an uninterrupted stretch and benefits from the student being fresh. Online delivery is what makes any of this flexible: with no travel on the tutor's side, a session can move within the week when an academy fixture collides, shift post-Iftar during Ramadan, and stop cleanly when the block is done.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the mistake almost everyone makes
paragraphs: The Personal Project in Middle Years Year 5 is the first substantial independent piece most students attempt, assessed against its own criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and reporting. It is also the best rehearsal available for the Extended Essay two years later, which is why it is worth getting right for reasons beyond the grade itself.

The mistake is almost always the same, and it is made in the first fortnight: the goal is too large, and it depends on other people. Jumeirah Golf Estates students propose community events, fundraising drives, builds requiring parts that have to be shipped, and collaborations with clubs whose calendars they do not control. When the external dependency fails in month three, the project fails with it, and no amount of writing recovers a process journal describing a thing that did not happen.

So the highest-value conversation happens in week one and lasts an hour: is this goal achievable by this student alone, within this timeline, with resources already available? Scoping down is almost always the right move. A small project executed and documented well scores considerably better than an ambitious one abandoned, and students find that genuinely surprising to hear.

The second half of the work is the process journal, which must be kept as the project happens rather than reconstructed afterwards. Reconstruction is visible to an assessor and it is also, in a real sense, not honest. A tutor here can question the goal, hold the student to their own timeline, explain what each criterion rewards, and give feedback on the journal and report the student has written. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any of it, supply the goal as a finished product, or edit a draft to completion, and ours decline when asked.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside the programme
paragraphs: A Middle Years timetable in Dubai is fuller than the programme brochure suggests, and new arrivals in Jumeirah Golf Estates are regularly surprised by it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position behind this is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The organisation is prescribed in detail. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for Arab and non-Arab groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the regulator's sign-off for those subjects.

Two consequences for a family planning tuition. Instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. That is genuine timetable space competing with the eight Middle Years subject groups, and it is a real argument against adding two weekly tuition slots in Year 8.

Second, for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Tutoring in Arabic or Islamic Education therefore has to follow the school's own material rather than an outside scheme, and where the school is the better route we will say so rather than taking the booking.

sections.heading: From criteria to the Diploma: the gap worth closing early
paragraphs: Middle Years Year 5 students in Jumeirah Golf Estates are usually a year away from the Diploma, and the handover produces a predictable set of surprises. The criteria model is excellent at teaching inquiry, process and reflection. It is less visibly demanding on two things the Diploma assumes from the first term: algebraic fluency and sustained writing under time pressure.

The algebra point is concrete. A student entering Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, or Physics or Chemistry at Higher Level, needs confident equation rearrangement, standard form, unit manipulation and radian measure on day one. The criteria model rewards finding and justifying a general rule, which is a different and more sophisticated skill, but it does not drill manipulation to automaticity. Four to six sessions in the summer before Year 12 closes that gap cheaply.

The writing point is similar. Middle Years assessment is typically completed over days with access to resources. Diploma Paper 2 is ninety minutes with nothing. Students who write thoughtfully over a week can produce very little in an hour, and discovering that in a Year 12 mock is an expensive way to find out. Timed extended writing practice, three or four sessions, transfers to every essay-based subject at once.

What does transfer well is everything else. A student who can unpack a task against its criteria, evaluate a source, and keep an honest process journal arrives at the Diploma's internal assessments already able to do what most of their cohort meets for the first time in Year 12. That is worth saying to a Year 9 parent worrying about a criterion score: the thing being taught here is the thing that pays later.

sections.heading: What Middle Years tuition costs, and why it should be small
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates do not vary much by programme, so a Middle Years session costs roughly what any other session costs. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at about AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. Budget online tuition, typically a university student, runs from AED 45 to AED 150, with one platform listing from AED 33 to AED 52 and another from AED 45 to AED 65. In-home visits including travel are advertised at AED 180 to AED 500.

What should vary is the quantity, and at this age it should be small. A four to six session criteria block at a mid-band rate is roughly AED 800 to AED 1,200, and that is the right order of magnitude for most Middle Years problems. A Personal Project block of four or five sessions is similar. By contrast, a weekly slot running a full academic year at the same rate is in the region of AED 6,000 to AED 7,000, and for a Year 8 student it is very rarely justified by anything on the report.

There is one case where the budget band genuinely fits, and it is worth naming because this page is otherwise sceptical of it. A Year 7 student who simply will not begin homework unaided may need supervision and routine rather than subject expertise, and a permitted university-student tutor at AED 60 an hour provides exactly that. Paying a specialist rate for that service is a waste; paying a budget rate for criteria coaching is also a waste. Match the band to the problem.

Every figure above was read from the provider's own published page in October 2026 and describes the market rather than IB Gram, whose fee follows a free trial lesson. For wider context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, so school fees are the stable line in your budget this year and tuition is the variable.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor, and what no provider holds
paragraphs: Ask the question a Jumeirah Golf Estates parent actually has: who is permitted to sit at the dining table and talk a Year 9 through criterion C. The answer is anybody holding a private tuition work permit, and the striking part is how light that document is to obtain. MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee at all and a two-working-day completion time, with the application made through the MoHRE smart app, the website or the e-services system. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and once granted runs free of charge for two years before it needs renewing. Two working days and nothing to pay is not a high barrier, which is exactly why the permit evidences eligibility to tutor rather than competence at Middle Years criteria.

The eligible categories matter particularly at this age range, because the budget band is a realistic option for younger students. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. So a permitted nineteen-year-old providing homework structure to a Year 7 student is operating entirely within the rules. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted.

One boundary to observe. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being relied on as exact wording. The practical rule holds anyway: do not engage your child's own subject teacher privately, however convenient it seems when the issue is a criterion only that teacher has clarified.

Finally, what nobody holds. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Nor do we reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, criteria documents or assessment material; tutors work from what the school has issued and reference the official source.

process.title: Send the report and two returned tasks
process.description: The report shows the criterion profile and the returned tasks show the teacher's task-specific clarifications and what the student actually wrote against them. Together they usually identify a single criterion and a single habit, which is a four to six session block rather than a term of general support.

process.title: Name the subject group, not just the subject
process.description: Criterion D means different things in Mathematics, Sciences, Individuals and societies and Design. Tell us the subject group and the year, and we will match somebody who can say what that letter asks for in your child's subject and what a strong response to it looks like.

process.title: Give us a realistic hour
process.description: Middle Years students tire earlier than Diploma students. Tell us the campus, the finish time, the drive, and whether there is an academy in Dubai Sports City. We will propose sixty minutes between 6pm and 7.30pm rather than the four o'clock slot that looks free and never works.

process.title: Use the free trial on a returned task
process.description: You and your child meet the proposed tutor over live video. Give them the task that came back with a low criterion score. Afterwards you get their read on which habit is operating, a session count and the fee, and you decide. No payment is required to reach that point.

process.title: Agree the end before you start
process.description: Four to six sessions, then stop and watch the next report. If the criterion has moved, nothing more is needed. If it has not, we change the approach or the tutor. At this age the single most useful thing a provider can do is finish, and almost nobody offers it.

whyPoints.title: We read the criterion profile, not the grade
whyPoints.description: A subject grade of 4 can be four mediocre criterion scores or two strong and two weak, and those need completely different responses. Reading across the letters rather than down the subjects is how a report turns from worrying into diagnostic, and it takes about ten minutes.

whyPoints.title: Short blocks that are designed to end
whyPoints.description: Middle Years tuition should usually be four to six sessions aimed at one criterion, after which it stops. A standing weekly slot through Years 7 to 9 is the most common way money is spent in this part of the market without anything measurable changing, and we will say so.

whyPoints.title: Task-specific clarifications come first
whyPoints.description: The teacher's clarification document says what the criterion means for that task, and it is the least read paper in the programme. A student who reads it before the question scores better immediately, and teaching that habit is most of what a good Middle Years tutor does.

whyPoints.title: Timed for a younger student's day
whyPoints.description: A thirteen-year-old home at 4.20pm after a Dubai school day and an academy session produces more in a focused sixty minutes at 6.30pm than in a stretched ninety at five. Online delivery is what makes the later, shorter slot possible at all.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the Personal Project
whyPoints.description: The project is usually lost in week one by choosing a goal that depends on other people. We spend the first session scoping it down, which is unglamorous and is the single highest-value hour in the whole engagement. We never write, rewrite or complete any part of it.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery and no invented claims
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE, as in-person home tutoring exists only in our India service. No guaranteed grades, no statistics without a sample size and method, and every AED figure here credited to its published source.

faqs.question: What do the numbers on my child's MYP report actually mean?
faqs.answer: They are criterion scores, not percentages. Each subject is assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, each scored on a published band running up to 8, based on descriptors the teacher applied to a specific task. The four sum to a maximum of 32 and convert to a subject grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries your school can give you. The pattern across the letters is the useful information: the subject grade itself is the least informative number on the page, because very different situations produce the same grade.

faqs.question: My child scores 6 on one criterion and 3 on another. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a diagnosis rather than a problem, and a cheaper one than it looks. A student strong on knowing and understanding and weak on the criterion asking for critical thinking or evaluation is writing what they know instead of what the criterion asked for. That is a task-reading habit, not a knowledge gap, and it typically moves in four to six sessions working from their own returned tasks. A uniformly low profile across all four criteria in one subject is the different, genuinely subject-specific situation.

faqs.question: Does criterion D mean the same thing in every MYP subject?
faqs.answer: No, and this is where parents and some tutors come unstuck. In Mathematics it is applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences it is reflecting on the impacts of science. In Individuals and societies it is thinking critically. In Design it is evaluating against the student's own specification. In Physical and health education it is reflecting on and improving performance, which is written work rather than sport. A tutor who claims to know the programme should be able to tell you what criterion D is in your child's specific subject.

faqs.question: How long should MYP tutoring last?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions, in most cases, and then it should stop. The thing being taught is a transferable skill — reading a task against its criteria and answering the criterion — rather than a body of content, so once a student can do it they do not need to keep paying for it. A standing weekly slot through Years 7 to 9 is the commonest way money gets spent in this part of the market with nothing measurable happening. Agree the end at the start and watch the next report.

faqs.question: What are task-specific clarifications and why do they matter?
faqs.answer: They are the documents your child's teacher writes to say what each criterion means for a particular task: what counts as investigating patterns in this piece of maths, or as evaluating in this history essay. They are the most useful and least read papers in the whole programme. A student who reads the clarification before reading the question scores better immediately, because the criterion is the real question. Teaching that habit is most of what a good Middle Years Programme tutor actually does.

faqs.question: When can a session realistically happen for a Jumeirah Golf Estates MYP student?
faqs.answer: Between 6pm and 7.30pm on weekdays, and sixty minutes rather than ninety. Campus finish runs from about 2.45pm to 3.30pm, the gate queue costs ten to twenty minutes, and the drive is twelve to thirty-five minutes depending on whether the school sits in Al Barsha South or out towards Al Sufouh, so most children are home between 4.00pm and 4.40pm. Many then leave again for academies in Dubai Sports City. The four o'clock slot parents instinctively suggest is almost always the worst hour available.

faqs.question: Why is my child's Personal Project going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because the goal is too large and depends on other people. Students here propose community events, fundraising drives and builds needing shipped parts, and when the external dependency fails in month three the project fails with it. A small project executed and documented well scores considerably better than an ambitious one abandoned. The fix is one hour in week one spent scoping the goal down to something achievable alone, within the timeline, with resources already to hand.

faqs.question: What exactly is a Personal Project supervisor-style tutor allowed to do?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the help is most valuable earliest. A tutor can question whether the goal is achievable, hold the student to their own timeline, explain what each project criterion rewards, and give feedback on the process journal and report the student has written. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it, supply the goal as a finished product, or edit a draft to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line, and a process journal reconstructed afterwards is visible to an assessor anyway.

faqs.question: My child is sporty but scores badly in physical and health education. How?
faqs.answer: Because two of the four criteria are written rather than physical. Alongside applying and performing sit knowing and understanding, planning for performance, and reflecting on and improving performance, and the last of those asks for analysis of performance data and a revised plan rather than a description of the activity. Strong athletes in this community are regularly surprised by their grade for exactly this reason. It is one of the quickest criterion fixes available, usually two or three sessions, because the physical ability is already there.

faqs.question: Which Diploma skills does the criteria model leave unbuilt?
faqs.answer: For most of what matters, yes, and better than its reputation. A student who can unpack a task against its criteria, evaluate sources and perspectives, and keep an honest process journal arrives at the Diploma's internal assessments already able to do what much of their cohort meets for the first time in Year 12. Two things do need separate work: algebraic manipulation to automaticity for Higher Level maths and sciences, and sustained writing under time pressure, since criteria assessment is usually completed over days with resources available.

faqs.question: Neighbours here are on IGCSE at 14 and we are not. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: That is a school and family decision rather than a tutoring one, and it usually comes down to the post-16 plan and the child. Schools around Jumeirah Golf Estates are split, so neighbours in the same street can be on different models. What is worth knowing is the gap either way: a student moving to IGCSE needs calculation fluency and timed written technique, and a student moving to the Middle Years Programme needs to learn to write to a criterion. Both gaps are real and both are short blocks of work.

faqs.question: How much extra timetable do the mandatory UAE subjects add here?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language and for Islamic Education for Arab students. Instructional time is built on a 40-minute lesson unit, which is real load alongside eight subject groups when you are planning tuition.

faqs.question: How much should MYP tuition cost?
faqs.answer: A four to six session criteria block at a mid-band market rate is roughly AED 800 to AED 1,200, and that is the right order of magnitude for most Middle Years problems. Published Dubai rates run about AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online, with a budget band of AED 45 to AED 150 that genuinely suits homework routine support for a Year 7 student. A weekly slot across a full academic year is AED 6,000 to AED 7,000 and is rarely justified at this age. Market figures, researched October 2026.

faqs.question: Should we wait for the next report before buying anything?
faqs.answer: In Years 7 to 9, often yes. Criterion scores swing between tasks at that stage, because each task assesses different criteria with different clarifications, and a single low score is frequently noise rather than signal. Wait for a pattern: the same criterion weak across two reporting cycles, or the same letter weak across several unrelated subjects. In Years 10 and 11 the calculation changes, because the profile starts to influence which Diploma courses get offered, and acting on a clear pattern early is worth more then.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-esta.closingHeading: Read across the letters, buy four sessions, then stop
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-esta.closingBody: A Middle Years Programme report is a diagnostic document pretending to be a verdict. Read across the criterion letters rather than down the subject list, find the one that is weak in several places, and buy a short block aimed at that. For most Jumeirah Golf Estates students that is four to six sessions working from their own returned tasks, timed at 6pm or later once the school run and the academy are done. Send us the report and two marked tasks and we will propose a tutor you can test in a free trial lesson over live video. No home visits in the UAE and no promised grades.

intro.heading: The three documents an MYP specialist asks for
paragraphs: Here is the fastest test of whether a tutor understands the Middle Years Programme. Ask what they want from you before the first session. A specialist asks for three documents: the task sheet, the criterion descriptors for that subject, and, if you can get it, the school's own grade boundary table. A subject tutor asks for the textbook and the topic.

That difference is not pedantry. MYP assessment does not work from a syllabus of examinable content; it works from criteria. Each subject group has four, lettered A to D, each marked on a 1-8 scale against published descriptors, with the four marks converted into a reported 1-7 grade using boundaries the school applies. The task sheet states which criteria a particular task assesses, and it is often only two of the four.

So a student can know the content thoroughly and score in the middle, because the criterion they are weakest on drags the total. And a student can write an excellent answer against a criterion the task does not assess, which earns nothing. Neither of those is a content problem, and neither is visible to a tutor working from a textbook.

Supply makes this harder to solve locally. The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum, and Middle Years students are a subset of that figure spread across a handful of continuum schools. Jumeirah Islands has no school inside the gates at all, so the community's MYP families attend several different schools with different boundary tables.

The practical consequence is that there is no local MYP cohort and no reason the right tutor for your child's subject group lives a short drive away. Filtering by distance in this programme selects almost entirely for travel willingness, which correlates poorly with criterion fluency.

There is a second diagnosis worth making before you buy any subject at all. The programme teaches research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills across every subject rather than as a subject of their own. If a child's marks are uniformly middling across unrelated subjects, the problem is rarely eight separate content gaps; it is more often one skills problem applied to long tasks, and that is a single fixable thing.

IB Gram matches a tutor who works from your school's documents and teaches live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For this programme the format is a genuine advantage, because task sheets, descriptors, drafts and rubrics can all be open on a shared screen while a tutor points at the exact line the work does not yet meet.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-islands.subjectsIntro: The eight subject groups with the four criteria each uses. Ask a prospective tutor to name them for your child's subject; a specialist does it instantly and from memory.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Marks are lost on investigating patterns, where a student finds a result and never generalises it, and on communicating, where correct work carries no notation or explanation.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The two middle criteria hold almost all the lost marks: an unrepeatable method, an uncontrolled variable, an evaluation that reports success rather than assessing the method.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students summarise where the criterion asks them to analyse how meaning is constructed, and lose organising marks for essays with no visible structure. Both respond quickly to work on thesis sentences and paragraph planning.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is what separates a 6 from a 4, and it requires weighing sources and perspectives rather than reporting them. Investigating marks depend on a research question narrow enough to answer.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, with phase-based rather than year-based expectations. Students lose marks producing accurate but simple language where the phase descriptor expects range, and by not addressing the task's stated audience and purpose explicitly.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Design is where criterion discipline shows most plainly: a strong product with no documented specification or testing against it scores well below a modest product that is properly evidenced.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than students expect, and responding marks require genuine engagement with other work rather than description of their own.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written criteria surprise students who assumed the subject was practical, and reflection is where the accessible marks sit.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units combining two subject groups, assessed against interdisciplinary criteria rather than the subject ones. Students apply one subject's thinking well and treat the other as decoration, which is exactly what the criteria do not reward. Send the task sheet if a unit is running.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills, taught across the programme rather than as a subject. In practice this is where MYP tutoring often does most good: planning a long task, keeping a journal, meeting staged deadlines, and checking work against a rubric before submitting it.

sections.heading: Why the three documents matter more than the textbook
paragraphs: In an examined system the syllabus is the shared standard, and a tutor who knows it knows what to teach. The Middle Years Programme does not work that way. The standard for a given piece of work is set by the task sheet, the criterion descriptors and the boundaries your child's school applies, and none of those is in a textbook.

The task sheet is the most immediately useful of the three. It states which criteria the task assesses, which is frequently two of the four rather than all of them, and what form the response should take. A student who writes beautifully against a criterion this task does not assess has done excellent work for no marks, and that happens more often than anyone admits.

The descriptors are the standard itself. They describe, band by band, what the work has to demonstrate, in language that students find abstract until someone sits with them and maps their own draft against it. That mapping is the single most useful thing an MYP tutor does, and it cannot be done from memory or from a general knowledge of the subject.

The boundaries are the conversion. Four criterion marks out of 8 give a total out of 32, which becomes a reported 1-7 grade through a boundary table the school applies. Schools report at different points in the year with different amounts of evidence, which is one reason two children with similar work receive different-looking reports.

So when a tutor asks for the textbook, they are planning to teach content. Content is occasionally the problem, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, and it usually is not. The table below sets out what each document gives a tutor and what goes wrong without it.

sections.heading: The criteria, named by subject group
paragraphs: A parent cannot judge a tutor's claim to know the programme without knowing what the criteria are called, so here they are by subject group. Ask a prospective tutor to name the four for your child's subject. A specialist does it from memory and immediately; a subject tutor talks about the subject in general terms.

The pattern across groups is informative in itself. Every group has a knowledge criterion, and in most groups it is the one students score best on and parents worry about most. The other three are process criteria: investigating, communicating, evaluating, reflecting, applying. That is where the marks are lost, and it is why content teaching so often fails to move a grade.

In the sciences the two middle criteria, inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating, hold almost all the lost marks. In mathematics it is investigating patterns and communicating. In Individuals and Societies it is thinking critically. In Design it is evaluating against a specification the student wrote. The subject changes; the shape of the failure does not.

This also explains why a short, well-timed block often outperforms a term of weekly teaching in the MYP. If the problem is one process criterion on a particular kind of task, two or three sessions with the descriptors open can change the band. A term of content teaching leaves the student knowing more and scoring the same.

Criterion names and allocations are set by the IB and revised between syllabus cycles, so confirm them against your school's current documents rather than against this page. The table lists them as commonly published, with that caution attached.

sections.heading: Why content teaching so often fails here
paragraphs: This is the mechanism behind most disappointing MYP tutoring, and it is worth understanding before you buy anything. A student brings home a 4. The parent, reasonably, concludes the subject is not understood and hires a subject tutor. The tutor, reasonably, teaches the subject. The next report says 4.

What happened is that the 4 came from a criterion profile rather than from a lack of knowledge. A student scoring well on the knowledge criterion and poorly on two process criteria has a middling total, and the route to improvement runs through the weakest criterion. Teaching more content raises the score on the criterion that was already strong.

The second mechanism is the task sheet. A student who does not check which criteria a task assesses, and does not compare their draft against those descriptors before submitting, leaves marks on the table in every single task. That is a habit, not an ability, and it is the fastest change available in the whole programme.

The third is generalisation and evaluation, which across subject groups is the same failure wearing different names. Finding a pattern in four cases and not expressing it as a rule. Reporting that an experiment worked rather than assessing which control was weakest. Summarising two sources rather than weighing them. Students describe where descriptors ask them to assess.

So the first question to put to the school is not about the subject. It is: which criterion scores produced this grade? That question is free, takes one email, and turns an unreadable report into a plan. A tutor who suggests asking it is telling you they understand what they are being hired for.

sections.heading: What to ask the school, and what it changes
paragraphs: Four questions, none of them awkward, all answerable in one reply. They cost nothing and they determine whether any tutoring you buy can be targeted. Families here ask them less often than families at the school's own gates do, simply because there is no playground conversation inside a community with no school in it.

First: which criterion scores produced this grade? That is the question that converts a report into a plan. Second: which criteria does the current task assess, and may we have the descriptors? Third: when do the next tasks and the next report fall? Fourth, in the final MYP year: what is the Personal Project timeline and who is supervising?

The answers change the shape of the tutoring completely. Criterion scores tell a tutor where to work. The task sheet tells them what to work on this fortnight. The calendar tells them when coaching has to happen, because feedback after submission is interesting and worthless. The project timeline prevents the standard late scramble.

There is a fifth question worth asking at a different moment, which is how the school converts criterion totals into reported grades. Schools apply boundaries and report at different points with different evidence, and knowing your school's policy stops you comparing a mid-year report against a neighbour's end-of-year one and drawing conclusions from the difference.

The table sets these out with what each answer changes. Take them to the subject teacher rather than the office, since the subject teacher holds the task sheets and sets the standard your child is actually being measured against.

sections.heading: What we can honestly staff in this programme
paragraphs: Coverage in the MYP is uneven and no competitor in this market publishes a limit, so here is ours. Mathematics, the sciences, Language and Literature and Individuals and Societies are well covered and usually matched within the same week. Language Acquisition depends entirely on the language and the phase. Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education are thin.

For the thin groups we will often say that criterion coaching on the student's own task is the useful thing we can offer rather than subject teaching, and we say it before you book rather than after. That is a genuine service in those subjects, because Design and Arts marks are frequently lost to documentation and evaluation rather than to the making.

The second honest point concerns interdisciplinary units. They are assessed against interdisciplinary criteria rather than the subject ones, they come round rarely, and a tutor who has never seen one will coach the subject criteria by default. If a unit is running and the mark matters, send the task sheet, because the descriptors are not the ones your child is used to.

On scheduling, Jumeirah Islands has no school inside the gates so every pupil travels out, arriving home between roughly 15:40 and 16:50. For this age group the workable window is around 16:30 to 20:00, with younger MYP students doing better earlier because criterion work is reading and comparison rather than energy.

Where a tutor covering a UAE family is based outside the UAE and teaches on Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book. A parent is entitled to know who is teaching their child and from where, and two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE numbers without mentioning it.

sections.heading: Approaches to learning, which is where the real problem often sits
paragraphs: The MYP teaches a set of skills across every subject rather than as a subject: research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills. Parents rarely identify these as the issue and in a surprising number of cases they are. A student who cannot plan a three-week task, keep a journal or meet a staged deadline will underperform in every subject group simultaneously.

That diagnosis is worth making deliberately, because it changes what you buy. If a student's marks are uniformly middling across unrelated subjects, the problem is unlikely to be eight separate content gaps. It is more likely to be self-management applied to long tasks, which is a single fixable thing rather than eight.

The work looks unglamorous: breaking a task into stages with dates, writing a journal entry at the point of doing rather than afterwards, checking a draft against the descriptors before submitting, and keeping research notes with sources attached. None of that is subject teaching, and all of it transfers across every subject group at once.

It also transfers forward. The Diploma's Extended Essay, internal assessments and CAS reflections all require exactly these habits, and a student who built them in the Middle Years Programme arrives at sixteen with an advantage that no amount of content teaching provides. For a family here deciding where to spend, that is a strong argument.

The reason this is under-bought is that it does not look like tutoring. An invoice for self-management coaching reads oddly next to one for mathematics. The marks say otherwise, and a tutor who raises it with you rather than selling a subject is probably reading the reports properly.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the largest independent piece of work in the programme and it fails in predictable ways. The first is scope: a goal so ambitious the product cannot be finished or properly evidenced in the time available. The second is the process journal, which rewards documentation as the work happens and punishes reconstruction, and students almost always underestimate this.

The third is the report, where students describe what they made instead of evidencing their process against the criteria. A modest product with a well-documented journey scores better than an impressive product with no visible process, which is counter-intuitive to every student who has ever started one and is worth saying early.

What a tutor may legitimately do is coach the process: narrowing the goal to something achievable and evidenceable, planning staged deadlines, explaining what a useful journal entry looks like and when to write it, teaching referencing, and reading the student's own draft report and saying which criterion band it currently meets and why.

What a tutor may not do is produce, write, part-write or rewrite any part of the project, the journal or the report. Submitting work that is not the student's own is an academic honesty matter handled by the school and the IB, and the consequence falls on the student. Operators in this market sell completed internal assessments at four-figure prices; treat that offer as a reason to walk away.

We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides or assessment documents. Your child's school holds what it needs and the supervision arrangement is the school's. A tutor works alongside that, never in place of it, and the fastest way to sort providers is to ask what they will do with a draft.

sections.heading: Rates, the Diploma step, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB work sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65, which buys supervision rather than criterion coaching. In-home visits run AED 180-500 including travel.

For planning, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 a month for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. In the MYP the better value is usually short and specific rather than weekly: two or three sessions timed to a real task often changes more than a term of content teaching. All figures are the providers' own, read in October 2026, and none is ours.

On the Diploma step, the most useful thing to buy in the final MYP year is not more content. It is timed writing, command-term discipline and, for intended Analysis and Approaches students, a block on surds, indices, rearrangement and algebraic fractions done quickly without a calculator, because that course has a non-calculator paper and the MYP does not drill for it.

We publish no rating, review count or satisfaction percentage, because a statistic without its sample size, date and method cannot be checked. We do not write or supply coursework of any kind, and we do not distribute subject guides or assessment documents.

And we claim no approval we do not hold. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation or the IB, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit. Individual tutors in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free of charge and valid for two years.

faqs.question: What should an MYP tutor ask us for before the first session?
faqs.answer: Three documents and one artefact: the task sheet, the criterion descriptors for the subject, the school's boundary table if you can get it, and a recent marked task. Those set the standard your child is being measured against, and none of them is in a textbook. A tutor who asks only for the year group and the topic is planning to teach content, which in this programme is usually not the binding problem.

faqs.question: Why did a term of subject tutoring not change our child's MYP grade?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because the grade came from a criterion profile rather than a knowledge gap. Four criteria are each marked out of 8, totalled out of 32 and converted to a 1-7 grade, so a student strong on the knowledge criterion and weak on two process criteria sits in the middle. Teaching more content raises the score on the criterion that was already strong. Ask the school which criterion scores produced the grade; that single question usually explains the whole year.

faqs.question: Can you name the four criteria for our child's subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and so should any tutor you are considering, from memory. Sciences: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, reflecting on the impacts of science. Mathematics: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, applying in real-life contexts. Language and Literature: analysing, organising, producing text, using language. Individuals and Societies: knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, thinking critically. Names and allocations are revised between cycles, so confirm against your school's current documents.

faqs.question: Are there MYP tutors living near Jumeirah Islands?
faqs.answer: Very few, and the reason is structural rather than local. The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum, Middle Years students are a subset of that, and the continuum schools sit in Al Barsha, The Meadows, Umm Suqeim and further out. There is no school inside these gates, so the community's MYP families are scattered across several schools with different boundary tables and no shared cohort.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to the villa for MYP sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no centre here either. MYP support for families inside these gates is live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time. For this programme the format is a genuine advantage, because the task sheet, the descriptors and the draft can all be open on a shared screen while the tutor points at the exact line the work does not yet meet.

faqs.question: Our child's marks are middling in several unrelated subjects. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Usually that the problem is not eight content gaps but one skills problem. The MYP teaches research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills across every subject, and a student who cannot plan a three-week task, keep a journal or meet a staged deadline underperforms everywhere at once. That is a single fixable thing. The work is unglamorous, transfers across all eight subject groups, and transfers forward into the Diploma's Extended Essay and internal assessments.

faqs.question: How many sessions does criterion coaching usually take?
faqs.answer: Two or three, timed to a real task, if the problem is a specific criterion rather than general knowledge. That is often all that is needed, and it is why we recommend short blocks over open-ended weekly arrangements in this programme. Where there is a genuine content gap, usually in mathematics or the sciences, a weekly hour is the right instrument instead. A marked task tells us which case you are in, which is why we ask for one.

faqs.question: Should we compare our child's MYP report with a neighbour's IGCSE grades?
faqs.answer: It is not a meaningful comparison, and in this area almost every family tries it, because the surrounding communities are largely British curriculum. The MYP reports a 1-7 grade derived from criterion totals assessed internally against descriptors; IGCSE reports a 9-1 grade from external examinations. Different instruments measuring different things at different points. If you want a comparison that means something, ask both schools what their sixth form expects for entry to the subject your child wants.

faqs.question: What is the Personal Project most likely to go wrong on?
faqs.answer: Scope first: a goal too ambitious for the product to be finished and properly evidenced in the time available. Then the process journal, which rewards documentation written at the point of doing and punishes reconstruction afterwards, and which students consistently underestimate. Then the report, where students describe what they made rather than evidencing their process against the criteria. A modest product with a well-documented journey scores better than an impressive one with no visible process.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups can you not easily cover?
faqs.answer: Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education are thin, and Language Acquisition depends on the language and the phase. For those we will usually offer criterion coaching on your child's own task rather than subject teaching, and we say so before you book. That is a real service in Design and Arts in particular, where marks are frequently lost to documentation and evaluation rather than to the making itself.

faqs.question: Our child says a task only assessed two criteria. Is that right?
faqs.answer: Very likely, and noticing it is one of the most useful habits a student can build. A task sheet states which criteria it assesses, and many tasks assess only two of the four. A student who writes brilliantly against a criterion the task does not assess has done excellent work for no marks. Checking which criteria apply before starting, and comparing the draft against those descriptors before submitting, is a habit rather than an ability and it is the fastest improvement available.

faqs.question: Our child moves into the Diploma next September. What do we buy now?
faqs.answer: Not more content. The Diploma assumes two things the MYP does not drill: timed recall and command-term discipline. So timed writing practice, short answers to specific command terms, and for intended Analysis and Approaches students a block on surds, indices, rearrangement and algebraic fractions done quickly without a calculator, because that course has a non-calculator paper. If your child is also changing school at sixteen, ask the receiving school which Higher Level combinations it can actually timetable.

faqs.question: Our child joined an MYP school from a British curriculum mid-year. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With the system rather than the subject. A student arriving from Key Stage 3 or an IGCSE pathway has usually never read a task sheet, never compared a draft against band descriptors and never kept a process journal, and will lose marks on all three while knowing the content perfectly well. Two or three sessions on how criterion assessment works, applied to a live task, is the fastest and cheapest intervention available in that situation.

faqs.question: Do interdisciplinary units need their own support?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and they catch students out when they do. An interdisciplinary unit is assessed against interdisciplinary criteria rather than the subject criteria, and it rewards genuine integration of two subject groups. Students typically apply one subject's thinking well and treat the other as decoration, which is precisely what the criteria do not reward. They also come round rarely, so send the task sheet if a unit is running and the mark matters, because the descriptors are unfamiliar.

faqs.question: What time should MYP sessions be from these gates?
faqs.answer: Between about 16:30 and 20:00, with younger MYP students earlier. With no school inside Jumeirah Islands every pupil travels out and arrives home between roughly 15:40 and 16:50, so 17:00 is the dependable start. Criterion work is reading and careful comparison rather than energy, which means it suffers less from a later slot than mathematics does, and Year 10 and 11 students often work well after dinner. Saturday morning suits long tasks and project work.

intro.heading: Why a good subject tutor can be useless in the MYP
paragraphs: Here is the honest answer to the question behind this search. Plenty of competent tutors live within reach of Jumeirah Park. Far fewer understand how the Middle Years Programme is actually marked, and in the MYP that gap matters more than subject knowledge, because a student can know the content thoroughly and still score a 4.

MYP assessment works through criteria rather than through a syllabus of examinable content. Each subject group has four criteria, lettered A to D, each marked on a 1-8 scale against published descriptors. The four criterion marks are then converted into a 1-7 grade using boundary tables. A task sheet tells the student which criteria the task assesses and what the descriptors require at each band.

That changes what tutoring has to do. A student losing marks in MYP science is usually not short of knowledge; they have written a method nobody could repeat, left a variable uncontrolled, or produced an evaluation that reports whether the experiment worked rather than assessing it. A student losing marks in MYP maths has often found the right answer without generalising the pattern or communicating the reasoning.

A tutor who has only taught examined courses will teach content, because that is what they know how to do, and the student will finish the term knowing more and scoring the same. A tutor who understands the system opens the task sheet, reads the descriptor for the band the student is aiming at, and works on the specific thing that is missing.

The supply picture explains why this is hard to solve locally. The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum, and Middle Years students are a subset of that figure spread across a handful of continuum schools, none of them inside this community. There is no reason the right tutor for your child's subject group happens to live a short drive away.

So the honest local answer is this: filter for criterion fluency, not for distance. IB Gram matches your child to a tutor who works from the school's own task sheets and descriptors, teaching live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and that is stated plainly rather than discovered later.

There is a practical advantage to the format here. MYP work is documentary: task sheets, descriptors, drafts, rubrics, project journals. All of that can be open on a shared screen while a tutor points at the exact line in a descriptor that the student's work does not yet meet. That is harder to do with two people and one printed sheet on a kitchen table.

programmes.name: Early MYP

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent project with a product or outcome, a process journal and a report, assessed against its own criteria. dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.subjectsIntro: The eight MYP subject groups, with the four criteria each uses and where marks are most often lost. Ask any prospective tutor to name the criteria for your child's subject; a specialist does it instantly.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Marks go missing on investigating patterns, where students find a result without generalising it, and on communicating, where correct work is presented without notation or explanation.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The two middle criteria are where almost all the lost marks sit: an unrepeatable method, an uncontrolled variable, or an evaluation that reports success rather than assessing the method.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students summarise where the criterion asks them to analyse how meaning is constructed, and they lose organising marks for essays with no visible structure. Both respond quickly to work on thesis sentences and paragraph planning.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the criterion that separates a 6 from a 4, and it requires evaluating sources and perspectives rather than reporting them. Investigating marks depend on the research question being narrow enough to answer.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, with phase-based expectations rather than year-based ones. Students lose marks by producing accurate but simple language where the phase descriptor expects range, and by not addressing the task's audience and purpose explicitly.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Design is where criterion discipline is most visible: a strong product with no documented design specification or testing against it scores far below a modest product that is properly evidenced.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than students expect, and responding marks require genuine engagement with other work rather than description of their own.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written criteria surprise students who assumed the subject was practical, and reflection is where the accessible marks are.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units that combine two subject groups and are assessed against interdisciplinary criteria rather than the subject ones. Students apply one subject's thinking and ignore the integration, which is precisely what the criteria reward. Rare in tutoring and worth asking about when a unit is running.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills, taught across the programme rather than as a subject. In practice this is where MYP tutoring often does the most good: planning a long task, keeping a journal, meeting a staged deadline, checking work against a rubric before submitting.

sections.heading: How four criteria become a 1-7 grade
paragraphs: This is the mechanism almost no parent has had explained, and once it is clear the reports stop being mysterious. Each subject group is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D. Each criterion is marked out of 8 against published descriptors, giving a maximum criterion total of 32 for the subject. That total is then converted into a 1-7 grade using boundary tables.

The consequence is that the four criteria are not interchangeable. A student scoring 7 and 7 on the two criteria they find comfortable and 3 and 3 on the other two has a total of 20, which is a middling grade, while a student scoring 5 across all four has the same total. The route to a better grade runs through the weakest criterion, not through more work on the strongest.

That is why the task sheet matters so much. A task sheet states which criteria it assesses, and it is entirely normal for a task to assess only two of the four. A student who writes brilliantly against criterion A on a task that assesses C and D has done excellent work for no marks, and this happens more often than anyone admits.

Boundary tables and descriptors are set by the IB and applied by your child's school, and schools report at different points in the year with different amounts of evidence. Confirm the boundaries and the reporting policy with the school rather than relying on any tutoring page, including this one. The table shows the published shape of the conversion.

The practical instruction for a parent is short. When a grade disappoints, ask the school which criterion scores produced it. That single question turns an unreadable report into a plan, and it is free.

sections.heading: How many MYP specialists are genuinely nearby
paragraphs: The honest answer is: few, and that is a structural feature of this market rather than a reflection on Jumeirah Park. The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum. MYP students are a subset of that, spread across a handful of continuum schools, none of which is in this community.

So a tutor who has genuinely worked with MYP criteria, in your child's subject group, with a free slot in your window, and willing to drive into Jumeirah Park at 17:30, is a very short list. The last condition is what collapses it, because a tutor in demand has no reason to spend ninety minutes in traffic.

We publish our coverage position rather than imply unlimited availability. Mathematics, sciences, Language and Literature and Individuals and Societies are well covered. Language acquisition depends on the language and the phase. Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education are thinner, and for those we will sometimes tell you that criterion coaching is the useful thing we can offer rather than subject teaching.

Where a tutor covering a UAE family is based outside the UAE and teaches on Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book. Two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning it, which is the same fact handled dishonestly.

sections.heading: Test any MYP tutor in four minutes
paragraphs: You do not need to understand the programme to test someone who claims to. Four questions do it, and they have right answers rather than impressions. Ask them in the trial session, before any discussion of price, and listen for specificity.

First: name the four criteria for my child's subject. A specialist does this immediately. Second: what is the maximum criterion total for a subject and how does it become a grade? The answer is 32, converted by boundary tables applied by the school. Third: what will you ask me to send before the first session? The right answer includes the task sheet and the criterion descriptors.

Fourth, and most revealing: what will you do with my child's draft? A specialist describes reading it against the descriptor for the band being aimed at and naming what is missing. Anyone who offers to improve the writing, tidy it up or add to it has told you they do not understand the limit, and in the Personal Project that limit is an academic honesty matter.

Notice that none of these questions is about experience, qualifications or enthusiasm. Those answers cannot be checked. These four can, and a tutor who cannot produce them has not worked in this system regardless of how good they are at the subject.
