sections.heading: Where MYP marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Across subject groups the pattern is consistent, and it is not about content. The first recurring loss is communication: correct work presented without the notation, labelling, structure or explanation the criterion requires. A mathematics investigation with the right answer and no reasoning. A science graph without labelled axes. An essay with no visible organisation.

The second is evaluation and critical thinking, which is the criterion that separates a 6 from a 4 in most subject groups. Students describe where the descriptor asks them to assess: reporting that an experiment worked rather than identifying which source of uncertainty dominated, or summarising two sources rather than weighing their perspectives against each other.

The third is generalisation. In mathematics, finding a pattern in four cases and not expressing it as a rule. In sciences, drawing a conclusion from the data without connecting it to the underlying science. In Individuals and Societies, answering a research question without ever stating what the answer implies.

The fourth is simply not reading the task sheet. A student who does not check which criteria a task assesses, and does not compare their draft against the band descriptors before submitting, leaves marks on the table every single time. This is a habit rather than an ability, and it is the fastest thing to change.

A good MYP tutor spends the first session establishing which of these four dominates, using a marked task rather than a conversation. If the answer is a plan to revise the subject from the start of the unit, the task has not been read properly.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the largest independent piece of work in the MYP and it fails in predictable ways. The first is scope: a project so ambitious that the product cannot be finished or properly evidenced in the time available. The second is the process journal, which rewards documentation as the work happens and punishes reconstruction afterwards, and students almost always underestimate this.

The third is the report, where students describe what they made instead of evidencing their process against the criteria. A modest product with a well-documented journey scores better than an impressive product with no visible process, which is counter-intuitive to every student who has ever started one.

What a tutor may legitimately do is coach the process. Narrowing the goal to something achievable, planning staged deadlines, teaching what a useful journal entry looks like, teaching referencing, and reading the student's own draft report and saying which criterion band it currently meets and why. That is genuinely valuable and it is where the marks are.

What a tutor may not do is produce, write, part-write or rewrite any part of the project, the journal or the report. Submitting work that is not the student's own is an academic honesty matter handled by the school and the IB, and the consequence falls on the student. There are operators in this market selling completed internal assessments at four-figure prices; treat that offer as a reason to walk away.

We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides or assessment documents. Your child's school holds what it needs and the supervision arrangement is the school's. A tutor works alongside that, never in place of it.

sections.heading: MYP 5 into the Diploma: what to do in the final year
paragraphs: This is the most valuable advice on the page for a Jumeirah Park family, because the step from the MYP into the Diploma is where well-prepared students stumble. MYP students arrive at the Diploma strong on process, independent work and documentation, and often under-trained in the two things examinations demand: timed recall and exam technique.

The specific gaps are predictable. Writing to time, which a programme built on extended tasks rarely drills. Answering a question that demands a specific command term rather than a full exploration of a topic. And in mathematics, algebraic fluency at speed, because the Diploma's Analysis and Approaches assumes manipulation that is fast and exact, with a non-calculator paper.

The best use of the final MYP year is therefore not more content. It is timed writing practice, command-term discipline, and in mathematics a block on surds, indices, rearrangement and algebraic fractions done quickly and without a calculator. Those three things, in that year, remove most of the first-term difficulty in the Diploma.

For students moving school at sixteen, which is common in this community because the local school runs the British curriculum, add one more item: find out which Higher Level subjects the receiving school can actually timetable together. Option blocks constrain combinations more than parents expect, and that is a question to ask before results rather than after.

sections.heading: Scheduling from Jumeirah Park, and what it costs
paragraphs: MYP students in this community all travel to school, because the school inside Jumeirah Park runs the British curriculum. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30, and a bus route serving Al Barsha or Jumeirah Village gets most children home between 15:20 and 16:40 depending on district. There is no metro station inside the community.

The usable weekday window is roughly 16:30 to 20:00 for this age group. Younger MYP students do better earlier, because criterion work requires reading and careful comparison rather than energy. Year 10 and 11 students can take a later slot. A Saturday morning session suits long tasks and project work, which is where a ninety-minute block genuinely helps.

On cost, published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB work sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65, which buys supervision rather than criterion coaching.

Bestimate's monthly estimates are the better planning tool: AED 240-600 for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. In-home visits carry a travel premium at AED 180-350, and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. All figures are the providers' own, read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price.

Where MYP families get the best return is short and specific: a block of criterion coaching timed to a real task, rather than an open-ended weekly subject arrangement. Two or three sessions on reading task sheets and checking a draft against descriptors often changes more than a term of content teaching.

faqs.question: Why is my child's MYP grade low when they clearly know the subject?
faqs.answer: Because MYP marks come from four criteria rather than from content recall, and the weakest criterion drags the total. Each criterion is marked out of 8 against published descriptors, giving a total out of 32 that is converted into a 1-7 grade by boundary tables the school applies. A student strong on knowledge and weak on communication or evaluation scores in the middle. Ask the school which criterion scores produced the grade; that single question usually explains the whole report.

faqs.question: Which documents does a tutor need from us to be any use at all?
faqs.answer: The task sheet and the criterion descriptors for the subject, plus a recent marked task if you have one. The task sheet states which criteria the task assesses, which is frequently only two of the four, and the descriptors state what each band requires. Without them a tutor can only teach content, which is rarely the binding problem. A tutor who asks only for the textbook or the topic has told you what the sessions will look like.

faqs.question: Are there MYP specialists living near Jumeirah Park?
faqs.answer: Very few, and the reason is structural. The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum, MYP students are a subset of that, and the continuum schools are in Al Barsha, The Meadows and further out rather than in this community. Narrow it to one subject group with a free early-evening slot and a willingness to drive here, and the list is almost empty. Matching online solves it.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to the house in Jumeirah Park?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no centre here either. MYP support for Jumeirah Park families is live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time. For this programme the format is genuinely well suited, because task sheets, descriptors, drafts and rubrics can all be open on a shared screen. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-500 an hour including travel if presence in the room is essential.

faqs.question: How does the 1 to 8 criterion marking turn into the grade on the report?
faqs.answer: Four criteria, each marked out of 8, give a total out of 32, which is converted into a 1-7 grade using boundary tables. Broadly, 28-32 reports as a 7, 24-27 as a 6, 19-23 as a 5, 15-18 as a 4, 10-14 as a 3 and below that a 1 or 2. Boundaries are set by the IB and applied by the school, and schools report at different points with different evidence, so confirm your school's policy rather than relying on this page.

faqs.question: My child says the task only assessed two criteria. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Entirely normal, and it is one of the most useful things for a student to notice. A task sheet states which criteria it assesses, and many tasks assess only two. A student who writes brilliantly against a criterion the task does not assess has done excellent work for no marks. Checking which criteria apply before starting, and comparing the draft against those descriptors before submitting, is a habit rather than an ability and it is the fastest improvement available.

faqs.question: Where exactly does legitimate Personal Project coaching stop?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful help is mostly in the places students neglect. A tutor can help narrow an over-ambitious goal, teach staged planning, explain what a useful process journal entry looks like and when to write it, teach referencing, and read the student's own draft report and say which criterion band it currently meets. A tutor may never produce, write or rewrite any part of the project, journal or report. The consequence of crossing that line falls on the student.

faqs.question: Should we compare an MYP report with a neighbour's IGCSE grades?
faqs.answer: It is not a meaningful comparison, though almost every family in this community tries it. The MYP reports a 1-7 grade derived from criterion totals across four criteria, assessed internally against descriptors; IGCSE reports a 9-1 grade from external examinations. They measure different things with different instruments at different points. If you want a comparison that means something, ask both schools what their sixth form expects for entry into the subject your child wants.

faqs.question: What should the final MYP year be spent on if the Diploma is next?
faqs.answer: Not more content. The Diploma assumes two things the MYP does not drill: timed recall and command-term discipline. So timed writing practice, short answers to specific command terms, and in mathematics a block on surds, indices, rearrangement and algebraic fractions done quickly without a calculator, because Analysis and Approaches has a non-calculator paper. Those three things remove most first-term Diploma difficulty. If your child is also changing school, ask what Higher Level combinations can actually be timetabled.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups can you not easily staff?
faqs.answer: Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education are thin, and Language Acquisition depends on the language and the phase. For those we will often say that criterion coaching on the student's own task is the useful thing we can offer rather than subject teaching, and we say it before you book rather than after. Mathematics, sciences, Language and Literature and Individuals and Societies are well covered and usually matched within the same week.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough to move an MYP grade?
faqs.answer: Often one short block is better than a weekly arrangement. Because the problem is usually a specific criterion rather than general knowledge, two or three sessions timed to a real task, with the task sheet and descriptors open, can change more than a term of content teaching. Where there is a genuine knowledge gap, usually in mathematics or sciences, a weekly hour is the right instrument. We will tell you which case you are in from a marked task.

faqs.question: What does criterion D usually mean, and why is it the weakest?
faqs.answer: It varies by subject group but it is frequently the evaluative or applied criterion: reflecting on the impacts of science, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, thinking critically in Individuals and Societies, evaluating in Design. It is the weakest because it asks students to assess rather than to report, which is a harder skill and one rarely taught directly. It is also the criterion that most reliably separates a 6 from a 4, which makes it the best target for a short block.

faqs.question: Our child joined an MYP school mid-year from a British curriculum. What now?
faqs.answer: Spend the first sessions on the system rather than the subject. A student arriving from an IGCSE or Key Stage 3 background has usually never read a task sheet, never compared a draft against band descriptors, and never kept a process journal, and they will lose marks for all three while knowing the content perfectly well. Two or three sessions on how criterion assessment works, applied to a live task, is the fastest intervention available in this situation.

faqs.question: What tells us the criterion coaching has actually worked?
faqs.answer: The evidence is the school's next marked task, not our impression of the sessions. We look for the weakest criterion moving up a band, and for the student checking their own draft against the descriptors before submitting without being told to. If neither has happened after a short block, either the diagnosis was wrong or the match is, and we change one of those rather than adding hours. Nobody can honestly promise a grade.

faqs.question: Do interdisciplinary units need separate support?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and they catch students out when they do. An interdisciplinary unit is assessed against interdisciplinary criteria rather than the subject criteria, and it rewards genuine integration of two subject groups. Students typically apply one subject's thinking well and treat the other as decoration, which is exactly what the criteria do not reward. If a unit is running and the mark matters, send the task sheet, because the descriptors are different from the ones your child is used to.

intro.heading: No single deadline, which is exactly why the timing goes wrong
paragraphs: Every other page about tutoring in Dubai can count backwards from an examination. The Middle Years Programme cannot, and that single fact explains most of the money wasted on it. There is no external paper in the great majority of schools. The grade is assembled from classroom tasks assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, each scored on a published band, with task-specific clarifications written by the teacher. Nothing in the year has the gravitational pull of a May session.

So families in Jumeirah Village Circle hire on emotion instead of on a calendar — usually within a week of a report arriving that nobody can read — and then keep paying because there is no natural end point. A standing weekly slot through Years 7 to 9 is the commonest arrangement in this part of the market and almost never the right one.

There are three clocks that do run, and they are the ones worth planning around. The first is the reporting cycle, because a criterion score is noise in isolation and signal when the same letter is weak twice running or weak across several unrelated subjects. The second is the option and stream dates, usually at the end of Middle Years Year 3 and again at the end of Year 4, when subject choices, mathematics streams and language phases narrow the path towards the Diploma. The third is the Personal Project timeline in Year 5, which is won or lost in its first fortnight.

The fourth clock only appears at the very end: the handover into the Diploma, where the criteria model's strengths transfer well and two specific skills do not. Those two — algebraic manipulation to automaticity and sustained writing under time pressure — are worth four to six sessions in the summer before Year 12 and are cheaper then than at any later point.

There is a structural fix that follows from all of this and that almost nobody offers: end the block before the next report. A four to six session block scheduled to finish before the next reporting cycle turns the report into the measurement rather than the trigger for further spending. If the targeted criterion has moved, nothing more is needed. If it has not, the approach or the tutor changes. In a programme with no examination to count back from, that is the only honest substitute for a deadline.

IB Gram teaches Jumeirah Village Circle students one-to-one over live video at a fixed time in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Our fee follows a free trial lesson, and in this programme more than any other we will sometimes advise waiting for the next report rather than booking anything at all.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-c.subjectsIntro: Each subject group has its own four criteria with its own vocabulary, and the useful question is which letter is weak rather than which subject. Here is what each group assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · standard and extended streams
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students who calculate quickly often score poorly on investigating patterns, which wants a general rule found and justified rather than an answer produced.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The design criterion concentrates the marks and the losses, usually because a method is written with no stated controlled variable.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. A student can write fluently and still lose the analysing criterion for describing what a text says rather than how it achieves its effect, which is the most common pattern in this group.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · phases 1 to 6
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed by phase rather than year group. Phase placement is worth checking before buying anything: a student assessed above their actual phase appears to be failing when they are simply in the wrong band.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. The thinking-critically criterion wants evaluation of sources and perspectives and gets more description, which is the single most coachable error in the programme.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Students who build competently lose marks on documentation, because the criteria sit as much in the recorded design process as in the product.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. The process journal carries real weight and talented performers routinely underscore because the process was reconstructed afterwards rather than recorded as it happened.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on and improving performance. Two of the four criteria are written rather than physical, which surprises sporty students in this community every year.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Research, communication, thinking, social and self-management skills, assessed indirectly through every subject's criteria. When the same criterion letter is weak across four unrelated subjects, this is usually what is being measured rather than subject knowledge.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units combining two subject groups, assessed on disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection. Students treat them as double homework rather than as a distinct task type, which is why the marks return lower than either parent subject.

sections.heading: The reporting cycle is the clock
paragraphs: With no external paper to count back from, the reporting cycle is the only regular signal a family gets, and reading it properly is most of what good timing in this programme consists of. Each subject is assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, each scored on a published band up to 8, with the four summing to a maximum of 32 and converting to a subject grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries the school publishes.

The crucial point about timing is that a single criterion score is usually noise. Each task assesses different criteria against different task-specific clarifications, so a student can score well on one piece and poorly on the next without anything having changed. In Years 7 to 9 especially, one low number is not a reason to buy anything.

A pattern is different, and there are two kinds worth acting on. The same criterion letter weak across two consecutive reporting cycles in the same subject is a genuine signal about that subject. The same letter weak across several unrelated subjects in one cycle is a signal about an untaught skill — usually evaluation, critical thinking or structured communication — and that is the more valuable finding, because one short block improves several subjects at once.

So the discipline is to read across the letters rather than down the subject list, and to wait for the second data point when the first is ambiguous. From Year 10 the calculation shifts, because criterion profiles start influencing which Diploma courses are offered at sixteen, and acting on a clear pattern early is worth more then. The table sets out what to do with each shape of report.

sections.heading: The option and stream dates that narrow the path
paragraphs: The second clock is quieter and more consequential. At the end of Middle Years Year 3 and again at the end of Year 4, most schools make decisions that shape what will be available at sixteen: which subject groups a student continues with, whether they take standard or extended mathematics, and which language acquisition phase they sit in.

The mathematics stream is the one with the longest shadow. A student placed in standard rather than extended mathematics at 14 is, at most schools, less likely to be offered Analysis and Approaches Higher Level at 16, and that in turn affects which degree courses remain open. Nobody announces this and most families discover it in Year 11 when the Diploma option form appears.

The practical consequence is that a criterion pattern showing weakness in mathematics in Year 9 is a more urgent signal than the same pattern in Year 8, because a stream decision is imminent. Four to six sessions on the mathematics criteria, or on the algebraic fluency underneath them, taken in the second term of Year 9 can change a placement that the same block taken a year later cannot.

Language phase is the second. Placement above a student's actual phase makes a capable child look as though they are failing, and it is a question for the school rather than a tuition problem. Ask what phase your child is assessed in and why, before buying language support. Subject group continuation is the third and the least reversible: a student who drops a subject group at 14 may not be able to pick it up at 16.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, month by month
paragraphs: The third clock is the only one in the programme with a genuine deadline, and it runs across most of Middle Years Year 5. The project is assessed against its own criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and reporting, with a process journal kept throughout and a report at the end. It is also the best rehearsal available for the Extended Essay two years later.

The decisive moment is the first fortnight, and almost every failure traces to it. Students in Jumeirah Village Circle reliably propose goals that depend on other people: a community event, a fundraising drive, a build requiring parts that have to be shipped, a collaboration with a club whose calendar they do not control. When the external dependency fails in month three, the project fails with it, and no amount of writing rescues a journal describing something that did not happen.

So the highest-value hour available in the whole programme is a week-one conversation asking whether this goal is achievable by this student alone, within this timeline, with resources already to hand. Scoping down is almost always right. A small project executed and documented well scores considerably better than an ambitious one abandoned, and students find that genuinely surprising to hear.

After that the calendar is about the journal rather than the product. It must be kept as the project happens, not reconstructed afterwards — reconstruction is visible to an assessor and is not honest. The boundary throughout: a tutor questions the goal, holds the student to their own timeline, explains what each criterion rewards and gives feedback on what the student has written. A tutor does not write, rewrite or complete any of it, supply the goal, or edit a draft to completion, and ours decline when asked.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units, and why the marks come back low
paragraphs: Interdisciplinary units appear at intervals through the programme and they produce a predictable surprise: a student who scores well in both parent subjects comes back with a lower mark than either. The reason is that an interdisciplinary unit is assessed against its own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection, and synthesis is a distinct skill that neither parent subject teaches directly.

Students treat these units as double homework — do the history part, do the science part, staple them together. The criteria want the two disciplines brought into genuine contact: a claim that could not be made from either subject alone, with an explicit account of how the combination produced it. That is a specific thing to be taught and it is almost never taught explicitly.

The calendar point is that these units are scheduled, so a family can see them coming. When a unit is announced, one session on what synthesis means and what the reflection criterion wants is usually enough, and it transfers to every subsequent interdisciplinary unit. That is a far better purchase than reacting to the mark afterwards.

It is also a useful early indicator for the Diploma. Students who handle synthesis and reflection well in a Middle Years interdisciplinary unit tend to handle Theory of Knowledge comfortably two years later, because the demand is recognisably the same. Students who struggle with it are showing you, at 13 or 14, exactly which part of the Diploma core will need attention.

sections.heading: The handover into the Diploma, counted backwards
paragraphs: The last clock appears in Middle Years Year 5 and runs into Year 12. Most of what the criteria model builds transfers very well: a student who can unpack a task against its clarification, evaluate a source and keep an honest process journal arrives at the Diploma's internal assessments already able to do what much of their cohort meets for the first time in Year 12. That is worth saying to a worried Year 9 parent.

Two things do not transfer, and both are specific. The first is algebraic manipulation to automaticity. The criteria model rewards finding and justifying a general rule, which is a more sophisticated skill, but it does not drill manipulation until it is automatic — and Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, Physics Higher Level and Chemistry Higher Level all assume automaticity on day one. Four to six sessions in the summer before Year 12 closes that gap at its cheapest.

The second is sustained writing under time pressure. Middle Years assessment is typically completed over days with access to resources; a Diploma Paper 2 is ninety minutes with nothing. Students who write thoughtfully over a week can produce very little in an hour, and discovering that in a Year 12 mock is an expensive way to find out. Three or four sessions of timed extended writing transfers to every essay-based subject at once.

Counted backwards, then: the summer before Year 12 is the moment for both blocks, because it competes with nothing. The second-best moment is the first term of Year 12, where it competes with new content. The worst is Year 13, where the same work costs several times as much because it is being done alongside examination preparation.

sections.heading: Holidays, Ramadan and the usable hour
paragraphs: The UAE academic year runs in three terms from late August to early July, with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break later. For a Middle Years student those breaks matter less than for a Year 11 or Year 13 student, because there is no examination bearing down — with one exception. In Middle Years Year 5, the winter break usually sits at the point where a Personal Project is either on schedule or quietly not, which makes it the best moment for a mid-project review.

Ramadan shortens school days and restructures evenings around Iftar, and the effect on a thirteen-year-old's available concentration is larger than on an older student's. Because Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, it currently falls inside the spring term. The sensible response for this age group is to pause rather than reschedule: a four-session criteria block will achieve more in the weeks after than spread through it.

On the ordinary week, this community has a specific shape for younger students. Most travel five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South, or eight to fifteen to Motor City, and are home by about 3.40pm. Dubai Sports City is adjacent and its academies take younger children out between four and six. A thirteen-year-old needs food and a genuine break — more than a Diploma student does, not less.

So sessions for this age group work between 5.45pm and 7.15pm on weekdays, kept to sixty minutes rather than ninety. A younger student produces more in a focused hour than in a stretched ninety minutes, and the shorter session is easier to defend in a family calendar, which matters because consistency is what makes a four-session block land. Weekend mornings are the right slot for Personal Project work.

sections.heading: What it costs, and why waiting is often the right answer
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates do not vary by programme, so a Middle Years session costs what any other session costs: roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, with a budget band of AED 45 to AED 150 typically delivered by a university student, and in-home visits including travel at AED 180 to AED 500. One provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What should vary is the quantity, and at this age it should be small and time-bound. A four to six session criteria block at a mid-band rate is roughly AED 800 to AED 1,200. A Personal Project block is similar. A pre-Diploma transition block is the same again. By contrast, a weekly slot across a full academic year is in the region of AED 6,000 to AED 7,000, and for a Year 8 student it is very rarely justified by anything a report actually shows.

There is one case where the budget band fits well and it is worth naming. A Year 7 student who will not begin homework unaided needs supervision and routine rather than subject expertise, and a permitted university-student tutor at AED 60 an hour provides exactly that. Paying a specialist rate for that service wastes money; paying a budget rate for criteria coaching wastes it differently.

And the honest position on waiting. In Years 7 to 9, when a single low criterion score is usually noise, the correct advice is frequently to do nothing until the next reporting cycle confirms a pattern. We give that advice regularly and it costs us bookings. Every figure here was read from the provider's own published page in October 2026 and describes the market rather than IB Gram, whose fee follows a free trial lesson. For context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects and the timetable they occupy
paragraphs: A calendar point specific to Dubai, and one new arrivals in Jumeirah Village Circle regularly miss. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position behind this is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The organisation is prescribed. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for Arab and non-Arab groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

For planning purposes the figure that matters is the time. Instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. That is genuine timetable space competing with eight Middle Years subject groups, and it is a real argument against adding two weekly tuition commitments in Year 8.

One further constraint shapes what tuition in these subjects can even be. For the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so support has to follow the school's own material rather than an outside scheme. Where the school is the better route we will say so rather than taking the booking.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor, and what nobody holds
paragraphs: A Middle Years Programme runs five years; a private tuition work permit runs two. That mismatch is worth knowing before a Jumeirah Village Circle family settles into a long arrangement with one tutor, because the document will need renewing more than once across a child's time in the programme. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, which grants it free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Which means a tutor whose permit has lapsed can be back in order inside a week, and a tutor who has never applied has no cost to point at as the reason.

The eligible categories matter particularly in this age range, because the budget band is a realistic option for a younger student. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. So a permitted nineteen-year-old providing homework routine to a Year 7 student is operating entirely within the rules. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted.

One boundary to observe, and it is tempting in this programme because the criterion language is written for teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being treated as exact wording. Do not engage your child's own subject teacher privately, however convenient it seems when only they have written the clarification.

And what nobody holds. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, criteria documents or assessment material; tutors work from what the school has issued.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report looks bad. Should we hire a tutor now?
faqs.answer: Often not yet, and this is the most useful thing we can say about timing. Each Middle Years task assesses different criteria against different task-specific clarifications, so a single low criterion score is usually noise rather than signal, particularly in Years 7 to 9. Wait for the next reporting cycle. Act when a pattern appears: the same criterion letter weak across two consecutive cycles in one subject, or the same letter weak across several unrelated subjects at once, which is the more valuable finding.

faqs.question: What makes a criterion score a pattern rather than a bad week?
faqs.answer: Repetition in one of two directions. Vertically: the same letter weak in the same subject across two consecutive reporting cycles, which says something about that subject. Horizontally: the same letter weak across several unrelated subjects in a single cycle, which says something about an untaught skill — usually evaluation, critical thinking or structured communication. The second is better news, because one four to six session block improves several subjects simultaneously rather than one.

faqs.question: When does the maths stream decision happen, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: Usually at the end of Middle Years Year 3, and it has the longest shadow of anything in the programme. A student placed in standard rather than extended mathematics at 14 is, at most schools, less likely to be offered Analysis and Approaches Higher Level at 16, which in turn affects which degree courses stay open. Nobody announces this and most families discover it when the Diploma option form appears in Year 11. A mathematics criteria block in the second term of Year 9 can change a placement that the same block later cannot.

faqs.question: Could my child be in the wrong language acquisition phase?
faqs.answer: It happens, and it is worth checking before buying any language support. Language acquisition is assessed by phase rather than by year group, so a student placed above their actual phase appears to be failing when they are simply in the wrong band — and the report will look like a learning problem. Ask the school which phase your child is assessed in and on what basis. The answer is free, arrives within a day, and occasionally removes the need for tuition entirely.

faqs.question: When should Personal Project help start?
faqs.answer: In the first fortnight, and the single most valuable hour is spent asking whether the goal is achievable by this student alone, within the timeline, with resources already to hand. Almost every project failure traces to a goal that depended on other people — an event, a fundraiser, a build needing shipped parts, a club collaboration. When the dependency fails in month three the project fails with it. A small project executed and documented well scores considerably better than an ambitious one abandoned.

faqs.question: Why does my child score lower on interdisciplinary units than in either subject?
faqs.answer: Because an interdisciplinary unit is assessed against its own criteria, including synthesis, which neither parent subject teaches directly. Students treat these units as double homework — do the history part, do the science part, staple them together — where the criteria want a claim that could not be made from either subject alone, with an explicit account of how the combination produced it. One session when a unit is announced covers it and transfers to every later unit.

faqs.question: What should we do in the summer before the Diploma starts?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions on the two things the criteria model does not drill. First, algebraic manipulation to automaticity, because Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and the Higher Level sciences assume it on day one while the criteria model rewards finding and justifying a general rule instead. Second, sustained writing under time pressure, since Middle Years assessment is typically completed over days with resources and a Diploma Paper 2 is ninety minutes with nothing. That summer is when both are cheapest, because they compete with nothing.

faqs.question: Does the MYP leave my child behind for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: In most respects the opposite. A student who can unpack a task against its clarification, evaluate sources and perspectives, and keep an honest process journal arrives at the Diploma's internal assessments already able to do what much of their cohort meets for the first time in Year 12. Two specific skills need separate attention — timed extended writing and automatic algebraic manipulation — and both are four to six session blocks. Everything else the programme builds is exactly what the Diploma asks for.

faqs.question: How long should an MYP block run for?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions, ending before the next reporting cycle. That is the structural answer to a programme with no examination: let the report be the measurement rather than the trigger for more spending. If the targeted criterion has moved, nothing further is needed. If it has not, change the approach or the tutor. A standing weekly slot through Years 7 to 9 is the commonest arrangement in this part of the market and almost never justified by what a report actually shows.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to pay for MYP support?
faqs.answer: A four to six session criteria block at a mid-band market rate is roughly AED 800 to AED 1,200, and that is the right order of magnitude for most Middle Years problems. Published Dubai rates run about AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online, with a budget band of AED 45 to AED 150 that genuinely suits homework routine support for a Year 7 student. A weekly slot across a full academic year is AED 6,000 to AED 7,000 and is rarely justified at this age. Market figures, researched October 2026.

faqs.question: Should sessions continue through Ramadan at this age?
faqs.answer: Usually pause rather than reschedule, which is different advice from what we would give a Year 13 student. School days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and the effect on a thirteen-year-old's available concentration is larger than on an older student's. A four-session criteria block will achieve more in the weeks after Ramadan than spread thinly through it. The exception is Middle Years Year 5, where a Personal Project deadline may not wait and a short mid-project review is worth keeping.

faqs.question: When can a session realistically run for a younger student in the Circle?
faqs.answer: Between 5.45pm and 7.15pm on weekdays, and sixty minutes rather than ninety. Most Jumeirah Village Circle students travel five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South, so they are home by about 3.40pm — but Dubai Sports City is adjacent and its academies take younger children out between four and six, and a thirteen-year-old needs food and a genuine break afterwards. A focused hour produces more than a stretched ninety minutes and is easier to defend in the family calendar.

faqs.question: Is the winter break worth using for a Middle Years student?
faqs.answer: Less than for an examination year, with one real exception. In Middle Years Year 5 the winter break usually sits at the point where a Personal Project is either on schedule or quietly not, which makes it the right moment for an honest mid-project review against the student's own timeline. For Years 7 to 9 there is no deadline bearing down, so the break is better spent as a break. The UAE year runs in three terms from late August to early July.

faqs.question: What if the report shows my child is already improving?
faqs.answer: Then buy nothing, and be sceptical of anyone who suggests otherwise. A student on an upward line after a weak cycle will usually keep improving without a tutor, and nobody in this market volunteers that. The same applies when criterion scores are simply moving around between tasks, which is normal in Years 7 to 9. We would rather say so and lose the booking, because an arrangement that was never needed is the easiest kind of spending to avoid.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-c.closingHeading: Act on the pattern, not on the report
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-c.closingBody: The Middle Years Programme has no examination to count back from, so timing has to come from somewhere else: the reporting cycle, the stream and phase decisions at the end of Year 3, the Personal Project calendar in Year 5, and the summer before the Diploma. Send us the report, two returned tasks and where your child is in the five years. If what you have is noise, we will tell you to wait. If it is a pattern, we will propose a four to six session block that ends before the next report, and you can test the tutor in a free trial lesson over live video.

intro.heading: A report full of numbers out of eight, and what they mean
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme reports differently from everything a British or Indian curriculum parent has seen before, and that is the first problem. There is no percentage and no letter. Instead each subject returns four achievement levels, one per criterion, each out of 8, which are then totalled out of 32 and converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. A parent looking at 5, 6, 4, 3 in Mathematics has a precise diagnosis in front of them and no way to read it.

Reading it changes what you buy. The four MYP mathematics criteria are Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A student scoring well on the first and poorly on the third does not have a mathematics problem; they have a communication problem, and no amount of extra topic teaching will fix it. A student scoring well on the first and poorly on the fourth cannot transfer a technique into an unfamiliar context, which is a different intervention again. The report is telling you which of the four to work on, and most families never find out.

The second thing worth knowing is that the criteria differ by subject group. The sciences use Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science. Language and literature uses Analysing, Organising, Producing text, and Using language. Individuals and societies uses Knowing and understanding, Investigating, Communicating, and Thinking critically. Learning which four apply to which subject takes ten minutes and makes every future report legible. It also makes a parents' evening a different conversation, because you can ask about a named criterion rather than asking whether the term went well.

Third, the Personal Project, which students complete in the final MYP year. It is assessed against its own criteria, it is the single largest independent piece of work a student has produced to that point, and it is where a tutor's role is narrowest — process coaching only, because the project must be the student's own. Families in Jumeirah Village Triangle ask about it more than any other MYP component, usually in the term it is due rather than the year before. That timing is itself the problem: the criteria reward a documented process, and a process cannot be documented retrospectively without it showing.

And fourth, the comparison a Dubai family actually faces: MYP or IGCSE at fourteen. Both lead to the Diploma or to A Levels, both are respectable, and they prepare a student differently. This page sets out that comparison honestly rather than advocating, because the right answer depends on the child and on where they are heading. Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

sections.heading: Reading an MYP report: criteria, levels and the 1-7 conversion
paragraphs: An MYP subject report gives four achievement levels, one per criterion, each from 0 to 8. Those four are added to give a total out of 32, and the total is converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries published by the IB. The two-step structure is the key to reading the report: the grade tells you roughly where the student sits, and the four levels tell you exactly what to do about it.

That diagnostic detail is far better than a percentage, and it is routinely wasted. A student with 7, 7, 3, 3 and a student with 5, 5, 5, 5 can end up on the same total and the same grade, while needing completely different work. The first has secure knowledge and cannot communicate or transfer it; the second is uniformly mid. Teaching both of them more content is the wrong response, and in the first case it is actively wasteful.

The criterion names are published in each subject guide and differ by subject group. In mathematics they are Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In the sciences they are Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science. In language and literature they are Analysing, Organising, Producing text, and Using language. Learning which four apply to your child's subjects is a ten-minute job that makes every subsequent report legible.

A note on comparability. Because assessment is internal and continuous, MYP levels are awarded by the school against the published descriptors rather than by an external examiner. Schools moderate internally and the IB provides guidance, but a level 6 at one school and a level 6 at another are not calibrated against each other the way an examination grade is. This is not a criticism of the programme; it is a reason to read the descriptors yourself rather than to treat the number as absolute.

sections.heading: The four criteria, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: The criterion sets are the single most useful thing an MYP parent can learn, because they explain why a bright student can score poorly and a methodical one can score well. Each subject group has four, and they assess genuinely different things. Teaching a student more content when the weak criterion is Communicating or Reflecting is the most common error in MYP tutoring, and it is made because nobody looked up the criterion names.

In the sciences, Inquiring and designing rewards a testable hypothesis with a clear rationale, identified variables and a method a peer could follow. Processing and evaluating rewards correct processing, honest presentation and discussion of the method's limitations. A student who runs an experiment well and writes 'the results were as expected' has produced no evidence for either criterion. These are writing skills attached to scientific thinking, and they are teachable.

In individuals and societies, Thinking critically is where separation happens: evaluating sources for origin, purpose and limitation, recognising that an account has a perspective, and weighing competing interpretations rather than listing them. In language and literature, Analysing rewards writing about how a text produces its effect rather than what it contains, which is the step most capable readers have to be taught explicitly.

In design and the arts, the process is assessed alongside the product, which catches out students who make something good without documenting how. A beautifully finished design artefact with no recorded inquiry or development stage loses marks across two criteria, and the student experiences that as unfair because the thing they made is clearly good. Explaining the criterion structure to them, once, usually fixes it permanently.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and where a tutor must stop
paragraphs: The Personal Project is completed in the final MYP year and assessed against its own criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting, and the evidence recorded in the process journal. The single most important thing a family can know about it is that the product is not what carries the marks. The documented process is. A student who builds something impressive and keeps no usable journal scores poorly; a student who makes something modest and documents the inquiry, the decisions, the setbacks and the reflection scores well.

That reverses most students' instincts. Asked to choose a goal, they pick the most ambitious thing they can imagine, and the ambition then consumes the time that should have gone into documentation. The useful early intervention is to narrow the goal until it is genuinely achievable in the time available and genuinely documentable, which is a conversation worth having in the first fortnight rather than the last.

The process journal deserves its own paragraph because it is so often misunderstood. It is not a diary and it is not a scrapbook to be made pretty at the end. It is evidence: decisions made and why, sources consulted and what they changed, problems met and how they were addressed, skills attempted and how they developed. A journal assembled retrospectively reads as assembled retrospectively, and the criteria are written to detect exactly that.

Where a tutor must stop is clear and worth stating in full, because this is the component where the line is most often blurred. A tutor may question a proposed goal until it is achievable, explain what each criterion credits using the published descriptors, look at the journal and say which criterion lacks evidence, teach a research or referencing skill, and read a report draft the student wrote and name where it falls short. A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product, write or rewrite any part of the report, or construct the journal. Every word submitted and every decision recorded must be the student's.

sections.heading: MYP or IGCSE: the comparison a Dubai family actually faces
paragraphs: At Year 9 options, or at a school move, families in Jumeirah Village Triangle frequently find themselves choosing between an IB continuum school running MYP and a British-curriculum school running IGCSE. Both routes lead onward to either A Levels or the Diploma. Neither is better in the abstract, and the comparison is almost always made on reputation rather than on assessment model, which is the wrong basis.

The substantive difference is what each one trains. MYP assesses against criteria continuously and internally, rewarding inquiry, design, transfer into unfamiliar contexts, and reflection. A student who comes through it well can plan an investigation, justify a method, communicate reasoning and write about their own learning. What they typically have not done is sit a large number of timed written examinations, or drill a procedural skill to automaticity against a clock.

IGCSE assesses externally through timed papers, rewarding content security, procedural fluency, mark-scheme awareness and performance under time pressure. A student who comes through it well can execute reliably at speed and knows what an examiner credits. What they typically have not done is design their own investigation, document a process, or write reflectively about their own thinking.

The practical consequence is that each route leaves a different gap, and both gaps are closable. An MYP student entering DP1 usually needs procedural fluency and timed practice. An IGCSE student entering DP1 usually needs the internally assessed components — the investigation, the Exploration, the Extended Essay — because nothing in IGCSE prepared them for independent extended work. Knowing which gap you are buying is more useful than deciding which curriculum is superior.

sections.heading: The MYP to Diploma step, and the cheapest time to close it
paragraphs: This is the single most common reason a Jumeirah Village Triangle family calls about MYP, and it almost always arrives too late — in the first term of DP1, after a set of marked papers has come back lower than the MYP grades suggested it would. The step is real, it is predictable, and it is cheap to close in advance and expensive to close afterwards.

What changes is the assessment model, not the difficulty. MYP mathematics rewards investigating patterns and communicating reasoning; Diploma mathematics Paper 1 on the Analysis and Approaches route is sat without a calculator and rewards accurate manipulation at speed. MYP sciences reward inquiry and design; Diploma sciences Paper 2 rewards naming a principle and applying it inside a time limit. MYP language and literature rewards analysis developed over a term; Diploma Paper 1 is guided analysis of an unseen text under examination conditions.

In each case the student has the thinking and not the execution. That is good news, because execution is the more teachable of the two. Eight to twelve sessions of targeted procedural work before DP1 begins — indices, surds, rearrangement and function notation for mathematics; moles, concentration and unit prefixes for the sciences; timed writing against a clock for the humanities — closes most of the gap. The same work after the first DP1 assessment takes longer, because the student is now also behind on new content.

The long holiday between MYP and DP1 is therefore the highest-value tutoring window in the whole continuum, and it is the one almost nobody uses. A family that spends ten sessions in July and August rather than twenty in October and November gets a better result for less money, and the student starts DP1 feeling capable rather than behind.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs in Dubai, and why it should cost less than DP
paragraphs: MYP support should be cheaper than Diploma support and often is not, which is worth knowing before you agree a rate. The reason it should be cheaper is that MYP work is criterion-targeted and finite: a student with a weak Communicating level needs six to eight sessions practising the presentation of reasoning, not a two-year weekly commitment. The reason it often is not is that providers price by level of study rather than by the work involved.

The published Dubai bands, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 150-300 for qualified online subject tutors, AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one, AED 200-450 or above for IB and IGCSE specialists, and independent home tutors reaching AED 500 including travel; TutorChase at AED 270; BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240-600, AED 600-1,200 and AED 1,000-2,000 or above across the tiers.

For MYP the sensible shapes are short. A criterion block is six to eight sessions. Personal Project supervision is four to six spread across the project period. A Diploma preparation block is eight to twelve in the holiday before DP1. None of those is an open-ended weekly commitment, and a provider proposing one for a Year 8 student with a single weak criterion is selling a subscription rather than solving a problem.

One context figure worth having: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat, so tutoring is the discretionary line, which is exactly why the shape of the commitment matters more than the hourly rate.

sections.heading: Format, scheduling and the claims we do not make
paragraphs: MYP students near Jumeirah Village Triangle are commuters, because the continuum schools are in the Dubailand corridor rather than inside the community. From the Triangle that means a realistic earliest session start of about 17:00, with later slots to 21:00 on Gulf Standard Time for families whose early evening is taken. Sessions run 45 or 60 minutes and are recorded, which matters at this age because a student will often rewatch an explanation rather than ask for it twice.

Home visits exist in the Dubai market and for younger MYP students there is a genuine case for them: a Year 7 or 8 child who cannot yet self-manage a screen works better with an adult in the room. The published bands are AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table, rising to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — so this comparison is offered to inform rather than to argue.

Availability for MYP is good across mathematics, the sciences, language and literature, and individuals and societies, with a match normally inside one to three working days. Language acquisition in a minority language and some arts and design specialisms are thinner, and Personal Project supervision for an unusual goal may need a subject match rather than a general one. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, the tutor comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking.

And the claims we do not make. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and has no UAE office or centre. Separately, private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

process.title: Send the report with the four levels
process.description: An MYP report carries four achievement levels per subject, each out of 8. Those four numbers are a diagnosis. Send the report rather than a description of how the term went, and the first conversation can be about which criterion to target instead of about the subject in general.

process.title: Look up the criterion names together
process.description: The four criteria differ by subject group and are published in the subject guide. Ten minutes identifying which four apply to your child's subjects makes every future report legible and prevents the commonest mistake in MYP tutoring, which is teaching more content when the weak criterion is a writing skill.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge, spent on the student's own work against the relevant criterion descriptors. For a Communicating problem that means looking at how reasoning is presented. For an Inquiring and designing problem it means reading a method the student wrote and testing whether a peer could follow it.

process.title: A short block with a defined endpoint
process.description: Six to eight sessions for one criterion, four to six for Personal Project supervision, eight to twelve for a Diploma preparation block. MYP work should be finite. If a provider proposes an open-ended weekly slot for a single weak criterion, ask what the endpoint is.

process.title: Checked against the next school assessment
process.description: Progress is judged on the next criterion-assessed task the school sets, read against the descriptor rather than against our own exercises. If the level has not moved, either the descriptor was misread or the work between sessions did not happen, and both are better found early.

whyPoints.title: The report read as a diagnosis
whyPoints.description: Four achievement levels out of 8 per subject tell you exactly which of four distinct skills is weak. We start there rather than with a topic list, because a student with secure knowledge and low Communicating levels does not need more content.

whyPoints.title: Criterion descriptors used directly
whyPoints.description: Each level has published wording, and the target is the wording of the level above. Working from the actual descriptor rather than from a general sense of what good looks like is what makes a criterion block finite and checkable.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project treated as process
whyPoints.description: The product carries less than students assume and the documented process carries more. We narrow the goal early so it is achievable and documentable, review the journal for criterion evidence, and never write, make or assemble any part of it.

whyPoints.title: Short blocks, not subscriptions
whyPoints.description: Six to eight sessions for a criterion, four to six for the Personal Project, eight to twelve before DP1. MYP work has natural endpoints and we propose them, which bills less than an open-ended weekly slot and is the honest shape for the work.

whyPoints.title: The Diploma step closed in advance
whyPoints.description: MYP builds reasoning and the Diploma tests execution under time, so the gap is predictable. Ten sessions in the holiday before DP1 is cheaper and more effective than twenty in October, and the long holiday is the window almost nobody uses.

whyPoints.title: MYP and IGCSE compared honestly
whyPoints.description: Neither route is superior; each leaves a different gap for the Diploma. We set out the assessment models side by side so a Year 9 options decision in Jumeirah Village Triangle rests on how your child is assessed rather than on a school's reputation.

faqs.question: What do the four numbers out of eight on an MYP report mean?
faqs.answer: They are achievement levels, one per assessment criterion, each scored from 0 to 8 against published descriptors. The four are added to give a total out of 32, which the school converts to a grade from 1 to 7 using IB boundaries. The levels are the useful part: a student with 7, 7, 3, 3 and a student with 5, 5, 5, 5 can reach the same grade while needing completely different work. Look at which criterion is lowest and read the descriptor for the level above it, because that wording is the target.

faqs.question: Which criteria does MYP mathematics use?
faqs.answer: Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. That set explains a pattern parents find baffling: a child who is good at mathematics scoring poorly overall. Knowing and understanding is the computational criterion; the other three are about recognising structure, presenting reasoning clearly, and transferring a technique into an unfamiliar context. A student strong on the first and weak on the third needs practice presenting working, not more topic teaching, and six to eight sessions normally moves it.

faqs.question: Why is my child's science level low when the experiment went well?
faqs.answer: Because two of the four science criteria assess writing attached to scientific thinking. Inquiring and designing credits a testable hypothesis with a rationale, identified variables and a method a peer could follow. Processing and evaluating credits correct processing, honest presentation and discussion of the method's limitations. A student who runs the experiment competently and writes 'the results were as expected' has produced no evidence for either. The experiment going well is not what is being marked, and this is teachable in a handful of sessions once named.

faqs.question: How should my child choose a Personal Project goal?
faqs.answer: Narrower than instinct suggests. The product carries less than students assume; the documented process carries more, assessed through planning, applying skills, reflecting and the process journal. A goal too ambitious to finish consumes the time that should have gone into documentation, and then two criteria suffer. The useful test is whether the goal can be completed in the time available and whether every decision along the way can be recorded as it happens. That conversation belongs in the first fortnight of the project, not the last.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without breaching IB rules?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may question a proposed goal until it is achievable, explain what each criterion credits from the published descriptors, read the process journal and say which criterion lacks evidence, teach a research or referencing skill, and give feedback on a report draft the student wrote. A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product, write or rewrite any part of the report, or help construct the journal retrospectively. Every recorded decision and every submitted word must be the student's own.

faqs.question: Is the process journal really assessed, or is it just a record?
faqs.answer: It is assessed, and it is the component students most often misunderstand. It is not a diary and not a scrapbook to be tidied at the end: it is contemporaneous evidence of decisions made and why, sources consulted and what they changed, problems met and how they were addressed, and skills attempted and how they developed. A journal assembled retrospectively reads as assembled retrospectively, and the criteria are written to detect that. Keeping it badly is the most common reason a good Personal Project scores poorly.

faqs.question: Should a Dubai family choose MYP or IGCSE at Year 9?
faqs.answer: It depends on the child, and the comparison should be made on assessment model rather than reputation. MYP assesses continuously against criteria and rewards inquiry, design, transfer and reflection, but gives a student relatively little timed examination practice. IGCSE assesses externally through timed papers and builds content security, procedural fluency and mark-scheme awareness, but gives a student almost no experience of independent extended work. Each route therefore leaves a different gap for the Diploma, and both gaps are closable if you know which one you are buying.

faqs.question: Why did my child's grades drop when they started DP1 after MYP?
faqs.answer: Because the assessment model changed rather than because the work got harder. MYP mathematics rewards investigating patterns and communicating reasoning; Diploma Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and rewards accurate manipulation at speed. MYP sciences reward inquiry and design; Diploma science papers reward naming a principle and applying it inside a time limit. The student usually has the thinking and not the execution, which is the more teachable of the two. Eight to twelve sessions of procedural work closes most of it.

faqs.question: When is the best time to prepare for the Diploma from MYP?
faqs.answer: The long holiday before DP1 begins, and it is the window almost nobody uses. Ten sessions in July and August on indices, surds, rearrangement and function notation for mathematics, or moles, concentration and unit prefixes for the sciences, or timed writing against a clock for the humanities, closes most of the gap before the first DP1 assessment. The same work in October and November takes longer and costs more, because by then the student is behind on new content as well as short on execution.

faqs.question: Are MYP levels comparable between schools?
faqs.answer: Not in the way an examination grade is. MYP assessment is internal and continuous, awarded by the school against published descriptors, with internal moderation and IB guidance but no external examiner calibrating one school's level 6 against another's. That is not a criticism of the programme, which is designed that way deliberately, but it is a reason to read the descriptors yourself rather than treating the number as absolute. It also means a sixth-form conversation about MYP grades usually needs the descriptors alongside them.

faqs.question: Where can a JVT family find MYP schooling nearby?
faqs.answer: Not inside the community. Sunmarke School and Arcadia Global School are British-curriculum, so MYP students from Jumeirah Village Triangle commute. The closest continuum options are Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City and Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, with Nord Anglia International School Dubai, North London Collegiate School Dubai and Emirates International School Meadows also within range. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them IB-curriculum, creating 16,846 places. We name schools as context and hold no relationship with any.

faqs.question: Does an MYP tutor come to the house in Jumeirah Village Triangle?
faqs.answer: Not from us. Home visits exist in the Dubai market at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table, up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included, and for a Year 7 or 8 student who cannot yet self-manage a screen there is a genuine case for one. IB Gram delivers UAE tuition one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and runs home visits only in India. Sessions are 45 or 60 minutes, start from about 17:00 once the commute is done, and are recorded.

faqs.question: How long should an MYP tutoring block last?
faqs.answer: Shorter than most providers propose. Six to eight sessions moves a single criterion reliably. Personal Project supervision is four to six sessions spread across the project period. A Diploma preparation block is eight to twelve in the holiday before DP1. None of those is an open-ended weekly commitment, and a provider offering a year-long slot for a Year 8 student with one weak criterion is selling a subscription rather than solving a problem. Ask what the endpoint is and how it will be measured.

faqs.question: What are interdisciplinary units and why do they score badly?
faqs.answer: They are units assessed against interdisciplinary criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting, where a student has to integrate two subjects rather than work within one. They often produce a student's lowest levels of the year, and the reason is structural: integrating two disciplines is the skill being assessed and it is rarely taught as a skill in its own right. Students default to presenting two separate pieces of subject work side by side, which evidences disciplinary grounding and almost nothing for synthesising.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-t.closingHeading: Read the four levels, then buy a short block
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-jumeirah-village-t.closingBody: An MYP report is more useful than a percentage once you can read it. Four achievement levels out of 8 per subject tell you which of four distinct skills is weak, and the descriptor for the level above tells you what the target actually is. Target one criterion at a time in a block of six to eight sessions. Start the Personal Project early and keep the journal as you go, because the process is what carries the marks. And if the Diploma is next, spend ten sessions in the holiday before DP1 rather than twenty in October. Send the report and take the free diagnostic lesson.
