Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a LA Mer MYP student that means a timetable already carrying eight subject groups plus the mandatory subjects, which is the real reason one well-placed tutoring hour outperforms two.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: What MYP 5 students in continuum schools move into. The Diploma reintroduces terminal examinations, which is the single largest change a student experiences, along with internal assessments carrying fixed percentages. Students who have been marked only against criteria for five years meet timed recall under exam conditions for the first time.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is the moment tutoring demand in this cluster peaks. The specific gap is not knowledge; it is timed performance and the conventions of a mark scheme. Work done in MYP 5 on writing to a mark allocation and on finishing under time pressure is worth more than content coverage, and it is cheaper then than in the first Diploma term.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The stage before MYP in continuum schools. Students arriving in MYP 1 from PYP are used to inquiry-led work and to being assessed on process, and the change they feel most is the arrival of four named criteria with numerical marks attached to each.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving a child from a British-curriculum primary school into MYP 1 at a Jumeirah continuum school see the opposite shock: a student used to right-answer marking meets criterion C and discovers that presenting the reasoning is worth as much as reaching the answer. Two or three sessions in the first term usually settle it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-la-mer.subjectsIntro: MYP tutoring in this cluster concentrates on particular criteria within particular subject groups. These are the combinations that generate the most sessions, with what each criterion actually rewards.

subjects.name: Mathematics criterion A: knowing and understanding
subjects.description: Selecting and applying the right procedure to a familiar problem. The closest thing in MYP to conventional maths marking, and the criterion most students score well on. Low marks here usually indicate a genuine content gap rather than a presentation issue.

subjects.name: Mathematics criterion B: investigating patterns
subjects.description: Finding a rule, describing it, and justifying why it holds. The criterion that most often separates a five from a seven, because students spot the pattern and then stop, where the top band requires a general statement and a justification.

subjects.name: Mathematics criterion C: communicating
subjects.description: Using appropriate notation, structuring a solution and presenting reasoning so another reader can follow it. The most teachable criterion in the whole programme, and the one families are most surprised to find carries equal weight with content.

subjects.name: Mathematics criterion D: applying mathematics in real-life contexts
subjects.description: Setting up a model, interpreting a result in context, and commenting on the model's limitations. Students lose marks by producing a correct calculation and no interpretation, which is a habit rather than a shortfall in ability.

subjects.name: Sciences criterion B: inquiring and designing
subjects.description: Writing a testable question, identifying variables, and designing a method someone else could follow. Rewards precision in method writing, and it is the direct ancestor of the Diploma scientific investigation, which makes it worth investing in early.

subjects.name: Sciences criterion C: processing and evaluating
subjects.description: Presenting data, drawing a conclusion the data supports, and evaluating the method honestly. The usual failure is a conclusion that overstates what the data shows, and an evaluation that lists limitations without proposing specific improvements.

subjects.name: Language and literature criterion A: analysing
subjects.description: Reading a text closely and explaining how a choice the writer made creates an effect. Students describe what happens in the text when the criterion asks how it works, which is a reliable and correctable misreading of the task.

subjects.name: Language and literature criterion C: producing text
subjects.description: Writing with a clear purpose, structure and deliberate stylistic choices. Improves faster than almost anything else in MYP when a student is shown the descriptor for the band above the one they are in and asked to rewrite a single paragraph.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies criterion D: thinking critically
subjects.description: Evaluating sources, recognising perspective and bias, and building an argument that handles counter-evidence. The criterion Dubai students most often lose marks on, because school tasks reward research effort and the descriptor rewards judgement.

subjects.name: The MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, each from zero to eight, with a process journal alongside the product. A tutor coaches the process, questions the goal and reads reflections; the student does every part of the work themselves.

sections.heading: How an MYP grade is actually built, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: A one-to-seven MYP grade is not a percentage and it is not an average of test scores. Each subject has four criteria, each marked from zero to eight on individual tasks, and the teacher arrives at a final criterion level for the reporting period by judging the student's recent performance against the descriptors rather than by taking a mean. Those four levels, totalling up to 32, are then converted to a grade from one to seven using published boundaries.

The practical consequence is that a student can be good at a subject and receive a middling grade, because two of the four criteria are untouched by whatever they are good at. A mathematically confident MYP 4 student who writes nothing down will score highly on knowing and understanding and poorly on communicating, and those two carry equal weight. The grade reflects both honestly. Families frequently read that grade as a verdict on ability when it is a verdict on two specific behaviours.

This is why reading the criterion marks matters more than reading the grade. The table below sets out the four criteria for the subject groups LA Mer families ask about most, which makes the pattern easier to find in a folder of returned work. A criterion that is low in one subject is a subject issue. The same criterion low across three subjects is a skill issue, and a skill issue is what one weekly hour can genuinely change.

One caution on the numbers. The zero-to-eight scale is not linear in the way a mark out of eight feels: the descriptors describe qualitatively different performances, and moving from a four to a six usually means doing something the student is not currently doing at all rather than doing the same thing better. That is why the most effective MYP session involves reading the descriptor for the next band aloud and rewriting one piece of work to meet it.

sections.heading: Where LA Mer MYP students lose criterion marks most predictably
paragraphs: Across subjects and across schools in this cluster, the losses cluster in the same three places, and all three are habits rather than deficits.

The first is stopping at the answer. In mathematics criterion B, a student finds the pattern, writes the rule, and stops. The upper bands require a general statement and a justification of why the rule holds, which is one further sentence of a kind nobody has asked them to write. In sciences criterion C, a student presents the data and concludes that the hypothesis was supported, where the descriptor wants a conclusion that is proportionate to the data and an evaluation that proposes a specific improvement. The marks are not lost through error; they are lost through finishing early.

The second is describing where the task asks for analysis. Language and literature criterion A rewards explaining how a writer's choice produces an effect. Individuals and societies criterion D rewards judgement between competing accounts. In both, students produce careful, well-organised description and receive a middling mark, which feels arbitrary until the descriptor is read next to the work. This is the single most common complaint parents in this cluster bring to a first session, and it has a concrete answer.

The third is presentation treated as optional. Criterion C in mathematics and criterion D in language and literature both reward communication directly. Students who regard setting out their reasoning as a formality rather than as assessed work are conceding a quarter of the available marks before the task begins. Fixing it is a matter of rewriting two or three pieces of work with the descriptor visible, and it moves faster than any other intervention available in the programme.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: what a tutor may coach and what it must not touch
paragraphs: In MYP 5 the Personal Project becomes the single largest piece of independent work a student has produced, and it is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, each from zero to eight, with a process journal kept alongside the product. It is also where the boundary around tutoring has to be stated most plainly, because it is the piece of work most often outsourced.

What goes wrong is rarely the product. It is the goal and the journal. Students choose a goal that cannot be shown to have been achieved, or one so large that the applying-skills criterion has nothing specific to point at. Then the process journal is written retrospectively in a weekend, which is visible to any experienced reader and which makes the reflecting criterion impossible to score well. Both failures happen early and both are preventable by asking better questions at the start.

That is the legitimate role for a tutor, and it is genuinely useful. Questioning whether a goal is specific enough to be evidenced. Explaining what each of the three criteria rewards and what the descriptors actually say. Asking the student what they did this week and why, so the journal is a record rather than a reconstruction. Reading a reflection the student has written and asking what is missing from it.

What a tutor does not do is write, draft, redraft or supply any part of the project, the report or the journal, and nobody here will. The work must be the student's own, and submitting work that is not is a malpractice risk that falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it. At least one operator appearing in these searches sells completed assessed work outright, which should be read as a warning rather than as an option.

sections.heading: The MYP 5 to Diploma step, and why it is not a content problem
paragraphs: The most valuable tutoring a continuum family in LA Mer can buy is often not MYP tutoring at all. It is work in the final MYP year aimed at the Diploma, because the step between the two is larger than the step between any two MYP years and it catches confident students.

The reason is structural. A student who has spent five years being assessed against criteria on teacher-designed tasks, with drafting, feedback and often a second attempt, arrives in the Diploma to meet terminal examinations, externally set questions, fixed mark allocations and a clock. Nothing about their content knowledge is the problem. What is new is finishing, writing to the marks available, recognising command terms, and accepting that a first attempt is the only attempt.

The specific gaps show up in the first Diploma term with some consistency. Students write beautifully structured answers that are twice as long as the mark allocation justifies and run out of time. They treat a four-mark explain question as an invitation to discuss rather than as a demand for four distinct points. In the sciences they are strong on inquiry design, which MYP rewarded heavily, and under-practised at quantitative questions under time pressure. In mathematics they are comfortable investigating and uncomfortable with speed and accuracy on routine procedure.

None of that needs a great deal of time to address, but it needs to be addressed deliberately. Six to eight sessions in MYP 5 spent on timed tasks, mark allocations and command terms is a cheaper and more effective purchase than a term of catch-up in Year 12, and it leaves the student entering the Diploma with the habit already formed.

sections.heading: Fitting an MYP session into the Jumeirah afternoon
paragraphs: MYP students are between eleven and sixteen, and the younger end of that range has a usable evening considerably shorter than a Diploma student's. That changes the timetable arithmetic in this cluster in a way most tutoring pages ignore.

The sequence is familiar. School in the Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim cluster ends between about 2:45pm and 3:30pm. The drive home across Al Wasl Road or along Jumeirah Beach Road takes thirty to forty-five minutes. Activity programmes occupy roughly 4pm to 6pm for most students. For a Diploma student that leaves a workable 6:45pm or 7:30pm slot. For an MYP 2 student it frequently does not: concentration on a criterion-focused task after 7:30pm produces compliance rather than learning, and the session becomes expensive supervision.

The practical answer is to find an early slot on the one or two days a week when the activity calendar allows it, and to accept one hour rather than two. Where no early slot exists, 6:30pm is the latest that reliably works for the younger years, and the session should be shorter rather than later. A forty-five minute session that the student is awake for is worth more than an hour they are not.

The table maps the afternoon as it actually runs. The useful conclusion is that an MYP family in LA Mer should be choosing a slot before choosing a tutor, because the slot is the scarcer resource. One criterion-focused hour at a time the student can think is the whole intervention most of these families need.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects alongside eight MYP subject groups
paragraphs: An MYP timetable in Dubai is fuller than the eight subject groups suggest, and this is worth understanding before adding tutored hours to it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required these arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The requirements are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, and the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is not permitted, which limits how any tutoring in those subjects can honestly be described.

For a LA Mer family the arithmetic is the point. Eight MYP subject groups, the mandatory subjects, an activity programme, and in MYP 5 the Personal Project, all inside a week that ends at 3:30pm. That is the reason this page recommends one targeted hour rather than a package of several, and the reason the hour should be aimed at a criterion rather than at a subject.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs in Dubai, and why travel is the wrong thing to pay for
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the common search and the honest answer starts with the market. In-home one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the usual range at AED 180 to AED 350. Qualified online subject tutors are published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB rates from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. Budget online options sit lower, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. Those are market figures from the named providers, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

For MYP specifically the premium is harder to justify than at Diploma level, because the thing a family most needs is not a rare specialism. It is somebody who can read a criterion descriptor next to a marked task and show a thirteen-year-old what the band above requires. That is skilled work and it is not scarce work, and paying a travel premium for it is paying for a drive down Al Wasl Road.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. LA Mer families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For criterion work the format has a direct benefit: the descriptor and the student's own task sit side by side on screen, the rewritten paragraph is produced in the session and kept, and the comparison between a four and a six becomes something the student can see rather than something they are told.

The budget point worth making is the opposite of an upsell. Most MYP families in this cluster need one diagnostic session and then one weekly hour on a single criterion for a term, after which the habit holds and the tutoring can stop. A provider recommending three subjects at once to an MYP 2 student is selling hours rather than solving anything.

process.title: Send the marked tasks, not the report grade
process.description: The useful material is two or three returned tasks per subject with criterion marks written on them. The grade tells you a level; the criterion marks tell you which of four things is holding it down. Most families already have this in a folder and have never read it as a pattern.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge, taught rather than pitched, with the student. The tutor reads a marked task against the published descriptor and starts working. One trial lesson per student, before any booking; if the match is wrong, say so and nothing is owed.

process.title: Pick one criterion, not three subjects
process.description: If communicating is low in mathematics, in the sciences and in individuals and societies, that is one skill problem rather than three subject problems. The hour targets the criterion and the improvement shows up across all three, which is how one session does the work of several.

process.title: Choose the slot before the tutor
process.description: For MYP the scarcer resource is an hour when the student can still think. We ask for school finish time and activity days first, and recommend an earlier, shorter session over a longer, later one. After 8:30pm nothing useful happens for this age group.

process.title: Stop when the habit holds
process.description: Most MYP interventions are a term, not a year. Once the student is routinely writing the justification sentence or setting out reasoning without being asked, the tutoring has done its job. We will say so rather than extend the booking, and in MYP 5 the hours redirect to the Diploma step instead.

whyPoints.title: Criteria taught, not just subjects
whyPoints.description: An MYP grade is four criteria each marked zero to eight, and two of them usually have nothing to do with content. Sessions work from the published descriptors next to the student's own marked task, because that is what the mark was actually given against.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from work you already have
whyPoints.description: Returned tasks with criterion marks are a dataset most families never read as one. A single session spent reading them across subjects frequently shows one skill problem rather than three subject problems, and sometimes removes the need for ongoing tutoring entirely.

whyPoints.title: Timing matched to the student's age
whyPoints.description: A twelve-year-old's usable evening in this cluster ends earlier than a Diploma student's. We recommend an earlier and shorter session rather than a longer later one, and we will say when a requested slot is too late to be worth paying for.

whyPoints.title: Descriptors and work side by side on screen
whyPoints.description: The fastest change in MYP comes from reading the band above aloud and rewriting one paragraph to meet it. Online delivery puts the descriptor and the student's own task in view together, and the rewritten version is kept rather than lost on paper.

whyPoints.title: Firm limits on the Personal Project
whyPoints.description: A tutor questions the goal, explains what each criterion rewards, and asks what went into the process journal this week. No part of the project, the report or the journal is written, drafted or supplied here, because the work has to be the student's own.

whyPoints.title: An end point, stated in advance
whyPoints.description: Most MYP tutoring should last a term. No grade or improvement is guaranteed, because none honestly can be, and the recommendation at the end of a term is sometimes to stop. A provider proposing three subjects at once for an MYP 2 student is selling hours.

faqs.question: What does an MYP tutor actually do when there are no exams to prepare for?
faqs.answer: Works on the four criteria the student is marked against. Every MYP subject is assessed on four criteria, each from zero to eight, on tasks the class teacher designs. A tutor reads the student's returned work next to the published descriptors, identifies which criterion is holding the grade down, and teaches that specifically. Often it is communicating or thinking critically rather than knowing and understanding, which means more practice questions would change nothing. The work is reading the descriptor for the band above and rewriting to meet it.

faqs.question: How is a one-to-seven MYP grade calculated from criterion marks?
faqs.answer: Each of the four criteria is given a level from zero to eight for the reporting period, based on the teacher's judgement of recent performance against the descriptors rather than an average of scores. The four levels total up to 32, and that total converts to a grade from one to seven using published boundaries. The practical consequence is that a student strong in two criteria and weak in the other two receives a middling grade, which parents often read as a verdict on ability rather than on two specific behaviours.

faqs.question: My child scores well on criterion A but badly on criterion C. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: It means the thinking is sound and the communication of it is not, and that is the most fixable pattern in the programme. In mathematics criterion C rewards notation, structure and reasoning another reader can follow. In language and literature the equivalent is producing text. Students who regard setting out their working as presentation rather than as assessed work concede roughly a quarter of the available marks before starting. Rewriting two or three pieces with the descriptor visible usually shifts it within a term.

faqs.question: Why do careful, well-researched MYP essays still get middling marks?
faqs.answer: Usually because the task asked for analysis and received description. Language and literature criterion A rewards explaining how a writer's choice creates an effect, not recounting what happens. Individuals and societies criterion D rewards judgement between competing accounts, not the volume of research gathered. A student can work hard, organise well, and land in the middle bands because they have answered a slightly different question. Reading the descriptor next to their own paragraph is usually the moment it becomes obvious.

faqs.question: What stops a mathematics criterion B mark from reaching the top band?
faqs.answer: Stopping at the rule. Criterion B rewards investigating patterns, and students reliably find the pattern, state it, and finish. The upper bands want a general statement of the rule and a justification of why it holds, which is one more sentence of a kind nobody has explicitly asked them to write. It is not a mathematical shortfall; it is an unwritten expectation. Once a student has written that sentence three or four times with feedback, they write it automatically, and the criterion mark moves.

faqs.question: What time should an MYP session start for a LA Mer student?
faqs.answer: Earlier than you would schedule a Diploma session. School in this cluster ends between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, the drive home takes thirty to forty-five minutes, and activity programmes run to about 6pm. A 4:45pm start on a day without activities is the best option. Where that does not exist, 6:30pm works for the younger years and should be kept short. After 8:30pm an eleven or twelve-year-old produces compliance rather than learning, and the hour becomes expensive supervision.

faqs.question: Is a forty-five minute MYP session better than a full hour?
faqs.answer: For MYP 1 to 3, often yes, if the shorter session is at a time the student is genuinely alert. Criterion work requires reading a descriptor, comparing it with their own writing and producing something new, which is demanding in a different way from drilling practice questions. Forty-five focused minutes at 4:45pm will produce a rewritten paragraph; an hour at 8pm will produce agreement that the paragraph could be better. For MYP 4 and 5 a full hour is normally the right unit.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the MYP Personal Project in MYP 5?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes; with the work, no. A tutor questions whether the goal is specific enough to be evidenced, explains what the planning, applying skills and reflecting criteria each reward, and asks what went into the process journal that week so it is a record rather than a reconstruction. A tutor does not write, draft, redraft or supply any part of the project, report or journal. Submitting work that is not the student's own is a malpractice risk that falls on the student alone.

faqs.question: Why do Personal Projects lose marks even when the product is good?
faqs.answer: Because the marks are not for the product. They are for planning, applying skills and reflecting, each from zero to eight. Two failures dominate: a goal so broad that nothing specific can be shown to have been achieved, and a process journal written retrospectively in a weekend, which any experienced reader can spot and which makes the reflecting criterion impossible to score well. Both happen in the first few weeks, which is why early questioning of the goal is worth more than late help with the writing.

faqs.question: Is the MYP 5 to Diploma step really that difficult for a strong student?
faqs.answer: It catches strong students in particular. Five years of criterion marking on teacher-designed tasks, with drafting and feedback, gives way to terminal examinations, externally set questions, fixed mark allocations and a clock. Content knowledge is rarely the problem. What is new is finishing, writing to the marks available rather than to the quality the student wants, recognising command terms, and accepting a single attempt. Six to eight sessions in MYP 5 on timed tasks costs less than a term of catch-up in Year 12.

faqs.question: Does MYP prepare a Dubai student adequately for IGCSE if they transfer?
faqs.answer: It prepares them well for some things and leaves a specific gap. A student moving from MYP 5 into an IGCSE cohort arrives confident designing investigations and constructing arguments, and short on timed recall of defined content and on the conventions of an external mark scheme. That gap is real and bounded: roughly a term of work on definitions, formulae and paper technique rather than on thinking. It is far cheaper to close in the summer before the transfer than in the middle of Year 11.

faqs.question: How do Dubai's mandatory subjects affect an MYP week?
faqs.answer: They add real timetable load on top of eight subject groups. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and KHDA advises at least 25 minutes per mandatory lesson. Schools must also organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in the relevant subjects. One targeted tutored hour fits that week; a package of three does not.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to homes in LA Mer?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. LA Mer families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For criterion work this format has a specific benefit: the published descriptor and the student's own marked task sit side by side on screen, the rewritten paragraph is produced during the session and kept, and the difference between a four and a six becomes visible rather than described.

faqs.question: How long should MYP tutoring last before we stop?
faqs.answer: A term, for most families. Once a student routinely writes the justification sentence, sets out reasoning without being asked, or proposes a specific improvement in an evaluation, the habit has formed and the paid hours stop adding much. Continuing past that point buys reassurance rather than progress. In MYP 5 the sensible move is to redirect the hours towards the Diploma step instead, which is a different and time-limited piece of work. No tutor can honestly guarantee a grade or a criterion level.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-la-mer.closingHeading: Read the criterion marks before buying anything
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-la-mer.closingBody: The most useful hour an MYP family in LA Mer can spend costs nothing: pulling two or three marked tasks per subject out of the folder and reading the criterion marks across them rather than the grades. Nine times in ten a pattern appears, and it is one skill rather than three subjects. Bring that pattern to the free trial lesson, which is a taught session rather than a sales call, and ask the tutor to work from the published descriptor for the band above. Teaching runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, at an hour the student can still think.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-living-legends.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work with Middle Years Programme students in Living Legends and the neighbouring communities. Each profile names the subject group and the MYP year, because a criterion brief in MYP 2 and a pre-Diploma brief in MYP 5 are different pieces of work.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near you who can actually read an MYP rubric?
paragraphs: This is the question behind the search, and it has a sharper answer than most parents expect. The Middle Years Programme does not mark content against a syllabus. Every subject carries four criteria, labelled A to D, each judged on a 0-8 scale against a published descriptor that describes a quality of work rather than a quantity of correct material. A student can produce something factually accurate and sit in a middle band because the descriptor asked for something the work does not contain.

That makes the useful qualification in a tutor unusual. It is not a degree in the subject, although that helps. It is fluency in the criterion language: knowing that investigating patterns in mathematics asks for a general rule and a justification, that processing and evaluating in sciences asks for limitations with their effect on the result, that thinking critically in individuals and societies asks for sources weighed against one another rather than summarised in turn, and that analysing in language and literature asks how a text produces an effect rather than what happens in it.

Most subject tutors have never read a descriptor. They teach the content capably, the student's knowledge improves, and the criterion judgement does not move, because nobody addressed what was actually being assessed. Parents then conclude that tutoring does not work for the MYP, when in fact the wrong thing was bought. This is the single most common failure in Middle Years Programme tutoring and it is entirely avoidable.

Living Legends narrows the local supply further. It is a single gated community of villas and apartment towers off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, between Dubai Sports City, Motor City and Remraam, with no secondary school inside the gates. The number of households here with an MYP student in a particular subject group in a particular year is small, so no independent specialist builds a diary from it, and the tutors who are nearby are generalists responding sensibly to a dispersed market.

IB Gram matches on subject group, MYP year and the criterion that is actually underperforming, teaches one-to-one over live video, and does not send anybody to a Living Legends address because home visits are a service we run only in India. The first session is a free full-length trial with no card, used to read the student's marked work against its rubric rather than to make a pitch. What follows is the verification detail: what each criterion asks for, the phases nobody checks, the Personal Project boundary, and what this costs. A parent who works through it can run the check themselves in a single conversation, which is worth more than any directory of names sorted by how far away somebody happens to live.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-living-legends.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme spans five years and changes substantially across them. These notes describe what is being assessed at each stage rather than what is being taught.

programmes.name: MYP 1 and 2
programmes.description: The transition out of the Primary Years Programme or into the IB from another curriculum. The content is manageable; the new demand is being judged on process. Criterion B in mathematics and sciences asks students to investigate and design rather than to answer, and most arrive with no experience of being assessed on that at all.
programmes.countryNote: Students from this community attend nearby schools in Motor City, Sports City and Remraam for these years, so journeys are short and afternoon sessions are realistic. The work at this stage is largely about understanding what a criterion is, which is quick and pays off for four more years.

programmes.name: MYP 3
programmes.description: The year the gap between students who explain and students who describe becomes visible in grades. Interdisciplinary work appears, and written communication starts to drive marks across every subject group rather than only in language and literature. Approaches to learning skills become an explicit part of how work is judged.
programmes.countryNote: This is also when families in this community decide between continuing to MYP 4 and 5 or moving to a British school for International GCSE. Either way the reasoning and writing built here transfers, which makes MYP 3 work good value regardless of the route chosen afterwards.

programmes.name: MYP 4 and 5
programmes.description: Subject content deepens and the Personal Project arrives. Some schools enter students for MYP eAssessment with on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, and some assess internally throughout; ask which applies, because it reshapes the final year. Criterion descriptors become noticeably more exacting in their top-band language.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 and 5 students here travel out of the community for school and are the latest home, so a 6pm session that holds every week is worth more than an earlier one that is rescheduled. Online delivery is the only version that can be pinned that precisely.

programmes.name: The Diploma Programme that follows
programmes.description: Six subjects across two levels plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. The step from the MYP is about volume and independence rather than content, and students who never built a research and drafting habit in the Personal Project feel it immediately in the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: Candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. The deadlines a Diploma student works to are set by their own coordinator months ahead, so a student who learned to manage a long project in MYP 5 has a real and measurable advantage over one who did not.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-living-legends.subjectsIntro: Each of the eight MYP subject groups applies its four criteria differently. These notes name the criterion that most often underperforms and what the descriptor actually asks for, which is what a tutor should be able to say unprompted.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns asks for a general rule and a justification; students find the pattern and stop. Communicating marks are lost to working that is correct and unreadable.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Processing and evaluating asks for data interpreted and limitations stated with their effect on the result; students present correct data and declare the experiment successful.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically asks for sources weighed against one another; students summarise each in turn accurately and cannot reach the top band because no weighing has occurred.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Analysing asks how a text produces an effect; confident readers explain what happens instead and sit in the middle band. This is the most common single misreading in the whole programme.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written text, communicating, and using language. Students are assessed within a phase rather than a year group, so a parent must know their child's phase before any plan is made or any expectation set.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The documentation carries the marks rather than the artefact, and students who build something impressive without recording decisions against the criteria score poorly and feel unfairly treated.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal is where the marks live and it is the part students treat as an afterthought, because the finished piece feels like the point of the subject.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Written reflection is assessed as seriously as physical performance, which surprises athletic students and their parents in equal measure.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An extended independent project with a process journal and a report, assessed against its own criteria. Planning, applying skills and reflecting are marked, not the ambition of the product, and the report is where otherwise strong projects lose bands.

sections.heading: How to verify that a tutor can read an MYP rubric
paragraphs: A parent cannot assess criterion fluency directly, but they can assess specificity, and three questions produce it reliably. First: in my child's subject group, which criterion do students most often underperform, and what does the descriptor actually ask for? Second: if I send you a returned task and its rubric, what will you do in the first session? Third: what is the difference between the band my child achieved and the band above it, in the descriptor's own words?

Somebody who works with the programme answers all three without hesitation. They will name a criterion, quote or paraphrase the descriptor accurately, and describe a first session that involves reading the marked task, identifying the gap and having the student rewrite one section to the higher band. That answer requires no preparation from a person who does this weekly.

A subject tutor who has never read a descriptor answers differently, and the pattern is recognisable. The first answer becomes a comment about the subject being conceptually demanding. The second becomes a plan to go over the topic again. The third becomes advice about revising more thoroughly and checking work. None of it is dishonest, and none of it will move a criterion judgement, because the criterion was never the target.

This matters more in the MYP than in any other programme, because the gap between content knowledge and assessed performance is widest here. A student can genuinely know more at the end of a term of subject tutoring and have exactly the same grades, which is the outcome that makes parents distrust tutoring generally. The table below extends the three questions into a verification list.

sections.heading: The four criteria across the subject groups
paragraphs: Each MYP subject group has its own four criteria, and the pattern of what students miss is consistent enough to be useful. Across almost every group the underperforming criterion is the one asking for evaluation, justification or critical weighing rather than for knowledge, because those are the skills nobody teaches explicitly and every descriptor rewards.

A worked example makes the mechanism clear. In sciences, processing and evaluating asks a student to present data, interpret it, and evaluate the validity of the method and its limitations. A student who records results neatly, draws a correct graph and writes that the experiment worked well has delivered the data and missed two of the three things the descriptor names. Adding a paragraph identifying a specific limitation and the specific effect it had on the result can lift the judgement a band without changing a single number.

The same shape recurs. In mathematics, investigating patterns asks for a general rule with a justification; students find the rule and stop. In design, evaluating asks for the solution tested against stated success criteria; students describe how they made the artefact. In arts, the process journal evidences development and reflection; students submit a strong final piece with a thin journal. In physical and health education, written reflection on performance carries marks alongside the performance itself.

What follows for a tutoring plan is counter-intuitive and important. Do not buy support in the subject with the lowest grade. Buy support for the criterion that recurs as weakest across several subjects, because criteria are transferable in a way subject content is not. A student weak in evaluation is usually weak in it in sciences, design and individuals and societies simultaneously, and one block of work improves three subjects at once.

sections.heading: Language Acquisition phases: the question nobody asks
paragraphs: This is the most frequently missed fact in MYP tutoring and it is worth a section of its own. Language Acquisition in the Middle Years Programme is assessed by phase, not by year group. A student in MYP 4 could be in phase 2 or phase 5 depending on their prior experience of the language, and the expectations, the texts and the band descriptors differ accordingly.

The consequence is that a tutor who plans by year group will either pitch the work far too high or far too low, and both waste the hour. A phase 2 student given phase 5 material concludes they are hopeless at the language. A phase 5 student given phase 2 material is bored and makes no progress, while the parent sees a cheerful report and no grade movement. Neither outcome is the student's fault and both are preventable by asking one question.

So ask the school for the phase, in writing, for each language the child studies. Then ask the tutor what that phase expects. A tutor who works with the programme will immediately describe the kind of text, the kind of task and the productive expectations appropriate to that phase. A tutor who has never encountered the phase system will talk about year-group level, which is the clearest single signal available that they are outside the programme.

There is a UAE layer worth knowing alongside this. Arabic is compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and KHDA requires that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold appropriate approval to teach those subjects. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so support works from the school's own material by design.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units and approaches to learning
paragraphs: Two features of the Middle Years Programme are invisible to most subject tutors and increasingly consequential as a student moves through it. The first is interdisciplinary work, where students are assessed on their ability to combine understanding from two subject groups into something neither would produce alone. The second is approaches to learning, the explicit skills framework running underneath every subject.

Interdisciplinary units trip up students who are strong in both contributing subjects, because the assessed skill is the synthesis rather than the content. An essay that explains the science accurately and then explains the history accurately, without ever making them speak to each other, has avoided the task. A tutor who understands this spends the session on the join rather than on either side of it, which is a different lesson entirely from subject revision.

Approaches to learning covers thinking, communication, social, self-management and research skills. These are not graded separately in most schools, but they are what the criterion descriptors keep asking for in disguise. A student who cannot organise a long answer is failing a communication skill. A student who cannot plan a project across six weeks is failing self-management, which is exactly what the Personal Project will expose in MYP 5. Addressing those directly is often more productive than more subject content.

For a family in this community there is a practical upside. These skills transfer, which means a single block of work on long-answer organisation or on planning and self-management improves performance across every subject group at once. In a household where the usable study time is limited by a long commute, a transferable intervention is worth considerably more than a subject-specific one, and it is rarely what a local generalist will propose.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: supervisor, tutor and the line between
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is where the roles need to be clear, because the student already has a supervisor at school and adding a tutor without understanding the boundary creates risk rather than support.

The school supervisor oversees the project, holds the formal meetings, signs off the process and confirms academic integrity. That role belongs to the school and nothing a tutor does replaces or duplicates it. What a tutor can legitimately add is teaching: testing whether the goal is achievable and whether the success criteria are specific enough to be evaluated against later, explaining what each criterion rewards in its own language, teaching the process journal as assessed evidence rather than a diary, and giving criterion feedback on a report the student has written.

The band is determined by planning, applied skills, journal evidence and reflection rather than by the ambition of the product, and this is the misunderstanding that produces most disappointment. A student builds something genuinely impressive, keeps no usable record of decisions made along the way, writes a report describing what they made, and receives a middling band that cannot be fixed afterwards because the evidence was never captured. A modest project with meticulous documentation and honest reflection scores well.

The hard boundary is absolute. A tutor must never produce the project, write the report, supply sections of it, or edit it until the voice is no longer the student's. One page ranking in this market sells completed assessed work outright; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student. Where a school requires an authentication declaration, the student signs it, and a tutor who crossed the line has put that signature at risk. Nor do we reproduce IB programme or assessment documents, which are the organisation's copyright.

sections.heading: Transition into and out of the programme
paragraphs: In this part of Dubai the school supply mixes British and IB provision within a few kilometres, so transition in both directions is common and both directions break predictably. Families in Living Legends encounter this more than most, because housing turnover and school place availability push mid-phase moves.

Arriving into the MYP from a British or Indian curriculum, the student usually has the content and no experience of being assessed on process. They answer the question well and score in the middle band, repeatedly, and cannot understand why. The fix is criterion literacy rather than content work, and it is quick: three to five sessions working from the first returned tasks is often enough for the pattern to click, after which the student self-corrects.

Leaving the MYP for International GCSE, the problem inverts. These students are usually strong at explaining, evaluating and reflecting, and comparatively weak at procedural fluency and recall-based questions, which Cambridge 0580 and the science specifications reward heavily. They also meet tiering for the first time, and Cambridge Core and Extended entries cap grades differently, so a student placed on evidence from a system that measured something else can end up on the wrong tier.

Leaving the MYP for the Diploma, the difficulty is volume and independence rather than content. MYP tasks arrive with a rubric that tells the student what is wanted; Diploma papers arrive with markschemes that reward method and precise command-term reading, and nobody supplies the rubric. The Extended Essay then lands on students who may never have managed a long project, which is why the Personal Project experience matters well beyond its own grade.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs from this community
paragraphs: Middle Years Programme support sits lower in the market than Diploma support, for a defensible reason: the content depth is less and much of the work is assessment literacy rather than advanced subject knowledge. That makes the qualified band the sensible target and the budget band genuinely usable for the earliest phases.

Every figure below names the provider or source that published it, which matters in a market where three of the six most visible pages publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel.

The practical mapping is this. MYP 1 to 3 fluency and reading work sits comfortably in the budget band, where frequency and patience matter more than descriptor fluency. Criterion coaching in MYP 4 and 5, Personal Project support and any transition diagnostic belong in the qualified band at minimum, because they require somebody who reads descriptors properly. Monthly, Bestimate's estimates give AED 240 to 600 for budget provision and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range for a weekly session.

One cost deserves specific attention for MYP families, because they are the households most likely to have two children at different phases. A visiting tutor in a gated community loses minutes at the gate on every session, and two children at different hours means either two visits with two travel premiums or one compromised slot. Online delivery makes consecutive slots with two specialists cost nothing extra. None of the figures above is an IB Gram price list, and the MoHRE private tutor permit is free of charge, so no licensing cost belongs in any quote.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and honest availability
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the facts are short. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow from that permit, and the second matters more in the Middle Years than it does in the Diploma. First, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any amount quoted anywhere is unverified. Second, a conduct rule sits alongside it: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct does likewise. That reporting is press-sourced, so verify it against the current ADEK document. The Middle Years reason to care is criterion marking itself - the teacher who wrote the task-specific clarifications and awarded the five on Criterion C is precisely the person a Living Legends parent most wants to hire privately, and that is the arrangement the rule exists to prevent.

School regulation sits with the emirate. Dubai is KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education and inspects on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them, nor from the IB, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE.

On availability, criterion coaching in mathematics, sciences, individuals and societies and language and literature matches quickly. Language Acquisition in a less commonly taught language at a specific phase is the narrowest request in the programme, along with short-notice Personal Project support close to a school deadline. Where no suitable specialist is free we give a date rather than offering a near-fit. No competitor in the clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and specialists may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced IB teachers outside the Emirates.

process.title: Ask the school for the criterion breakdown
process.description: Not the subject grade but the four criterion judgements behind it, for each subject, plus the Language Acquisition phase where relevant. That breakdown tells you which criterion recurs as weakest, which is where the effort belongs.

process.title: Send a marked task with its rubric
process.description: The returned work and the descriptor it was judged against is the most useful document a parent can supply. It turns the first session into a diagnosis of a specific criterion rather than a general conversation about effort and confidence.

process.title: Ask the three verification questions
process.description: Which criterion underperforms in this subject group and what does the descriptor ask? What happens in session one with a returned task? What separates this band from the next, in the descriptor's words? A programme-literate tutor answers all three immediately.

process.title: Target the criterion, not the subject
process.description: A student weak in evaluation is usually weak in it across sciences, design and individuals and societies at once. One block on that criterion improves three subjects, which no subject-by-subject plan achieves for the same money.

process.title: Use the free trial to test a rewrite
process.description: A full session, no charge, no card. Ask the tutor to show what the band above requires in the descriptor's own words and have the student rewrite one section to it. If that cannot happen within the hour, the match is wrong.

whyPoints.title: Criterion fluency is the credential we match on
whyPoints.description: MYP grades come from criterion judgements against published descriptors, so the useful qualification is fluency in that language rather than subject knowledge alone. Most subject tutors have never read a descriptor, which is why content improves and grades do not.

whyPoints.title: The weakest criterion treated as one problem
whyPoints.description: Weakness in evaluating or communicating appears in three subject groups at once. Treating it as a single transferable skill rather than three subject problems is faster and cheaper, and in a household with limited study hours it is worth considerably more.

whyPoints.title: The Language Acquisition phase established first
whyPoints.description: Language Acquisition is assessed by phase, not year group, so a tutor planning by year will pitch the work far too high or too low. We ask for the phase before planning, and a tutor who does not know the phase system is outside the programme.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project kept the student's own
whyPoints.description: The school supervisor oversees the project and nothing we do replaces that. A tutor tests the goal and success criteria, teaches the journal as assessed evidence and gives criterion feedback on the student's own report. Nothing is drafted, supplied or rewritten.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band names who published it. MYP support sits in the budget band for the earliest phases and the qualified band for criterion coaching, and saying so is more useful to a family than selling upward at every stage.

whyPoints.title: No approval claimed and no material reproduced
whyPoints.description: No KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry or IB approval, no UAE office, no grade promise. IB programme documents, assessment material and grade boundary information are the organisation's copyright; ask the school for its own boundaries and breakdowns.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor understands MYP criteria?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions. In my child's subject group, which criterion do students most often underperform and what does the descriptor actually ask for? If I send a returned task and its rubric, what will you do in the first session? What separates the band my child achieved from the one above, in the descriptor's own words? A programme-literate tutor names the criterion, paraphrases the descriptor accurately and describes reading the marked task then having the student rewrite one section. A subject tutor talks about revising more thoroughly.

faqs.question: Why did a term of subject tutoring not move my child's MYP grades?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because the criterion was never the target. MYP subjects are judged on four criteria against published descriptors describing a quality of work rather than a quantity of correct content, so a student can genuinely know more at the end of a term and receive identical judgements. The remedy is to work from the student's returned task and the rubric it was marked against, identify the gap to the next band in the descriptor's language, and have the student rewrite a section to that standard.

faqs.question: What is a Language Acquisition phase and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: Language Acquisition in the MYP is assessed by phase rather than by year group, with six phases, so a student in MYP 4 might be in phase 2 or phase 5 depending on prior experience of the language. The expectations, texts and band descriptors differ accordingly. A tutor planning by year group pitches the work far too high or too low and wastes the hour either way. Ask the school for the phase in writing for each language, then ask the tutor what that phase expects.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion should we work on first?
faqs.answer: Whichever one recurs as weakest across several subjects, because criteria transfer in a way subject content does not. A student weak in evaluation is usually weak in evaluating in sciences, in design and in thinking critically in individuals and societies simultaneously, so one block of work lifts three subjects. Communicating is the other frequent cross-subject weakness, visible as correct mathematics nobody can follow and strong ideas in disorganised paragraphs. Buying support in the lowest-graded subject is the intuitive move and the less efficient one.

faqs.question: Why does my child's accurate science work get a middling mark?
faqs.answer: Because processing and evaluating asks for more than accurate data. The descriptor wants data interpreted and the method's validity and limitations evaluated, with the effect of each limitation on the result. A student who records results neatly, draws a correct graph and writes that the experiment worked well has delivered one of three things asked for. Adding a paragraph that names a specific limitation and its specific effect can lift the judgement a band without changing a single measurement.

faqs.question: Is there an MYP specialist based near Living Legends?
faqs.answer: Unlikely, and the arithmetic explains it. A single gated community holds a limited number of households, only some have MYP students, and only some need a particular subject group in a particular year. That cannot sustain a criterion-fluent specialist locally, so the tutors who are nearby are generalists responding sensibly to a dispersed market. Matching on subject group, MYP year and the underperforming criterion, without a distance filter, is what actually produces a useful tutor for a family here.

faqs.question: What are interdisciplinary units and why do they catch students out?
faqs.answer: They assess a student's ability to combine understanding from two subject groups into something neither would produce alone, so the skill being judged is the synthesis rather than the content. A student strong in both contributing subjects can still avoid the task entirely by explaining the science accurately, then the history accurately, without ever making them speak to each other. A tutor who understands this spends the session on the join rather than on either side, which is a different lesson from subject revision.

faqs.question: Does the Personal Project band depend on how impressive the project is?
faqs.answer: No, and that misunderstanding produces most of the disappointment around it. The band reflects planning, applied skills, the evidence in the process journal and the quality of reflection in the report. A student can build something genuinely impressive, keep no usable record of decisions, write a report describing what they made, and receive a middling band that cannot be fixed afterwards. A modest project with meticulous documentation and honest reflection scores well, which is worth knowing before the work starts.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do on the Personal Project, and what must they not?
faqs.answer: They may test whether the goal is achievable and whether the success criteria are specific enough to be evaluated against later, explain what each criterion rewards in its own language, teach the process journal as assessed evidence rather than a diary, and give criterion feedback on a report the student has written. They must never produce the project, write or supply sections of the report, or edit it until the voice is no longer the student's. The school supervisor oversees the project and nothing a tutor does replaces that role.

faqs.question: My child joined the MYP from a British school and keeps scoring mid-band. Why?
faqs.answer: Because they have the content and no experience of being assessed on process. They answer the question well, which is what their previous school rewarded, and the descriptor is asking for investigation, evaluation or critical weighing that the answer does not contain. This is the most common transition pattern in this area and it is quick to fix: three to five sessions working from the first returned tasks is often enough for the pattern to click, after which the student self-corrects without further help.

faqs.question: How do approaches to learning skills affect MYP grades?
faqs.answer: They are what the descriptors keep asking for in disguise. Thinking, communication, social, self-management and research skills are not usually graded separately, but a student who cannot organise a long answer is failing a communication skill and a student who cannot plan across six weeks is failing self-management, which the Personal Project will expose in MYP 5. Working on those directly is often more productive than more subject content, and because they transfer, one block improves performance across every subject group.

faqs.question: What should MYP tutoring cost for a family in this community?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours. For MYP 1 to 3 fluency and reading work, budget online provision at AED 45 to 150 an hour is honest value, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Criterion coaching in MYP 4 and 5, Personal Project support and transition diagnostics belong in the qualified band of AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240 to 600 budget and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range for a weekly session.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two children in different MYP phases?
faqs.answer: They can, and two specialists usually serve a household better. An MYP 2 student needs to understand what a criterion is; an MYP 5 student needs subject depth and Personal Project discipline. They also arrive home at different times, since the earlier phases attend nearby schools and the later ones travel out of the community. Two consecutive online slots with two specialists costs nothing extra because nothing travels, where a visiting arrangement means two journeys or one compromised session.

faqs.question: Will you give us the MYP grade boundaries and criterion descriptors?
faqs.answer: No, for two reasons. Programme documents, assessment material and grade boundary information are the IB's copyright, so distributing them is not ours to do. And boundaries can be revised, which means a table restated on a tutoring page risks being wrong without anybody touching it. Ask the school for the boundaries it applies and for the criterion breakdown behind each subject grade. Both are legitimately available to a parent, and the school's own figures are the ones that apply to your child.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-living-legends.closingHeading: Hire criterion fluency, not just subject knowledge
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-living-legends.closingBody: An IB MYP tutor in Living Legends is worth hiring when they can name the criterion your child underperforms, paraphrase its descriptor accurately, and show what the band above requires in the descriptor's own words. That is a different credential from subject knowledge, and it is the one that moves MYP grades. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown and the Language Acquisition phase, send a marked task with its rubric, and book a free full-length trial lesson that ends with the student rewriting one section to a higher band.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-meydan.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work to MYP criteria rather than to a textbook chapter list, which is the difference between moving a criterion C mark and simply covering more content. Each teaches one-to-one online in a slot that survives a Meydan weekday, and you meet them before paying anything.

intro.heading: Why the cheap years are the ones nobody buys
paragraphs: Spending on tutoring in Dubai follows exam pressure rather than need. Families buy heavily in DP2 and in Year 11, lightly in the Diploma's first year, and almost nothing across MYP 1 to 5, because nothing external is being examined. The arithmetic is the wrong way round. An MYP student has time, no public assessment deadline and a gap that is still small, so an hour spent now changes a trajectory. A DP2 student has eight weeks, six subjects and a gap that has compounded, so an hour buys damage limitation at a higher rate.

Dubai market rates make the point sharply. Published figures put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and exam-year specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase listing AED 270 and Bestimate putting specialist exam-year monthly costs at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for a weekly session. Bestimate's budget band for the same weekly hour sits at AED 240 to 600 a month. MYP work generally belongs in the lower bands because it is teaching rather than triage, and the same intervention later belongs in the upper ones.

The second thing that makes MYP money easy to waste is that parents cannot read the report. A criterion-based report does not say your child scored 68 per cent. It gives four criterion marks out of eight each, converts the total out of 32 through published boundaries into a grade from 1 to 7, and says nothing explicit about why. A family that cannot see which criterion is low buys general tutoring, which is the most expensive form of help per unit of improvement. A family that can see it buys three sessions on criterion C and stops.

Meydan's own situation is worth stating because it affects who is available. There is no school inside Meydan. MYP students here attend the IB continuum schools in Nad Al Sheba, principally North London Collegiate School Dubai and GEMS Modern Academy, or cross Ras Al Khor Road to Hartland International School and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai. The pool of tutors who understand criterion marking rather than content coverage is small anywhere, and narrowing it to people who can drive to Meydan by six o'clock shrinks it without improving it.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. MYP support for Meydan families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. What follows is a cost argument: what the Dubai market charges, what the criterion marks mean, where MYP money is thrown away, what the Personal Project does and does not permit, and which MYP year gives the best return on a paid hour.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-meydan.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme spans five years that behave very differently, and the price of fixing something rises steadily across them. These are the stages a Meydan family is choosing between.

programmes.name: The early Middle Years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria each, and no external assessment at all. Reports arrive as criterion marks out of eight with a converted grade, and the criteria that cause trouble are usually the process ones rather than the knowledge one. This is where number fluency, algebraic habits, method writing and extended-answer structure are either established or quietly skipped.
programmes.countryNote: In Meydan this is the cheapest tutoring money available and the least spent. A short block here on the specific low criterion costs a fraction of the same intervention in DP1, and the Dubai market charges its lower band for it rather than its exam-year band.

programmes.name: The years that decide the Diploma start
programmes.description: Subject content deepens, the Personal Project arrives in MYP 5, and option choices begin to close routes. Some schools offer MYP eAssessment for the IB MYP certificate; others do not, and that changes whether anything external is sat at all. The skills that matter for what comes next are rearranging formulae, handling data, writing an argued paragraph and meeting a deadline without supervision.
programmes.countryNote: For Meydan families this is the decision point, because the Nad Al Sheba and Hartland schools split between the IB Diploma and A Level at sixth form. Ask which route your school's own sixth form expects before treating MYP 5 as simply the year before DP1.

programmes.name: Where the Diploma picks it up
programmes.description: The Diploma assesses with examination papers, mark schemes and internal assessments against published criteria, which is a different contract from MYP criterion marking. Students arriving with a 6 in MYP sciences or mathematics frequently meet a first DP1 test that marks them down for answers they consider correct, because the Diploma pays for visible reasoning rather than for explanation.
programmes.countryNote: The September gap is the single most predictable event in a Meydan family's school career and the one least planned for. Four hours in the summer before DP1 costs a fraction of a rescue term in November at Dubai specialist rates.

programmes.name: The other route out of MYP
programmes.description: Some students leave the MYP after MYP 3 for a British-track IGCSE at a different school, which means moving from criterion marking to tiered examinations with syllabus codes, a Core or Extended entry and a June or November series. The content overlap is substantial; the assessment culture is not, and the adjustment is in technique rather than knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: This route is common in the Meydan corridor because the British-curriculum schools nearby run it. If it is under consideration, a short block on examination technique in the final MYP year transfers better than extra content coverage does.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-meydan.subjectsIntro: An MYP student carries all eight groups at once, so help has to be aimed. These are the groups and the criterion that most often costs the mark in each, which is where a paid hour should go first.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding usually looks fine while applying mathematics in real-life contexts does not, because that criterion asks for a model, a justification and a reflection on whether the answer is sensible. Most low marks here are structural rather than numerical.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating are where marks go. Students explain well and plan loosely, so the method is not repeatable and the evaluation names a limitation without explaining its effect. Both are quick to teach and rarely taught.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing and producing text split cleanly: students who read well often write without structure, and the criterion rewards a controlled argument. Three sessions on paragraph architecture frequently move a mark that a term of extra reading did not.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Marked in phases rather than years, which confuses parents more than any other part of the programme. A student can move year group and stay in the same phase. Productive help targets the specific skill being assessed, usually speaking or writing to a prompt.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigating and communicating carry the marks, and the common failure is description where analysis was wanted. Source handling and the habit of stating significance rather than content are the two teachable moves.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A full design cycle assessed across four criteria, with inquiring and analysing and evaluating usually the weak ones. Students build before they specify and then cannot evaluate against criteria they never wrote. The fix is in the planning stage.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Developing skills and responding are assessed alongside the work itself, so the process journal matters as much as the outcome. Students lose marks for undocumented process rather than for weak work, which is worth knowing before buying lessons in the art form.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Planning for performance and reflecting on performance are written criteria inside a practical subject, and a capable athlete can score poorly on both. Help here is writing support rather than coaching, which surprises most families.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed against planning, applying skills and reflecting. It must be the student's own work throughout, and the legitimate support is process questioning and deadline structure rather than any contribution to the product.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria across combined subjects, and frequently the lowest marks on a report because nobody revises for them. Worth checking on the report before assuming a subject is the problem.

Three sessions aimed at one criterion routinely move a mark that a term of general subject tutoring did not.
