sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and which band MYP work belongs in
paragraphs: Published rates in this market cover an enormous range for the same job title. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya's comparison panel starts around AED 33 to 52. The qualified online subject band runs roughly AED 150 to 300, where Unitors states an IGCSE rate from AED 150 and an IB rate from AED 200. Specialist exam-year work is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED asks AED 650 an hour for a named examiner.

Most MYP work belongs in the lower half of that spread, and a family paying specialist exam-year rates for MYP 2 mathematics is paying for triage they do not need. The reason is structural rather than a judgement about MYP teaching. Specialist bands exist for diagnosis under time pressure and for marking against a published external scheme. An MYP student has no external paper, no grade boundary deadline and a gap that is still simple, so the work is teaching rather than rescue.

Monthly figures are the more useful way to think about it, because that is how the money leaves the account. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for exam-year specialist support. Packages circulate at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. A three-session MYP criterion block sits well below any of those monthly commitments.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list on these pages, and nothing above is our quote. Every figure is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it and was read in October 2026. What we do instead is give the first lesson free so the comparison is made on teaching rather than on copy, and recommend a short block rather than a standing arrangement where a short block is what the report actually indicates.

sections.heading: Reading a criterion report before you buy anything
paragraphs: An MYP report is the cheapest diagnostic instrument a Meydan parent will ever be handed, and most of them go unread because they do not look like marks. Each subject carries four criteria, each marked out of eight, assessed against published descriptors that say what an eight looks like and what a two looks like. The four add to a total out of 32, and published boundaries convert that total into a grade from one to seven. The grade is a summary. The four numbers behind it are the information.

The pattern to look for is uneven rather than low. A student with marks of seven, three, four and six does not have a subject problem; they have a specific criterion problem, and in sciences or mathematics that is almost always one of the process criteria rather than the knowledge criterion. Knowing and understanding tends to be the strongest mark on a Meydan report because it is the closest thing to traditional content assessment, and the criteria asking the student to plan, justify or evaluate are the ones that sit low.

That observation converts directly into money. A family that sees the uneven pattern buys three sessions on one criterion. A family that sees only the grade buys weekly general tutoring in the subject, which in the Dubai middle band means a commitment of several hundred dirhams a month to work that may never touch the actual weakness. The second family will often report that tutoring did not help, and they will be right, because the target was wrong rather than the teaching.

Two further things worth checking on the report. Interdisciplinary unit marks are assessed against their own criteria and are frequently the lowest numbers on the page, because nobody prepares for them. And language acquisition is marked in phases rather than year groups, so a child can change year and stay in the same phase without anything having gone wrong. Both are regularly mistaken for subject failure.

sections.heading: The four ways MYP money gets wasted in this corridor
paragraphs: The first is buying the subject instead of the criterion. A term of weekly mathematics tutoring for a student whose knowledge criterion is already a seven delivers more of what they can do and none of what they cannot. The report named the problem and the purchase ignored it. This is the most common pattern we see in MYP enquiries from Meydan and the most expensive, because it runs for months before anyone concludes that tutoring does not work for their child.

The second is paying exam-year rates for a non-exam year. There is no external paper in most MYP years, so there is no mark scheme to be marked against and no grade boundary to be beaten. The premium bands in the Dubai market exist for exactly those two things. Paying AED 400 an hour for MYP 3 science is buying capability the situation does not call for, and the same money spread across a short block and a summer bridging block would do considerably more.

The third is waiting for the Diploma. The September after MYP 5 is the most predictable difficulty in a Dubai school career: criterion marking gives way to examination marking, and a student used to explaining has to start showing a working line. Families consistently meet this in November of DP1 and buy help at exam-year prices. Four to six sessions the previous July, at the same hourly rate for materially easier work, is the single clearest cost saving available in this programme.

The fourth is paying for travel in a community where it buys nothing extra. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for qualified online work, and the gap is the drive. For an MYP student the thing being paid for is usually an adult in the room, which is a real need for some children and no benefit at all for others. Decide which your child is before paying the premium every week for a year.

sections.heading: The MYP 5 to DP1 gap, and what it costs to close late
paragraphs: The gap is not about content. Most students arriving in DP1 from a Nad Al Sheba continuum school have met the material. What changes is what earns credit. MYP criteria reward explanation, process and reflection, assessed against descriptors by a teacher who knows the student. Diploma assessment rewards a visible reasoning line marked against a published scheme by somebody who does not. A student who writes a confident paragraph and omits the working line was rewarded for that in MYP 4 and is penalised for it in DP1.

The specific habits that have to change are small and teachable. Show the substitution, not just the answer. Answer the command word that was used rather than the question you expected. Write units at every stage. Round at the end rather than the middle. State the principle before applying it. Treat an uncertainty as part of the result rather than as an afterthought. None of that takes a term; it takes a handful of sessions and some marked practice, and it has to happen before the first DP1 assessment rather than after it.

The cost difference between doing it early and doing it late is the whole argument. In the July after MYP 5 this is a short bridging block in the Dubai qualified band. In November of DP1, after a bad first report, it is a rescue term and families tend to buy it from the specialist band, in two subjects at once, because they cannot tell which subject the problem lives in. The hourly rate rises and the hours multiply, and the underlying fix was the same handful of habits in both cases.

There is a second route out of MYP in this corridor, towards a British-track IGCSE at another school, and the same logic applies with different details. That move swaps criterion marking for tiered entries, syllabus codes and a June or November series. The adjustment is again technique rather than knowledge: command words, mark allocation and the discipline of timed practice. Buy it in the summer, not in the spring of Year 11.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and exactly where a tutor stops
paragraphs: The Personal Project runs in MYP 5 and is assessed on planning, on applying skills and on reflecting, with a process journal supporting the whole thing. It must be the student's own work throughout. This matters more than families assume, because the project looks like the sort of thing an adult could help with, and some of the help available in this market crosses the line without announcing it. The product is the student's. The journal is the student's. The reflection is the student's.

What legitimate support looks like is almost entirely questioning. Is the goal achievable in the time available with the resources the student actually has. Are the criteria the student has set for their own product testable, or are they aspirations. Does the journal record enough decisions, dead ends and changes of direction to support a reflection at the end, or is it a list of activities. Has the student confused being busy with applying a skill. Those questions improve a project substantially and contribute nothing to it.

What a tutor must not do is choose the goal, design the product, make any part of it, write or edit the report or the journal, or supply material the student then presents as their own work. IB Gram provides none of those things. A tutor who offers to help finish a Personal Project is creating a risk that sits with your child, not with them, and the school authenticates the work.

The practical shape of useful Personal Project support is two or three sessions early, at the scoping and planning stage, and possibly one near the end on reading the reflection against the criteria. It is a small, cheap, time-limited purchase. Anything presented as ongoing weekly Personal Project support should prompt the question of what exactly is being done each week.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects beside eight MYP groups
paragraphs: An MYP student in Dubai is carrying eight subject groups and the mandatory UAE subjects at the same time, which is a heavier week than the programme description suggests. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Those periods occupy timetable space that has to come from somewhere.

The rules on organisation are specific and worth knowing before buying any help in these subjects. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and KHDA states that combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic must be the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, while non-Arabs take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Instructional time is counted in 40-minute lesson units, schools may vary actual lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold the appropriate KHDA approval. There is also a content restriction that rules out the obvious tutoring approach: for these subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited.

For a Meydan family planning MYP tutoring, the consequence is about scheduling rather than content. Count the mandatory periods and the sport or activity commitments before choosing a slot. A slot chosen from the whole week survives the term; a slot chosen from the subject timetable alone gets moved repeatedly and then abandoned, which is the quietest way of all to waste money.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit, and what IB Gram does not claim
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Every Meydan MYP student's school falls under it and is inspected on a published band scale. The national map is broader than most tutoring pages mention: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; Sharjah with SPEA; Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education.

There is a useful piece of cost context in KHDA's own announcements. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Separately, Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. For a family budgeting MYP support, a flat fee year is the right year to spend on a short block.

Tutoring is regulated separately. The private tuition work permit comes from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it is free, there is no good reason for a tutor working with UAE families to be without one, so ask to see it. No fine schedule is published, so nobody should quote an amount at you.

To be explicit: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and claims none anywhere on this site. We are an independent platform that matches families with subject specialists and teaches online. Describing what a regulator does helps a parent. Suggesting one stands behind us would be the most misleading thing these pages could do.

faqs.question: How much should a Meydan family expect to spend on MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: Less than on Diploma support, and usually as a fixed block rather than a monthly commitment. Published Dubai rates put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, which is where most MYP work belongs, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band. A three-session criterion block sits well below any monthly figure. Those are market numbers read in October 2026, not our price list; the first lesson with us is free.

faqs.question: Why is MYP tutoring better value than Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: Because the gap is still small and there is time to close it. An MYP student has no external paper, no grade boundary deadline and a weakness that is usually a single criterion rather than a compounded content debt. That makes the work teaching rather than triage, which belongs in a lower rate band and takes fewer hours. The same habits fixed in DP2 are bought at specialist exam-year rates, often across two subjects at once, because by then nobody can tell where the problem actually lives.

faqs.question: What do four criterion marks out of eight actually tell me?
faqs.answer: More than the converted grade does. Each subject is assessed against four published criteria, each out of eight, totalling 32 before boundaries convert it into a grade from one to seven. The pattern is what matters. Marks of seven, three, four and six indicate a specific criterion problem rather than a subject problem, and in sciences and mathematics the low one is almost always a process criterion rather than the knowledge criterion. That single observation tells you whether to buy three sessions or a term.

faqs.question: My child holds 6s in the MYP but the school says that is not enough for Higher Level. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the two systems reward different things. MYP criteria pay for explanation, process and reflection, judged against descriptors by a teacher who knows the student. Diploma assessment pays for a visible reasoning line, marked against a published scheme by an examiner who does not. A student who writes a confident paragraph without showing substitution was rewarded for that in MYP 4 and will be marked down for it in DP1. The fix is a handful of habits, not more content, and it is far cheaper bought in July.

faqs.question: Is a weekly MYP tutor usually the right purchase?
faqs.answer: Only where the criterion marks show an even content gap across the subject. Where the knowledge criterion is strong and a process criterion is weak, a weekly arrangement delivers more of what the child can already do, and families then conclude that tutoring does not work for them. The better default is a fixed block of three or four sessions on the single low criterion, with the student producing two pieces against it, and a deliberate stop. Audit anything weekly every term against the written notes.

faqs.question: Which MYP year gives the best return on a paid hour?
faqs.answer: MYP 3 and MYP 4 for habits, and the summer after MYP 5 for the transition. In the earlier years the skills that transfer are number fluency, rearranging formulae, writing a repeatable method and structuring an argued paragraph, and none of them is under deadline pressure yet. The summer block is different: it targets the move from criterion marking to examination marking, which is the most predictable difficulty in a Dubai school career and the one most consistently paid for too late.

faqs.question: Why is the lowest mark on my child's report an interdisciplinary unit?
faqs.answer: Usually because nobody prepares for it. Interdisciplinary units are assessed against their own criteria across combined subjects, and they rarely feature in revision or in parents' attention, so the mark sits low without indicating a problem in either contributing subject. Check it before concluding that a subject is failing. It is worth asking the school what the unit asked for, but it is rarely the thing to spend money on, and it is frequently mistaken for a science or humanities weakness.

faqs.question: My child's language acquisition phase has not changed all year. Is something wrong?
faqs.answer: Probably not. Language acquisition is marked in phases rather than year groups, and phases cover a range of ability that a student can spend more than one academic year inside. Moving year group without moving phase is ordinary. What is worth asking the teacher is which specific skill the next phase requires, because the answer is usually concrete, such as sustained speaking to a prompt or writing to a given text type, and that is something a short block can address directly.

faqs.question: May a tutor help my child with the MYP Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Only by questioning, never by contributing. A tutor may ask whether the goal is achievable with the time and resources available, whether the success criteria the student set are testable, and whether the process journal records enough decisions to support a genuine reflection. A tutor may not choose the goal, design or make the product, write or edit the report or the journal, or supply material the student presents as their own. IB Gram provides none of that; the school authenticates the work and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Do MYP students sit external examinations at the end of MYP 5?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the school. MYP eAssessment exists as a route to the IB MYP certificate, and some schools in Dubai enter students for it while others do not and report on internal criterion assessment alone. The answer changes what a final MYP year should look like, so ask your school directly rather than assuming. For most Meydan families the more consequential question is which sixth-form route the school's own students take, since that decides what MYP 5 is preparing for.

faqs.question: Which schools near Meydan run the MYP?
faqs.answer: Meydan has no school inside it, so students travel. The IB continuum schools in the nearest belt, Nad Al Sheba, include North London Collegiate School Dubai and GEMS Modern Academy, with Repton School Dubai and Kent College Dubai also within a short drive. Across Ras Al Khor Road families use Hartland International School and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, the latter running the bilingual route. Each sets its own criterion assessment calendar and Personal Project deadline. These schools are named as context only; no affiliation is implied.

faqs.question: Does paying for an in-home MYP tutor in Meydan buy anything extra?
faqs.answer: It buys an adult in the room, which genuinely helps some children of this age and does nothing for others. Published Dubai rates put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for qualified online work, and the difference is the drive. Meydan adds a specific problem: the approach from Al Quoz or Al Khail Road between four and six is slow, so a local tutor's earliest offer is usually later than you wanted. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India.

faqs.question: What time can an MYP session start on a Meydan weeknight?
faqs.answer: About quarter past four is realistic once the Nad Al Sheba school run is finished, and that assumes the student can begin without a parent in the room. Many Meydan parents work in Business Bay or DIFC and are not back until five or later, which is one practical advantage of the online format at this age: the session starts on time and the written note tells the parent what happened. If a parent wants to be present, half past five is the honest earliest.

faqs.question: How do the Dubai mandatory subjects fit into an MYP timetable?
faqs.answer: They take real space. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, counted in 40-minute lesson units with 25 minutes the advised minimum for any mandatory lesson. Separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs and combined classes are prohibited. For these subjects, additional or different content without prior Ministry of Education permission is not allowed. Count those periods before choosing a tutoring slot, or the slot will be moved repeatedly and then dropped.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two children in the same Meydan household?
faqs.answer: Often yes, in separate slots, and MYP work is where this makes the most sense. Two children in different MYP years frequently have the same underlying weakness, typically a process criterion or basic algebraic fluency, so one tutor who has diagnosed it in one child recognises it quickly in the other. Each child still needs their own session, because criterion work is specific to their own produced pieces. There is no travel to price twice, which is part of why the online format is economical for larger households.

faqs.question: Will an MYP tutor promise my child's grade will rise?
faqs.answer: No, and be careful with anyone who does. Criterion marks reflect work the student produces between sessions, judged against descriptors by their own teacher, so no tutor controls the outcome. What a tutor can do is name the low criterion, explain what the descriptor actually rewards, have the student produce pieces against it and show the difference. Several pages in this market publish improvement percentages with no sample size, date or method behind them. Ask how the figure was calculated and watch what happens next.

intro.heading: Why MYP help is nearly always a calendar problem first
paragraphs: Parents in Mirdif rarely search for an IB MYP tutor in Mirdif because of a general worry. They search because a date is approaching. A Sciences investigation is due in eleven days, the Individuals and Societies summative is the week after, and the end-of-term report lands before either piece can be improved. The Middle Years Programme makes this sharper than a British-curriculum middle school does, because every assessed task reports against named criteria rather than a single percentage, and a weak criterion keeps reappearing until someone teaches the skill behind it.

The Dubai academic year gives the problem its shape. Schools in Mirdif open in late August or early September, close for a winter break in mid-December, run a second term from January to the spring break, and finish in early July. Inside that, each MYP subject sets two to four summative tasks per term. Work backwards from a report date and the real number of teaching weeks available is almost always smaller than a parent assumes. Eight weeks of weekly one-to-one lessons is roughly one term's worth of a single criterion moving up two mark bands, which is a realistic target. Four weeks is a repair job on one task.

The second thing the calendar decides is the hour. Most Mirdif schools finish between 2:30pm and 3:15pm, and a child living in Uptown Mirdif or Mirdif Hills is home quickly because the school is inside the community. A child at Deira International School in Dubai Festival City, or at Dubai English Speaking College in Academic City, is travelling for twenty-five to forty minutes in afternoon traffic on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. That difference decides whether a 4pm slot is sensible or whether 5pm is the first honest start. Online lessons let a family pick the slot that matches the actual arrival time rather than the slot a tutor can drive to.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated plainly because the search phrase for this kind of help is often a home-tutor phrase, and a parent deserves to know the format before they book rather than after. What the online format buys in exchange is a subject specialist instead of whoever is free within a twenty-minute drive of Mirdif — and in the MYP, where Design, Arts and Language Acquisition specialists are thin on the ground locally, that trade is the whole argument.

Everything below is organised by time. The criteria table tells you what is being marked. The year-counted-backwards table tells you where your child is in the cycle. The cost table tells you what the Dubai market charges for this level of help, with each figure attributed to whoever published it. The last sections cover the parts of MYP life that catch families out late: the Personal Project in MYP 5, the mandatory UAE subjects that run alongside the programme in every Dubai private school, and what a tutor is allowed to do with coursework that must remain the student's own.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mirdif.programmesIntro: Mirdif families meet the MYP from two directions: children moving up from a PYP primary inside the same school, and children arriving from a British or Indian middle school into MYP 3 or 4. Both need different things, and both are heading for the same decision at the end of MYP 5.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and reports against learner profile attributes and conceptual understanding rather than subject marks. There are no examinations and no criterion scores. Children finish it fluent in asking questions and presenting findings, and often less practised at the two things MYP summatives demand immediately: writing to a command term under time pressure, and showing working that a marker can follow.
programmes.countryNote: Uptown International School in Mirdif runs the full IB continuum, so a child there moves from PYP into MYP without changing school, uniform or friendship group. The transition still bites in Mathematics and Sciences, where Criterion C and Criterion D ask for structured written reasoning for the first time. Tutoring in MYP 1 and 2 is usually about that writing, not about content.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and four assessment criteria in every one of them. Each criterion is marked out of 8 against published descriptors, giving 32 marks per subject, which the school converts to a 1-7 grade using IB grade boundaries. Interdisciplinary units, Approaches to Learning skills and Service as Action run through all five years, and MYP 5 adds the Personal Project.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP competes directly with IGCSE for the 14-16 age group, and several Mirdif families switch school at that point precisely to sit IGCSEs instead. Staying in the MYP is a defensible choice, but it means the first external examination a child meets is in the Diploma Programme two years later, so examination technique has to be taught deliberately rather than absorbed.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment is mostly external, sat in a single examination session, with internal assessment coursework in every subject. The step up from MYP 5 is largely a step up in volume and in the precision mark schemes expect.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 students in Mirdif who are heading for the DP have one decision that matters more than the rest: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and at which level. Criterion B investigation marks in MYP Mathematics are the best early signal there is, which is why a tutor working in MYP 4 and 5 should be asked about that route choice, not just about the current unit.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mirdif.subjectsIntro: The MYP has eight subject groups and all eight are assessed. Families usually ask about Mathematics and Sciences first, then discover that Design and Language Acquisition are where the marks are actually being lost, because those two are taught by fewer specialists and misunderstood by most parents.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Standard and Extended)
subjects.description: Criterion A tests knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, and D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Most lost marks sit in B and D: students find the pattern but never generalise it, or they produce a correct calculation with no interpretation of what it means. The Extended route from MYP 4 is the pathway into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Sciences (Integrated, Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
subjects.description: Criterion B asks the student to design a controlled investigation, C to process and evaluate data, and D to reflect on the impacts of science. The commonest failure is a hypothesis with no mechanism behind it and a conclusion that restates the graph. Teaching a student to write an evaluation that names a specific source of error, and what it did to the data, moves C and D faster than more content revision.

subjects.name: Language and Literature (English)
subjects.description: Criteria run analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Analysis is the bottleneck: students describe what a writer says rather than how the choice of word or structure creates the effect. A short, repeatable paragraph frame built around one quotation and one technique lifts Criterion A within a few weeks, because the skill being marked is narrow and teachable.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition (Arabic, French, Spanish)
subjects.description: Assessed in listening, reading, speaking and writing, with students placed in a phase rather than a year group. Mirdif families often discover late that their child has been sitting in a phase too low to reach the Diploma language requirement. Tutoring here is phase-targeted: the vocabulary and text types for the phase above the current one, plus the oral task format.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: History, geography and economics content assessed through knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. Criterion D is where marks vanish: students summarise sources instead of evaluating origin, purpose and limitation. Source work is a drill, and eight well-chosen sources with a fixed evaluation structure will usually do more than a term of re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Four criteria covering inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Design is almost always the lowest grade on a Mirdif MYP report, because students treat the design cycle folder as paperwork. The folder is the assessment. Teaching a student to write specifications that are actually testable, then test against them, is the single highest-return intervention in the subject.

subjects.name: Arts (Visual Arts, Music, Drama)
subjects.description: Marked on knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than the finished piece, which surprises families every year. Support here is about documenting intention and revision honestly and in enough detail, and about writing the artist-statement reflections that Criterion D rewards.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Includes a written and reflective component, not only performance. Students lose marks on the planning for performance criterion and on the reflection, where a training plan has no measurable targets. A few sessions on goal setting, data recording and evaluation language usually fixes a grade that a child assumed was about fitness.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Each year the school runs at least one unit assessed against separate interdisciplinary criteria, where two subjects are brought together and the student is marked on synthesis. These units are rarely revised for because they sit outside the normal subject rhythm. Knowing the four interdisciplinary criteria before the task is set is most of the work.

subjects.name: Personal Project (MYP 5)
subjects.description: A year-long independent project with a process journal, a product or outcome, and a report, assessed on planning, applying skills, and reflecting. A tutor may coach the process, question the goal and teach referencing. A tutor may not write the report or make the product. The honest version of help here is deadline architecture and better questions.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mirdif.regionsIntro: Mirdif sits in Dubai's eastern suburbs, a villa-and-low-rise belt where families stay for years and children often change school without changing neighbourhood. The practical consequence for tutoring is that the school a child attends, and therefore the finishing time, varies far more than the postcode does.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Villas and low-rise apartments either side of Algeria Street, with Uptown International School and GEMS Royal Dubai School inside the community. Children at those schools are home by about 3pm, which makes a 4pm online lesson comfortable on a weekday.

regions.name: Uptown Mirdif and Mirdif Hills
regions.note: Denser apartment blocks with a younger family profile and a high share of first-time IB parents. Demand here is heaviest in MYP 1 to 3, where the four-criterion marking is new and a report card needs translating before it can be acted on.

regions.name: Al Mizhar
regions.note: Large villa plots to the north-east, with Al Mizhar American Academy nearby and a mix of American-curriculum and IB families. Students often carry a GPA mindset into MYP criteria, and the first tutoring job is explaining that a 6 out of 8 is not 75 per cent.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej
regions.note: Spread-out villa communities where the school run is longer in both directions. Families here lean towards later session slots, 5pm or 6pm, and towards fewer, longer sessions rather than two short ones a week.

regions.name: Al Warqa
regions.note: A dense residential belt feeding several large Indian and British-curriculum schools. MYP enquiries from Al Warqa are often from families who moved into an IB school mid-year and need a bridging plan for Sciences and Design.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya and Nad Al Hamar
regions.note: Older established neighbourhoods close to the airport road, with short commutes to Festival City schools. The practical constraint here is siblings on different timetables, which usually means one tutoring slot has to serve two children on different evenings.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Home to Deira International School and Universal American School, so a large share of Mirdif's secondary students travel here daily. Arrival home is realistically 3:45pm to 4:15pm, and a 4pm start works only for students who finish earlier on a short day.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: The corridor along Dubai-Al Ain Road that carries Dubai English Speaking College and several university campuses. Afternoon traffic is the limiting factor, and online lessons remove the second half of the journey entirely.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif and Uptown Mirdif
schoolClusters.note: The immediate cluster. One full IB continuum school and several strong British-curriculum schools sit within the community, which is why MYP and IGCSE families here often live on the same street and compare notes across two different assessment systems.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Festival City and the Academic City corridor
schoolClusters.note: Where a large share of Mirdif's older students actually spend the day. These schools run IB Diploma alongside British pathways, so MYP 5 students here are making the DP decision in a building where both options are visible.

schoolClusters.city: Al Warqa and Al Qusais
schoolClusters.note: The larger-roll schools to the east and north, mostly Indian and British curriculum. Students arriving from here into an IB school mid-key-stage are the most common bridging case we see in the eastern suburbs.

The tutor works from the school's unit planner and task sheet rather than a generic scheme, so the week before a summative is spent on that task's criteria and the week after is spent on the feedback. This is the format that moves a criterion two mark bands over eight weeks.

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks actually have to achieve
paragraphs: Start with the report date, not with the subject. In a Dubai MYP school there are usually two reporting points per term, and the marks that feed them are the summative tasks already on the unit planner. If the next report is six weeks away and two summatives fall inside that window, the realistic goal is to raise the criteria those two tasks assess. Trying to lift a whole subject grade in six weeks is how families end up paying for sessions that produce no visible change, because an MYP grade is a conversion of four criterion scores and only the criteria being assessed in the window can move.

Eight weeks is the number that keeps appearing because it is roughly half a Dubai term and it is long enough for a skill to be taught, practised on a real task, marked, and practised again. A plausible eight-week shape for a Sciences student stuck on data handling: two sessions reading the Criterion C descriptors against the last marked piece, two sessions on processing raw data into a usable table and graph, two sessions writing evaluations that name a specific error and its direction of effect, and two sessions applying all of it to the live investigation. That is one criterion, taught properly, with evidence at the end.

What does not fit into eight weeks is three subjects at once. Families in Mirdif frequently open with Mathematics, Sciences and English together, and the honest answer is to pick the subject where the criterion is both weakest and most teachable, work it until the next report, then move. Two subjects at one session a week is the practical ceiling for a child who also has a school day, Arabic, Islamic Education, Service as Action and, in MYP 5, a Personal Project running in the background.

The last thing to settle before booking is what counts as evidence that it worked. A marked task against a named criterion is evidence. A child saying they feel more confident is encouraging but is not a measurement. Ask for the criterion score before and after, and judge the eight weeks on that.

sections.heading: The four MYP criteria, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group is assessed against exactly four criteria, labelled A to D, and each is marked out of 8 against published descriptors. Four criteria out of 8 gives 32 marks per subject, which the school converts to a 1-7 grade using IB grade boundaries. The criteria are different in each subject group, which is why a parent who understands Criterion C in Mathematics still cannot read a Design report. The table below sets them out together, and it is the single most useful thing on this page to print and keep.

Reading a report with this table in hand changes the conversation. A 7 out of 8 in Mathematics Criterion A and a 3 in Criterion B does not describe a child who is bad at maths; it describes a child who can execute a method and cannot yet investigate a pattern and generalise it. Those are different lessons. In Sciences, strong A with weak C is a child who knows the content and cannot process data. In Language and Literature, strong C with weak A is a child who writes fluently about a text without analysing how it works.

The descriptors themselves are written in bands of two marks, which is why movement happens in jumps. A student sitting at 3-4 in a criterion is being told they can do the thing with support or in simple cases. Reaching 5-6 almost always requires one specific addition — a justification, an evaluation, a generalisation — rather than more of what they already produce. That is what makes criterion work efficient: the gap between bands is usually a nameable missing move, and once a student knows which move is missing they can add it to every piece.

Schools publish their own task-specific clarifications of these descriptors on each task sheet. Those clarifications are what the teacher actually marks against. Any tutoring session that starts without the task sheet in front of both people is guessing.

sections.heading: The Dubai MYP year counted backwards
paragraphs: Nobody in this search results page publishes a calendar, which is strange, because a calendar is what a parent is actually holding. A Dubai private school year opens in late August or early September and closes in early July, with a winter break around mid-December and a spring break in the second half of March or early April. Inside that, the MYP runs on unit cycles rather than on examination series, so the pressure points are internal deadlines, not public ones.

That changes in MYP 5 for schools offering the optional MYP eAssessment, where on-screen examinations and ePortfolios lead to the IB MYP Certificate. Those sit in a session in the first half of the calendar year, and the ePortfolio components have internal upload deadlines weeks earlier. If your child's school enters students for eAssessment, the deadline that matters is the upload date your coordinator gives you, and it is always earlier than parents expect. Confirm it with the MYP coordinator directly rather than taking a date from any website, including this one.

Ramadan sits inside the second half of the Dubai school year and moves earlier each year. Schools shorten the day, after-school activities thin out, and families reorganise evenings around Iftar. In practice this is the easiest period of the year to schedule tutoring, because a shortened school day frees the early afternoon and online sessions can move to a post-Iftar slot without anybody driving anywhere. The table below is the shape of the year as it affects a tutoring plan; your school's own calendar overrides it.

The reason to work from this table rather than from a term plan is that it tells you when not to book. Buying sessions in the fortnight before a winter break, when summatives are finished and reports are already written, buys nothing. The same money spent in the two weeks after the break, pre-teaching the next unit, is worth considerably more.

sections.heading: What Middle Years Programme support costs in Dubai, and what the hour buys
paragraphs: Three of the six pages currently ranking for Dubai tutoring queries publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars, which is not the currency a Mirdif family transacts in. So here are the Dubai market bands in dirhams, each attributed to whoever published it. Read them as the market, not as an IB Gram price list: our own model is a free trial lesson first and a quoted plan after, because an MYP Design block and an MYP 1 Mathematics block are not the same piece of work.

At the cheap end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52, both online and both typically delivered by university students or generalists. That tier is viable for homework supervision and is a poor match for criterion work, because marking against MYP descriptors is a trained skill and an undergraduate who has never seen a rubric cannot teach to one. The qualified-subject-tutor band online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors are quoted around AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 plus. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for named or examiner-level tutors.

In-home visits are the band that distorts everything. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Compare that with online monthly packages advertised around AED 799 for eight sessions. The gap is not teaching quality; it is a car, a driver and forty minutes of Dubai traffic each way, paid for by the hour. For a Mirdif family that premium buys proximity and nothing else, and proximity is the one thing an online lesson does not need.

What the hour actually buys is worth separating from what it costs. An hour with a tutor who has marked MYP work produces a named criterion, a descriptor band, and a specific missing move. An hour with a generalist produces completed homework. Both cost money; only one of them changes a report.

sections.heading: Online lessons against a tutor driving into Mirdif
paragraphs: A parent typing a home-tutor phrase into Google is asking a reasonable question, and it deserves a real answer rather than a sales line. In-home tutoring in Mirdif is genuinely available from independent tutors and small agencies, it is priced as the table above shows, and it suits some families — particularly those with a young child who will not settle in front of a screen, or a household where a dedicated quiet room is not available.

The costs of that choice are concrete. The tutor pool shrinks to people willing to drive to the eastern suburbs at 5pm, which in practice means generalists rather than MYP Design or Language Acquisition specialists. The rate carries a travel premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour over the online equivalent. Cancellations rise, because traffic on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Al Khawaneej Road makes a fixed arrival time fragile. And the session cannot easily move: a child who is ill at 4:30pm either takes the lesson or loses it, where an online slot can shift by a day.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE. Every UAE lesson is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and home visits exist only in our India service. The argument for that is not cost; it is the pool. A Mirdif student who needs someone who has marked MYP Sciences Criterion B, or who can work in Arabic Phase 3, is choosing from every available specialist rather than from the subset who live within a half-hour drive. On a four-criterion assessment system with eight subject groups, that difference is the whole game.
The table sets the two formats side by side on the dimensions that actually differ. Teaching quality is not in the table, because format does not determine it; the tutor does.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, term by term
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the piece of MYP 5 that most reliably goes wrong, and it goes wrong for a scheduling reason rather than an academic one. It runs across most of a school year, it is supervised rather than taught, and it is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting — all three of which are evidenced by a process journal kept over months. A student who produces a good product and a thin journal scores badly. A student who keeps an honest, dated, reflective journal and produces a modest product usually scores well.

A workable shape for a Mirdif student: goal and context settled before the winter break, the bulk of the making and the skill-building through January and February, and the report written in the weeks after the spring break with the journal already complete. That leaves the Ramadan period for lower-intensity journal work and reflection, which is exactly what fits a shortened school day. Schools set their own internal deadlines and those override everything here, so the first job in MYP 5 is to write the school's dates on a wall calendar at home.

Where a tutor helps is narrow and worth stating precisely. Questioning whether the goal is specific enough to be achievable. Teaching the research and referencing skills the project demands. Reading the assessment criteria with the student so they know what the report has to evidence. Holding weekly accountability so the journal does not become three entries written the night before. Teaching the student how to write a reflection that identifies a decision, its reason and its consequence.

Where a tutor does not help, under IB academic honesty rules, is in producing the work. A tutor must not write the report, make the product, or draft the journal entries. That boundary is not a disclaimer; it is the difference between support and malpractice, and a family paying for help is entitled to know which one they are buying.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed to deliver. This is a federal requirement reflected in KHDA's own mandatory-subject guidance, which states that its requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For an MYP family in Mirdif this means your child's timetable carries these subjects in addition to the eight MYP subject groups, and they appear on the report alongside criterion grades.

The organisational rules are specific and useful to know. KHDA requires schools to run separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for Arab and non-Arab students are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught primarily in Arabic for Arab students; and for non-Arab students Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies are taught in the language of the school's licensed curriculum.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary the lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete thing a parent can ask about at a meeting. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so tutoring in these subjects stays inside the prescribed curriculum rather than importing outside material.

In practice, Mirdif families ask us about Arabic twice: once in MYP 1 to 3, when a non-Arab child is struggling with a subject that carries real timetable weight, and once in MYP 4 and 5, when Arabic as a Language Acquisition phase starts to interact with Diploma language requirements. Both are legitimate tutoring needs and both sit inside the school's own scheme of work.

sections.heading: Where a tutor's job stops: MYP academic honesty
paragraphs: Some of the pages competing for this search sell finished coursework. One sells completed Internal Assessments outright. A family should understand what that is: under IB rules it is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the website that took the money. For an MYP student the exposure is lower than in the Diploma, but the habit formed is the problem, because the same student will be submitting Internal Assessments and an Extended Essay two years later under a regime that checks.

The line is drawn by whose thinking appears in the submitted work. A tutor may teach a skill, explain a concept, model an example on a different question, read the criteria with the student, mark a completed draft against descriptors, and ask questions that make the student notice a gap. A tutor may teach referencing and show how to acknowledge a source correctly. A tutor may run accountability check-ins so a process journal stays current.

A tutor may not write any part of the submission, draft the report, dictate sentences for a student to transcribe, make or assemble a product, invent data for an investigation, or edit a piece to the point where the final text is the tutor's rather than the student's. The practical test we use is simple: if the student could not explain, in their own words, why a particular sentence or decision is in the work, it should not be there. Any tutor who declines to work that way is not giving your child a shortcut; they are putting the submission at risk.

Families sometimes worry that this makes tutoring less useful. It makes it more useful. A child who has been taught to evaluate their own data against a descriptor can do it again in the next unit, next year, and in the Diploma. A child handed a finished evaluation has learned nothing transferable and has an inconsistency on their record waiting to be noticed.
bullets: Allowed: teaching, modelling on a different question, marking a draft against descriptors
Allowed: referencing instruction, criteria reading, weekly accountability
Not allowed: writing or drafting the submission, making the product, inventing data
The test: can the student explain, unprompted, why each decision is there?

sections.heading: KHDA, the Mirdif school cluster, and what a band on a report means
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects schools and publishes a rating on a six-band scale, and those reports are public. IB Gram is not inspected, approved or licensed by KHDA, and nobody offering private tuition should imply otherwise; a KHDA educational services permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, which is a different kind of operation altogether.

The scale of the market Mirdif sits inside is worth knowing. Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, American 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. Seven new private schools were confirmed for the 2026-27 intake — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — adding 16,846 places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

What this means for a Mirdif MYP family is supply. The IB share of Dubai enrolment is small relative to the UK curriculum, and three of the seven new schools are IB, so demand for people who can actually mark MYP criteria is rising faster than the local supply of them. That is the structural reason an online pool beats a local one for this specific programme, and it is why a parent should ask a prospective tutor which subject groups they have marked rather than how many years they have taught.

Private tuition in the UAE is also permitted work rather than informal work. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. Abu Dhabi adds a further rule reported in the local press: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction.

process.title: Tell us the date, not just the subject
process.description: The useful first message names the next summative or report date, the subject, and the criterion letters from the last marked piece. With those three things a plan can be built in one reply. Without them the first session is spent diagnosing what a report card already said.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one per subject
process.description: One free trial lesson per subject, booked before any payment is taken, with the student's most recent marked task in front of both people. The purpose is diagnostic: the tutor should finish it able to name the criterion to target and the missing move inside it.

process.title: An eight-week plan written down
process.description: After the trial you get a short written plan: the criterion being targeted, what each block of sessions covers, which school task it is aimed at, and what evidence will show it worked. If two subjects are needed, the plan says which one comes first and why.

process.title: Fixed weekly slots in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are booked as fixed weekly slots chosen around the actual school arrival time, not a notional one. Mirdif-based schools usually allow a 4pm start; Festival City and Academic City commutes usually mean 5pm. Slots move for Ramadan and for breaks.

process.title: Review at the next marked task
process.description: The plan is reviewed when the next criterion score comes back from school, not on a fixed monthly cycle. If the criterion moved, the next one is chosen. If it did not, the tutor or the approach changes, and we say which we think it is.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-literate, not just subject-literate
whyPoints.description: The tutors matched to MYP requests have marked against MYP descriptors, which is a different skill from knowing the content. Ask any prospective tutor which subject groups and which criteria they have assessed; the answer separates a specialist from a graduate with good subject knowledge.

whyPoints.title: Rates on the page, with sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands above are published Dubai market figures with the publisher named, read in October 2026. We do not print an invented price list, and we do not quote dollars to a dirham household. Our own cost is quoted after the free trial, against a written plan.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the format
whyPoints.description: UAE lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video. We say so before you book rather than after, even though the phrase parents search is a home-tutor phrase. Home visits are part of our India service only, and no page of ours will suggest otherwise.

whyPoints.title: A pool, not a postcode
whyPoints.description: Because lessons are online, a Mirdif student is matched from every available specialist rather than from those willing to drive to the eastern suburbs at 5pm. For MYP Design, Arts and Language Acquisition, where local specialists are genuinely scarce, that is the difference between the right tutor and an available one.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated, not assumed
whyPoints.description: We teach, model, mark and question. We do not write reports, make products or draft journals, and the section above says exactly where the line falls. In a search result that contains sellers of finished coursework, that boundary is worth reading before you choose.

whyPoints.title: Built around the school's own calendar
whyPoints.description: Plans are written against your school's unit planner and task dates, with the winter and spring breaks treated as planning decisions rather than interruptions. The highest-value window in a Dubai MYP year is January to February, and a plan should spend money there rather than in December.

faqs.question: What does an IB MYP tutor in Mirdif actually do in the first month?
faqs.answer: The first month is diagnosis then one target. Session one reads the most recent marked task against its criterion descriptors and names which of the four criteria is costing marks. The next two or three sessions teach the specific missing move in that criterion, usually a justification, an evaluation or a generalisation, and practise it on past questions. The fourth week applies it to whatever live task the school has set. By the end of the month you should have a marked piece showing the criterion score and a short written note saying what changed. A month that produces only completed homework has not worked.

faqs.question: How does a mark out of 32 become a 1 to 7 on my child's MYP report?
faqs.answer: Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, and each criterion is marked out of 8 against published descriptors. The four add to a maximum of 32. The school then converts that total into a 1-7 grade using IB grade boundaries. This is why a parent cannot read an MYP report as a percentage: 24 out of 32 is not 75 per cent of anything, it is a profile of four separate skills. Two children on the same total can need completely different teaching, because one may be weak in communication and the other in investigation.

faqs.question: My child scored 3 in Criterion C. What does that actually mean?
faqs.answer: Criterion C differs by subject, so the first step is to check which one applies. In Mathematics it is communicating; in Sciences it is processing and evaluating; in Language and Literature it is producing text; in Design it is creating the solution. A 3 sits in the 3-4 band, which in most descriptors means the student can do the task in simple situations or with support. Moving to 5-6 usually needs one nameable addition rather than more effort: showing working a reader can follow, evaluating data rather than describing it, or meeting a specification they wrote themselves.

faqs.question: When should a Mirdif MYP 5 student start the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary. The project is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, all evidenced through a process journal kept over months, so a journal started late cannot score well however good the product is. A workable shape is goal and context settled before the winter break, skill-building and making through January and February, and the report written after the spring break with the journal already complete. Your school sets internal deadlines that override any general timeline, so get those dates from the MYP coordinator in the first term and put them on a wall calendar at home.

faqs.question: What do Dubai families pay per hour for Middle Years Programme support?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market figures, read in October 2026, run from roughly AED 33-65 an hour at the budget online end, where Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65. Qualified subject tutors online sit around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialists are quoted AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180-500 including travel. Those are market rates, not IB Gram's price; ours is quoted after a free trial lesson, against a written plan, because an MYP Design block and an MYP 1 Mathematics block are different work.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a villa in Mirdif or Uptown Mirdif?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing. Home visits are part of our India service and are not offered anywhere in the UAE, including Mirdif. We state that before you book because the phrase many parents search is a home-tutor phrase. What the online format gives a Mirdif family in return is access to every available MYP specialist rather than only those willing to drive to the eastern suburbs during the afternoon peak, which matters most in Design, Arts and Language Acquisition.

faqs.question: If school finishes at 3pm, what is a realistic session start time?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school rather than the neighbourhood. A child at Uptown International School or GEMS Royal Dubai School is inside Mirdif and usually home by about 3pm, so a 4pm start is comfortable. A child travelling to Deira International School or Universal American School in Dubai Festival City, or to Dubai English Speaking College in Academic City, realistically arrives between 3:45pm and 4:15pm, which makes 5pm the first honest slot. Online lessons let you pick the time that matches the real arrival, and move it permanently if the route changes.

faqs.question: Is the MYP eAssessment compulsory for my child?
faqs.answer: No. The on-screen examinations and ePortfolios that lead to the IB MYP Certificate are an option a school chooses, and many Dubai schools do not enter students for them. If your school does, the dates that matter are the internal upload deadlines for the ePortfolio components, which fall weeks before the on-screen session and are set by the school. Ask your MYP coordinator directly for those dates rather than relying on any website, including this one. If your school does not use eAssessment, your child's MYP 5 outcome is reported on school-assessed criterion grades.

faqs.question: How many weeks does a Criterion B investigation in Sciences need?
faqs.answer: Four to six weekly sessions is typical if the student already knows the content and is losing marks on design. The work is a sequence: read the descriptors against the last marked investigation, write a research question that names an independent and a dependent variable, list controlled variables with a reason for each, design a method someone else could repeat, and plan how the data will be processed before collecting any. Students who go straight to the practical and write the plan afterwards lose Criterion B marks every time, because the descriptor rewards the planning, not the result.

faqs.question: Which schools near Mirdif run the MYP rather than IGCSE at 14?
faqs.answer: Uptown International School in Mirdif runs the full IB continuum, so students there continue into the MYP at 14 rather than switching to IGCSE. GEMS Modern Academy and a number of other Dubai schools also run IB programmes, while GEMS Royal Dubai School, Star International School Mirdif, Dubai English Speaking College and most of the Al Warqa and Al Qusais schools follow British or Indian pathways with IGCSE at 16. Check the school's own current programme listing and KHDA's published inspection report, since curriculum offerings change as new schools open.

faqs.question: Will MYP tutoring help my child choose Diploma subjects correctly?
faqs.answer: It should. The most consequential Diploma decision a Mirdif MYP 5 student makes is Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and at which level, and the best early evidence is their Criterion B investigation marks in MYP Mathematics rather than their overall grade. A tutor working in MYP 4 and 5 should be able to read those scores and say which route the student is currently suited to, and what would have to change for the other. Ask that question explicitly; many tutors will only discuss the current unit unless prompted.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic and Islamic Education in an IB school in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states its requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These subjects appear on your child's report alongside the MYP criterion grades and carry real timetable weight.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without breaking IB honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may question whether the goal is specific enough, teach research and referencing skills, read the assessment criteria with the student, hold weekly accountability so the process journal stays current, and teach the student how to write a reflection that names a decision, its reason and its consequence. A tutor may not write the report, draft journal entries, make or assemble the product, or edit the text until it is theirs rather than the student's. The working test is whether the student can explain any sentence in the submission without prompting.

faqs.question: Is a private tutor working with my child legally permitted in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tuition in the UAE is permitted work. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through its app, website or e-services with a stated two-working-day completion. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount with suspicion.

faqs.question: How do lessons work during Ramadan and the shortened school day?
faqs.answer: Better than during the rest of the year, usually. Dubai schools shorten the day and reduce after-school activities, which frees the early afternoon, and online sessions can also move to a post-Iftar slot without anyone travelling. Families typically keep one subject moving at a reduced intensity and use the period for lower-pressure work: process journal entries in MYP 5, consolidation of a criterion already taught, or reading ahead into the next unit. The plan is agreed before the period starts so the slot does not simply vanish for a month and then need rebuilding.

faqs.question: What happens if no MYP Design or Arts specialist is free?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Design and Arts are the two MYP subject groups where specialist supply is thinnest, partly because the assessment sits in a process folder and a journal that few tutors have marked. If nobody suitable is available we say so, give an honest estimate of when one will be, and if the deadline cannot wait we will say that a generalist can help with the written reflections but not with the design cycle itself. That is less satisfying than a yes and considerably more useful than a mismatch.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mirdif.closingHeading: Start from the date on the calendar
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mirdif.closingBody: If there is a summative or a report date inside the next eight weeks, that date is the brief. Send the subject, the date and the criterion letters from the last marked task, and we will come back with a plan that says which criterion we would target first and why. The first lesson is free, one per subject, taken before any payment, and it works best with the most recent marked piece of work open on screen. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time and booked around the real Mirdif school run rather than an idealised one.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-rashi.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover MYP subject groups for families across Mohammed Bin Rashid City. Each works to Gulf Standard Time, holds a fixed weekly slot sized to the student's age, and works from the school's own task sheets and criterion descriptors rather than a generic subject scheme.

intro.heading: A twelve-year-old's evening is shorter than the timetable assumes
paragraphs: Most tutoring advice is written for examination students, and applying it to a Middle Years student produces a session at half past six that nobody benefits from. An eleven or twelve-year-old has a usable working window that closes around half past five, and a thirteen or fourteen-year-old's closes not much later. Anything scheduled after that is an hour during which a child is awake, polite and absorbing very little, and parents pay for it anyway because the slot was the one on offer.

The geography makes the window narrower here than the clock suggests. Schools serving this district finish between roughly 2:45pm and 3:30pm. A child at a school inside the district or in Nad Al Sheba is home within twenty minutes. One travelling from Al Safa, Al Barsha or further west is in afternoon traffic, and the final stretch into a gated community adds to it, so arriving between 3:45pm and 4:15pm is normal. Subtract the time a younger child needs to eat and stop, and the usable window may be an hour wide.

The second difference from Diploma scheduling is that MYP does not set work nightly. It sets tasks: an investigation, a design cycle, an essay, a presentation, each arriving with a week or two of notice and each absorbing several evenings when the deadline approaches. A weekly tutoring hour placed without reference to that cycle will sometimes land in a week with nothing to work on and sometimes land in a week where the child has three other things due.

What a near-me search returns, in a district like this one, is tutors prepared to drive here, and a tutor leaving the western cluster at four is in the same traffic as your child. Arrival between a quarter to five and a quarter past is routine, which for a Diploma student is inconvenient and for an MYP student means the session happens at the edge of their capacity. That is a bigger problem at twelve than at seventeen, and almost nobody says so.

IB Gram delivers MYP tuition to Mohammed Bin Rashid City as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, in sessions sized to the student's age rather than sold as a standard hour. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below set out session length by MYP year, where a session belongs in a task cycle, when one fits after the school run, and what the Personal Project needs in MYP 5.
Nothing here promises a grade. It gives you the scheduling decisions that make a younger student's tutoring hour actually work, which in this age group matter more than the choice of tutor does.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-rashi.subjectsIntro: MYP has eight subject groups, and they differ in how much evening time a task consumes. These are the groups we cover for households in this district, noted for their scheduling weight rather than their difficulty.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Sets shorter, more frequent work than other groups, so it fits a short early session well. Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where marks are lost, and that work needs the student alert rather than at the end of a long evening.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Investigation tasks absorb several evenings near a deadline, with criterion C processing and evaluating the usual weak point. A session early in the cycle, before data is collected, is worth three near the submission date.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Reading and drafting both happen in the student's own time and cannot be compressed into a session. The hour is best spent on criterion A analysing, which is a skill discussion rather than a writing exercise.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Research tasks eat evenings, and criterion D thinking critically carries the contested marks. Discussion-led, so it survives a slightly later slot than mathematics or sciences do.

subjects.description: The design cycle runs over weeks and the making happens at home or at school, so a session belongs at the inquiry and the evaluation stages rather than in the middle. Thin coverage in this market, so book early.

subjects.description: The process journal does much of the assessment work, and it has to be kept as the work happens rather than written up afterwards. A session is useful for explaining that and little else.

subjects.description: The written and reflective components surprise students who expected a practical subject. Low evening load except around a reflection deadline, which makes it easy to schedule around.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed with their own criteria and frequently the lowest mark on a report because nobody explained that integration itself is being assessed. Usually a single-session fix, placed as soon as the task is set.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: A long independent piece with its own internal deadlines, which reshapes the whole MYP 5 year. Our support is process coaching placed at the planning stage, and the goal, product and report remain entirely the student's own.
