sections.heading: Session length and timing by MYP year
paragraphs: The standard product in this market is a sixty-minute weekly session, sold identically to an eleven-year-old and a seventeen-year-old. For the eleven-year-old it is the wrong length and usually the wrong hour, and both errors are easy to avoid once somebody names them. Attention, not content, is the binding constraint in the early MYP years, and a session should be built around it.

Forty minutes is a better unit in MYP 1 and 2. A child who finishes a session still engaged has learned something and will return to the next one willingly; a child who endures the last twenty minutes of an hour has learned that tutoring is something to be survived, which is expensive in a way that does not show up for a year. By MYP 4 and 5 an hour is appropriate, and in MYP 5 a longer session around a major task can be justified.

Timing matters more than length. A younger student's usable window closes around half past five, and the journey home from the western school cluster can consume most of what precedes it. That is why the single most useful scheduling decision in this district is giving the MYP child the earlier slot when two children in the household need sessions, even though the Diploma sibling's examinations feel more urgent. A seventeen-year-old can still work at seven; a twelve-year-old cannot.

The table sets out what works by year. It is a starting point rather than a rule, because children differ, and the honest test is whether your child is still contributing in the last ten minutes. If they are not, the session is too long or too late, and shortening or moving it costs nothing while adding a second session costs a great deal and makes the problem worse.

sections.heading: The MYP task cycle, and where a session belongs in it
paragraphs: MYP does not set homework in the way an IGCSE course does. It sets tasks, each with a sheet, a set of criteria being assessed and a deadline a week or two away, and each absorbing several evenings as the deadline approaches. A tutoring slot fixed to a day of the week without reference to that cycle will sometimes arrive with nothing to do and sometimes arrive in the week the student has three things due.

The cycle has four stages and they want different things. At the start, when the task sheet is handed out, the valuable intervention is reading the sheet and the criterion descriptors with the student and planning an approach. That is one session and it determines most of the eventual mark, because a task planned against the descriptor scores better than a task written well and aimed at nothing in particular.

In the middle, while the student is researching or making or drafting, a session adds little and competes with the work itself. This is the stage to leave alone. Near the end, once a draft exists, a session reviewing what the student has written against the descriptor is genuinely useful, and it is the point at which a 4 out of 8 often becomes a 6. After submission, a short conversation about the returned mark closes the loop and sets up the next cycle.

The practical consequence is that a weekly fixed slot is less useful in MYP than it is at Diploma level, and a flexible arrangement anchored to task cycles is better. We ask for the school's assessment calendar if one exists, or the task sheet as soon as it is issued, and place the session at the stage where it does the work. That is more administration for us and it is the difference between a mark moving and an hour passing.

sections.heading: When a session fits after the school run
paragraphs: The timing chain for an MYP student is the same as for anyone else and the consequences are sharper, because the window it leads into is shorter. When the school day ends, how long the journey home takes at that hour, how long a younger child needs to eat and settle, and therefore when a session can begin while the child is still able to contribute.

Read the table and the pattern is clear. A student at a school inside the district or in Nad Al Sheba comfortably makes a four o'clock session, which is inside the usable window with room to spare. A student travelling from the western cluster is home around a quarter past four, ready at about twenty to five, and a forty-minute session then finishes at around twenty past five, which is just inside the window. Add an in-home tutor's own journey and the same session starts at a quarter past five and finishes at six, which for a twelve-year-old is past the point of value.

That is the clearest practical argument for online delivery in this age group, and it has nothing to do with teaching quality. The forty-five minutes an in-home arrangement costs at each end is tolerable for a Diploma student and decisive for an MYP student, because it is drawn from a window that is only an hour or so wide to begin with.

The last row of the table is the one households should check first. A club, a sport fixture or a music lesson removes the usable window entirely on that day for a younger child, and a session pushed to six o'clock on that evening is not a session in any useful sense. Move it to another day. If no day is free before half past five, a weekend morning is a better answer than a late weekday hour.

sections.heading: Why criterion work needs drafting evenings, and how many
paragraphs: MYP marks are earned by work the student produces against published descriptors, which means the improvement happens while they are drafting rather than while a tutor is talking. A household planning tutoring therefore needs to plan drafting evenings as deliberately as session evenings, and in a week with a journey home this long that is a real constraint rather than a formality.

The mechanism is simple and almost never explained to students. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of 8, giving a total out of 32 that converts to the reported 1 to 7 grade by published boundaries. A student who writes a task without reading the descriptor is guessing at what is wanted and will usually land around the middle. A student who reads the descriptor, drafts, compares the draft to the descriptor and revises once will usually land a band or two higher for the same subject knowledge.

That second version requires two drafting sessions of the student's own, spaced a few days apart, with the revision happening after feedback rather than in the same sitting. So a task cycle needs roughly three evenings of the student's time and one or two tutoring sessions, placed at the start and after the draft exists. A household that books a weekly hour and leaves no drafting evenings has bought the smaller half of the process.

The practical rule is to protect two evenings per task cycle for the student's own work, and to keep those evenings free of tutoring rather than filling them. In a district where the journey home already costs an hour, that sometimes means accepting one tutoring session per cycle instead of one per week, which is cheaper and works better. We will say so rather than selling the weekly slot.

sections.heading: The Personal Project in MYP 5, and the calendar it needs
paragraphs: The Personal Project reshapes the MYP 5 year, and scheduling it badly is the commonest reason a capable student produces a weak one. It is a long independent piece assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal and a report as the evidence, and it runs alongside subject tasks rather than replacing them.

Two scheduling facts matter more than anything else. The first is that the process journal is contemporaneous evidence: it has to be kept as the work happens, in short entries across months, not written up in a weekend near the deadline. A student who understands that in September has a far easier year than one who discovers it in February. Explaining it is a single session and it belongs at the very start.

The second is that the goal has to be achievable in the time the week actually contains. An over-ambitious goal is the usual cause of a poor project, and in a district where the journey home consumes an hour a day, ambition has to be calibrated against a genuinely narrow weekly window. One conversation questioning the goal until it is specific and achievable is the highest-value hour in the whole project, and it costs almost nothing.

After those two, the project needs protected evenings rather than tutoring sessions. Three or four short process-coaching sessions across the year is the right volume: one at the start on the goal and the journal, one at the planning stage, one when a draft report exists, and perhaps one before submission. Filling the deadline weeks with sessions produces a tired student and, at worst, the pressure in which help gets accepted that should not be.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and a school day that is fuller than it looks
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspection on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. For an MYP family the relevant part of a report is the middle-phase commentary rather than the headline band, because a school strong at primary or Diploma level is not automatically strong in between.

The scheduling fact is the mandatory UAE subjects, which run alongside MYP rather than instead of it, and which families new to Dubai routinely underestimate. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. It also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. KHDA also requires that school teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential question for a school rather than for a tutoring service. For an MYP student the effect is a fuller school day, more work coming home, and a usable evening window under more pressure than the programme on paper suggests.

On our own position, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, which is a different thing entirely from an individual tutor or an online matching service.

sections.heading: What a tutor must not do with a Personal Project or any MYP task
paragraphs: The pressure that produces academic-honesty problems is built out of calendars, which is why this section sits on a scheduling page. A student with a Personal Project report due in ten days, an empty process journal and no free evenings is the student most likely to accept help they should not accept, and at least one operator ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed assessed work at a published price.

What a tutor legitimately does is explain the criteria in the language the school is using, question a goal or a task focus until it is specific and achievable, explain that a process journal is contemporaneous evidence rather than something written up at the end, teach a skill the task depends on, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. That is substantial help and it is what the sessions on this page are for.

What a tutor may not do is choose the goal or the focus, make or contribute to the product, supply content for the report, write or edit the text, or fabricate journal entries. We state all of that to the student directly in the first session rather than burying it, because at fifteen the pressure arrives later and a boundary explained under deadline is explained too late to help.

The scheduling remedy is to protect the deadline weeks rather than fill them, and to place the valuable conversations early: the goal, the journal, the criteria. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides or assessment materials; we reference them and point to the school's own copies, which are the versions that apply to your child's cohort.

sections.heading: Getting started, and the four things we ask before proposing a time
paragraphs: Four questions decide the arrangement for a younger student, and we ask them before proposing anyone. Which school, and what time the day ends. What fixed commitments sit in the week, including clubs and music. Which subject group and MYP year. And whether there is a Diploma sibling competing for the same window, because if there is, the MYP child should usually get the earlier slot.

Then the useful documents: the criterion breakdown behind the last reported grade if the school provides it, the teacher's last comment quoted rather than summarised, and the school's own task sheet for the most recent piece of work. Task design varies between schools under the same programme, so the sheet your child was actually given tells us more than any description of MYP does.

We run a free trial lesson at the time you would really use and at the length we think suits the year, which for MYP 1 or 2 means forty minutes rather than an hour. Afterwards, ask for a criterion-level account in writing: not that your child should read more, but that the marks are going on criterion C because notation is informal, or on criterion D because the evaluation restates the method.

And the honest part. MYP coverage is thinner across this market than Diploma or IGCSE coverage, and thinnest in Design, Arts, Physical and Health Education and Language Acquisition beyond the commonly taught languages. Early slots in this district fill first and MYP families often lose them to Diploma families. When nothing suitable is free we say so and offer another hour, a weekend morning, or a tutor based outside the UAE with genuine MYP experience working to Gulf Standard Time.

process.description: The journey home plus a younger student's shorter window decides both the slot and the session length. A forty-minute session at four o'clock and a sixty-minute session at six are not two versions of the same purchase.

process.title: Say whether a Diploma sibling is competing for the evening
process.description: If one is, the MYP child should usually get the earlier slot, because capacity falls away sooner at twelve than at seventeen. Households rarely allocate it that way without being prompted, and it is free to change.

process.title: Send the task sheet and the criterion breakdown
process.description: Task design varies between schools under the same programme, and the criterion marks behind a reported grade turn a vague worry into a named target. Both are more useful to us than the grade on its own.

process.title: Place the session at the start of a task cycle
process.description: Reading the descriptors and planning the approach determines most of the eventual mark. A session in the middle of the cycle competes with the work itself, and one in the submission week is too late to change anything.

process.description: We run the trial in the hour you intend to use and at the length that suits the year. Afterwards, ask for the criterion-level account in writing and judge how specific it is rather than how the session felt.

whyPoints.description: Forty minutes in MYP 1 and 2, an hour by MYP 4. A child who finishes a session still engaged comes back willingly; one who endures the last twenty minutes learns that tutoring is to be survived, which is expensive a year later.

whyPoints.title: Placed in the task cycle, not the diary
whyPoints.description: MYP sets tasks in bursts rather than homework nightly, so a session at the start of a cycle is worth three near the deadline. We ask for the task sheet and place the hour where it changes the mark.

whyPoints.title: The younger child gets the early slot
whyPoints.description: Where a Diploma sibling competes for the same window we recommend giving it to the MYP student, because a seventeen-year-old can still work at seven and a twelve-year-old cannot. It costs nothing and almost nobody suggests it.

whyPoints.title: Drafting evenings protected

whyPoints.title: No journey at either end
whyPoints.description: An in-home arrangement costs about forty-five minutes at each end in this district, which is tolerable for a Diploma student and decisive for an MYP student whose usable window is only an hour or so wide.

whyPoints.description: Process coaching only, explained in the first session rather than in small print: the goal, the product, the journal and the report are entirely the student's own, and the pressure that tests that arrives later.

faqs.question: Is a full hour too much for a Year 7 or Year 8 student?
faqs.answer: Forty minutes in MYP 1 and 2, forty-five to sixty in MYP 3, and a full hour by MYP 4 and 5. Attention rather than content is the constraint in the early years, and a child who finishes a session still contributing will come back to the next one willingly. One who endures the last twenty minutes of an hour learns that tutoring is something to be survived, which costs you more a year later than the shorter session would have saved.

faqs.question: What is the latest a session should start for a twelve-year-old here?
faqs.answer: Around a quarter to five, and earlier is better. A younger student's usable working window closes near half past five, and the journey home from the western school cluster can consume most of the time before it. A student at a school inside the district or in Nad Al Sheba comfortably makes a four o'clock start. One travelling from Al Barsha is ready at about twenty to five, which leaves room for forty minutes and not for an hour.

faqs.question: Would a tutor come to the house for MYP work?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. For a younger student the online structure matters more than it does at Diploma level, because an in-home arrangement costs about forty-five minutes at each end in this district and that time comes out of a window only an hour or so wide. Local in-home tutors exist here, and in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel.

faqs.question: My MYP child and my Diploma child both need help. Who gets the early slot?
faqs.answer: The younger one, in almost every case, and households rarely arrange it that way without being prompted. A seventeen-year-old can still do useful work at seven in the evening; a twelve-year-old cannot. Give the MYP student the first slot after they are home and settled, and put the Diploma student's session afterwards, choosing a subject for them that survives a later hour, such as Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay discussion or an essay subject rather than timed mathematics.

faqs.question: Does a weekly fixed slot make sense for MYP?
faqs.answer: Less than it does for Diploma or IGCSE. MYP sets tasks in bursts rather than homework nightly, so a fixed weekly hour sometimes arrives with nothing to work on and sometimes arrives in a week with three things due. An arrangement anchored to task cycles works better: one session when the task sheet is issued, to read the descriptors and plan, and one once a draft exists. That is often one or two sessions per cycle rather than four a month.

faqs.question: When in a task cycle is a session actually worth booking?
faqs.answer: At the start, and again once a draft exists. Reading the task sheet and the criterion descriptors with the student and planning the approach determines most of the eventual mark, because a task aimed at the descriptor scores better than a task written well and aimed at nothing. In the middle, while the student researches or makes or drafts, a session competes with the work itself. In the submission week it is too late to change anything and the evenings should be protected.

faqs.question: How many evenings does an MYP task actually need?
faqs.answer: Roughly three of the student's own, spread across the cycle, plus one or two tutoring sessions. The drafting and the revision after feedback have to happen on different evenings to be real, because revising in the same sitting as writing produces tidying rather than improvement. In a district where the journey home already costs an hour a day, that means protecting two drafting evenings per cycle and keeping them free of tutoring rather than filling them with it.

faqs.question: What are the four MYP criteria and how do they become a grade?
faqs.answer: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D and differing by subject group, with each marked out of 8. The four give a total out of 32, which converts to the reported 1 to 7 grade using published boundaries. Because the conversion is not proportional, one weak criterion holds a grade down more than parents expect. That is encouraging, because a single named criterion is the most tractable thing in the programme and usually moves in three to five sessions.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for an eleven or twelve-year-old?
faqs.answer: It works with one condition: an adult in the house, not in the room, for the first few sessions, so the child knows help is available if something technical goes wrong. Beyond that, younger students often engage well because a shared screen gives them something concrete to work on. The honest counterpoint is that presence matters more at eleven than at seventeen, so if your child genuinely needs someone beside them, a local arrangement is better and we will say so.

faqs.question: When should Personal Project support happen in MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Early, and then sparingly. Two conversations do most of the work: one at the very start explaining that the process journal is contemporaneous evidence to be kept in short entries across months rather than written up near the deadline, and one questioning the goal until it is achievable in the time the week actually contains. After those, three or four short process-coaching sessions across the year is the right volume, with the deadline weeks protected rather than filled with appointments.

faqs.question: My child's interdisciplinary unit mark was much lower than their others. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because nobody explained that the integration itself is being assessed, with its own criteria. A student who produces good work in each discipline separately, without connecting them, is answering a question that was not asked. It is typically a single-session fix once they see what is being marked, and the session belongs as soon as the task is set rather than after the mark comes back. It is worth asking about specifically, because the mark often sits oddly low on an otherwise consistent report.

faqs.question: Does MYP have examinations, and does that change the schedule?
faqs.answer: Most MYP assessment is internal and criterion-based with no external papers. Some schools additionally enter students for the IB's optional MYP eAssessment, which combines on-screen examinations and ePortfolios and leads to the MYP Certificate. Where it applies, the on-screen format and timing are unfamiliar and need rehearsing, which adds a short block to the MYP 5 calendar. Whether a school enters varies school by school and sometimes year by year, so confirm it with the MYP coordinator.

faqs.question: Why is the school day fuller than the MYP timetable suggests?
faqs.answer: Because the mandatory UAE subjects run alongside it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. The effect for an MYP student is more work coming home into an evening window that was already narrow.

faqs.question: Is a weekend morning better than a weekday session for a younger child?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is underused. A Saturday morning reaches a rested child with no journey at either end and no competition from a club, which for a longer task-planning session in MYP 4 or 5 is a real advantage. The drawback is that weekend slots are easier to cancel than a weekday routine. For MYP 1 to 3 the better answer is usually a short early weekday session, because frequency and routine matter more than length at that age.

faqs.question: What if no early slot is available when we ask?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than selling a six o'clock hour to a twelve-year-old. The alternatives are a different weekday with a free early window, a weekend morning, a shorter session that fits what remains, or a tutor based outside the UAE with genuine MYP experience working to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed as such. MYP coverage is also thinner than Diploma coverage overall, and thinnest in Design, Arts, Physical and Health Education and the less common languages, which we flag before you book.

faqs.question: What should I send to get a useful recommendation for an MYP student?
faqs.answer: Four things about the week and two about the work. The school and the time the day ends; the fixed commitments including clubs and music; the MYP year; and whether a Diploma sibling is competing for the same evening. Then the criterion breakdown behind the last reported grade if the school provides it, and the school's own task sheet for the most recent piece of work, because task design varies between schools under the same programme.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-rashi.closingHeading: Short, early, and placed where the task cycle needs it
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-rashi.closingBody: MYP tutoring works when the session is the right length for the age, early enough that the child is still able to contribute, and placed at the stage of a task cycle where it changes the mark. Tell us the school and the finishing time, the MYP year, the fixed commitments and whether an older sibling is competing for the same hour. Send the last task sheet and the criterion marks behind the grade, and we will propose a tutor and run the trial at the time and length we think fits.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-motor-city.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach MYP subjects against the published criteria for students at the IB continuum schools serving the Motor City area, including Personal Project supervision and the preparation that belongs in the summer before DP1.

intro.heading: Continuous assessment means the timing is the whole problem
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme has no terminal examination for most students, which sounds like relief and is actually a different kind of pressure. Instead of one window at the end, assessment happens continuously: each subject assesses against four criteria across the year, each task is marked against descriptors, and the grade at the end is a conversion of what accumulated. There is no catch-up term and no final push that can rescue a year, because by the time a report shows a problem the tasks that produced it have been marked and filed. That is not a criticism of the programme, which is designed to assess learning as it happens, but it does mean a family reacting to reports is permanently one cycle behind the thing they are reacting to.

That changes the tutoring question from what to buy to when to act. A family that reads a December report and intervenes in January is acting on information about September and October. The criterion that was weak has probably already been assessed twice more by then. Acting earlier requires knowing the cycle rather than waiting for the report, and the cycle is knowable: schools publish assessment calendars, and subject teachers will say which criterion the next task carries if asked.

The second timing problem is the Personal Project, which runs across the final MYP year and is assessed on a documented process rather than on a product. A project begun in earnest in the term it is due cannot have a contemporaneous process journal, because the process already happened unrecorded. That is a scheduling failure that reads as a criterion failure, and it is the single most common Personal Project problem in this corridor.

The third is the transition out. A Year 11 MYP student moving into DP1 has a predictable gap — strong reasoning and communication, slower procedural execution — and the long holiday before DP1 is the cheapest window in the whole continuum to close it. Almost nobody uses it, and the same work in October costs more and achieves less because the student is simultaneously keeping up with new content.

Motor City's position is worth noting. GEMS Metropole School inside the community runs a British curriculum, so MYP students here attend the continuum schools across the Dubailand corridor — Fairgreen International School and Greenfield International School principally — and commute. That puts realistic session starts at about 17:00, and it means the moments described on this page have to be planned around a drive rather than slotted in after school. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, sessions run 45 or 60 minutes to 21:00, and there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-motor-city.programmesIntro: The MYP sits between the Primary Years Programme and the Diploma, and the calendar changes completely at each boundary. These three stages cover the continuum enquiries from the Motor City area.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led across six transdisciplinary themes, with no external examinations and continuous teacher assessment ending in the Year 6 Exhibition. Reporting is descriptive rather than numerical, so the arrival of criteria and achievement levels in Year 7 is the first time a continuum parent sees a number and has to learn to read one.
programmes.countryNote: Primary-age families around Motor City most often have children at Victory Heights Primary School or Bradenton Preparatory Academy in Dubai Sports City. Where the plan is an IB continuum, the Year 6 into Year 7 holiday is the right window for written-structure work, before criterion-referenced marking begins.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups across five years, each assessed against four criteria scored from 0 to 8, with the criterion total out of 32 converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. Assessment is internal and continuous unless the school uses MYP eAssessment in the final year, and the Personal Project runs across that final year.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students near Motor City attend Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City or Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, since GEMS Metropole School inside the community runs a British curriculum. That commute puts realistic session starts at about 17:00 and makes the later slots the busiest.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six examined subjects at Higher and Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, graded out of 45. The assessment model inverts: external examinations carry most of the weight, each subject has an internally assessed component worth 20-25%, and criterion-referenced feedback gives way to papers and mark schemes.
programmes.countryNote: The step into DP1 is the most common reason a Motor City family calls about MYP, usually in Year 11 and usually too late to use the best window. MYP builds reasoning and communication and drills procedural execution less, so eight to twelve sessions in the summer before DP1 closes most of the gap.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-motor-city.subjectsIntro: MYP subject groups as they appear in an assessment calendar, with a note on when each one's weaker criteria tend to be assessed. Knowing the timing is what makes early intervention possible.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria are Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns and Applying usually arrive via a longer task set once or twice a year, which means a weak level in either is visible rarely and late.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria are Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science. The middle two arrive through practical write-ups clustered at particular points in the year rather than spread evenly.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria are Analysing, Organising, Producing text, and Using language. Assessed frequently through written tasks, which makes this the subject where a weak criterion shows soonest and where early intervention is most straightforward.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Students progress by phase rather than year group, so a phase change mid-year resets expectations and is a moment worth watching.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria are Knowing and understanding, Investigating, Communicating, and Thinking critically. Investigating and Thinking critically usually arrive through extended research tasks placed at a particular point in the unit cycle, so the opportunity to prepare is finite and datable.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria are Inquiring and analysing, Developing ideas, Creating the solution, and Evaluating. Assessed across a design cycle that spans weeks, so the documentation requirement starts long before the product does and is where marks are usually conceded.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria are Knowing and understanding, Developing skills, Thinking creatively, and Responding. The process journal is assessed alongside the final piece, which means the recording has to be contemporaneous and cannot be assembled at the end of a unit.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and reflective components surprise students who expect a practical subject to be assessed only practically.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against interdisciplinary criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting, and usually placed at a fixed point in the school year. Students default to presenting two separate pieces of subject work side by side, which evidences grounding and almost nothing for synthesising.

sections.heading: The rolling criterion cycle, and why a report arrives too late
paragraphs: In the MYP each subject assesses against four criteria across the year, but not evenly and not simultaneously. A unit will carry one or two criteria, the next unit another combination, and across a year every criterion gets assessed at least once and usually more. The grade reported at the end is a conversion of the accumulated levels, which means the reported number is a summary of events rather than a forecast.

The practical consequence is that a report is historical. A December report describing a weak Communicating level in mathematics is describing tasks set in September and October. By the time a family reads it and arranges help in January, the next Communicating task may already have been set or sat. Acting on reports alone means always working one cycle behind, which is why MYP tutoring so often feels like it is not landing.

The alternative is to work from the assessment calendar rather than from the report. Most schools publish one, and where they do not, a subject teacher will usually say which criteria the next unit carries if asked directly. With that information, two or three sessions can be placed before a task rather than six after it, which is both cheaper and effective. A student who knows that the next science task is assessed on Inquiring and designing can practise writing a testable hypothesis with justified variables in advance.

This is also the answer to a question families ask constantly, which is why MYP tutoring is hard to judge. It is hard to judge because the feedback loop is long and the data is retrospective. Shortening the loop — by working to the calendar, by asking which criterion is next, by reading the descriptor for the level above before the task rather than after it — is most of what good MYP support consists of.

sections.heading: The Personal Project as a year-long calendar
paragraphs: The Personal Project is assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and the process journal, and it runs across the whole final MYP year with checkpoints set by the school. The single most important thing to understand about it is that the documented process carries more than the product does, which means the project cannot be compressed. A student who does all the work in the final term has a product and no contemporaneous record of how it came about, and the criteria are written to detect exactly that.

The year has a shape. The first stage is choosing and narrowing a goal, and it should be finished within the first few weeks. The failure here is ambition: students choose the most impressive thing they can imagine, and the ambition then consumes the time that should have gone into documentation. The useful intervention is to narrow the goal until it is genuinely achievable in the time available and genuinely documentable step by step.

The middle stages are doing the work and recording it as it happens. The process journal is not a diary and not a scrapbook to be made presentable at the end: it is evidence of decisions made and why, sources consulted and what they changed, problems met and how they were addressed, and skills attempted and how they developed. Reviewing it monthly against the criteria — rather than reading it once at the end — is what keeps it usable.

The final stage is the report, and by then most of the marks are already determined by what the journal contains. A tutor's role across the whole year is narrow and specific: question the goal until it is achievable, explain what each criterion credits using the published descriptors, review the journal for missing criterion evidence, teach a research or referencing skill, and give feedback on a report draft the student wrote. A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product, write any part of the report, or help construct the journal retrospectively.

sections.heading: Five moments in an MYP year worth acting on
paragraphs: Because MYP support is about timing, it helps to name the moments that actually repay intervention. There are five, and outside them an open-ended weekly slot for an MYP student is usually a subscription rather than a plan. A provider who proposes one for a Year 8 student with a single weak criterion should be asked what the endpoint is.

The first is the arrival of criteria in Year 7, for a student coming from the PYP or from a different system. Learning to read a report that gives four numbers out of eight, and learning that a low Communicating level is not a content problem, saves two years of misdirected effort. One or two sessions with the parent as much as the student.

The second is a confirmed weak criterion with a known next task, which is where pre-task preparation belongs. The third is a phase change in Language Acquisition or a set change in mathematics, both of which reset expectations mid-year and often produce a dip that looks like regression and is actually recalibration. The fourth is the start of the Personal Project year, in the first few weeks, where narrowing the goal is worth more than any later help.

The fifth is the summer before DP1, which is the largest single opportunity in the continuum and the least used. A student who spends eight to twelve sessions in July and August on procedural execution starts DP1 able to keep pace; the same student starting in October is behind on new content as well as adapting to a new assessment model, and the work takes longer and costs more. Outside these five, the honest answer is often that no tutoring is needed yet.

sections.heading: The summer before DP1, in detail
paragraphs: This is the section worth reading twice if a Motor City family has a Year 11 MYP student. The step into the Diploma is a change in assessment model rather than in difficulty, and it is entirely predictable. MYP mathematics rewards investigating patterns and communicating reasoning; Diploma Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and rewards accurate manipulation at speed. MYP sciences reward inquiry and design; Diploma science papers reward naming a principle and applying it inside a time limit. MYP humanities reward sustained analysis; Diploma Paper 1 is guided analysis of an unseen text under examination conditions.

In every case the student has the thinking and not the execution, which is good news because execution is the more teachable of the two. What it needs is volume and a clock, neither of which the MYP has required of them. Eight to twelve sessions across July and August on indices, surds, rearrangement and function notation for mathematics, on moles, concentration and unit prefixes for the sciences, and on writing a timed analytical paragraph for the humanities, closes most of the gap.

The reason the summer specifically is that nothing competes for it. During term, a student doing this work is also keeping up with new Diploma content, managing six subjects plus the core, and adjusting to a new school in many cases. In July they are doing one thing. Ten sessions in the holiday routinely achieve more than twenty in October, and they cost less because fewer are needed.

The secondary benefit is confidence, which is not a marketing point in this context but a measurable one. A student who arrives in DP1 able to execute at the expected pace engages with new content differently from one who is immediately behind. The first set of marked DP1 papers then confirms competence rather than establishing a problem, and the whole two years start from a different place.

sections.heading: Reporting cycles, parents' evenings and what to ask
paragraphs: A Dubai MYP school typically reports two or three times a year with a parents' evening attached to at least one. Those are the formal information points and they are usually used badly, because the conversation defaults to how the term has gone rather than to anything actionable. Three questions change that, and they take two minutes each.

The first is which criterion is lowest and what the descriptor for the level above says. That converts a number into a target with wording attached, and the wording is what a student can actually work towards. The second is which criteria the next unit assesses, which is the information that makes pre-task preparation possible instead of retrospective repair. The third is what evidence the teacher would need to see to award the next level, which is a more precise question than asking how the student can improve.

For the Personal Project year, add a fourth: what the next checkpoint requires and by when. Schools set those dates and they are the ones that actually bind, and a family who has them written down in the first term of the final year can place supervision sessions before each rather than after the fact.

One further note on comparability, because it affects how a report should be read. MYP assessment is internal and continuous, awarded by the school against published descriptors, with internal moderation and IB guidance but no external examiner calibrating one school's level 6 against another's. That is a deliberate design feature rather than a flaw, but it means the descriptors matter more than the number, and a sixth-form or Diploma conversation about MYP grades usually needs the descriptors alongside them.

sections.heading: The Dubai academic year and where MYP work fits
paragraphs: A UAE academic year has its own rhythm — a long summer break, National Day, a winter break, a spring break and the Ramadan period — and MYP work fits it differently from examination-year work. There is no terminal series to count back from, which removes one pressure and removes one organising principle with it. The result is that MYP support drifts unless it is pinned to something.

The long summer break is the most valuable window and it is valuable twice: once for the Year 6 into Year 7 transition, where written structure can be built before criterion marking begins, and once for the Year 11 into DP1 transition described above. Both are periods when nothing competes, and both are almost entirely unused by the families who would benefit most.

During term, work should be pinned to the assessment calendar rather than spread evenly. Two or three sessions before a known task in a weak criterion is the model. The winter and spring breaks are short and often involve travel, so they suit a single catch-up on one named thing rather than an ambitious plan. The Ramadan period shortens the school day and moves the productive window to after Iftar, which suits review and reflective work — and for the Personal Project specifically, it is a good period for writing up journal entries and reflecting, which is exactly the criterion work that gets neglected.

Sessions move to post-Iftar timing, typically 20:30 to 22:00 on Gulf Standard Time, on request and at no additional cost. Because every session is recorded, a rescheduled or missed week loses nothing in content, which matters more at MYP age where a student is more likely to rewatch an explanation than to ask for it twice.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs, timed rather than continuous
paragraphs: MYP support should cost less than Diploma support because the right shapes are short and timed, not continuous. The published Dubai bands, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 150-300 for qualified online subject tutors, AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one and AED 200-450 or above for IB and IGCSE specialists, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is included; TutorChase at AED 270; BartyED at AED 650.

The five moments described above cost what the table below shows, and what it makes visible is that the whole of an MYP year's sensible support frequently comes to fewer sessions than a single term of a weekly slot. A pre-task block is two or three sessions. A criteria explanation session is one. Personal Project supervision is four to six spread across a year. The summer before DP1 is the largest single purchase at eight to twelve, and it is the one with the clearest return.

Against that, an open-ended weekly slot for a Year 8 student with one weak criterion is thirty or more sessions a year at AED 150-300, which is AED 4,500-9,000 for a problem that two or three well-timed sessions would have addressed. We say that even though the subscription bills better, because the alternative is a family paying for attention the student does not need and then having no budget left for the summer before DP1, which they do.

IB Gram publishes no fixed hourly rate on this page because subject, level and urgency move it, and a quote follows the free diagnostic lesson. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total.

sections.heading: Starting, with the scheduling and the footnotes
paragraphs: Send the report with the four achievement levels per subject, the school's assessment calendar if you have it, and — in the final MYP year — the Personal Project checkpoint dates. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson against the relevant criterion descriptors and sends a written note within a working day naming which of the five moments you are at and what, if anything, is worth buying. Nothing is charged before you read it, and sometimes the honest note says to wait.

Availability is good across MYP mathematics, the sciences, language and literature, and individuals and societies, with a match normally inside one to three working days. Language acquisition in a minority language, some arts and design specialisms, and Personal Project supervision for an unusual goal are thinner and may need a subject match rather than a general one. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, the tutor comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking.

Scheduling from Motor City: MYP students commute to the continuum schools across the Dubailand corridor, so sessions start at about 17:00, with slots to 21:00 on Gulf Standard Time for families whose early evening is taken. Sessions run 45 or 60 minutes and are recorded, which matters at this age. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing, typically 20:30 to 22:00, which suits review and journal work well.

And the claims we do not make. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and has no UAE office or centre. Private tutoring is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

faqs.question: Why does acting on an MYP report always feel too late?
faqs.answer: Because it is. MYP assessment is continuous, so a report is a summary of a period that has already closed. A December report describing a weak Communicating level is describing tasks set in September and October, and by the time help is arranged in January the next task in that criterion may already have been set. The alternative is to work from the school's assessment calendar, or simply to ask the subject teacher which criteria the next unit carries, so two or three sessions can land before the marking rather than after it.

faqs.question: What should I ask at an MYP parents' evening?
faqs.answer: Three questions, two minutes each. Which criterion is lowest, and what does the descriptor for the level above say — that turns a number out of eight into a target with wording attached. Which criteria does the next unit assess — that is the information that makes preparation possible instead of repair. And what evidence would the teacher need to see to award the next level — a more precise question than asking how the student can improve. In the Personal Project year, add a request for the checkpoint dates in writing.

faqs.question: When should the Personal Project actually start?
faqs.answer: In the first few weeks of the final MYP year, and the goal should be narrowed almost immediately. The criteria assess planning, applying skills, reflecting and the process journal, which means the documented process carries more than the product does. A student who does the work in the final term has a product and no contemporaneous record of how it came about, and the criteria are written to detect exactly that. Narrowing the goal until it is achievable and documentable is the single highest-value intervention available.

faqs.question: Can the process journal be written up at the end of the project?
faqs.answer: It can be, and it reads as what it is. The journal is assessed as evidence of decisions made and why, sources consulted and what they changed, problems met and how they were addressed, and skills attempted and how they developed. A retrospective account cannot contain the dead ends, the changes of direction or the dated reasoning that make it evidence, and the criteria credit precisely those. Reviewing the journal monthly against the descriptors while the work is happening is what keeps it usable, and it takes very little time.

faqs.question: Why did my child's MYP level drop after a phase change?
faqs.answer: Because the expectations reset rather than because the student regressed. In Language Acquisition students progress through phases rather than year groups, and a move to a higher phase means the same performance is measured against more demanding descriptors. The same effect appears after a set change in mathematics. It looks like a dip and it is a recalibration, and two or three sessions of work against the new phase's descriptors usually settles it. Worth asking the teacher to confirm a phase change has happened before concluding anything else.

faqs.question: Is there any point tutoring an MYP student with no exams coming?
faqs.answer: At five specific moments, yes, and outside them often not. The five are: criteria arriving in Year 7 for a student new to the system; a confirmed weak criterion with a known next task; a phase or set change mid-year; the first few weeks of the Personal Project year; and the summer before DP1. Each of those has a defined purchase of one to twelve sessions. An open-ended weekly slot for a Year 8 student with a single weak criterion is a subscription rather than a plan, and we will say so.

faqs.question: How much does a year of MYP support actually need to cost?
faqs.answer: Frequently less than one term of a weekly slot. A criteria explanation session is one session, AED 150-450 at published bands. A pre-task block is three. Personal Project supervision is four to six spread across a year. The largest purchase is the summer before DP1 at eight to twelve sessions. Against that, a weekly slot across a year is thirty or more sessions, which at AED 150-300 is AED 4,500-9,000 for something two or three well-timed sessions would often have addressed.

faqs.question: What exactly should we do in the summer before DP1?
faqs.answer: Procedural execution, because that is what the Diploma assumes and the MYP does not drill. For mathematics: indices, surds, rearrangement and function notation, since Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. For the sciences: moles, concentration, unit prefixes and significant figures. For the humanities and language: writing a timed analytical paragraph against a clock rather than against a criterion. Eight to twelve sessions, with nothing competing for the time, and it routinely achieves more than twenty sessions in October.

faqs.question: Why is the summer window better than term time for the DP1 step?
faqs.answer: Because in July a student is doing one thing. During term they are keeping up with new Diploma content, managing six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, and in many cases adjusting to a new school. The same procedural work then has to compete with all of that and takes longer. There is also a confidence effect that is measurable rather than rhetorical: the first set of marked DP1 papers confirms competence instead of establishing a problem, and the two years start differently.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect MYP work specifically?
faqs.answer: Favourably, if the work is chosen to suit it. School hours shorten and the productive window moves to after Iftar, which does not suit new content or long tasks but does suit review and reflection. For a Personal Project student that is close to ideal: writing up journal entries, reflecting on what a stage produced, and preparing for a checkpoint are exactly the activities that fit a short post-Iftar session. Sessions move to 20:30 to 22:00 on Gulf Standard Time on request, at no additional cost, and every session is recorded.

faqs.question: If two MYP subjects are weak, should we use one tutor for both?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and for MYP the question arises less often than families expect, because the right purchases are short and single-subject rather than continuous across several. Where a student does need work in two subject groups at once — mathematics and sciences, say — one tutor covering both is better, because the criteria overlap conceptually and the student re-explains less context. Ask directly which subject groups a tutor has taught in the MYP specifically, because criterion-referenced marking is a different skill from teaching the same content in an examined system.

faqs.question: Where do MYP students near Motor City go to school?
faqs.answer: Out of the community. GEMS Metropole School inside Motor City runs a British curriculum, so MYP students commute to the continuum schools across the Dubailand corridor — principally Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City and Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, with Nord Anglia International School Dubai, North London Collegiate School Dubai and Emirates International School Meadows also within range. That commute puts realistic session starts at about 17:00. We name schools as market context and hold no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: Are MYP grades from different Dubai schools comparable?
faqs.answer: Not in the way an examination grade is. MYP assessment is internal and continuous, awarded by the school against published descriptors, with internal moderation and IB guidance but no external examiner calibrating one school's level 6 against another's. That is a deliberate design feature rather than a flaw, but it has a practical consequence: the descriptors are more informative than the number, and a conversation with a receiving school about MYP grades usually needs the descriptors alongside them.

faqs.question: Does an MYP tutor come to the house in Motor City?
faqs.answer: Not from us. Home visits exist in the Dubai market at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included, and for a Year 7 or 8 student who cannot yet self-manage a screen there is a genuine case for one. IB Gram delivers UAE tuition one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and runs home visits only in India. Sessions are 45 or 60 minutes, start from about 17:00 after the commute, and are recorded.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-motor-city.closingBody: Two things would improve most MYP outcomes in this part of Dubai and neither is a weekly slot. Get the school's assessment calendar, find out which criteria the next units carry, and place two or three sessions before a task instead of six after a report — because continuous assessment means a report always arrives after the window to influence it has closed. And if your child is in Year 11, book the summer before DP1: eight to twelve sessions on procedural execution while nothing competes for the time. Send the report and the calendar, and take the free diagnostic lesson.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mudon.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work with Middle Years Programme students across the subject groups most requested from Dubailand. Each profile names the subject group and year level, because a Year 7 criterion conversation and a Year 11 one are different pieces of work.

intro.heading: A criterion mark is not a percentage, and that is the whole problem
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme reports differently from every other system a family in Dubai is likely to have met. Each subject group is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each marked out of eight, and those marks are converted to a 1 to 7 grade through published boundaries. A 5 on Criterion C does not mean five eighths of the content was learned. It means the work demonstrated a specific level of a specific skill, described in a descriptor the student has probably never read.

That misreading causes most of the anxiety. A parent sees a 4 and assumes a content gap, so they ask for more teaching of the topic. The descriptor often says something else entirely: that the student described where the task asked them to analyse, or applied a method without justifying the choice, or communicated a finding without using the subject's own conventions. Teaching more content does not move that mark, because the mark was never about content.

Mudon families meet the MYP in two ways. Some arrive at it in Year 7 after a British-curriculum primary, which is the most common route in this belt, and the first reporting cycle is where the confusion starts. Others are in a continuum school from Primary Years upward and the language is familiar, in which case the questions are about the later years and the Personal Project. The community sits off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand with no school inside its own boundary, so students travel to Fairgreen International in The Sustainable City, GEMS International School Al Khail, Nord Anglia in Al Barsha South or elsewhere.

The useful work is therefore narrow and quite unlike exam coaching. It is reading the actual descriptors next to the student's own marked task, naming the gap in the terms the descriptor uses, and practising that one skill until the next task shows it. Students are usually relieved by this, because a criterion gap is specific and closeable, while a vague sense of being bad at a subject is neither.

There is a second reason families in this belt ask about the MYP specifically. Middle Years provision around Dubailand is thinner than IGCSE provision, so choosing it often means a longer school run and a school whose reporting looks nothing like the one a neighbour's child brings home. Comparing the two systems becomes unavoidable at Year 6 and again at Year 9, and the comparison is hard to make when one side of it is written in a vocabulary the family has never been taught. Half of this page exists to supply that vocabulary.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so a session can sit early for a student home from Al Khail or later where both parents commute. For this age group shorter sessions often work better than a full hour. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and nothing here should be read as an offer to arrive at a Mudon door.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-mudon.subjectsIntro: These are the MYP subject groups most often requested from this part of Dubailand, with the criterion each one tends to lose marks on.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Four criteria covering knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the usual weak point, because it rewards generalising and justifying rather than reaching an answer.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Students lose marks on designing a method another person could follow and on evaluating rather than concluding.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. The critical-thinking criterion is where marks go: students describe sources where the descriptor asks them to evaluate reliability and perspective.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Analysis is the criterion most often under-served, because students summarise what a text says instead of examining how it achieves its effect.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed by phase rather than by year group. A student can be in different phases in different skills, which surprises parents reading a single reported grade.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Taught both as an MYP language and as a KHDA-mandated subject, with separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language. Two different sets of expectations can therefore appear on one report.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Marks are lost on the design cycle documentation rather than on the artefact, which students find counter-intuitive.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than the finished piece, and students who treat it as an afterthought lose marks they cannot recover later.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Reflection is assessed, which makes written work part of a subject students assume is practical.

sections.heading: What the Middle Years Programme actually assesses
paragraphs: The MYP assesses skills demonstrated in tasks, judged against published descriptors, in eight subject groups. That is a different proposition from a syllabus examined at the end, and it has three consequences a family should hold onto. Marks describe what a piece of work showed. Descriptors are public and readable. And the same four criterion letters mean different things in different subject groups, which is the detail that confuses almost everybody.

Criterion A is broadly about knowing and understanding across most groups, which is the one that behaves most like a traditional test. Criterion B diverges sharply: in mathematics it is investigating patterns, in sciences it is inquiring and designing, in language and literature it is organising, in design it is developing ideas. A parent who learns what B means in one subject and applies it to another will misread the report.

Beyond the subject groups sit three further elements that appear in reporting and in school conversations. Approaches to learning skills are taught across the curriculum and referenced in feedback. At least one interdisciplinary unit runs each year, assessed on its own criteria. Service as action runs throughout, and the Personal Project arrives in the final year.

None of this is examined externally unless a school opts into the eAssessments, which some do and many do not. The practical effect is that the school's own judgement, moderated internally, produces the grades, so understanding how that school applies the descriptors matters more than it would in an examined system.

sections.heading: Reading a criterion mark without misreading it
paragraphs: Start by refusing the arithmetic. A 5 out of 8 is not 62 per cent and should never be treated as a near-miss on a content test. The descriptors are written in bands, usually in pairs of marks, and each band describes a qualitatively different level of performance. Moving from one band to the next means doing something different, not doing the same thing slightly better.

Then read the descriptor the school used, which is published and which most students have never looked at. The language is specific and it is the key to everything: describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, justify, apply, synthesise. A student sitting at the lower end of a band is usually performing one verb below the one the next band asks for, and once that is named, the gap stops being mysterious.

The third step is to look across criteria rather than at one. A student with a strong Criterion A and a weak Criterion D in sciences knows the content and is not reflecting or evaluating; a student with the reverse pattern is thoughtful and has gaps in knowledge. Those two students need completely different help, and a single reported grade hides the difference entirely.

Finally, treat the converted grade with care. Boundaries are published and a total near a boundary can move a reported grade by one on the strength of a single criterion. That is worth knowing before a family concludes that a child has dropped a grade in a subject when in fact one task slipped a band.
bullets: Bands describe qualitatively different performance, not percentages
The descriptor's verb names the gap: describe against analyse against evaluate

sections.heading: Command terms and task instructions in MYP
paragraphs: MYP tasks carry command terms in the same way Diploma papers do, and students treat them as synonyms in exactly the same way. The difference is that in the MYP the command term is usually embedded in a longer task instruction, sometimes with several parts, so skipping it is easier and the consequence is less obvious.

The high-frequency terms are worth learning deliberately: describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, justify, compare and contrast, apply, outline, discuss. Each obliges something different. Describe wants features without reasons. Explain wants causes stated as a chain. Analyse wants a breakdown into parts with their relationships. Evaluate wants strengths, limitations and a judgement. Justify wants reasons for a position already taken.

The repair is the same mechanical drill that works in the Diploma, adapted to this age. Take four or five of the student's own past task instructions, cover everything except the command term, and ask them to say what the task obliged them to produce. Most students in Years 7 to 9 cannot do this at first, and most can after a fortnight. The marks follow quickly because the knowledge was already there.

One MYP-specific trap: tasks often ask for a response in a particular form, such as a report, a letter, an annotated design or a process journal entry. Producing good content in the wrong form loses marks under the communicating or producing criteria, and students who are strong writers lose more to this than weaker ones, because they write fluently in whatever form they prefer.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, coached as process
paragraphs: The Personal Project runs in the final MYP year and is assessed on planning, applying skills, reflecting and the report, rather than on how impressive the product is. Students and families consistently invert this, putting effort into an ambitious outcome and treating the process journal as paperwork to be assembled at the end. The marks sit in the paperwork.

Goal setting is where most projects are won or lost. A goal needs to be achievable within the time available, specific enough that progress can be evidenced, and connected to a global context the student can actually discuss. Grand goals produce thin evidence; narrow goals produce rich journals. A single session interrogating the goal before any work starts is worth more than several later.

The process journal has to be kept while the work happens, which cannot be retrofitted honestly. Dated entries recording decisions, difficulties, changes of direction and the reasoning behind them are what the criteria reward. Students who photograph their workspace and write three lines a week after each working session end up with better evidence than those who write a polished account at the end, and the difference is visible to a supervisor.

The boundary here is strict. A tutor may explain each criterion, interrogate the goal, ask the questions the descriptors imply, suggest journal habits, and give feedback on the student's own report draft. A tutor may not plan the project, produce any part of the product, draft the report or write journal entries. The project is authenticated by the school, and the point of it is the student's own learning.
bullets: Assessed on planning, applying skills, reflecting and the report, not on the product
A narrow, specific goal produces richer evidence than an ambitious one
The process journal must be written while the work happens

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units, service as action and the eAssessment option
paragraphs: Three parts of the MYP sit outside the subject groups and cause a reasonable amount of confusion in this belt. Interdisciplinary units run at least once a year, combining two or more subject groups and assessed against their own criteria. Students often treat them as a lighter project; they are assessed work, and the criteria reward integration rather than two separate pieces stapled together.

Service as action runs throughout the programme and is documented rather than graded in the same way. Families moving from a British-curriculum school sometimes underestimate the documentation expectation, and then scramble in the final year. The useful habit is recording activity as it happens, which is the same habit the Personal Project journal requires and worth establishing early for both reasons.

The eAssessments are optional and some schools enter students for them while many do not. Where a school does, the student sits externally marked on-screen examinations and an ePortfolio in some subjects, which produces a formal qualification at the end of the MYP. Where a school does not, the final MYP grades are internal. Which of these applies changes what the final year looks like considerably, and it is a question for the school rather than for a tutor.

For a Mudon family comparing schools, the eAssessment question is worth asking directly during an open day, because it affects both the workload of the final year and whether the student leaves the MYP with an external qualification to show a receiving sixth form.
bullets: Interdisciplinary units are assessed work and reward integration, not two stapled pieces
Service as action is documented; the habit should start early rather than in the final year

sections.heading: The Year 11 fork: Diploma, A Levels, or an IGCSE year
paragraphs: At the end of the MYP a student moves on, and in Dubai the destinations differ enough to matter. A continuum school usually leads into the IB Diploma. Some families move to a British-curriculum school for A Levels, and because many of those schools run IGCSE in Years 10 and 11, a mid-phase move can mean crossing into a different assessment system partway through.

The jump into the Diploma is smoothest from the MYP, because the assessment language carries over: criteria, command terms, internally assessed work and the expectation that a student justifies rather than states. What does not carry over is the examination load, since the MYP has little or no external examination and the Diploma is heavily examined. Students who have never sat a timed paper find the first mock a shock.

The jump to A Levels is a larger change of kind. A Levels are examined, narrow and content-dense, and a student arriving from the MYP without IGCSE has usually covered less subject content and more skill development than their new classmates. That is not a deficit in every respect, but it is a real gap in specific content, and it is best closed over a summer rather than discovered in October.

Crossing into an IGCSE year mid-phase is the hardest of the three and should be planned carefully with both schools. Content order differs, tiering decisions may already have been made for the cohort, and the student arrives without the two-year build-up their classmates have had. Where this is unavoidable, a bridging block before the move is the difference between a difficult term and a lost year.

sections.heading: MYP provision around Mudon, and the mandatory UAE subjects
paragraphs: MYP provision in this part of Dubai is thinner than IGCSE provision, which shapes the practical choices a Mudon family has. The nearest continuum options are Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City and GEMS International School Al Khail, with Nord Anglia International School Dubai further along Al Khail Road in Al Barsha South. Most of the schools immediately around Mudon, including Jebel Ali School, GEMS Metropole and South View School, run British curriculum through IGCSE.

That means a family committed to the MYP generally accepts a longer school run than a family following the British route, and the length of that run is worth factoring into any tutoring plan. A student home at half past four has a different evening from one home at half past five, and at this age the second evening does not support a full hour of additional work after homework.

Alongside the eight subject groups sit the mandatory UAE subjects. Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies whatever international curriculum it is licensed for, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

For those subjects, instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, at least 25 minutes per lesson is advised, and the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited. Any support in them therefore works with the school's own material rather than substituting something else.
