faqs.question: What does a criterion level of 5 out of 8 on an MYP report actually mean?
faqs.answer: It is a judgement against a published descriptor rather than a percentage, so it describes what the student can do rather than how many marks they scored. More useful than the number itself is the comparison between the four criteria in that subject. Each carries a level from zero to eight, the four sum to thirty-two, and that total converts to a grade from one to seven using published boundaries. A student at seven on one criterion and three on another has a specific, teachable gap.

faqs.question: Our MYP report has four different numbers per subject. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With the gap between them. High on knowing and understanding and low on inquiring and designing means the content is secure and the process skill was never taught, which is four to six sessions of work. High on analysing and low on organising means ideas without structure, which is similar. Even levels across all four mean no specific gap and respond to ordinary subject teaching. High everywhere means your child needs extension, and the honest advice is to spend the money elsewhere.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion predicts how the Diploma will go?
faqs.answer: Investigating patterns in mathematics, more reliably than any overall grade. It asks for generalisation from specific cases rather than calculation, and that is exactly what extended mathematics and then Analysis and Approaches demand. A student strong on knowing and understanding and weak on investigating patterns is fluent at procedures and weak at generalising, and that pattern is visible from MYP 3 and is teachable in four to six sessions, long before it becomes a Diploma problem.

faqs.question: Should our child take standard or extended mathematics in MYP 4?
faqs.answer: Extended, if any quantitative Diploma route is plausible. Extended keeps Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level realistically open; standard leads comfortably to Applications and Interpretation at either level and to Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level with bridging. Standard into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is possible and makes for a genuinely hard first Diploma year. Make the decision knowingly rather than discovering the consequence in October of DP1, when it costs far more to address.

faqs.question: How much does the Personal Project product actually matter?
faqs.answer: Less than students and parents assume. The criteria cover planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight, and the process journal plus the reflection carry a large share of that. A modest product with thoroughly evidenced planning, skill development and honest reflection outscores an impressive product with a thin journal. The practical consequence is that one session near the start on how to keep the journal is the highest-value hour in the whole project year.

faqs.question: Can the process journal be written up at the end of MYP 5?
faqs.answer: It can be attempted and it reads exactly as what it is. The criteria reward regular, dated evidence of development, and a journal produced retrospectively in one weekend cannot show development because it has no timeline. This is the single most common avoidable loss in the Personal Project. The fix costs nothing and has to happen early: agree what gets recorded, how often, and what counts as evidence that a skill was developed rather than merely used.

faqs.question: Does our Dubai school's MYP include eAssessment and does it matter?
faqs.answer: Not every IB school offers it, so ask. Where it runs, MYP 5 adds on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the formal MYP Certificate, and the year looks materially different as a result. One thing worth knowing: the on-screen examinations reward process and the application of concepts to unfamiliar material, while Diploma papers reward precise answers to specific command terms. A strong eAssessment result can therefore create false confidence going into DP1.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject group causes the most trouble for Dubai students?
faqs.answer: Sciences and design, for the same reason. Both have two criteria out of four that reward documenting a process rather than performing a task, and students who are good at the subject and careless about recording lose levels systematically. In sciences it is inquiring and designing plus processing and evaluating; in design it is inquiring and analysing plus evaluating. That is the commonest systematic underperformance in the programme and among the easiest things to fix, because it is a habit.

faqs.question: Which schools near Nad Al Hamar run the Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: The IB continuum schools in the Mirdif and Al Mizhar belt, including Uptown International School, and schools in the Festival City cluster offering IB programmes, which is a fifteen to twenty-five minute drive. Other eastern-suburb schools run British or Indian curricula to IGCSE instead, so a family here can compare an MYP route against an IGCSE route at sixteen within a short radius. Schools are named as local context only, with no affiliation or endorsement implied.

faqs.question: How long should a tutoring session be for an eleven-year-old in MYP 1?
faqs.answer: Forty-five minutes, and twice a week rather than once if anything is being built. Attention rather than content is the binding constraint at that age, and the habits worth building, justifying an answer, recording a process, structuring a piece of writing, respond to frequency rather than to depth. Door times in Nad Al Hamar run from about 3.50pm to past 4.35pm, so a 5pm or 5.30pm start works better than a Diploma student's 6.30pm slot.

faqs.question: Does an MYP student who is coping need a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: No, and we will say so. The genuinely useful purchases in this programme are narrow: four to six sessions on a criterion that sits well below the others, three or four on documentation habits, a handful spread across the Personal Project year, and the summer bridge into Diploma mathematics if the standard route was taken. That is a small total across five years. A provider proposing continuous weekly support throughout the programme is selling a subscription.

faqs.question: What is the biggest step from MYP 5 into the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: The volume of independent long-form work. MYP produces one Personal Project across a year; the Diploma produces an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and an internal assessment in every subject, with most of them clustered in DP2. A student who struggled to organise the Personal Project will find that cluster considerably harder, which makes it the most useful predictive signal a parent has. Planning, drafting and finishing habits are the thing to build in the summer.

faqs.question: Will you help our child with the Personal Project report itself?
faqs.answer: We will explain what each criterion rewards, discuss whether a proposal can generate real development, demonstrate what a well-kept journal looks like using an entirely different project, and read your child's own journal and draft report and ask questions about evidence, success criteria and honesty of reflection. We will not choose the project, make any part of the product, write or rewrite the report, or construct the journal. The project is the student's own by design, and a malpractice finding falls on them.

faqs.question: Do MYP students in Dubai also have to take Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: In Dubai private schools, yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. That is timetabled time families rarely count when adding tutoring on top of eight subject groups.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-nad-al-hamar.closingHeading: Read the four numbers, fix one, then leave it alone
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-nad-al-hamar.closingBody: The Middle Years Programme gives parents better diagnostic information than any other curriculum and almost nobody uses it. Look at the four criterion levels in each subject rather than the grade, find the one that sits well below the others, and buy four to six sessions on it. In MYP 5, spend a handful of hours early on the Personal Project proposal and journal rather than many at the deadline. And decide the standard or extended mathematics question with the Diploma in view. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home tutoring is an India-only service. dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Middle Years Programme subjects to students across Dubai's central corridor, working to the published criteria rather than to a textbook. Each will ask for the criterion levels on the last report before teaching anything, because a student scoring 6, 6, 6 and 3 needs something very different from one scoring 5 across the board.

intro.heading: A report full of numbers out of 8, and what to do with it
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme produces the least legible school report in the Dubai market. A parent receives a set of numbers out of 8 against criteria labelled A to D, a converted grade from 1 to 7, and commentary written in programme language. Most families in Nad Al Sheba read the converted grade, note whether it went up or down, and put the report away. The criterion levels underneath it are where the useful information is, and they are specific enough to act on.

Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of 8, giving 32 marks that convert to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. The criteria differ by subject group but the structure does not. A student at 6, 6, 6 and 3 and a student at 5, 5, 5 and 5 can land on the same converted grade while needing entirely different help: the first has one broken criterion and three strong ones, the second has a consistent ceiling. Buying generic subject tutoring for the first case is close to useless.

This page is also a comparison, because Nad Al Sheba is a district where the comparison is live. Repton School Dubai, Kings' School Nad Al Sheba and Hartland International School sit inside or beside the district running British secondary routes to IGCSE, while GEMS Modern Academy and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai run IB continuums through MYP. Families here genuinely choose between the two at eleven and sometimes revisit the choice at fourteen, which makes an honest comparison more useful than an argument for either.

Dubai held 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the IB at 7%. The emirate's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. So the IB share is growing from a small base, which means MYP cohorts in individual schools remain modest and specialist MYP tutoring supply stays correspondingly thin on the ground.

IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a thirteen-year-old that trade is worth naming honestly: a tutor in the room notices drift faster than one on a screen. What the screen buys is a tutor who has read the actual MYP criteria for that subject group, which is a narrower thing to find locally than a general subject tutor.

One practical instruction before the detail. Ask the school for the subject guide criterion descriptors for whichever subject is causing concern, and bring them to the first conversation along with the last report. Schools will supply them and almost no parent asks. With the descriptor in front of you, the conversation stops being about whether your child is good at the subject and becomes about which band their work reached and what the next band up asks for that it did not provide. That is a question a thirteen-year-old can usually answer themselves once somebody reads them the words.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.programmesIntro: MYP sits between two other programmes and beside an alternative, and a Nad Al Sheba family will meet all four within one school search. These are the four, described by what each one asks of a student rather than by its aims.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no terminal assessment, ending in the exhibition — the first extended independent project most children produce. Strong PYP reporting can coexist with insecure written number work and spelling, because the programme assesses inquiry and communication rather than drilled accuracy. The useful diagnostic before MYP is whether the child can explain a method aloud and then write it down.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, PYP runs alongside KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, required in every private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. For families new to the emirate, Arabic as a timetabled subject from a standing start is often the first tutoring request, and it is cheapest to address in the PYP years rather than in MYP.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed on four criteria out of 8 for a 32-mark total converting to a 1-7 grade. Interdisciplinary units, service as action and approaches to learning run across the whole programme. The final year carries the Personal Project, marked on three criteria over 24 marks, and in some schools MYP eAssessment leading to the MYP Certificate.
programmes.countryNote: Nad Al Sheba sits beside schools running MYP straight into the Diploma within one building, so the pacing is set internally and the transition is invisible from outside. The hidden consequence is examination experience: a student assessed through criteria-based tasks for five years meets their first two-hour paper in DP1 with no practice at pacing one.

programmes.name: IGCSE, the alternative at the same age
programmes.description: Terminal examinations in eight to ten separate subjects, graded by the board, with tiering in some subjects and a published syllabus code for each. Where MYP assesses skills against criteria continuously, IGCSE assesses content under timed conditions at the end. Neither is harder; they reward different students and produce different habits.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in and around Nad Al Sheba run IGCSE and then split students towards A Level or the IB Diploma at sixteen. A family choosing between MYP and IGCSE at eleven is therefore not choosing their child's post-sixteen route, which is a common misunderstanding and worth correcting before it drives the decision.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and CAS. Both MYP and IGCSE students enter it, arriving with opposite strengths: MYP students are comfortable with extended independent work and unused to timed papers, IGCSE students the reverse. Identifying which profile your child has is the most useful preparation available.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No specific IB session or results date appears on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Confirm every one with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly rather than from a search result.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.subjectsIntro: MYP runs eight subject groups, each with its own four criteria. Below are the groups as Nad Al Sheba students meet them, described by which criterion most often holds a grade down rather than by the content covered.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text and using language. The criterion that most often sits low is organising: students with good ideas and weak structure cap at a 5 regardless of insight. Essay planning taught explicitly, with a paragraph purpose stated before writing, moves this criterion faster than more reading does.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed within a phase rather than a year group. Students lose marks by producing accurate but unambitious language, because the descriptors reward range alongside accuracy. Knowing which phase the student is being assessed in is essential and parents are rarely told.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the usual ceiling: a student who describes two viewpoints without evaluating them has met the lower descriptors only. Source evaluation taught as a routine rather than an instinct is the specific fix.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Inquiring and designing is where marks concentrate and where schools have least time: naming variables, justifying a control and writing a testable hypothesis are learnable in three sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5, four criteria, standard and extended
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Communicating is the quiet killer: correct working with no explanation, undefined variables and unlabelled graphs cap the criterion. The extended route in the later years is the one that prepares a student for Higher Level Diploma maths.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than students expect, and a strong final piece with a thin journal scores below a modest piece with a documented process. That is the single most useful thing to tell an arts student in MYP 4.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Written components are genuinely assessed, which surprises families who treat the subject as practical only, and the planning and reflecting criteria are where grades are made.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Entirely process-assessed: the design cycle has to be evidenced at each stage, and a finished product with undocumented development cannot reach the upper bands however good it looks. Documentation discipline is the whole subject.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units drawing on two or more subject groups with their own criteria, including evaluating and reflecting on interdisciplinary learning. Students treat them as a double dose of two subjects rather than as a distinct task with its own descriptors, which is why able students sometimes score oddly low on them.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.levels: Final MYP year, three criteria, 24 marks
subjects.description: Planning, applying skills, and reflecting, each out of 8. Assessed on the process journal and the report rather than on the product, which students consistently misread. A beautifully made product with a thin journal cannot reach the top bands; a modest product with rigorous documentation can.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning
subjects.description: Thinking, communication, social, self-management and research skills, woven into subject criteria rather than graded separately. Self-management is the one that most often explains a capable student's mediocre report: deadlines missed, drafts not kept, journals written retrospectively the night before.

subjects.name: Arabic within the MYP timetable
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students. Depending on the school this may be assessed as language acquisition, as language and literature, or alongside the MYP structure as a mandatory subject.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.regionsTitle: Nad Al Sheba and the communities around it
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.regionsIntro: What differs across this block of communities is the school run and the programme their schools run. For an MYP family both matter, because the programme decides the help needed and the commute decides when it can happen.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Repton School Dubai, Kings' School Nad Al Sheba and GEMS Modern Academy inside the district, between them covering both the British route and an IB continuum. Short school runs make a 15:30 session realistic, which suits a younger student's concentration.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai sit inside the community. Easiest scheduling of the block, and the most common MYP request from here is Personal Project support in the final year.

regions.name: Meydan
regions.note: Newer stock around the racecourse with many families in their first or second UAE year. Mid-programme arrivals are frequent, and a student joining MYP 3 from a national curriculum needs the criteria explained before anything else.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Rashid City
regions.note: District One villa plots with long internal roads and limited exits onto Al Khail. Pick-up traffic absorbs twenty minutes inside the community, which matters more for a younger student whose useful window closes earlier in the evening.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Quoz 4
regions.note: Mixed residential and industrial, with longer journeys to the Nad Al Sheba schools. Weekday starts land after 17:00, which for an MYP student usually means a shorter session rather than a later one.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Apartments and short commutes, with students mostly at Downtown and Al Jaddaf schools. Evening slots work here, and a 45-minute criterion-focused session suits that window better than a long content block.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: No school on site, so every family drives out and back. For MYP the narrow after-school window argues for fortnightly longer sessions around assessment deadlines rather than a thin weekly hour.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf and Culture Village
regions.note: Swiss International Scientific School Dubai anchors this end with a bilingual IB continuum from the early years. Requests from here often involve the written communication criteria rather than subject content.

regions.name: DIFC
regions.note: Few families, almost all in apartments with long parental working days. Weekend sessions dominate, and for a younger student that is often better anyway: a Saturday morning beats a Tuesday at 20:00.

schoolClusters.city: Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland
schoolClusters.note: Schools inside or beside the district, between them covering an IB continuum through MYP and British routes to IGCSE. A family comparing the two programmes at eleven is usually comparing schools from this short list.

schoolClusters.city: The IB continuum schools across the corridor
schoolClusters.note: Schools running the IB across more than one programme, which is where most MYP enquiries from this page originate. Several of them also run the Diploma, so the MYP-to-DP transition happens internally.

sections.heading: MYP against IGCSE at sixteen
paragraphs: This is the comparison a Nad Al Sheba family actually makes, because schools within a few kilometres of each other offer both and the choice is real. It is usually presented to parents as a philosophy question — inquiry and skills against content and examinations — which is accurate and not very useful. The practical differences are more concrete than that.

MYP assesses continuously against four published criteria per subject, each out of 8, with the 32 marks converting to a 1-7 grade. Nothing is externally examined unless the school enters students for MYP eAssessment. IGCSE assesses content under timed conditions at the end of two years, graded by an exam board, with a syllabus code and in some subjects a tier that caps the grade. One produces students comfortable with extended independent work; the other produces students comfortable with a clock.

Neither is harder and neither closes the Diploma. Both routes feed into DP1 and into A Level. What differs is the habit each leaves behind, and that habit is worth planning around rather than discovering. An MYP student entering the Diploma has never sat a two-hour paper. An IGCSE student entering the Diploma has never written 4,000 words or kept a process journal. Each gap is addressable in the final year of the respective programme and expensive to address later.

The decision also has a UAE administrative dimension. Ministry of Education equivalency rules for the British track are published in detail — five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No IB equivalency figure is published on a source this project could verify, so a family for whom UAE university entry is the likely route should check the current requirement for their child's qualification on moe.gov.ae directly rather than take any page's word for it.

sections.heading: How MYP marking works, and how to read the report
paragraphs: Each MYP subject has four criteria, labelled A to D, each marked out of 8 against published descriptors. The four add to 32, and that total converts to a 1-7 grade using boundaries the school applies. The descriptors are not secret; they are published in the subject guides and most schools will supply them on request. Almost no parent asks, which is the gap this section exists to close.

The reason the criterion levels matter more than the converted grade is arithmetic. A student at 6, 6, 6 and 3 scores 21. A student at 5, 5, 5 and 5 scores 20. The converted grades may be adjacent and the two students have nothing in common: one has three strong criteria and one broken one, the other has a consistent ceiling. The first needs one specific intervention of three or four sessions. The second needs a term of subject work.

The criteria that most often sit low across subject groups are the ones about expression and evaluation rather than knowledge. Communicating in mathematics. Organising in language and literature. Thinking critically in individuals and societies. Inquiring and designing in sciences. Evaluating in design. In every case the student knows the material and has not met the descriptor's demand, which is a different problem from not knowing the material and has a much faster fix.

So the first action for any Nad Al Sheba parent holding an MYP report is to ask the school for the criterion descriptors for the subject in question, read the level-7-8 band aloud with the child, and ask them to say in their own words what it requires that their work did not provide. Most students can answer that in five minutes once they have read the words. Most have never read the words.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: three criteria, twenty-four marks, one journal
paragraphs: The Personal Project in the final MYP year is the piece of work students most consistently misunderstand, and the misunderstanding is simple: they believe they are being assessed on the product. They are not. It is marked on three criteria — planning, applying skills, and reflecting — each out of 8 for a total of 24, and the evidence for all three sits in the process journal and the report.

The practical consequence is counterintuitive and worth saying to a student in MYP 5 early. A beautifully made product with a thin, retrospective journal cannot reach the upper bands, because there is no evidence of planning or of skills applied. A modest product with a rigorous journal — decisions recorded as they were taken, difficulties documented, skills identified and evidenced — can. Students find this unfair for about a week and then find it liberating.

The failure mode is almost always self-management rather than ability. The journal is written the night before submission from memory, which produces reflection that reads as description because there is nothing recorded to reflect on. The fix is procedural: a fixed ten minutes after each working session, with a date, a decision and a difficulty recorded. A tutor can enforce that rhythm and check the journal periodically against the criteria.

What a tutor may and may not do here deserves stating plainly. A tutor may discuss whether a goal is achievable in the time available, help the student write success criteria they can actually test against, explain what each criterion asks for, and give written feedback on the journal and report the student has written. A tutor may not choose the goal, make or contribute to the product, write any part of the journal or report, or edit either to completion. The declaration on the submitted work is the student's.

sections.heading: MYP into DP against IGCSE into DP
paragraphs: Both routes arrive at the Diploma and both arrive with a gap, but the gaps are opposite and that is genuinely useful to know a year in advance. The comparison matters in this district because several schools run MYP straight into DP internally while others run IGCSE and then offer the Diploma as one of two sixth-form options.

The MYP student arrives comfortable with extended independent work, with documented process, with criteria-based feedback and with research skills. They arrive without examination technique: five years of criteria-based tasks, however demanding, do not teach a student to pace a two-hour paper, to decide in ninety seconds which optional question to answer, or to abandon a question and come back. In DP1 that shows up as a capable student with mediocre test results.

The IGCSE student arrives the other way round. Examination technique is secure, timing is drilled, and command terms are familiar. What is missing is sustained independent work: nothing in Years 10 and 11 required 4,000 words, a documented process over six months, or a self-chosen research question. In DP1 that shows up as a strong test performer whose internal assessments and Extended Essay stall.

Both gaps are cheap to close in the final year of the preceding programme and expensive to close in DP1, when six subjects and five components are already competing. For an MYP 5 student in Nad Al Sheba that means timed paper practice during the final MYP year, particularly in maths and the sciences. For a Year 11 IGCSE student it means one extended piece of writing to a word limit, planned and drafted properly, which no part of their curriculum will otherwise require.

sections.heading: Approaches to learning, and the capable student with a poor report
paragraphs: The most common MYP case in this corridor is not a student who cannot do the work. It is a capable student whose report sits at 4s and 5s because of how the work arrives: late, undrafted, unplanned, with the journal written retrospectively and the research done the evening before. MYP calls these approaches to learning, and the relevant one is self-management.

Approaches to learning are not graded separately. They are woven into the subject criteria, which is why their absence shows up as a subject problem and gets treated as one. A student losing marks on the organising criterion in language and literature usually has an outlining problem rather than a writing problem. A student losing marks on inquiring and designing in sciences often has a planning problem rather than a science problem. Buying subject content for either case is buying the wrong thing.

What works is procedural and slightly boring. A single shared planning document for the fortnight ahead, with assessed tasks and their criteria listed. Ten minutes of journal entry after each working session, dated, naming one decision and one difficulty. A draft produced two days before a deadline rather than on it, so there is something to give feedback on. None of that requires a subject specialist, which is worth saying because it means some MYP problems are cheaper to fix than parents fear.

Where a tutor adds value is enforcement and modelling rather than instruction. A weekly slot that opens with the plan and closes with the journal creates a rhythm the student will not create alone at thirteen. Over a term that rhythm moves several criteria at once across several subjects, which is a better return than a term of content work in one of them.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs, and why the market barely prices it
paragraphs: MYP is the least-priced segment of the Dubai tutoring market. The competitor pages researched for this project price IB broadly or price the Diploma specifically; almost none distinguish MYP, and three of six publish no price at all. So a Nad Al Sheba parent researching MYP support is working from figures that were quoted for something else, and it is worth knowing which something.

The published bands, read in October 2026, belong to whoever published them: budget online or undergraduate tutoring AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; a qualified subject tutor online AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; an IB specialist AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase publishing AED 270; in-home one-to-one AED 180 to 500 including travel; and a premium end reaching AED 650 at BartyED.

For MYP specifically the specialist premium is harder to justify than it is for Higher Level Diploma subjects, with one exception. Ordinary subject content at MYP level is within reach of a competent qualified tutor, so the middle band is usually the right purchase. The exception is criteria work and the Personal Project, where somebody who has actually read the subject guide descriptors is doing a different job from somebody teaching the topic, and that experience is not reliably present at the lower bands.

Monthly, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, with specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more — a band that mostly does not apply to MYP, because MYP has no terminal exam year unless the school enters eAssessment. Packages seen include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Ask about session length, VAT and what happens if you stop after one lesson.

sections.heading: MYP eAssessment, and whether your school uses it
paragraphs: Most parents in this district have never heard of MYP eAssessment, and a significant number of MYP students never meet it, because entering students is the school's choice rather than a programme requirement. It is worth establishing which case your child is in, because it changes whether the final MYP year contains an external examination at all.

Where a school enters students, eAssessment provides on-screen examinations in a set of subjects alongside moderated ePortfolios, leading to the MYP Certificate. Where a school does not, the final MYP year is assessed internally against the same criteria and the student leaves with school reports and the Personal Project rather than an externally certified qualification. Both are legitimate; they are not equivalent documents.

The practical question for a Nad Al Sheba family is one email to the school: does my child sit MYP eAssessment, in which subjects, and when. If the answer is yes, the final MYP year contains the examination practice that MYP is otherwise criticised for lacking, and the DP1 transition is correspondingly easier. If the answer is no, that gap is real and should be closed deliberately with timed practice during MYP 5.

There is also a comparison worth drawing for families weighing MYP against IGCSE. A student who sits eAssessment leaves MYP with external certification and examination experience; a student who does not leaves with neither, which is the single strongest practical argument IGCSE has in this comparison. Knowing which version of MYP your school runs makes the choice between programmes a real decision rather than an abstract one.

sections.heading: Arabic and the mandatory subjects inside an MYP week
paragraphs: MYP already runs eight subject groups, and in Dubai those sit alongside subjects the emirate requires. KHDA mandates Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and its published requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisational rules are specific and worth knowing, because families moving into Nad Al Sheba from outside the region frequently meet them for the first time. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and KHDA states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language.

There is a timetable arithmetic that MYP parents feel more acutely than most, because MYP's eight subject groups are already broad. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Those minutes come out of a week that also has to hold eight subject groups, interdisciplinary units and service as action.

For tutoring there is one firm constraint. KHDA states that for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited. So support for Arabic, Islamic Education or Social Studies works within the school's own approved material rather than bringing in an alternative syllabus, and any provider offering a parallel curriculum for those subjects is offering something that does not fit the rules.

sections.heading: A thirteen-year-old on a video call: the honest version
paragraphs: Everything else on this page argues from criteria and comparison. This section argues from the thing parents of younger students actually worry about, which is whether a thirteen-year-old will engage with a tutor on a screen. It deserves a straight answer rather than a reassurance.

Presence matters more at this age than at seventeen. A tutor in the room notices a wandering attention faster, and a parent can see the session happening. Those are genuine advantages and the market charges roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour extra for them. For a student who needs supervision as much as teaching, that premium can be the right purchase, and IB Gram does not sell it — we do not offer home visits in the UAE, and that service exists only in India.

What a screen gives in exchange is specific to MYP. The criterion descriptors can be open beside the student's own work, which is the whole method for criteria-based teaching. A shared document holds the fortnightly plan and the project journal where both tutor and student can see them between sessions. And the tutor is drawn from the whole timezone, which matters because somebody who has read the MYP subject guide descriptors for the relevant subject group is a narrow profile to find within a twenty-minute drive of any one district.

The practical mitigations for a younger student are worth naming. Shorter sessions: 45 minutes beats 60 at this age. Earlier slots: 15:30 or 16:00 rather than after dinner, which is achievable in Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland where the schools sit inside the community. Camera on, shared screen, and a parent within earshot for the first few sessions. And the free trial lesson, which is the only honest way to find out whether a particular child works in this format before anything is paid.

sections.heading: From a 5 to a 7: what the top band actually asks for
paragraphs: The question most Nad Al Sheba MYP parents want answered is how a 5 becomes a 7, and there is a real answer that is not more effort. The published descriptors change in kind between the middle and upper bands, not in degree, and a student working harder at what earned a 5 will earn a slightly better 5.

Across subject groups the upper bands consistently ask for three things the middle bands do not. Independent judgement rather than reported content: an evaluation reached and defended rather than two viewpoints described. Consistency under less scaffolding: the same quality when the task is open as when it is structured. And explicit reasoning made visible: the thinking shown on the page rather than implied by a correct conclusion.

That translates into specific, slightly unglamorous practice. Ask the student, after any piece of work, what judgement they reached and what their best evidence for it was. Give them one task a fortnight with the scaffolding deliberately removed. Require a sentence explaining each step rather than only the steps. None of that is subject content, which is why a term of content teaching rarely moves a 5 to a 7 while a term of this often does.

One caution, because it matters more than any technique. Nobody can promise a grade, and no honest tutor will put a number on an outcome. What can be promised is a named diagnosis, specific practice against a published descriptor, and a written note each session saying what was worked and what comes next. A provider promising a particular grade is telling you something about themselves at no charge, and the researched set for this market contains several.

process.title: Send the criterion levels, not the grade
process.description: The useful opening message gives the subject, the MYP year, and the four criterion levels from the last report. A student at 6, 6, 6 and 3 and one at 5, 5, 5 and 5 may share a converted grade and need entirely different help. If you have the subject guide descriptors, send those too; if not, the school will supply them.

process.title: A free diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: One live session spent reading the relevant criterion descriptor with the student and looking at a recent piece of their own work against it. The purpose is to establish whether the gap is content, expression or self-management. You get a written note naming which and what the next few sessions should target. No payment is involved.

process.title: Work the criterion, not the chapter
process.description: Where one criterion is low, sessions work that criterion's demand directly: paragraph purpose for organising, variable naming for inquiring and designing, explanation of steps for communicating in mathematics. Three or four sessions on the actual descriptor usually moves it, where a term of topic revision does not.

process.title: Set the fortnightly plan and the journal rhythm
process.description: A shared document listing the assessed tasks for the fortnight and their criteria, opened at the start of each session, plus ten minutes of dated journal entry after each working session. At thirteen that rhythm will not appear on its own, and over a term it moves several criteria across several subjects at once.

process.title: Protect the Personal Project early
process.description: In the final MYP year, the goal and success criteria are tested for feasibility before work starts, and the journal is reviewed periodically as the assessed document it is. The single most common failure is a journal written retrospectively, which produces reflection that reads as description because nothing was recorded.

process.title: Bridge into the Diploma deliberately
process.description: If DP1 is next, the final MYP terms add the one thing the programme does not drill: timed written papers under a real clock, particularly in maths and the sciences. It is a short block rather than an ongoing arrangement, and it ends when the Diploma starts.

whyPoints.title: We start from the criterion levels
whyPoints.description: The converted 1-7 grade hides the information. Four criteria out of 8 each, totalling 32, is where the diagnosis lives, and a single broken criterion among three strong ones is a three-session problem rather than a term-long one.

whyPoints.title: The descriptors are read, not paraphrased
whyPoints.description: Criteria-based teaching means having the published descriptor open beside the student's own work and asking what the upper band requires that this did not provide. Most MYP students have never read the words, which is the cheapest gap on this page to close.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project treated as a journal, not a product
whyPoints.description: Three criteria over 24 marks, all evidenced in the process journal and report. A beautiful product with a thin journal cannot reach the upper bands. We enforce the journal rhythm and give feedback on the student's own writing, and produce none of it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what video costs at thirteen
whyPoints.description: Presence matters more at this age, and we do not sell it in the UAE — home visits are an India-only service. Shorter sessions, earlier slots and the free trial lesson are how that trade is managed rather than argued away.

whyPoints.title: The right band, not the top one
whyPoints.description: Ordinary MYP subject content sits within a competent qualified tutor's reach, so the middle market band is usually the right purchase. The specialist premium is worth paying for criteria work, the Personal Project and the Diploma bridge, and we say which is which.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees and no borrowed credentials
whyPoints.description: Nobody can promise a grade and we do not. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and claims none; regulators are explained here because parents need to understand them.

faqs.question: Is the MYP tutoring delivered in Nad Al Sheba or online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a younger student that trade is worth naming: presence matters more at thirteen than at seventeen, and we do not sell it here. What the format buys instead is a tutor who has read the published criterion descriptors for that subject group, which is a narrow profile to find within a short drive of any one district.

faqs.question: What do the numbers out of 8 on my child's MYP report mean?
faqs.answer: Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each marked out of 8 against published descriptors, giving 32 marks that convert to a 1-7 grade using boundaries the school applies. The criterion levels carry more information than the converted grade. A student at 6, 6, 6 and 3 has one broken criterion among three strong ones; a student at 5, 5, 5 and 5 has a consistent ceiling. Those need completely different help and may show the same grade.

faqs.question: Should we choose MYP or IGCSE for our child at eleven?
faqs.answer: Both lead to the Diploma and to A Level, so the choice is about habits rather than doors. MYP assesses continuously against four published criteria per subject and leaves students comfortable with extended independent work and unpractised at timed papers. IGCSE assesses content under exam conditions and leaves the reverse. One question changes the comparison materially: ask whether the MYP school enters students for eAssessment, because without it there is no external examination before the Diploma.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion is usually the one holding a grade down?
faqs.answer: Across subject groups it is consistently the criteria about expression and evaluation rather than knowledge. Communicating in mathematics, where correct working is given with no explanation. Organising in language and literature, where good ideas arrive unstructured. Thinking critically in individuals and societies, where two views are described and neither evaluated. Inquiring and designing in sciences, where variables go unnamed. In each case the student knows the material and has not met the descriptor's demand.

faqs.question: How is the Personal Project actually marked?
faqs.answer: On three criteria — planning, applying skills and reflecting — each out of 8 for a total of 24, with the evidence drawn from the process journal and the report rather than from the product. Students consistently misread this and invest in the product. A beautifully made outcome with a thin, retrospective journal cannot reach the upper bands because there is no evidence of planning or skills in use; a modest outcome with a rigorous dated journal can.

faqs.question: How do we stop the process journal being written the night before?
faqs.answer: Make it procedural rather than motivational. Ten minutes after each working session, with a date, one decision taken and one difficulty met. That is the whole system, and it produces the evidence the reflecting criterion needs, because reflection on recorded decisions reads as evaluation while reflection on remembered ones reads as description. At fourteen the rhythm will not appear unprompted, so a weekly session that opens with the plan and closes with the journal is what enforces it.

faqs.question: My child is clearly capable but the MYP report is mediocre. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually self-management rather than ability. Approaches to learning are assessed inside the subject criteria rather than separately, so late, undrafted, unplanned work presents as a subject weakness and gets treated as one. A student losing marks on organising generally has an outlining problem, not a writing problem. The fix is a fortnightly plan listing assessed tasks with their criteria, and a draft produced two days early so there is something to give feedback on.

faqs.question: What is MYP eAssessment and does every school use it?
faqs.answer: It is the optional external component of MYP: on-screen examinations in a set of subjects alongside moderated ePortfolios, leading to the MYP Certificate. Entering students is the school's decision rather than a programme requirement, so plenty of MYP students never meet it. Ask the programme coordinator whether your child sits it, in which subjects, and when. If the answer is no, the final MYP year contains no external examination, and that gap is worth closing with timed practice.

faqs.question: Will my child struggle in DP1 coming from MYP?
faqs.answer: In one specific way, and it is addressable. MYP students arrive comfortable with extended independent work, documented process and criteria-based feedback, and arrive without examination technique — five years of criteria-based tasks do not teach pacing a two-hour paper or deciding quickly between optional questions. That shows up in DP1 as a capable student with mediocre test results. Timed paper practice in the final MYP year, particularly in maths and the sciences, closes it cheaply.

faqs.question: How much does MYP tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The market barely prices MYP separately, so figures quoted for IB usually mean the Diploma. Bands read in October 2026: AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB specialist, TutorChase publishing AED 270. For ordinary MYP content the middle band is usually the right purchase.

faqs.question: Does a 5 become a 7 by working harder?
faqs.answer: No, and that is why effort alone frustrates students at this level. The published descriptors change in kind between the middle and upper bands: the upper ones ask for independent judgement rather than reported content, consistency when the task is unscaffolded, and reasoning made visible on the page. A student working harder at what earned a 5 earns a slightly better 5. The practice that moves it is naming a judgement and its evidence after every piece of work.

faqs.question: How does MYP mathematics prepare a student for Higher Level Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the student took the extended route in the later MYP years, which is the one that carries the content Higher Level assumes. The communicating criterion matters here too: MYP maths rewards defining variables, labelling graphs and explaining steps, which is exactly what the Diploma's mathematical exploration is marked on. Students strong on investigating patterns and weak on communicating tend to struggle most with that exploration, and that is visible from the MYP report.

faqs.question: Why is Arabic on the timetable alongside eight MYP subject groups?
faqs.answer: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, inside a week already holding eight subject groups.

faqs.question: Can a tutor use a different Arabic or Islamic Education syllabus?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA states that for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited. So support for Arabic, Islamic Education or Social Studies has to work within the school's own approved material rather than bringing in an alternative programme. Any provider offering a parallel curriculum for those subjects is offering something that does not fit the rules, which is worth knowing before paying for it.

faqs.question: Will a 45-minute session really be enough?
faqs.answer: For an MYP student it is often better than an hour. Concentration at this age falls away before the clock does, and a focused 45 minutes on one criterion with the descriptor open beats 60 minutes that drifts into conversation. Earlier slots help too: 15:30 or 16:00 is achievable for families whose school sits inside Nad Al Sheba or Sobha Hartland, and an alert student at 16:00 outperforms a tired one at 19:00 by a wide margin.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee my child's MYP grade will improve?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honest will. What can be committed to is a named diagnosis from the criterion levels, specific practice against the published descriptor rather than against a topic, and a written note after each session saying what was worked and what comes next. The researched set of competitors in this market includes providers promising specific outcomes and publishing self-asserted ratings; both are claims a parent should treat as information about the provider rather than about the outcome.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.closingHeading: Send the criterion levels and we can be specific
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.closingBody: The fastest way to use an IB MYP tutor in Nad Al Sheba is to skip the converted grade and send the four criterion levels from the last report, with the subject and the MYP year. From those we can usually say in one message whether this is a single broken criterion worth three sessions, a consistent ceiling worth a term, or a self-management pattern that will move several subjects at once. The first lesson is a free diagnostic spent reading the descriptor alongside your child's own work, with a written note afterwards naming what to target.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-oud-metha.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Middle Years Programme subjects to students in Oud Metha and across the Bur Dubai belt. Read the subject group and the MYP year first, then the criterion each tutor names as their strength, because that pairing is what decides whether a term of sessions changes a report card.

intro.heading: Why MYP tuition is hard to budget and easy to waste
paragraphs: In most curricula a parent can read a report and see the problem. A percentage is low, a topic is named, a tutor is hired for that topic. The Middle Years Programme does not work that way. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, and the four are added to produce a raw total out of thirty-two which the school converts to a grade from one to seven. A family sees the grade. The four marks underneath it are where the money should go, and they are usually not on the page you were sent.

This creates a specific and expensive pattern across Oud Metha and Bur Dubai. A Year 9 student comes home with a 4 in Sciences. The family hires a science tutor, who teaches science content, because that is what the request said. Four months and perhaps AED 4,000 later the grade is still a 4, because the content was never the problem: the student scored well on knowing and understanding and badly on inquiring and designing, which is a method skill nobody addressed. Nothing dishonest happened. The brief was wrong.

So the right first question is not how much does an MYP tutor cost. It is which criterion is low. Ask the school for the criterion marks behind each subject grade, by email if the report does not carry them. Teachers hold them, they are not confidential, and with them in hand a family can buy four sessions on one specific weakness rather than a term of general subject support. That request costs nothing and it is the largest single saving available on this page.

The Dubai market rates matter too, and they are published here with attribution. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted across the city at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour as of October 2026. The same tutor travelling to an apartment is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India. For an MYP family the online format also widens the pool, which matters because MYP specialists are rarer than subject graduates.

What follows is a cost page built around the criteria. It sets out what each of the four assesses and which one moves a grade fastest, explains why an MYP grade is not a percentage and what that does to a family's reading of progress, prices the Dubai market cheapest first, maps the MYP5 to Diploma transition subject by subject, states exactly what a tutor may and may not do with a Personal Project, and sets the whole budget against the KHDA fee position for 2026-27. Every figure carries its source.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-oud-metha.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme is not one stage. The first three years and the last two behave differently, the Personal Project arrives at the end, and the Diploma waits behind it. Budget each separately, because what is useful in MYP2 is not what is useful in MYP5.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, years one to three
programmes.description: Eight subject groups taught concurrently, assessed against four criteria each, with interdisciplinary units linking them. Grades move a lot in these years and most of the movement is in the two method criteria rather than in knowledge. This is the cheapest stage at which to intervene and the stage at which almost nobody does, because nothing visible is at stake yet.
programmes.countryNote: In the Bur Dubai belt, MYP provision sits mainly in Al Jaddaf and across the Creek rather than inside Oud Metha itself, so families here are usually commuting to it. That makes a weekday session awkward by car and easy over video. Four sessions on one weak criterion in MYP2, at the AED 150 to 300 band, is a smaller commitment than a term of anything bought later.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, years four and five
programmes.description: Subject choice narrows slightly, the work lengthens, and criterion descriptors become noticeably harsher at the top bands. MYP5 carries the Personal Project alongside everything else. Students who have never been taught to write a reflection against a descriptor lose marks here in every subject at once, which is why a single piece of technique work pays across the whole report.
programmes.countryNote: MYP5 is when most Oud Metha families actually buy tuition, and it is the most expensive moment to start. The Diploma subject-choice conversation lands at the same time as the Personal Project and the hardest descriptors of the five years. Families who bought four sessions in MYP3 typically spend less in total across the whole programme than families who begin in MYP5.

programmes.name: MYP eAssessment and the MYP Certificate
programmes.description: Some schools enter MYP5 students for the IB's on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, leading to the MYP Certificate. Many do not, and award school-based results instead. The difference changes how the final year should be prepared, because an on-screen examination rewards timed performance while a portfolio rewards sustained drafting.
programmes.countryNote: Ask your child's school directly whether it enters students for eAssessment, because it is a school-level decision and it is rarely explained in a prospectus. Do not plan a revision schedule around an examination your child may not sit, and confirm any assessment date with the school's MYP coordinator rather than from a page online, including this one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, the stage behind it
programmes.description: The Diploma assesses by examination and internal assessment rather than by criterion across every unit, so a student who has coasted on strong knowledge criteria meets a wall. The skills the Diploma assumes, experimental design, structured extended writing and independent drafting, are precisely the MYP method criteria that families tend not to buy support for.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision reachable from Oud Metha sits mainly in Al Jaddaf and Dubai Festival City. If the Diploma is the plan, the transition cost is paid either in MYP4 at a low rate or in DP1 at exam-season intensity. The table later on this page maps it subject by subject so the decision can be made with numbers rather than hope.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-oud-metha.subjectsIntro: An MYP student carries eight subject groups at once, which is what makes the budgeting hard. These are the groups we teach, written as what each one's criteria actually reward rather than as a topic list.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing texts, producing texts, using language, and the organisation of an argument. Marks are lost in organisation far more often than in analysis: students who see the point of a text and cannot structure a paragraph about it score in the middle bands repeatedly.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Assessed in listening, reading, speaking and writing, and placed in a phase rather than a year group. A student in the wrong phase looks weak when they are misplaced, which is worth checking with the school before paying for anything.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. The investigating criterion is where the marks sit and where the teaching is thinnest: students are asked to frame a research question and are rarely shown how one is built.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, reflecting on the impacts of science. Inquiring and designing is the criterion that decides most Sciences grades, and it is the one that transfers directly into Diploma internal assessment work.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-world contexts. Investigating patterns is where confident calculators lose marks, because it asks for a generalisation and a justification rather than an answer.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The least understood group by parents and the easiest criterion gains available, because most of the marks are in documented process rather than in the finished object.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, responding. Students who perform or make well and keep no process journal are scoring two criteria out of four, which reads as a lack of talent and is not.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Includes a planning-for-performance criterion and a reflecting criterion, both written. A physically able student with no written reflection sits in the middle bands, which surprises families more than any other grade on the report.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed with their own criteria, including evaluating the interdisciplinary synthesis. Often the lowest marks on a report because no single subject teacher owns the skill, and therefore one of the quickest things a tutor can address.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Planning, applying skills, reflecting, assessed on the process journal and the report rather than the product. Support here is coaching and feedback on the student's own work; no tutor may write, draft or produce any part of it.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs in Oud Metha, cheapest option first
paragraphs: The least expensive useful thing a parent in Oud Metha can do costs nothing: email the subject teacher and ask for the four criterion marks behind the grade. With those in hand, a family can often buy four sessions rather than a term. At the qualified online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour that is somewhere between AED 600 and AED 1,200, against roughly AED 2,400 to 4,800 for a full term of weekly support. The information is free and it changes the size of the purchase.

If paid support is needed, the Dubai market runs in clear tiers. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, at the budget online end, usually delivered by university students. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing from AED 200 for IB. Specialist IB support is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500.

For the MYP specifically, the tier that matters is the middle one, and the reason is not prestige. Criterion-referenced assessment has its own vocabulary, and a tutor who has not taught against MYP descriptors will teach content well and leave the criterion where it was. That is not a budget-tier failing, it is a familiarity one, and it is the specific thing to ask about. None of the figures above is an IB Gram rate; our pricing follows a free trial lesson used as a criterion diagnostic.

sections.heading: The four criteria, and which one moves a grade fastest
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each marked out of eight. The labels differ by subject but the pattern does not: one criterion rewards knowledge, one rewards investigation or planning, one rewards communication or application, and one rewards reflection or evaluation. The four raw marks add to a total out of thirty-two, which the school converts to a grade from one to seven.

The practical consequence is that two students with the same grade can need completely different help. A student scoring seven, three, six, three has a method problem. A student scoring three, six, four, six has a knowledge problem. Hiring a subject tutor helps the second student and does almost nothing for the first, and the first pattern is the more common one in Oud Metha because local tutoring supply is content-strong and criterion-weak.

If the marks are unavailable, the reliable guess is the reflection criterion. It is written, it is last in every unit, it is the one students run out of time for, and it is marked against descriptors that reward specificity about their own work rather than general enthusiasm. Teaching a student to write a reflection that names what they changed and why is perhaps two sessions. It lifts marks in several subject groups at once, which makes it the best value intervention in the entire programme. Ask the school for the four criterion marks per subject rather than the single reported grade, because the grade hides the pattern and the pattern is the only thing a tutor can act on.

sections.heading: Why an MYP grade 5 is not seventy-one per cent
paragraphs: Families arriving from a percentage-based system read MYP grades wrongly, and it costs them money in both directions. The grade is not a proportion of a possible score. It is a band, produced by adding four criterion marks and applying the school's conversion. That means a one-mark gain on a single criterion can move a grade, and a four-mark gain spread thinly across all four can move nothing at all. Buying general improvement is therefore a poor strategy; buying one criterion is a good one.

It also means progress looks flat when it is not. A student who goes from two to four on the investigation criterion while the other three hold has made real progress and the reported grade may be unchanged. Parents who cannot see criterion marks interpret that as tuition failing and stop, often one unit before the grade would have moved. This is the most common way MYP tuition is abandoned at exactly the wrong moment in this part of Dubai.

Do not accept a boundary table from a tutor, from a forum or from this page. Conversion boundaries are set within the framework the IB publishes and applied by the school, and the only authoritative version is your child's school's. Ask the MYP coordinator how the conversion works at that school and ask for the criterion marks each reporting cycle. Two emails a year give a family better information than any amount of paid diagnosis.

sections.heading: The reflection criterion: two sessions, several subjects
paragraphs: Reflection is the most consistently underscored criterion in the Middle Years Programme and the least taught. Students are asked to evaluate their own work and they write what they feel: it went well, I enjoyed it, next time I will try harder. The descriptors reward something narrower, which is specific, evidenced statements about the work itself and about what would be done differently and why.

The teaching is unglamorous and quick. Take the student's own marked piece. Find the sentence where they said the task went well. Ask what the evidence for that was, and write the answer. Ask what they would change, and then ask what would happen if they changed it. Repeat across three pieces from three different subjects. Most students move bands on this criterion in under a month, and the gain appears in Sciences, Design, Arts, Physical and Health Education and the interdisciplinary units simultaneously.

This is also where the economics of MYP tuition are clearest. A parent in Karama or Al Mankhool who buys six AED 200 sessions aimed at reflection across three subject groups has spent AED 1,200 and bought movement on perhaps five criterion marks. The same AED 1,200 spent on general Sciences content buys six lessons on material the student mostly has. The difference is not the tutor's quality. It is what the sessions were pointed at. Ask for the criterion marks before and after, on the same subjects, so the change is visible rather than asserted by whoever sold the sessions.
bullets: Use the student's own marked work, never a generic exercise
Replace feeling words with evidence sentences, line by line
Three pieces from three subject groups, not three from one
Expect movement within a month; expect the grade to lag the marks
Ask the school for criterion marks again after the next reporting cycle

sections.heading: The Personal Project: what a tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: The Personal Project arrives in MYP5 and is assessed on the process journal and the report rather than on the object the student produces. That surprises families, and it is the single most important thing to understand before paying for support. A beautiful finished product with a thin journal scores badly. A modest product with a rigorous, honest, well-evidenced journal scores well.

What a tutor may legitimately do is considerable. The goal can be interrogated before any work starts, which is where most weak projects are saved, because an unachievable or unmeasurable goal produces a report that cannot evidence anything. The success criteria can be challenged for specificity. Journal habits can be established in week one rather than reconstructed in week twelve. The student's own draft report can be read and returned with written feedback naming what a descriptor asks for and where the draft does not answer it.

What a tutor must never do is write, draft, edit to completion or produce any part of the project or the report. The student declares the work as their own. A breach falls on the student's record, and IB academic-honesty rules treat it seriously. IB Gram does not write, complete or supply assessed work in any subject or at any level. One operator found during research for this project sells completed internal assessments outright at AED 3,750; that is not a cheaper form of tutoring, it is a malpractice risk a family should not buy at any price.

sections.heading: MYP5 into the Diploma: the gap, costed
paragraphs: The transition is where MYP underspending becomes visible. The Diploma assesses by examination and by internal assessment, and it assumes skills the MYP method criteria were building. A student with strong knowledge criteria and weak investigation criteria arrives in DP1 able to learn content and unable to design an investigation, which is exactly what the Diploma sciences ask for in a component worth a fifth of the grade.

The repair costs the same work whenever it is done, but not the same money. Done in MYP4 at a qualified online rate of AED 150 to 300 an hour, across a planned handful of sessions, it is a few hundred dirhams per subject. Done in DP1 it competes with content teaching for the same hours. Done in DP2 it is bought at specialist exam-season intensity, where Bestimate estimates AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month for an exam-year student, and it is bought in the weeks when nothing else can be dropped.

The table below maps the common moves subject by subject with a realistic number of weeks for each. Use it to decide which gap to close before Year 12 and which to leave. Not every gap needs closing in advance: a student heading for Diploma Language and Literature who writes well does not need a transition block, while the same student taking Sciences at Higher Level almost certainly does. Decide this in Year 10 rather than in the Diploma year, when every hour already has a claim on it and the cheapest version of the repair is no longer available.
