sections.heading: The Personal Project and the evening it needs
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is where the commute does the most damage, because it is the piece of work most easily postponed and the one that cannot be reconstructed at the end. It has a goal, a product or outcome, a process journal and a report, and it is the journal that catches people out.

The criteria reward documented planning and honest reflection rather than an impressive final artefact. A project with a polished outcome and an empty journal, written up from memory in the last fortnight, cannot score well — and the criteria are designed to detect exactly that. For a student getting home at 16:45 across a whole year, the journal is the first thing to go, because it feels optional in a way a due task does not.

The fix is small and structural: a twenty-minute slot once a week, from the first fortnight, in which the student records what they decided and why. Not a diary, not a narrative, just decisions and reasons. Done weekly from the start, it produces the evidence base the criteria want and makes the final report straightforward. Done retrospectively, it produces something the markers recognise immediately.

The other early intervention is testing the goal. A goal must be achievable with the time and resources the student actually has — which for a Serena student includes a long commute and a limited evening — and it must generate something assessable. 'Build an app' from no prior coding, with fifty minutes a day lost to the road, is a goal that produces a thin product and a frustrated sixteen-year-old. Narrower goals with documented iteration score better and teach more. A tutor may question the goal, explain the criteria and prompt the journal; they may not choose the goal, make the product, write journal entries retrospectively, or draft the report.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units, service as action, and other hidden load
paragraphs: Three MYP requirements regularly surprise families in this belt, and all three consume evening time that nobody budgeted for. None of them is onerous in itself; the problem is that they arrive on top of a week already shortened by the commute.

Interdisciplinary units are assessed in their own right, on integrating disciplines and reflecting on that integration. Students treat them as double homework from two subjects, which is why their marks here often sit below the same student's single-subject performance. A single session reading the interdisciplinary criteria properly usually fixes the approach for the rest of the programme, because the misunderstanding is conceptual rather than academic.

Service as action is a programme requirement documented by the student rather than a graded subject, and schools differ in how much documentation they expect. It consumes real time in MYP 4 and 5, often at weekends, which is precisely when a long-commute student most needs a clear morning. Finding out early what the school requires — and documenting as you go rather than at the end — prevents a scramble.

The third is the mandatory UAE subjects. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes must be organised for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are prohibited. For a non-Arab student that is genuine homework in a language not used at home, and it is frequently the part of the week nobody is supporting.

sections.heading: What to do when the report lands
paragraphs: MYP reports are more informative than examination reports and are read less carefully, because the criterion marks look like jargon. They are not: they name the problem precisely, which makes the week after a report the most efficient time to buy anything.

Each criterion is marked from 0 to 8, giving a total out of 32 per subject, which converts to the 1 to 7 grade shown on the report using boundaries set by the IB and applied through the school's assessment policy. The arithmetic matters: moving one weak criterion from a 3 to a 6 adds three marks to the total and often crosses a boundary, while lifting all four by one adds four marks for four times the work. So the useful question is never 'how do we improve in Sciences' but 'which criterion, and what does its descriptor require'.

The practical routine is short. Read each subject's four criterion marks and find the lowest. Compare it with last term's to see whether it dropped or has always been low. Check whether the same criterion is low across several subjects, which usually points at a transferable skill — investigation design, or critical evaluation — rather than at a subject. Then ask the teacher what that criterion looked like in the last task.

That half-hour tells you what to buy, and often tells you that four to six sessions is the whole intervention. It is also the right moment to adjust the week: a criterion that needs task-based work needs a weekend slot, while a criterion that needs marking discipline fits a weekday evening after a long drive.

sections.heading: Cost, availability and the commute premium
paragraphs: MYP support sits in the middle of the Dubai market on price and at the difficult end on availability, which is the opposite of what families expect given how many tutors advertise the subjects involved.

On price: a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Budget online tuition at AED 33 to 65 — Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 — buys supervision, which for a younger MYP student who will not start a task alone can be exactly the right purchase. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, per Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500.

Serena sits at the upper end of that in-home range, because the round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes on a weekday afternoon. The premium is the drive rather than the teaching, and for MYP work it buys very little: the material is task sheets, descriptors and drafts, all of which work better on a shared screen that both people can annotate and that keeps the file. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE in any case, as that is an India-only service.

On availability, we would rather say it than let a family discover it. MYP Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education criterion work, and first-language Arabic at MYP level, are the hardest things to staff. Where we cannot cover a request we say so and suggest looking elsewhere rather than placing a general subject tutor into criterion marking they have never done.

faqs.question: Why do MYP families in Serena have a longer school run?
faqs.answer: Because IB provision is concentrated outside the Dubailand belt. The area is dense with British-curriculum schools, while full IB continuum provision sits mostly around Al Barsha and Jumeirah South, so most Serena MYP families drive past several schools to reach an IB one. International Baccalaureate programmes account for about 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment against 37 per cent on UK curricula, per Dubai Media Office figures for 2024-25, which is the market reason behind the geography.

faqs.question: What time can an MYP session start for a Serena student?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school. Children at the nearest Dubailand or Sustainable City schools are home around 15:50 and can start at 16:30, which is the best MYP slot available in this community. Students travelling back from the Al Barsha IB schools arrive between 16:20 and 16:50, which makes 18:00 the earliest sensible weekday start. For that second group the task-based work is better moved to a weekend morning, with the weekday slot used for marking and planning.

faqs.question: Why does a late MYP session achieve less than a late IGCSE one?
faqs.answer: Because the MYP has no past papers. In an examination-based course a tired student can still work through short questions usefully. MYP assessment is task-based — designing an investigation, generalising a pattern, analysing a text — and that work needs an uninterrupted stretch with an alert student. There is no equivalent filler, so a badly placed hour tends to produce nothing at all rather than something modest, which families often misread as the tutoring not working.

faqs.question: Which MYP work can be done late in the evening?
faqs.answer: Anything that responds to something already on the page. Marking a completed piece against the criterion descriptor, annotating a text, labelling a diagram, learning definitions, making a Personal Project journal entry, and planning what the next task will do differently. What does not work late is the task itself: investigation design, pattern generalisation, extended drafting and design specification all need concentration and belong in the best slot the week has, which for a long commute often means a weekend.

faqs.question: My child's MYP homework arrives in bursts. How do we manage it?
faqs.answer: With a calendar rather than more tutoring. MYP homework is task-based and eight subject groups do not coordinate, so load clusters unpredictably: a quiet week followed by one carrying a science write-up, a design specification, an extended piece of writing and an interdisciplinary unit. Get every deadline from every subject into one visible place as soon as it is set. Nearly every MYP crisis we see in this belt was a student discovering on Sunday that three tasks were due on Tuesday.

faqs.question: How should we read the criterion marks on an MYP report?
faqs.answer: Find the lowest of the four in each subject, because that is where the cheap improvement is. Each criterion is marked 0 to 8 for a total out of 32, converted to the 1 to 7 grade by boundaries the school applies, so moving one criterion from a 3 to a 6 adds three marks and often crosses a boundary while lifting all four by one adds four marks for four times the work. Then check whether the same criterion is low across several subjects, which points at a transferable skill rather than a subject.

faqs.question: What if the same criterion is weak in several subjects?
faqs.answer: Then you have a transferable skills gap, which is good news because one block of work improves several subjects at once. The usual candidates are investigation and design — Criterion B in Sciences and Mathematics — and critical evaluation, which is Criterion D in Individuals and Societies and appears in different wording elsewhere. Four to six sessions on the underlying skill, using the student's own marked tasks from two different subjects, typically moves marks in both rather than in one.

faqs.question: How much time does the Personal Project really need each week?
faqs.answer: Twenty minutes, every week, from the first fortnight — and that is the whole discipline. The criteria reward documented planning and honest reflection rather than an impressive final product, so the process journal is the evidence base and cannot be reconstructed from memory at the end. A project with a polished outcome and an empty journal cannot score well, and markers recognise a retrospective journal immediately. For a student losing fifty minutes a day to the road, the weekly slot has to be protected deliberately.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project goal?
faqs.answer: They can question it, which is the useful part. A goal must be achievable with the time and resources the student actually has — including a long commute and a short evening — and must generate something assessable. Narrower goals with documented iteration score better than ambitious ones with thin outcomes. What a tutor may not do is choose the goal, make the product, write journal entries retrospectively, or draft or rewrite the report. The school supervisor remains in charge throughout.

faqs.question: Does my MYP child still have to do Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: In a Dubai private school, yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes must be organised for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are prohibited. For a non-Arab student those are real timetabled periods with real homework, competing for the same shortened evening as the eight MYP subject groups.

faqs.question: Will an MYP tutor travel to our home in Serena?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, there is no IB Gram office or centre in the country, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, at the upper end for Serena because the round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes. For MYP work the premium buys little, since the material is task sheets, descriptors and drafts, which work well on a shared screen.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost from a Serena address?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Budget online tuition is AED 33 to 65, per Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which buys supervision — often the right purchase for a younger MYP student who will not start a task alone. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel. The usual efficient purchase here is a four to six session criterion block rather than a standing weekly arrangement.

faqs.question: Are group classes useful for the MYP?
faqs.answer: Rarely, because MYP assessment is individual and task-based. A group class delivers one sequence at one pace, which can help with subject content, and cannot address a specific criterion in a specific student's work — which is what MYP marks actually turn on. Counted properly a centre visit also costs about two hours of household time from Serena, given the drive to Motor City and the waiting. For criterion work, a short one-to-one or paired block is both cheaper and more effective.

faqs.question: Which MYP subjects are hardest to find tutors for?
faqs.answer: Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education criterion work, and first-language Arabic at MYP level. The subject content is not the obstacle; the obstacle is finding somebody who has marked those criteria and knows what the descriptors actually require. Where we cannot cover a request properly we say so and suggest looking elsewhere, rather than placing a general subject tutor into criterion marking they have never done. For those subjects, asking three to four weeks ahead is sensible with any provider.

intro.heading: MYP is not examined, which is why so few tutors can teach it
paragraphs: The honest answer to whether anyone nearby knows this programme is that fewer people do than for any other curriculum in Dubai, and the reason is structural rather than geographical. MYP has no external examination papers in most subjects and no past papers to work through. Instead each subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each marked out of 8, with descriptors written in language that a student has usually never been shown and a tutor has usually never read.

That makes MYP tutoring a different job from Diploma or IGCSE tutoring. A tutor who can teach the content of MYP Sciences to a competent standard may be entirely unable to explain why a student's investigation scored 4 out of 8 on criterion B rather than 6, which is the only question that matters to the grade. A parent who asks a prospective tutor what criterion C rewards in their child's subject will know within ten seconds whether the conversation is worth continuing.

There is a second reason the supply is thin. MYP is taught by IB continuum schools, which are a minority of Dubai's private sector: the International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of private-school enrolment in the emirate in 2024-25, against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum. Sobha Hartland is better served than most communities, with IB provision inside it and more a short drive away, but the number of teachers who have actually marked MYP work to criteria and live within a twenty-minute drive is small.

So rather than claim a local specialist, this page gives you the substance. It publishes the four criteria for each MYP subject group, because almost no competitor page in this market names a single one. It explains how four marks out of 8 are converted into the 1 to 7 grade that appears on a report, which is the piece parents most often misunderstand. It sets out the Personal Project boundary plainly, and it maps the MYP-to-Diploma gap subject by subject, because that transition is where most Hartland families first ask for help.

IB Gram delivers MYP tuition to Sobha Hartland as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the subject group rather than to the postcode. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons work from the criterion descriptors the school is using and from the student's own marked task sheets, because in a programme with no past papers the student's own work is the only legitimate evidence available.

Nothing on this page promises a grade. What it offers is the vocabulary to have a precise conversation with your child's teacher and with any tutor you are considering, which in a programme this widely misunderstood is worth more than a promise. A parent who can name the criterion their child is losing marks on has already done the hard part of the diagnosis.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.programmesIntro: MYP spans five years and its demands change substantially across them. These three stages carry different answers to the question of what tutoring should do, and conflating them is the commonest error in this part of the market.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, early years
programmes.description: The years where criterion language is introduced and where most students never quite learn it. Tasks are shorter, the content load is manageable, and the useful work is teaching a student to read the descriptor before starting rather than writing something and hoping. A student who learns in MYP 2 what criterion A actually asks for carries that into every subsequent task in every subject group.
programmes.countryNote: In the central corridor these are also the years when families transfer between schools and sometimes between curricula, arriving from British, American or Indian systems where criterion assessment does not exist. Those students are not behind on content; they are unfamiliar with how they are being judged, which is a quick and specific thing to fix.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, final years
programmes.description: The years that carry the Personal Project and the decisions about what follows. Tasks lengthen, criterion D in several subjects begins to demand genuine evaluation rather than description, and students who have coasted on content knowledge start to plateau. This is also when the Diploma or A Level choice is made, so readiness for Higher Level subjects becomes a live question rather than a distant one.
programmes.countryNote: Schools near Sobha Hartland offer both the IB Diploma and A Levels after MYP, so the final MYP years are a decision point rather than a formality. One session testing readiness for a particular Higher Level subject is the highest-value tutoring a Hartland family buys at this stage.

programmes.name: MYP eAssessment and the MYP Certificate
programmes.description: Some schools enter students for the IB's optional MYP eAssessment, which combines on-screen examinations and ePortfolios and leads to the MYP Certificate. Where it applies, preparation differs from ordinary coursework because the on-screen format and timing are unfamiliar. Where it does not apply, the school's internal criterion assessment stands alone, and a tutor needs to know which situation a student is in.
programmes.countryNote: Whether a school enters for eAssessment varies school by school and sometimes year by year, so it must be confirmed with the MYP coordinator rather than assumed from the fact that a school runs MYP. We ask the question before proposing a tutor, because the two situations need different preparation.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.subjectsIntro: MYP has eight subject groups and each has its own four criteria. These are the groups we cover for Sobha Hartland families, with the criterion that most often costs marks in each, because that is the level at which useful tutoring operates.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Marks are most often lost on investigating patterns, where students find a rule and never justify or generalise it, and on communicating, where notation is informal.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Processing and evaluating is the usual weak point: data presented without uncertainty, and evaluation that restates the method instead of criticising it.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria are analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students lose marks on analysing by describing what happens rather than how meaning is constructed, which is the same habit that limits Diploma English grades two years later.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Phase placement matters more than year group, and a student in the wrong phase will look weak while being correctly placed, or vice versa.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria are knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is where most of the contested marks sit, and it rewards weighing sources and perspectives rather than assembling more information.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria are inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Students frequently build something competent and lose marks because the inquiry and the testing against their own specification were thin.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria are investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. The process journal does much of the work here, and students who document after the fact rather than during lose marks they have genuinely earned in practice.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and reflective components surprise students who expected a practical subject to be assessed practically.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed separately with their own criteria, and frequently the lowest grade on a report because nobody has explained what is being asked. Usually a one-session fix once the student sees that integration itself is what is being marked.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: The culminating independent piece, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal and a report. Our support is process coaching only: the goal, the product and the writing are entirely the student's own.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.modesIntro: Three formats, all one-to-one and online, built around the criteria rather than around a syllabus. Which one applies depends on whether the problem is a criterion, a transition or the Personal Project.

modes.title: Criterion-focused weekly
modes.description: One session a week aimed at one named criterion in one subject group. The tutor reads the descriptor with the student, looks at the student's last marked task, and works specifically on what moves a 4 out of 8 towards a 6. Because MYP has no past papers, the material is the student's own work and the school's own task sheets, used with the student's teacher's marking visible.

modes.description: Four to six sessions in MYP 5 aimed at readiness for a particular post-16 subject. The student chooses the goal, makes the product and writes the report, and we say that to them in the first session.

sections.heading: The four criteria, by letter, for every MYP subject group
paragraphs: This is the content no competitor page in this market publishes. Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, each marked out of 8, and the criteria differ by subject group. A student does not have a general MYP ability. They have a profile across sixteen or more criteria spread over eight subject groups, and a report showing a 5 in Sciences and a 5 in Individuals and Societies can describe two completely different problems.

The table sets them out. What becomes obvious reading down it is how much of MYP assessment is about process rather than recall. Knowing and understanding appears as one criterion of four in several groups, which means content knowledge accounts for roughly a quarter of the grade in those subjects. The rest rewards inquiry, communication, evaluation and critical thinking, which are teachable skills that most students are never explicitly taught and most tutors never explicitly address.

Use it as a diagnostic tool. Ask your child which criterion their last task scored lowest on, in which subject. If they do not know, that is itself the finding, and the first session should be spent reading the descriptor with them. One caution: schools interpret task design differently within the programme and the IB revises subject guides periodically, so confirm the current criteria and the school's own task expectations with the MYP coordinator rather than relying on this or any other page.

One further point about reading the table. The criteria are not weighted equally in every reporting cycle, because an individual task may assess only two of the four, and schools combine marks across tasks in their own way within the programme's requirements. That is another reason to ask the school for the breakdown rather than inferring it, and a good reason to ask a prospective tutor how they would find out.

sections.heading: How four marks out of 8 become a grade from 1 to 7
paragraphs: This is the piece parents most often misunderstand, and understanding it changes how a report is read. Each of the four criteria is marked out of 8, giving a possible total of 32 for a subject. That total is then converted into the reported grade from 1 to 7 using published grade boundaries, which means the relationship between criterion marks and the final grade is not proportional and not linear.

The practical consequence is that one weak criterion can hold a grade down disproportionately. A student scoring 7, 7, 7 and 3 has a strong profile with a single specific problem, and the arithmetic treats them considerably worse than their classwork suggests. That is encouraging news rather than discouraging, because a single weak criterion is the most tractable thing in the whole programme: it is one skill, named, with a descriptor explaining exactly what a higher mark requires.

It also explains why generic MYP tutoring achieves so little. Working broadly across a subject spreads effort across four criteria, three of which may already be strong. Working on the one criterion that is weak moves the total by the most marks for the fewest hours. Ask the school for the criterion breakdown behind a reported grade rather than the grade alone; most schools record it and many report it, and it is the single most useful document in a Hartland family's possession.

One caveat on boundaries. The conversion from a total out of 32 to a grade from 1 to 7 is set by published grade boundaries that the IB defines for the programme, and schools apply them when reporting. They are not something a tutor should be guessing at, and a tutor who claims to know precisely what total produces a 6 without reference to the published boundaries is overstating what anyone can know from outside the school.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the culminating independent piece of MYP 5, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with a process journal and a report as evidence. It is also where tutoring is most likely to go wrong, because a student under deadline pressure with a half-finished product and an empty journal is exactly the customer an essay mill is looking for. At least one operator ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed assessed work outright, and the consequence of submitting it falls on the student.

What a tutor legitimately does is process coaching and nothing else. They may explain the criteria in the language the school is using. They may question a goal until it is specific and achievable within the time available, which is the single most valuable intervention because an over-ambitious goal is the usual cause of a poor project. They may explain that a process journal is contemporaneous evidence rather than something written up at the end, and they may teach a skill the project depends on.

What a tutor may not do is choose the goal, make or contribute to the product, supply content for the report, write or edit the report, or fabricate journal entries. We say all of that to the student directly in the first session, because a fifteen-year-old deserves the boundary before they are standing on it rather than afterwards. The same applies to any interdisciplinary unit or extended task, and we do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides or assessment materials; we reference them and point to the school's own copies.

sections.heading: The MYP-to-Diploma gap, subject by subject
paragraphs: This is where most Hartland families first look for a tutor, and it is worth being precise about what the gap actually is. It is not content. MYP students arriving in DP1 generally know enough and sometimes know more than their peers from examination systems. What they have not done is sit timed examination papers, work to mark schemes, or produce answers under the constraint of a command term. Those are the three things that cost them marks in the first DP1 term.

The gap differs by subject in a way that is predictable enough to plan around. In mathematics it is algebraic speed and no-calculator fluency, because MYP rewards investigation and does not test rapid manipulation. In the sciences it is the data-based paper and the discipline of showing calculation steps. In the humanities it is command terms, because MYP criterion language and Diploma command terms are different vocabularies for related ideas. In languages it is timed writing under pressure.

The good news is that each of these responds quickly, because they are procedural rather than conceptual. Four to six sessions in MYP 5 or early DP1, aimed at the specific procedural gap for a named subject, usually closes it. That is a far better purchase than a year of general support, and it is also the block that tells you whether a Higher Level choice is sound, which is the most expensive decision in the whole transition.

One thing the table cannot capture is attitude. A student who has spent five years being assessed on inquiry and reflection sometimes finds the Diploma's emphasis on timed recall a step backwards, and says so. That is a reasonable reaction and it is also not an argument, because the examination will happen either way. Naming the shift explicitly, as a change in what is being measured rather than a change in what matters, usually gets a student to engage with it faster than encouragement does.

rows: Algebraic speed; working without a calculator
A term of weekly drill for Higher Level

sections.heading: Six questions that reveal whether a tutor has taught MYP
paragraphs: Because there are no past papers to work through, MYP tutoring is unusually easy to fake and unusually easy to test. A tutor who has taught the programme can discuss criteria without notes; one who has not will talk about the subject instead. These six questions take two minutes and they are the most useful filter available to a Sobha Hartland parent.

Ask which four criteria apply to your child's subject group, by name. Ask what each criterion is marked out of, and what the subject total is. Ask how criterion marks become the 1 to 7 grade on the report. Ask what distinguishes a 6 from a 4 on the specific criterion your child scored lowest on. Ask whether the school enters students for MYP eAssessment, and what difference that makes. And ask what they will and will not do with a Personal Project.

A tutor who answers all six has taught MYP. A tutor who answers none may still be an excellent subject teacher and will be learning the assessment model on your time, which at a Diploma or IGCSE rate is not what you are paying for. Apply the questions to us as readily as to anyone else; we would rather be tested than believed, because in a programme this poorly understood a confident claim costs nothing to make.

One caution on how to use them. These are questions for a first conversation, not a test to spring on a tutor mid-lesson, and a tutor who needs to check a subject guide before answering the fourth one is being careful rather than ignorant. What you are listening for is whether criterion language is their working vocabulary or a translation they have to make, and that distinction is audible almost immediately.
bullets: Name the four criteria for my child's subject group
What is each criterion marked out of, and what is the subject total?
How do criterion marks become the 1 to 7 reported grade?
What separates a 6 from a 4 on the criterion my child scored lowest on?
Does my child's school enter for MYP eAssessment, and what changes if so?
What will you and will you not do with the Personal Project?

sections.heading: Online against a nearby tutor for an MYP student
paragraphs: MYP changes the balance of this comparison in two ways that are worth stating, because the honest answer is less one-sided than it is for a Diploma student. The first is age: an MYP 1 student is eleven, and presence in the room matters more at eleven than at seventeen. The second is scarcity: MYP-literate tutors are thin everywhere in Dubai, which makes the wider pool that online delivery opens up more valuable rather than less.

On matching, online wins decisively, and it is the point of this page. The number of people within a twenty-minute drive of Hartland who have marked MYP work to criteria in your child's subject group is very small, while the number available online is materially larger. On continuity, online wins, because families in this corridor move apartment and school more often than they plan to. On evidence, online tends to win, because drafted work against a descriptor exists as a document a parent can read.

On presence and on supervision of a younger child, a nearby tutor has a genuine advantage and we will not pretend otherwise. Market in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour because travel sits inside the figure, against about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online; those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so for a family who needs someone physically present, a local arrangement is the right route and these bands are what to judge it against.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and the MYP timetable
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspection on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. For an MYP family, the relevant part of a report is the commentary on the middle phase rather than the headline band, since a school strong at primary or Diploma level is not automatically strong in between.

Something that catches families new to Dubai is that the mandatory UAE subjects run alongside MYP, not instead of it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. It requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

The detail matters for scheduling. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. It also requires that school teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential question for the school rather than for a tutoring service. On our own position, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited and does not claim to be, since a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

The practical effect for a Hartland MYP student is a fuller timetable than the programme on paper suggests, with fewer free periods than a parent assumes when planning tutoring. That argues for one well-used weekly session rather than two, and for scheduling it early in the evening while the student is still able to work.

sections.heading: Getting started from Sobha Hartland, and what we say when a subject group is thin
paragraphs: Send four things. The subject group and the MYP year. The last reported grade with the criterion breakdown behind it if the school provides one, which is the single most useful document available. The teacher's last written comment, quoted rather than summarised. And the school's own task sheet for the most recent piece of work, because task design varies between schools under the same programme.

We propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson, which is a diagnosis rather than a sales call. Run the six questions from earlier in this page on whoever takes it. Afterwards, ask for a criterion-level account in writing: not that your child should read more, but that the losses sit in criterion C because notation is informal, or in criterion D because the evaluation restates the method. If the answer does not name a criterion, do not book the block.

And the honest part. MYP coverage is thinner than Diploma or IGCSE coverage across the whole market, and within MYP it is thinnest in Design, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Language Acquisition beyond the commonly taught languages. When nobody suitable is free we say so and offer a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE with genuine MYP experience working to Gulf Standard Time. We will not put a subject teacher with no criterion experience in front of an MYP student and charge a specialist rate for them to learn the model.

process.title: Send the subject group, the year and the criterion breakdown
process.description: MYP has eight subject groups with different criteria, so the group matters more than the subject name. If the school provides the criterion marks behind a reported grade, send them: they turn a vague worry into a named target in one step.

process.title: Include the school's own task sheet
process.description: Task design varies between schools under the same programme, so the sheet your child was actually given is better evidence than any general description of MYP. It also shows which criteria that particular task was assessing, which is rarely all four.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then the six questions
process.description: The first session costs nothing. Ask the tutor to name the four criteria for the subject group, what each is marked out of, and what separates a 6 from a 4 on the weakest one. A tutor who cannot will be learning the model on your time.

process.title: Target one criterion, not the subject
process.description: Working broadly spreads effort across four criteria, three of which may already be strong. Working on the weak one moves the total by the most marks for the fewest hours, which is why we ask for the breakdown before recommending anything.

process.title: Draft, redraft, against the descriptor
process.description: Because MYP has no past papers, the work between sessions is the student's own drafting measured against the descriptor rather than past-paper questions. The student reads the descriptor themselves; we do not summarise it for them.

process.title: Review against the next school task
process.description: Progress is judged on the next piece of marked school work, not on our impression of the sessions. If the criterion mark has not moved after two tasks, the plan changes rather than continuing.

whyPoints.title: The criteria published, by letter and by subject group
whyPoints.description: Almost no page in this market names a single MYP criterion. We publish all four for each of the eight subject groups, because that is the level at which MYP grades are actually decided and the level at which a tutor's knowledge can be tested.

whyPoints.title: The grade conversion explained
whyPoints.description: Four criteria out of 8 give a total out of 32, converted to a 1 to 7 grade by published boundaries. That is why one weak criterion holds a grade down disproportionately, and why it is also the most tractable problem in the programme.

whyPoints.title: Six questions instead of a claim
whyPoints.description: Rather than assert criterion literacy, we give you the questions that test it in two minutes, including what separates a 6 from a 4 on a named criterion. Apply them to us as readily as to anyone else.

whyPoints.title: The transition gap mapped by subject
whyPoints.description: MYP students arrive in DP1 without timed papers, mark schemes or command terms, and the gap differs by subject in a predictable way. Four to six targeted sessions usually closes it, which is a better purchase than a year of general support.

whyPoints.title: Personal Project boundaries stated to the student
whyPoints.description: Process coaching only: the goal, the product, the journal and the report are entirely the student's. We say so to them in the first session rather than in small print, because the pressure arrives later.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed
whyPoints.description: MYP is thinner across this market than Diploma or IGCSE, and thinnest in Design, Arts, Physical and Health Education and the less common languages. We say so before you book, and we will not have a subject teacher learn the assessment model at your expense.

faqs.question: Why is an MYP tutor harder to find than a Diploma or IGCSE one?
faqs.answer: Because MYP has no external examination papers in most subjects and no past papers to work through. Each subject is assessed against four criteria marked out of 8, with descriptors most tutors have never read, so the skill required is criterion literacy rather than examination technique. On top of that, MYP is taught by IB continuum schools, which are a minority of Dubai's private sector, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum. The teaching population is simply smaller.

faqs.question: What are the four MYP criteria in my child's subject?
faqs.answer: They differ by subject group. Mathematics uses knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Sciences uses knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Language and Literature uses analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. The full set for all eight groups is in the table on this page. Each criterion is marked out of 8, and subject guides are revised periodically, so confirm the current set with the MYP coordinator.

faqs.question: How does a mark out of 8 turn into the grade on my child's report?
faqs.answer: The four criterion marks, each out of 8, give a subject total out of 32, which is then converted into the reported grade from 1 to 7 using published grade boundaries. The relationship is not proportional, which is why one weak criterion can hold a grade down more than a parent expects. A profile of 7, 7, 7 and 3 totals 24 and describes a strong student with one specific gap. That is encouraging, because a single named criterion is the most tractable thing in the programme.

faqs.question: My child's MYP grade dropped but the teacher says they are doing well. Which is it?
faqs.answer: Often both, and the criterion breakdown resolves it. Different tasks assess different criteria, so a grade can fall because a task weighted towards a weak criterion came round, rather than because performance declined. Ask the school for the criterion marks behind the reported grade rather than the grade alone. If three criteria are strong and one is weak, the teacher's impression and the arithmetic are both accurate, and the fix is a few sessions on the named criterion rather than general subject support.

faqs.question: How much help is a tutor allowed to give on the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Only with process, and the boundary is specific. A tutor may explain the criteria, question a goal until it is specific and achievable in the time available, explain that a process journal is contemporaneous evidence rather than something written up at the end, and teach a skill the project depends on. A tutor may not choose the goal, make or contribute to the product, supply content, write or edit the report, or fabricate journal entries. We state this to the student in the first session, because the deadline pressure arrives later.

faqs.question: What is the real gap between MYP and the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Not content, in most cases. MYP students usually arrive in DP1 knowing enough, and sometimes more than peers from examination systems. What they have not done is sit timed papers, work to a mark scheme, or answer under the constraint of a command term. In mathematics the gap is algebraic speed and no-calculator fluency; in the sciences it is data-based papers and showing calculation steps; in the humanities it is command terms. Each responds to four to six targeted sessions because the gap is procedural rather than conceptual.

faqs.question: Is my child ready for Higher Level sciences after MYP?
faqs.answer: A single session can give you a defensible answer, and it is the most valuable tutoring an MYP 5 family buys. Readiness is not the MYP grade; it is whether the student can handle examination-format questions under time with calculation steps shown, which MYP does not test. We give a written verdict you can take to the school. Getting this wrong is the most expensive decision in the transition, because a student placed above their foundation may need weekly support across both Diploma years just to hold a 4.

faqs.question: Does MYP have exams, and what is eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Most MYP assessment is internal and criterion-based, with no external papers. Some schools additionally enter students for the IB's optional MYP eAssessment, which combines on-screen examinations and ePortfolios and leads to the MYP Certificate. Where it applies, preparation differs because the on-screen format and timing are unfamiliar. Whether a school enters varies school by school and sometimes year by year, so confirm it with the MYP coordinator. We ask the question before proposing a tutor, since the two situations need different work.

faqs.question: My child moved from a British school into MYP. What do they need?
faqs.answer: Usually the assessment model explained rather than the content retaught, which is a quick and specific job. A student arriving from a system without criterion assessment will write something competent and score moderately, because they are answering a question nobody asked. One or two sessions reading the descriptors with them, followed by a redrafted task measured against the descriptor, typically changes the next grade. Mid-year transfers are common in this corridor, so this is one of the more frequent requests we see from Hartland families.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups are hardest to find tutors for?
faqs.answer: Design, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Language Acquisition beyond the commonly taught languages, because few tutors have marked those criteria and tuition centres build around examination syllabuses instead. Mathematics, Sciences, Language and Literature, and Individuals and Societies are better covered. We tell you which category your subject group falls into before you book, and when nobody suitable is free we offer a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor outside the UAE with genuine MYP experience, disclosed as such.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education requirement affect MYP students?
faqs.answer: It does, and families new to Dubai are often surprised. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of these subjects. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. The practical effect is a fuller timetable than the programme suggests, which argues for one well-used weekly session rather than two.

faqs.question: What is an interdisciplinary unit and why did my child score badly on it?
faqs.answer: It is a unit assessed across two or more subject groups with its own criteria, and students frequently score below their usual level because nobody has explained that the integration itself is what is being marked. A student who produces good work in each discipline separately, without connecting them, is answering the wrong question. It is usually a one-session fix once they see what is being assessed, and it is worth asking about specifically, because an interdisciplinary mark often sits oddly low on an otherwise consistent report.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring suitable for an eleven or twelve year old?
faqs.answer: It works, with one condition: an adult in the house, not in the room, for the first few sessions, so the student knows help is available if something technical goes wrong. Beyond that, younger students often engage well because a screen-shared document gives them something concrete to work on. The honest counterpoint is that presence matters more at eleven than at seventeen, so if your child genuinely needs someone beside them, a local arrangement is better. We do not send tutors to UAE homes at all.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a single weak criterion take to move?
faqs.answer: Three to five, in most cases, because a criterion is one named skill with a descriptor explaining exactly what a higher mark requires. The work is reading the descriptor, looking at the last marked task, drafting against the descriptor and redrafting. Progress is judged on the next piece of marked school work rather than on our impression of the sessions. If the criterion mark has not moved across two subsequent tasks, the plan changes rather than the block being extended.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit for MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: The permit requirement is about private tutoring generally rather than about any programme. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications run through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: What should I send to get the most useful recommendation?
faqs.answer: Four things, and one of them does most of the work. The subject group and MYP year. The criterion breakdown behind the last reported grade, if the school provides it, which turns a vague worry into a named target immediately. The teacher's last written comment, quoted rather than paraphrased. And the school's own task sheet for the most recent piece of work, because task design varies between schools under the same programme and the sheet shows which criteria that task actually assessed.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.closingHeading: Ask for the criterion, not the subject
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-sobha-hartland.closingBody: MYP grades are decided criterion by criterion, and a report showing a 5 can describe four completely different problems. The useful first step is not booking hours but finding the criterion: ask the school for the breakdown behind the grade, send it with the subject group, the year and the school's own task sheet, and we will propose a tutor and run the first session free. Then ask the six questions on this page, and judge the criterion-level account you get afterwards rather than the impression of the lesson.

intro.heading: Why MYP tutoring is the easiest thing in Dubai to overbuy
paragraphs: Every other tutoring purchase has a natural end. An IGCSE arrangement finishes at the June series. A Diploma arrangement finishes when the papers are sat. The Middle Years Programme has no terminal examination for most of its length, which means there is nothing in the structure of the programme that tells a family when to stop. A weekly session arranged in MYP 2 because a report looked disappointing can still be running in MYP 5, and nobody has decided it should be.

That is the single most expensive feature of MYP support in this market, and it is nobody's fault in particular. Published Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session, read in October 2026, put budget tutoring at AED 240 to 600 a month, mid-market at AED 600 to 1,200 and specialist support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more, according to Bestimate's rate table. Run the mid-market figure across three school years without a stopping point and the total is a serious number that nobody ever decided to spend.

The second expensive feature is that MYP reports hide the lever. A subject grade from 1 to 7 is the sum of four criterion levels out of 8, converted through published boundaries. A student on a total of 18 is one achievement level short of the next grade. A student on 15 has a whole band to climb. Those two families get the same letter, receive the same worry, and buy the same package, and only one of them was ever a few sessions away from a visible result.

So this page prices the thing in the only unit that makes sense, which is what it costs to move an achievement level. It names the interventions that are cheapest, including two that cost nothing at all and that most Barsha Heights families never think to request from the school. And it names the five ways MYP money reliably disappears, none of which involves a dishonest tutor and all of which are visible in advance.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the task sheet, the rubric and the student's own draft shared on screen. Barsha Heights has no large school campus of its own, so children are bussed outward and return late, and the absence of a fourth journey in the week is worth something. What the format mainly buys, though, is a tutor who has taught that subject group's criteria.

Two disclaimers belong at the front rather than the back. Nothing here claims that IB Gram is approved or accredited by the International Baccalaureate or by any UAE regulator, because it is not. And no examination or results date appears anywhere on this page, because the International Baccalaureate's own site blocks automated access and no date in this project has been confirmed from source; the May session is the one UAE schools sit, and your MYP coordinator holds the authoritative internal deadlines that actually shape a term.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-tecom.programmesIntro: Where a student sits in the programme changes what is worth spending, and in MYP the difference between the stages is larger than in any other curriculum.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The years with the least at stake and therefore the years where open-ended spending is hardest to justify. Nothing here feeds a certificate or a sixth-form application. What is genuinely worth buying is rubric literacy: a short block teaching a student to read a task sheet, identify which criteria are assessed and recognise that a strand asking for evaluation will not pay for description.
programmes.countryNote: Barsha Heights students travel to campuses across Al Barsha, Al Barsha South and Al Sufouh, and families moving between school groups mid-key-stage arrive without the rubric habit. The first term's grades usually reflect that adjustment rather than the child's understanding, which is a reason to wait a term before buying anything.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 10 to 11
programmes.description: Where spending starts to earn its keep. Tasks lengthen, interdisciplinary work appears, the Personal Project runs across MYP 5, and for certificate candidates the on-screen examinations arrive at the end. These are the years where a concentrated block timed to a specific deadline produces a visible change rather than a reassuring feeling.
programmes.countryNote: Certificate requirements, including minimum grades and a points total, are published by the International Baccalaureate and administered by schools, so confirm the current conditions with your MYP coordinator. The on-screen examination session UAE schools sit is in May; no date is published here, since none in this project has been confirmed from the IB's own site.

programmes.name: The Handover to the Diploma
programmes.description: The highest-return spend in the whole programme and the one most families miss, because it falls in a holiday. Six to eight sessions converting criterion-trained habits into timed, mark-scheme answering. Done in the summer it is unhurried and cheap; discovered in October after a poor first Diploma assessment, it is a rescue with a confidence problem attached.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, as part of 16,846 new places. More Barsha Heights families than before will be running this handover, and treating it as a defined summer block rather than an open term-time arrangement is both cheaper and more effective.

programmes.name: The IGCSE Alternative at 16
programmes.description: Several campuses this community feeds run Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE at 16 instead of MYP 4 and 5, and families cross between the systems without moving house. The crossover is worth a term of specific support in either direction, because criterion-based and mark-scheme-based assessment reward genuinely different behaviour from a student.
programmes.countryNote: A student moving from MYP 3 into a Year 10 IGCSE cohort has strong research habits and no experience of tiered, timed papers. A student moving the other way has to stop writing the maximum and start writing to a strand. Budget one term for the adjustment rather than treating the first set of grades as a verdict.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-tecom.subjectsIntro: MYP assesses eight subject groups on four criteria each. These are the groups Barsha Heights families most often ask about, with the strand where the levels are and an honest note on what it costs to shift.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is the outlier and the cheapest to improve: it wants a general rule found, described, verified and justified, and students stop at the pattern. Two or three sessions on that habit typically move a level.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C costs the most levels and is inexpensive to fix, because students process data correctly and then describe their graph where the strand wants an evaluation of method validity.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.levels: Phases set by school, criteria A-D
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Criterion A is where the levels sit: students summarise where the strand rewards analysis of the writer's choices and their effect. Slower to shift than a mathematics strand, because it is a reading habit rather than a procedure.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. The important variable here is free: phase placement. A student assessed in a phase above their fluency after a school move will score low whatever tutoring is bought, and the school can review it.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Criterion D is the hardest strand in the programme: interpretation of sources, recognition of perspectives, evaluation of limitations. A confident narrative answer earns almost nothing, and the fix is a template rather than more content.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The group most often under-prepared because it feels practical. The levels sit in the documentation: a research plan, testable specifications, and an evaluation against those specifications rather than against appearance.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. Genuinely talented students lose levels on the two written criteria, because contextual knowledge and critical response are assessed alongside the work and the process journal carries more weight than the finished piece suggests.

subjects.name: MYP Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Two of the four criteria are written, which is why athletic students score lower than families expect. Criterion D wants an evidenced reflection against a plan, not an account of a match.

subjects.name: MYP Interdisciplinary Learning
subjects.description: Assessed against its own criteria, requiring integration of two subject groups and a reflection on the integration itself. Treated as a project rather than an assessment by most students, and the reflection strand is where levels vanish because the writing describes activity rather than evaluating the integration.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: Planning, applying skills and reflecting, evidenced through a process journal and a report alongside the product. The product is not marked. Money spent on building a more impressive product buys nothing; money spent on journal discipline early in MYP 5 buys the whole component, and it cannot be bought late.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside MYP in every Dubai private school regardless of licensed curriculum. For non-Arab students, Arabic as an additional language usually sits inside Language Acquisition, where phase placement after a school move is a recurring and free-to-check source of unexpected grades.

subjects.name: Rubric literacy as a subject in itself
subjects.description: Not a subject group but the cheapest useful purchase in the programme. Reading a task sheet, identifying the assessed criteria, distinguishing describe from explain from evaluate, and self-assessing a draft against a descriptor. Three or four sessions, once, and it transfers to all eight groups for the rest of the programme.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs in Dubai, and in what unit
paragraphs: Begin with the published market, every figure credited to the provider that published it and read in October 2026, none of it IB Gram's price list. Budget online and university-student tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International Baccalaureate from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session give the other view: AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. In-home rates themselves are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, travel included.

Now the unit that matters, which is not the hour. In the Middle Years Programme the thing a family is buying is an achievement level. Each of four criteria is marked out of 8, the four are summed to a total out of 32, and that total converts to the reported 1-7 grade through published boundaries that are not evenly spaced. So the right question is not what an hour costs. It is how many achievement levels are available, in which criterion, and what the block to move them would cost.

That reframing changes decisions immediately. A student whose criterion profile is 7, 7, 3, 6 has a single large lever and a three-to-five session block aimed at one strand will show on the next report. A student whose profile is 5, 5, 5, 5 has no single lever, needs rubric literacy across the board, and should be buying a short general block rather than a subject-specific retainer. Same grade, different purchases, different amounts of money, and the grade alone does not distinguish them.

sections.heading: What one achievement level is actually worth
paragraphs: This is the arithmetic that should sit underneath every MYP spending decision and almost never does. Four criteria, each out of 8, summed to a total out of 32, converted to a grade from 1 to 7 through published boundaries. The boundaries are uneven, which means the value of one achievement level depends entirely on where the student currently sits. Ask the MYP coordinator for the criterion levels rather than the grade, because the grade hides this completely.

Read the table and find your child. A total of 18 sits one level below the next grade. A total of 23 sits one level below the one after that. A total of 15 is at the bottom of its band with a long climb ahead. Those three students might all be described by a parent as doing alright but not brilliantly, and the right purchase for each is different: a narrow block, a narrow block, and a broader piece of work respectively.

There is a second, subtler point in the table. Levels are cheapest to buy at the top of a band, because the student is already producing work close to the next descriptor and the gap is usually a specific missing move, such as a justification sentence or an evaluation paragraph. Levels are most expensive at the bottom of a band, because the gap is understanding rather than execution. A family at the bottom of a band who buys a three-session block will be disappointed, and the honest thing is to say so before they buy it.

Used this way the arithmetic also tells a family when to stop, which is the thing MYP structurally fails to do. If the criterion profile has moved and the subject is now consistently strong across all four strands, the work is done and the block should end. A tutoring arrangement that never recommends its own conclusion is selling reassurance, and in a programme with no terminal examination that arrangement can run for three years before anybody notices.

sections.heading: The five ways MYP money disappears
paragraphs: None of these involves a dishonest tutor. They are mismatches between what was bought and what the student needed, and every one is visible before the money moves. A family that recognises its own pattern here will usually spend less and see more, which is an odd argument for a tutoring page and is also true.

The first is tutoring the subject rather than the strand. A student losing levels on Criterion C in sciences does not need more science; they need three sessions on evaluating method validity rather than describing a graph. Buying a term of general science support is competent and ineffective. The second is a retainer running across MYP 1 to 3, where nothing feeds a certificate or an application and where the first term's grades after a school move usually reflect adjustment rather than ability.

The third is paying for the Personal Project product. Families fund materials, equipment and extra sessions aimed at making the product more impressive, and the product is not what is marked. Planning, applying skills and reflecting are, evidenced through the process journal and the report. Money spent on the product buys nothing assessable; money spent on fortnightly journal discipline early in MYP 5 buys the component outright and cannot be spent usefully late.

The fourth is buying exam preparation in a programme that has no examinations until the end of MYP 5, which is a mismatch that sounds reassuring and teaches the wrong habits. And the fifth is the most expensive: paying for something the school would have fixed for free. Phase placement in Language Acquisition and set placement in mathematics are both reviewable on request, and a student assessed in a phase above their fluency after a school move will score low no matter what is bought.

sections.heading: The two free fixes most families never ask for
paragraphs: Before buying anything, there are two requests a parent can make of the school that cost nothing and that occasionally remove the problem entirely. Both are routine administrative reviews, both are reasonable to ask for, and both are more likely to be relevant to a Barsha Heights family than to most, because this community has a high rate of mid-year school moves driven by employer relocations and tower-to-villa changes.

The first is phase placement in Language Acquisition. The group is organised in phases from 1 to 6, and placement should reflect fluency rather than year group. A student arriving from another school is frequently placed by age or by a brief assessment taken in their first week, and if the phase is above their actual fluency they will score low on every criterion indefinitely. No amount of tutoring corrects a placement error; the coordinator can review it, and the review is free.

The second is set placement in mathematics, where schools running Standard and Extended mathematics have to decide which a student takes. A student in Extended who is not ready produces mid-band work across all four criteria and looks weaker than they are. A student in Standard who is comfortable produces high levels and may be under-challenged. Either way the school holds the data, and asking what the placement was based on is a reasonable question with a free answer.

There is a third free request worth making even when nothing is wrong, which is for the four criterion levels behind each reported grade. Schools hold them, some blend them with internal percentages for parent-facing reports, and the raw levels are the only version of the information that tells you what to do next. Asking for them costs an email and changes every subsequent spending decision, because it converts a letter into a lever.

sections.heading: The cheapest interventions in the programme, ranked
paragraphs: Ranked by what they cost against what they move, which is a different order from how often they are sold. The top of this list is dominated by short, narrow, one-off work and by things the school does for nothing. The bottom is dominated by open-ended arrangements that feel responsible and produce little.

Rubric literacy sits at the top of the paid items and is bought once. Three or four sessions teaching a student to read a task sheet, identify the assessed criteria, distinguish describe from explain from evaluate, and self-assess a draft against the descriptor. It transfers to all eight subject groups and lasts the rest of the programme, which makes the cost per subsequent task extremely low. Most families buy content instead, which transfers to nothing.

A single-criterion block is next: three to five sessions aimed at one strand in one subject group, timed to a specific summative deadline. It is narrow by design, because narrow work produces a visible level change and broad work usually produces a reassuring feeling. Below that comes Personal Project journal discipline, cheap per session and spread fortnightly across MYP 5, which is the only version of that support that works at all.

The summer handover block before the Diploma sits oddly in this ranking, because it is more expensive per hour than anything above it and still represents the best value in the whole programme. Six to eight sessions converting criterion habits into timed, mark-scheme answering, bought in a holiday rather than in a term. The alternative is discovering the gap in October of DP1 after a poor first assessment, which costs more in sessions and considerably more in confidence.

sections.heading: MYP 5 eAssessment, the one place exam-style spending makes sense
paragraphs: Most of this page argues against buying examination preparation in the Middle Years Programme, so the exception needs stating clearly. Students entered for the IB MYP certificate sit on-screen examinations at the end of MYP 5, in the session UAE schools take in May, alongside moderated ePortfolios for the subject groups assessed that way and the Personal Project. For many Dubai students this is the first timed external assessment of their school life.

That makes a short block of timed practice in the final term genuinely worthwhile, and it is the only point in the programme where it is. The skills are specific: working to a clock, reading a question under pressure, producing a complete answer rather than the best possible answer, and navigating an on-screen format rather than paper. None of those are taught by criterion work, and all of them are foreign to a student who has spent four years producing drafts with feedback available.

Confirm the certificate requirements with your MYP coordinator rather than with any tutoring provider. The International Baccalaureate publishes minimum grades and a points total and schools administer the process directly, so the coordinator holds the authoritative current conditions. No examination or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated access and no date in this project has been confirmed from source. The May session is the one UAE schools sit.

On spending shape, treat this as a defined block in the final term rather than a reason to start a year-long arrangement in MYP 4. Four to six sessions of timed practice, scheduled around the school's own mock and preparation calendar, with the hours going into execution rather than content. A student whose criterion levels are already strong needs very little of it; a student whose levels are strong and whose timed performance is poor needs exactly it and nothing else.

sections.heading: Spending in MYP against spending in the Diploma
paragraphs: The useful comparison for a Barsha Heights family is not this term against last term. It is the Middle Years Programme years against the Diploma years, because the Diploma is where the expensive tutoring actually sits and where a grade has consequences for an application. Money spent in MYP is only well spent if it reduces what has to be spent later, and some of it genuinely does.

Two MYP purchases reduce Diploma spending reliably. Rubric literacy produces a student who can read assessment criteria, which is exactly the skill the Diploma Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay demand. And the summer handover block produces a student who can write to time against a mark scheme, which is the single most common gap in a DP1 cohort arriving from the Middle Years Programme. Both are short, defined and one-off.

Several MYP purchases reduce nothing. A three-year weekly retainer through MYP 1 to 3 produces a student accustomed to having help available, which is not a transferable skill and is sometimes an obstacle. Funding an impressive Personal Project product buys nothing assessable in MYP and nothing at all in the Diploma. Premium rates for middle-school content teaching spend Diploma money a year or two early and leave less for the year when it counts.

For context on the household rather than the subject: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. A frozen fee year is a reasonable moment to fund the two MYP purchases that carry forward, and a poor moment to start an open-ended arrangement that will still be running when the Diploma does.
