sections.heading: Personal Project boundaries, copyright and status
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the component where the market around Dubai is most likely to cross a line, because it is a discrete document and a product that somebody could simply produce. Research for this project found a provider selling completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. That is not tutoring, and its malpractice consequences fall on the student rather than the seller.

What a tutor may legitimately do is clear enough to apply. Teach the assessment criteria, discuss the student's goal, explain what the report has to evidence, ask the questions that make a reflection sharper, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A useful test is whether the school's own supervisor could do the same thing openly in a scheduled meeting. If they could, so can a tutor.

What a tutor may not do: write the report, write journal entries, design or build the product, or edit text until the words stop being the student's. Nor may anybody legitimately distribute International Baccalaureate subject guides, criteria documents or assessment materials as downloads, because those are the IB's copyright. We reference them, link to the official source and work from them inside a session, and your child's school can reach the material directly.

On status: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, certified or licensed by the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, and claims none of those relationships. We run no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, with the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years; tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule.

sections.heading: Booking, and the block we will tell you not to buy
paragraphs: Send the subject group, the MYP year, the most recent task sheet with its rubric, and the four criterion levels behind the reported grade if the school has given them to you. If they have not, ask for them first, because they decide the size of the purchase. The first session is free and is spent on that real task with the descriptors open, and the student working rather than listening.

You then receive a short written note: which strand is costing levels, whether the profile is spiky or flat, and the smallest block that would realistically move it. Sometimes that note says three sessions. Occasionally it says to speak to the school about a phase or set placement before buying anything at all. We would rather send that note than sell a term, because in a programme without a terminal examination a term quietly becomes three years.

Scheduling follows the bus. Barsha Heights has no large campus of its own, so children return on multi-stop routes between a quarter past five and six, and the workable weekday slots are 17:30 and 18:00. Personal Project sessions usually move to weekend mornings, which suits sustained writing after a full school week better than a weekday evening. During Ramadan, sessions shift to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there, with the same tutor keeping the same student.

Two coverage limits stated before you commit. MYP Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education are thinner on our side than mathematics, sciences and language and literature, and a specific weekend slot in one of those takes longer to staff. We will give you a date rather than take a booking and hope. And if no UAE-based tutor is free for your combination, we will say whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time, and you may decline. IB Gram runs no home visits in Dubai.

process.description: Progress is measured on the next criterion level the school issues. whyPoints.description: The Middle Years Programme is bought by the hour and measured in criterion levels, and the two are not the same thing. whyPoints.description: MYP has no terminal examination for most of its length, so nothing in its structure tells a family when to stop. Our blocks are three to five sessions aimed at one strand and one deadline, measured on the next criterion level, and they finish rather than renew.

whyPoints.description: Six to eight summer sessions after MYP 5, converting criterion habits into timed answering against a mark scheme, is the highest-return spend in the programme and the one most often skipped because it falls in a holiday. It also reduces what has to be spent in the Diploma, which is where the expensive years are.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for MYP support in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Less than most families end up spending, and the unit matters more than the figure. Published Dubai estimates read in October 2026 put a weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist support, according to Bestimate. But the Middle Years Programme has no terminal examination for most of its length, so a monthly arrangement has no natural end. Budget for a defined block aimed at one criterion rather than for a monthly commitment.

faqs.question: Why is MYP tutoring so easy to overbuy?
faqs.answer: Because nothing in the programme's structure tells you when to stop. Other arrangements end at an examination; most of MYP is internally assessed through summative tasks spread across terms, so a weekly session arranged in MYP 2 after a disappointing report can still be running in MYP 5 without anybody having decided it should. Reports also hide the lever, showing a 1-7 grade rather than the four criterion levels behind it, so a family cannot see whether they are one achievement level away or six.

faqs.question: What does one MYP achievement level actually cost to move?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on where the student sits in their band, which is why the criterion levels matter more than the grade. At the top of a band, say a total of 18 out of 32, the gap to the next grade is often one specific missing move such as a justification sentence or an evaluation paragraph, and three to five sessions on that strand will show on the next report. At the bottom of a band the gap is understanding rather than execution, and a short block will disappoint. We say which you have before quoting.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion gives the best return for a short block?
faqs.answer: The evaluation or reflection strand, in almost every subject group. Criterion C in sciences wants an evaluation of method validity and students describe their graph. Criterion B in mathematics wants a general rule justified and students stop at the pattern. Criterion D in individuals and societies wants source evaluation and students write confident narrative. Each of those is a specific missing move rather than a body of knowledge, which makes three to five sessions a realistic size for a visible change.

faqs.question: What free fixes should we ask the school about first?
faqs.answer: Three, all routine and all more relevant after a mid-year school move, which Barsha Heights families make often. Whether the Language Acquisition phase matches your child's actual fluency, because a student placed above it will score low indefinitely and no tutoring corrects a placement error. What the mathematics set placement was based on and when it is reviewed. And the four criterion levels behind each reported grade, which the school holds and which convert a letter into something you can act on.

faqs.question: Is the Personal Project product worth spending money on?
faqs.answer: No, because it is not what is assessed. The marks go to planning, applying skills and reflecting, evidenced through the process journal and the report that accompany the product. A modest product with a thoroughly documented process consistently outscores an impressive product with a thin journal. Money spent on materials, equipment or extra sessions aimed at the product buys nothing assessable. Money spent on fortnightly journal discipline from the start of MYP 5 buys the whole component, and it cannot be spent usefully in the final month.

faqs.question: Should we buy exam practice for an MYP student?
faqs.answer: Only in the final term of MYP 5, and only for certificate candidates. Most of the programme is internally assessed against criteria, so timed-paper practice in MYP 2 or 3 teaches a habit the programme does not yet assess. Students entered for the IB MYP certificate do sit on-screen examinations at the end of MYP 5, and for many Dubai students that is their first timed external assessment, which makes a four to six session block of execution practice genuinely worthwhile at that point and not before.

faqs.question: What is the single best-value spend across the whole programme?
faqs.answer: The summer handover block after MYP 5, six to eight sessions converting criterion-trained habits into timed answering against a board mark scheme. It is more expensive per hour than most of what sits above it on a value ranking and still the best purchase, because the alternative is discovering the gap in October of DP1 after a poor first assessment. That costs more in sessions and considerably more in a student's confidence, and it falls in a term rather than a holiday.

faqs.question: Is rubric literacy really worth paying for separately?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest genuinely useful thing in the programme, and it is bought once. Three or four sessions teaching a student to read a task sheet, identify which criteria are assessed, distinguish describe from explain from evaluate, and self-assess a draft against the descriptor before a teacher sees it. It transfers to all eight subject groups and lasts the rest of MYP, which makes the cost per subsequent task very low. Most families buy subject content instead, and subject content transfers to nothing.

faqs.question: Does paying a premium rate help a middle-school student?
faqs.answer: Rarely. Published Dubai rates reach AED 650 an hour at the premium end, with specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, and almost nothing in the Middle Years Programme requires that level of specialism. A qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 covers criterion work and rubric literacy perfectly well, and routine supervision in MYP 1 to 3 sits comfortably in the budget band. Paying premium rates in middle school spends Diploma money a year or two early, when the Diploma is where the grade actually has consequences.

faqs.question: Is in-home MYP tutoring worth the extra cost in Barsha Heights?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the local arithmetic is against it. Published in-home rates are AED 180 to 350 from Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, with travel inside the figure, and a tutor driving into Barsha Heights at half past five arrives with a variable twenty minutes attached. What is scarce in MYP is a tutor who has actually taught that subject group's criteria, and MYP cohorts in this corridor are small, so the nearby pool is thin. Presence in the room is real but it is not the scarce thing.

faqs.question: How do we know when to stop paying for MYP support?
faqs.answer: When the criterion levels have moved and the strand is consistently strong. That is the only honest measure, and it requires having asked the school for the levels in the first place. A total of 28 or more out of 32 reported as a grade 7 means the subject is secure across all four criteria and the money is better moved to the Diploma handover. An arrangement that never recommends its own conclusion is selling reassurance, and in a programme with no terminal examination it can run for years unchallenged.

faqs.question: What time can MYP sessions run for Barsha Heights families?
faqs.answer: Usually 17:30 or 18:00 on a weekday. The community contains no large school campus, so children are bussed outward and return on multi-stop routes between a quarter past five and six rather than at a bell. Personal Project sessions generally move to weekend mornings, which suits sustained writing better than a weekday evening after a full school day and a commute. During Ramadan, sessions shift to post-Iftar slots for families who want them there, with the same tutor keeping the same student.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of the Personal Project report?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria, discuss the student's goal, explain what the report has to evidence, ask the questions that sharpen a reflection, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write the report, write journal entries, design or build the product, or edit text until the words stop being the student's. A workable test is whether the school supervisor could do the same thing openly. The student declares the work authentic and a breach falls on them.

faqs.question: What if you cannot staff the MYP subject group we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a date, rather than taking the booking and hoping. MYP Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education are thinner on our side than mathematics, sciences and language and literature, and a specific weekend slot in one of those takes longer to fill than a mathematics request on a weekday. If no UAE-based tutor is free for your combination, we will say whether a tutor based elsewhere can cover your hour in Gulf Standard Time, and you may decline. No competitor researched for this project publishes a coverage limit.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-tecom.closingHeading: Ask for the criterion levels before you ask for a quote
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-tecom.closingBody: Almost every expensive mistake in Middle Years Programme tutoring starts with a reported grade and a worry rather than with the four numbers behind it. A total of 18 out of 32 is one achievement level from the next grade and a short block will show on the next report. A total of 15 is a band away and will not. The school holds those numbers, the request is free, and the answer determines the size of everything that follows. Ask for them, check whether a phase or set placement needs reviewing, and then send us the subject group, the MYP year and the last task sheet with its rubric. The free trial will come back with the smallest block that would realistically move the level. Lessons are one-to-one online, in Gulf Standard Time.

Each names the groups and year levels they have taught, so you can check the match before the first session.

intro.heading: Why nobody near you seems to know this programme
paragraphs: The scarcity is real and it has a cause. The Middle Years Programme is a five-year framework rather than an examined syllabus. There is no public question bank to work from, no mark scheme to memorise, and no standard textbook that maps onto what a school actually assesses. A tutor who has spent a decade teaching Cambridge IGCSE has nothing transferable except the subject content itself, and in the MYP the subject content is the smaller half of the grade.

What is being assessed instead is four criteria per subject group, each marked on a band from zero to eight. In mathematics those criteria are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student can be fluent in the mathematics and score poorly, because two of the four criteria are not about getting answers right.

That is why the usual Dubai tutoring conversation fails here. A parent reports a grade 4 in MYP 4 sciences. A tutor hears a weak student and offers content revision. The actual problem is often criterion C, processing and evaluating, where the student records data accurately and never evaluates the method. Thirty hours of content teaching will not move that number, and the family will conclude that tutoring does not work when what failed was the diagnosis.

The second reason the programme feels opaque is the grade itself. Criterion levels are added to a total out of thirty-two and converted to a final grade from one to seven using published boundaries, so a child with three strong criteria and one weak one can sit a whole band below where their work feels. Parents reading a report without that mechanism explained cannot tell whether a grade 5 reflects a gap in knowledge or a gap in reflective writing.

Then there is eAssessment, which is optional and which many schools do not enter candidates for at all. Where it does happen it involves on-screen examinations in some subject groups, teacher-moderated ePortfolios in others, and the Personal Project. A family who assumes their child will sit MYP examinations, and a family who assumes they will not, are both sometimes wrong, and the only way to know is to ask the school directly.

This page is written to make you a harder customer. It sets out the criteria by subject group, five questions that reveal within a minute whether a tutor has taught the programme, how criterion levels become a report grade, what may and may not be done on the Personal Project, and what the step into the Diploma actually requires. All IB Gram lessons in the UAE are delivered one-to-one over live video; home visits are a service offered only in India.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-greens.programmesIntro: Four distinct jobs sit under the phrase MYP tutoring, and they need different people. The year level matters as much as the subject, because what the criteria demand changes substantially between MYP 1 and MYP 5.

programmes.name: MYP 1 to 3, the early years
programmes.description: The three years where habits are set rather than grades decided. Criterion-based marking is introduced gradually, approaches-to-learning skills are taught explicitly, and students meet key concepts, related concepts and global contexts for the first time. Support here is usually about study skills and written communication rather than about subject content.
programmes.countryNote: For families in The Greens the useful intervention at this stage is narrow and cheap: teaching a child to read a task sheet, identify which criterion is being assessed and answer that criterion. Students who learn that in MYP 2 stop losing bands in MYP 4 for reasons that have nothing to do with ability.

programmes.name: MYP 4 and 5, the upper years
programmes.description: Two years where the criteria tighten, mathematics splits into standard and extended routes in many schools, and the Personal Project arrives. Report grades here feed subject choices for the Diploma or for a move to another curriculum, so a band lost to weak reflective writing has consequences beyond the report.
programmes.countryNote: This is where almost all MYP tutoring demand in the Emirates Living cluster sits. The common pattern around The Greens is a student performing well on criterion A and losing bands on the investigative and reflective criteria, which is a teachable gap and not a content problem.

programmes.name: The Personal Project in MYP 5
programmes.description: An independent project with a product and a report, assessed in the current guide against three criteria, each marked from zero to eight. Students are assigned a supervisor at school, and that supervision is part of the assessment framework. The project is as much about documenting a process as about the thing produced.
programmes.countryNote: Personal Project enquiries peak in the autumn term in this community, usually when a student has chosen an ambitious product and has not recorded the process behind it. The honest help available is coaching on planning and reflection; the school supervisor remains the person who oversees the work.

programmes.name: Interdisciplinary units and the community project
programmes.description: Units that combine two or more subject groups and are assessed against their own interdisciplinary criteria, plus the community project that many schools run in MYP 3 or 4. Both are assessed on synthesis and process rather than on subject recall, which is why strong single-subject students sometimes find them harder than the subjects themselves.
programmes.countryNote: These are the tasks Greens parents most often do not know how to help with, because they look like group work and are marked like research. A single session on how the interdisciplinary criteria differ from the subject criteria is usually enough to change how a student approaches them.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: Eight subject groups, plus three things that sit across them. Each group has its own four criteria, which is the detail that decides whether a tutor is useful or merely knowledgeable about the subject.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Assessed on analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Students who read widely still lose bands on organising, because the criterion rewards a visible structure rather than good sentences, and on analysing, which asks for the effect of a choice rather than the identification of it.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Four criteria covering listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed at a phase level rather than a year level. The phase matters more than the age, and families regularly discover a child has been placed in a phase that no longer matches their fluency in either direction.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. The critical thinking criterion is where most bands are lost, because it asks for evaluation of a source or an argument and students supply description and context instead.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Two of those four are about the inquiry cycle, so a student who knows the science and writes a thin method or no evaluation sits well below their apparent level.

subjects.name: Mathematics, standard and extended
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the criterion that surprises families most: it requires generalising a rule and justifying it, which is closer to proof than to calculation.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. Three of the four criteria are documentation rather than performance, which means a talented student with a thin process journal scores below a methodical one. This is the clearest example of process being the assessed object.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. It carries written assessment that parents rarely anticipate, and the planning and reflecting criteria behave like any other written task.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating. The design cycle is the assessment, so a working product with no documented research and testing cannot score highly. Students used to being graded on outcomes find this counter-intuitive.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary learning
subjects.description: Units combining two or more subject groups, assessed against interdisciplinary criteria on synthesis and reflection rather than subject recall. Strong single-subject students often score lower here than they expect, because the skill being measured is connection rather than knowledge.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Thinking, communication, social, self-management and research skills, taught explicitly and embedded in task design. They are not separately graded, but they are what the investigative and reflective criteria actually measure, which makes them the highest-leverage thing a tutor can work on.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: A product and a report assessed in the current guide against three criteria, each from zero to eight, with a school-assigned supervisor. Planning and reflection carry the weight; the product itself is evidence rather than the assessment. A tutor's role is coaching, strictly within the supervision framework.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the MYP
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. They sit on the timetable beside the eight MYP groups and carry their own workload.

regions.note: Served by an IB continuum campus on the Springs and Meadows side, with families who often intend the full Diploma. Enquiries here are frequently forward-looking: what the MYP 5 to Diploma step requires rather than what this term's grade means.

regions.note: Shares schools with The Greens, so it shares the same MYP cohort. The common question here is how a criterion level converts into a report grade, which is the single most useful thing a parent can have explained before a parents' evening.

regions.note: Mostly British-curriculum at secondary, which means enquiries from here are often about moving the other way: whether a child leaving the MYP can slot into IGCSE at Year 10 or Year 11, and what the content gap looks like.

schoolClusters.note: Reachable from The Greens on a longer journey, and chosen for the continuum rather than for proximity. Families who travel for one of these are usually committed to the full programme through to the Diploma.

schoolClusters.note: Students at these campuses sit IGCSE at sixteen rather than completing MYP 5, which is a different assessment with different demands. Families comparing the two frameworks should compare what the student is asked to produce rather than the reputations.

sections.heading: What the criteria actually are, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: Everything in the Middle Years Programme follows from the criteria, so a parent who knows them by letter can read a report properly. Each of the eight subject groups has four, and each criterion is marked on a band from zero to eight against published descriptors. The descriptors are specific: the difference between a level 5 and a level 7 is usually a named quality of reasoning or communication rather than a quantity of correct content.

The table below sets out the criteria for six of the groups. Read your child's row and then read their last marked task. In most cases the lost bands are concentrated in one criterion and the parent has been told, accurately but unhelpfully, that the student needs to work harder. Knowing that the loss sits in criterion D, thinking critically, or criterion B, inquiring and designing, converts that into something a tutor can actually address.

Two patterns recur across the groups. First, at least two of the four criteria in every group are about process, communication or evaluation rather than about subject knowledge, which is why content revision so often fails to move a grade. Second, those process criteria are the transferable ones: a student who learns to write an evaluation in sciences usually improves in individuals and societies without further help.

Descriptors are published by the programme and are held by the school, which supplies the task-specific clarifications students are actually marked against. Nothing on this page reproduces them, and the right source is your child's subject teacher or the school's assessment policy rather than any tutoring site.

sections.heading: Five questions that reveal whether a tutor knows the MYP
paragraphs: This is the practical answer to the question at the top of the page. You cannot assess a tutor's MYP knowledge from a profile, because subject qualifications look identical whether or not the person has taught this framework. You can assess it in about three minutes of conversation, using the five questions in the table below. Each one has an answer that is impossible to improvise.

The most revealing is the fourth. A tutor who offers a bank of MYP past papers either does not understand the programme or is selling IGCSE material relabelled. Outside the optional eAssessment specimen materials, there is almost nothing of the kind, and that absence is a defining feature of the framework rather than a gap in anyone's resources. A tutor who says so plainly has taught it.

The second question is nearly as good. Statements of inquiry combine a key concept, one or more related concepts and a global context, and they shape what a task is actually asking for. A tutor who treats a statement of inquiry as a lesson title will coach the subject and miss the task. One who can explain how it narrows the expected response has sat in the planning meetings where these are written.

None of this is about credentialism. It is about not paying for thirty hours of content teaching when the lost bands sit in a criterion that content teaching does not touch. The questions cost nothing to ask and they are the single most useful thing on this page.

sections.heading: From criterion levels to a report grade
paragraphs: This is the mechanism that makes MYP reports hard to read. Each of the four criteria in a subject group is marked from zero to eight, so the maximum criterion total is thirty-two. That total is then converted into a final grade from one to seven using published boundaries. The conversion is not a percentage, and treating it as one produces exactly the wrong conclusions about what to fix.

Work through a case. A student scores seven in criterion A, seven in criterion C, six in criterion B and two in criterion D. Their knowledge is strong, their communication is strong, and their total is twenty-two. The grade that follows sits well below what three of the four criteria suggest, and a parent reading only the grade will reasonably assume a general weakness. The actual weakness is one criterion, and it is a writing problem.

The reverse case also exists and is worth guarding against. A student with four level-five criteria has a respectable total and no obvious problem, which is a fair description of a student who is doing everything adequately. Tutoring there has a lower return than in the first case, because there is no single band to recover, and an honest provider should say so rather than sell a standing weekly hour.

The actionable version is simple. Ask the school for the criterion levels rather than the grade, which they hold for every assessed task. Look for the criterion that is two or more bands below the others. That criterion, in that subject group, is what a tutor should be hired for, and a clinic of two or three sessions is usually the right size of purchase.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is an independent piece of work with a product and a report, assessed in the current guide against three criteria, each marked from zero to eight. Students are assigned a supervisor at school and that supervision is part of the framework. Most of the available marks are for planning and reflection rather than for the product, which is why ambitious products with thin documentation score poorly and modest products with excellent process journals score well.

The legitimate help is real and useful. A tutor can press a student to narrow an unmanageable idea into something achievable and documentable. They can explain what the planning criterion expects to see in a process journal, and why a journal written retrospectively reads differently from one kept as the work happened. They can read a reflection the student wrote and say where it describes rather than evaluates, and they can ask the questions that turn description into evaluation.

The line is absolute and it is worth stating in plain words. No tutor at IB Gram will write the Personal Project, produce a draft for submission, or edit a report until the words are no longer the student's. Submitting work a student did not produce is malpractice under programme rules and the consequence falls on the student, not on the provider. Operations in this market do advertise finished assessed work; what they sell is risk transferred to a fifteen-year-old.

There is a practical point about the supervisor too. The school supervisor is the person who oversees the project and signs off on the academic honesty declaration, so anything a tutor does should be visible to and consistent with that supervision. A tutor who suggests working around the supervisor is describing something other than tutoring.

sections.heading: eAssessment: what is sat, and whether your school enters it
paragraphs: MYP eAssessment is the optional route to the IB MYP Certificate at the end of MYP 5, and the first thing to establish is whether your child's school enters candidates for it at all. Many do not, and a school report grade is unaffected either way. Asking the question directly is more reliable than inferring from whether the school is an IB continuum campus.

Where it does happen, two formats run in parallel. On-screen examinations, taken in two-hour sessions, cover language and literature, sciences, mathematics, individuals and societies, and interdisciplinary learning. Teacher-moderated ePortfolios cover language acquisition, the arts, design, and physical and health education. The Personal Project is moderated separately. The on-screen examinations are the only part of the whole programme that resembles a timed written paper.

That difference changes what preparation means. An ePortfolio is built across the year and cannot be revised for in the ordinary sense; the useful work is doing the coursework well as it happens. An on-screen examination can be prepared for, and the specimen material published for it is the closest thing to an MYP past paper that exists. A tutor who conflates the two will prepare the wrong half of the entry.

The table below sets this out. Treat the last two rows as the ones to act on: confirm with the school whether eAssessment is happening, and understand that the certificate requires the full set rather than a selection. Nothing on this page reproduces specimen material, which belongs to the programme and should be accessed through your school.

sections.heading: MYP 5 into the Diploma: the gap you are really buying help with
paragraphs: A large share of MYP enquiries from The Greens are not really about the MYP. They are about the step into the Diploma, asked a year early by parents who can see it coming. That is a sensible thing to worry about, because the step is real and it is almost entirely about assessment format rather than about content.

Criterion-based marking rewards process, communication and reflection over extended tasks. Diploma papers reward accuracy and command-term discipline under time. A student who has spent five years producing considered written work and almost no timed papers arrives in Year 12 with the knowledge and without the exam habits, and the first set of Diploma marks reads as a collapse in ability when it is a collapse in format familiarity.

Mathematics is the sharpest case. In most MYP schemes a calculator is routinely available, and Analysis and Approaches sits Paper 1 without one at both levels. The sciences are nearly as sharp: the Diploma courses assess uncertainty handling, data analysis and command terms in a way the MYP inquiry cycle approaches from a different angle. Language and literature shifts from analysis against criteria to guided analysis and comparative essays written to length under time.

The cheapest intervention is a bridging block of four to eight sessions in the summer before Year 12, aimed at one or two subjects and at format rather than content. Families who buy that arrive in September with the step already taken. Families who wait buy remedial work in December, at a busier point in the calendar, having already absorbed a set of marks that damaged a child's confidence unnecessarily.

sections.heading: Which schools around The Greens run the MYP
paragraphs: Only IB continuum campuses run the Middle Years Programme, and they are a minority of the schools within reach of The Greens. Dubai held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum at thirty-seven per cent of enrolment and the International Baccalaureate at seven. That seven per cent share is the reason MYP cohorts are small and MYP-experienced tutors are scarce.

The nearest continuum campuses to The Greens sit in The Meadows and towards Emirates Hills, with others along the Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha stretch and in Jumeirah. Families from this community therefore either have a short run to an MYP school or a long one, with very little in between. Programme offerings do change, so confirm with the school rather than relying on any third-party list, this one included.

KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports. For an MYP parent the subject-level commentary is the part worth reading, since a school can be strong overall and thin in one subject group. Dubai is also adding seven new private schools for 2026-27, three of them International Baccalaureate, which creates 16,846 new places.

One more thing a Greens family should know. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, including the IB continuum campuses, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. They sit alongside the eight MYP subject groups on the timetable, and for those subjects the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is strictly prohibited.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs, and why it prices differently
paragraphs: Published 2026 rates across Dubai put budget and university-student online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors online at about AED 150 to 300, and subject specialists from around AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with premium named tutors at AED 500 to 650. Bestimate's Dubai cost table puts a single weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram prices.

MYP support prices differently from Diploma support for a reason that cuts in the family's favour. Diploma tutoring is often a two-year standing commitment because there are papers to prepare for continuously. MYP problems are usually narrow and criterion-shaped, which makes a clinic of two or three sessions the right purchase rather than a weekly hour. The total spend is therefore smaller, provided the diagnosis is right.

The exception is MYP 4 and 5 in mathematics or sciences where a genuine content gap exists alongside the criterion problem, and the Diploma is two years away. There a weekly hour across a year is defensible, because the content has to be built rather than corrected. Even then the hours should alternate between content and the written criteria rather than treating the subject as content alone.

In-home visits are quoted in Dubai from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and advertised monthly packages of four two-hour visits run at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Against online rates at the same level, the difference buys transport. IB Gram has no Dubai office and makes no home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India, and the in-home figures here belong to other providers and are shown so the premium is visible.

process.title: Send the criterion levels, not the grade
process.description: Ask the school for the criterion levels behind the report grade and send those, with the subject group and the MYP year. A criterion two or more bands below the others is a specific, fixable problem; a grade on its own tells a tutor almost nothing useful about what to do.

process.title: Ask us the five questions
process.description: Before booking, put the questions from this page to whoever you speak to. A tutor who can name your child's four criteria by letter, explain a statement of inquiry and say that MYP past papers barely exist has taught the programme. One who offers a past-paper bank has not.

process.title: Use the free session on a marked task
process.description: The trial is a full session with no card details taken. The most productive use is the student's most recent marked task plus the rubric, because that lets the tutor identify the criterion losing the bands and show what the next band up requires in writing.

process.title: Buy the clinic before the weekly hour
process.description: Two or three sessions on one criterion is the right size of purchase for most MYP families. A standing weekly hour is defensible in MYP 4 and 5 mathematics or sciences where content has to be built as well as corrected, and it should be reviewed at every reporting period.

process.title: Plan the Diploma step a year early
process.description: If the Diploma is the destination, book a bridging block for the summer before Year 12 rather than remedial sessions for the December after it. Four to eight sessions on timed technique, non-calculator work and command terms costs a fraction of the alternative and protects a child's confidence.

whyPoints.title: Criteria named by letter before you book
whyPoints.description: Every match states which MYP subject groups and year levels they have taught and can name the four criteria for your child's group. That one check removes the commonest waste in this market, which is paying for content teaching when the lost bands sit in a process criterion.

whyPoints.title: No past-paper bank, because almost none exists
whyPoints.description: Outside the optional eAssessment specimen material there is very little MYP past-paper provision, and anyone offering a bank of it is selling relabelled IGCSE questions. Saying so costs us a sales line and saves you a wasted term.

whyPoints.title: The grade mechanism explained, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Four criteria from zero to eight, a total out of thirty-two, converted to a grade from one to seven. Parents who understand that can read a report and identify the single criterion to work on, which is usually a two or three-session job rather than a year-long one.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit on Personal Project help
whyPoints.description: Tutors narrow a scope, explain what the planning criterion expects of a process journal and respond to reflections the student wrote. Nobody here produces a report or supplies a draft, and nothing is done that the school-assigned supervisor could not see.

whyPoints.title: The Diploma step treated as a format problem
whyPoints.description: The MYP 5 to Diploma gap is overwhelmingly about timed papers, non-calculator technique and command terms rather than about content. Naming it that way means a short summer block often does the work that a term of remedial sessions is otherwise sold for.

whyPoints.title: Rates shown as the market's
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here comes from published Dubai rate cards and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table and is labelled as such, including the in-home premium charged by other providers. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Is there anyone near The Greens who actually knows the MYP syllabus?
faqs.answer: Fewer people than for IGCSE, and the reason is structural rather than local. The Middle Years Programme has no public question bank, no standard mark scheme and no textbook that maps onto what a school assesses, so experience teaching IGCSE transfers only the subject content. Removing the travel requirement widens the pool from whoever is free in western Dubai at half past four to everyone who has actually taught the framework, which is the variable that matters here more than in almost any other subject.

faqs.question: Why is an MYP tutor harder to find than a DP tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the Diploma has papers, past papers and published weightings, and the MYP has criteria and task-specific descriptors held by each school. A Diploma tutor can prepare from public material; an MYP tutor has to understand how units are planned and how criterion descriptors are applied. The International Baccalaureate accounted for about seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, and MYP cohorts are a subset of that, so the pool of experienced teachers is genuinely small.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a tutor really understands MYP criteria?
faqs.answer: Ask four things. Which criteria does my child's subject group use, by letter? What is a statement of inquiry and how does it shape a task? How does a criterion level of five become a report grade? And what MYP past papers exist? The last one is the clearest test: the honest answer is almost none outside eAssessment specimen material, and anyone offering a past-paper bank is selling relabelled IGCSE questions.

faqs.question: What do MYP criteria A to D actually assess?
faqs.answer: They differ by subject group, which is the detail most parents are never told. In mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In language and literature they are analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Each is marked on a band from zero to eight against published descriptors.

faqs.question: How does the MYP 1-8 scale convert to a school report grade?
faqs.answer: Each of the four criteria in a subject group is marked from zero to eight, so the maximum criterion total is thirty-two, and that total converts to a final grade from one to seven using published boundaries. It is not a percentage. A student scoring seven, seven, six and two has strong knowledge and communication and a total of twenty-two, which produces a grade well below what three of the four criteria suggest. Ask the school for the criterion levels rather than the grade.

faqs.question: What may an MYP tutor legitimately do on the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Narrow an unmanageable idea into something achievable and documentable. Explain what the planning criterion expects of a process journal, and why one written retrospectively reads differently from one kept as the work happened. Read a reflection the student wrote and say where it describes rather than evaluates. No tutor here will write the Personal Project, produce a draft for submission, or edit a report until the words stop being the student's own, and the school-assigned supervisor remains the person overseeing the work.

faqs.question: Is MYP eAssessment compulsory for a student in The Greens?
faqs.answer: No. It is the optional route to the IB MYP Certificate at the end of MYP 5, and many schools do not enter candidates at all. Ask your school directly rather than inferring from the fact that it runs the continuum. Where it happens, on-screen examinations of two hours cover language and literature, sciences, mathematics, individuals and societies and interdisciplinary learning, while language acquisition, the arts, design and physical and health education are assessed by teacher-moderated ePortfolio. School report grades are unaffected either way.

faqs.question: Which schools around The Greens run the MYP?
faqs.answer: Only IB continuum campuses, which are a minority of the schools within reach. The nearest sit in The Meadows and towards Emirates Hills, with others along the Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha stretch and in Jumeirah, so families from this community face either a short run or a long one with little in between. Programme offerings do change, so confirm with the school rather than relying on any third-party list. Schools are named on this page as context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP 5 to the Diploma. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Format rather than content, almost entirely. Five years of criterion-based marking rewards process, communication and reflection over extended tasks; Diploma papers reward accuracy and command-term discipline under time. Mathematics is the sharpest case, since Analysis and Approaches sits a non-calculator paper at both levels and MYP work routinely allows a calculator. Four to eight sessions in the summer before Year 12 on timed technique and command terms costs a fraction of remedial work in December.

faqs.question: Does MYP tutoring cost more or less than DP tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Usually less in total, and the reason favours the family. Diploma support is often a two-year standing commitment because papers need continuous preparation. MYP problems are usually narrow and criterion-shaped, so a clinic of two or three sessions is the right purchase rather than a weekly hour. Hourly rates are the same market: roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to 450 and upwards for a specialist, on published 2026 Dubai rates.

faqs.question: Is there past-paper practice for MYP, like there is for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Almost none, and this is one of the defining differences between the two frameworks. The MYP assesses task-specific work against criterion descriptors held by the school, so there is no public bank of questions and no mark scheme to drill. The nearest equivalent is the specimen material published for the optional on-screen eAssessments, obtained through your school. Useful practice therefore means working on your child's own marked tasks against the rubric, which is exactly what a criterion clinic does.

faqs.question: How often should an MYP 4 student have tutoring?
faqs.answer: Less often than most families assume, and for a shorter period. If the problem is one criterion sitting two or more bands below the others, two or three sessions on that criterion usually does it, and a standing weekly hour would be buying reassurance. A weekly hour becomes defensible in MYP 4 and 5 mathematics or sciences where there is a genuine content gap and the Diploma is approaching, and even then the hours should alternate between content and written criteria.

faqs.question: Does the MYP prepare a child for IGCSE if we change school?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps substantially and the assessment does not. A student moving from MYP 4 into Year 10 or Year 11 IGCSE has usually met most of the subject material but has written very few timed papers, and on the Cambridge sciences they will also meet a practical or alternative-to-practical paper format that the MYP inquiry cycle approaches differently. The useful preparation is a short block on timed technique and paper structure rather than content revision.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit alongside the MYP?
faqs.answer: They sit on the timetable beside the eight MYP subject groups. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, including IB continuum campuses, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. For those subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, so support must work with the school's own material.

faqs.question: What should I send a tutor before the first MYP session?
faqs.answer: Four things, and none of them is a report grade on its own. The subject group and the MYP year level. The criterion levels behind the grade, which the school holds for every assessed task. The most recent marked task together with the rubric the student was marked against. And the statement of inquiry for the current unit if it is available. With those, a first session can identify the criterion losing the bands rather than spending the hour working out what the problem is.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-greens.closingHeading: Send the criterion levels and ask the five questions
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-greens.closingBody: The most useful thing you can do before booking anything is get the criterion levels behind your child's report grade from the school, and then ask whoever you speak to the five questions on this page. If they can name the four criteria for your child's subject group by letter, explain how a statement of inquiry shapes a task, and tell you plainly that MYP past papers barely exist, they have taught this programme. Send us the subject group, the year level, the criterion levels and the most recent marked task, and the free first session will go on identifying the band that is missing rather than on finding out what the question is. All UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Why MYP reports are the hardest thing a Dubai parent has to read
paragraphs: A British-curriculum report says 62 per cent and a predicted grade. An MYP report says criterion A 6, criterion B 4, criterion C 5, criterion D 7, and then a number out of seven that bears no obvious relationship to any of them. Parents in The Lakes who moved from another system, and there are a great many, find this genuinely opaque. The usual reaction is either to ignore the letters and look only at the final number, which hides the actual problem, or to treat a 4 as a failure, which it is not. Neither response helps the child, and both are the reason MYP tutoring is so often booked a year later than it should be.

The letters are the useful part. Each MYP subject group is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, and the criteria measure different things. In Sciences, criterion A is knowing and understanding, B is inquiring and designing, C is processing and evaluating, and D is reflecting on the impacts of science. A child scoring 7 on A and 3 on C does not have a science problem. They have a data-handling problem, and that specific weakness will follow them into Diploma Physics or IGCSE Chemistry unless somebody names it. The whole value of an MYP report is that it tells you which of four skills is failing, and the whole tragedy is that most parents never find out how to read it.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For this age group the format has a specific advantage that parents notice quickly: sessions can be short. A forty-five-minute slot at 4:30pm for an MYP 2 student is practical on a screen and absurd for a visiting tutor, because nobody drives across Emirates Living for forty-five minutes. Being able to buy the right amount of time for an eleven-year-old, rather than the amount of time that justifies a journey, changes what tuition at this age can be.

The rest of this page sets out what the programme contains and what a tutor should actually be doing in it. The eight subject groups and their criteria. How a criterion total becomes a grade from 1 to 7. The MYP 5 year, with the Personal Project and the optional eAssessment. The parts of the programme that look like jargon and are not, meaning global contexts, key concepts, approaches to learning and interdisciplinary units. The two bridges out of MYP, into the Diploma and into IGCSE, and the gap in each. How Language Acquisition phases work alongside the Arabic that every Dubai private school is required to teach. And what this costs in AED at the shorter session lengths this age group actually needs.
If your child is in MYP 4 or MYP 5, read the transition table first. That is the one with a deadline behind it.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-lakes.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme sits in the middle of a longer sequence, and a Lakes family usually needs to know what came before and what comes next as much as what is happening now. These four stages cover almost every conversation.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The programme that feeds MYP 1 in a continuum school. Assessment is largely formative and reported against learning outcomes rather than against four criteria, so the arrival of criterion marks in MYP 1 is a genuine change for both child and parent. Students coming into MYP 1 from a non-IB primary school meet the criteria system with no preparation at all.
programmes.countryNote: Emirates International School Meadows runs the full continuum within a few minutes of The Lakes, so some local children move from PYP into MYP without changing building. Those who join MYP 1 from a British or Indian primary school in the same neighbourhood need a term to understand what the letters mean, and that is a reasonable thing to ask a tutor for help with.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria out of eight. The programme also carries approaches to learning skills, key concepts, six global contexts, at least one interdisciplinary unit a year, service as action, and the Personal Project in the final year. Grades are reported from 1 to 7 after a published conversion from the criterion total.
programmes.countryNote: MYP enquiries from Emirates Living cluster at two points. The first is MYP 1 and 2, when a family new to the system wants the reports explained. The second is MYP 4 and 5, when subject choices for sixteen are approaching and a weak criterion that nobody addressed in MYP 2 has become a real obstacle.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The usual destination for a continuum student. Assessment changes shape entirely: criterion marks out of eight are replaced by examination papers marked against mark schemes and command terms, plus internally assessed work with its own criteria. Students arrive strong on inquiry and weaker on timed written technique, which is a predictable and teachable gap rather than a surprise.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Emirates International School Meadows both offer the Diploma within reach of The Lakes, so a local MYP student often continues into DP without moving school. The handover year is MYP 5, and the students who cope best are the ones who practised timed writing before they needed it.

programmes.name: The IGCSE alternative at fourteen
programmes.description: A real option in this neighbourhood rather than a theoretical one, because several nearby schools run the British route. A student leaving MYP 3 for a Year 10 IGCSE course meets subject-specific syllabuses with numbered codes, tiering on some Cambridge subjects and terminal examinations instead of continuous criterion assessment. The content overlap is substantial; the assessment culture is not.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai British School Emirates Hills, Regent International School and Dubai College all run IGCSE within reach of The Lakes, which is why this switch happens more often here than the continuum schools' numbers suggest. Families considering it should ask both schools what bridging work they expect, since the answer differs by subject.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-lakes.subjectsIntro: The grid below is the programme itself: eight subject groups, each with its own four criteria. Knowing the criterion names for your child's weakest subject is the most useful thing a Lakes parent can take from this page, because it turns a vague report into a specific instruction for a tutor.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C is the one that predicts Diploma and IGCSE performance most reliably, because data processing and evaluation are examined directly in both systems and are rarely practised outside school.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B surprises parents from other systems: a child who computes accurately can still score poorly because the criterion rewards generalising a rule and justifying it, not getting the answer.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: A analysing, B organising, C producing text, D using language. The split matters because a strong writer with weak analysis scores unevenly and is often told to 'write more', which is the wrong instruction. Criterion A improves through close reading practice rather than through more writing.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing. Organised into six phases rather than by year group, so two children in the same MYP year can sit in different phases of the same language. Phase placement, not age, determines what a tutor should be teaching.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion D is where the marks are won in MYP 4 and 5, and it is also the criterion most students have never been taught explicitly, because critical thinking is assumed rather than instructed.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The documented design cycle carries most of the marks, which means a beautifully made product with a thin research and evaluation record scores below a modest product documented properly.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. Students with genuine talent often score lower than expected because the process journal is where criteria A, B and D live. Support here is almost entirely about documenting thinking rather than about technique.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. Half the assessment is written, which regularly catches out able athletes and their parents, and it is straightforward to improve once anybody says so.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: An independent project in the final MYP year, assessed against planning, applying skills and reflecting, each out of eight for a total of 24. Support is process coaching only: goal setting, time planning and questions about the report the student is writing. The project and the report must be the student's own work.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: At least one a year, combining two subject groups around a shared concept, with their own criteria for disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection. Students who treat them as two homework tasks stapled together lose the synthesis marks, which is the whole point of the unit.

sections.heading: How to read an MYP report without a glossary
paragraphs: Take the subject your child is weakest in and find its four criterion marks. Each is out of eight. Then look up what those four criteria are called in that subject group, because the names are the diagnosis. In Sciences a low criterion C is data processing. In Mathematics a low criterion B is pattern investigation and justification. In Language and Literature a low criterion A is textual analysis. In Individuals and Societies a low criterion D is critical thinking. Those are four completely different problems with four completely different remedies, and all of them look identical on a report that only shows the final grade.

The second thing to look at is the shape of the profile rather than its height. A child with four marks of 5 is consistent and needs general work. A child with 7, 7, 3, 6 has one specific hole, which is far better news and far cheaper to fix. The uneven profile is the common one in Dubai, particularly for students who joined the MYP from another system, because the criteria that reward process and reflection are unfamiliar to anyone trained on content tests.

The third thing is the trend. Criterion marks move slowly and a single assessment is noisy, so compare the same criterion across two or three reporting points before concluding anything. A drop from 6 to 4 in one unit may just mean a harder task; the same drop sustained over a year is a real decline. Bring two reports to a first conversation with a tutor rather than one, and the plan will be better for it. sections.heading: From four criterion marks to one grade out of seven
paragraphs: The conversion is the part that makes MYP reports feel arbitrary, and it is not. The four criterion marks are added to give a total out of 32, and that total is then placed in a band to produce a grade from 1 to 7. The bands are not equal in width, which is why a small change in criterion marks can move a grade and a larger change sometimes cannot. Your school's MYP coordinator can give you the exact boundary table they apply, and asking for it is a reasonable request that most coordinators are happy to meet.

Two practical consequences follow. The first is that the cheapest grade improvement available is usually in the weakest criterion, not the strongest subject. Moving a 3 to a 5 adds two marks to the total for a fraction of the effort that moving a 6 to a 7 would take, and the grade conversion does not care which criterion the marks came from. A parent who understands that stops asking for general subject help and starts asking for criterion-specific work, which is both cheaper and more effective.

The second is that a grade of 4 is not a failure. The 1 to 7 scale is the same scale the Diploma uses, where 4 is a pass in most subjects, and MYP tasks are deliberately set to stretch. Parents arriving from systems where 70 per cent is respectable and 40 per cent is alarming read a 4 as a crisis and respond by buying the wrong amount of tuition. The useful question is not whether the number is high but whether the profile is even and the trend is upward.

sections.heading: MYP 5: the Personal Project, eAssessment and the year that decides the next two
paragraphs: The final MYP year carries more than the ones before it. The Personal Project runs across it: an independent piece of work chosen by the student, assessed against three criteria, planning, applying skills and reflecting, each out of eight for a total of 24. Service as action continues. Subject choices for sixteen are made. And some schools enter candidates for MYP eAssessment, the optional on-screen examinations and ePortfolios that lead to the IB MYP Certificate.

The Personal Project fails in predictable ways and almost none of them are about ability. Students choose a goal that is too large, start the report in the final fortnight, or keep no record of the process, which is where most of the marks live. The project is marked on planning, skill application and reflection rather than on the finished object, so a modest goal documented carefully outscores an ambitious one documented badly. The support that helps is a weekly fifteen-minute discipline on the process journal, started early, which is dull and extremely effective.

On eAssessment, the honest position is that whether your child sits it is the school's decision, not yours, and the first thing to do is ask. Where a school does enter candidates, the on-screen examination is a different skill from criterion-assessed coursework and benefits from specific practice. The boundary on the Personal Project is the same as on any assessed work: a tutor may ask questions, teach planning and time management and read a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply content for the project or draft the report. No IB Gram tutor will produce a Personal Project for a student.

sections.heading: Global contexts, key concepts and approaches to learning, in plain words
paragraphs: MYP vocabulary puts parents off, and most of it describes something ordinary. Key concepts are the big ideas a unit is built around, sixteen of them across the programme, things like change, systems, identity and relationships. Global contexts are the six real-world framings a unit can be set in, including identities and relationships, scientific and technical innovation, and globalisation and sustainability. Approaches to learning are five skill categories, thinking, communication, social, self-management and research, taught alongside subject content rather than separately.

None of these is graded on its own, which is why parents reasonably wonder whether they matter. They matter because they shape the tasks. A Sciences unit framed in the global context of globalisation and sustainability will set an assessment about a real system with competing considerations, and a student who answers it as a pure content question will lose criterion D marks. Understanding the framing is not an extra; it is how the task is read correctly.

Interdisciplinary units work the same way. At least one a year combines two subject groups around a shared concept and is assessed on disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection. Students who treat it as two separate pieces of homework attached to each other lose exactly the marks the unit exists to award. Approaches to learning deserve a specific note for this age group: self-management is the one that most often limits a capable MYP 3 or MYP 4 student, and it is teachable, which makes it one of the better uses of a tutoring hour at thirteen.

sections.heading: Where an MYP session actually fits in a Lakes afternoon
paragraphs: MYP students are eleven to sixteen, and the scheduling problem is not the same as it is for a Diploma student. A twelve-year-old cannot concentrate at 8:30pm, so the late weekday window that works for a sixteen-year-old is useless here. Most Emirates Living schools finish the academic day between 2:30pm and 3:30pm, children at schools inside the community are home by about 3:15pm, and those commuting back from Al Barsha arrive closer to four. Activities run to around five on the days they are scheduled.

That leaves two genuinely good windows for this age group, and both are short. The first is 4pm to 5:30pm on a day with no activity, when a child is home, fed and still alert. The second is immediately after dinner, roughly 6pm to 7pm, before tiredness takes over. Both suit a forty-five or sixty-minute session rather than a ninety-minute one, and that is the format most MYP 1 to MYP 3 students should be buying. For MYP 4 and 5 the later windows open up and ninety minutes becomes useful, particularly for timed writing.

This is where the delivery format does real work rather than marketing work. A forty-five-minute slot is not economic for a visiting tutor, because the drive across Emirates Living costs more than the lesson, so families are pushed into longer sessions than their child can use. On a screen, the session can be the length the child needs. Two short sessions a week also become practical, which for criterion-specific work at this age is usually more effective than one long one. sections.heading: The two bridges out of MYP, and the gap in each
paragraphs: Every MYP student leaves the programme at sixteen, either into the Diploma or out of the IB system into A Levels, and in this neighbourhood both happen often because both kinds of school sit within twenty minutes. The content overlap in either direction is larger than families fear. The assessment-culture gap is larger than they expect, and it is the gap that costs grades in the first term after the switch.

Into the Diploma, the change is from criterion-assessed tasks with time to think to examination papers marked against command terms under time pressure. An MYP student who has written thoughtfully for five years may never have written a full answer in twenty-five minutes. The internally assessed work is more familiar territory, since inquiry and evaluation are what MYP criteria have been rewarding all along, and continuum students often outperform on those components while struggling on papers.

Into IGCSE, the change is from concept-framed inquiry to syllabus content with numbered codes, defined specification points and, on some Cambridge subjects, a Core and Extended tier decision. MYP students usually arrive with better investigative skills and thinner content coverage in specific topics, because MYP units select depth over completeness. The remedy is a content audit against the specification rather than general tuition, and it is best done in the summer before Year 10 rather than in the Christmas term of it. Ask the receiving school for the specification and work through it topic by topic with the student, marking each one as secure, shaky or never taught.

sections.heading: Language acquisition phases and the Arabic every Dubai school must teach
paragraphs: Two language systems run in parallel for an MYP student in Dubai and they are often confused. The first is MYP Language Acquisition, organised into six phases rather than by year group, so a child's phase depends on prior experience in that language rather than on age. Two students in the same MYP 3 class can sit in Phase 2 and Phase 5 of the same language and be assessed against the same four criteria at genuinely different levels. For a tutor the phase is the useful information; the year group tells you almost nothing.

The second is the UAE requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and lessons for any mandatory subject are advised to run at least 25 minutes.

The rules on how those classes are organised are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. That last point means Arabic support should be arranged with the school's guidance rather than around it.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs in AED, priced by the session length a child can use
paragraphs: Most published tutoring rates are quoted per hour, which hides something that matters for this age group. If a twelve-year-old gets real value from forty-five minutes and nothing from the ninety that follows, the honest unit is the session rather than the hour. Dubai market rates per hour, as published in October 2026, run roughly AED 45 to 150 for budget online generalists, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes around AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate work gives the specialist band.

Convert those to the session lengths an MYP student actually uses and the arithmetic looks different. A forty-five-minute session at a mid-band rate is roughly three quarters of the hourly figure, and two of them in a week will usually beat one ninety-minute block for criterion-specific work at twelve or thirteen. That option barely exists with a visiting tutor, because travel makes a short session uneconomic: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500, with the drive paid for inside the hour. Monthly packages observed in the Dubai market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visiting sessions.

Every figure above is another provider's published rate or a survey band as of the October 2026 research, not an IB Gram price list. Ask about our own rates on the consultation call, where the session length can be set to the child rather than to a package. Useful context for a household budget: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.
