sections.heading: Starting MYP support from The Lakes, and what the first session should look like
paragraphs: Bring two reports rather than one, and bring the subject you are least happy about. Name the four criterion marks in it if you have them. With that, a tutor can tell you in a single reply whether the issue is content, method, writing or self-management, and quote a plan against a named criterion instead of a subject. An enquiry that says 'MYP 2, struggling in Sciences' takes a session to decode; one that says 'MYP 2 Sciences, criterion A 7, criterion C 3, same pattern last term' does not.

The first session should not be a lesson. For an MYP student it should be a diagnostic: a short task that exposes the weak criterion, a look at a piece of returned work and the task-specific clarifications it was marked against, and a plain explanation to the parent of what the letters mean and which one is worth spending money on. That conversation is where most of the value sits, and a family that has it properly often needs fewer sessions than they expected rather than more.

Then a free trial lesson, one per student and bookable without card details, with the tutor who would continue. Ask for a session length that fits your child rather than the one that fits a package, and if the match is wrong say so and ask for another; that costs nothing. The honest caveat: the 4pm to 6pm window that suits MYP 1 to MYP 3 is narrow and it is contested, and some subject groups, Design and Arts in particular, have fewer specialists than Sciences and Mathematics. If nobody suitable is free in the window you need, you will be told with a date rather than matched to whoever is available.

process.title: Send two reports and the criterion marks
process.description: Name the subject you are least happy about and give the four criterion marks from the last two reporting points. That is enough for a tutor to identify whether the problem is content, method, writing or self-management, and to quote a plan against a named criterion rather than against a whole subject.

process.title: A diagnostic before a lesson
process.description: The first session is spent finding the weak criterion rather than teaching. A short task, a look at returned work and the clarifications it was marked against, and a plain explanation of what the letters mean. Families who do this properly often buy fewer sessions than they first expected.

process.title: A trial at the length your child can use
process.description: One free trial per student, no card details needed, with the tutor who would continue, and at 45, 60 or 90 minutes depending on age. Buying ninety minutes for a twelve-year-old wastes half of it, and the only reason that is usually on offer elsewhere is that somebody has to justify a journey.

process.title: Work one criterion at a time
process.description: Each block of sessions targets a single named criterion so progress is measurable against the next report rather than felt. Moving a 3 to a 5 adds more to the grade total than moving a 6 to a 7 and takes a fraction of the time, which is why criterion-specific work is both cheaper and faster.

process.title: Reassess at each reporting point
process.description: MYP criterion marks move slowly, so the review point is the school report rather than the week. At each one the plan is checked against the new profile and the frequency adjusted, and a criterion that has recovered is dropped from the plan rather than kept on for the sake of the booking.

whyPoints.title: The report explained before anything is sold
whyPoints.description: The first useful thing in MYP tutoring is understanding what criterion A to D mean in your child's weakest subject. That conversation happens before a plan is written, and it sometimes ends with a recommendation for fewer sessions in a narrower area than the family came in expecting.

whyPoints.title: Sessions sized for an eleven-year-old
whyPoints.description: Forty-five and sixty-minute sessions are genuinely available, which matters because a younger MYP student gets little from the second hour. Short sessions only work when nobody is travelling to them, which is why visiting arrangements push families into lengths their child cannot use.

whyPoints.title: Taught by criterion, not by year group
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to the specific criterion that is costing marks, whether that is data processing in Sciences, pattern investigation in Mathematics or critical thinking in Individuals and Societies. Those are four different teaching jobs and a general year-group tutor treats them as one.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project stays the student's
whyPoints.description: Support on the Personal Project is goal setting, planning discipline, process-journal habits and questions about a draft the student has written. No content is supplied and no report is drafted. The project, the product and the write-up have to be the candidate's own work throughout.

whyPoints.title: Transition planned a year early
whyPoints.description: The gap between MYP and either the Diploma or IGCSE is an assessment-culture gap rather than a content one, and it is cheapest to close in MYP 4 and the summer after it. The transition table on this page exists because no competing page in this search maps it subject by subject.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, with the October 2026 research date, and converted to the session lengths this age group actually uses. IB Gram holds no KHDA, Ministry of Education or IB accreditation and claims none; the regulator facts here are cited, not borrowed.

faqs.question: What do the A, B, C and D marks on my child's MYP report actually mean?
faqs.answer: They are four separate assessment criteria, each marked out of eight, and each measures something different. In Sciences, A is knowing and understanding, B is inquiring and designing, C is processing and evaluating, and D is reflecting on the impacts of science. In Mathematics, B is investigating patterns rather than computing answers. The names are the diagnosis: a low C in Sciences is a data-handling problem, not a science problem. Look up the four criterion names for your child's weakest subject group, and the report stops being opaque and starts being useful.

faqs.question: How does a criterion mark out of eight turn into a grade out of seven?
faqs.answer: The four criterion marks are added to give a total out of 32, and that total falls into a band that produces a grade from 1 to 7. The bands are not equal in width, which is why a small change sometimes moves a grade and a larger one sometimes does not. Ask your school's MYP coordinator for the boundary table they apply; it is a reasonable request. The practical consequence is that the cheapest marks are always in the weakest criterion, because the conversion does not care which criterion the marks came from.

faqs.question: Is a grade of 4 in the MYP something to worry about?
faqs.answer: Not in itself. The MYP uses the same 1 to 7 scale as the Diploma, where 4 is a pass in most subjects, and MYP tasks are deliberately set to stretch rather than to be completed comfortably. Parents arriving from systems where percentages are the currency often read a 4 as a crisis and buy the wrong amount of tuition in response. The better questions are whether the four criterion marks are even and whether the trend across two or three reporting points is upward. An uneven profile is more informative than a low average.

faqs.question: Should a child in The Lakes stay in the MYP or move to IGCSE at fourteen?
faqs.answer: Both routes are available within twenty minutes of The Lakes, which is why this comes up so often here. The content overlap is larger than families fear and the assessment-culture gap is larger than they expect. MYP students usually arrive at IGCSE with stronger investigative skills and thinner coverage of specific specification content, because MYP units choose depth over completeness. If you are considering the move, ask both schools what bridging work they expect, and plan a content audit against the specification for the summer before Year 10.

faqs.question: What is the Personal Project and when does my child do it?
faqs.answer: It is an independent project in the final MYP year, chosen by the student and assessed against three criteria, planning, applying skills and reflecting, each out of eight for a total of 24. The marks go to the process rather than to the finished object, which is why a modest goal documented carefully outscores an ambitious one documented badly. The predictable failures are a goal that is too large, a report started in the last fortnight and a process journal nobody kept. A weekly fifteen minutes on the journal from the start prevents all three.

faqs.question: Does my child have to sit the MYP eAssessment?
faqs.answer: That is the school's decision rather than the family's, and the first step is simply to ask. Where a school does enter candidates, eAssessment combines optional on-screen examinations with moderated ePortfolios and leads to the IB MYP Certificate. The on-screen examination is a different skill from criterion-assessed classroom work, so it benefits from specific timing and technique practice using official sample material. Where a school does not enter candidates, MYP 5 grades come from internal criterion assessment and the Personal Project remains the fixed external-facing piece of work.

faqs.question: How long should a tutoring session be for a child in MYP 1 or MYP 2?
faqs.answer: Forty-five to sixty minutes, and not longer. An eleven or twelve-year-old gets real value from the first forty-five minutes of focused work and very little from the hour after it, so a ninety-minute session is mostly a billing decision rather than a teaching one. Two short sessions a week usually beat one long one for criterion-specific work at this age. Short sessions only make sense when nobody is travelling, which is why they are rarely offered by visiting tutors: the drive across Emirates Living would cost more than the lesson.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups do Emirates Living families ask about most?
faqs.answer: Sciences and Mathematics lead, usually because of criterion C in Sciences and criterion B in Mathematics, the two criteria that reward process rather than recall and that students from content-tested systems have never practised. Language and literature comes next, almost always for criterion A analysis rather than for writing. Individuals and societies arrives in MYP 4 and 5, when criterion D critical thinking starts carrying real weight. Design and Arts generate fewer enquiries but have fewer specialists available, so they are worth asking about earlier in the term.

faqs.question: Do global contexts and key concepts affect my child's marks?
faqs.answer: Not directly, because neither is graded on its own, but they shape every task your child is set. A Sciences unit framed in the global context of globalisation and sustainability will set an assessment about a real system with competing considerations, and a student who answers it as a pure content question loses criterion D marks. Understanding the framing is part of reading the task correctly rather than an optional extra. The same applies to interdisciplinary units, where the synthesis marks exist precisely for connecting two subject groups rather than answering each separately.

faqs.question: My child scores highly on criterion A and poorly on criterion C. What does that tell me?
faqs.answer: That the content is secure and a process skill is missing, which is good news. In Sciences a low C means data processing and evaluation: plotting, interpreting, judging whether a conclusion is supported. In Arts or Design it points at the documented process rather than the product. The remedy is narrow and measurable, which makes it cheap: a block of sessions aimed at that one criterion, then a check against the next report. A child with 7, 7, 3, 6 needs far less tuition than a child with four marks of 4, even though the totals are close.

faqs.question: How do MYP Language Acquisition phases work alongside compulsory Arabic?
faqs.answer: They are two separate systems. MYP Language Acquisition is organised into six phases based on prior experience rather than on age, so two students in the same MYP year can sit in different phases of the same language and be assessed against the same four criteria at different levels. Compulsory Arabic is a UAE requirement: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab groups. Ask the school which phase and which Arabic stream your child is in.

faqs.question: What is the gap between MYP 5 and the first term of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: It is a writing-under-time-pressure gap more than a content gap. Five years of criterion-assessed tasks give a student room to think, redraft and reflect, and the Diploma then asks for a full answer in twenty-five minutes against a command term. Continuum students often outperform on internally assessed work, where inquiry and evaluation are exactly what MYP criteria have been rewarding, while struggling on papers. The fix is timed writing practice started in MYP 4 rather than discovered in DP1, and it is one of the most cost-effective blocks of tutoring available.

faqs.question: What should a Lakes family budget for MYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai hourly rates run roughly AED 45 to 150 for budget online generalists, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists, per Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate work. For MYP the useful conversion is to session length: at a mid-band rate a forty-five-minute session is roughly three quarters of the hourly figure, and two short sessions a week often beat one long one at this age. Those are other providers' published figures as of October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without doing any of it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the only acceptable arrangement. A tutor may help a student set a realistic goal, build a weekly discipline around the process journal, teach planning and time management, explain what each of the three criteria rewards, and ask questions about a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply content, make the product or draft the report. The project and the write-up have to be the candidate's own work from start to finish, and no IB Gram tutor will produce a Personal Project for a student.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-lakes.closingHeading: Start with the letters, not the number
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-lakes.closingBody: Find your child's weakest MYP subject, write down the four criterion marks, and look up what those four criteria are called in that subject group. In ten minutes you will know whether the problem is content, method, writing or organisation, and that single piece of information is worth more than a term of general tutoring aimed at the subject as a whole. Send those marks through with your child's MYP year and the afternoon window that is reliably free, and the trial lesson can be set at the length that suits their age rather than the length that suits a package.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-meadows.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the Middle Years Programme the way Dubai schools actually report it: four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a grade from 1 to 7. Ask any of them to show you which criterion your child is losing marks on before you buy a block of hours.

intro.heading: What a Meadows family actually pays for MYP help, and what the money buys
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number that decides whether tutoring survives past February. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate work puts a weekly one-hour slot at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more where an exam-year specialist is involved. Monthly packages advertised in this market sit in the same territory: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour villa visits. Those are market figures from other providers, dated and attributed, not an IB Gram price list.

The Middle Years Programme costs less per hour than the Diploma, and that is precisely where Meadows households lose money. Because most Dubai schools run no external MYP examination, the programme feels consequence-free, so families underspend through MYP 1 to MYP 3, notice a problem in MYP 4, and then buy specialist Diploma-band hours in a panic the autumn after. The cheapest version of MYP tutoring is three terms of correctly aimed work at the qualified-tutor rate, finishing before DP1 starts. The expensive version is doing nothing until the first DP1 report card.

Aiming the work correctly is the whole of it. An MYP subject grade is not a percentage; it is built from four criteria, lettered A to D, each marked from 0 to 8 and reported separately. A child can be strong on criterion A, knowing and understanding, and be losing most of the grade on criterion C, communicating, which is a writing and presentation problem rather than a content one. Generic homework help touches neither. A tutor who asks to see the criterion breakdown from the last report before quoting is worth more than one who quotes faster.

The Meadows sits inside Emirates Living, so the geography is specific and it matters to the bill. Emirates International School Meadows runs the IB continuum inside the community itself; plenty of other Meadows children travel out to Al Barsha, Al Sufouh or Al Barsha South, which puts them home somewhere between 15:45 and 16:40 depending on the bus route. An in-home tutor crossing from Al Barsha into Meadows 6 at that hour is paying for the traffic with your money, and the published in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour reflects it.

What IB Gram does is narrow and worth stating plainly. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor sharing a screen and marking in real time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; villa visits are a service offered only in India. The trial lesson is free, in one subject, with no card details taken, and it exists so you can judge the teaching against the rates published further down this page before anything is spent.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-meadows.programmesIntro: The Meadows feeds schools running two different routes to 18, and the MYP is the five-year stretch where the two still look alike. Here is what each programme is for, and what a Dubai family should expect to pay attention to inside it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, assessed against four published criteria per subject rather than by examination. Each criterion is marked from 0 to 8 and the four combine into a grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries the school applies. MYP 5 carries the Personal Project and, in some schools, optional on-screen eAssessment leading to the IB MYP Certificate. Interdisciplinary units and Service as Action run alongside the subjects.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the MYP is the minority route by enrolment, which is why MYP-specific tutoring is harder to find than IGCSE help. Emirates International School Meadows runs the continuum inside Emirates Living; Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills is the other nearby IB school a Meadows family is likely to be looking at. Both report criterion marks, so ask for the letters, not an average.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary learning organised around transdisciplinary themes and closing with the Grade 5 or Year 6 Exhibition. There are no external tests and no grades in the MYP sense, so the useful tutoring question in PYP is narrow: is reading fluency, number fact recall or written structure behind where the next programme will assume it to be.
programmes.countryNote: Meadows families coming out of a PYP primary and into MYP 1 usually meet the same two gaps: extended writing to a criterion, and the arithmetic fluency that MYP Extended mathematics assumes. Both are cheap to fix at the budget tutoring band in Year 6 and expensive to fix at the specialist band in MYP 4. That timing is the single biggest cost lever in this whole programme.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment is external examinations in the May session for UAE schools, combined with internal assessments marked by teachers and moderated by the IB. The jump from criterion marking to percentage-weighted papers is abrupt and catches MYP 5 leavers out.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma-band tutoring is where Dubai rates climb: TutorChase publishes AED 270 an hour and Bestimate puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. A Meadows family that gets the MYP 5 foundations right spends in the lower half of that band in DP1 rather than the upper half. That arithmetic is the argument for funding MYP properly.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: The British-curriculum alternative to MYP 4 and 5, examined externally with syllabus codes on every paper: Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics. Cambridge runs June and November series; Pearson runs May/June and November. Entries close months before the exam, which is the mechanical difference from the MYP calendar.
programmes.countryNote: Several Meadows children sit IGCSEs at schools in Al Barsha and Al Sufouh rather than MYP 4 and 5, and some switch between the two at 14. The UAE Ministry of Education equivalency route for British-curriculum students asks for five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-meadows.subjectsIntro: MYP subjects are graded against criteria, so a subject list is only useful if it says which criterion usually costs the marks. These are the eight groups plus the two components that sit outside them, with the honest diagnosis for each.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Most lost marks sit in investigating patterns, where a student finds the rule but cannot justify or generalise it, and in communicating, where working is missing. Extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 is the stream that feeds Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B and C are where the scientific investigation marks live: variables defined properly, a method someone else could repeat, uncertainty discussed rather than ignored. Content revision alone does not move them.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria are analysing, organizing, producing text, and using language. Analysis marks are lost by narrating the plot instead of commenting on choices the writer made. Organising marks are lost by essay structure that has no visible argument. Both are teachable in six to eight sessions, which is why this is the cheapest MYP subject to improve.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Graded by phase rather than year, so two children in the same MYP class can be assessed against different phase descriptors. Criteria cover listening, reading, speaking and writing. Ask the school which phase your child is in before buying tutoring, because teaching to the wrong phase descriptor wastes every hour of it.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria are knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. The thinking-critically criterion is the one that separates a 5 from a 7: evaluating sources, recognising perspective and limitation, and saying what the evidence does not show. It is a habit, not a content gap.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria are inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Design is frequently the subject dragging an otherwise strong MYP profile down, because the written design cycle folder is marked as heavily as the artefact. Students who build well and document badly lose half the available marks.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria are knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more weight than most families expect, and responding asks for informed comment on other artists' work. Tutoring here is usually about documentation discipline rather than technique.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria are knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The two written criteria can be prepared the same way any other written criterion is, and they are routinely the reason a sporty child carries a 4 in this subject.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: A self-directed project with a supervisor at school, assessed against the criteria in the current MYP projects guide covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of 8. The process journal is the evidence. A tutor may coach planning and reflection; the project itself must be the student's own work throughout.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units and Service as Action
subjects.description: Interdisciplinary units are separately assessed against their own criteria and are easy to neglect because no single subject teacher owns them. Service as Action is recorded rather than graded but is a condition of programme completion. Both show up on the MYP record a DP admissions conversation looks at.

schoolClusters.note: The schools a Meadows child can reach without crossing Sheikh Zayed Road, and the only cluster where the IB continuum is available locally. Ask each one whether it enters MYP 5 students for eAssessment, because the answer differs school to school and changes what MYP 5 tutoring is for.

schoolClusters.note: Where a large share of Meadows secondary students actually study, mostly on the British route through IGCSE rather than MYP 4 and 5. sections.heading: What MYP support costs around The Meadows, counted by the month
paragraphs: A direct answer before the detail: an MYP tutor working online with a Meadows family costs between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour at the qualified-subject-tutor band, which is roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month for one weekly hour. Below that band sit university-student tutors from about AED 45 an hour. Above it sit IB-experienced specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and more. All of those are market figures published by other providers in 2026, and each is attributed in the table.

The monthly view is the one that matters because tutoring is a subscription in everything but name. A family that signs at AED 300 an hour for two subjects has committed to AED 2,400 a month, and that commitment usually fails somewhere around the second term. The same budget spent as one weekly hour at AED 200 on the single weakest criterion, running from October to May, finishes the job. Hours concentrated on a diagnosis beat hours spread across a subject.

Note what the in-home premium is actually buying. Dubai in-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against AED 150 to AED 300 for an equivalently qualified tutor working online. The difference is not teaching quality; it is petrol, a Sheikh Zayed Road crossing at 16:30, and the fact that the tutor can only serve the families living within a 20-minute drive. For a Meadows household that means choosing from whoever is nearby rather than from whoever actually teaches MYP Extended mathematics.

One more number worth knowing before you budget. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package the government valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are the fixed cost in a Dubai education budget and tutoring is the variable one, so a year without a fee increase is the year to spend deliberately on the variable rather than reactively.

sections.heading: The criterion letters are where tutoring money actually moves
paragraphs: An MYP report does not say 68 per cent. It says criterion A: 6, criterion B: 4, criterion C: 3, criterion D: 5, and a subject grade of 5. That breakdown is the most valuable thing a Meadows parent owns, and most tutoring is bought without anyone reading it. Each criterion is marked from 0 to 8 against published descriptors, and the four are combined into a 1-7 grade using boundaries the school applies. A child losing marks on one criterion needs a different set of lessons from a child losing them on another.

Take mathematics. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is routine procedure under time pressure. Criterion B, investigating patterns, asks the student to find a rule, test it, justify it and generalise it. Criterion C, communicating, marks whether the working is laid out so a reader can follow it. Criterion D asks for mathematics applied to a real context with a reflection on how well the model fits. A student can be fluent and still lose a third of the available marks on B and D, and no amount of extra practice on procedure touches that.

The same split runs through every subject group. Sciences hides its marks in inquiring and designing and in processing and evaluating, which are investigation skills rather than content. Language and Literature loses them in analysing, where plot summary gets written instead of comment on the writer's choices. Design loses them in the written design cycle, where students who build a good artefact document it badly. The table below sets the criterion names out by subject group so you can match a report line to a teachable skill.

What this means in cash terms is simple. Six sessions aimed at one criterion, with the student's own marked work in front of both of them, costs around AED 1,200 to AED 1,800 at the qualified-tutor band and moves a reported mark. A year of general subject support at the same rate costs AED 7,000 or more and often moves the same mark by the same amount. Ask any prospective tutor which criterion they intend to work on in the first three lessons. A tutor who cannot answer has not read the report.

sections.heading: Three ways Emirates Living families overspend on the Middle Years Programme
paragraphs: The first is paying Diploma rates for middle-school work. A tutor who teaches Higher Level Chemistry is not the right purchase for an MYP 2 science criterion, and charging AED 400 an hour for it is the market working exactly as intended. MYP 1 to MYP 3 is almost always a job for the AED 150 to AED 300 band, and often for the lower half of it. Save the specialist rate for MYP 5 and the bridge into DP1, where the teacher's Diploma experience is the thing you are actually buying.

The second is buying hours instead of feedback cycles. A student improves on a criterion by writing something, having it marked against the descriptor, and writing the next one differently. That cycle takes a week, not an hour, and a tutor who fills every session with new teaching never completes one. Two sessions a fortnight with marked work in between frequently beats one session a week with nothing in between, at two-thirds of the monthly cost. Ask how written work gets marked between lessons before you ask the hourly rate.

The third is the sibling discount trap. Emirates Living households often have two or three children in the same school, and a provider offering a household rate for all of them is selling convenience rather than teaching. Two children in different MYP years, with different weak criteria, in different subject groups, need two different tutors. A single tutor stretched across both usually ends up supervising homework for both, at the combined price of two subject specialists.

There is a fourth, smaller leak worth naming: paying through the long Dubai summer out of fear of losing the tutor. A pause is a scheduling conversation, not a cancellation, and a six-week gap in MYP 2 costs nothing measurable. The exception is the summer between MYP 5 and DP1, which is the one holiday where paid work changes the following year's outcome. Spend there and pause elsewhere.

sections.heading: MYP year by year: what is worth funding, and what is not yet
paragraphs: MYP 1 to MYP 3 are the cheap years and the ones where spending has the longest payback. Nothing external is at stake, which is exactly why a reading-fluency or extended-writing gap can be closed for a few hundred dirhams a month instead of several thousand later. The questions worth paying someone to answer here are narrow: can the child write four paragraphs to a structure, and is arithmetic automatic enough that MYP Extended mathematics will not be a struggle.

MYP 4 and MYP 5 change the stakes without changing the assessment style. Subject selection narrows, Extended and Standard mathematics streams separate, and the Personal Project arrives. This is where a Meadows family should be spending deliberately, because the MYP 5 record is what a Diploma conversation is based on and because the Personal Project is the first piece of genuinely self-managed work most students have met. It is also the year where the school's own position on eAssessment starts to matter to your budget.

The DP1 entry point is the expensive boundary. Marking changes from criterion descriptors to percentage-weighted papers, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay appear, and six subjects run at once. Families who arrive without timed written practice spend the autumn of DP1 buying specialist hours at AED 270 and upwards. The table sets out, year by year, what is genuinely worth funding and what can safely wait, so the money lands where it compounds.

One caution across all five years. MYP grades are reported by the school, and schools differ in how strictly they apply the boundaries. A 6 at one Dubai school is not automatically a 6 at the next one, and a tutor claiming to know your school's boundaries is guessing. The reliable signal is the criterion mark and the descriptor it was awarded against, which is published and which does not move between schools.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: a line item with a hard honesty limit
paragraphs: The Personal Project sits in MYP 5 and is the most commonly mishandled purchase in the whole programme. It is a self-directed piece of work with a school supervisor, assessed against the criteria in the current MYP projects guide - planning, applying skills and reflecting in the present edition - each marked out of 8, with the process journal as the evidence base. Confirm with the school's MYP coordinator which edition of the guide your child's cohort is assessed under, because the criterion set has been revised.

What a tutor may legitimately do here is coaching, and it is genuinely valuable. Questioning whether the goal is achievable in the time available. Checking that the journal records decisions as they happen rather than being reconstructed the week before submission. Reading what the student has written and saying where a criterion descriptor is not yet met. Rehearsing the reflection so it discusses what went wrong rather than listing what was done. That is six to ten hours of work, spread across the year, not a weekly slot.

What a tutor must never do is produce the thing. A tutor does not write the report, does not build the product, and does not draft the journal entries. IB academic honesty rules make authorship the student's responsibility, and a project that is not the student's own work is a malpractice matter for the student, not a service failure for the tutor. Any provider offering to hand over a finished Personal Project is selling a risk dressed as a shortcut, and the Dubai market contains providers who do exactly that.

On cost, the useful comparison is against a weekly slot. Ten coaching hours at the AED 200 to AED 300 band is AED 2,000 to AED 3,000 across a whole academic year. A weekly hour across the same year at the same rate is AED 7,000 or more. The coaching block is cheaper and better matched to how the project is actually assessed, because the marks are awarded at three points, not thirty-six.

sections.heading: eAssessment or a school-reported grade: the question that sets your budget
paragraphs: Not every MYP school enters its MYP 5 students for external assessment. The IB offers optional on-screen eAssessment and ePortfolio moderation at the end of MYP 5, leading to the IB MYP Certificate, and schools choose whether to run it. Some Dubai schools do; others report MYP grades internally and move students straight into DP1 or into an A Level programme. The answer changes what MYP 5 tutoring is for, so it is the first question to ask the school, before the first question you ask a tutor.

If the school runs eAssessment, MYP 5 has an external examination shape and the money should go into timed, on-screen written practice under conditions. If it does not, the MYP 5 grade is a school judgement and the real stake is the DP1 place and the Higher Level subject choices that follow. In that case the spend belongs in the bridge over the summer rather than in exam technique during the spring. Two genuinely different budgets follow from one administrative fact.

Ask the question precisely, because the answers are often vague. Does the school enter students for MYP eAssessment; if so, in which subject groups; and is the Personal Project submitted for IB moderation. The IB sets the conditions for the certificate itself, and the school's MYP coordinator is the only reliable source on what your child's cohort will actually sit. Nothing on this page should be treated as a statement about your particular school's practice.

There is a related question parents rarely ask and should. If the school does not run eAssessment, how does it decide its MYP grade boundaries, and will the DP1 subject recommendations be based on those grades. That is the decision a Meadows family is actually buying tutoring to influence in MYP 4 and 5. Knowing whether the gatekeeper is an external script marker or a departmental meeting tells you where the hours should go.

sections.heading: Twelve months before DP1: the cost in context from a Meadows villa
paragraphs: Tutoring is easier to judge next to the other numbers in a Dubai education budget. School fees are the large fixed cost and they are flat this year: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for 2026-27, under the second economic incentives package Dubai valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. The emirate also added seven new private schools for 2026-27 - four UK curriculum and three IB - creating 16,846 new places, after six opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

Against that backdrop, one MYP subject at one online hour a week is a AED 600 to AED 1,200 monthly line. Two subjects doubles it. The Personal Project coaching block is a one-off of a few thousand dirhams spread across the year. The MYP 5 to DP1 summer bridge is the largest single discretionary item and the one with the clearest return. The table lays the whole twelve months out in dirhams, with the market in-home rate included for comparison rather than as an offer.

Two things are deliberately absent from that table. There is no IB Gram price list, because our quote depends on subject, level and the criterion involved, and it is given after a free trial lesson rather than before. And there is no VAT position, because the UAE treatment of tuition fees is a Federal Tax Authority question rather than ours to assert; ask any provider directly whether a quoted figure includes it and get the answer in writing.

The practical use of a table like this is to decide what to cut. Most Meadows families who overspend do so by running two or three subjects at once through the middle years, then having nothing left for the one summer where it counts. Running one subject at a time, on the weakest reported criterion, and banking the difference for the DP1 bridge, is the version of this budget that finishes the programme with money still in it.

sections.heading: Paying an MYP tutor lawfully in Dubai, and what to ask before you transfer money
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' and lists a two-working-day completion time.

Two consequences follow for a Meadows household. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws - no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat any figure you see quoted as unverified. And because the permit is free and takes two days, a tutor who cannot discuss their permit position has chosen not to deal with it. Asking is reasonable, and the answer tells you something about how the rest of the arrangement will be run.

A second distinction matters. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram is not a Dubai training institute and holds no KHDA permit, no ADEK registration and no IB or Cambridge accreditation, and any provider implying otherwise should be asked to produce the permit number. Naming a regulator is not the same as being endorsed by one.

In Abu Dhabi there is an extra rule worth knowing even from Dubai, because families move between emirates. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct to similar effect. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical point stands either way: do not go looking for your child's own class teacher privately.

sections.heading: Starting from The Meadows, with the limits stated up front
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Tell us the school, the MYP year, the subject, and the criterion letters from the last report. We come back with a tutor who has taught that subject group at that level, a proposed focus for the first three lessons, and a rate. You take the free trial lesson in one subject, with no card details collected, and decide afterwards. Nothing is charged before that lesson and there is no package to commit to in order to get it.

Here is the limit. MYP-specific tutors are scarcer than IGCSE ones everywhere, including Dubai, because the programme is a small share of the market - the IB accounts for about 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent for UK curricula. For a mainstream MYP subject group we can usually match within a few days. For a narrow combination - Language Acquisition at a specific phase, Design at MYP 5, Music - it can take longer, and the tutor may be based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time. We say which before you book, not after.

Scheduling is the other thing to settle early. A Meadows child home at 16:10 from Emirates International School Meadows can hold a 16:30 slot; one travelling back from Al Barsha South or Motor City usually cannot start before 17:00. Pick the slot that survives a bad traffic week rather than the one that works on a good one, because a session that gets moved three times stops being weekly and stops working. Sessions can shift later during Ramadan, including post-iftar slots.

If the honest answer is that tutoring is not what your child needs yet, we will say that too. An MYP 1 student with a 4 on criterion C in two subjects usually needs a writing structure taught once, not a year of weekly hours. That conversation costs nothing and it is the cheapest thing on this page.

process.title: Send the criterion marks, not a general worry
process.description: The useful first message names the school, the MYP year, the subject and the criterion letters from the most recent report. Criterion A: 6, criterion C: 3 tells a tutor more than a paragraph about confidence does, and it lets us match on the specific skill rather than on the subject label.

process.title: We match on subject group and level
process.description: A tutor who has taught that MYP subject group, at that year, and ideally into the Diploma beyond it. If the match needs a narrow specialism we say how long it will take and whether the tutor is UAE-based or teaching into Gulf Standard Time from elsewhere, before you commit anything.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one subject, no card
process.description: Sixty minutes with the student's own marked work open on screen. You are judging one thing: does the tutor identify the same weakness the report does, and can they explain how it gets fixed. No card details are collected to book it and there is no obligation afterwards.

process.title: Agree a focus and a review point
process.description: Before the second lesson we write down which criterion the next six sessions target and how you will know it moved. Marked written work between sessions is part of that plan, not an extra. The review happens at six sessions and the options include stopping.

process.title: Reschedule rather than lose sessions
process.description: School trips, tournaments and travel are normal in Emirates Living. Sessions move; they are not forfeited. During Ramadan slots shift later, including after iftar, and over the long summer a pause is a scheduling decision rather than a cancellation of the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: The rates on this page have sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or rate study that published it, read in October 2026. Three of the six competitor pages researched in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars. A Meadows family can check our numbers against the original pages, which is the point of printing them.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-first, not subject-first
whyPoints.description: Tutoring is aimed at a named criterion from your child's own report, with a written focus agreed before the second lesson and a review at six. That is what makes a block of hours measurable. Subject-in-general tutoring is the most expensive way to buy a small improvement.

whyPoints.title: Online for a reason we can defend
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. What a Meadows family gets instead is a tutor chosen for teaching MYP Extended mathematics rather than for living near Emirates Living.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is stated, not assumed
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, reads drafts and gives feedback on work the student has written. No Personal Project, investigation or coursework is produced for a student under any arrangement. Providers in this market do sell completed assessed work; that is an IB malpractice trigger for the student, and we say so plainly.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed before you book
whyPoints.description: Where a niche MYP subject has no UAE-based specialist free, we say so and name the alternative, including when a tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into your evening. No competitor page researched in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

whyPoints.title: No regulator borrowed as a badge
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE and the Ministry of Education are named on this page to explain what each one governs. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from any of them, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none.

faqs.question: How much does an IB MYP tutor in The Meadows cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates put a university-student tutor at roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300, and an IB-experienced specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 or more. For most MYP work in The Meadows the middle band is the right purchase; the specialist band earns its premium only in MYP 5 and the bridge into DP1. Those figures come from other providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, read in October 2026. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, against the specific subject and criterion involved.

faqs.question: Is MYP tutoring cheaper than IB Diploma tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the gap is substantial. Diploma support sits at the specialist end of the Dubai market, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 an hour and Bestimate's exam-year band runs from AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Most MYP work is properly priced at AED 150 to AED 300. That price gap is the argument for spending in MYP 4 and MYP 5 rather than waiting: the same weakness costs less to fix before DP1 than after it. The exception is the summer bridge between MYP 5 and DP1, which needs a Diploma-experienced teacher and is priced accordingly.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report shows criterion letters instead of percentages. What am I actually paying a tutor to fix?
faqs.answer: One or two of those letters. Each MYP subject is graded against four criteria, A to D, each marked from 0 to 8 against published descriptors, and the four combine into a grade from 1 to 7. A student scoring 6 on criterion A and 3 on criterion C has a presentation and communication problem, not a knowledge problem, and the lessons that fix those two things look nothing alike. Send the criterion marks when you enquire. A tutor who agrees a focus of criterion C before the second lesson is doing the job; one who proposes general subject revision has not read the report.

faqs.question: Should we start MYP tutoring in Year 7 or wait until MYP 4?
faqs.answer: Start early only for a specific, named gap. In MYP 1 to MYP 3 the two things worth paying to fix are extended writing structure and arithmetic fluency, because both are assumed later and both are cheap to teach now at the AED 150 to AED 300 band. Waiting until MYP 4 to address either means buying the same repair in a year where subject selection and the Personal Project are already competing for the same hours. What is not worth buying in MYP 1 is subject-specialist teaching, which has nothing external to prepare for yet.

faqs.question: What is a realistic monthly tutoring budget for one MYP subject in Emirates Living?
faqs.answer: For one weekly online hour with a qualified subject tutor, AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month is the band the Dubai market quotes, with Bestimate placing budget tutors at AED 240 to AED 600 and exam-year specialists at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more. Advertised monthly packages in this market include roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. Compare any package against the hourly rate before signing, and check whether unused sessions expire, because that is where the real cost of a package usually hides.

faqs.question: Does my child's school run MYP eAssessment, and does the answer change what we should spend?
faqs.answer: It changes it significantly, and only the school can tell you. The IB offers optional on-screen eAssessment and ePortfolio moderation at the end of MYP 5 leading to the IB MYP Certificate, and each school decides whether to enter students. If yours does, MYP 5 has an examination shape and money belongs in timed written practice under conditions. If it does not, the MYP 5 grade is a school judgement and the real stake is the DP1 place, so the spend belongs in the summer bridge instead. Ask the MYP coordinator which subject groups are entered, if any.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover MYP mathematics and MYP sciences for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but it is not usually the saving it looks like. A teacher with a physics or engineering background often covers both credibly at MYP level. The question to ask is which criteria are weak in each subject: if it is investigating patterns in mathematics and inquiring and designing in sciences, those are related investigation skills and one tutor is efficient. If the weaknesses are communicating in one and content knowledge in the other, you are asking one person to run two unrelated programmes in alternating weeks, which tends to produce homework supervision.

faqs.question: How much should Personal Project support cost, and what may a tutor actually do?
faqs.answer: Six to ten hours spread across MYP 5 is the realistic shape, which is roughly AED 2,000 to AED 3,000 at the mid band rather than a weekly slot costing several times that. A tutor may question whether the goal fits the time available, check that the process journal records decisions as they happen, read drafts the student has written and say where a criterion descriptor is not yet met. A tutor must never write the report, build the product or draft journal entries. The project has to be the student's own work, and IB honesty rules make that the student's exposure.

faqs.question: Why do some Dubai providers quote MYP lessons in 45-minute blocks?
faqs.answer: Partly because younger students concentrate better in shorter sessions, and partly because it makes an hourly rate look smaller. Compare on cost per month rather than per session: four 45-minute slots at AED 200 is AED 600 a month for three hours of teaching, while four 60-minute slots at AED 225 is AED 900 for four. For MYP 1 to MYP 3 a 45-minute lesson is often genuinely better. For MYP 5 timed writing it is too short to complete a piece and mark it. Ask what the rate is per hour and decide the length separately.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for an MYP tutor when there is no external exam at the end?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the MYP 5 grade is used for at your school, which is why the eAssessment question comes first. Where there is no external assessment, the MYP record still drives Diploma subject recommendations and Higher Level permissions, and those decisions shape the next two years. The case for spending is strongest in MYP 4 and MYP 5 for that reason. The case is weakest in MYP 1 and MYP 2 unless there is a named gap, and a provider pushing weekly hours in Year 7 without naming one is selling a subscription.

faqs.question: What does the bridge from MYP 5 into DP1 cost across a summer?
faqs.answer: At the specialist band of AED 200 to AED 450 an hour, a six to eight week bridge of one or two subjects runs into a few thousand dirhams, and it is the MYP-adjacent spend with the clearest return. What it buys is the jump the MYP does not prepare students for: percentage-weighted papers, timed writing marked against Diploma criteria, and the algebraic fluency Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes from week one. Because lessons are over live video, the bridge continues while the family travels, which matters in a Dubai summer when most households leave.

faqs.question: Do MYP tutors working with Dubai families need a MoHRE permit, and is there a fee?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, with a stated two-working-day completion time, and the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so treat quoted figures as unverified.

faqs.question: Will Arabic and Islamic Education still be on my child's timetable alongside the MYP?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be in place from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Tutoring in these subjects must follow the Ministry-set content, since additional material needs prior Ministry permission.

faqs.question: Which schools near The Meadows run the MYP rather than a British Key Stage 3?
faqs.answer: Inside Emirates Living the IB continuum option is Emirates International School Meadows, with Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills the other nearby IB school a Meadows family commonly considers. Dubai British School Emirates Hills and Regent International School in The Greens run the British route, as do most of the Al Barsha and Al Sufouh schools Meadows children travel to. The IB accounts for about 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent for UK curricula, which is why MYP-specific tutors are scarcer locally than IGCSE ones. Named schools here are context, not partners.

faqs.question: Halfway through a term, how do I tell whether the tutoring money is working?
faqs.answer: By looking at a criterion mark, not at a mood. Agree before the second lesson which criterion the next six sessions target, then compare the mark awarded on that criterion in the next piece of marked school work. If it has not moved after six sessions, the diagnosis was wrong, the format is wrong, or the tutor is wrong, and all three are fixable. Session notes after each lesson should name what moved and what did not. A provider who reports only that your child is more confident is not giving you anything you can check.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-springs.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Middle Years Programme subjects to students in The Springs and across Emirates Living. Each one works from the criteria for their own subject group rather than from a generic syllabus, and every lesson is one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: The money goes wrong because the assessment is unfamiliar
paragraphs: A Springs parent with a child in MYP 3 or MYP 4 usually arrives at tutoring from a report that is hard to read. There are letters where percentages used to be, numbers out of eight, and a final figure between 1 and 7 that nobody has explained. The instinct is to buy more lessons in the subject with the lowest number. The problem is that the lowest number is often produced by one criterion out of four, and a general weekly hour spends four lessons on content when the gap was in a specific assessed skill.

Here is the structure, because it changes what is worth paying for. Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, and each criterion is marked on a scale of 1 to 8. The four marks add to a raw total out of 32, which is converted into a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. In mathematics the criteria are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In the sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student can be strong in criterion A and weak in criterion B, and the report will show one grade for both.

That is why the first question is which criterion, not which subject. A student losing marks on criterion B in sciences needs to learn how to write a method with controlled variables and a testable hypothesis, which is a different job from revising the content of the unit. A student losing criterion D in mathematics needs to learn how to apply a technique to an unfamiliar real-world context and comment on the limitations of their model. Neither of those is fixed by more worked examples, and both are commonly mistaken for content weakness.

The second reason money goes wrong is timing. There is no external examination in most MYP years, so the usual exam-year logic does not apply. What does have hard deadlines is the Personal Project in MYP 5, the interdisciplinary units, and the transition at the end of MYP 5 into the Diploma or into IGCSE. Those are the three points where a small number of well-chosen hours makes a measurable difference, and they are the three that families typically address last.

Delivery is stated plainly before any figures. All UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, because home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For MYP work this matters less than parents expect and helps more than they assume: criterion-based feedback on a piece of written work happens on a shared screen, and the annotated version stays available to the student afterwards.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-springs.programmesIntro: MYP spans five years, and what a tutor should be doing changes completely across them. Separating the years is how a Springs family avoids paying for the wrong kind of help at the wrong time.

programmes.name: MYP 1 to 3
programmes.description: The years where habits are set and tutoring is cheapest. The useful work is learning what each criterion asks for, how to write a method, how to structure an analysis, and how to reflect in a way that earns marks rather than fills a box. Content support here is secondary to assessment literacy.
programmes.countryNote: Schools serving The Springs typically run the community project in MYP 3 or MYP 4, depending on where their programme ends. Ask which year yours uses, because that project is the first piece of extended independent work a student produces and it is where process-journal habits are formed or missed.

programmes.name: MYP 4
programmes.description: The year the workload rises and the subject set narrows. Students begin to meet criterion tasks that resemble Diploma assessments in miniature: investigations with hypotheses, extended written analyses, and mathematical explorations in all but name. This is the cheapest point to address a weak criterion properly.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 4 is also when a Springs family should start asking what happens at 16. Some students will continue into the Diploma at an IB campus in or near Emirates Living; others will move to a British-curriculum school and sit IGCSE. The two routes need different preparation, and knowing which one is likely changes the plan.

programmes.name: MYP 5
programmes.description: The year with real deadlines: the Personal Project with its process journal, product and report, plus any eAssessment the school offers. Support here is supervision and feedback on the student's own work, scheduled against the school's internal dates rather than anything published centrally.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai school offers MYP eAssessment, it combines on-screen examinations in some subject groups with ePortfolios in others. Ask your coordinator which subjects your child will sit on screen and which are portfolio-assessed, because the preparation for the two is not remotely the same.

programmes.name: After MYP 5
programmes.description: The transition year, and the point where MYP students most often need paid help. A student moving into the Diploma meets formal examinations for the first time; a student moving to IGCSE meets a content-dense two-year syllabus with tiered entry. Both gaps are closable in a summer if addressed deliberately.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, and enrolment rose six per cent during 2025-26. A Springs family's post-MYP options are wider than they were for an older sibling, so the destination should be checked rather than assumed.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-springs.subjectsIntro: These are the MYP subject groups Emirates Living families ask about, with the four criteria that actually produce the grade. Testing a prospective tutor against the right four is the fastest way to tell whether they know the programme.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where most marks are lost, because pattern investigation and generalisation are rarely taught as a separate skill. Criterion D needs modelling and a comment on limitations.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B demands a testable hypothesis with controlled variables; criterion C demands data processing with evaluated conclusions. Both are writing skills as much as scientific ones.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criteria: analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students who read well still lose criterion A marks for summarising rather than analysing, and criterion B marks for an essay that has paragraphs but no structural argument.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria: listening, reading, speaking and writing, with a phase rather than a year group determining the expectation. A Springs student can be in phase 2 French and phase 4 Arabic in the same timetable, and a tutor needs the phase before anything else.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Criterion D is the one that separates grades: evaluating sources, recognising bias and weighing competing interpretations rather than reciting content.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria: inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The most process-heavy subject in the programme and the one where a well-kept design folder earns marks that a good final product cannot recover on its own.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The written and reflective components carry real weight, which surprises families who think of arts as a practical subject and plan accordingly.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Two of the four are written, so a capable athlete can hold a middling grade while the physical performance is strong.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed with their own criteria around disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting. Students often treat an interdisciplinary task as two subjects stapled together, which is exactly what the synthesis criterion is designed not to reward.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed against planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight, with a process journal, a product or outcome and a report. A tutor may supervise, question and give feedback; the project and the writing must be entirely the student's own.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Communication, social, self-management, research and thinking skills, taught across subjects rather than in one. Self-management and research are the two that most often explain a bright student's inconsistent criterion marks, and both are teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.levels: MYP years, as required in Dubai
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These sit alongside the MYP subjects and have their own ministry-set content expectations.

sections.heading: Four criteria, not a percentage: what you are actually paying to improve
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a Springs parent can do before spending anything is find out which criterion is low. Schools publish criterion marks in their reporting systems, usually as four numbers out of eight per subject, and those four numbers tell you what kind of help is needed. Two students with the same grade 4 in sciences can need completely different tutoring: one is weak on knowing and understanding, which is content, and the other is weak on inquiring and designing, which is scientific writing.

The criteria are not interchangeable between subject groups, and this is where unqualified tutors reveal themselves quickly. Mathematics has knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Sciences has knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Language and literature has analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Somebody who refers to criteria generically, without naming the four for your child's subject, has not worked inside the programme.

The second thing the criterion marks tell you is whether the problem is general or specific. A student with three sixes and a two has one fixable skill gap. A student with four fours is coasting across the subject and needs a different conversation, probably about workload and self-management rather than about content. The first is a four-lesson block; the second is a term.

Ask the subject teacher one additional question: which task produced the low criterion mark, and what did the descriptor at the next level up require that the student did not do. Teachers can answer that in a sentence, and it converts a vague request for a tutor into a specific, short, measurable piece of work.

sections.heading: From 32 raw marks to a grade of 7: reading the report properly
paragraphs: Four criteria at eight marks each give a raw total out of 32, and that total converts to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. The conversion is the part that confuses parents arriving from a percentage system, because the bands are uneven and a single raw mark can move a grade at a boundary. A student on 23 and a student on 19 can both be reported as the same grade, and a student on 24 is a grade higher than the one on 23.

What follows from that is a piece of practical advice worth more than most tutoring. If a child sits one raw mark below a boundary, the useful intervention is not a term of general lessons; it is finding which criterion is furthest from its next descriptor and doing four lessons of marked practice on that one. If a child sits in the middle of a band, a single mark changes nothing, and the honest answer may be that tutoring is not the priority this term.

The second thing to understand is that criterion marks are not cumulative averages in the way a percentage is. Teachers judge against descriptors on specific tasks, and a best-fit judgement across the year is what lands on the report. A single poor task early in a unit does not permanently depress a grade, which is reassuring, and a single good one does not lift it, which is less so.

Finally, the report tells you nothing about Diploma readiness on its own. A grade 6 in MYP mathematics does not translate into a prediction for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, because the two are assessed on entirely different things. That judgement belongs to the subject teacher and the Diploma coordinator, and it is worth asking for explicitly in MYP 5 rather than inferring.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs around Emirates Living, and how to verify it yourself
paragraphs: Everything in this section can be checked by a parent in twenty minutes, which is the point. The figures below are published on providers' own pages and in a public Dubai rate table, and the reason to show the sources is that a quote you cannot benchmark is a quote you cannot judge. Three of the six most visible providers in this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars.

The published positions, read in October 2026: EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which at that level generally means a university student working from a textbook. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which sits inside the AED 150 to 300 band for qualified subject tutors teaching online. TutorChase lists AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table shows AED 200 to 450 and above for IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500.

For a household budget the monthly figures matter more. Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to 600 a month in the budget band, AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work. Monthly packages visible in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Set that against a school fee position KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026, when it stated there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for 2026-27 under the emirate's AED 1.5 billion incentives package.

MYP sits awkwardly in these bands because almost nobody prices it separately. Providers advertise IB rates, and those rates are built around Diploma demand. A family paying Diploma specialist rates for MYP 2 mathematics is paying for scarcity that does not apply. The questions worth asking are whether the tutor has taught MYP specifically, whether the rate differs from the Diploma rate, and what the four criteria are for the subject group in question.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: supervision, a process journal, and a hard line
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is the first substantial independent piece a student produces, and it is assessed against planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight. The deliverables are a process journal kept throughout, a product or outcome, and a report. Most of the marks that get lost are lost in the journal, because students treat it as paperwork to be assembled near the deadline rather than as the evidence of the process the criteria are actually marking.

Where a tutor earns their fee is at the start. A project scoped too widely cannot be completed; a project scoped too narrowly cannot evidence planning. Three sessions in the early weeks - choosing something achievable, setting a realistic goal with criteria for success, and establishing a journal habit of short dated entries - do more for the final marks than ten sessions of rescue work in the final month. This is the clearest value in the whole MYP budget and the one families most often skip.

The line is absolute and worth hearing before anybody starts. A tutor may discuss the choice of project, ask the questions a good supervisor asks, explain what each criterion rewards, and give feedback on a journal or report the student has written. A tutor must never write the report, produce the product, or edit the student's writing to completion. Providers in this market sell finished coursework at four-figure prices; buying that purchases an academic-honesty problem that attaches to the student.

The school's own internal deadline is the date that governs everything, not anything published centrally, because the school needs time to supervise, authenticate and mark. Ask for that date in the first weeks of MYP 5 and build the plan backwards from it.

sections.heading: The fork at the end of MYP 5, and what each route costs to prepare for
paragraphs: Every MYP 5 student in Emirates Living is heading somewhere, and the three realistic destinations need different preparation. Continuing into the Diploma at an IB campus means meeting formal written examinations for the first time, plus internal assessments with their own criteria. Moving to a British-curriculum school means starting a two-year IGCSE course with tiered entry and content density that MYP does not match. Moving abroad means whichever system the destination uses, usually with a mid-year entry point.

The Diploma gap is mostly about examination conditions and procedural fluency. MYP assesses understanding through tasks; the Diploma assesses it under timed conditions with no second attempt. A student who has never sat a two-hour paper will lose marks to pacing in the first term of DP1 regardless of ability. Six to ten summer lessons on timed practice and on procedural accuracy close most of that, and in mathematics specifically the algebraic fluency gap is the single most common one.

The IGCSE gap is about volume and specificity. Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses name content precisely, mark schemes reward particular wording, and tier entry caps the grade available. A student arriving from MYP has strong investigative skills and may never have memorised a defined list. The preparation is content mapping - establishing what the syllabus requires that the MYP units did not cover - and it is best done before the first term rather than discovered in it.

The table sets out the three routes with the gap and the typical support shape. Nobody needs tutoring to make a transition successfully; what tutoring buys is a shorter adjustment period, which in a two-year course is worth real marks.
