sections.heading: Where MYP money is wasted in a Springs household
paragraphs: The first and biggest waste is buying examination technique for a programme that mostly does not examine. A tutor who arrives with past papers and timed drills for an MYP 3 student is selling a Diploma product. There is a place for timed practice - the transition year, and any subject the school assesses on screen through eAssessment - but for most MYP years the marks come from criterion-based tasks, and preparing for the wrong thing is expensive.

The second is paying Diploma specialist rates for middle-years content. Published IB rates in this market are built around Diploma scarcity: Unitors lists IB from AED 200, Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above. MYP 2 mathematics does not require that scarcity. Ask whether the rate quoted is the provider's Diploma rate applied without adjustment, and ask what the tutor has actually taught at MYP level.

The third is general homework supervision sold as subject tutoring. A good number of MYP referrals in this community are really about self-management: work not started, deadlines missed, a process journal not kept. That is a real problem with a real solution, and the solution is cheaper than a subject specialist. Conflating the two means paying specialist rates for something a structured routine would fix.

The fourth is the open-ended weekly arrangement with no stated target. In a programme without external examinations there is no natural end point, so a weekly MYP slot can run for two years without anybody asking what changed. A block with a named criterion, a number of lessons and a written endpoint is the version a family can audit, and in MYP it is almost always the right structure.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units, service as action, and the Dubai-mandated subjects alongside them
paragraphs: Three parts of the programme sit outside the ordinary subject timetable and generate questions from Springs parents every year. Interdisciplinary units are assessed with their own criteria around disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting, and students commonly treat them as two subjects stapled together. The synthesis criterion is specifically designed not to reward that, so the teachable skill is building a single argument that genuinely needs both disciplines.

Service as action is a programme requirement rather than a graded subject, and it is not something a tutor should be involved in beyond helping a student reflect on it in writing where the school asks for that. Any provider offering to arrange or document service for a student has misunderstood what it is for.

The mandated UAE subjects are the third. Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and the guidance advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes.

One constraint follows from that and it shapes how support can honestly be described. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Tutoring in these subjects therefore works with the school's own material and the ministry-set content, not with a parallel curriculum, and KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic in schools hold appropriate approval to teach them.

sections.heading: Starting MYP support from The Springs, and what we say before you pay
paragraphs: The first step costs nothing and saves the most. Open the school's reporting system and write down the four criterion marks for the subject in question, then ask the subject teacher which task produced the low one and what the next descriptor required. With those two pieces of information a tutor can name the first four lessons before anybody pays, and a parent can tell whether a provider actually understands the programme from how they react to it.

Then the practical arrangement. Pick the slot the week can genuinely hold: for a middle-years student in this community that usually means 16:15 to 17:00 on a weekday, because the bus reaches the higher Springs numbers closer to 16:45 and a 19:00 lesson for an MYP 2 student produces a tired hour and a cancellation the following week. Personal Project supervision works better on a Saturday morning, which gives a longer uninterrupted block.

The free trial lesson is sixty minutes of teaching on the student's own work rather than a sales conversation. It ends with the tutor writing down which criterion is the gap, whether the cause is content, skill or self-management, and how many lessons that justifies. If the honest answer is four lessons rather than a term, that is what the note will say, and a four-lesson block that ends because the skill changed is the outcome this is built to produce.

Three limits stated before payment. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, because home tutoring is an India-only service. IB Gram holds no accreditation from the IB or from any UAE regulator and does not present itself as holding one; a provider in this market claiming board approval for its tutors is making a claim worth questioning closely. And on the Personal Project the line is absolute: a tutor must never write the report.

faqs.question: What do the four letters on my child's MYP report actually mean?
faqs.answer: They are the four assessment criteria for that subject, each marked from 1 to 8. The four marks add to a raw total out of 32, which converts to the reported grade of 1 to 7 using published boundaries. The criteria differ by subject group: mathematics uses knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, while sciences uses knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Which one is low tells you what kind of tutoring is needed, and often that it should be short.

faqs.question: Why does my child get a good grade in one MYP subject and a poor one in another with the same effort?
faqs.answer: Because the criteria reward different things. A student who is strong on content will score well where criterion A carries the weight and poorly where the subject leans on process criteria, such as inquiring and designing in sciences or investigating patterns in mathematics. Those process criteria are rarely taught as separate skills, so a capable student can lose a quarter of the available marks on something nobody has explicitly shown them. Four lessons of marked practice on the specific criterion usually transfers to every future task assessed the same way.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for MYP tutoring when there are no public exams?
faqs.answer: It is, for three specific things, and often not worth it for general subject support. The three are a diagnosed weak criterion, the Personal Project in MYP 5, and the transition at the end of MYP 5 into the Diploma or IGCSE. Those have clear targets and short timeframes. A rolling weekly slot in a programme with no external examination has no natural end point, which is how a Springs household ends up two years into an arrangement nobody has reviewed. Buy blocks with stated endpoints.

faqs.question: How much should MYP tutoring cost compared with Diploma tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market are built around Diploma demand, so check what you are being charged for. Unitors lists IB from AED 200 an hour and Bestimate's Dubai specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above; qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300 generally. Middle-years content does not require Higher Level Diploma specialism, so ask whether the quoted figure is simply the provider's IB rate applied without adjustment, and ask what the tutor has actually taught at MYP level. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026.

faqs.question: My child is one mark below a grade boundary. What should we actually do?
faqs.answer: Find which criterion is furthest from its next descriptor and do four lessons of marked practice on that one. Because the raw total out of 32 converts to a grade in uneven bands, a single mark genuinely matters at a boundary and genuinely does not in the middle of a band. Ask the subject teacher which criterion has the most headroom and what the next descriptor requires. That is a cheap, short, measurable piece of work, and it is a much better purchase than a term of general lessons in the subject.

faqs.question: How does the Personal Project get marked, and where do students lose marks?
faqs.answer: It is assessed against planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked out of eight, with a process journal, a product or outcome, and a report. Most lost marks sit in the journal, because students treat it as paperwork to assemble near the deadline instead of as the evidence of process that the criteria are actually marking. Short dated entries kept weekly from the start score far better than a reconstructed document. Scoping the project realistically in the early weeks is the other decisive factor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child finish the Personal Project if the deadline is close?
faqs.answer: A tutor can supervise, ask the questions a good supervisor asks, explain what each criterion rewards and give feedback on a journal or report the student has written. A tutor must never write the report, produce the product or edit the writing to completion. If the deadline is close and little exists, the honest work is helping the student salvage and document what they actually did, not manufacturing a process that did not happen. Providers selling finished coursework are selling your child an academic-honesty problem.

faqs.question: What should a Springs family do in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1?
faqs.answer: Six to ten lessons on timed conditions and procedural accuracy, which is the real gap rather than content. MYP assesses understanding through tasks; the Diploma assesses it under timed conditions with no second attempt, and a student who has never sat a two-hour paper loses marks to pacing in the first term regardless of ability. In mathematics specifically, algebraic fluency is the commonest gap. This is the cheapest useful intervention in the whole transition and almost nobody buys it.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP 5 to a British school for IGCSE. What changes?
faqs.answer: Content specificity and tier. Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses name required content precisely, mark schemes reward particular wording, and entry tier caps the grade available. A student arriving from MYP usually has strong investigative skills and little experience of memorising a defined list. The right preparation is content mapping before the first term: establishing what the new syllabus requires that the MYP units did not cover. Done early it is a short piece of work; discovered in November of Year 10 it is a term's catch-up.

faqs.question: What are interdisciplinary units and why does my child score badly on them?
faqs.answer: They are units assessed with their own criteria around disciplinary grounding, synthesising and reflecting, and the commonest error is treating the task as two subjects stapled together. The synthesis criterion is specifically designed not to reward that. What earns marks is a single argument that genuinely requires both disciplines, where neither alone would answer the question. It is a teachable structure and usually takes two or three sessions, because the difficulty is in the framing rather than in either subject's content.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic and Islamic Education in the MYP?
faqs.answer: In a Dubai private school, yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA's guidance requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit.

faqs.question: Can we get tutoring in the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the MYP ones?
faqs.answer: Support is possible, with one real constraint worth knowing. For the mandatory subjects, KHDA's guidance states that using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Tutoring therefore works with the school's own material and the ministry-set content rather than a parallel curriculum. KHDA also requires that school teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate approval to teach those subjects, which is a school-level requirement rather than something a private tutor can claim.

faqs.question: Is a weekly MYP slot or a short block better value?
faqs.answer: A short block, in most cases. MYP has no external examination in most years, so a weekly arrangement has no natural stopping point and tends to renew by default. A block built around one named criterion, with a stated number of lessons and a written handover at the end, is auditable: you can see what changed. A weekly slot is the right answer where the student is genuinely behind across a whole subject rather than weak on one assessed skill, and even then it should carry a review date.

faqs.question: Do MYP lessons continue during Ramadan and the long summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the hour moved rather than the plan changed. School days shorten during Ramadan and the useful window shifts later, so a 16:30 slot typically becomes an evening one for the month; families who arrange that in advance keep continuity. The long summer break, from late June or early July into early September, is the right time for transition work between MYP 5 and whatever follows, because it is the only uninterrupted block available. Lessons continue while a family travels, since everything runs over video.

faqs.question: Does the person tutoring an MYP student in Dubai need a licence?
faqs.answer: They need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, with MoHRE's service page listing a two-working-day completion time. The u.ae guidance states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published nobody should quote you an amount.

faqs.question: What if no MYP specialist is free in the subject and hour we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you. A narrow request - MYP design, or a specific language acquisition phase, at a fixed half-hour - cannot always be filled from the UAE-based pool. The options are then a specialist elsewhere teaching in your Gulf Standard Time slot at the same rate, a different hour with the right person, or an honest wait with an estimate. Filling the slot with somebody who cannot name the four criteria for that subject group is how families conclude that MYP tutoring does not work.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-springs.closingHeading: Find the criterion first, then decide what to buy
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-springs.closingBody: Before comparing rates, open the reporting system and write down the four criterion marks for the subject that worries you. Ask the teacher which task produced the low one and what the next descriptor required. With those two answers, a specialist can name the first four lessons and you can judge whether a provider actually knows the programme from how they respond. Then take the free trial lesson. Most Springs families who work in that order discover they need a short block rather than a year of weekly sessions.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-sustainable-ci.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Middle Years Programme subjects to students in The Sustainable City and the surrounding Dubailand communities, from MYP 1 through to the Personal Project year. Each works to the published criteria for their subject group rather than offering general homework support, because criterion marks are what the report card is made of.

intro.heading: A report card that needs translating before anything else
paragraphs: Middle Years Programme reporting confuses capable parents, and that is not a failure of attention. A Diploma report gives a predicted grade against an examination. An IGCSE report gives a mark on a paper. An MYP report gives four criterion scores out of eight each, per subject, with a 1 to 7 grade derived from their total through published boundaries. A child can score well on knowledge and poorly on communication, finish on a 4, and leave a parent unable to say what the problem is or whether it matters.

Translating that report is the first thing a useful MYP tutor does, and it takes about one session. The criteria differ by subject group but the structure is consistent: one criterion is usually about knowing and understanding, and the others cover inquiry, process, communication or reflection depending on the subject. The pattern across criteria tells you what kind of help is needed. A student losing marks on knowing and understanding needs content teaching. A student losing them on communication or reflection needs something else entirely, and content teaching will not touch it.

This page is organised around the calendar because that pattern has deadlines attached. MYP assessment is continuous, with summative tasks landing through every term, so there is no single revision window to work towards and no examination to count down to. What there is instead is a sequence: tasks each term, the Personal Project in the final year, and a Diploma or IGCSE subject decision that closes in the second term of MYP 5 whether or not the family is ready for it.

In The Sustainable City the practical picture is specific. Most Middle Years students here attend the IB continuum school inside the community, which means they are home by mid-afternoon and the useful late-afternoon hours genuinely exist. It also means cohorts are relatively small, so a subject is typically taught by one teacher and a student who does not follow that teacher's explanation has no second option inside the building. That is the most common and most legitimate reason families here engage a tutor.

Delivery is online and stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in this community. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own task sheets and marked work on screen. Home visits exist in our India operation only. For criterion work the format is well suited, because the useful material is the student's own writing and the published criteria beside it, which are easier to read side by side on a screen than across a kitchen table. The format also removes the two car journeys a visit would need, which is why a session can run while a thirteen-year-old is still able to concentrate rather than at the end of a long evening.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-sustainable-ci.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme spans five years and the work changes substantially across them. These are the stages we tutor and what each one actually needs, rather than a description of the programme's philosophy.

programmes.name: The early Middle Years
programmes.description: The transition out of the Primary Years Programme, where graded criterion marks appear for the first time and often come as a surprise. Nothing here affects a final qualification, which makes it the cheapest place to build habits: writing a justified answer rather than an answer, showing working, and reading a task sheet to find which criterion is actually being assessed.
programmes.countryNote: Children moving up inside the continuum school in The Sustainable City make this transition without changing buildings, which smooths the social side and hides the academic shift. Families arriving from British or American systems elsewhere in Dubai often need a term to understand that the criteria, not the content, are what the marks respond to.

programmes.name: The middle years of the programme
programmes.description: Content depth increases and subject choices begin to narrow. This is where mathematics splits into standard and extended pathways in most schools, and where a student's trajectory towards Higher Level Diploma subjects is effectively set. Criterion marks on inquiry and process criteria become harder to lift, because they reward a way of working rather than a body of knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: For students in this community aiming at Higher Level sciences or Analysis and Approaches two years later, MYP 4 is the real decision point. Algebraic fluency and data-handling skills built here are what make those options genuinely available in MYP 5, when the choice is made administratively rather than academically.

programmes.name: The final year and the Personal Project
programmes.description: The busiest MYP year by a distance: summative tasks across eight subject groups, the Personal Project with its own deadlines and assessed criteria, Service as Action commitments, and the Diploma or IGCSE subject decision. Schools offering MYP eAssessment add on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, which changes the final term substantially for those students.
programmes.countryNote: The decision that matters in this community is whether a student continues into the Diploma at the continuum school or moves to an IGCSE or A Level route at a school in Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Arabian Ranches. That choice is usually locked in the second term, which means any strengthening meant to influence it has to happen in the first.

programmes.name: MYP into the Diploma or IGCSE
programmes.description: The two destinations demand different preparation. The Diploma asks for independent extended writing, so the Personal Project experience transfers directly. An IGCSE route asks for examination technique under timing, which MYP assesses least, and a student moving that way usually needs a short block on timed papers and mark-scheme reading before Year 11 begins.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students moving from MYP 5 into a one-year IGCSE route, or into Year 11 at a British-curriculum school, face the sharpest version of this. MYP does not drill timed examination performance, so capable students can look weaker than they are for a term purely on pacing and command-word reading.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-sustainable-ci.subjectsIntro: What follows is the Middle Years subject groups with the criterion that most often costs marks in each. A tutoring enquiry naming a subject and a criterion letter gets a far better first session than one naming a subject alone.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Capable students lose most ground on investigating patterns, because describing a pattern is not the same as justifying a general rule, and on communicating, where notation and structure are assessed rather than the answer.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowledge and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Students strong on recall often sit on a 4 or 5 because the design and evaluation criteria are about method, and those are the criteria the Diploma investigation later assesses at 20%.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. The recurring loss is in analysing, where students summarise a text rather than examine how it achieves its effect. Fluent writers can score well on using language and poorly on analysing, which produces a confusing report line.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Students are assessed against a phase rather than a year group, so a parent should ask which phase their child is in before comparing marks with anyone else's.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the usual shortfall: students present information accurately and do not evaluate sources or weigh interpretations, which is specifically what that criterion rewards.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Marks are lost in evaluating, because students describe what they made rather than testing it against the design specification they wrote at the start.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more marks than students expect, and a strong final piece with a thin journal scores lower than a modest piece with a documented development process.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and reflective criteria are where marks move, which surprises students who assume the subject is assessed on physical ability alone.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on planning, applying skills, and reflecting, against a student-set goal and product. The commonest failure is a goal too large to evidence properly in the time available, which weakens every criterion at once because the process journal has nothing concrete to document.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These sit alongside the MYP subject groups and are frequently the weakest line for families who arrived mid-phase.

sections.heading: What the four criteria actually reward
paragraphs: This is the translation most families need and almost nobody publishes. Every Middle Years subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, and the four totals convert to a 1 to 7 grade through boundaries the school publishes. The criteria differ in name between subject groups but they do the same structural job: one tests what the student knows, and the others test how the student inquires, works, communicates and reflects. That division is the whole diagnostic value of an MYP report.

Read the pattern rather than the grade. A student with a strong knowing and understanding mark and weak communicating and reflecting marks does not have a content problem, and content tutoring will not move the grade. A student with the reverse pattern does have a content problem, and criterion coaching would be beside the point. A student weak across all four usually has a task-reading problem: they are answering what the question looks like rather than what the criterion being assessed requires.

This also explains a thing parents find genuinely baffling, which is a capable child sitting on a 4 across several subjects. The inquiry, process and reflection criteria reward behaviours — planning before producing, documenting development, evaluating against a stated specification — that a confident student often skips because they can produce a good outcome without them. The outcome is not what is marked. Once a student sees that on their own task sheet, the correction is usually fast.

sections.heading: The MYP 5 year counted backwards
paragraphs: MYP 5 is the busiest year in the programme and the one where a calendar genuinely helps, because the pressure comes from several directions that do not coordinate with each other. Summative tasks arrive across eight subject groups through every term. The Personal Project runs alongside them with its own internal deadlines. Service as Action commitments continue. And the Diploma or IGCSE subject decision has to be made in the middle of all of it, usually in the second term.

Work the sequence backwards and the priorities become clearer. The subject decision is the hardest deadline because it closes options permanently rather than just costing marks, so anything meant to influence it — strengthening mathematics to keep a Higher Level route open, for instance — has to happen in the first term. The Personal Project is the second hardest, because its process journal cannot be reconstructed after the fact and a late start shows in the planning and reflecting criteria.

For schools running MYP eAssessment, the final term adds on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, which changes the shape of the year for those students and introduces something closer to a conventional revision window. Not every school in Dubai offers it, so confirm with your child's coordinator whether it applies. The table below is the order of events rather than specific dates, because dates are set by the school and differ between them. The final column is what should already be finished by each point, which is the part a family can actually act on.

sections.heading: How criterion marks become a grade, and what moves them
paragraphs: The conversion from criterion totals to a 1 to 7 grade uses boundaries the school publishes, and understanding roughly how it works changes where a family spends effort. Four criteria marked out of eight give a total out of thirty-two, and the grade bands sit across that range. The practical consequence is that lifting one weak criterion from a 3 to a 6 moves the total more than nudging all four up by a point, and it is usually easier, because weak criteria tend to have a single identifiable cause.

That makes criterion marks a better planning tool than the grade. A parent who asks which criterion is lowest and what the task feedback said about it is asking a question that produces an action. A parent who asks how to move a 4 to a 5 is asking a question nobody can answer specifically. Schools publish the criteria and the task-specific clarifications, and a tutor should be working from those documents rather than from a general sense of the subject.

There is one caution worth stating. Criterion marks are not percentages and should not be read as them; an 8 is not a hundred per cent and a 4 is not a fail. They describe the level of achievement a piece of work demonstrated against a published descriptor. A student who scores 5 on a criterion for the first attempt at a genuinely hard task has done well, and treating it as a mediocre result is how a parent accidentally teaches a child to avoid difficulty.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and where it goes wrong
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the Middle Years Programme's culminating piece of independent work: a student-set goal, a product or outcome, a process journal and a report, assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It is also the first genuinely independent extended project most students have attempted, which makes it a useful rehearsal for the Diploma's Extended Essay and a reliable source of stress in MYP 5.

Almost every weak Personal Project has the same root cause: a goal too large or too vague to evidence properly. A student who sets out to build something ambitious spends the available time building and has nothing documented about planning or skill development, which weakens three criteria at once. A student with a modest, specific goal and a well-kept journal scores better with less work. Testing the scope of the goal at the outset is therefore the single most valuable session available.

The boundary on tutoring here is strict, and worth stating because the project is the easiest thing in the programme to outsource. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, question whether a goal is achievable, ask how a claim in the journal is evidenced, discuss skills the project needs, and comment on writing the student has produced. A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product, write or redraft the report or journal, or supply a model to adapt. The school supervises the project formally, and nothing a tutor does should bypass that.

sections.heading: MYP 5 into the Diploma or into IGCSE
paragraphs: This is the decision the calendar forces in the second term of MYP 5, and in this part of Dubai it is usually a real choice rather than a formality, because the continuum school offers the Diploma while several nearby schools offer IGCSE and A Levels. The two destinations reward different preparation, and a student who is strong in the Middle Years can be underprepared for one of them in a specific, fixable way.

A student continuing into the Diploma carries most of their Middle Years habits forward usefully. Independent extended writing, documented process and reflection are exactly what the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the subject internal assessments demand, so the Personal Project turns out to have been a rehearsal. What such a student typically needs is subject-specific depth in whichever two or three subjects will be taken at Higher Level, built in the final MYP term.

A student moving to an IGCSE or A Level route faces the opposite gap. The Middle Years Programme does not drill timed examination performance, mark-scheme reading or command-word discipline, because it does not assess them. A capable MYP student can therefore look weaker than they are for a full term purely on pacing. Four to six sessions on timed papers before that year starts usually removes the problem, and it is far cheaper than discovering it in a first set of mock results. The table sets out both destinations and when the gap in each is best closed.

sections.heading: What Middle Years tutoring costs, and how little of it is usually needed
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. In-home visits are AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, and specialists are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 with one premium provider advertising AED 650.

The honest point for Middle Years families is about quantity rather than rate. A great deal of what MYP students need is short and specific: one engagement on task-reading, four sessions on journal habits, a term of criterion-targeted work in one subject. Open-ended weekly tutoring across several subjects is rarely the right purchase at this stage, because the programme does not have an examination to prepare for and the gains come from changing how work is done rather than from more coverage.

Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home visits, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour are AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market. Every figure here belongs to the company or rate guide that published it and was read in October 2026. IB Gram publishes no hourly list on these pages and quotes after a free trial, for the actual subject and year group.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, the mandatory subjects and the regulator
paragraphs: Middle Years assessment is almost entirely coursework, which makes the honesty boundary more important here than in an examined programme, not less. A tutor may teach content, explain what a criterion rewards, question how a claim is evidenced, discuss what a task is asking for, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor may not write or redraft a task, a journal entry or a report, choose a Personal Project goal, produce a product, or supply a model to be adapted. Work submitted must be the student's own and schools authenticate it.

Materials are the second point. IB subject guides, criteria documents and assessment materials are the IB's copyright, and your child's school holds them legitimately. We reference and cite them and work from the student's own task sheets and marked work rather than distributing anything. A tutoring service offering a library of IB documents invites a fair question about where it came from.

On the UAE context, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited, and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those subjects sit alongside the eight MYP subject groups and account for part of why a Middle Years week is fuller than it appears. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry or IB approval, accreditation or partnership and no UAE office. An individual tutoring privately in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: When a Middle Years session should actually happen
paragraphs: Attention is the binding constraint at this age, more than content or motivation. A thirteen-year-old at the end of a long school day and a long car journey will sit through a session and retain very little of it, which is money spent on the appearance of support. That makes session timing a genuine variable rather than an administrative detail, and it is one of the few areas where living in this particular community helps.

Students attending the school inside The Sustainable City are home by mid-afternoon, which makes a 3.30pm or 4pm start realistic and puts the session in the window where a Middle Years student can still work properly. Families commuting out to Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Arabian Ranches are realistically limited to 5.30pm or later on a school day, and for younger students a weekend morning is frequently a better choice than a tired weekday evening.

The UAE calendar does the rest. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, leaving Saturday and Sunday as the only full days. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the useful window moves after Iftar. We hold slots in Gulf Standard Time, move them after Iftar with the same tutor retained, and pause blocks during a school's own assessment fortnight rather than adding sessions that produce fatigue. We also keep the same tutor across a term, because a tutor who knows which criterion a particular student neglects is carrying information worth more than a full diary.

process.title: Send the report with the criterion marks
process.description: Not the grade summary but the criterion breakdown, and the most recent marked task sheets if you have them. The pattern across criteria is what tells us whether the problem is content, structure, process or task-reading, and those need different sessions and sometimes different tutors.

process.title: Say which year and which destination
process.description: MYP 3 and MYP 5 need different work, and a student heading for the Diploma needs different preparation from one moving to an IGCSE route. If the Personal Project is underway, say where it has reached, because it usually becomes the first priority.

process.title: A free trial on the weakest criterion
process.description: Run by the tutor who would continue, working on the criterion the marks point to rather than a general topic, using the student's own task sheet. It ends with the tutor naming what they would address first and why. If the match is wrong, we propose someone else.

process.title: A written plan naming criteria
process.description: You receive a plan naming the subject, the criterion letters being targeted and the tasks the work will attach to, plus the dates it counts back from. Named criteria mean the plan can be checked against the next report rather than taken on trust.

process.title: Weekly sessions with criterion-level notes
process.description: Each session note names the criterion worked on and what changed, rather than listing topics covered. Over a term that record either shows the weak criterion moving or it does not, and if it does not we change the approach or the tutor rather than extending the arrangement.

whyPoints.title: The report translated before anything is bought
whyPoints.description: Four criterion marks out of eight per subject are a diagnosis, not a score. Reading the pattern tells you whether the problem is content, structure, process or task-reading, and it prevents a family paying for content teaching a student did not need.

whyPoints.title: Criterion letters in every session note
whyPoints.description: Sessions name the criterion being worked on rather than the topic covered, which is what makes progress checkable against the next report. It also keeps the work aligned with how the school is actually marking.

whyPoints.title: Personal Project scope tested first

faqs.question: What do the four criterion marks on an MYP report actually mean?
faqs.answer: Each Middle Years subject is assessed against four criteria, marked out of eight each, and the four totals convert to a 1 to 7 grade through boundaries your school publishes. The criteria differ in name by subject group but do the same job: one tests what the student knows, the others test how they inquire, work, communicate and reflect. Read as a pattern, they are a diagnosis. A strong knowledge mark with weak communication marks means the problem is structure and notation, not content, and content tutoring will not move the grade.

faqs.question: Why is my capable child sitting on a 4 in several subjects?
faqs.answer: Usually because the inquiry, process and reflection criteria reward behaviours a confident student skips: planning before producing, documenting development as it happens, and evaluating against a stated specification. A student who can produce a good outcome without those steps still loses the marks attached to them, because the outcome is not what is being marked. Once the child sees that on their own task sheet, against the published criterion descriptor, the correction tends to be quick. It is one of the fastest improvements available in the programme.

faqs.question: Which criterion should we work on first?
faqs.answer: The lowest one, in the subject where the pattern is clearest, because criterion marks do not move evenly. Lifting a single weak criterion from a 3 to a 6 changes the total more than nudging all four up by a point, and it is usually easier, since weak criteria tend to have one identifiable cause. Ask the teacher what the task feedback said about that criterion specifically. That question produces an action; asking how to move a 4 to a 5 produces a conversation nobody can answer.

faqs.question: When does the Diploma or IGCSE decision have to be made?
faqs.answer: In most Dubai schools, during the second term of MYP 5, which means anything intended to influence it has to happen in the first term. That matters most for mathematics and the sciences: a student hoping to keep Higher Level Analysis and Approaches or a Higher Level science open needs the fluency and data-handling evidence in place before selections are locked. After that point the decision becomes administrative rather than academic, and no amount of later work reopens an option that has closed.

faqs.question: When in MYP 5 should my child begin work on the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most students do, and the first session should be about scope rather than content. Almost every weak project traces back to a goal too large or too vague to evidence properly: the student spends the time producing and has nothing documented about planning or skill development, which weakens three assessed areas at once. A modest, specific goal with a dated, honest process journal scores better with less total work. Reconstructing a journal near the deadline is visible to a supervisor and costs marks directly.

faqs.question: What exactly is a tutor allowed to do on a Personal Project?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a strict boundary. A tutor may explain what each assessed area rewards, question whether a goal is achievable in the time, ask how a claim in the journal is evidenced, discuss the skills the project will need, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product, write or redraft the report or journal, or supply a model to adapt. The school supervises the project formally and nothing a tutor does should bypass that supervision or substitute for it.

faqs.question: Does MYP prepare a student properly for IGCSE exams?
faqs.answer: For content and written fluency, yes. For examination performance, not directly, because the Middle Years Programme does not assess timed paper technique, mark-scheme reading or command-word discipline. A capable MYP student moving into a Year 11 IGCSE route can therefore look weaker than they are for a full term, purely on pacing and on answering the question as asked. Four to six sessions of timed paper work before that year begins usually removes the problem, and it is considerably cheaper than discovering it in the first mock results.

faqs.question: What is MYP eAssessment and does it apply to my child?
faqs.answer: It is the IB's optional on-screen examination and ePortfolio route in the final Middle Years year, leading to the MYP Certificate, and it changes the final term for students who take it by introducing something closer to a conventional revision window. Not every school in Dubai offers it, so confirm with your child's MYP coordinator rather than assuming either way. If it does apply, on-screen examination practice is worth planning for in the final term, because it is a format most students have not worked in before.

faqs.question: Is it worth tutoring in MYP 3 or MYP 4, or should we wait?
faqs.answer: MYP 4 is the year that quietly matters most, because mathematics pathways split and a student's trajectory towards Higher Level Diploma subjects is effectively set by the end of it. Fluency and data-handling built in MYP 4 are what make Higher Level options genuinely available when selections are made in MYP 5. Waiting until MYP 5 means working against a deadline rather than towards an option. Even so, the right quantity is usually one subject, one weekly hour, not broad support across the timetable.

faqs.question: What should a Middle Years family expect to spend, and on how many hours?
faqs.answer: Published rates put qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Bestimate's monthly estimate for one weekly hour at AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65. The more useful point for Middle Years families is quantity: much of what helps is short and specific, such as a few sessions on task-reading or a transition block, rather than open-ended weekly support across subjects. Those figures were read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in The Sustainable City for MYP support?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in this community. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own task sheets and marked work on screen. Home tutoring is a service we operate in India only. For criterion work the format suits the material well, because what matters is the student's own writing read against the published criterion descriptors, which is easier to do side by side on a screen.

faqs.question: My daughter is in MYP 2 and the marks dropped from PYP. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Very. The Primary Years Programme reports descriptively and the Middle Years Programme reports graded criterion marks, so the first MYP reports frequently read as a drop when nothing has actually changed about the child. What has changed is that inquiry, communication and reflection are now marked explicitly. The useful response is to treat the early Middle Years as the cheap place to build habits — justified answers, shown working, reading the task sheet for the criterion — rather than as a performance problem to solve.

faqs.question: Why does my son's strong final piece in Arts or Design score lower than expected?
faqs.answer: Because the process carries marks that the product does not. In Arts, the process journal is assessed; in Design, the evaluation against the specification the student wrote at the start is assessed. A strong outcome with thin documentation scores below a modest outcome with a well-evidenced process. Students find this counter-intuitive and it is entirely consistent with the published criteria. The fix is habit rather than talent: documenting decisions as they happen, and writing the evaluation against the original specification rather than describing the result.

faqs.question: Do you work from the IB's own criteria documents?
faqs.answer: We work from the published criteria and from your child's own task sheets and marked work, which is what the school is marking against. IB subject guides, criteria documents and assessment materials are the IB's copyright and your child's school holds them legitimately, so we reference and cite them rather than distributing anything. A service offering a library of IB documents for download invites a fair question about provenance. Working from the student's own materials is also simply more useful, because it is the actual evidence.

faqs.question: How quickly should a criterion mark move?
faqs.answer: For a structure or task-reading cause, often by the next summative task, because the change is in how the work is approached rather than in what the student knows. For a content cause, one to three weeks per topic. For process and reflection criteria, a term, since they reward a way of working that has to be practised rather than understood. Session notes name the criterion worked on, so progress is checkable against the next report. We publish no improvement statistics, because figures without a sample size and method are not evidence.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-sustainable-ci.closingHeading: Send the criterion marks, not the grade
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-sustainable-ci.closingBody: The most useful first message attaches the criterion breakdown from the report rather than the grade summary, says which Middle Years year your child is in, and names where the Personal Project has reached if it is underway. The pattern across those four criterion marks usually tells us whether the problem is content, structure, process or task-reading, which decides what the first sessions should contain. Next is a free trial lesson on the weakest criterion with the tutor who would continue, then a short written plan naming criteria and tasks. Lessons run one-to-one over live video into The Sustainable City in Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

Each works to the published criteria for their subject group rather than offering general homework help, because criterion marks are what the report is made of.

intro.heading: Two systems, often in the same household
paragraphs: The Valley is a newer community on the road to Al Ain with no school inside its own boundary at the time of writing. Children here travel outward in two broad directions, and the schools at the end of those journeys include some running the IB Middle Years Programme and some running the English National Curriculum into IGCSE. It is entirely normal in this community for siblings to be in different systems, and for parents to be reading two incompatible kinds of report at the same kitchen table.

That is why this page is built as a comparison. It sets MYP against the British curriculum on the things that actually confuse families: how criterion marks out of eight differ from percentages, what is examined and when, what the Personal Project demands that a British Year 11 does not, and what transfers if a child moves between the two. Only after that does it get to the criterion detail, which is the same whichever school a child attends.

The first thing to establish is that an MYP report is a diagnosis rather than a score. Every subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, with the four totals converted to a 1 to 7 grade through boundaries the school publishes. One criterion usually covers knowing and understanding; the others cover inquiry, process, communication or reflection depending on the subject group. Read as a pattern, those four numbers say what kind of help a child needs.

A British curriculum report says something different and simpler: a percentage or a working-at grade against a scheme of work, with external examination only at IGCSE. Neither system is better, and parents who try to convert one into the other usually reach a wrong conclusion. A child on a 4 in MYP is not the equivalent of a child on 40 per cent, and treating it that way is how families end up either panicking over nothing or ignoring a real problem for a term.

Delivery is stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in The Valley. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own task sheets and marked work on screen. Household visits exist in our India operation only. For criterion work the format suits the material, because what matters is the student's own writing read against the published descriptors, side by side on one screen. The format also removes the two car journeys either side of a visit, which for a thirteen-year-old who has already travelled outward and back is the difference between a session they can use and one they merely attend.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-valley.programmesIntro: Three stages of the Middle Years Programme, plus the alternative families here frequently weigh it against. The stage matters more than the school name in a community whose children are spread across several.

programmes.name: The early Middle Years
programmes.description: Graded criterion marks appear for the first time, usually after a Primary Years Programme that reported descriptively, and the drop families perceive is often a change of reporting rather than of performance. Nothing here affects a final qualification, which makes it the cheapest place to build habits: justified answers, shown working, and reading a task sheet to find the criterion being assessed.
programmes.countryNote: In The Valley children arrive at these years from several different primary schools and sometimes from other countries, so a cohort is less homogeneous than in a continuum-school community. Families moving in from a British or American system typically need a term to understand that the criteria rather than the content are what the marks respond to.

programmes.name: The middle years of the programme
programmes.description: Content depth increases and pathways begin to separate, with mathematics splitting into standard and extended routes in most schools. Inquiry and process criteria become harder to lift because they reward a way of working rather than a body of knowledge, and a capable student who skips planning and documentation will sit on a 4 regardless of what they know.
programmes.countryNote: For students in this community aiming at Higher Level Diploma subjects or at a strong IGCSE profile after a system change, these are the decisive years. Fluency and data-handling built here is what makes options genuinely available later, when selections are made administratively rather than academically.

programmes.name: The final year and the Personal Project
programmes.description: The busiest year: summative tasks across eight subject groups, the Personal Project with its own deadlines and assessed areas, Service as Action, and the decision about what follows. Schools offering MYP eAssessment add on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, which changes the final term substantially for those students.
programmes.countryNote: In The Valley the decision at the end of MYP 5 is frequently between continuing to the Diploma at one school and moving to A Levels at another in a different travel direction. That choice is usually locked in the second term, so anything meant to influence it has to happen in the first term rather than the third.

programmes.name: The British curriculum alternative
programmes.description: Key Stage 3 through to IGCSE, with content-led schemes of work, percentage or working-at grades, and external examination at 16. There is no criterion structure and no equivalent of the Personal Project, and timed examination technique is drilled far earlier because the qualification depends on it.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools reachable from The Valley run this route, which is why so many families here are genuinely choosing rather than simply attending. Students who respond to clear content targets and timed tests often do better on it, while students who work well independently and write at length tend to prefer the Middle Years Programme.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-valley.subjectsIntro: The Middle Years subject groups with the criterion that most often costs marks in each. An enquiry naming a subject and a criterion letter gets a far better first session than one naming a subject alone.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Capable students lose most on investigating patterns, because describing a pattern is not justifying a general rule, and on communicating, where notation is marked rather than the answer.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowledge and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Students strong on recall often sit on a 4 or 5 because design and evaluation are about method, which is also what the Diploma later assesses at 20%.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. The recurring loss is in analysing, where students summarise a text instead of examining how it achieves its effect. Fluent writers can score well on language and poorly on analysis, which produces a confusing report.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Students are assessed against a phase rather than a year group, so ask which phase your child is in before comparing marks with anyone else's child.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the usual shortfall: accurate information is presented and sources are never evaluated, which is precisely what that criterion exists to reward.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Marks are lost in evaluating, because students describe what they made rather than testing it against the design specification they wrote themselves at the start of the unit.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries more marks than students expect, so a strong final piece with thin documentation scores below a modest piece with an evidenced development process.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and reflective criteria are where marks move, which surprises students who assume the subject is assessed on physical ability.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting, against a student-set goal and product. The commonest failure is a goal too large to evidence properly, which weakens every assessed area at once because the process journal has nothing concrete to document.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. These sit alongside the eight subject groups and are often the weakest line for a mid-phase arrival.

sections.heading: MYP against the British curriculum, for a family comparing
paragraphs: In most Dubai communities this comparison is settled by the school a family chose. In The Valley it is frequently live, because the two travel directions contain both systems and siblings are sometimes in each. The honest version is that neither is better and they reward different behaviours, so the right question is which one suits a particular child rather than which produces stronger outcomes in general.

The Middle Years Programme assesses four criteria per subject, each out of eight, across eight subject groups, with no external examination until the Diploma unless the school offers eAssessment. It rewards independent planning, documented process, reflection and extended writing. The British curriculum runs content-led schemes of work with percentage or working-at grades and external examination at IGCSE, and it rewards timed performance, precise recall and examination technique drilled from Year 9 onwards.

The practical consequence is that a child can look strong in one and ordinary in the other without changing at all. A student who plans, documents and writes at length may sit comfortably at a 6 or 7 in MYP and find the timed precision of an IGCSE paper uncomfortable. A student who performs under timed conditions and resists documenting process may do the reverse. The table sets out the dimensions that actually decide it, which is more useful than any ranking of the two systems. It is worth reading with a particular child in mind rather than in the abstract, because the answer differs between siblings in the same household.

sections.heading: Criterion marks against percentages, and how to read each
paragraphs: This is the single most common source of unnecessary worry among families in this community, particularly those with children in both systems. A criterion mark is not a percentage. An 8 is not a hundred per cent and a 4 is not a fail; each number corresponds to a published descriptor of what the work demonstrated. A student who scores 5 on a hard first attempt has done well, and reading that as fifty per cent is how a parent accidentally teaches a child to avoid difficult tasks.

The conversion to a 1 to 7 grade uses boundaries the school publishes across a total out of thirty-two. The useful consequence is that lifting one weak criterion from a 3 to a 6 moves the total more than nudging all four up by a point, and it is usually easier, because weak criteria tend to have a single identifiable cause. That makes the criterion breakdown, not the overall grade, the thing a parent should ask about at a parents' evening.

A British curriculum report answers a different question: how much of the content is secure, measured against a scheme of work. Both are useful and neither translates. The practical approach for a family with children in both systems is to ask the two questions separately — which criterion is weakest in one child, how much content is secure in the other — rather than trying to compare the two numbers at the same table.

sections.heading: What the four criteria actually reward
paragraphs: Whichever school a child attends, the criterion structure is consistent in shape. Every Middle Years subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight. One tests what the student knows, and the others test how the student inquires, works, communicates and reflects. The names differ by subject group but the division is the same, and that division is the entire diagnostic value of a Middle Years report.

Read the pattern rather than the grade. A student with a strong knowing and understanding mark and weak communicating and reflecting marks does not have a content problem, and content tutoring will not move the grade. A student with the reverse pattern does. A student weak across all four usually has a task-reading problem: they are answering what the task looks like rather than what the criterion being assessed requires, which is a fifteen-minute fix repeated until it becomes habit.

This also explains the thing parents find most baffling, which is a confident, capable child sitting on a 4 in several subjects. The inquiry, process and reflection criteria reward behaviours — planning before producing, documenting development as it happens, evaluating against a stated specification — that a strong student often skips because they can produce a good outcome without them. The outcome is not what is marked, and once a student sees that on their own task sheet the correction is usually quick. The table below sets out the structure by subject group so a parent can place their own child's report against it.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and what the British route asks instead
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the Middle Years Programme's culminating independent work: a student-set goal, a product or outcome, a process journal and a report, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. For most students it is the first genuinely independent extended project they have attempted, which makes it both a useful rehearsal for the Diploma's Extended Essay and a reliable source of stress in MYP 5.

A British curriculum Year 11 has no direct equivalent. The comparable demand arrives later or in a different form, and the practical consequence is that a student moving from MYP to a British route carries a skill the new system will not immediately ask for, while a student moving the other way may never have managed a long independent piece before. Families in this community move in both directions, so both situations are common here.

Within the project, almost every weak outcome traces to the same cause: a goal too large or too vague to evidence properly. A student with an ambitious goal spends the time producing and has nothing documented about planning or skill development, which weakens all three assessed areas at once. A modest, specific goal with a dated journal scores better with less work. The honesty boundary is strict: a tutor may question scope and ask how a claim is evidenced, and may not choose the goal, make the product or write any part of the report or journal. The school supervises the project formally and nothing a tutor does should bypass that.

sections.heading: Switching systems: what transfers and what does not
paragraphs: Because The Valley is new and still filling, a high proportion of its students have changed school within the last year or two, and some have changed system. That is worth treating as its own problem rather than as being behind, because the gaps a system change produces are specific and uneven. Content transfers reasonably well in mathematics and the sciences, where the underlying material is similar. Habits transfer badly in both directions, and habits are what the marks respond to.

A student moving from the Middle Years Programme into a British Year 10 or 11 usually arrives able to write at length and plan independently, and unpractised at timed precision, command-word reading and mark-scheme awareness. That student can look weaker than they are for a full term purely on format, and four to six sessions of timed paper work generally resolves it. The content is rarely the problem; the clock and the mark scheme are.

A student moving the other way, into MYP from a British school, usually arrives with secure content and no experience of criterion-marked tasks, process journals or self-set objectives. Their first reports often show strong knowledge marks and weak process and reflection marks, which is exactly the pattern this page describes. One term of criterion-focused work usually closes it, and recognising the cause prevents a family concluding their child has suddenly become a weaker student when in fact the marking has changed what it measures.

sections.heading: Which criterion to work on, and in which subject
paragraphs: Once a family can read the criterion breakdown, the next decision is narrow and cheap. Work on the lowest criterion in the subject where the pattern is clearest, because criterion marks do not move evenly. Lifting one criterion from a 3 to a 6 changes the total more than nudging four criteria up by a point each, and it is usually easier, since a weak criterion tends to have one identifiable cause named in the task feedback.

The second decision is whether the weakness is subject-specific or general. If the same criterion is weak across three subjects — communicating, say, or reflecting — the cause is a habit rather than a subject gap, and one engagement addresses all three. If one subject is weak across all four criteria while others are fine, that is a genuine content or engagement problem in that subject. The pattern across the report answers this without any tutor involvement.

This matters because Middle Years support should usually be short and specific rather than open-ended. A few sessions on task-reading, a term in one subject, a scoping block for the Personal Project, or a transfer diagnostic after a system change: those are the engagements that change marks. Continuous weekly tutoring across several subjects is rarely the right purchase at this stage, because the programme has no examination to prepare for and the gains come from changing how work is done rather than from covering more ground.

sections.heading: What Middle Years support costs, and how little is usually needed
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency advertising IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Budget online tutoring runs AED 33 to AED 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. In-home visits are AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is included, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market.

For Middle Years families the honest point is about quantity rather than rate. Much of what helps is short: one to three sessions on task-reading, four to six on Personal Project scoping and journal habits, a transfer diagnostic after a system change, or a term of criterion work in a single subject. Open-ended tutoring across several subjects rarely suits this stage, because there is no examination to prepare for and the gains come from a change in method.

Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour home visits. Every figure here belongs to the company or rate guide that published it and was read in October 2026. IB Gram publishes no hourly list on these pages and quotes after a free trial, for the actual subject and year group, and will say when a short engagement is more appropriate than a term.

sections.heading: Honesty, the mandatory subjects and the regulator
paragraphs: Middle Years assessment is almost entirely coursework, which makes the honesty boundary more important here rather than less. A tutor may teach content, explain what a criterion rewards, question how a claim is evidenced, discuss what a task is asking for, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor may not write or redraft a task, a journal entry or a report, choose a Personal Project goal, produce a product, or supply a model to be adapted. Submitted work must be the student's own and schools authenticate it.

Materials are the second boundary. IB subject guides, criteria documents and assessment materials are the IB's copyright, and your child's school holds them legitimately. We reference and cite them and work from the student's own task sheets and marked work rather than distributing anything. A tutoring service offering a library of IB documents invites a fair question about where it came from, and the student's own materials are more useful anyway because they are the actual evidence.

On the UAE context, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited, and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Those lessons account for part of why a Middle Years week is fuller than it appears. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, Ministry or IB approval, accreditation or partnership and no UAE office, and an individual tutoring privately in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: When a Middle Years session should happen in this community
paragraphs: Attention is the binding constraint at this age, more than content or motivation, and in a community with no school inside its boundary the attention budget is smaller than families expect. A thirteen-year-old who has travelled outward and back will sit through a weekday evening session and retain very little of it, which is money spent on the appearance of support rather than on support.

That makes weekend mornings genuinely better for this age group here, which is the opposite of the advice that suits a Diploma student. A Middle Years student is sharper on a Saturday morning than at seven on a Tuesday evening, and criterion work in particular — reading a task sheet, comparing an answer with a descriptor, redrafting a paragraph — needs attention rather than stamina. Shorter sessions of thirty to forty minutes often work better than a full hour at this age.

The UAE calendar shapes the rest. The working week runs Monday to Friday with a half-day Friday, leaving Saturday and Sunday as the only full days. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the useful window moves after Iftar. We hold slots in Gulf Standard Time, move them after Iftar with the same tutor retained, and pause blocks during a school's own assessment fortnight. We also keep the same tutor across a term, because a tutor who knows which criterion a particular student neglects is carrying information worth more than a full diary, and rebuilding it with somebody new takes most of a term.
