faqs.question: How does an MYP report compare with a British curriculum one?
faqs.answer: They answer different questions and neither converts into the other. An MYP report gives four criterion marks out of eight per subject, converted to a 1 to 7 grade through published boundaries, and it tells you which skill is weak. A British curriculum report gives a percentage or working-at grade and tells you how much of the content is secure. A 4 in MYP is not forty per cent. Families with children in both systems should ask the two questions separately rather than trying to line up the numbers.

faqs.question: Is the Middle Years Programme better preparation than the British route?
faqs.answer: Neither is better, and they reward different behaviours, which is why the useful question is which suits a particular child. MYP rewards independent planning, documented process, reflection and extended writing, with no external examination until the Diploma unless eAssessment is offered. The British route rewards recall, precision and timed examination technique, drilled from Year 9 to IGCSE. A child can look strong in one and ordinary in the other without changing at all, which is worth knowing before concluding anything from a single report.

faqs.question: Our son moved from a British school into MYP and his marks fell. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly format rather than ability. He will have arrived with secure content and no experience of criterion-marked tasks, process journals or self-set objectives, so his first reports typically show strong knowledge marks alongside weak process and reflection marks. That is a recognisable pattern rather than a decline. One term of criterion-focused work usually closes it, and identifying the cause stops a family concluding their child has suddenly become weaker when the marking has simply changed what it measures.

faqs.question: Our daughter is moving from MYP into a British Year 11. What should we prepare?
faqs.answer: Timed paper technique, mark-scheme awareness and command-word reading, none of which the Middle Years Programme drills because it does not assess them. She will arrive able to write at length and plan independently, which is genuinely valuable, and unpractised at the clock. That combination can make a capable student look weaker than they are for a full term. Four to six sessions of timed paper work before the year starts usually removes the problem, and it costs far less than discovering it in the first mock results.

faqs.question: With four criteria weak in two subjects, where do we start?
faqs.answer: The lowest one, in the subject where the pattern is clearest, because criterion marks do not move evenly. Lifting a single criterion from a 3 to a 6 changes the total more than nudging all four up by a point, and it is usually easier since weak criteria tend to have one identifiable cause named in the task feedback. If the same criterion is weak across three subjects, the cause is a habit rather than a subject gap, and one engagement then addresses all three at once.

faqs.question: Why is our capable child sitting on a 4 in several subjects?
faqs.answer: Usually because the inquiry, process and reflection criteria reward behaviours a confident student skips: planning before producing, documenting development as it happens, and evaluating against a stated specification. A student who can produce a good outcome without those steps still loses the marks attached to them, because the outcome is not what is being marked. Once the child sees that on their own task sheet against the published descriptor, the correction is usually quick. It is one of the fastest improvements in the programme.

faqs.question: What does the Personal Project ask that a British Year 11 does not?
faqs.answer: A long independent piece with a self-set goal, a dated process journal and a report, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. A British curriculum Year 11 has no direct equivalent, so a student moving out of MYP carries a skill the new route will not immediately use, while a student moving in may never have managed a long independent project before. Within the project, almost every weak outcome traces to a goal too large or too vague to evidence properly in the time available.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a strict boundary. A tutor may explain what each assessed area rewards, question whether a goal is achievable in the time, ask how a claim in the journal is evidenced, discuss the skills the project needs, and comment on writing the student produced. A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product, write or redraft the report or journal, or supply a model to adapt. The school supervises the project formally, and nothing a tutor does should bypass or substitute for that supervision.

faqs.question: Is it worth tutoring in MYP 4, or should we wait for MYP 5?
faqs.answer: MYP 4 is the year that quietly matters most, because mathematics pathways separate and a student's trajectory towards Higher Level Diploma subjects or a strong IGCSE set is effectively set by the end of it. Fluency and data-handling built then is what makes options available when selections are made in MYP 5. Waiting means working against a deadline rather than towards an option. The right quantity, though, is usually one subject and one weekly hour rather than broad support across the timetable.

faqs.question: How much Middle Years tutoring does a child actually need?
faqs.answer: Usually less than families expect, and short rather than continuous. One to three sessions on task-reading often fixes a flat criterion pattern across several subjects. Four to six sessions scope a Personal Project and establish journal habits. Two or three sessions diagnose a system transfer. A term of criterion work in one subject addresses a repeated weakness. Open-ended tutoring across several subjects rarely suits this stage, because there is no examination to prepare for and the gains come from changing how work is done.

faqs.question: When should sessions happen if the school run is long?
faqs.answer: Weekend mornings, for this age group, which is the opposite of what suits a Diploma student. A thirteen-year-old who has travelled outward and back will sit through a weekday evening session and retain very little, and criterion work in particular needs attention rather than stamina: reading a task sheet, comparing an answer with a descriptor, redrafting a paragraph. Shorter sessions of thirty to forty minutes often work better than a full hour at this age, and the slot is held in Gulf Standard Time either way.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in The Valley for MYP support?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, and nobody will arrive at an address in this community. Lessons are one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own task sheets and marked work on screen. Home tutoring is a service we operate in India only. For criterion work the format suits the material well, because what matters is reading the student's own writing against the published descriptors, which is easier side by side on a screen.

faqs.question: What is MYP eAssessment and will it apply to our child?
faqs.answer: It is the IB's optional on-screen examination and ePortfolio route in the final Middle Years year, leading to the MYP Certificate, and it changes the final term for students who take it by introducing something closer to a conventional revision window. Not every school in Dubai offers it, and in this community children attend several different schools, so confirm with your own child's MYP coordinator rather than assuming either way. If it applies, on-screen examination practice is worth planning for in the final term.

faqs.question: Our two children are in different systems. Can you help with both?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common request in this community because the two travel directions contain both systems. The work is genuinely different: criterion-targeted sessions for the MYP child, content and technique sessions for the British-curriculum child, and we would normally suggest separate tutors matched to each. Consecutive slots on the same evening work well online, with no travel charge attached to the second one. What we would avoid is applying one system's logic to the other child's report.

faqs.question: Why no success statistics on this page?
faqs.answer: Because a figure without a sample size, a date and a method is a marketing claim rather than evidence, and criterion-based progress in particular does not reduce to a percentage honestly. Several providers in this market publish self-asserted ratings that differ from their own page text. What this page publishes instead is checkable: the criterion structure, the AED bands with their publishers and the month read, the KHDA requirements as published, and a plain statement of the approvals we do not hold.

intro.heading: What a search for an IB MYP tutor in The Views is really asking
paragraphs: The search phrase carries a hidden assumption: that somewhere between Fairways and The Links there is a teacher who knows the Middle Years Programme, and the job is to find them. The assumption is reasonable for IGCSE, where a specification code pins down exactly what a tutor needs to know. It breaks down for the MYP. There is no MYP syllabus document a parent can download, no set textbook, no archive of released papers, and no single examination at the end of most years. What exists instead is a framework, and a framework is a much harder thing to shop for.

That framework is why the local search returns so little. A maths graduate living two buildings away can teach quadratics. Very few of them can tell you what criterion B, investigating patterns, asks a MYP 4 student to produce, or why a student who solved every question correctly still landed on a 4. In this programme the mark is not awarded for the answer. It is awarded for the process the answer demonstrates, judged against published strands of descriptors, out of eight, four separate times in every subject.

So the honest reply to the question behind the search is that distance is the wrong filter. The Views sits inside Emirates Living, a few minutes from Sheikh Zayed Road and ten from Al Barsha, and the schools families here use for the MYP are spread from The Meadows to Emirates Hills to Umm Suqeim. A tutor who lives in Travo may know nothing about the programme. A teacher who knows the programme properly may live anywhere at all, and in practice usually does.

IB Gram resolves that by teaching one-to-one over live video rather than by driving anyone anywhere. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India. For a MYP family the trade is a good one. Instead of whoever happens to be free in Emirates Living on a Tuesday evening, your child works with a teacher who has written MYP unit plans, marked criterion grids and taken students through the MYP 5 exit point. A shared screen carries the grid, the draft and the task sheet side by side.

This page sets out what that teacher has to know, how four marks turn into the grade on the report, where the MYP year puts the pressure, what the Dubai market charges for this kind of help in dirhams, and what a tutor may and may not touch on a Personal Project. If you read nothing else, read the eight questions further down. They are the ones that separate a subject graduate from somebody who has actually taught this programme in a classroom.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-views.programmesIntro: Families in The Views usually arrive at the MYP from one of two directions: a PYP classroom in the same school, or a British Year 7 somewhere else. Where a student goes afterwards matters as much as where they are now, so the programmes below are set out as a route, with what each one demands of a student living in Emirates Living.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and carries no external examination. Students work through transdisciplinary themes and finish with the PYP Exhibition in the final year. Reports describe learner-profile attributes and approaches to learning rather than percentages, which is why parents moving in from a British or Indian school often find the first one hard to read. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of recording a method, because MYP 1 assumes all three.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP places sit mostly inside continuum schools, so a family in The Views choosing one is usually also choosing the MYP and the Diploma that follow. KHDA licenses the curriculum, and Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies run alongside it from the start, in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 11-16 · MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly Years 7-11
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and assessment that is criterion-referenced from the first week. Each group publishes four criteria, A to D, each marked out of eight against strands the teacher clarifies for every task. There are no cumulative percentages and no end-of-year paper in MYP 1 to 4. The Personal Project runs in MYP 5 in most schools, and the programme can close with optional on-screen eAssessment where the school licenses it.
programmes.countryNote: Students living in The Views travel to MYP schools in The Meadows, Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim, so the same programme reaches them on four different unit calendars. A tutor has to work from your child's own task sheet rather than a generic scheme, because the unit one school runs in November is not the unit another runs down the same road.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment returns to external examinations with internal components, and the scale moves from criterion totals to subject grades out of seven plus up to three core points. The jump from MYP 4 into DP1 is more about examination technique and timed writing than about missing content.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai MYP students stay in the continuum for the Diploma, but a real minority leave at MYP 5 for IGCSE or A Level at a British school in Al Barsha or Emirates Hills. Both routes are open from The Views, and the choice is far better made in MYP 4 than in the spring of MYP 5 when option blocks have closed.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route pairing Diploma courses with a career-related study and a core of personal and professional skills, a reflective project, service learning and language development. Fewer Dubai schools license it than the Diploma. It suits a student who wants IB rigour in two or three subjects alongside an applied qualification rather than six academic subjects and a full core.
programmes.countryNote: For a household in The Views the CP matters mainly as a fallback worth knowing about before MYP 5 subject choices close. Check the licensed programme list on the school's own KHDA page rather than a prospectus, because programme licences change between academic years and a brochure can be a year behind.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-views.subjectsIntro: MYP assessment is organised by subject group rather than by named course, and the four criteria differ in every group. The list below gives each group with the criteria it is actually marked against and the place marks usually go missing. Name the group and the MYP year when you enquire; a teacher who is right for MYP 2 Sciences is not automatically right for MYP 5.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Marked on knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where most marks go: students find the pattern and then never state a general rule, justify it or test it. The Extended route in MYP 4 and 5 adds content depth Standard does not, and the choice feeds directly into Diploma Analysis and Approaches entry.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5 · Biology, Chemistry, Physics or integrated
subjects.description: Four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C punishes a student who tabulates data then writes one sentence of conclusion. Criterion D is the one British-curriculum transfers have never met, because it asks for evaluated impacts with sources rather than a paragraph of opinion.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5 · English and other school languages
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Written tasks are judged on how a student handles one specific text, so revision cannot be generic. The commonest fault is retelling the plot where the criterion asks for analysis of the writer's choices, and that fault survives all the way into Diploma Paper 1 if nobody names it early.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Marked on comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Phases matter more than year groups: a student can sit in MYP 4 working in phase 2. Arabic as an additional language is the common case in Dubai, and the phase printed on the report is what a tutor needs before planning anything at all.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5 · History, Geography and Economics strands
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Students lose marks on investigating by writing a question too broad to answer inside the task length, then on communicating by citing sources in a format the task sheet did not ask for. Source evaluation here transfers straight into Diploma History paper work.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. The design cycle is assessed as a cycle, so a working product with no documented specification scores badly. This is the group where strong students are most often surprised by a 4, because the folder rather than the artefact carries the majority of the available marks.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5 · Visual arts, music and drama
subjects.description: Investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. Process journals are assessed, which means a student who produced good work over two late nights has nothing to show for criterion B. Support here is largely about documenting intent and artistic influence in the journal while the work is being made rather than afterwards.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on and improving performance. The written components surprise families who assume the group is practical only. Planning and reflection are produced in writing and marked against strands, so a capable athlete can still sit on a 3 for criterion A all year.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units and the Personal Project
subjects.description: Interdisciplinary units are reported against their own criteria, and schools often assess them in the term parents are least expecting. The Personal Project is supervised inside school; a tutor may discuss process, planning and the structure of the report, and may never produce any part of the work itself.

sections.heading: Is there anyone in The Views who actually teaches the MYP?
paragraphs: Start with the literal question. There is no register of MYP tutors in Emirates Living, and if there were, living in Fairways would not be evidence of anything. The programme is taught in Dubai by schools holding an IB licence for it, and the teachers who deliver it are employed by those schools. Under the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and under ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi school staff, a teacher is barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. The obvious candidate is also the one you cannot use.

What is left is a smaller pool than a page of search results suggests: teachers who have delivered MYP units somewhere, moderators who have standardised them, and subject graduates who have learned the framework properly. Almost none of them live within walking distance of The Links, and the few who do will already be booked by families in the same building. Hiring by postcode in this situation produces a tutor who can explain the topic and cannot explain the mark, which is the specific failure that wastes a term.

The honest version of the answer is this. IB Gram does not place a tutor in your building, and does not run home visits anywhere in Dubai; that service exists only in India. What it does is match a student in The Views with an MYP-trained teacher wherever that teacher happens to be, then run the lesson live over video on Gulf Standard Time with the criterion grid and the student's own draft open on a shared screen. For a programme assessed on documented process rather than on a final answer, a shared screen is not a compromise. It is the natural place for that work to happen.

sections.heading: Why a framework is harder to shop for than a syllabus
paragraphs: An IGCSE parent has a short, decisive question available: which specification? Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different documents with different papers, and a tutor either knows the one your child sits or does not. The answer is checkable in a minute from an entry slip. MYP parents have no equivalent. The IB publishes subject-group guides to schools, and each school writes its own units from them, so two MYP 3 Sciences classes in Dubai can spend the same term on entirely different content while being assessed against the same four criteria.

That shifts what a tutor has to supply. There is no bank of released papers to work through, because in MYP 1 to 4 there are no papers. There is no mark scheme in the IGCSE sense, because the descriptors stay generic until the teacher writes the task-specific clarification. The useful material for a session is therefore the material your child's school produced: the unit statement of inquiry, the task sheet, the clarification, and the last marked grid. A tutor who asks for those four things in the first message is telling you something worth knowing.

It also changes what good looks like. Progress in the MYP is a criterion mark moving, and a criterion mark moves when a student produces different evidence, not when they know more facts. A session that ends with the topic revised has usually failed. A session that ends with the student understanding what criterion C wanted, and having written one paragraph that supplies it, has usually worked. The table sets out what disappears when the syllabus does, and what has to take its place.

sections.heading: Eight questions that separate an MYP teacher from a subject graduate
paragraphs: Before the first lesson, ask these. A teacher who has run the programme answers all eight in a sentence each. Somebody who has read a summary answers three and hedges on the rest. None of them is a trick question; they are the ordinary working vocabulary of MYP assessment, and a tutor without that vocabulary will spend your money teaching content your child's school has already covered twice.

The questions also protect you from the opposite failure, which is a tutor who knows the framework well and the subject thinly. A Language Acquisition phase 4 student needs somebody who can hear a tense error in spoken Arabic, not only somebody who can quote criterion C. Put the framework questions and one hard subject question in the same message, then read which half of the reply is specific and which half is general.

If you want one question rather than eight, use this: what would you need from us before the first session? The answer you want names the task sheet, the task-specific clarification, the last marked grid and the most recent report. The answer that should worry you is just the topic. In a criterion-referenced programme the topic is the least informative thing a parent can send, and asking for nothing else is a reliable signal.

Read the answers for working detail rather than confidence. A teacher who has stood in front of an MYP class will tell you that a clarification is written by the subject teacher for each task, that approaches-to-learning comments are reported but not graded, and that a supervisor on a Personal Project may question and may not produce. Those answers are short because they are known. Somebody reciting a summary tends to give a longer reply with fewer nouns in it, and you can hear the difference in two minutes on a phone call.

sections.heading: Criterion A to D, by subject group, with the strands named
paragraphs: The four criteria are not interchangeable labels. Each subject group has its own set, and the distance between two of them is where most of the confusion on a Dubai MYP report comes from. A parent who learns that criterion B means investigating patterns in Mathematics will reasonably assume it means something similar in Sciences, where it is inquiring and designing, or in Design, where it is developing ideas. Those are three different tasks demanding three different kinds of evidence from a student.

Each criterion is marked out of eight, in bands, against strands set out in the subject-group guide the school holds. The teacher then writes a task-specific clarification turning those generic strands into the wording of the actual task, and that clarification is the single most useful document a tutor can read before a session. It is usually printed on the task sheet. It is almost never forwarded to a tutor unless somebody thinks to ask for it, and most people do not.

The table below names the four criteria for the groups most often requested by families in The Views. Use it to read your child's report properly: a 6, 6, 3, 5 line is not a student who is doing fine in some bits. It is a student with one identifiable strand of evidence missing, and that is a fixable problem inside a handful of sessions rather than a term of general revision that touches everything and changes nothing.

sections.heading: How four marks out of eight become one grade out of seven
paragraphs: This is the mechanism that surprises every family new to the programme, and it is worth understanding properly because it explains almost every confusing report. Each criterion is marked out of eight, so a subject carries a total out of thirty-two across its four criteria. The school does not average those into a percentage. It takes the criterion levels, applies the conversion published in the IB's own programme documentation, and reports a single grade from 1 to 7 for the subject.

Three consequences follow. A student can be strong in three criteria and still land on a 4, because the total is what converts. A criterion assessed once in a term carries the same structural weight as one assessed four times, so the single task that happened to touch criterion D matters far more than it looked at the time. And a grade can fall between reports without any ability being lost, simply because that term's tasks hit the strands your child is weakest on.

What a parent can do with that is specific. Ask the school which tasks assessed which criteria this term, and ask whether a best-fit or a most-recent judgement was used where a criterion was assessed more than once; schools publish that in their assessment policy and the answers differ between them. Then target the weakest criterion rather than the subject as a whole. The steps below set out where the mark actually travels, and where parents commonly misread it.

sections.heading: What MYP support costs around Emirates Living, in dirhams
paragraphs: Take the monthly number first, because that is the one a household actually budgets. One sixty-minute session a week is four or five sessions a month depending on where the half-terms fall. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more where an exam-year specialist is involved. Packages advertised in this market sit alongside those bands: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits in the home.

Working back to an hourly figure, published rates in Dubai spread wider than most parents expect. EdFlik lists online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both at the university-student end of the market. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED's named-examiner rate is AED 650. In-home one-to-one with travel included is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and as high as AED 500 by independent providers.

The gap between the online figure and the in-home figure is the thing worth examining, because it is not a quality premium. It pays for a car, for the forty minutes between Al Barsha and Emirates Living at four o'clock, and for the fact that a travelling tutor can only serve families inside that radius. A household in The Views paying it is funding travel first and then choosing from whoever the travel radius contains. Spend the same money without the travel and the choice widens to anyone who can teach MYP Sciences on a Tuesday evening. Every figure here is the Dubai market as published by the provider named, on the date its page carried that rate; IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page, and the trial lesson is free so the comparison can be made on teaching rather than on a brochure.

sections.heading: The MYP year as a Dubai three-term school actually runs it
paragraphs: Dubai private schools on the September start run three terms, with the long break across July and August, a winter break around the turn of the year, and a spring break in March or April. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. That stability is useful background for a tutoring decision, but the calendar matters more than the fees, because MYP assessment is spread across the year rather than concentrated at the end of it.

The practical consequence is that the useful moments to intervene are fixed by the school rather than by an examination board. The first is the week after an interim report, when a criterion mark has moved and nobody yet knows why. The second is three or four weeks before a summative task, which is when a task-specific clarification exists and there is still time to produce evidence against it. The third is the end of MYP 4, when subject choices for MYP 5 and the Diploma begin to close. A short block timed to any of those three does more than a year of weekly hours timed to none of them.

Ramadan reshapes the week, and in Dubai it shortens school hours too. Families in The Views routinely move a 17:00 slot to after Iftar, and a lesson delivered online absorbs that without renegotiating anybody's drive. The same applies across the long summer, when much of Emirates Living is abroad: a student in London or Mumbai in July keeps the same teacher and the same slot, time-converted, which is the quiet operational argument for video over a car in a city this mobile.

sections.heading: Who may legally tutor your child in Dubai, and how you check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The route is a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the MoHRE service page titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligibility is wider than parents assume. Teachers registered in government or private schools qualify, as do employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so any specific figure circulating online should be treated with suspicion. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute instead.

What this gives a parent is a question with a verifiable answer. Ask whether the person teaching your child holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit and when it expires, then ask separately whether they are currently employed by the school your child attends, because the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school and ADEK's professional-ethics rules say the same for Abu Dhabi staff. Neither question is rude. Both are the sort of thing somebody who has done the paperwork answers in one line.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, academic honesty, and what a tutor may not touch
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the MYP's exit piece, supervised inside the school by a named supervisor, and it is the component where outside help most often goes wrong. The rule is simple to state and easy to breach by accident. The product, the process journal and the report must be the student's own work. A tutor may discuss how to choose a goal, how to keep a journal that will satisfy the criteria, how a report is structured, and how to read the assessment criteria. A tutor may never write the report, draft sections of it, or supply the content of the product.

The same boundary applies in miniature to every assessed MYP task. Reviewing a student's own draft against a criterion and saying which strand is unmet is teaching. Rewriting the paragraph is not. The distinction matters more in this market than in most, because the search results for queries like this one contain operations selling completed assessed work outright at prices in the thousands of dirhams. Under IB academic-honesty rules that produces a malpractice finding against the student, not against the seller.

Two practical habits keep a family on the right side of it. Keep every draft, dated, so the development of the work is visible if anyone ever asks. And take the tutor's feedback in writing as comments on strands rather than as edits to the text, because comments are evidence of teaching and tracked changes inside a submitted file are evidence of something else entirely. Subject guides, past papers and mark schemes are published by the IB and the awarding bodies on their own sites; a tutor may point you to them and should never be supplying copies.

process.title: Send the task sheet, not the topic
process.description: Tell us the subject group, the MYP year and the school, and attach the most recent marked criterion grid and task-specific clarification if you have them. Those four things decide which teacher is the right match. A topic name on its own usually produces a tutor who revises content your child already knows well.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the condition stated
process.description: One sixty-minute lesson at no charge, booked before any payment and with no card details taken beforehand. It is a working lesson rather than a sales call: the tutor reads the grid, teaches against one criterion, and sends written feedback afterwards so you can judge the teaching rather than the pitch.

process.title: Name the criterion before the block starts
process.description: Agree in writing which criterion the next few sessions target and what evidence the student will produce. In a criterion-referenced programme a goal like improve in Sciences cannot be assessed by anyone. A goal like produce an evaluated conclusion that meets criterion C can be, inside a fortnight.

process.title: Lessons run live online, on your clock
process.description: Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time and run over live video with screen sharing, so the grid, the draft and the task sheet are visible to both sides. A slot held for the term can move for Ramadan or travel without losing the teacher, because nothing in the arrangement depends on a drive.

process.title: Review against the school's report, not ours
process.description: The measure of whether this worked is the criterion mark on the next school report and the teacher's comment beside it. At that point we continue, change tutor, or stop. If no specialist is free for the subject group and the slot you need, we say so rather than sending somebody approximate.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the framework, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: The pool of teachers who can read and move an MYP criterion grid is small and scattered. Searching Emirates Living for one narrows it to almost nothing. Matching across the whole pool and teaching over video widens it to everyone who can actually do that work on the evening your child is free.

whyPoints.title: The task-specific clarification is read first
whyPoints.description: Every session starts from the document the school issued for the task being assessed, because that is where generic strands become the actual requirement. A tutor working from a general scheme of work is guessing at what the marker wants, and in this programme the marker is your child's own subject teacher.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what the Personal Project allows
whyPoints.description: Supervision of the Personal Project belongs to the school. We teach process, journal discipline and report structure, and produce no part of the work. That boundary is stated here rather than buried, because the alternative sold elsewhere in this market ends as an academic-honesty finding against your child.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, with their sources
whyPoints.description: The dirham figures on this page are attributed to the provider that published them, so each one can be checked before you decide anything. Three of the pages ranking for queries like this quote no price in any currency at all, and two quote only US dollars.

whyPoints.title: A trial lesson before any commitment
whyPoints.description: The first lesson is free and the condition is stated plainly: one session, before payment, with written feedback afterwards. If the match is wrong we change the tutor. If no suitable teacher is available for your subject group and slot, we tell you that instead of filling the hour anyway.

faqs.question: Is there an IB MYP tutor in The Views, or does the lesson happen online?
faqs.answer: The lesson happens online. IB Gram does not send anyone to a residential address in Dubai; home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the criterion grid, the task sheet and your child's draft are visible to both sides at once. For the MYP that is an advantage rather than a concession, because the pool of teachers who can mark a criterion grid properly is small and scattered across time zones. Restricting the search to Emirates Living narrows it to almost nobody.

faqs.question: Why can't I just hire a maths graduate who lives in Fairways?
faqs.answer: You can, and for IGCSE revision it often works. For the MYP it usually does not. A graduate can teach quadratics; the question your child's report is answering is whether they stated a general rule, justified it and tested it, which is criterion B. A tutor who has never seen a task-specific clarification will teach the topic, your child will get the answers right, and the criterion level will not move. The mark in this programme is awarded for documented process against published strands, so the framework knowledge matters at least as much as the subject knowledge.

faqs.question: Which schools near The Views actually run the Middle Years Programme?
faqs.answer: Families in The Views typically use IB continuum schools in The Meadows, Emirates Hills, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim, including Emirates International School Meadows, Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills, GEMS World Academy Dubai and Raffles World Academy. Other strong schools in the same catchment are British-curriculum and take students to IGCSE at sixteen instead. Programme licences change between academic years, so check the licensed programmes on the school's own KHDA listing rather than relying on a prospectus or a league-table article. IB Gram has no affiliation with any of these schools and names them only as local context.

faqs.question: What is a task-specific clarification, and why does a tutor keep asking for it?
faqs.answer: MYP criteria are published as generic descriptors, which means they describe the quality of work in general terms rather than naming what a particular task requires. The teacher bridges that gap by writing a task-specific clarification: the same strands, rewritten in the language of the actual assignment. It is usually printed on the task sheet. Without it a tutor is guessing at what the marker will reward, and in this programme the marker is your child's own subject teacher rather than an external examiner. It is the single most useful document you can forward before a first session.

faqs.question: My child's MYP report shows 6, 6, 3, 5 in one subject. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: It means one criterion is costing the grade and three are fine. Those four levels total twenty out of thirty-two, and the school converts the total rather than averaging it into a percentage, so the single 3 drags the reported grade down more than it looks like it should. The useful next step is to find out which tasks assessed that criterion this term and what evidence was missing from them. That is a problem a few targeted sessions can move, unlike general revision across the whole subject, which tends to change nothing.

faqs.question: Does criterion B mean the same thing in Sciences as it does in Mathematics?
faqs.answer: No, and assuming it does is the commonest misreading of an MYP report. In Mathematics criterion B is investigating patterns. In Sciences it is inquiring and designing. In Design it is developing ideas, in Individuals and Societies it is investigating, and in Language and Literature it is organising. Each one demands different evidence, so a student can be strong on criterion B in one subject and weak on it in another without any contradiction. The letters are positions in a subject-group set, not a shared scale running across the whole timetable.

faqs.question: There are no past papers in MYP 3. What does a tutor practise with instead?
faqs.answer: The school's own materials. In MYP 1 to 4 there is no external examination and no bank of released papers, so the practice material is the task sheet, the statement of inquiry, the task-specific clarification and the student's previous marked work. A good session takes a strand that was unmet last time and has the student produce one piece of evidence that meets it, then marks that against the grid. Where a school runs optional eAssessment at MYP 5, timed on-screen task practice becomes available and is worth using in the final year.

faqs.question: Is Standard or Extended Mathematics the right route in MYP 4?
faqs.answer: It depends on where your child is heading after MYP 5 rather than on how they feel about algebra now. Extended Mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 carries additional content depth and is the more comfortable entry point into Diploma Analysis and Approaches, particularly at Higher Level. Standard is a sound route into Applications and Interpretation, and into A Level for a student leaving the continuum. Make the decision in MYP 4 with the school's recommendation and the current criterion profile in front of you, because moving between routes later is harder than choosing carefully once.

faqs.question: What should an hour of MYP support cost in Dubai, and per month?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai market runs from roughly AED 45 an hour at the university-student end, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, to AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at around AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for exam-year specialist help. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and that premium buys travel rather than better teaching. Those are market figures from the providers named, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both MYP Sciences and MYP Mathematics for my child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. The two groups share criterion A wording and a good deal of data-handling practice, so a teacher strong in both can run a single session that serves both reports. It stops being sensible at MYP 5, especially where a student is heading for Higher Level Physics or Chemistry in the Diploma, because the subject depth starts to pull apart. Tell us both groups and both current grades when you enquire and we will say honestly whether one teacher covers them or two are needed.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 4 in a Language Acquisition phase 2 class. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Not in itself. Language Acquisition is organised by phase rather than by year group, so a student can sit in MYP 4 working in phase 2 and be placed entirely correctly. The phase determines which descriptors apply and therefore what the four criteria are asking for, which is why the phase on the report is the first thing a tutor needs. What matters is whether the phase is moving across reports. A phase that has not shifted in two years is worth a conversation with the school before booking any tutoring at all.

faqs.question: When in the school year is MYP tutoring actually worth starting?
faqs.answer: Three moments do most of the work. The week after an interim report, when a criterion level has moved and nobody yet knows which strand caused it. Three or four weeks before a summative task, when the task-specific clarification exists and there is still time to produce evidence against it. And the end of MYP 4, before subject choices for MYP 5 and the Diploma close. A short block timed to one of those three achieves more than a year of weekly hours timed to none of them, which is the opposite of how most families buy tutoring.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher at an Emirates Living school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers it. The code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition work permit bars a permit holder from serving students affiliated with their own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules state the same prohibition for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff. The conflict is obvious: the person tutoring your child would also be the person marking the criterion grids. A teacher from a different school who knows the same programme gives you the subject knowledge without the conflict of interest.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private tutor in Dubai holds the MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the permit itself, issued in the tutor's own name, and ask when it expires. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, there is no financial excuse for not holding one. People offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published.

faqs.question: What happens if no MYP specialist is free for our subject group and slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you. The pool of teachers who can mark a criterion grid in a specific subject group is genuinely limited, and MYP 5 Design or a high Language Acquisition phase can be thin at a particular hour. The options are then a different evening, a short wait for a slot to open, or a different teacher whose subject depth we describe honestly before you decide. What we will not do is fill the hour with somebody approximate and let you discover the gap from the next report.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education run alongside the MYP in a Dubai school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated in forty-minute lesson units. For an MYP family this means the weekly timetable is fuller than the eight subject groups suggest, which is worth remembering before adding two tutoring sessions to a Year 10 week.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-views.closingHeading: Start with the grid, not the topic
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-the-views.closingBody: If your child is in the Middle Years Programme at a school in The Meadows, Emirates Hills, Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim, the useful first step is to find the last marked criterion grid and the task sheet that produced it. Send those with the subject group, the MYP year and the school name, and the match becomes a short conversation rather than a guess. The trial lesson is free and the condition is stated: one session, before any payment, with written feedback on one criterion afterwards. Lessons run live online on Gulf Standard Time and can move for Ramadan or for travel without losing the teacher. If nobody suitable is free for the slot you need, we will say so.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Middle Years Programme subjects for Tilal Al Ghaf and the Dubailand communities around it. Each works from the published criteria and descriptors for the subject group, and from the school's own assessed tasks rather than a generic scheme.

intro.heading: What a level 8 actually asks for
paragraphs: Middle Years reports are written in a language nobody teaches parents. Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight on a set of level descriptors, summed to a total out of thirty-two and converted to a grade from one to seven. A pupil who scores five on a criterion is being told they met a particular descriptor and not the one above it, and the descriptors are published. Almost no parent has read them, and almost no tutor in this market works from them.

They are worth reading, because the distinctions are specific rather than vague. The descriptors are banded in pairs — roughly 1 to 2, 3 to 4, 5 to 6 and 7 to 8 — and each band changes the verb. A lower band asks a pupil to state or describe; the next to explain or apply; the next to analyse or justify; the top to evaluate, synthesise or create with consistent accuracy. A pupil stuck on five is almost always producing work at the explain level when the task asked for analysis, and that is a teachable gap rather than a general capability.

This page therefore works through the content rather than the admin. The four criteria in each of the eight subject groups and what each rewards. The command terms the Middle Years Programme uses and what each one requires structurally. The task-specific clarifications your child's teacher writes, which are the actual assessment instrument and which most families have never asked to see. And the Approaches to Learning skills, which explain why a capable pupil can produce weak criterion scores.

Tilal Al Ghaf has a practical advantage worth using with this age group. The community has a school inside its boundary and DAMAC Hills, Dubai Sports City and Motor City all have their own provision nearby, so pupils are frequently home before four. For an eleven- or twelve-year-old that is the difference between a session with attention available and one spent managing tiredness, and at this age a forty-five minute session held early beats an hour held late.

One honest note about format before the detail. For Middle Years pupils we will say plainly when a screen is the wrong medium. A distractible pupil in the early years who needs an adult physically present to stay on task is better served in person, and since IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is a service we run only in India — the useful thing we can do in that case is tell you to look elsewhere.

Everything below is drawn from the published assessment structure of the programme. Where the IB revises its guides, the current guide is the authority, so confirm criteria and descriptors with your child's teacher. The point of setting them out here is that no competitor page in this market names a single Middle Years criterion in any subject group, which makes the information itself the differentiator.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme spans five years and the descriptor demands rise within the same criteria. These are the stages, with what changes at each.

programmes.name: MYP Years 1 and 2
programmes.description: The same four criteria per subject but assessed against the year-one-and-two descriptors, which ask for description and application rather than analysis and evaluation. The gap that matters here is written stamina and number fluency, because the programme assumes both and builds neither explicitly.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai many families arrive mid-programme from another country or curriculum, so a pupil can meet criterion assessment for the first time at twelve or thirteen. The first job is usually explaining what the criteria reward, which nobody has done for them.

programmes.name: MYP Year 3
programmes.description: The descriptors step up and the analysis demand becomes explicit. This is where a pupil who has been scoring well on knowledge criteria and poorly on investigation or thinking criteria starts to see the gap widen, because the upper bands now require justification rather than correct content.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools place pupils into Diploma or IGCSE routes on the strength of Year 9 performance, so this is also the year in which criterion patterns start to have consequences beyond the report itself.

programmes.name: MYP Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: The final descriptors, which ask for evaluation, synthesis and consistent accuracy at the top bands. MYP5 adds the Personal Project, assessed against three criteria of eight marks each, where most of the available marks reward documented process rather than the finished product.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai schools enter MYP5 candidates for IB eAssessment, producing the formal MYP certificate through on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, while others award school-based grades. Ask which, because the final year's preparation differs completely between them.

programmes.name: Into the Diploma or IGCSE
programmes.description: Middle Years pupils arrive in the Diploma strong on investigation and reflection and often light on executional fluency, particularly in mathematics. Those moving into IGCSE instead need exam-format work, because a terminal written paper marked against a scheme is a different instrument from criterion assessment.
programmes.countryNote: In this part of Dubailand provision is predominantly British curriculum, with IB continuum schools a short drive out towards Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills Estate. So a Tilal Al Ghaf MYP pupil may well be heading into IGCSE at a different school, which makes the format transition a real piece of work.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.subjectsIntro: These are the eight MYP subject groups with their four criteria named and what each actually rewards. Compare this against your child's criterion marks and the weak component is usually obvious within minutes.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: A Knowing and understanding · B Investigating patterns · C Communicating · D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts
subjects.description: Criterion B is where most pupils score worst, because it rewards generalising a pattern and justifying the generalisation, not calculating correctly. Arithmetic practice does not improve it; structured investigation practice does. Criterion C rewards correct notation and clear reasoning rather than neat presentation.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.levels: A Knowing and understanding · B Inquiring and designing · C Processing and evaluating · D Reflecting on the impacts of science
subjects.description: Criterion C is the usual weak point: pupils process data correctly and then stop, where the upper bands require discussing the validity of the method and of the conclusion. Criterion D rewards reasoned discussion of implications and is routinely under-prepared because it feels peripheral.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.levels: A Analysing · B Organising · C Producing text · D Using language
subjects.description: Fluent writers frequently score low on criterion A because they describe what a text says instead of examining how it creates an effect. That is a single teachable distinction and it moves one criterion out of four. Criterion D rewards register and accuracy rather than vocabulary range.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.levels: A Listening · B Reading · C Speaking · D Writing
subjects.description: Assessed by phase rather than year group, across six phases, so a pupil moving up a phase is measured against a harder standard. Criterion C rewards interaction and spontaneity, which is why rehearsed answers score below genuinely responsive ones.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.levels: A Knowing and understanding · B Investigating · C Communicating · D Thinking critically
subjects.description: Criterion D separates grades at the top and rewards evaluating sources and weighing interpretations rather than presenting more content. Pupils who write at length on criterion A and thinly on D produce a mid-band total from strong knowledge.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.levels: A Inquiring and analysing · B Developing ideas · C Creating the solution · D Evaluating
subjects.description: The most process-dependent subject group. A strong final product with no design folder behind it cannot score well, because criteria A, B and D all assess the documented process. Capable makers are surprised by this every year.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.levels: A Knowing and understanding · B Developing skills · C Thinking creatively · D Responding
subjects.description: Criterion D carries marks for reflecting on one's own and others' work, and it is routinely the lowest criterion for talented practitioners who do not write about what they make. Half the assessment is reflective rather than practical.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.levels: A Knowing and understanding · B Planning for performance · C Applying and performing · D Reflecting and improving performance
subjects.description: Two of the four criteria are written rather than physical, which is why able athletes sometimes bring home a grade their family cannot explain. Criterion B rewards a documented plan and criterion D a reasoned evaluation of performance.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.levels: A Planning · B Applying skills · C Reflecting, each out of 8
subjects.description: Twenty-four marks in total, with the bulk rewarding documented process rather than the product. Success criteria written after the product was made score badly, because criterion A assesses the plan and the criteria the pupil set in advance.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Combine two subject groups and reward explicit synthesis — showing how the two disciplines together produce an understanding neither gives alone. Pupils score lower here than in either parent subject because nobody has shown them what synthesis looks like in writing.

subjects.name: Approaches to Learning
subjects.levels: Thinking, social, communication, self-management and research skills
subjects.description: Taught across subjects rather than separately and not graded directly, but visible in criterion scores. Weak self-management shows up as missed deadlines across several subjects at once, which looks like motivation and is usually planning.

subjects.name: Arabic in the MYP
subjects.levels: Language and literature or language acquisition, plus mandated strands
subjects.description: Compulsory in Dubai private schools alongside the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Tutoring splits along the same line.

sections.heading: Inside the level descriptors: the verb is the ladder
paragraphs: The published descriptors for each criterion are banded, roughly in pairs across the eight marks, and the thing that changes between bands is the cognitive demand expressed as a verb. That is the single most useful fact about Middle Years assessment, because it turns a vague target into a concrete one. A pupil does not need to be 'better at science'; they need to produce discussion of validity where they are currently producing correct processing.

Reading across the subject groups, the pattern is consistent. The lowest band asks a pupil to state, list or outline. The next asks them to describe or apply with some guidance. The next asks them to explain, analyse or apply independently. The top band asks them to evaluate, justify, synthesise or create, consistently and accurately. A pupil stuck at five or six is almost always doing the band below well rather than the band above badly, and the gap is a kind of thinking rather than an amount of effort.

That reframes what a tutoring session should look like. Teaching more content moves a pupil up within a band and not across it. Moving across requires practising the harder cognitive act explicitly: taking a correct explanation and asking what its limitations are, taking a set of processed data and asking what would make the conclusion unsafe, taking an analysis and asking which interpretation is better supported and why. Those are specific exercises and they are what a criterion-focused session actually consists of.

Confirm the current descriptors with your child's teacher, since the IB revises its subject guides and the live guide is the authority. But ask for them, because reading the band your child is in alongside the one above is usually enough for a parent to see the gap for themselves — and that is a conversation most families have never been offered.

sections.heading: The task-specific clarification is the real assessment
paragraphs: Here is something most families have never been told. The published criterion descriptors are generic across a subject group, and for each assessed task the teacher writes task-specific clarifications: a version of the descriptors adapted to that task, saying what analysis or evaluation looks like for this particular piece of work. That document, not the generic descriptor, is what the pupil's work is actually marked against.

Pupils are usually given it and usually do not read it. Parents are usually not given it and do not know it exists. It is worth asking for, because it converts an abstract target into an instruction: for this task, the upper band requires comparing two data sets and commenting on which better supports the hypothesis. A pupil who reads that before starting produces different work from one who writes what they know and hopes.

This is also the single most useful thing a tutor can work from. A session planned around the generic descriptor is better than one planned around the topic, and a session planned around the task-specific clarification is better again, because it is aimed at the exact thing the teacher will mark. Our first request after a report is for the clarifications attached to the next assessed task in the weak criterion, because that is what makes the session concrete.

There is a secondary benefit for the pupil. A child who learns to read a task-specific clarification before beginning any assessed task has acquired a transferable habit that works for the remaining years of the programme and, later, for Diploma internal assessment criteria. It is close to the highest-leverage skill in the Middle Years Programme, it takes one session to teach, and almost nobody teaches it.

sections.heading: The command terms, and what each one requires structurally
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme uses a defined set of command terms and they appear in task instructions and in descriptors alike. Each asks for a different structure of response, and a pupil who treats them as synonyms for 'write about this' produces work that cannot reach the upper bands however much they know.

'Identify' and 'state' want a short answer with no elaboration. 'Describe' wants an account of what something is or does. 'Explain' wants reasons or mechanisms — the why behind the what. 'Analyse' wants the thing broken into parts with relationships between them made explicit. 'Evaluate' wants a judgement supported on both sides, with limitations acknowledged. 'Justify' wants reasons for a specific choice already made. 'Synthesise' wants two or more elements combined into something neither gives alone, which is also exactly what interdisciplinary units assess.

Teaching these explicitly is the most efficient intervention available in the Middle Years Programme, for the same reason it is in the Diploma: the verbs recur across every subject group. A pupil who learns to evaluate properly improves in sciences criterion C, individuals and societies criterion D, arts criterion D and physical education criterion D simultaneously. No content teaching produces that spread, and most families buy content teaching because the report named subjects rather than verbs.

The method that works is marked rewrites rather than explanation. The pupil writes an answer, the tutor marks it against the descriptor band, the pupil sees which band they produced and why, and rewrites it to reach the next one. Three or four sessions of that changes how a pupil writes for the rest of the programme. Explaining the difference between analyse and evaluate without the rewriting produces a pupil who can define the terms and still cannot execute them.

sections.heading: Approaches to Learning: why a capable pupil scores badly
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme teaches five categories of Approaches to Learning skills across subjects: thinking, social, communication, self-management and research. They are not graded as a subject, but they are visible everywhere in criterion scores, and they explain the pupil who is plainly able and keeps bringing home fives.

Self-management is the one that does most damage in Dubai schools. Because MYP marks come from assessed tasks across the year rather than from a terminal paper, a task done late or badly because the pupil lost track of it is a mark permanently inside the final grade. A pupil who is coping academically and drowning organisationally loses grades for work they could have done well, and the report records it as subject weakness across several subjects at once. That looks like motivation and is almost always planning.

Research skills are the second. Criteria that reward investigation — mathematics B, sciences B, individuals and societies B, design A — all assume a pupil can frame a question, find and judge sources, and record what they found. A pupil who has never been taught to do that systematically produces investigation work that is thin regardless of their subject knowledge, which is why the same criterion is often weak across three subjects at once.

The practical consequence for a family is that the right purchase is sometimes not subject tutoring at all. A pupil whose pattern is missed deadlines and thin investigation across several subjects needs planning and research habits, and one tutor working on those through whichever subject the pupil likes most will lift several grades. Three subject tutors would each teach content and none would touch the cause. We will say that rather than take the larger booking, because three evenings of tutoring produces a tired child and no change.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: three criteria, twenty-four marks
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP5 is assessed against three criteria — planning, applying skills, and reflecting — each marked out of eight for a total of twenty-four. Confirm the current criteria with your child's school, since the IB revises its guides. The structural point that surprises almost every family is that the bulk of the available marks reward documented process rather than the finished product.

Criterion A, planning, assesses a clear goal, the success criteria the pupil set for their own product, and a plan for achieving it. The decisive word is 'set': success criteria written after the product exists are not a plan, they are a description, and markers can tell. Criterion B, applying skills, assesses the skills developed and applied to the goal, which requires a record of what was learned along the way rather than a finished object that implies it. Criterion C, reflecting, assesses reflection on both the product and the learning.

So the commonest failure in Dubai schools is a strong product with a thin process journal. A pupil builds something genuinely impressive, writes the journal in the fortnight before submission, and lands in the middle because the evidence the criteria ask for was never created. Nothing can be done afterwards, because reconstructing a journal is visible to a reader and is not what the criteria assess anyway.

The fix is a cadence, not an intervention. A short entry each week recording what was attempted, what went wrong, what was learned and what changes next produces exactly the evidence the criteria want, as a by-product of doing the project properly. A tutor's legitimate role is to hold that cadence, check the pupil's own success criteria are being addressed, teach any skill the project requires, and give feedback on the pupil's own report. The tutor chooses nothing, makes nothing and writes nothing.

sections.heading: eAssessment, and what the on-screen format demands
paragraphs: Some Dubai schools enter MYP5 candidates for IB eAssessment, which produces the formal MYP certificate through on-screen examinations and ePortfolios. Others award school-based grades moderated internally. A surprising number of parents do not know which their school uses, and the two arrangements make the final year a completely different proposition.

If your school uses eAssessment, there is an examination component with externally set deadlines, and preparation has a recognisable shape. The on-screen examinations present unfamiliar stimulus material and require responses to command terms within a fixed window, which is a format skill as much as a subject one. A pupil who has only ever produced coursework-style assessed tasks over days has never written to a criterion under timing, and that is the gap worth closing before the examination rather than during it.

The ePortfolio components require work assembled against a published brief, which rewards exactly the organisational habits discussed above. A pupil with weak self-management and good subject knowledge will under-perform on an ePortfolio for reasons that have nothing to do with the subject, which is worth knowing in advance because it is addressable.

If your school awards school-based grades instead, the final year is an internal matter and the useful preparation is simply doing each assessed task well against its clarifications. Either way, ask what the final MYP grade will be used for: in some schools it informs Diploma course and level placement, which makes it consequential, and in others it is reported and largely superseded. That answer should decide how much weight the final year gets.

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary units, and what synthesis looks like
paragraphs: Interdisciplinary units combine two subject groups and are assessed against their own criteria, which reward explicit synthesis. Pupils routinely score lower on them than in either parent subject, and the reason is not that the content is harder. It is that nobody has shown them what synthesis looks like on paper.

Synthesis is not summarising two subjects in turn. A pupil who writes a paragraph of science and a paragraph of geography has produced two disciplinary accounts side by side, which is what weak interdisciplinary work looks like and what most pupils produce. Synthesis means using the two together to reach an understanding neither gives alone: the scientific mechanism explains why the geographical pattern takes the form it does, and the geographical pattern constrains which scientific explanations are plausible.

That is a structure, and structures are teachable. The sentence pattern that works is explicit: this disciplinary insight, combined with that one, produces this understanding, which neither alone would support. Pupils who have been shown one worked example of that pattern can usually reproduce it, and it is worth a band on the relevant criterion almost immediately.

The same skill reappears later. Diploma Theory of Knowledge rewards exactly this kind of cross-disciplinary reasoning, and the Extended Essay in several subjects rewards drawing on more than one body of knowledge coherently. So an hour spent on what synthesis looks like in MYP4 is not only worth a criterion band now; it is the earliest available preparation for a Diploma core component.

sections.heading: What criterion-focused tutoring costs
paragraphs: Start with what the market publishes, then notice how little of it was priced with a Year 8 in mind. Bestimate's Dubai table puts IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, with monthly estimates of AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Named providers run from AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik, through Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, up to TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. Every one of those tiers is built around an examination year, and the Middle Years Programme has none - a Tilal Al Ghaf parent is buying movement on a criterion marked out of eight, not marks on a terminal paper, and the published premium exists to buy the second of those. All figures are the competitors' own, read in October 2026.

For the Middle Years Programme the premium band is usually unnecessary, and saying so costs us money. A specialist Diploma tutor at AED 450 an hour is not three times as useful to a Year 8 as a qualified teacher at AED 150, because the content is not where the difficulty lies. What the Middle Years needs is someone who works from the descriptors and the task-specific clarifications, and that is available in the AED 150 to AED 300 band.

Where the spending is genuinely well targeted is in three places. Criterion coaching, because moving one criterion lifts every subsequent assessed task in that subject. A command-term block of three or four sessions, because the verbs recur across subject groups and the gains show in several subjects at once. And Personal Project process coaching across MYP5, because the marks sit in documentation that cannot be recovered later and a fortnightly slot across six months is a modest total.

Where it is usually wasted is three parallel subject tutors for what a full report shows to be one weak criterion or one Approaches to Learning gap, and premium rates for early Middle Years content. IB Gram publishes no hourly rate on this page, because the right figure depends on subject, year and whether the work is criterion coaching, command terms or project process. The market band lets you judge any quote including ours, and the first lesson is free.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and the limits we work to
paragraphs: Middle Years assessment is largely coursework, which makes the honesty boundary more consequential here than families expect. A tutor explains what a criterion rewards, reads the task-specific clarification alongside the pupil, teaches the content or skill required, demonstrates a worked example, and gives feedback on the pupil's own work. A tutor does not write, make, assemble or complete any part of an assessed task, a Personal Project product, a journal or a project report.

There is a practical argument alongside the ethical one, and it is the one worth making to a fifteen-year-old directly. The criteria assess planning, skill development and reflection — the pupil's own thinking, documented over time. Work produced by someone else reads exactly as such and loses precisely those marks, which are the majority. The pupils who score well on a Personal Project are the ones who kept the journal from week one, not the ones with the most impressive product.

On materials: we do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, assessment criteria documents or published materials. We reference them, point to the official source, and teach the pupil to read their own school's clarifications. We also do not describe tutors as IB examiners where current status cannot be evidenced, and IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

On regulation: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The requirement does not depend on the age of the pupil. Those operating without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so distrust quoted amounts.
