faqs.question: What is the difference between a 5 and a 7 on an MYP criterion?
faqs.answer: A kind of thinking rather than an amount of effort. The published descriptors are banded in pairs across the eight marks and the verb changes between bands: the 5 to 6 band typically asks a pupil to explain or analyse independently, while the 7 to 8 band asks them to evaluate, justify or synthesise consistently. A pupil on five is usually doing the lower band well rather than the upper band badly, which means more content teaching moves them within the band rather than across it.

faqs.question: What is a task-specific clarification and why should I ask for it?
faqs.answer: It is the version of the criterion descriptors that your child's teacher adapts for a particular assessed task, stating what analysis or evaluation looks like for that specific piece of work. It is what the work is actually marked against, rather than the generic descriptor. Pupils are usually given it and usually do not read it; parents are usually not given it and do not know it exists. Reading it before starting a task is a one-session habit that works for the rest of the programme.

faqs.question: Which MYP criteria do pupils most often score worst on?
faqs.answer: The thinking criteria rather than the knowledge ones. Mathematics criterion B, investigating patterns, because it rewards generalising and justifying rather than calculating. Sciences criterion C, processing and evaluating, because pupils process data correctly and then stop where the upper bands want discussion of validity. Individuals and societies criterion D, thinking critically, because it rewards weighing interpretations rather than presenting more content. In each case the subject knowledge is often fine.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to homes in Tilal Al Ghaf?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run only in India. For this age group we will also say honestly when a screen is the wrong medium: a distractible pupil in the early Middle Years who needs an adult physically present to stay on task is better served in person, and in that case the useful thing we can do is point you elsewhere rather than sell a format that will not work.

faqs.question: Why is my capable child scoring fives across several subjects?
faqs.answer: Two common causes, and neither is subject knowledge. One is the band problem: the pupil produces sound explanation where the upper bands want evaluation, and the same gap appears in every subject because the thinking demand is the same. The other is Approaches to Learning, particularly self-management: because MYP marks come from assessed tasks across the year, a task done late or hurriedly is a mark permanently in the final grade, and that shows up as weakness in several subjects at once.

faqs.answer: Structurally, and that is what decides the band. 'Describe' wants an account of what something is or does. 'Explain' wants reasons or mechanisms. 'Analyse' wants the thing broken into parts with relationships made explicit. 'Evaluate' wants a judgement supported on both sides with limitations acknowledged. 'Justify' wants reasons for a choice already made. 'Synthesise' wants elements combined into something neither gives alone. A pupil treating them as synonyms cannot reach the upper bands however much they know.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Personal Project and where do they sit?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four, across three criteria of eight marks each: planning, applying skills, and reflecting. Confirm the current criteria with your school, since the IB revises its guides. The bulk reward documented process rather than the finished product, and the decisive detail in criterion A is that the success criteria must have been set by the pupil in advance. Criteria written after the product exists are a description rather than a plan, and markers can tell.

faqs.question: What makes interdisciplinary units score lower than the parent subjects?
faqs.answer: Pupils produce two disciplinary accounts side by side rather than synthesis. Writing a paragraph of science and a paragraph of geography is not synthesis; using the two together to reach an understanding neither gives alone is. The sentence pattern that earns the marks is explicit: this insight, combined with that one, supports this conclusion, which neither alone would. Pupils shown one worked example can usually reproduce it, and it is often worth a band immediately.

faqs.answer: Ask, because the two arrangements make the final year completely different and many parents do not know which applies. Some Dubai schools enter MYP5 candidates for IB eAssessment, producing the formal certificate through on-screen examinations and ePortfolios with externally set deadlines. Others award school-based grades moderated internally. Also ask what the final MYP grade is used for, because in some schools it informs Diploma course and level placement and in others it is largely superseded.

faqs.answer: Writing to a criterion under timing, which a coursework-trained pupil has usually never done. The on-screen examinations present unfamiliar stimulus material and require responses to command terms within a fixed window, so the skill is partly format rather than subject: reading quickly on screen, identifying the verb, and producing an upper-band response without the days of drafting that assessed tasks allow. That gap is worth closing before the examination rather than discovering during it.

faqs.question: Which rate band suits Middle Years tutoring?
faqs.answer: The qualified subject tutor band, roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour read in October 2026, rather than the specialist band above it. A premium Diploma tutor at AED 450 an hour is not three times as useful to a Year 8, because content is not where the difficulty lies. What the Middle Years needs is someone who works from the published descriptors and the task-specific clarifications, and that does not require the top of the market.

faqs.question: Should we book three tutors for three weak subjects?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Read the whole report for repeated criteria first. A pupil weak on investigating in mathematics, inquiring and designing in sciences, and investigating in individuals and societies has one transferable weakness appearing three times, and one tutor working on the skill through the subject the pupil likes most will lift all three. That is a third of the cost and usually a better outcome, because three evenings of tutoring produces a tired child.

faqs.question: How long should a Middle Years session be?
faqs.answer: For the early years, forty-five minutes held weekly beats an hour that loses its final third. An eleven- or twelve-year-old at six in the evening has limited useful attention, and a longer session adds time rather than learning. From MYP4 onwards an hour is usually productive. Tilal Al Ghaf's local school provision means pupils are often home before four, so the early slot is available here and worth taking for this age group in particular.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an assessed MYP task?
faqs.answer: With understanding it and with feedback on the pupil's own work, yes. A tutor can read the task-specific clarification alongside the pupil, explain what the upper band requires, teach the content or skill needed, demonstrate a worked example on a different question, and give feedback on the pupil's draft. A tutor cannot write, make or assemble any part of what is submitted. The criteria assess the pupil's own planning and thinking, so outsourced work loses the marks it was meant to gain.

faqs.question: Why is Arabic on an MYP timetable in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because the emirate requires it regardless of the licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies and prohibits combined classes, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. The timetable therefore carries subjects beyond the eight MYP groups, and Arabic is among the most requested tutoring streams in the emirate.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.closingHeading: Ask for the descriptors, then read one band up
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-tilal-al-ghaf.closingBody: Three requests change a Middle Years plan more than any amount of subject tutoring. Ask the school for the four criterion marks out of eight behind each grade. Ask for the task-specific clarification attached to the next assessed task in the weakest criterion. And ask to see the published descriptor for the band your child is in alongside the band above it. Together those make the gap visible: content, analysis, evaluation or consistency. If the same criterion is weak in three subjects, one tutor on that thinking skill will lift all three, and we will say so rather than taking the larger booking. Tilal Al Ghaf sessions run live and one-to-one over video at Gulf Standard Time. We make no home visits in the UAE and promise no grades.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-town-square.tutorsIntro: MYP tutors matched to Town Square students work from the subject-group criteria your child is marked against and hold a slot chosen for their age rather than for whatever hour happened to be free.

intro.heading: What hour of a Town Square week does an MYP child actually have?
paragraphs: Everything about MYP tutoring out here begins with one number: what time your child reaches the door. Town Square is a Nshama community off Al Qudra Road, and the schools running the Middle Years Programme are not in it — families travel to The Sustainable City, Motor City, Al Barsha or Silicon Oasis, which means a school day ending at half three becomes a 4:30pm arrival home at best and closer to five from the inner city.

Then age enters the calculation, and this is where MYP differs sharply from Diploma tutoring. A seventeen-year-old can work at half eight in the evening and often prefers it. An eleven-year-old who has been awake since six and spent fifty minutes in a car cannot, and no amount of goodwill from either side changes that. A session booked at half six for a Year 7 student is a session the family pays for and the child does not use.

That makes the window narrow and worth defending. For most MYP students the hour that works is around five o'clock: late enough to have decompressed and eaten something, early enough to still concentrate. MYP 4 and 5 students — Years 10 and 11 — stretch comfortably to six. Below MYP 3 we would rather propose a weekend morning than take a weekday evening, and we say so rather than book it.

A visiting tutor cannot reach that window from Town Square. They leave another part of Dubai in the same afternoon traffic, arriving at half six at the earliest, which is precisely the hour at which a younger MYP child stops absorbing anything. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only — so the five o'clock slot exists at all.

The second thing worth knowing is that the MYP is five years and they need different things. MYP 1 to 3 is where criterion-based working becomes a habit or does not. MYP 4 and 5 is where the demand rises and where the Diploma subject choices get decided. And Year 11 adds the Personal Project on top of a full subject load, which is the single most predictable scheduling crunch in the programme.

The IB accounts for around 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools, and MYP-specific tutoring is thinner still, because many tutors advertising IB experience mean the Diploma. A Diploma specialist handed an MYP 3 student teaches excellent content against the wrong target, which looks satisfactory for a term and changes nothing on the report.

There is a fifteen-second test for that, and it is the most useful thing on this page: ask a prospective tutor to name the four criteria for the subject group in question. Somebody who has taught the MYP names them and says roughly what each one rewards. Somebody who has not says the programme is criterion-based and moves on to describing their years of experience. Apply it to us as readily as to anybody else.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-town-square.programmesIntro: The MYP spans five years and asks for different things at each end, and the usable session hour changes with the age as well. These are the stages we cover for Town Square families.

programmes.name: MYP Years 1 and 2, Years 7 and 8
programmes.description: The transition years. Students meet tasks that ask them to investigate, communicate and reflect rather than simply answer, and reports begin to show the four-criterion profile parents find hard to read. Those who treat every task as a test of recall score below what they know.
programmes.countryNote: This is the age group where the hour matters most and gets chosen worst. After a Town Square school run an eleven-year-old has an hour of useful attention left, not three. Sessions here work at 4:45pm or 5pm, or on a weekend morning, and we will say so rather than take a later booking that will quietly stop working.

programmes.name: MYP Year 3, Year 9
programmes.description: The year that decides the next two. Subject choices are made or narrowed, the demand in each subject steps up, and the criterion profile starts to carry real information about which Diploma routes will suit. Still no external examination, which is why it feels less urgent than it is.
programmes.countryNote: Town Square has many mid-stage arrivals, and a child joining in Year 9 from another system meets criterion-based assessment for the first time. They are frequently quick and accurate and still marked down, because the task wanted a justified generalisation and they produced an answer. A fixable mismatch rather than a weakness.

programmes.name: MYP Years 4 and 5, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Demand rises sharply and the stakes become real, because these years decide Diploma subject and level choices. Year 11 adds the Personal Project, a substantial independent piece assessed against its own criteria, competing with everything else for the same hours.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most of our Town Square MYP work sits, and where a 5:30pm or 6pm session becomes workable. It is also where the week genuinely runs out of room, which is why the Personal Project needs a protected slot rather than whatever time is left over after everything else.

programmes.name: The step into the Diploma
programmes.description: The largest step in the IB continuum. Criterion-based internal assessment gives way to external examination plus Internal Assessments, content depth rises sharply, and Higher Level subjects demand sustained independent work. Students comfortable in MYP 5 can be struggling by November of Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: The criterion profile predicts this and almost nobody reads it that way. A weak sciences processing and evaluating criterion forecasts difficulty with the Diploma individual investigation; weak mathematics communication forecasts the Exploration. Both are addressable in Year 11, cheaply, before the Diploma starts.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-town-square.subjectsIntro: The MYP subject groups Town Square families ask about, with the criteria that apply and where marks are genuinely lost in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B rewards generalising from a pattern and justifying it, which no traditional lesson drills, and criterion C marks the quality of communication rather than the answer.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B asks for an investigation designed with controlled variables; criterion C for data processed and the method evaluated.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Students lose marks by summarising a text rather than analysing how it produces meaning, exactly as they later will in Diploma Paper 1. Organisation is marked explicitly, which rewards planning first.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria cover listening, reading, speaking and writing, assessed by phase rather than by year group. A student can sit in a different phase from their year peers, which confuses parents and is entirely normal. Progress is measurable because the skills are discrete.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. The critical-thinking criterion is where most marks go: students describe sources rather than evaluating their reliability and usefulness, which is teachable technique.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating. Documentation carries the marks, and students routinely produce a good outcome with almost no record of the design cycle, which caps the score regardless of quality.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. The process journal is where marks sit, and students who treat it as an afterthought lose credit their practical work had already earned.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and reflective components surprise families expecting a purely practical subject, and that is where marks are usually lost.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and communicating. Process documentation decides the score far more than the product does, which is why establishing a dated journal habit in the first fortnight is the highest-value intervention available.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Thinking, research, communication, social and self-management skills, assessed implicitly through the subject criteria. Weak self-management shows as low scores across several subjects at once — the pattern worth spotting before any subject tutoring is bought.

sections.heading: Which hour works at which MYP age
paragraphs: This is the part of MYP tutoring that providers skip and families discover. Scheduling for a Diploma student is a matter of preference; scheduling for an eleven-year-old is a matter of whether the session happens at all in any useful sense.

The constraint is cumulative fatigue. An MYP 1 student has been awake since six, has had a full school day, and has spent perhaps fifty minutes in a car on the Al Qudra Road approach. The attention they have left is roughly one hour, and it is available from about a quarter of an hour after they get home until somewhere around six o'clock. After that they are present and not learning, which is a distinction a tutor can see and a parent in another room cannot.

The window widens with age. MYP 4 and 5 students — Years 10 and 11 — handle a 5:30pm or 6pm session comfortably and can sustain ninety minutes when a criterion-assessed task is due. By the Diploma the useful hour has moved to eight in the evening. That progression is predictable enough to plan around, and it is why we ask the year group before anything else.

Weekend mornings are the alternative and they are better than their reputation. For a Year 7 or Year 8 student, two hours on a Friday morning with a clear head is worth considerably more than three tired weekday half-hours, and for a household running school runs to two or three schools they are frequently the only honest answer. We propose them readily, including when a family has asked for a weekday evening, because the alternative is a session nobody is using.

sections.heading: Year 11 is a double load, and the calendar shows it
paragraphs: MYP 5 is the year the week runs out of room, and it does so predictably enough that it can be planned for rather than survived. A Year 11 MYP student is carrying a full subject load with criterion-assessed tasks across eight subject groups, the Personal Project, and in many schools the subject and level decisions for the Diploma that follows.

The Personal Project is the part that gets squeezed, because it has no weekly lesson defending it. Subject tasks have deadlines a teacher chases; the project has a distant deadline and a student's own judgement, which in a busy term loses every time. That is why the documentation almost always suffers rather than the product: the making happens because it is engaging, and the recording of decisions, difficulties and changes of direction does not happen at all.

That matters because the criteria reward planning, applying skills, reflecting and communicating the process rather than the quality of what was produced. A modest project with a thorough, dated journal outscores an impressive one documented retrospectively in the final month — and retrospective documentation reads as reconstruction, because it is.

So the recommendation for a Town Square Year 11 is structural rather than academic: protect a slot for the project specifically, early, when the habit can still be established. Ninety minutes a fortnight from the start of the year is worth more than six hours in April. The table sets the Year 11 crunch out against what should be happening when, so the pressure points are visible before they arrive.

sections.heading: Reading the criterion profile, and when to act on it
paragraphs: MYP reports give four criterion scores per subject, each out of eight, and no overall grade. Families coming from a percentage-based system read that as a puzzle. It is closer to an instruction, and the most useful thing a tutor can do in a first conversation is translate it.

The criteria differ by subject group. Mathematics marks knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Sciences mark knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Individuals and Societies covers knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. They measure genuinely different capabilities, which is why a profile of 7, 4, 5, 3 is informative and the average of those four numbers is not.

The pattern most worth finding is a single criterion low across several subjects at once. A student scoring poorly on communication in mathematics, organising in Language and Literature and documentation in Design has one structuring and self-management problem appearing in three places, not three subject weaknesses. Fixing it once lifts all three, which is both cheaper and faster than three subject tutors. This is the first thing we look for and almost never what a family arrives asking about.

On timing: act on a criterion pattern as soon as it repeats across two reporting cycles, because a single low score can be one bad task. By MYP 5 the criteria that forecast Diploma difficulty deserve specific attention — a weak sciences processing and evaluating criterion predicts trouble with the Diploma individual investigation, and weak mathematics communication predicts the Exploration. Both are cheap to address in Year 11 and expensive in Year 12.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: This is a real part of a Town Square MYP student's week and it is absent from almost every competitor page. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The structure is specific. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with Arabic the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two further details are worth knowing as a parent. KHDA requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete and checkable credential point about school staff. And mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advice that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

One constraint applies directly to tutoring in these subjects: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That is a genuine limit on how any provider may describe Arabic, Islamic or Social Studies support, and it is why we describe this work as helping a student with the material their school teaches rather than as an alternative curriculum. These subjects sit alongside the MYP rather than inside it, and they still occupy hours in the same week.

sections.heading: An MYP tutor is not a Diploma tutor at a lower level
paragraphs: This is the mismatch that costs Town Square families the most, and it is invisible for a whole term. Many tutors advertising IB experience mean the Diploma, because that is where most of the market is and where the fees are highest. Handed an MYP 3 student, a Diploma specialist will teach the subject very well against entirely the wrong target.

What they will do is add depth. More content, harder examples, faster pace — all of which is good teaching and none of which addresses a criterion B score of 3. The MYP was not asking for more content. It was asking for a justified generalisation, or a designed investigation with controlled variables, or a documented process, or an evaluation rather than a description. A tutor who has never worked to the criteria does not know that is the target, and the sessions feel productive because they are, just not for the thing being marked.

The test is a single question and it takes fifteen seconds: name the four criteria for this subject group. Somebody who has taught the MYP names them and says roughly what each rewards. Somebody who has not says the MYP is criterion-based and moves on to describing their experience. Treat the second answer as a no, politely, and ask the same question of the next candidate.

The related trap is the opposite direction: a tutor experienced with younger children who has never seen a criterion-assessed task either. The MYP sits in an awkward middle where neither primary nor Diploma experience transfers automatically, which is precisely why MYP-specific tutoring is thinner in this market than the number of MYP students would suggest.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs around Town Square
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates, read from provider pages in October 2026. Budget online tutoring from AED 33-65 an hour, with Tutopiya at AED 33-52 and EdFlik at AED 45-65. Qualified online subject tutors AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate putting the band at AED 200-450 plus. In-home visits AED 180-500 including travel. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end.

MYP sits in an unusual place on that ladder. The budget band is more viable here than at Diploma level for straightforward content help, because a capable graduate genuinely can support an MYP 2 student with content and confidence. What it cannot do is work to the criteria, so if the report shows a criterion problem rather than a content problem, the cheap option addresses the wrong thing however pleasant the sessions are.

The expensive mismatch runs the other way: paying specialist rates for a Diploma tutor with no MYP experience. Same published band, excellent teaching, wrong target. That one is worth guarding against specifically, because it carries the price signal of quality and delivers depth to a student whose report was asking for documented process or justified generalisation.

By the month the same bands read as follows. Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for one weekly hour at the budget band, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist work, with advertised packages at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. The MYP distortion is that families read those as a five-year figure and flinch, when almost no MYP student needs five years of anything: the load concentrates in the final year, and before that the pattern that works is a short block when a criterion profile goes wrong, then nothing. Every figure above belongs to the provider named beside it, and none of them is an IB Gram price. Ours comes after the diagnostic, because an honest number depends on the MYP year, on which criterion is actually failing, and on whether the Personal Project is in play.

sections.heading: Ramadan, prayer times and a younger student's week
paragraphs: The UAE academic calendar affects MYP students more than Diploma students, because a shorter school day and a reorganised evening hit a child with less reserve harder. Planning for it is straightforward provided it happens in advance.

During Ramadan, school days shorten and the evening reorganises around Iftar. For MYP students the usual five o'clock slot often stops working entirely, and families here typically move to a late-morning or early-afternoon session on the shortened school days, shift to a post-Iftar slot for older MYP students, or pause part of the month and resume afterwards with a weekend block. Content should also move towards consolidation rather than new material, which suits a shorter attention span better anyway.

Prayer times matter all year and move through the calendar, so we build slots around them from the start rather than waiting for a family to raise it. The same applies to the long summer and the travel weekends normal in this community — sessions continue while a family is away, because the tutor's location is already part of the arrangement and only the time of day needs adjusting.

With younger students the drift risk is higher than with Diploma candidates, because nobody is chasing a deadline. A cancelled session becomes a rescheduled one becomes a cancelled one, and by February the arrangement has ended without anyone deciding it should. The commitment we ask for is small and specific: tell us the new pattern and we move the fixed slot deliberately rather than letting a run of missed weeks make the decision.

sections.heading: What we will not claim about MYP progress
paragraphs: No guarantee of a criterion score, a grade or an improvement. Criterion scores move when a student changes how they approach a task, which takes practice and happens on their timeline rather than ours, and an offer that ignores that is a sales device rather than a commitment.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which means none published. No average criterion scores achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction figure, no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish such numbers routinely, occasionally in two conflicting versions on the same page, and almost never say how any of them was produced. Self-asserted review markup also breaches Google's structured-data policy.

No regulator claim of any kind. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE or IB approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, has no office or centre anywhere in the UAE, and does not claim KHDA teaching approval — which is a real credential required of school teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education, and not something a tutoring platform holds. We also host no IB material as downloads; subject guides and criteria belong to the IB and we reference them.

And we will turn down an hour rather than take it. If a family proposes half six for a Year 7 student after a long run from Al Barsha, we will say the hour is too late to be useful and offer a weekend morning instead. Occasionally we will read a report and tell a family their child is doing fine and the unfamiliar scale was the problem, which is the smallest possible sale and sometimes the correct answer.

process.title: Tell us the year group and the door time
process.description: Which MYP year, which school, and what time your child actually reaches home rather than the bell time. Those two facts together decide which hour is usable, and for a Year 7 student they decide whether a weekday session is viable at all.

process.title: Send the actual criterion scores
process.description: The four scores per subject, not a summary. A parent's description — doing badly in science — discards exactly the information that distinguishes a content gap from an investigation-design gap or a reflection gap, which need three different kinds of work.

process.title: We look for one criterion low across subjects
process.description: Before recommending subject tutoring, we check whether a single transferable skill is dragging several subjects at once. Communication in maths, organising in language, documentation in design is one problem in three places, and fixing it once lifts all three.

process.title: Free trial lesson at the hour you would use
process.description: One full lesson with the tutor who would continue, no card required and no obligation, at the time you intend to keep. At MYP age the hour and the rapport matter more than credentials, so this session tests both at once.

process.title: Fix the slot, and protect the project slot separately
process.description: The weekly time stays put, around prayer times and sport, with a planned Ramadan change. For Year 11, the Personal Project gets its own protected slot from the start of the year rather than whatever time is left over, which is reliably none.

whyPoints.title: We plan from age as well as the school run
whyPoints.description: An eleven-year-old home at half four has about an hour of useful attention; a seventeen-year-old is sharpest at eight in the evening. We ask the year group before anything else, because the usable window moves with age and is narrow at the younger end.

whyPoints.title: The five o'clock slot exists because nobody drives
whyPoints.description: A visiting tutor leaving another part of Dubai in afternoon traffic arrives at half six, which is exactly when a younger MYP child stops absorbing. Online delivery is what makes the hour that works available at all from Town Square.

whyPoints.title: MYP experience, not Diploma experience scaled down
whyPoints.description: A Diploma specialist adds depth, and an MYP criterion problem does not want depth — it wants a justified generalisation, a designed investigation or a documented process. Ask any candidate to name the four criteria for the subject group.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project gets its own slot
whyPoints.description: In Year 11 the project has no weekly lesson defending it, so it receives whatever time is left over, which is none. A protected fortnightly slot from week one is worth more than six hours in April, because the criteria reward documented process.

whyPoints.title: We read the report as a prediction
whyPoints.description: A weak sciences processing criterion forecasts trouble with the Diploma individual investigation; weak mathematics communication forecasts the Exploration. Those signals sit in MYP reports for five years and almost nobody uses them.

whyPoints.title: We decline a bad hour, and sometimes the sale
whyPoints.description: If a proposed slot is too late for a Year 7 student, we say so and offer a weekend morning. Occasionally we read a report and tell a family their child is doing fine and the unfamiliar scale was the problem.

faqs.question: What time should an MYP session be for a Town Square family?
faqs.answer: Around five o'clock for most MYP students: late enough to have decompressed after the run from The Sustainable City, Motor City or the inner city and eaten something, early enough to still concentrate. MYP 4 and 5 students stretch comfortably to 5:30pm or 6pm. Below MYP 3 a weekend morning is usually better than any weekday evening, and we will propose that rather than take a later booking. These times are only possible because nobody is driving to you.

faqs.question: Why can't my Year 7 child have a 6:30pm session?
faqs.answer: Because the attention is gone. An MYP 1 student has been awake since six, had a full school day, and spent perhaps fifty minutes in a car on the Al Qudra Road approach. What remains is roughly one hour of useful concentration, available from shortly after they get home until around six. After that they are present and not learning — a distinction a tutor sees clearly and a parent in another room does not. We would rather offer a weekend morning than bill for that hour.

faqs.question: Does the usable hour change as a child moves up the MYP?
faqs.answer: Yes, and predictably. MYP 1 and 2 students work in a 4:45pm to 5:45pm window, sixty minutes at most. MYP 3 extends to about six. MYP 4 and 5 handle 5pm to 7pm and can sustain ninety minutes when a criterion-assessed task is due. By the Diploma the productive hour has moved to eight in the evening, which is why Diploma tutoring scheduling advice does not transfer to a Year 7 student. We ask the year group before proposing any slot.

faqs.question: Why does the Personal Project always get squeezed in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Because it has no weekly lesson defending it. Subject criterion tasks have deadlines a teacher chases; the project has a distant deadline and relies on a fifteen-year-old's own judgement in a term already full. What suffers is the documentation rather than the product — the making happens because it is engaging, and recording decisions, difficulties and changes of direction does not. Since the criteria reward planning, skills, reflection and process communication rather than the object, that is exactly the wrong thing to lose.

faqs.question: When should Personal Project support start?
faqs.answer: Week one of Year 11, in a protected fortnightly slot. Ninety minutes a fortnight from the start of the year is worth more than six hours in April, because what the criteria reward is a documented process and that cannot be reconstructed convincingly — a journal written retrospectively in one weekend reads as reconstruction, because it is. The coaching itself is scope narrowing, establishing a dated documentation habit, explaining what each criterion rewards, and feedback on the student's own journal.

faqs.question: How do I read my child's MYP criterion scores?
faqs.answer: As an instruction rather than a puzzle. Four scores per subject, each out of eight, measuring genuinely different capabilities that differ by subject group — mathematics marks knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying maths in real-life contexts, while sciences mark knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting. A profile of 7, 4, 5, 3 tells you the content is known and something else is not. Averaging those four numbers discards the only information the report contained.

faqs.question: When should we act on a low criterion score?
faqs.answer: Once a pattern repeats across two reporting cycles, because a single low score can be one bad task on one bad week. What is worth acting on immediately is a criterion low across several subjects at once — communication in mathematics, organising in Language and Literature, documentation in Design — because that is one structuring and self-management problem appearing in three places rather than three subject weaknesses, and fixing it once lifts all three.

faqs.question: Is an MYP tutor different from a Diploma tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the difference costs a term when it is ignored. Many tutors advertising IB experience mean the Diploma. Handed an MYP 3 student, a Diploma specialist adds depth — more content, harder examples, faster pace — which is good teaching aimed at the wrong target, because the MYP was asking for a justified generalisation or a documented process. The test takes fifteen seconds: ask them to name the four criteria for the subject group. A vague answer about criterion-based assessment is a no.

faqs.question: Which schools do Town Square MYP students attend?
faqs.answer: No MYP school sits inside Town Square, so every family here is driving. Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City runs the full continuum and is one of the shortest runs available. Others travel to Bradenton Preparatory Academy, Dubai International Academy in Al Barsha, GEMS Wellington Academy in Silicon Oasis, Nord Anglia International School Dubai or North London Collegiate School Dubai. We name these as local context and have no affiliation with any of them; the school matters because it sets the finish time.

faqs.question: Do Town Square MYP pupils also take Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These sit alongside the MYP, not inside it.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost for a Town Square family?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026: budget online from AED 33-65 an hour (Tutopiya, EdFlik), qualified online subject tutors AED 150-300 with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, IB specialists AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270, and in-home visits AED 180-500 including travel. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid and AED 1,000-2,000 plus for specialist work. The budget band is more viable at MYP than at Diploma for content help, but it cannot work to the criteria.

faqs.question: Would an in-home tutor suit a younger MYP child better?
faqs.answer: On presence, genuinely yes — somebody physically there can take a phone off the table and notice attention going, which matters more at eleven than at seventeen. On timing, no, and from Town Square the timing wins the argument. A visiting tutor leaving another part of Dubai in afternoon traffic arrives around half six, which is exactly when a younger MYP child stops absorbing. We make no UAE home visits in any case; in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only.

faqs.question: How do MYP sessions change during Ramadan here?
faqs.answer: They move, and younger students need the change more than Diploma students do. School days shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so the usual five o'clock slot often stops working entirely. Town Square families typically switch to a late-morning or early-afternoon session on shortened days, move older MYP students to post-Iftar, or pause part of the month and resume with a weekend block. Content should also shift towards consolidation rather than new material, which suits a shorter attention span better.

faqs.question: What should we do in MYP 5 to prepare for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Target the criteria that forecast trouble, which the report already names. A weak sciences processing and evaluating criterion predicts difficulty with the Diploma individual investigation, worth 20% of a science grade. Weak mathematics communication predicts lost marks in the Exploration. Weak critical thinking in Individuals and Societies predicts the Extended Essay. A short block in the second half of Year 11 or over the summer, aimed at one or two of those, costs a fraction of a Year 12 rescue and arrives before two years of content is built on the gap.

faqs.question: Might you tell us our child does not need tutoring?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it has happened more than once with MYP reports. A criterion profile that looks alarming to a parent coming from a percentage-based system sometimes describes a student doing perfectly well, with the unfamiliar scale being the actual problem. In that case we say so, which is the smallest possible sale. The other cases where we decline are a proposed session hour too late for the child's age, and situations where a conversation with the subject teacher is the right first step rather than a tutor.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-town-square.closingHeading: Send the year group, the door time and the report
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-town-square.closingBody: An IB MYP tutor in Town Square is only useful in an hour your child can still concentrate in, and that hour moves with age as much as with the school run. Send the MYP year, what time they actually reach home, and the actual criterion scores per subject, and we will tell you which window is workable, whether one criterion is dragging several subjects at once, and whether the Personal Project needs its own protected slot. Then a free trial lesson at that hour with the tutor who would continue. One-to-one over live video, with no UAE home visits.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.tutorsIntro: Middle Years enquiries from Umm Al Sheif usually name a grade rather than a topic: a five in Sciences, a four in Mathematics, a report comment nobody can decode. We match by subject group, because the four criteria in Sciences are not the four in Mathematics and a tutor needs the right set.

intro.heading: A grade of five is a message, and most families cannot read it
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme does not mark out of a hundred. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, labelled A to D, each scored from zero to eight. The four add to a maximum of thirty-two, and that total converts to a grade from one to seven using published boundaries. A child who comes home with a five has been told something precise, and almost no parent has been given the key to read it.

The precision is the useful part. A student scoring seven on criterion A and four on criterion D in Sciences is not a weak scientist; they know the material and cannot reflect on the impact of science in writing. Another student with the reverse profile has the opposite problem. Both appear as a five on a report card. The remedy for each is completely different, and generic revision helps neither.

That is why a Middle Years tutor has to be matched by subject group. The criteria are not generic. In Mathematics they are knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A tutor who does not know which four apply cannot explain a mark.

The second thing this page covers is the Personal Project, which arrives in the final Middle Years year and dominates it. It is assessed against three criteria of eight marks each, twenty-four in total, covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It is the student's own work from first idea to final report, and the single most common way families go wrong with it is by treating the product as the assessment when the process report is where the marks sit.

Umm Al Sheif sits in a well-served part of Dubai for continuum schools. Several schools within a short drive run the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes in one building, so a student here may move from Middle Years into the Diploma without changing school. That continuity is an advantage and it conceals a specific risk, which this page addresses: criteria-based assessment does not train a student for timed papers, and nobody tends to notice until the first Diploma assessment arrives.

IB Gram delivers to Umm Al Sheif as one-to-one teaching over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. What follows is the detail: how thirty-two marks become a grade, the four criteria in each subject group, the command terms inside the strands, the Personal Project, where marks are lost by subject, the handover into the Diploma, and what support costs here. Every figure carries the source it came from and the month it was read.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.programmesIntro: The Middle Years Programme spans five years and changes character substantially across them. Support that suits a Year 7 student is close to useless for a Year 11 one, which is why these are described by stage rather than as one programme.

programmes.name: Middle Years, the first two years
programmes.description: The transition out of primary inquiry into subject-specific criteria. Students meet eight subject groups, each with its own four criteria and its own vocabulary, and the volume of new expectations is the real difficulty rather than the content. The highest-value teaching here is reading a task sheet properly: which criterion is being assessed, and what the strand asks for.
programmes.countryNote: Year 7 and 8 students in Umm Al Sheif are generally home before 15:15 because journeys along this coast are short, and they carry the lightest homework load in the house. Thirty-minute sessions twice a week suit this stage far better than an hour, which is longer than most twelve-year-olds sustain on a single piece of written work.

programmes.name: Middle Years, the middle years
programmes.description: Content depth increases and so does the weight of criteria B and D, the investigative and evaluative strands, which is where strong recall stops being enough. Many schools run the community project in one of these two years. Students who learn to plan an investigation and write an evaluation here find the Personal Project and, later, Diploma Internal Assessments dramatically easier.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where Umm Al Sheif families most often first notice a problem, because grades stop tracking effort. A student working hard and still scoring fives is usually losing marks on one criterion consistently, and identifying which one takes a single session with two or three marked tasks in front of a specialist.

programmes.name: Middle Years, final year
programmes.description: The Personal Project year, assessed against three criteria of eight marks each. Some schools also enter students for MYP eAssessment, the optional on-screen examinations and ePortfolios that lead to the IB MYP Certificate, and many do not. Alongside that sit Diploma subject choices, including the mathematics route, which has consequences at university application.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Umm Suqeim and Al Safa cluster run the full continuum, so Umm Al Sheif students often move into the Diploma in the same building. Ask your school whether it enters candidates for eAssessment, because the answer changes what the final Middle Years year looks like and whether timed examination practice is already happening.

programmes.name: What the Middle Years Programme leads into
programmes.description: Six Diploma subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity Activity Service. The assessment model changes fundamentally: timed external papers carry most of the weight, with an Internal Assessment at around twenty per cent. Criteria-based skills transfer well to the Internal Assessment and not at all to the papers.
programmes.countryNote: The handover is where continuum students in Dubai most often stumble, and it is not about content. A student with consistent sixes on extended criteria-based tasks may never have sat a timed written paper. Three to five weeks of timed practice in the summer between the two programmes removes most of that shock, and it is the cheapest intervention of the whole five years.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.subjectsIntro: Each Middle Years subject group has its own four criteria, and those criteria are the whole assessment. Below is the set for each, with the strand that typically costs marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the usual loss: strong arithmetic students find the pattern and do not generalise it or justify the general rule, which is where most of the marks in that criterion sit.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The fourth criterion is the one students neglect, because it asks for discussion of science in context rather than for scientific content they have revised.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is where a well-informed essay scores a five: the student explains what happened thoroughly and never weighs competing interpretations or questions a source.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Organising is more mechanical than students expect and more valuable: a clear structure with signposted argument gains marks that fluent but shapeless writing does not, whatever the quality of the insight.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Four criteria across comprehending spoken and visual text, comprehending written and visual text, communicating, and using language. Phase placement matters enormously; a student in the wrong phase will look weak against criteria written for a different level of proficiency.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Students over-invest in creating the solution, which is one of four criteria, and under-invest in the research and evaluation that bracket it. The design folder is the assessment, not the finished object.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. The process journal carries a large share of the marks, and students who produce strong work without documenting their development score lower than students whose work is weaker and whose journal is thorough.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. Two of the four criteria are written rather than physical, which regularly surprises families whose child is athletic and receives a four.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Three criteria of eight marks each: planning, applying skills, and reflecting, totalling twenty-four. The product is not the assessment; the process report is. Students who build something impressive and write three pages about it score below students with a modest product and a rigorous account of their own learning.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed against their own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesising and evaluating. Students treat these as a double piece of homework and lose the marks specific to integration, which reward explaining how two subjects' perspectives combine rather than answering twice.

sections.heading: How thirty-two marks become a grade from one to seven
paragraphs: Each Middle Years subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, every one scored from zero to eight. The four are added to give a total out of thirty-two, and that total is converted into the final grade using published boundaries. The conversion is not linear in any intuitive sense, and the shape of it explains a great deal of parental confusion.

The boundaries are the part worth knowing. The band for a grade five is wide, which is why so many students sit in it for years and why a term of effort can produce no visible movement at all. The band for a grade seven is narrow and sits at the top of the range, which means reaching it requires consistency across all four criteria rather than brilliance in two.

That arithmetic has a direct consequence for how support should be bought. A student scoring seven, seven, six and four has twenty-four marks and a grade six. Lifting the weakest criterion by three points lifts the total to twenty-seven and may not change the grade at all; lifting it by four does. Meanwhile adding a point to an already strong criterion is harder work for less effect.

So the honest instruction is to find the lowest criterion and work only on that. It sounds obvious and almost nobody does it, because reports show grades rather than criterion scores. Ask the school for the criterion-level marks across the last two reporting cycles. They exist, they are recorded, and they are the single most useful document a Middle Years parent can hold.

sections.heading: The four criteria, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: This is the table every Middle Years parent should have on the fridge and almost none has. There are eight subject groups and each has its own four criteria with its own names. They are not variations on a theme; a criterion in Design has nothing in common with a criterion in Language Acquisition beyond being scored out of eight.

Reading across the table reveals the pattern that explains most unexpected grades. In nearly every subject group, criterion A rewards content knowledge and the later criteria reward process, investigation, communication and evaluation. Students who revise hard are optimising criterion A, which is a quarter of the marks. The other three quarters respond to different work entirely.

Two groups surprise families most. Physical and Health Education has two written criteria out of four, planning for performance and reflecting on performance, so an athletic child can receive a four. Arts awards a substantial share to the process journal, so a student producing strong work without documenting their development scores below a weaker student who documented thoroughly.

When you contact a tutor, name the subject group rather than the topic. A Sciences tutor needs to know the four criteria are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. If a tutor cannot list the four for the group you are asking about, they will not be able to explain a mark, which is the entire job.

sections.heading: Strands, command terms and the habit that fixes four subjects at once
paragraphs: Each criterion is broken into strands, and each strand opens with a command term: describe, explain, analyse, evaluate, justify, outline. The strand is the actual instruction, and the achievement level a student reaches depends on whether they did what the command term asked. A student who analyses where the strand said evaluate has written something competent that cannot reach the top band.

This is the highest-leverage teaching available in the Middle Years Programme, because the same command terms appear across every subject group. A student who learns the difference between explain and evaluate once improves in Sciences, in Individuals and Societies, in Language and Literature and in Mathematics simultaneously. Few interventions in education pay four times from one piece of work.

The method is mechanical rather than inspirational. Before writing, the student copies the strand wording at the top of the page and underlines its command term. Then they write the structure that term demands: for evaluate, a claim, evidence for, evidence against, and a judgement with a reason. Then the content goes into the structure. Three or four supervised attempts and the habit holds for years.

There is a second habit worth building alongside it: self-assessment. Have the student give themselves a level on each strand and say why, out loud, before any adult comment. They are usually too generous at first and accurate within a term. A student who can predict their own criterion score has internalised the standard, and that is the point at which tutoring can stop.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: twenty-four marks, and the product is not the point
paragraphs: The Personal Project arrives in the final Middle Years year and is assessed against three criteria of eight marks each, twenty-four in total, covering planning, applying skills and reflecting. It is the student's own work from the first idea to the final report, with a school supervisor who signs it off. For many Umm Al Sheif families it is the most stressful single piece of work of the five years.

The persistent misunderstanding is about what is being marked. Families and students focus on the product, the thing built, written, filmed or organised. The marks are in the process: whether the goal was defined with criteria for success, whether the plan was followed and adapted, whether the learning is evidenced, and whether the reflection is specific rather than sentimental.

That inversion explains the results every year. A student who builds something modest and keeps a rigorous process journal, with dated entries, abandoned approaches and honest problems, outscores a student who produced something impressive and wrote three pages about how much they enjoyed it. The journal is the evidence base for all three criteria, and it cannot be reconstructed afterwards.

A tutor's role here is narrow and genuinely valuable: narrow the goal until it is achievable, question whether the success criteria are measurable, ask what the journal actually evidences, and explain what each of the three criteria rewards. No tutor at IB Gram will produce the project, write the report or draft any part of it. The work must be the student's own, and the supervisor should know support exists.

sections.heading: Where Middle Years students lose marks, by subject group
paragraphs: The losses are patterned, and once a family can see the pattern the tutoring decision becomes obvious. Across subject groups, criterion A is the one students optimise, because it rewards content and content is what revision addresses. The marks sit elsewhere, in strands that reward investigation, structure, evaluation and reflection, and those are written skills rather than knowledge.

In Mathematics the recurring loss is in investigating patterns. A student finds the pattern, states the next term, and stops. The criterion wanted a general rule, expressed in algebra, with a justification of why it holds. That is a different activity from solving the problem, and it is taught rather than discovered. In Sciences the equivalent is reflecting on the impacts of science, which asks for discussion of context and is unrelated to anything revised for a test.

In Individuals and Societies the loss is thinking critically, where a thorough explanation of events scores a five because competing interpretations were never weighed and no source was questioned. In Language and Literature it is organising, which is more mechanical than students expect: signposted structure gains marks that fluent shapeless writing does not, whatever the insight behind it.

In Design and Arts the pattern inverts in an interesting way. Students over-invest in the visible output and under-invest in the folder or journal, where a large share of the assessment sits. The honest framing for a thirteen-year-old is that the evidence of thinking is the assessment, and the object is the proof that the thinking happened.

sections.heading: The handover from Middle Years into the Diploma
paragraphs: Continuum schools in the Umm Suqeim and Al Safa cluster let a student go from the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma without moving buildings, which removes a great deal of friction. It also conceals the one gap that matters, because the assessment model changes completely at that point and nothing in the final Middle Years year necessarily prepares a student for it.

Middle Years assessment is criteria-based, on extended tasks, usually with time and resources available. Diploma assessment is dominated by timed external papers, with an Internal Assessment at around twenty per cent. A student with consistent sixes on criteria-based work may never have produced correct work quickly under pressure, and the first Diploma assessment is where they find out.

The good news is that the transfer is excellent in one direction. Criteria-based skills map almost perfectly onto Diploma Internal Assessments, which are also marked against published criteria with mark allocations. A student who learned to read a strand and self-assess in the Middle Years Programme has a real advantage on the Internal Assessment that an IGCSE entrant does not.

So the bridge work is narrow: timed written practice, pacing, and command-term discipline under pressure. Three to five sessions in the final Middle Years term or the following summer is usually enough, and it is the cheapest useful tutoring in the whole five years because nothing else is competing for the student's hours at that point in the calendar.

sections.heading: What Middle Years support costs in Dubai, and when to buy it
paragraphs: Middle Years tutoring is cheaper than exam-year tutoring and more useful per dirham, which is the opposite of how families usually spend. The reason is simple: nothing is urgent, so the work can be slow and thorough, and the skills built are the same ones the Diploma will examine in two or three years. Buying criterion technique at thirteen is buying Internal Assessment marks at seventeen.

The Dubai market, with sources named, runs roughly as follows. University-student tutors online advertise from around AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik on their own published pages. A qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in.

For the Middle Years specifically, the middle band is usually right and the top band usually is not. What a student needs is somebody who can read a criterion strand and mark their work against it, which is a qualified-teacher skill rather than an examiner skill. The exception is the Personal Project, where a few hours of experienced supervision at the start can change all three criteria at once.

One piece of context on the wider budget. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is therefore the variable line this year, which is an argument for spending it early on criterion technique rather than late on exam rescue.

sections.heading: Umm Al Sheif practicalities and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Middle Years students tire earlier than Diploma students, and that single fact should drive scheduling. Umm Al Sheif helps here: journeys along this coast are short, most children are home between 14:45 and 15:45, and a 16:30 start is realistic. For a Year 7 or Year 8 student, two half-hour sessions a week at that hour will outperform a single hour, which is longer than most twelve-year-olds sustain on written work.

Fridays are worth naming. Dubai private schools generally finish between 12:00 and 12:30 on a Friday and the weekend runs Saturday and Sunday, so Saturday morning is the one time in the week a Middle Years student is genuinely rested. Extended tasks and Personal Project work belong there rather than at the end of a long weekday.

On the academic-honesty line, the Middle Years Programme is where habits form, which makes the boundary more important than at any later stage. A tutor may teach content, read criteria with a student, question a plan, ask what the journal evidences and explain why a paragraph is weak. Nobody at IB Gram writes a Personal Project, drafts a report or produces any assessed work in any subject group.

Finally, what this page does not claim. No regulator, examination board or school endorses IB Gram. KHDA, which oversees private education in Dubai, is named to explain what it does. Every dirham figure carries its source and the month it was read. There is no UAE office, no self-generated rating and no statistic without its method, and we would rather be judged on that than on a number nobody can check.
