process.title: Send the subject group and the criterion scores
process.description: Not maths, but Mathematics with the four criterion scores from the last two reporting cycles. The school records them and will supply them on request. Those eight numbers identify the problem in two minutes, which is faster and more accurate than any conversation about how your child is finding the subject.

process.title: Send two marked tasks
process.description: Two task sheets with the teacher's criterion levels on them tell us whether the loss is consistent in one strand or scattered. A consistent single-strand loss is a four-session fix. A scattered pattern usually means a content gap underneath, which is a different engagement with a different timescale.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One per family, before payment and with no card details taken. Ask the tutor to name the four criteria for your child's subject group. If they cannot, they cannot explain a mark, which is the whole job. Then check whether your child could say what their own work deserved and why.

process.title: Work on one criterion at a time
process.description: Pick the lowest criterion and work only on that until it moves. Spreading effort across all four produces a total that shifts by two or three marks and a grade that does not change. Lifting one weak strand by four points is what crosses a boundary, and it is a narrower job than it sounds.

process.title: Stop when the student can self-assess
process.description: The target is a student who can give themselves a level on each strand and be right. At that point the standard is internalised and tutoring has done its work. We will tell you when we think you are there, because an engagement that continues past its usefulness is a cost without a return.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject group, not by subject
whyPoints.description: The four criteria in Sciences are not the four in Mathematics or in Design. A tutor who does not know which four apply cannot explain why a mark was given, so we match by group and ask tutors to name the criteria before they are offered a student.

whyPoints.title: Criterion scores, not grades
whyPoints.description: A grade five is a wide band and tells you almost nothing. The four criterion scores tell you everything. We ask for them first, and we will show you how to get them from the school if nobody has offered them, because they are recorded for every assessed task.

whyPoints.title: One criterion at a time
whyPoints.description: Effort spread across four criteria moves a total by a few marks and a grade by none. Lifting the single weakest strand by three or four points is what crosses a boundary. That is a narrower and cheaper job than general subject tutoring, and we plan for it explicitly.

whyPoints.title: Built for the handover, not just for this term
whyPoints.description: Criterion technique learned at thirteen is Internal Assessment marks at seventeen, because Diploma Internal Assessments are also criterion-marked. We teach with that in mind and we say plainly which Middle Years skills do not transfer: pacing and timed performance.

whyPoints.title: Rates from the market with sources
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure here belongs to a named provider or a published rate table with the month it was read, and none is presented as our price. For the Middle Years the middle band is usually right, and we will say so rather than sell you the top one.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project boundary in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor narrows the goal, questions the plan and asks what the journal evidences. Nobody at IB Gram produces a Personal Project or drafts its report, and the school supervisor should know support exists. Habits form at this age, which makes the line matter more here than later.

faqs.question: What should an IB MYP tutor in Umm Al Sheif be able to do in the first session?
faqs.answer: Name the four criteria for your child's subject group from memory, read one of your child's marked tasks against the relevant strands, and say which single criterion is costing the grade. If a tutor talks about the subject in general rather than about criteria, they cannot explain a mark, and explaining marks is the entire job in the Middle Years Programme. Ask them to list criteria A to D for the group before you book anything; it takes thirty seconds.

faqs.question: Why has my child been a grade five in every subject for two years?
faqs.answer: Because the band for a five is wide. The four criteria each score out of eight, totalling thirty-two, and a five covers roughly nineteen to twenty-three marks. A term of real improvement can move a total by two points and leave the grade untouched, which is demoralising and also diagnostic. Ask the school for the criterion-level scores. Almost always one strand is sitting at four while others sit at six or seven, and that one strand is the whole problem.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an MYP tutor to a home in Umm Al Sheif?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Middle Years lessons for Umm Al Sheif families are one to one over live video, working from your child's own task sheets and the published criteria on screen. Market rates for in-home visits in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in, and if you want somebody physically present you want a different provider.

faqs.question: How do the four MYP criteria differ between subjects?
faqs.answer: Completely, beyond each being scored out of eight. Mathematics uses knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Sciences uses knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Design uses inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. There are eight subject groups and eight sets, which is why matching by group rather than by topic matters.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion do strong students lose marks on most often?
faqs.answer: Whichever one rewards process rather than content, and it varies by group. In Mathematics it is investigating patterns, where a student finds the pattern and never generalises or justifies a rule. In Sciences it is reflecting on the impacts of science, which revision does not touch. In Individuals and Societies it is thinking critically, where thorough explanation scores a five because interpretations were never weighed. Criterion A rewards content, and content is the quarter that revision already covers.

faqs.question: Is the MYP Personal Project marked on what my daughter builds?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the single most common misunderstanding of the final Middle Years year. The three criteria, each worth eight marks, cover planning, applying skills and reflecting, with the process journal as the evidence base for all three. The product demonstrates the goal was met and nothing more. A modest product with a rigorous dated journal outscores an impressive product with three pages of enjoyment, every year, in every school.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful help is narrow. Narrow the goal until it is achievable, insist the success criteria are measurable, ask what the journal actually evidences for each of the three criteria, and explain what each criterion rewards. Nobody at IB Gram produces the project or drafts the report; the work is the student's own from first idea to final submission. The school supervisor signs it off and should know outside support exists.

faqs.question: Do the Umm Suqeim continuum schools use MYP eAssessment in the final year?
faqs.answer: Some Dubai schools do and many do not, so ask yours directly. eAssessment is the optional set of on-screen examinations and ePortfolios in the final Middle Years year that leads to the IB MYP Certificate. The answer changes what that year looks like substantially: a school that enters candidates is already building timed examination practice, and a school that does not is relying entirely on criteria-based coursework, which leaves a gap before the Diploma.

faqs.question: How hard is the jump from MYP 5 into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The content step is manageable; the assessment step catches continuum students specifically. Middle Years work is criterion-marked on extended tasks, usually with time and resources available. Diploma grades are dominated by timed external papers. A student with consistent sixes may never have produced correct work quickly under pressure. Three to five weeks of timed section practice in the final Middle Years term or the following summer removes most of that shock and is the cheapest useful tutoring of the five years.

faqs.question: Do MYP skills help at all in the Diploma, or is it a fresh start?
faqs.answer: They help substantially in one direction. Diploma Internal Assessments are also marked against published criteria with stated mark allocations, so a student who learned to read a strand and self-assess in the Middle Years Programme arrives with a real advantage that an IGCSE entrant does not have. Extended written investigation transfers equally well to science investigations, mathematics explorations and the Extended Essay. What does not transfer is pacing and performance under timed conditions.

faqs.question: What session length suits a Year 7 or Year 8 student in Umm Al Sheif?
faqs.answer: Thirty to forty minutes, twice a week, rather than a single hour. Middle Years students tire earlier than Diploma students, and written craft work degrades quickly once attention goes. The short school journeys along this coast make that schedulable: most children here are home between 14:45 and 15:45, so a 16:30 start is realistic. Save extended tasks and project work for Saturday morning, the one time in a Dubai week a student is genuinely rested.

faqs.question: How do I get the criterion scores out of the school?
faqs.answer: Ask for them in writing, by subject, for the last two reporting cycles. They are recorded for every assessed task, so the request is routine rather than awkward. What you want is the A, B, C and D level for each task, not the converted grade. Eight numbers across two cycles will usually show one strand consistently three or four points below the others, and that is the entire tutoring brief, identified before you have spent anything.

faqs.question: Should we work on all four criteria or just the weakest one?
faqs.answer: Just the weakest, and this is counter-intuitive enough that most families get it wrong. The total out of thirty-two converts to a grade through bands, so lifting one strand from four to seven adds three marks and may cross a boundary, while adding a mark to each of four strands adds four marks and often changes nothing meaningful. Work on one strand until it moves, verify against a marked task, then choose the next lowest.

faqs.question: Is Middle Years tutoring worth paying for when there are no exams?
faqs.answer: It is the best value in the five years, for two reasons. Nothing is urgent, so the work can be slow and thorough rather than rushed. And criterion technique learned at thirteen is Internal Assessment marks at seventeen, because Diploma Internal Assessments use the same kind of published criteria. Published Dubai rates for a qualified subject tutor online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and the middle band is almost always the right one at this stage.

faqs.question: Is Design or Arts harder to staff than Maths for an Umm Al Sheif slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than offering a generalist. Mathematics, Sciences, Language and Literature and Individuals and Societies are usually matched within a few days. Design, Arts and specific Language Acquisition phases are narrower, and occasionally nobody suitable is free at your hour. Hearing that honestly is more useful than discovering in session two that the tutor is reading the criteria for the first time, which is the point at which the money has already gone.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.closingHeading: Ask the school for the criterion scores
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-umm-al-sheif.closingBody: Before you buy anything, send one email asking for your child's A, B, C and D levels in each subject across the last two reporting cycles. Those numbers almost always show a single strand sitting three or four points below the rest, and that strand is the whole brief. Send them to us with two marked task sheets and we will tell you which criterion is costing the grade and roughly how many sessions moving it takes. Then your child meets a specialist in that subject group on a free trial lesson, live online, one to one.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work in the MYP subject groups Umm Suqeim families ask about: Mathematics, Sciences, Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies and Language Acquisition, across MYP 1 to MYP 5.

intro.heading: The verification problem nobody warns MYP parents about
paragraphs: There is a practical reason MYP parents in Umm Suqeim struggle to choose a tutor, and it has nothing to do with how many are available. With an IGCSE subject you can test somebody in five minutes: ask which board, which syllabus code, which tier, what each paper is worth. Those facts are public, checkable and specific, and a tutor who does not know them has disqualified themselves. The MYP offers none of that. There are no past papers, no syllabus codes, no published paper weightings and no tier. There is a framework, and a tutor either understands it or does not, and from the outside the two look identical.

That is why the usual advice - ask about their experience, look at reviews, see if your child likes them - fails here more than anywhere else in the market. A tutor can be an excellent mathematician and a strong teacher and still be no use for MYP Mathematics, because MYP Mathematics is marked against four criteria with published descriptors and a task-specific clarification written by the teacher for that unit, and a tutor who teaches content without reading the clarification is marking a different exercise from the one the school is marking.

So this page is a verification toolkit rather than a sales page. It tells you which four documents to request from the school and what each one reveals. It explains the programme vocabulary - key concepts, related concepts, global contexts, statements of inquiry, Approaches to Learning - that appears in every unit planner and almost never in a conversation with a parent. It gives you an interview that works in the absence of a past paper. And it covers the one decision the MYP builds towards, which is what happens at the end of MYP 5.

On availability, the honest picture for this area. International Baccalaureate schools account for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, in a market of 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula. The MYP is a minority programme inside that minority, and the pool of tutors who have genuinely taught it is correspondingly small and distributed by where the IB schools are - Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Emirates Hills - rather than by residential street. Requiring one of them to also be near Umm Suqeim at 5pm on a Tuesday is how a request becomes unfillable.

IB Gram therefore teaches Umm Suqeim students one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer in India only. For MYP work the trade is especially favourable, because the material is the school's own unit documents and the student's own marked tasks, all of which share better on a screen than across a table.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.programmesIntro: The MYP is the middle five years of the IB continuum and the only stage where the assessment language is entirely internal. Understanding where it sits explains why its tutoring works differently from the stages either side of it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary and inquiry-led, with descriptive reporting and no external assessment, closing with the Year 6 Exhibition. Children leave the PYP able to ask good questions and frequently without the writing volume that MYP criteria will start demanding in Year 7.
programmes.countryNote: Several PYP schools serve families in Umm Suqeim and along the coast. The useful thing a parent can do in Year 5 or 6 is build writing stamina, because the volume expected by MYP Criterion C in Language and Literature catches PYP children out far more often than the content does.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade by school-set boundaries. Units are built around key concepts, related concepts and global contexts, with Approaches to Learning skills taught across subjects. MYP 5 includes the Personal Project and, at some schools, eAssessment.
programmes.countryNote: This is the programme in your search. Around Umm Suqeim the MYP sits beside British-curriculum schools running IGCSE in the same year groups, which means local advice about tutors, revision guides and past papers is usually advice about a different system entirely.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored out of 45 points. Assessment becomes largely external, with Internal Assessments carrying around a fifth of most subject grades. UAE schools sit the May session.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP's reflective and investigative criteria map directly onto DP Internal Assessment demands, which makes a student's MYP criterion profile a genuine predictor of how they will handle DP coursework. That is a more useful conversation in MYP 4 than in the week option forms are due.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Rare in Dubai and worth checking against the current KHDA school listing rather than an older guide, since availability shifts year to year.
programmes.countryNote: Where it is offered within reach of Umm Suqeim, the MYP Personal Project turns out to be good preparation for the CP reflective project, because both are assessed on documented process rather than on a finished artefact. The same academic-honesty boundary applies to both.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.subjectsIntro: The MYP's eight subject groups each carry four criteria. Below are the groups, with the criterion that most often holds a student back in each - which is the information a tutor needs before a first session.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating patterns, C Communicating, D Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. B asks for a conjecture tested and generalised; D asks for a real model built and then criticised. Fluent students stall on both because neither rewards getting the answer.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Inquiring and designing, C Processing and evaluating, D Reflecting on the impacts of science. D is the most common low mark across Dubai MYP cohorts because the ethical and global dimension is the part a crowded scheme of work covers last.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.levels: English, Arabic and other school languages
subjects.description: Criteria A Analysing, B Organizing, C Producing text, D Using language. Confident readers score on A and lose B, because their essays have insight and no visible structure. C and D separate craft from accuracy, so a stylish error-strewn piece drops only on D.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria A Comprehending spoken and visual text, B Comprehending written and visual text, C Communicating, D Using language. Phase placement matters more than year group, and a child advanced a phase too early looks weak on all four criteria when the real issue is placement.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Investigating, C Communicating, D Thinking critically. D separates the top grades: it wants sources interrogated, perspectives weighed and limitations named, which is a different activity from knowing more.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria A Inquiring and analysing, B Developing ideas, C Creating the solution, D Evaluating. The design cycle is the assessment, so a student who builds something impressive and documents nothing keeps C and loses the other three. Thinly staffed by tutors anywhere in Dubai.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Developing skills, C Thinking creatively, D Responding. The process journal is the evidence base for B and C, and a missing journal caps the grade whatever the finished work looks like.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria A Knowing and understanding, B Planning for performance, C Applying and performing, D Reflecting and improving performance. Able athletes routinely score at the top on C and near the bottom on B and D, because both are written tasks treated as paperwork.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed on the synthesis of two or more subject groups against their own criteria. Schools run them very differently, so the task-specific clarification is essential rather than helpful - assuming it mirrors a single-subject rubric is a reliable way to lose marks.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Criteria A Planning, B Applying skills, C Reflecting, assessed on the process journal and report rather than on the product. A tutor may teach project management, questioning and reflective writing; the project and every word of the report must be the student's own.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-umm-suqeim.regionsTitle: Umm Suqeim and where the MYP actually is

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Three sections of villas with a mix of British-curriculum and IB gates. MYP families here are a minority among IGCSE neighbours, which is why a well-meaning recommendation from the street is statistically likely to be for a different assessment system.

regions.note: Inland across Al Wasl Road, with an IB continuum school among its British-curriculum gates. A good illustration of how two schools a few streets apart can run entirely different assessment frameworks and different report-card languages.

regions.name: Jumeirah 2 and 3
regions.note: The strip towards town feeding several of the same gates, with a similar MYP density to Umm Suqeim. The two areas share the same shortage of MYP-literate tutors and the same solution to it.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: A dense school cluster inland of Sheikh Zayed Road including IB Diploma and continuum provision. Umm Suqeim students at these gates have the longest commute, which pushes a realistic session start past 5pm.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows

sections.heading: The four documents that make MYP tutoring possible
paragraphs: An IB MYP tutor in Umm Suqeim cannot work from a past paper, because none exists. What they can work from is the school's own documentation, and most parents do not know it exists or that they are entitled to ask for it. The table below lists the four documents worth requesting, what each one is, and what it reveals. Gathering them takes one email and makes the difference between criterion-level teaching and general subject revision.

The most important of the four is the task-specific clarification. For each summative task, the teacher rewrites the generic criterion descriptors in the language of that particular unit: what 'investigating patterns' means for this specific investigation, what counts as a justified conclusion in this context. It is the document the marking was actually done against, and a tutor who has it can explain a lost mark precisely. A tutor who does not have it is guessing, however well they know the subject.

The second is the unit planner or its summary, which names the key concept, the related concepts, the global context and the statement of inquiry for the unit. Those four things frame everything the student is being asked to do, and they are the reason an MYP question can look like it is about one thing while being assessed on another. The third is the marked summative itself, with the teacher's comments and the criterion marks awarded. The fourth is the school's grade boundary table, which converts the raw total out of 32 into the 1-7 grade on the report.

Schools generally share all four willingly when asked for a specific reason. Ask by email, name the unit, and say you want to support your child's work at home. Where a school declines, the marked task and the report card alone still support useful work, but the first session will spend time on reconstruction that the clarification grid would have made unnecessary.

sections.heading: The vocabulary every MYP unit is built on, in plain terms
paragraphs: Four words appear in every MYP unit planner and almost never in a conversation with a parent: key concept, related concept, global context and statement of inquiry. They are not decoration. They determine what a task is assessing, which is why a student can produce a technically correct piece of work and score in the middle.

A key concept is one of sixteen broad ideas the programme uses to connect subjects - change, systems, relationships, identity, form, logic, perspective, time place and space, and so on. A related concept is subject-specific and narrower: in Sciences, something like evidence or function; in Mathematics, something like representation or generalisation. A global context is one of six framings that give the unit its real-world purpose: identities and relationships; orientation in space and time; personal and cultural expression; scientific and technical innovation; globalization and sustainability; and fairness and development. A statement of inquiry is a single sentence combining the key concept, the related concepts and the global context, and it is the sentence the whole unit answers.

Here is why it matters practically. A Sciences unit with the key concept 'change', related concept 'transformation' and the global context 'scientific and technical innovation' will set a task whose top-band descriptor rewards explaining a transformation in an innovation context - not reciting the chemistry. A student who writes an excellent account of the reaction and never addresses the context scores exactly as the descriptor says they should, which is lower than their knowledge deserves. The parent sees an unfair mark. The teacher sees a student who did not answer the inquiry.

The fifth piece of vocabulary is Approaches to Learning, and it is covered in the next section. Together, these five terms are what a tutor must be fluent in to be useful in the MYP. A tutor who cannot say what a global context is, or who treats the statement of inquiry as a title, is going to teach good lessons on the wrong target - which is the specific failure this page exists to help you avoid.

sections.heading: Approaches to Learning: the skills marked inside subject criteria
paragraphs: The MYP teaches five categories of Approaches to Learning skills - communication, social, self-management, research and thinking - broken into clusters such as collaboration, organisation, affective skills, reflection, information literacy, media literacy, critical thinking, creative thinking and transfer. They are not a separate subject and usually do not appear as a separate grade. They are taught across subjects and then assessed inside subject criteria, which is why a student can be marked down for something nobody ever called a subject.

The table below maps the categories onto where they actually cost marks. A student with weak self-management loses Criterion B marks in Design and Arts because the process journal is thin. A student with weak research skills loses Criterion B in Individuals and Societies because sources are collected rather than selected. A student with weak thinking-skill development loses the top band of Criterion D almost everywhere, because every subject group's D criterion asks for some version of evaluation, reflection or critical judgement.

This is the single most useful idea for a parent reading an MYP report card for the first time. If the same criterion letter is low across several unrelated subjects, the problem is almost certainly an Approaches to Learning skill rather than four separate subject weaknesses. Low D marks in Sciences, Individuals and Societies and Mathematics together point at critical thinking and reflection, not at a child who happens to be bad at three things. One tutor working on that skill inside one subject often lifts the others, which is both cheaper and more effective than three subject tutors.

It also explains why MYP tutoring sometimes looks unlike tutoring. A session spent teaching a student how to keep a usable process journal, or how to interrogate a source rather than summarise it, or how to write a reflection that names a specific decision and its consequence, is subject teaching in the MYP's terms even though no content was covered. A parent expecting content coverage should be told that in advance rather than left wondering what they paid for.

sections.heading: How to interview an MYP tutor when there is no paper to test them on
paragraphs: Without syllabus codes and paper weightings, verification has to rest on programme vocabulary and on how the tutor proposes to start. The useful questions are few and the answers are hard to fake. Ask what the four criteria are for the subject group in question; a tutor who has taught it names them, and a tutor who has not gives a plausible paraphrase. Ask what a global context is; the answer is either immediate or it is not. Ask what they would want from the school before the first lesson; the right answer is the clarification grid and the marked summative, and anything else is a tutor who intends to teach their own scheme.

Then ask two questions about judgement. What would you do if my child's grade is a 5 with criterion marks of 7, 7, 6 and 2? The answer should be that the three high marks are not the problem and the single 2 is, and that the first job is to find out whether that criterion is weak in other subjects too. And what will you do about the Personal Project? The answer should name the boundary unprompted: teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own journal and report, with no drafting, rewriting or editing of any part of it.

One answer should end the conversation. If a tutor says they are IB approved, IB certified or IB accredited, that is not a status available to private tutors - the IB authorises schools to deliver its programmes, not individuals or companies to tutor them. Nor do KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education approve individual tutors; KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, which is a different thing entirely. A tutor who claims any of this is either careless about a claim a UAE regulator takes seriously or is repeating marketing they have not examined.

Finally, ask about the permit that does apply. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the service as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing'. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any amount circulating online is unverified.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs, and why the market is built for a different product
paragraphs: The Dubai tutoring market is built around examination boards, and that shapes what your money buys. Published budget rates start at AED 33-52 an hour from Tutopiya and AED 45-65 from EdFlik, and at that level the product is supervision and question-bank drilling. For an IGCSE student that has real value. For an MYP student it has almost none, because there are no past papers to drill and the marks are awarded against descriptors the tutor has not read. This is the clearest case of genuinely wasted spending in this market, and it is the one families in Umm Suqeim fall into most often because the price looks like a sensible first step.

The band that works for MYP is the qualified subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, rising into the specialist band at AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai guidance putting specialists at AED 200-450 or more. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650 - and examiner status is close to meaningless for the MYP, since the assessment is internal and teacher-marked. In-home visits run AED 180-500 with travel included, Bestimate quoting AED 180-350.

In monthly terms, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with advertised packages at AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Set against school fees, which KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, one subject group at the mid band is a modest addition and three is not.

The MYP-specific buying advice is therefore unusually simple. Pay for criterion literacy, which lives in the middle band, and do not pay for examiner credentials or question banks, which are products designed for a different assessment system. Ask what the rate buys per 60 minutes, whether VAT is included, what the cancellation terms are, and whether the tutor will work from your school's clarification grid. Every figure above is another provider's published rate read during the October 2026 research round, quoted as market context rather than as an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: The end of MYP 5: eAssessment, and choosing the next route
paragraphs: Two things happen at the end of MYP 5 and families often conflate them. The first is eAssessment, which not every MYP school in Dubai enters students for. Where a school does enter, MYP 5 results come from a mixture of on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios alongside the Personal Project, leading to the MYP Certificate. Where a school does not, MYP 5 ends with internal reporting and the student moves on without an external MYP result. Ask your MYP coordinator which applies, because it changes what Year 11 should look like.

This page deliberately publishes no certificate point threshold. The requirements for the MYP Certificate should come from the IB or from the school's coordinator rather than from a tutoring page, and the same applies to session and results dates: UAE schools sit the May session, and ibo.org is the only place to confirm specifics. Several pages in this market quote IB dates confidently from secondary sources, and a date a parent acts on is not a detail to get approximately right.

The second thing is the route decision - Diploma Programme, A Levels, or another option - and this is where a student's five-year criterion profile earns its keep. Strong investigation and reflection marks travel well into DP Internal Assessments, because the demands are structurally similar: a question framed, a method justified, data handled honestly, limitations named. A student carrying consistent 3s and 4s on reflective criteria will find the DP's coursework load heavier than its content, and that is worth knowing in MYP 4 rather than discovering in DP1.

The useful tutoring contribution here is evidence rather than advice. A tutor can say what the criterion profile suggests about coursework readiness and can teach the skills that close the gap. The decision itself belongs to the family, the school and the IB coordinator who knows the child, and any provider framing tutoring as necessary for progression has invented an urgency the programme does not contain.

sections.heading: Starting from Umm Suqeim, and the limits worth knowing first
paragraphs: Begin by gathering documents rather than by booking anything. Request the task-specific clarification for the most recent summative, the unit overview, the marked task itself and the grade boundary table. Send us the subject group, the year, the criterion marks from the latest report and whatever the school provides. From that we can tell you whether you need subject teaching, criterion technique or an Approaches to Learning skill, and those are three different tutors rather than three amounts of the same one.

Then the usual sequence: we match on subject group and MYP experience, you take a full-length trial lesson at no cost with your child's own marked task on screen, and you judge whether the tutor talks in criterion and descriptor language or in topics. Sessions run weekly in Gulf Standard Time, usually from 5pm for a student commuting back to Umm Suqeim from Al Sufouh or Al Barsha. Ramadan timings move to post-Iftar slots, and sessions can pause through a heavy summative week.

The disclosure. MYP Design, MYP Arts and several Language Acquisition phases are thinly covered by tutors anywhere in Dubai, and a request in those areas may be answered with a waiting position rather than a tutor. Interdisciplinary units are harder again, because the assessment varies so much between schools. We would rather say that than place somebody who is learning the framework alongside your child while you pay specialist rates. No competitor page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit at all, which is informative in itself.

And the fixed limits. No home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. No claimed approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson - IB Gram holds none, and a provider claiming any of them should worry you. No writing, drafting, rewriting or editing of a Personal Project, a journal, an Internal Assessment or any assessed work. No reproduction of IB documents; we reference and link the official sources and work from your school's own materials. No grade promises, and no statistics about our own outcomes without the sample, date and method that would make them mean anything.

faqs.question: How can I check that an MYP tutor really knows the programme if there are no past papers?
faqs.answer: Test the vocabulary and the proposed starting point. Ask them to name the four criteria for your child's subject group; someone who has taught it names them, and someone who has not produces a plausible paraphrase. Ask what a global context is - the answer is immediate or it is not. Then ask what they want from the school before lesson one. The right answer is the task-specific clarification and the marked summative. A tutor who wants nothing intends to teach their own scheme, which in a programme with no past papers means teaching a plausible version of somebody else's task.

faqs.question: What is a task-specific clarification and how do I get one?
faqs.answer: It is the document the marking was actually done against. For each summative task the teacher rewrites the generic criterion descriptors in the language of that unit: what investigating patterns means for this particular investigation, what counts as a justified conclusion here. Email the subject teacher, name the unit and the task, and say you want to support your child's work at home; schools generally share it. Without it, a tutor explaining a lost mark is guessing however well they know the subject. With it, the explanation becomes specific and the next draft can be aimed at something real.

faqs.question: What is a statement of inquiry and why does it change my child's mark?
faqs.answer: It is a single sentence combining the unit's key concept, its related concepts and its global context, and it is the sentence the whole unit answers. The top-band descriptors for a task are written against it. So a student can produce a technically excellent piece of work that never addresses the inquiry and score in the middle - the mark is correct and the knowledge was not the problem. Parents read that as unfair marking. Teachers read it as a student who answered a different question. Knowing the statement of inquiry before the task is written prevents the whole situation.

faqs.question: The same criterion letter is low in three different subjects. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly an Approaches to Learning skill rather than three subject weaknesses. The MYP teaches communication, social, self-management, research and thinking skills across subjects and then assesses them inside subject criteria. Low D marks in Sciences, Individuals and Societies and Mathematics together point at critical thinking and reflection. Thin process journals in Design, Arts and Physical and Health Education point at self-management. The practical consequence is encouraging: one tutor working on that skill inside one subject group usually lifts the others, which costs far less than three subject tutors.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be IB approved for MYP work?
faqs.answer: No. The IB authorises schools to deliver its programmes; it does not approve, accredit or certify private tutors or tutoring companies for the MYP or for anything else. KHDA, ADEK, the Sharjah Private Education Authority and the Ministry of Education do not approve individual tutors either - KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises, which requires initial approval and annual renewal and is a licence for an organisation with a physical location. The permit that applies to an individual tutor in the UAE is MoHRE's private tuition work permit. IB Gram claims none of these approvals.

faqs.question: Is budget tutoring ever a sensible starting point for MYP?
faqs.answer: Less often than for IGCSE, and this is worth knowing before you spend. Published budget rates in Dubai start around AED 33-52 an hour from Tutopiya and AED 45-65 from EdFlik, and what they buy is supervision and question-bank drilling. The MYP has no question bank, and the marks are awarded against descriptors the tutor has not read. For a child who simply will not sit down to work, supervision still has value. For a criterion problem it has close to none, which makes it the clearest case of wasted spending in this part of the market.

faqs.question: Does examiner experience matter for an MYP tutor?
faqs.answer: Very little, and a provider leading with it has misunderstood the programme. MYP assessment is internal and teacher-marked against published criteria, with task-specific clarifications written by the classroom teacher. There is no external paper for an examiner to have marked in the sense that applies to IGCSE or the Diploma Programme. What matters instead is whether the tutor has taught the subject group's criteria, can read a clarification grid, and knows how a raw total out of 32 converts to a 1-7 grade at your school. Premium rates of AED 500-650 buy scarcity and reputation rather than relevant skill here.

faqs.question: My child has moved into MYP from a British-curriculum school mid-year. What breaks first?
faqs.answer: Process documentation. A student arriving from a system that rewards correct answers writes the answer and stops, which scores on Criterion A and nothing else. The MYP's investigation and reflection criteria want the working visible: a conjecture tested across cases, a method someone else could follow, a reflection naming a specific decision and its consequence. The content is rarely the problem for a transferring student. The first useful intervention is reading three exemplars at different bands against the criterion descriptors, which often moves a band without any content teaching at all.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups are hardest to find a tutor for in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Design and Arts are the thinnest, followed by several Language Acquisition phases and by interdisciplinary units, where the assessment varies so widely between schools that experience at one school transfers poorly to another. Mathematics, Sciences and Language and Literature are the easiest to cover. Where a combination is genuinely hard to staff, the honest answers are a waiting position, a tutor in the same subject group who can work on the specific criterion, or no. We would rather say that than place somebody learning the framework alongside your child at specialist rates.

faqs.question: How much of a Personal Project can a tutor legitimately touch?
faqs.answer: The teaching and none of the writing. A tutor may teach goal setting, research method, project management and reflective writing, may ask the questions a supervisor will ask, and may explain what Criteria A, B and C reward - the project is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting through the process journal and report rather than on the product. A tutor may not write or draft the report, write journal entries, build the product or edit a submission into shape. IB academic-honesty rules place the consequence on the student, who authenticates the work, so agree this boundary explicitly in the first session.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether MYP 5 at our Umm Suqeim school ends in eAssessment?
faqs.answer: Not every MYP school in Dubai does, so ask the MYP coordinator rather than assume. Where a school enters, MYP 5 results come from on-screen examinations and moderated ePortfolios alongside the Personal Project and lead to the MYP Certificate. Where it does not, MYP 5 ends with internal reporting and the student moves on without an external result. It changes what Year 11 should contain: an entered cohort needs timed on-screen practice, while a non-entered cohort is better served by strengthening the criterion habits the Diploma Programme will demand. Confirm any session detail on ibo.org.

faqs.question: What does the MYP criterion profile tell us about readiness for the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: More than the overall grades do. DP Internal Assessments ask for a question framed, a method justified, data handled honestly and limitations named - which is structurally what the MYP's investigation and reflection criteria reward. A student with consistently strong B and D marks across subject groups tends to handle DP coursework well even if their content grades are middling. A student carrying 3s and 4s on reflective criteria will find the DP's coursework load heavier than its content. That is a conversation worth having in MYP 4, not in the week option forms are due.

faqs.question: How long before a criterion mark actually moves?
faqs.answer: Usually one summative cycle for technique criteria and two for the reflective ones. Criterion C, which rewards how clearly reasoning is communicated, often moves after a single round of exemplar work because the student simply did not know what the top band looked like. Criteria B and D take longer, because investigating properly and thinking critically are habits rather than formats. Expect to judge progress over six to eight weeks against a new summative in the same subject group, and expect the overall grade to lag the criterion by a reporting cycle. If nothing has moved after a full block, change something.

faqs.question: What time can an MYP session start for a student travelling back to Umm Suqeim?
faqs.answer: Allow 5pm, and later if the gate is in Al Barsha or Emirates Hills. Secondary release across the Dubai schools corridor runs roughly from 2:45pm to 3:30pm, and a student returning to Umm Suqeim from Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or further inland arrives between about 3:55pm and 4:35pm. Changing, food and a break take the rest, so the usable window opens near 5pm and closes around 6:45pm. Delivering over live video keeps that window whole, since nothing in the arrangement depends on how Sheikh Zayed Road happens to be moving.

faqs.question: Should we buy tutoring for more than one MYP subject group at once?
faqs.answer: Rarely. The MYP already fills a week with eight subject groups plus the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies requirements that apply in all Dubai private schools, so there is little slack to spend. More importantly, if several criterion marks are low the cause is usually a shared Approaches to Learning skill, and working on it inside one subject group transfers to the others. Two subject groups is occasionally right where the content gaps are genuinely separate. Three weekly sessions, in a programme this full, usually means three sessions attended with nothing done between them.

A tutor who names the four criteria, defines a global context without pausing and asks for the clarification grid has taught the programme. Send the criterion marks and the marked task, take a free trial lesson, and listen for descriptor language. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-villanova.tutorsIntro: The MYP specialists matched to Villanova families start from the task sheet and the criterion descriptors rather than from a textbook chapter. You meet yours in a free trial lesson, with your child's last two pieces of marked work on the screen.

intro.heading: The MYP is marked on criteria, and that is what a tutor must know
paragraphs: The honest answer to 'is there anyone near me in Villanova who knows this syllabus' is that the Middle Years Programme does not have a syllabus in the sense parents expect. There is no content list to drill and no past-paper archive to work through. There are eight subject groups, each assessed against four published criteria, each criterion marked from 0 to 8, and descriptors that say exactly what a 7 or 8 looks like. A tutor who has not read those descriptors is guessing.

This is why MYP tutoring goes wrong so often. A parent sees a 4 in Sciences and buys content revision. The marked work shows the 4 came from Criterion B, inquiring and designing, and Criterion C, processing and evaluating — which means the student knows the science and cannot plan an investigation or handle data. More content teaching changes nothing. Reading the descriptors with the task sheet in hand changes it in two sessions.

Villanova sits off Al Qudra Road in the Dubailand belt, and MYP provision around here is thinner than Diploma or British-curriculum provision. That has two consequences. Children travel further to school than their neighbours do, which shortens the evening. And the local pool of tutors who have actually taught the MYP — rather than taught a subject to an MYP student — is small. Proximity cannot fix either problem.

IB Gram matches on subject group and on the criteria that the marked work shows are failing, and teaches live online, one-to-one, scheduled around your child's real arrival time. No tutor travels to a Villanova address, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. The trade is explicit: no car in the driveway, and a tutor who can tell you what Criterion D asks for in your child's specific subject.

What follows is the detail that makes the MYP legible: the eight subject groups and their criteria, how criterion marks convert into the 1 to 7 grade on a report, where marks are actually lost, what a tutor may and may not do with the Personal Project, how eAssessment works for schools that use it, and the step into the Diploma that catches families in this belt every October.

Two standing notes. We publish no IB assessment or results dates anywhere on this site, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and a date a family plans around has to be checkable; ask your school's MYP coordinator. And MYP criteria naming and descriptors are set by the IB and interpreted within each school's assessment policy, so your child's school is the authority on how a particular task was marked.

A final framing point. Dubai's private sector runs 227 schools teaching 17 curricula to 387,441 students, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment against 37 per cent on UK curricula, per Dubai Media Office figures for 2024-25. The MYP is therefore a minority programme inside a very large market, which is precisely why criterion-level expertise is scarce and why a local search returns subject tutors rather than MYP teachers.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-villanova.programmesIntro: MYP support in Villanova households clusters around three stages, and they need different work. The programme runs five years, usually Years 7 to 11 in Dubai schools.

programmes.name: MYP Years 1 to 3
programmes.description: The years where habits are set and nobody is panicking yet, which makes them the most efficient years to spend in. The work that pays is reading a task sheet before starting, writing in paragraphs that answer a question, and number fluency without a calculator. Criterion-aware habits learned here carry through five years of marking.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai these years also carry the KHDA-mandated subjects — Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies — in addition to the eight MYP groups. For a non-Arab student the Arabic requirement is real timetabled work, with separate classes organised for Arabs and non-Arabs, and it is frequently the part of the week nobody supports.

programmes.name: MYP Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: Subject choice narrows, the Personal Project arrives, and in some schools eAssessment follows. Criterion marks start to matter for Diploma course placement, which means a weak Criterion B in Sciences can quietly close the door on Higher Level later. Tutoring here is diagnostic: which criterion, in which subject, and what does its descriptor actually require.
programmes.countryNote: For Villanova families this is also when the school question arises, because several schools in the belt run MYP to Year 11 and then expect a move for the Diploma. A change of school at sixteen means a change of commute, and in this part of Dubai that can be the difference between a 17:00 and an 18:00 session.

programmes.name: The step into the Diploma
programmes.description: The transition the MYP does not rehearse: timed written examinations deciding most of the grade. A student with strong MYP criterion marks can still arrive in DP1 unable to work a ninety-minute paper under pressure, because they have never had to. The gap is pace and structure before it is content, and it is predictable enough to prepare for.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session of the Diploma. Internal Assessment deadlines in Dubai schools typically fall weeks before the IB's own upload dates, so the planning anchor is the school's calendar. Ask the MYP and Diploma coordinators for both, and treat the earliest date as the real one.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent project with a product or outcome, a process journal and a report, supervised in school and assessed against criteria. It rewards evidence of planning and honest reflection rather than an impressive final product. Support is process coaching only: questioning the goal, checking the journal habit, and feedback on the student's own writing.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project runs alongside the KHDA-mandated subjects and, in many Dubai schools, alongside IGCSE entries taken by other students in the same year group. That timetable pressure is the usual reason journals go unwritten until the last fortnight, which is exactly what the criteria detect.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-villanova.subjectsIntro: These are the eight MYP subject groups with the criteria that decide their grades, plus what the marks actually hinge on in each. The criterion names differ by group, which is the detail most advertising ignores.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Criteria A to D: analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. Students lose marks in A by summarising rather than analysing, and in D through accuracy and register rather than ideas. The single most useful habit is annotating a text for technique before writing a word.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Phase-based rather than year-based, which confuses parents comparing children. Criteria cover listening, reading, speaking and writing. Marks hinge on performing the phase descriptors, so a strong speaker in a low phase can score better than a weaker one placed too high.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Criteria A to D: knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Criterion D is where most marks go missing, because critical thinking means evaluating sources and perspectives rather than expressing an opinion confidently.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Criteria A to D: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. B and C are the usual sources of loss — designing a fair investigation and handling data — while content knowledge is often fine.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria A to D: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B requires generalising a pattern and justifying it, which is a different skill from calculating correctly and is rarely taught directly.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria cover knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. The process journal carries more weight than students expect: documented development can outscore a more polished final piece with no visible process behind it.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Assessed on knowledge, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. The written and planning criteria are where academically strong students pick up marks and where sporty students most often lose them.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria cover inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating. The design cycle is the assessment, so a working product with no documented research and testing scores below a modest product with a complete cycle behind it.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed separately on integrating disciplines and reflecting on that integration. Students treat them as double homework rather than as their own assessment, which is why marks here are commonly below the same student's single-subject performance.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Not a subject but threaded through every criterion: research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills. Most MYP underperformance that parents describe as laziness is a self-management and research-skills gap, and it is teachable.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Goal, product or outcome, process journal and report, assessed against criteria that reward planning and honest reflection. The journal is the evidence base; a project with a strong outcome and an empty journal cannot score well, which surprises families every year.

subjects.name: Service as action
subjects.description: A programme requirement rather than a graded subject, documented by the student. Worth knowing about because it consumes time in MYP 4 and 5 alongside the Personal Project, and schools differ in how much documentation they expect.

sections.heading: What 'knows the MYP' has to mean in practice
paragraphs: Here is the test for any MYP tutor, local or otherwise. Ask what the four criteria are called in your child's subject. Ask what each is marked out of. Ask what the difference is between a 5 and a 7 on the criterion your child's report flagged. Somebody who has taught the programme answers all three. Somebody who has taught a subject to MYP students will answer the first vaguely and the other two not at all.

The reason this matters more in the MYP than in other systems is that there is no proxy for criterion knowledge. In IGCSE you can be a good mathematician, work through past papers, and do useful tutoring without ever reading the specification. In the MYP there are no past papers, and the thing being measured is defined entirely by descriptors. A tutor without them is teaching content and hoping it maps onto the marking.

The second test is about evidence. A competent MYP tutor asks for the last two pieces of marked work and the task sheets before the first session, because that is where the diagnosis lives. The criterion marks and the teacher's comments usually name the problem precisely. A tutor who instead asks which topics your child finds difficult is about to spend your money on the wrong thing, politely.

None of these questions is answerable by geography, which is the honest reply to the search that brought you here. In a belt where MYP provision is thin and students travel to a handful of IB schools across the city, the local tutor pool is not where MYP-experienced teachers happen to be concentrated. Matching online removes the constraint entirely.

sections.heading: The eight subject groups and the criteria that mark them
paragraphs: The criteria are labelled A to D in every subject group, but they are named and defined differently in each. That is the single most useful fact a parent can hold, because it means 'Criterion B' is not one thing: in Sciences it is designing an investigation, in Mathematics it is investigating patterns, in Language and literature it is organising a response.

The table below sets out the groups with their criteria and what the marks actually hinge on. Read it alongside your child's last report. If a report shows a 7 in A and a 3 in B for Sciences, the student knows the science and cannot yet design a fair test — a diagnosis that takes thirty seconds and points at four sessions of work rather than a year of content revision.

Three patterns show up repeatedly in Dubai cohorts. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is usually the strongest, because it is the closest thing to traditional content assessment and it is what schools teach most directly. The investigating and designing criteria are the weakest, because they are rarely taught explicitly and are assumed to develop by exposure. And the critical thinking or evaluating criteria are the most undervalued, because students read them as invitations to give an opinion.

Use the table as a diagnostic rather than a syllabus. The point is not to teach a criterion in the abstract; it is to mark a student's own piece against the descriptor, show them where the descriptor was and was not met, and have them write the next one knowing what it asks.

sections.heading: How criterion marks turn into the grade on the report
paragraphs: This is the part that confuses Villanova parents most, and it is worth understanding because it changes which criterion is worth attention. Each of the four criteria is marked from 0 to 8, giving a total out of 32 for the subject. That total is then converted to the 1 to 7 grade that appears on the report, using boundaries set by the IB and applied through the school's assessment policy.

The practical consequence is arithmetic. Moving one criterion from a 3 to a 6 adds three marks to the total out of 32, which is often enough to cross a grade boundary on its own. Moving all four criteria up by one adds four marks for four times the work. So the efficient intervention is always the weakest criterion, and the second most efficient is the second weakest — not an even effort across the subject.

It also explains a phenomenon parents find maddening: a child who 'knows the subject' and reports a 4. If Criterion A is 7 and the other three are 3, 4 and 3, the total is 17 out of 32 and the grade reflects that. The student is not being misjudged. They are being measured on four things and have been taught, in effect, for one of them.

Two cautions. Boundaries and conversion are applied by the school under its assessment policy, so the school is the authority on how a specific report grade was reached and should be asked directly. And criterion marks accumulate across a reporting period rather than coming from a single task, which means one bad piece of work rarely explains a grade and a pattern across pieces usually does.

sections.heading: Where MYP marks are actually lost
paragraphs: The losses cluster in a small number of recognisable places, and almost none of them are content gaps. This is why MYP tutoring that starts with a textbook underperforms so consistently.

The largest single category is not reading the task sheet. MYP tasks state which criteria are assessed and often include the strands being looked for. Students who start writing without reading that lose marks for omitting things they could easily have included. One session spent reading three old task sheets against three pieces of marked work usually produces visible change in the next assessment.

The second is treating the investigating and designing criteria as formalities. In Sciences, Criterion B wants a controlled, repeatable method with variables identified; students describe what they did rather than designing what should be done. In Mathematics, Criterion B wants a general rule found, tested and justified; students find the pattern and stop before the justification, which is where the upper marks live.

The third is the evaluating and critical-thinking criteria, where students assert instead of weighing. Criterion D in Individuals and Societies asks for evaluation of sources and perspectives; a confident opinion scores low however well written. Criterion C in Sciences asks for evaluation of the method and the data, not an apology about human error. The fourth, specific to Arts and Design, is an undocumented process: the journal and the design cycle are the assessment, and a strong final product with nothing behind it cannot score.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and where a tutor must stop
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is an independent piece of work with three components that matter: a goal, a product or outcome, and the evidence of process — the journal and the report. It is supervised in school, and it is assessed against criteria that reward planning, documentation and honest reflection rather than an impressive artefact.

The commonest failure has nothing to do with ability. It is a project with a good outcome and an empty process journal, written up in the final fortnight from memory. The criteria are specifically designed to detect that, and they do. The single most useful intervention is therefore the least glamorous: establishing the journal habit in the first two weeks, as a short weekly entry recording decisions and why they were made.

The second most useful is testing the goal. A goal must be achievable with the time and resources the student actually has, and it must generate something assessable. 'Build an app' from a standing start in a Dubai school term, with no prior coding, is a goal that will produce a thin product and a frustrated student. A narrower goal with documented iteration scores better and teaches more.

The boundary is firm and worth stating plainly. A tutor may question the goal, explain the criteria, help a student plan their time, prompt journal entries and give feedback on the student's own report drafts. A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product, write the journal retrospectively, or draft or rewrite any part of the report. Those are passing off another person's work as the student's own, which is academic misconduct and a matter for the school rather than a style point. The school supervisor remains in charge throughout.

sections.heading: eAssessment and the MYP Certificate
paragraphs: Some schools enter MYP 5 students for IB eAssessment, which leads to the MYP Certificate; others award school-based certification using the same criteria without external assessment. Which route your child's school uses changes what the final year looks like and should be confirmed with the MYP coordinator rather than assumed.

Where eAssessment is used, it combines on-screen examinations in some subjects with externally moderated ePortfolios in others, alongside the Personal Project. For a student used to internal criterion assessment across a term, an on-screen examination is a new experience: a fixed window, unfamiliar question formats, and no opportunity to revise a submission. That is worth rehearsing rather than meeting cold.

Where eAssessment is not used, the criteria still determine everything and the school's internal moderation carries the weight. Nothing about the criterion work described on this page changes; what changes is the absence of an external examination at the end, which in practice means the pattern of marks across the year matters more rather than less.

For Villanova families the practical question is usually simpler than either route suggests: does the final MYP year feed into this school's own Diploma programme, or into an application elsewhere. If elsewhere, the receiving school's expectations matter as much as the certificate, and criterion marks in the relevant subject groups are the evidence they will read. Ask both schools what they look at, early in MYP 4 rather than late in MYP 5.

Whichever route applies, keep the criterion marks themselves. They are the portable evidence of what your child can do, they are what a receiving school reads, and they are the only record that survives a change of school or a change of country mid-programme.

sections.heading: The MYP to Diploma step, and why October is busy
paragraphs: Every October this belt produces the same enquiry: a student with strong MYP marks who is struggling in DP1. It is not a mystery and it is not an ability problem. Three things change simultaneously, and only one of them is content.

The first is assessment format. The MYP is criterion-marked across a term with drafts, feedback and redrafts. The Diploma puts the large majority of each subject grade into timed written examinations. A student who has never produced finished work in ninety minutes under pressure meets that at sixteen, and the first difficulty is pace and structure rather than knowledge. Many can do every question given twice the time.

The second is the disappearance of the redraft. MYP work is often improved after feedback; Diploma examination answers are not. That changes what practice has to look like: timed attempts, marked strictly, with the student seeing what their first attempt was worth rather than what their third attempt became.

The third is subject depth, and it varies by course. The extended strand of MYP Mathematics builds enough algebra for Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, not automatically the fluency Higher Level assumes from week one. MYP Sciences builds investigation skill but not the derivation habit Diploma physics and chemistry require. A bridging block of ten to fifteen hours over the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 addresses all three far more cheaply than remediation in DP2, when Internal Assessments are also due.
bullets: The MYP redrafts; the Diploma marks a first attempt under time pressure
Pace and structure are the first problem, not content
MYP extended maths covers AA Standard Level, not automatically Higher Level fluency

sections.heading: Cost, availability and why proximity fails here
paragraphs: MYP tutoring sits in the middle of the Dubai market on price and at the difficult end on availability, which is the opposite of what families expect. The subject-level demand is lower than for IGCSE or Diploma work, so fewer tutors have real MYP experience, and the ones who do are not distributed evenly around Dubailand.

On price: a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Budget online tuition at AED 33 to 65 — Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 — buys supervision, which for a younger MYP student who will not start homework alone can be exactly the right purchase. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, per Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, with Villanova at the top of that range.

On availability, we would rather say it than let a family discover it: MYP Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education criterion work, and first-language Arabic at MYP level, are the hardest things to staff. Where we cannot cover a request we say so and suggest you look elsewhere, rather than placing a general subject tutor into criterion work they have never marked.

The reason proximity fails specifically for the MYP is the thin provision in this belt. Families here are already travelling past several schools to reach an IB one; the tutor pool within a twenty-minute drive is correspondingly small and is selected by willingness to drive rather than by MYP experience. Teaching online removes that filter completely. IB Gram has no UAE office or centre and does not offer home visits anywhere in the country, which is India-only.
