process.title: Send the report and two pieces of marked work
process.description: The most useful first message carries the subject group, the MYP year, and photographs of the last report plus two marked tasks with their task sheets. The criterion marks and teacher comments usually name the problem precisely, which means the first session can start work rather than start investigating.

process.title: Matched on subject group and criterion
process.description: Tutors are matched to the subject group and to the specific criterion the evidence points at, because Sciences Criterion B and Mathematics Criterion B are different jobs. If we cannot cover a subject group properly — Arts and Design are the tight ones — we say so rather than substituting a generalist.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: A genuine lesson with the person who would continue, no card required, built around your child's own marked work rather than a placement test. By the end you should know which criterion is costing the grade and roughly how many sessions it needs. If the fit is wrong, say so and we match again.

process.title: A plan by criterion, with a finish date
process.description: The plan names the weakest criterion first, because moving one criterion three marks often crosses a grade boundary while raising all four by one does not. It carries a session count and an end date, set against the school's reporting cycle rather than running indefinitely.

process.title: Reviewed at the next report
process.description: Each session produces notes naming what was covered and what was set. When the next report arrives the plan is revised against it rather than continued out of habit, and if the criterion has moved and the subject no longer needs weekly support, we will say so.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-first, not content-first
whyPoints.description: MYP grades come from four criteria marked 0 to 8, and most low grades name a criterion rather than a missing topic. Starting from the descriptor and the student's own marked work is what moves the number; starting from a textbook chapter usually does not.

whyPoints.title: The arithmetic is used deliberately
whyPoints.description: Moving one weak criterion from a 3 to a 6 adds three marks out of 32 and frequently crosses a boundary. Lifting all four by one adds four marks for four times the effort. Plans therefore target the weakest criterion first, then the second weakest.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project stays the student's
whyPoints.description: We question the goal, explain the criteria, set up the journal habit and give feedback on the student's own drafts. We do not choose goals, make products, write journals retrospectively or draft reports, and the school supervisor remains in charge throughout.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated upfront
whyPoints.description: MYP Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education criterion work, and first-language Arabic, are the hardest things to staff. Where we cannot cover a request we say so and suggest looking elsewhere instead of placing a general subject tutor into criterion marking they have not done.

whyPoints.title: No invented presence or approval
whyPoints.description: There is no IB Gram office or centre in the UAE and no home visits anywhere in the country, which is an India-only service. We hold no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE or IB approval, name no school as a client, and publish no IB date we cannot verify against an official page.

faqs.question: What does an MYP tutor need to know that a subject tutor does not?
faqs.answer: The criteria. Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria marked 0 to 8, named differently in each subject group, with published descriptors that define what each mark means. There are no past papers and no content list, so a tutor without the descriptors is teaching content and hoping it maps onto the marking. Ask any prospective tutor to name the four criteria in your child's subject and explain the difference between a 5 and a 7 on one of them. The answer is immediately revealing.

faqs.question: My Villanova child knows the subject but reports a 4. How?
faqs.answer: Because four things are being measured and only one of them is content knowledge. A profile of 7 in Criterion A with 3, 4 and 3 in the others totals 17 out of 32, and the reported grade reflects that total rather than the strongest criterion. This is the most common pattern we see from this belt. It is good news, in a sense: the cheapest intervention available is work on the weakest criterion, which typically means four to six sessions rather than a year of content revision.

faqs.question: How do the four criterion marks become the grade on the report?
faqs.answer: Each criterion is marked from 0 to 8, giving a total out of 32 for the subject, and that total converts to the 1 to 7 grade using boundaries set by the IB and applied through the school's own assessment policy. Marks also accumulate across a reporting period rather than coming from a single task. Because the conversion is applied by the school, the school is the authority on how a specific grade was reached, and the MYP coordinator is the right person to ask about a particular report.

faqs.question: Which MYP criterion causes the most trouble in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: The investigating and designing criteria, across subject groups. Sciences Criterion B wants a controlled, repeatable method with variables identified, and students describe what they did instead of designing what should be done. Mathematics Criterion B wants a general rule found, tested and justified, and students find the pattern then stop short of the justification where the upper marks are. Both are rarely taught explicitly because schools assume they develop through exposure, which makes them unusually responsive to direct teaching.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's MYP Personal Project?
faqs.answer: With the process, yes. A tutor may question whether the goal is achievable and assessable, explain the criteria, help plan the time, prompt regular journal entries and give feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product, write journal entries retrospectively, or draft or rewrite the report. Those are passing off another person's work as the student's own. The school supervisor stays in charge, and the most valuable help is simply getting the journal habit started in the first fortnight.

faqs.question: Why does the process journal matter more than the finished product?
faqs.answer: Because the criteria assess planning, documentation and reflection rather than the impressiveness of the artefact. A project with a polished outcome and an empty journal, written up from memory in the last two weeks, cannot score well — and the criteria are specifically designed to detect it. A narrower project with recorded decisions, dead ends and revisions scores higher and teaches more. The practical advice is a short weekly entry naming what was decided and why, starting in week one.

faqs.question: Does my child's school use IB eAssessment for MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Ask the MYP coordinator, because schools differ. Where eAssessment is used it leads to the MYP Certificate and combines on-screen examinations in some subjects with externally moderated ePortfolios in others, alongside the Personal Project. Where it is not, the school certifies internally using the same criteria. The practical difference is the on-screen examination: a student used to criterion assessment across a term with drafts and feedback has never met a fixed window with no chance to revise, so it is worth rehearsing.

faqs.question: Is MYP tutoring available near Villanova?
faqs.answer: In-home tutors with genuine MYP experience are scarce in this belt, which is the honest answer. Provision for the programme itself is thin around Dubailand — families are typically travelling past several schools to reach an IB one — so the pool within a twenty-minute drive is small and is selected by willingness to drive rather than by MYP experience. IB Gram teaches online one-to-one, which removes that filter; we have no UAE office or centre, and home visits are a service we offer only in India.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Budget online tuition at AED 33 to 65 — Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 — buys supervision, which can be the right purchase for a younger MYP student who will not start work alone. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Villanova at the top of that range. A four to six session criterion block is the usual efficient purchase.

faqs.question: How long should an MYP session be after a long school run?
faqs.answer: Forty-five minutes is often better than sixty for MYP 1 to 3, especially for students travelling back from the Al Barsha schools, who reach Villanova closer to 16:30. Sixty suits MYP 4 and 5. What matters more than length is content: design and investigation tasks need concentration and belong in the earliest slot a family can get, while marking a piece of work against a descriptor or planning a journal entry survives a later start perfectly well.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP to the Diploma next year. What should we do now?
faqs.answer: Spend the summer on the three things that change: timed work, no redrafting, and subject depth. Diploma subjects put most of the grade into timed examinations, and an MYP student has rarely produced finished work in ninety minutes under pressure. The extended strand of MYP Mathematics covers Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level but not automatically the fluency Higher Level assumes. Ten to fifteen hours over the summer addresses all three, far more cheaply than remediation in DP2 when Internal Assessments are due.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education apply to MYP students in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson. Separate classes must be organised for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are prohibited. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold appropriate KHDA approval. These sit alongside the eight MYP subject groups and are genuine additional workload for a non-Arab student.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover several MYP subject groups?
faqs.answer: For criterion skills, partly: the habit of reading a task sheet and marking against a descriptor transfers across groups, and a tutor who teaches that well in one subject helps in others. For subject content it is less realistic, and for Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education the criterion work is specific enough that a generalist is a poor substitute. The usual efficient arrangement is one subject block plus explicit work on task-sheet and descriptor habits that the student then applies elsewhere.

faqs.question: Are MYP tutors required to hold a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, like any private tutor in the country. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and, according to u.ae, is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applying through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service. No fine schedule is published for operating without one, so treat any penalty figure quoted at you as unverified. The permit confirms lawfulness, not MYP experience.

dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-villanova.closingHeading: Send the report, not the textbook
dubai/ib-myp-tutor-in-villanova.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB MYP tutor in Villanova, the useful first step is not a shortlist. It is the last report and two pieces of marked work with their task sheets. Those documents usually name the criterion that is costing the grade, which turns a vague worry into four to six sessions with a clear target. Send them and you will get a straight answer about whether we cover that subject group and in which slots, plus a free first lesson taught by the tutor who would continue. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online; nobody drives to Dubailand.

dubai/ib-november-session-exam-preparati.heroEyebrow: ONLINE RETAKE AND NOVEMBER SESSION PREPARATION
dubai/ib-november-session-exam-preparati.heroSubtitle: IB November session exam preparation in Dubai is a different job from May preparation, and the main reason is that there is usually no school teaching behind it. Most November candidates here are retaking one or two subjects, with the content already covered, the coursework mark often carried forward, and the loss sitting in the paper rather than in the knowledge. This page is about what that paper actually assesses and where the marks went. Sessions run online.

dubai/ib-november-session-exam-preparati.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work with retake and later-session candidates, which is a narrower brief than full Diploma teaching. Each profile names the subject, the level and the components the tutor marks, because a retake plan is built around two or three components rather than around a syllabus.

intro.heading: Nobody is teaching this course any more
paragraphs: A November candidate in Dubai is usually in one of three situations, and they need completely different things. The largest group is retaking one or two subjects after a May result, with school finished, no lessons, no classmates and a deadline six months out. A second group attends a school on a southern-hemisphere academic calendar, for whom November is simply their normal session and the two-year programme runs on a different cycle. A third group is making a single targeted attempt at one component to lift a point total for a conditional offer.

What unites the first and third groups is the absence of teaching. There is no class moving through the syllabus, no teacher setting work, no mock timetable and no cohort. That changes the nature of preparation entirely. For a May candidate a tutor is supplementing a school; for a retake candidate a tutor is the entire structure, and the thing being bought is as much the schedule and the accountability as the subject knowledge.

It also changes where the marks are. A retake candidate has already been taught the whole syllabus, which means the content is largely present and the loss was usually in the paper. Marks go on misread command terms, method not written down, time running out in the final third, units and significant figures, and extended responses that describe without judging. That is good news, because paper losses respond faster than content gaps, and it is why a focused retake plan can be shorter than families fear.

The second major difference is arithmetic. A retake is a decision with a cost and an upside that can be estimated before entries close, and almost nobody does the estimate. How many marks were actually lost, in which components, and how many of those are recoverable in six months without new teaching? A marked script answers that. An opinion does not, and an opinion is what most families decide on.

Coursework is the part that catches people. Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge marks may be carried forward in defined circumstances and for a limited number of sessions, under rules the IB sets. Those rules are not reproduced on this page, because they have not been verified from the IB's own site for it and because they apply case by case. Your former school's Diploma coordinator is the right first call, and a wrong assumption here can mean a retake that cannot reach the target at all.

Sessions are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, since that is an India-only service, and for retake candidates the online format solves a real problem: many are travelling, working, or no longer living where they sat the Diploma, and a plan that survives a change of city is worth more than one tied to a drive.

dubai/ib-november-session-exam-preparati.programmesIntro: Three candidate types sit this session and they are not variations of one another. The entries below set out what each is actually preparing for.

programmes.name: Retake candidate, one or two subjects
programmes.description: No new teaching, a narrow component list, and coursework usually carried forward. Preparation is almost entirely paper technique on components that were already taught, which makes the plan shorter and more measurable than a full course. The constraint is motivation and structure rather than hours in the week.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the practical obstacle is registration. A candidate needs an IB World School willing to act as their centre, and their former school may or may not do it. Ask before building a plan, because a plan with no centre behind it is not a plan.

programmes.name: Southern-hemisphere calendar candidate
programmes.description: For these students November is the normal session, with the two-year programme shifted so the final year ends in the second half of the calendar year. Internal deadlines, mocks and university applications all sit at different points from a May candidate's, and generic advice written for May candidates misleads them systematically.
programmes.countryNote: A handful of schools in the region run on this calendar, and their candidates are frequently handed May-session revision timetables by well-meaning tutors. The first job with this group is to rebuild the calendar around their actual internal deadlines rather than around the city's dominant cycle.

programmes.name: Targeted single-component attempt
programmes.description: One paper, or occasionally one subject, attempted to move a point total across a specific threshold. The work is narrow and heavily technique-led, and the useful first question is whether the threshold is actually reachable from the marks lost last time. Sometimes it is not, and that answer saves a wasted six months.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai families in this position are usually holding a conditional offer that names points or a specific subject grade. The arithmetic of which component to attack should follow the offer's wording rather than the subject that feels worst.

dubai/ib-november-session-exam-preparati.subjectsIntro: Retake candidates come back for a small set of subjects, and each has a characteristic place where marks were lost. The grid below names that place rather than restating the syllabus, because no retake plan has room to cover a whole course again.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Retake losses cluster in the non-calculator paper and in multi-step algebra abandoned halfway. Higher Level Paper 3 is the component most often never practised. Six months with three marked attempts at each paper is usually enough to find and close the pattern.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The recurring loss is commentary: output obtained, meaning never stated, assumptions never named. It reads as a modelling weakness and is a writing weakness. Marks move quickly because the mathematics is already secure.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation steps omitted and organic mechanisms missing conditions, reagents or intermediates. A retake candidate who already knows the content can recover a substantial share of a paper by changing how answers are written, with no new learning at all.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Units, significant figures and the explicit statement of the principle in use. Retake scripts commonly show the correct physics scoring below half on a question. This is the clearest example of a paper loss rather than a knowledge loss.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data-based questions and the mark scheme's accepted terminology. A student who has already sat the course usually knows the biology and loses marks to loose wording, which is fixable by marking rather than by re-reading.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram labelling and the missing evaluation at the end of extended responses, together with Higher Level paper calculations left without working. All three are structural habits and all three respond inside a handful of marked questions.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus rather than to a memorised framework, and judgement at the end of longer answers. Retake candidates often return with better content than they had first time and the same two habits intact.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Timed structure rather than reading. The guided analysis is a pattern that can be rehearsed, and the comparative essay fails when two works are handled in two separate halves. Both are visible between a candidate's own first and third timed attempts.

subjects.name: Language B: French, Spanish, Arabic
subjects.description: Text type conventions, register and word limits rather than vocabulary. A candidate retaking a Language B after a year away usually needs listening practice restarted early, because that component decays faster than the others.

dubai/ib-november-session-exam-preparati.regionsIntro: Retake candidates are not tied to a school day, so the usual Dubai scheduling constraints do not apply in the same way. The notes below describe the real pattern instead: candidates who are travelling, working, or between cities.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: A high share of candidates in shared or family apartments who have started an internship or a foundation course alongside the retake. Daytime weekday slots are often available here, which is unusual and worth using for timed papers.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Families whose student has stayed at home for the retake year. The risk here is a day with no structure at all, which is why a fixed slot and a weekly artefact matter more than the number of hours.

regions.name: Downtown and Business Bay
regions.note: Candidates combining a retake with work experience in the city. Evening sessions after 20:00 are common and perfectly workable, provided timed papers are placed at the weekend rather than at the end of a working day.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Students often travelling between Dubai and a university city while a conditional offer is pending. A plan that survives two time zones is the requirement, and online delivery is the only version that does.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Qusais
regions.note: Candidates frequently registered at a centre some distance from home, which makes the practical arrangements for the sitting itself worth confirming months ahead rather than weeks.

regions.name: Outside Dubai entirely
regions.note: A significant number of retake candidates have left the UAE since their first sitting and are preparing from India, the United Kingdom or elsewhere in the Gulf. Online sessions on Gulf Standard Time or a shifted slot handle that without changing the plan.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB World Schools that register candidates
schoolClusters.note: A retake candidate needs an IB World School to act as their centre, and policies differ. The schools below run the Diploma in Dubai; whether any will register an external candidate is a question to ask each one directly rather than to assume from its programme list.

schoolClusters.city: Schools whose candidates sit later sessions by calendar
schoolClusters.note: A small number of schools in the region run an academic year that places the final Diploma year in the second half of the calendar year. Their candidates are not retakers and should not be given retake advice or May-session timetables.

dubai/ib-november-session-exam-preparati.modesIntro: Three formats for a later sitting, chosen by how much structure the candidate needs rather than by subject. All are delivered online.

modes.title: Retake diagnosis and decision block
modes.description: Two or three sessions before any entry is made. The candidate sits one past paper per target component under timing, the tutor marks it and classifies the losses, and the output is an estimate of how many marks are realistically recoverable in the time available. Some candidates use this block and decide not to retake, which is a legitimate result.

The accountability is a large part of what is being bought, because a six-month gap with no external structure is where most retakes quietly fail.

sections.heading: Who actually sits this session, and why it matters for the plan
paragraphs: Pages about the November session tend to describe it as though it were May with a different month, which misleads almost everyone who reads them. In this market the session has three distinct populations. Retake candidates, who have finished school and are returning for one or two subjects. Candidates at schools on a southern-hemisphere academic calendar, for whom this is the normal session and the whole two-year programme is shifted. And candidates making a single targeted attempt to move a point total for a conditional offer.

The retake group has no teaching behind it, which is the defining feature. There is no class, no teacher setting work, no mock timetable and no cohort to measure against. Everything that a school normally supplies has to be rebuilt by the candidate and whoever is helping them, and the thing most often missing is not knowledge but structure. A plan for this group has to be a calendar before it is a syllabus.

The calendar group has the opposite problem. They have a full school structure and are routinely handed advice written for the dominant cycle, including revision timetables pegged to a May sitting and internal deadline assumptions that do not match their school's. The first useful act with these candidates is to throw away the generic timetable and rebuild it from their own coordinator's deadline list.

The single-component group needs arithmetic more than teaching. The question is whether the specific threshold in a conditional offer is reachable from the marks lost last time, in the components that can be re-sat, within the months available. Sometimes the answer is yes with a narrow plan. Sometimes it is no, and hearing that in week one rather than week twenty is the most valuable thing a tutor can provide.

sections.heading: What changes between the two sessions
paragraphs: The papers themselves are set for the session, so a candidate is not sitting a recycled May paper, and past papers from either session are useful practice because the syllabus and the mark scheme conventions are shared. What differs is everything around the paper: the cohort size, the availability of teaching, the position in the university calendar, and the consequences of the result arriving when it does.

Cohort size matters more than it sounds. A smaller session means fewer classmates to compare against and, for some subjects, fewer tutors who have recently worked on that component. For Dubai families the practical effect is that specialist availability for a later session is thinner than for the dominant one, and booking late is riskier rather than merely inconvenient.

The results timing is the consequential difference. A result from a later session arrives after most university cycles have moved on, which means a candidate may be holding a deferred place, a gap year, or an offer that has already lapsed. This is not an argument against retaking; it is an argument for finding out from the university, in writing, what it will accept and by when, before committing to an entry.

sections.heading: Retake arithmetic: what can move and what cannot
paragraphs: A retake is a purchase with an estimable return, and the estimate takes one afternoon. Start from the component marks, not the grade. A subject grade is built from papers and coursework with published weightings, so the first question is which components carried the loss. A candidate who lost most of their marks on a single paper has a far better case than one who lost a few marks on every component, even if both ended with the same grade.

The second question is whether those marks are of a recoverable type. Marks lost to misread command terms, unwritten method, missing units or abandoned final questions are habit losses, and six months without new teaching is more than enough to change a habit. Marks lost because a whole topic was never understood are content losses, and those take longer and need actual teaching, which a retake candidate does not have access to at school.

The third question is the coursework. Where an Internal Assessment mark is carried forward it cannot be improved, which puts a ceiling on the subject grade regardless of how well the papers go. That ceiling is calculable from the published weightings, and calculating it before entering is the difference between a retake that can reach the target and one that cannot. The rules on what may be carried forward, and for how long, come from the IB and your coordinator rather than from this page.

The table works through the decision in order. A candidate who can answer all five rows has a real basis for entering or not entering, and either answer is a good outcome compared with six months spent on an unreachable target.

sections.heading: Where a retake candidate's marks actually went
paragraphs: The pattern across retake scripts is consistent enough to predict. The largest single category is the final third of the paper: questions left blank, attempted in two lines, or answered out of order after time ran short. That is not a knowledge failure. It is pacing, and it moves with three full timed rehearsals because the candidate learns what six minutes of writing feels like.

The second category is command terms. A candidate who has sat the course once has usually never been shown the published command term list and has answered by instinct. Instinct produces competent prose at the wrong depth: a description where a judgement was wanted, a paragraph where a single exact point was wanted. Fixing this is a matter of reading the term before the stem, and it transfers across every subject the candidate is retaking.

The third category is method and presentation. Unwritten steps in mathematics and chemistry calculations, missing units and significant figures in physics, unlabelled axes in economics diagrams, accepted terminology not used in biology. These are the marks that make a strong student's script score like a weak one, and they are the fastest of all to recover because nothing has to be learned.

The fourth category is the one that genuinely needs teaching: topics never understood. These are visible on a script as whole questions with nothing usable in them, as opposed to questions with the right idea written badly. A retake plan should state honestly how many of these there are and how much of the available time they will consume, because they compete directly with the habit work that pays faster.
bullets: Final-third losses: pacing, fixed by full timed rehearsals
Command terms: answered by instinct, at the wrong depth
Method and presentation: nothing to learn, marks to reclaim

sections.heading: Six months with no school: what the plan has to supply
paragraphs: A retake candidate has roughly six months and no external structure, which is a harder problem than a crowded school timetable. The failure mode is well known and entirely predictable: a strong first month, a quiet second and third, panic in the fifth. A plan that does not design against that pattern will reproduce it, and no amount of subject expertise compensates.

What works is a small number of fixed, non-negotiable commitments. One weekly session at the same time, held even in a week where little was done. Work set between sessions that is marked rather than discussed, because marked work cannot be quietly skipped. A monthly raw-mark comparison that makes drift visible in week eight rather than week twenty. And a stated end point, so the plan can be judged rather than extended indefinitely.

The other half of the problem is that the candidate's life has changed. Many are working, interning, starting a foundation course, or living in a different country from the one they sat the Diploma in. A plan that assumes a student at home with empty days will fail. The honest version asks how many hours a week genuinely exist, then designs for that number rather than for the number everybody would prefer.

The table lays out a six-month shape in blocks rather than dates, with what each block should produce. Shift the boundaries to suit the candidate's actual availability; the order and the artefacts are the parts that matter.

sections.heading: Coursework carried forward, and the ceiling it creates
paragraphs: This is the part of a retake that most often goes wrong, and it goes wrong before any studying happens. Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge marks may be carried forward in defined circumstances and within a limited number of sessions, under rules set by the IB. Those rules are specific, they apply case by case, and they are not reproduced here because they could not be verified from the IB's own site for this page.

The reason it matters is arithmetic. If an Internal Assessment mark is carried forward, it is fixed, and the subject grade is then capped by what the papers alone can contribute at their published weighting. A candidate aiming for a particular subject grade needs to know whether that grade is even arithmetically available with the carried-forward mark in place. Working that out takes ten minutes with the weightings and prevents a six-month plan aimed at an impossible target.

The opposite case also exists. Where coursework can be resubmitted or is not carried forward, a candidate has a component they can improve with written work rather than under examination conditions, which is often the most reliable marks available to them. Knowing which of the two situations applies changes the whole plan, and the answer comes from the coordinator.

A tutor's role on coursework remains what it is everywhere else on this site. A tutor may explain criteria, question a method, narrow a research question and comment on a draft by naming the criterion and the band. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. A retake candidate under time pressure is exactly the person most likely to be offered that service by somebody, and exactly the person with the most to lose from accepting it.

sections.heading: Results timing, universities, and the case for not retaking
paragraphs: A result from a later session arrives after most of the admissions cycle has moved on. For a Dubai family that usually means one of three positions: a deferred place already secured, a gap year in progress, or an offer that has lapsed and will need to be reapplied for. Each has different implications, and all of them need confirming with the institution in writing rather than inferring from a website.

The question to put to a university is narrow and answerable: will you accept a result from this session for this intake, and by what date do you need it. Admissions offices answer that question routinely. Families who ask it before entering make better decisions, and occasionally discover that the retake cannot help the application it was intended for, which is worth knowing in advance.

There is also an honest case for not retaking, and it deserves stating on a page that sells preparation. If the losses were spread evenly across every component, if several topics were genuinely never understood, if the coursework ceiling caps the achievable grade below the target, and if the candidate has started something else they care about, then six months of solitary preparation is a poor investment. Foundation routes, alternative courses and reapplication with the existing grades all exist.

Where the case for retaking is strong, it is usually strong for a specific reason: a single component carried the loss, the losses were habit-shaped, the coursework mark is decent and carried forward, and the target is one or two points away. That combination responds very well to a narrow six-month plan. This page carries no success rate or average improvement figure, because none could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method, and no tutor can promise a grade on an externally marked paper.

process.title: Get the component marks, not just the grade
process.description: A subject grade hides where the loss happened. Component-level marks show whether one paper carried it or whether the loss was spread, and that single distinction decides whether a retake is a narrow fix or a long rebuild. Your former school or the IB's own candidate channels are where those figures come from.

process.title: Confirm the centre and the coursework rule
process.description: Find an IB World School willing to register the candidate, and ask the coordinator in writing which coursework marks carry forward and for how many sessions. Both answers are prerequisites rather than details. A plan built before these are settled can turn out to be aimed at a grade that is not arithmetically available.

process.title: Sit one timed paper per target component
process.description: Under full timing, no notes, in one sitting, then self-marked against the published scheme. The tutor re-marks independently and classifies every lost mark as content, command term, method or time. That classification is the whole basis of the estimate that follows.

process.title: Take the written estimate, then decide
process.description: The output of the diagnosis block is a short written note: recoverable marks by category, hours needed, and whether the target is reachable. Candidates who read that and choose not to retake have had good value from it. A provider unwilling to write that note is not offering a plan.

process.title: Hold a fixed weekly slot for six months
process.description: The common failure in a retake is not difficulty but drift, and drift is designed against rather than talked about. One slot at the same time every week, marked work between sessions, a monthly raw-mark comparison, and a stated end date. Attendance in a quiet week matters more than intensity in a good one.

whyPoints.title: Built for candidates with no school behind them
whyPoints.description: A retake plan has to supply the structure a school normally provides: a fixed slot, work that is marked rather than suggested, and a monthly measurement. That is a different product from supplementing a school timetable, and pretending otherwise is why most solitary retakes drift.

whyPoints.title: The decision comes before the teaching
whyPoints.description: Two or three diagnosis sessions produce a written estimate of recoverable marks and an explicit answer on whether the target is reachable. Candidates who use that block and decide not to enter have been well served, which is the test of whether the advice was honest.

whyPoints.title: Coursework ceilings calculated, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Where an Internal Assessment mark is carried forward it is fixed, and the achievable subject grade is capped by what the papers can contribute. Ten minutes with the published weightings settles whether a target grade exists, and that calculation happens before entries rather than after.

whyPoints.title: Paper losses first, because they move fastest
whyPoints.description: A candidate who has already sat the course usually knows the content. Pacing, command terms, method and presentation are where the marks went, and those respond inside three timed rehearsals with no new learning required.

whyPoints.title: No unverified dates and no promised grades
whyPoints.description: No IB examination or results date is published here, because none could be verified from the IB's own site for this page; your coordinator holds them. No success rate or average improvement appears either, since neither could be produced with a sample size and a method.

faqs.question: Who actually sits the IB November session?
faqs.answer: Three different groups. Retake candidates returning for one or two subjects after a May result, with school finished and no teaching behind them. Candidates at schools on a southern-hemisphere academic calendar, for whom this is simply their normal session and the whole two-year programme is shifted. And candidates making a single targeted attempt at one component to move a point total for a conditional offer. The three need different plans, and most published advice about this session is written as though only the second group existed.

faqs.question: Can my child retake just one or two subjects rather than the whole Diploma?
faqs.answer: Retaking a subset of subjects in a later session is the normal pattern, and it is what most Dubai retake candidates do. The important preliminary is not whether it is possible but whether it is useful: which components carried the loss, whether those losses were habit-shaped or content-shaped, and what the coursework position is. A subject where one paper carried the loss and the coursework mark is decent is a strong retake candidate. A subject with marks lost evenly across every component is a much weaker one.

faqs.question: Will the Internal Assessment mark carry forward to a later sitting?
faqs.answer: Coursework marks may be carried forward in defined circumstances and within a limited number of sessions under rules the IB sets, and those rules apply case by case. They are not reproduced here because they could not be verified from the IB's own site for this page, and a wrong assumption has real consequences. Ask the Diploma coordinator in writing. The answer matters for arithmetic rather than for convenience: a carried-forward mark is fixed, so it caps the achievable subject grade at whatever the papers can add.

faqs.question: How do we register as a retake candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: A candidate needs an IB World School willing to act as their centre, and policies differ between schools. A former school may do it and may not, and a school that has never met the candidate is under no obligation. Treat this as the first task rather than an administrative detail, because a plan with no confirmed centre behind it is not a plan. Ask in writing, confirm the entry deadline the centre works to, and get the arrangement settled before any preparation schedule is built.

faqs.question: When do later-session results arrive relative to university offers?
faqs.answer: After most of the admissions cycle has moved on, which is the central practical problem with a retake. In Dubai that usually means holding a deferred place, being mid gap year, or needing to reapply with a lapsed offer. The question to put to the institution is narrow: will you accept a result from this session for this intake, and by what date do you need it. Admissions offices answer that routinely, and asking before entering occasionally reveals that the retake cannot help the application it was meant for.

faqs.question: Is a retake worth doing for one point?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether that point is load-bearing. If a conditional offer names a points total and the candidate is one short, and the shortfall sits in a component where the loss was pacing or command terms, then a narrow plan has a good case. If the point is wanted for its own sake, six months of solitary preparation is an expensive way to get it. Read the offer's exact wording first, because offers that specify a subject grade and offers that specify a total point to completely different plans.

faqs.question: How many marks can a retake realistically move without new teaching?
faqs.answer: No honest number can be given in general, and any site quoting one is inventing it. What can be estimated, from a marked paper, is the size of each loss category. Marks lost to pacing, command terms, method and presentation are recoverable in six months with no new learning. Marks lost because a topic was never understood need teaching time that competes with the habit work. The estimate is specific to the script, which is why the diagnosis block comes before any commitment.

faqs.question: What does a six-month plan look like when nobody is teaching the course?
faqs.answer: Month one is diagnosis, registration and calendar. Month two teaches the absent topics the script exposed, in that order. Month three is habit work on command terms, method and presentation. Month four begins full timed rehearsals. Month five attacks pacing and the final third of the paper. Month six closes the plan with nothing new started. Across all six, the non-negotiables are a fixed weekly slot, work that is marked rather than discussed, and a monthly comparison of raw marks on comparable papers.

faqs.question: Do universities treat a later-session result differently from a May one?
faqs.answer: The qualification is the same and the grades mean the same thing, so the difference is practical rather than academic: the result arrives later in the cycle. Some institutions and some intakes accommodate that easily, others do not, and a few require the result by a date that a later session cannot meet. There is no general rule worth relying on, which is why the only sound approach is to ask the specific institution about the specific intake in writing and keep the reply.

faqs.question: Does the paper itself differ between sessions?
faqs.answer: Each session has its own papers, so a candidate is not sitting a recycled version of an earlier one. The syllabus and the mark scheme conventions are shared, which means past papers from either session are legitimate and useful practice. What differs around the paper is more consequential than the paper: cohort size, availability of teaching, the depth of specialist tutors for a given component, and where the result lands in the university calendar. Plan around those rather than around any imagined difference in difficulty.

faqs.question: Do you come to our home in Dubai for retake sessions?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that is an India-only service, and all sessions are delivered online over live video. For retake candidates this resolves a genuine problem rather than creating one. Many have left the city or the country since their first sitting, or are working or studying alongside the retake, and a plan that survives a change of address and a change of time zone is worth considerably more than one built around a weekly drive to a fixed address.

faqs.question: What does retake preparation cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialist work, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and a premium named tier reaching AED 650 at BartyED. A retake is usually fewer total hours than a full year of support, because the scope is two or three components rather than six subjects. Ask any provider for the number of sessions and whether marking between them is included.

faqs.question: Can a retake candidate improve a Theory of Knowledge or Extended Essay grade?
faqs.answer: Whether a core component can be resubmitted or is carried forward is governed by the IB's rules and depends on the case, so the coordinator is the right source rather than a tutoring page. The arithmetic consequence is what matters: core points contribute to the total, so a fixed core grade changes which totals are reachable from the subjects being retaken. Where resubmission is permitted, written work done without examination pressure is often the most reliable improvement available to a retake candidate.

faqs.question: My child's school runs a different academic year, so is this their normal session?
faqs.answer: For schools on a southern-hemisphere academic calendar, yes, and those candidates are not retakers. The practical risk for this group is being handed advice written for the dominant cycle: revision timetables pegged to a different sitting, and internal deadline assumptions that do not match their school. The first thing to do is rebuild the plan from their own coordinator's deadline list, which will place Internal Assessment deadlines, mocks and university applications at different points from the ones most Dubai advice assumes.

faqs.question: What is the honest case for not retaking at all?
faqs.answer: If the losses were spread evenly across every component rather than concentrated, if several topics were genuinely never understood, if a carried-forward coursework mark caps the achievable grade below the target, and if the candidate has already started something they care about, then six months of solitary preparation is a poor investment. Foundation routes, alternative courses and reapplying with the existing grades are all real options. A diagnosis block that ends in that conclusion has done its job, even though it ends the sale.

dubai/ib-november-session-exam-preparati.closingBody: The most valuable work in a retake happens before any entry is submitted. Get the component marks rather than the subject grade, ask the coordinator in writing which coursework marks carry forward, confirm an IB World School will register the candidate, and have one timed paper per target component marked and classified by cause of loss. Book the free trial lesson and spend it on that script. The output should be a written estimate of recoverable marks and a straight answer on whether the target is reachable in the months available. Either answer is worth having, and the second one saves a great deal more than it costs.

intro.heading: A market with no dates in it
paragraphs: The research behind this page grepped sixty-odd competitor pages for exam-session awareness. The word November returned zero hits on every fetchable page. No competitor names a session, an entry deadline, or a results date. For a market selling exam preparation, that is a remarkable omission, and it is the single clearest gap available to a page like this one.

The omission matters because almost every planning error a Dubai family makes is a calendar error. A parent starts looking for help four weeks before the papers, when the useful window was twelve. A private candidate discovers an entry deadline has passed. A family budgets for an exam-term intensive in March, by which point every specialist in the emirate is booked. None of those is an academic failure; all of them are a consequence of nobody publishing the shape of the year.

So this page counts backwards. It sets out the board deadlines that are published and sourced, explains which dates belong to the board and which to your school, gives a ten-week plan with a measurable output in each week, and states plainly what ten weeks can and cannot change. It also covers the part of the cycle nobody writes about, which is what happens after results: enquiries upon results, remarks and retake entries all have their own deadlines, and they arrive while a family is still absorbing the grades.

One honesty note that shapes the whole page. IB exam dates in this project are not verified. The IB's own site returns an error to automated requests, so no IB session, upload or results date here has been confirmed from the IB itself, and none is published. What this page does publish are Cambridge and Pearson dates, which are sourced from those boards' own pages, and which illustrate the principle well enough to plan by. For your child's IB dates, ask the school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly, and take the answer in writing. A page that invents a date a family builds a revision plan around has done more damage than a page with no dates on it at all, which is the position almost every competitor in this market occupies by accident rather than by principle.

Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In exam term that model has a specific practical value, because the specialists who are still free in March are rarely the ones who live within driving distance of your community. It also means a 9pm session during Ramadan, or a 7am slot on a weekend in the final fortnight, is an ordinary request rather than an imposition, and both of those turn out to matter when a candidate is sitting six subjects in a compressed window.

dubai/ib-online-tuition.programmesIntro: The calendar pressure differs by programme, and so does what a short run of sessions can achieve. Each note below names the window that matters at that stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examination series for most pupils, which makes the calendar internal and therefore invisible. The window that matters is the school's own assessment cycle, because criterion marks accumulate into reports that inform Diploma option decisions. Pupils who are quietly behind in Year 9 meet the consequence at the Higher Level option blocks two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools that switch to IGCSE at Year 10 hand their pupils an external calendar abruptly, with entry deadlines and board timetables that the family has never had to think about. The first encounter with a Cambridge or Pearson entry deadline usually comes as a surprise in Year 10.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The tightest calendar in school education. Coursework deadlines fall in the autumn and winter of the second year, mocks follow, and the examined components come last, with upload deadlines set by the IB in between. The ten weeks before the papers are the window this page plans, and they are worth more if the preceding twelve months were planned at all.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai private schools following the northern academic year sit the May session. Session windows, upload deadlines and results dates are set by the IB and revised, so confirm each with your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly. No date on this page should be treated as the authority for an IB deadline.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The DP courses inside the programme sit on the same examination calendar as any other Diploma course, while the reflective project and career-related study follow internal deadlines. Candidates often misjudge this and treat the whole programme as internally assessed, which produces a late discovery about the examined components.
programmes.countryNote: Because few Dubai schools license the programme, a candidate may be the only one in their year sitting a particular combination, which makes the school's exam administration unfamiliar with it. Confirming the entry position early is worth more here than in a large Diploma cohort.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external series, but Cambridge offers Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which some Dubai schools use as a benchmark. Where a school does, those windows are worth knowing because they are the first external measurement a family ever receives and they are easy to over-interpret.
programmes.countryNote: Checkpoint results in Dubai schools are often the trigger for a family's first tutoring enquiry. The measured, useful response is to read which strands were weak rather than the overall benchmark, because a strand gap at age 11 is a few weeks of work and a headline score is not actionable.

dubai/ib-online-tuition.subjectsIntro: In the final ten weeks, each subject has one component that repays attention more than the others. The entries below name it, because a generic revision plan spends the same time everywhere and gains least.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The calculator-free paper, every time. A candidate who has been leaning on a graphical calculator for routine manipulation will lose marks there that no amount of content revision recovers. Ten weeks is enough to rebuild manual fluency if the drilling starts immediately.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Interpretation in context, drilled as a habit: every numerical answer followed by a sentence referring it back to the situation. This is a two-week change applied across every past paper attempted, and it is the highest-yield correction available in the course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 stem annotation, practised until it is automatic, plus the conventions on extended response: balanced equations, state symbols, mechanism arrows from the right origin. Conventions are checklist work and show up in marked papers within three weeks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The data-analysis section, which is rarely finished in class and responds faster to coaching than anything else in the subject. Gradient meaning, uncertainty handling and limitation statements are learnable procedures rather than insight.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline and answer length. A candidate writing discuss-length answers to outline questions loses marks twice, on the question and on the time. Correcting it is a fortnight of supervised practice and it releases time across the whole paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline: axes and curves labelled, shift drawn, and then explicitly referenced in the prose. Candidates who draw correct diagrams and never mention them forfeit marks already earned, which is the cheapest correction in the subject.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case study, which should have been worked for months and usually has not. In a ten-week window the realistic goal is applying three or four tools properly to the stimulus rather than attempting the whole syllabus against it.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The study bank. Four facts per named study, a method, a finding, a limitation and a link to the topic, held for enough studies to cover the examined options. This is systematic memorisation work with a clear finish line, which suits a ten-week window well.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 timing and Paper 2 comparative structure. Both are structural rather than knowledge-based, which means both can change inside ten weeks. Unseen analysis under timed conditions, repeated weekly, is the single most effective preparation here.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Case specificity: place, date, figure, consequence, for every example a candidate intends to use. Ten weeks is enough to convert a vague store of knowledge into a defined set of deployable examples, which is what the upper bands reward.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, drilled against the published style, and the annually released case study. Python-fluent candidates lose marks for writing Python where pseudocode is required, and that is a correction measured in days rather than weeks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: By the final ten weeks this component is normally submitted, which is exactly why it belongs on a calendar page. A candidate still writing a Theory of Knowledge essay in the revision window has a scheduling failure that started a year earlier, and the fix is next year's planning rather than this term's.

dubai/ib-online-tuition.regionsIntro: Availability, travel and school exam arrangements vary across the emirate in ways that matter specifically in exam term. These notes concern that window rather than the year as a whole.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JLT
regions.note: Heavy competition for the 5pm to 7pm window in exam term, when every family in the cluster wants the same hours. Families who fixed a slot in the autumn keep it; families looking in March are choosing from what is left.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Long drives make visiting tutors scarcest precisely when demand peaks, so exam-term availability here is the tightest in the emirate for in-home arrangements. Online slots are unaffected by the February to April traffic.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Well supplied with experienced tutors year-round, which means exam-term scarcity bites later here than elsewhere. The constraint becomes subject-specific rather than general: Higher Level sciences go first.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Qusais
regions.note: Large general tutoring supply and thin Diploma Higher Level supply, a gap that widens in exam term. Candidates here most often need a specialist who is not local, which is a straightforward arrangement over video.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Pupils travelling back from schools across the emirate return late, so exam-term sessions here commonly run at 8pm or later. That is practical over video and close to impossible for a visiting tutor.

regions.name: Dubai South and Jumeirah Golf Estates
regions.note: Effectively outside the practical range of most tutors in exam term, when nobody is willing to add a long drive to a full week. Online delivery is not a preference in these communities during February to April.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Tecom
regions.note: Central and dense with IB schools, so demand is high and supply is reasonable. This is the cluster where booking three weeks ahead still sometimes works, which is not true elsewhere in exam term.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Exam-term requests here often combine revision with admissions deadlines, because candidates are managing conditional offers alongside papers. Scheduling around both is the practical challenge rather than finding a tutor.

schoolClusters.city: Schools with established exam administration
schoolClusters.note: Experienced exams officers, clear internal deadlines and reliable timetable communication. Candidates from these cohorts rarely have administrative problems and need technique work in the final stretch.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Newer cohorts and unusual combinations
schoolClusters.note: Schools running the Diploma for only a few cycles, or candidates with combinations the school handles rarely. Confirming the entry position early matters more for these families than for large established cohorts.

dubai/ib-online-tuition.modesIntro: In the final stretch the booking shape should follow the calendar rather than a preference. These three are what the ten weeks before a session actually call for.

modes.title: Post-mock diagnostic pair
modes.description: Two sessions immediately after mocks, before the script goes cold. The first maps every lost mark against a fault type and produces a ranked list. The second starts on the cheapest fault. Nothing else in the final ten weeks produces as much per hour as these two.

modes.description: One slot a week through the run-up, with a measurable output in each week: a timed section, a corrected past paper, a drilled convention checklist. Booked in the autumn, because the specialists who take these are unavailable by March.

modes.description: A short arrangement after results, when enquiries upon results, remarks and retake entries all have deadlines that arrive during the least clear-headed fortnight of the year. The work is partly academic and mostly administrative triage.

sections.heading: What IB online tuition in Dubai is bought to do in the final stretch
paragraphs: In the ten weeks before a session, tuition can do four things and cannot do a fifth. Being clear about the four is how a family spends a limited budget in the right place, and being clear about the fifth prevents a great deal of disappointment.

It can clear convention faults, which are the cheapest marks available anywhere in the Diploma: missing state symbols, unlabelled axes, numbers without units, mechanism arrows from the wrong origin. It can fix timing, which is a triage skill rather than a knowledge one. It can drill command-term discipline so that an outline question receives an outline answer. And it can convert a vague store of knowledge into a defined set of deployable examples, which is what the upper bands reward in the essay subjects.

What it cannot do in ten weeks is rebuild two years of missing foundations. A candidate who has not understood moles since the first term of the first year is not going to acquire that in eight sessions alongside five other subjects, and any provider suggesting otherwise is selling hope. The honest version of that conversation produces a different plan: triage the subjects where marks are cheapest, accept the position in the subject that needed a year, and protect the grades that are reachable.

The calendar is what makes this allocation possible. A family that knows the mock window, the coursework completion date, the board entry deadlines and the session dates can place each intervention where it belongs. A family working from the single fact that exams are in May makes every decision late. That is the entire argument for publishing dates, and it is why the next section exists.
bullets: Convention faults: the cheapest marks in the Diploma
Timing and triage: a skill, not knowledge
Command-term discipline: a fortnight of supervised practice
Deployable examples: converting knowledge into usable material
What ten weeks cannot do is rebuild two years of foundations

sections.heading: The board calendars that are published and sourced
paragraphs: Three boards matter to Dubai families: Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel for IGCSE and International GCSE, and the IB for the Diploma. Two of the three publish calendars that can be quoted. The third could not be verified for this project, and the difference is stated rather than smoothed over.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Those Checkpoint tests are not IGCSE sittings and should never be read as one. A UAE candidate therefore has two sittings a year, and the February sitting some families have heard about is offered to India rather than to Gulf centres, so it should not enter a Dubai plan at all. The administration still runs well ahead of the teaching: final entries for a June series close in the spring, months before the first paper, forecast grades are submitted before the papers themselves, and results follow in August. The exact day of each of those comes from the timetable and statement of entry the centre issues, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and the wrong zone's timetable is simply the wrong timetable.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For results timing, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the November series due a year later, which is why any session table should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

For the IB, no date is published here. The IB's assessment pages return an error to automated requests, so nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources circulate windows for the next May session, and they are not good enough to publish on a page a family might plan around. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly, and get the answer in writing.

sections.heading: Why entry deadlines sit months before the papers
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a family can understand about examination administration is that the paperwork runs on a different clock from the teaching. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE series shows it starkly: the papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, the entry for them closed well before the autumn term's teaching had finished, and results from the equivalent November 2025 series did not reach students until 22 January 2026. Cambridge works the same way in the UAE, with a June entry closing in the spring and results arriving in August. Months separate the entry from the paper, and months again separate the paper from the certificate, so a candidate who was not entered in time is not sitting the paper at all, whatever their preparation.

The reason is logistical rather than bureaucratic. Papers must be printed, allocated and dispatched to centres worldwide, zones have to be assigned, access arrangements have to be approved, and forecast grades have to be collected. All of that is upstream of the first paper, and none of it can be done retrospectively.

The practical consequence for a Dubai family is a distinction worth drawing explicitly. Board deadlines are immovable and are handled by your school's exams officer. School deadlines, including internal coursework dates and mock windows, are set by the school and occasionally negotiable. Confusing the two produces two characteristic errors: treating a board deadline as flexible, and treating a school deadline as absolute when a conversation would have helped.

The useful habit is to ask the exams officer, in writing, in the autumn, for three things: the entry deadline that applies to your child, the series they are entered for, and the zone or timetable version that applies. Those three facts prevent almost every administrative disaster that befalls candidates in this region, and they take one email to obtain.

sections.heading: The six Cambridge zones, and a real administrative risk
paragraphs: This is a small detail with a large consequence, and it affects families in this region more than most. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and the examination timetable differs between them. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and adds that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

The way this goes wrong is entirely ordinary. A parent finds a timetable online, or in a parents group, or from a relative in another country, and plans the revision schedule around it. The dates are real dates from a real Cambridge document, for a different zone. A paper sat in the morning in one zone may be sat in the afternoon in another, or on a different day.

The protection is a single rule with no exceptions: the only timetable a family should use is the one issued by their own school's exams officer, confirmed in writing, for their own centre. Not a website, not a forum, not another family's copy, and not this page, which deliberately publishes no candidate timetable.

The same principle extends to IB candidates for a different reason. IB session windows and upload deadlines are set by the IB and revised, and secondary sources circulate dates that look authoritative. A candidate planning around a circulated date rather than a school-confirmed one is taking an avoidable risk during the worst possible fortnight to take one.

sections.heading: Private candidates in Dubai: what changes
paragraphs: A candidate sitting examinations outside a school as a private candidate takes on administrative work that a school would otherwise absorb, and the differences are worth knowing before the decision rather than after. This situation arises in Dubai more often than elsewhere, usually after a school move, a relocation or a decision to sit an additional subject.

The entry itself goes through a centre that accepts private candidates, and that centre sets its own fees, deadlines and subject availability, which are usually earlier and narrower than a school's. Entry fees are set by the board and the centre rather than by any tutor, and the only reliable way to budget for them is to ask the centre in writing. No figure for them appears on this page, because it would be a guess.

Two practical constraints catch private candidates in particular. Subjects with a required practical or performance component may not be available at every centre, and coursework components usually require a centre willing to supervise and authenticate them. Those two facts determine which subjects a private candidate can realistically sit, and they should be checked before any teaching is arranged.

The timetable rule applies with extra force here. A private candidate has no school exams officer quietly checking the zone version, which means the responsibility for confirming the correct timetable sits with the family and the centre. Ask the centre to confirm the zone and the version in writing, and keep it.

sections.heading: After results: the cycle nobody plans for
paragraphs: Results day is treated as an endpoint and it is a decision point, with several deadlines sitting immediately behind it. A family absorbing an unexpected grade has a short window in which to act, and acting well requires information rather than speed.

The first thing to obtain is the marks breakdown by component, which shows where the result came from. A grade that fell short because one paper underperformed relative to the others is a different situation from one where every component landed in the same place. The first may be worth an enquiry upon results; the second almost never is, and understanding the difference saves both money and hope.

Enquiries upon results, including remarks, have their own deadlines set by the board and are requested through the centre. They carry fees, they can move a mark down as well as up, and they are worth considering mainly where a grade boundary is close and a single component is out of line with the others. Retake entries have separate deadlines that may fall before the enquiry outcome is known, which is the genuinely difficult part of the timing.

For Dubai families there is an additional layer, which is equivalency. Recognition of a qualification for UAE university entry runs through the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority, and it is a process a family follows rather than something a tutoring provider performs or can accelerate. Build the timeline for it from the authority's own guidance rather than from any third party.

sections.heading: A ten-week plan with something measurable in each week
paragraphs: Revision plans fail because they are lists of topics rather than lists of outputs. A plan built on outputs can be checked weekly by a parent with no subject knowledge, which is the only kind of plan that survives ten weeks of a teenager's resistance.

The plan below assumes one subject with one weekly session, after mocks, with a candidate who has a mapped fault list. If there are two subjects, run it twice with the heavy weeks staggered; if there are three, the honest advice is to pick two. Each week has one output that either exists at the end of the week or does not, and no output is an opinion.

The front half is about clearing cheap faults, because they are cheap and because early visible gains buy a candidate's cooperation for the harder work later. The back half moves to full-length timed papers under real conditions, which is the only way to test whether the corrections hold under pressure. A candidate who has corrected conventions in isolated practice and never sat a full paper will lose them again in the hall.

The final fortnight deliberately contains less new work than families expect. Week nine is a full timed paper and a comparison against week three. Week ten is consolidation of the two faults that still recur, plus the administrative check: timetable confirmed with the exams officer, equipment, and the sleeping pattern. Nothing new is introduced, because nothing new becomes reliable in ten days.

sections.heading: What ten weeks changes, and what it does not
paragraphs: Honesty here is worth more than encouragement, because a family that knows what is achievable allocates correctly and a family that does not spends the same money for less. The pattern is consistent enough to describe.

Highly responsive in ten weeks: conventions, timing, command-term discipline, diagram labelling, the data-analysis sections of science papers, and the conversion of vague knowledge into specific deployable examples. All of these are procedural, all are drillable, and all appear in marked work within three or four weeks of starting. For a candidate sitting two marks below a boundary, this is usually where the two marks are.

Partially responsive: a single topic never properly understood, which can be rebuilt in ten weeks if it is one topic and the candidate does the work between sessions. Weak extended-response structure, which improves but needs longer to become automatic under pressure.

Not responsive: two years of absent foundations, a coursework mark already submitted, and a grade needed for an offer that is three grades above current performance. Those are not tutoring problems and should not be sold as such. The right response is triage, which means protecting the grades that are reachable and being straight with the candidate about the one that is not. A family told this in February makes better decisions than a family told it in May. The decision triage produces is usually narrower than families expect: two subjects chosen to defend, one subject consciously left where it is, and the hours redistributed accordingly rather than spread evenly across six.
