sections.heading: Evidence in the final stretch, and why it matters more now
paragraphs: In a ten-week window there is no time to discover in week eight that the arrangement is not working, so the evidence requirements tighten rather than relax. Three artefacts carry the weight, and all three come out of the sessions themselves rather than from a progress report.

The first is the ranked fault list from week one, which is the baseline everything else is measured against. The second is the sequence of timed attempts, one in week three, one in week seven and one in week nine, which are directly comparable because they were sat under the same conditions. The third is the weekly output, which either exists or does not.

Because teaching is delivered over live video on a shared board, all of this persists as files rather than as paper in a bag. In the last fortnight that archive becomes the revision material: a candidate reviewing their own annotated attempts, with each correction beside the error that produced it, is revising their own faults rather than a generic checklist. It costs nothing extra, having been produced as a by-product of the teaching.

The review question in exam term is also sharper than usual. If the week-nine paper shows the same faults as week one, the ten weeks did not work and the remaining fortnight should be spent on the two cheapest marks rather than on continuing a plan that has been tested and failed. That is an uncomfortable conversation and a far better one than the alternative, which is finding out on results day.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge IGCSE exams actually take place?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. A UAE candidate sits June or November. The February sitting that occasionally comes up in conversation is offered to India, not to Gulf centres, so it is not an option for a Dubai student at all. Which of the two series your child sits is a decision made by the school, and the timetable that applies depends on the administrative zone your centre is allocated to, so the version to use is the one the exams officer issues.

faqs.question: How far before the papers does an exam entry close?
faqs.answer: Months, not weeks. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE series is the clearest dated illustration: the papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry for them closed well before that, earlier in the same academic year. A Cambridge June entry works the same way, closing in the spring with forecast grades submitted before the papers, and the exact day is on the statement of entry your centre issues rather than on any tutoring page. The reason is logistical rather than bureaucratic, since papers have to be printed, allocated and dispatched and access arrangements approved. A candidate not entered by the deadline does not sit the paper, however well prepared they are.

faqs.question: On what dates did Pearson release its recent International GCSE results?
faqs.answer: Pearson publishes results on a set schedule per series. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the version to work from rather than any restatement of it.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because none could be verified. The IB's own assessment pages return an error to automated requests, so no IB session window, upload deadline or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources circulate dates for upcoming sessions and they are not a good enough basis for a family's planning. The reliable route is your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly, with the answer taken in writing. A fabricated date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date at all.

faqs.question: What are the Cambridge exam zones and why do they matter?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs between them, including by day and by session. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. The failure mode is ordinary: a parent finds a real Cambridge timetable online that belongs to a different zone. Use only the version issued by your own centre's exams officer, confirmed in writing.

faqs.question: Which deadlines belong to the school and which to the exam board?
faqs.answer: Board deadlines are the entry deadline, access arrangement approval, forecast grade submission, the examination period itself and the results release. Those are immovable and are handled by the school's exams officer. School deadlines are internal coursework dates and mock windows, set by the school and occasionally negotiable. Two characteristic errors come from confusing them: treating a board deadline as flexible, which is fatal, and treating a school deadline as absolute when a conversation with the coordinator would have produced a sensible accommodation.

faqs.question: What changes if my child sits exams as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The administrative work that a school would absorb becomes yours. Entries go through a centre that accepts private candidates, and that centre sets its own fees, deadlines and subject availability, usually earlier and narrower than a school's. Entry fees come from the board and the centre, not from any tutor, so get them in writing from the centre. Two constraints catch private candidates: subjects with required practical components may not be offered everywhere, and coursework needs a centre willing to supervise and authenticate it.

faqs.question: Is it worth requesting a remark after disappointing results?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision should follow the component breakdown rather than the grade. A result where one paper underperformed relative to the others, with a grade boundary close by, is the situation where an enquiry upon results is most worth considering. A result where every component landed consistently is almost never worth it. Enquiries are requested through the centre, carry fees, run to deadlines set by the board, and can move a mark down as well as up. Read the breakdown before anyone pays for anything.

faqs.question: Can we plan a retake before the remark result comes back?
faqs.answer: Frequently you have to, and it is the genuinely difficult part of the timing. Retake entry deadlines for the next series can fall before an enquiry upon results is resolved, which means a family may be deciding on a retake without knowing whether the original grade will change. The practical approach is to establish both dates immediately: the enquiry deadline and the retake entry deadline for the next available series, both through the centre, and then decide with the calendar rather than the hope in front of you.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start exam preparation for the May session?
faqs.answer: Ten to twelve weeks is a genuine window and four weeks is not nothing, provided the expectations match. In ten weeks conventions, timing, command-term discipline, diagram marks and the data-analysis sections of science papers can all change measurably, because they are procedural and drillable. In four weeks the realistic work is timed paper practice plus the two cheapest convention faults. What neither window can do is rebuild two years of missing foundations, and a provider who suggests otherwise is selling hope rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Why does specialist availability run out in February?
faqs.answer: Because demand across Dubai concentrates in the same ten weeks and the supply of people who have taught a specific Higher Level subject is finite. The same tutor with open slots in October has none in March. Higher Level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches go first, then Economics at Higher Level. The practical consequence is that reserving the slot is the purchase and should be done in the autumn, separately from when the sessions actually happen. Families who book in March choose from what remains.

faqs.question: What should a ten-week revision plan actually contain?
faqs.answer: One measurable output per week rather than a list of topics, because nobody outside the room can tell whether a topic was revised or merely read. Week one produces a ranked fault list from the mock script. Weeks two to six clear cheap faults and introduce timed sections. Weeks seven and nine are full-length timed papers that can be compared against each other. Week ten contains no new learning at all, only consolidation of the two faults that still recur plus confirming the timetable with the exams officer in writing.

faqs.question: Should we use the mock grade or the mock script to plan with?
faqs.answer: The script, always. Mock grades are produced against boundaries the school selects, sometimes deliberately severe to create urgency, while real boundaries are set per session by the board afterwards and are not published in advance. A mock 4 and a mock 5 can be two marks apart on the same paper. The script, by contrast, shows exactly where the marks went, and mapping every lost mark against a fault type takes one session and produces the list the whole plan then runs on.

faqs.question: Do exam-term sessions have to fit around Ramadan and school timings?
faqs.answer: They have to, and they can. School timings shorten during Ramadan and the working day changes, which moves when a candidate can genuinely concentrate; post-Iftar sessions often work better that month than a tired shortened afternoon. Eid holidays fall on a lunar calendar and move each year relative to the exam season, so the number of usable weeks before the papers differs year to year. Count usable weeks rather than calendar weeks when building a plan, and schedule over video so that a 9pm session involves nobody driving.

faqs.question: Are exam-term lessons for Dubai candidates delivered online?
faqs.answer: Yes, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In exam term that model matters more than usual for a practical reason: the specialists still free in March are rarely the ones living within driving distance of your community, and a visiting tutor adding a long drive to an already full week in February is the first arrangement to be cancelled.

dubai/ib-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each profile states the subject, the level and the components taught. The practical question to ask any online tutor is what they put on the shared board in the first ten minutes, because a tutor who starts by talking has not prepared from the pupil's work.

intro.heading: Sixty minutes, described rather than advertised
paragraphs: Almost every page selling online tutoring to Dubai families describes the experience and not the content. Lessons are interactive. Tutors are passionate. The platform is easy to use. None of that tells a parent what will happen between 5pm and 6pm on a Tuesday, which is the only question that matters when the alternative is a person sitting at the kitchen table.

So here is the structure. A Diploma session opens on the pupil's own marked work, displayed on a shared board. The first block identifies and names the fault, out loud, with the script in front of both of them. The middle blocks work the fault: worked examples the tutor builds live, then the pupil working alone on the same board while the tutor watches the pen rather than the face. The final block sets what the pupil will produce before the next session and writes the note that records what was addressed.

What makes that work is not enthusiasm, it is the board. A shared annotation surface where both parties write is closer to sitting side by side at a desk than video conferencing suggests, because the attention of both people is on the same page rather than on each other. Diploma work is written work, and written work is what a shared board is for. A pupil solving a problem while the tutor watches each line appear is being taught in the only way that actually reveals where the method breaks.

The second thing that makes it work is that nothing evaporates. A tutor who visits a Dubai home leaves behind whatever happened to be written on paper, which goes into a school bag. A session on a shared board leaves every worked example, every annotated script and every correction as a file the pupil can reopen in April. In the final weeks before the May session, that archive is the revision material, and it is specific to one pupil's faults rather than generic.

IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE. In-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and teaching for Dubai families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The rest of this page is the honest version of what that means: the tools, the failure modes, how a science practical is handled, what the Dubai week does to scheduling, and what a camera genuinely costs compared with presence. None of it is an argument that screens are better than people. It is an argument that for written, specification-bound Diploma work the scarce resource in this emirate is a teacher who has marked that paper, and that such a person is reachable by video and usually not by car.
bullets: The session opens on the pupil's marked work, not on introductions
Both parties write on the same shared board throughout
Worked examples and annotated scripts persist as reviewable files
Session notes name the component and the criterion, not the topic
Connection, attention and practical work each have a stated answer
What presence provides is named rather than argued away

dubai/ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Session structure changes with age more than with subject, because attention span and independence change. The notes below describe what an online session actually looks like at each stage.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Shorter sessions, usually thirty to forty minutes, built around a small number of activities with visible progress inside each. A parent within earshot at the start helps, and the board is used for games and quick-fire work rather than for extended problems. This is the stage where presence genuinely helps most, and families should weigh that honestly.
programmes.countryNote: For Dubai primary pupils the practical scheduling constraint is the school transport window, which can return a child home as late as 4.30pm, and the mandatory UAE subjects that KHDA requires add to an already long day. A shorter, earlier session is almost always better than a longer one after 6pm.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sixty minutes, with the criterion being worked on named at the start and revisited at the end. Middle Years pupils benefit from seeing a descriptor on screen beside their own work, which is difficult to arrange on paper and trivial on a shared board. Independent work inside the session matters more here than at primary level.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Middle Years pupils in schools that switch to IGCSE at Year 10 often have a mixed assessment diet in Year 9, and an online session can hold both the criterion descriptor and an IGCSE specification extract on screen at once, which is the clearest way to show a pupil why the same answer scores differently.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The stage the online model suits best. Diploma work is written, specification-bound and evidence-based, and a sixteen-year-old can work independently on a shared board while a tutor watches the method rather than the room. Marked scripts, mark schemes, criterion descriptors and the pupil's own attempt can all be on screen simultaneously, which no kitchen table manages.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma candidates sit the May session, and the final ten weeks are when the retained session archive earns its keep: a pupil revising from their own annotated scripts works on their own faults rather than on a generic revision guide. Confirm all session dates with your school's Diploma coordinator or the IB directly.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Sessions mix Diploma course teaching with process coaching on the reflective project, and the mix shifts across the year. Because so few Dubai schools license the programme, the tutor is frequently not in the emirate at all, which makes live video the only practical arrangement rather than a preference.
programmes.countryNote: A Career-related Programme candidate in Dubai may be the only one in their school. Screen sharing a published criterion document and working through it line by line substitutes, imperfectly but usefully, for the peer group and departmental experience that a Diploma candidate has around them.

dubai/ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: What the screen is used for differs by subject. Each entry below names the specific thing an online session can do in that subject that a paper-and-table session cannot.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The pupil works a problem line by line on the shared board while the tutor watches the method appear. That is the single most diagnostic activity in maths teaching, and it is easier online than in person because the written work is large, saved and reviewable rather than squeezed into a margin.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical output, a graphing tool and the question can be on screen together, which is how the interpretation step is actually taught. A pupil who writes a conclusion with the data visible beside it learns to refer back to context, which is where this course's marks sit.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mechanisms drawn arrow by arrow with the tutor stopping the pen at the moment it starts from the wrong place. Paper 1 stems can be annotated on screen, which turns stem-reading from advice into a visible procedure the pupil repeats twenty times.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Graph work, gradient interpretation and uncertainty handling all benefit from a shared surface and a saved record. Data from the pupil's own practical can be loaded and worked on directly, which is more useful than any demonstration.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mark schemes and the pupil's answer side by side, which is the fastest way to teach command-term discipline. Diagram labelling and data-based questions work well on screen, and the annotated versions are retained for revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams drawn live, labelled live, and then referenced in a written paragraph in the same session. The commentary portfolio can be worked with the article open beside the syllabus section list, which makes the coverage rule concrete rather than abstract.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case study can be annotated collaboratively across several sessions, building a single marked-up document the pupil keeps. That document is the preparation, and it is the main reason to start on the case study months before the paper.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Study banks built as a shared document, four facts per study, growing session by session. The write-up of the experimental study is reviewed against its criteria on screen, with the descriptor visible beside the pupil's own paragraph.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen texts annotated together in real time, which is exactly how Paper 1 is actually done under exam conditions. For Paper 2, two sets of notes can be displayed side by side so the comparative spine of each paragraph is visible rather than described.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Code and IB pseudocode can be shown together, which is the quickest cure for the commonest mark loss in the subject. Screen sharing a development environment while the pupil types means the tutor sees the error being made rather than the finished bug.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A claim, a counterclaim and an example mapped on a shared board as the conversation happens, so the structure of the argument becomes visible to the pupil. The map is saved, and the candidate writes their own essay from their own map.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Oral components rehearsed on video, which is closer to the assessment format than a conversation across a table. Recordings of the pupil's own practice can be reviewed for range used accurately rather than range attempted, which is what the marking rewards.

dubai/ib-online-tutor.regionsTitle: What online delivery changes in each part of Dubai
dubai/ib-online-tutor.regionsIntro: The practical value of removing the commute differs sharply across the emirate. These notes describe what changes for a family in each cluster.

regions.name: Dubai South and Jumeirah Golf Estates
regions.note: The longest drives in the emirate, and the communities where many tutors simply decline. Online delivery here is not a convenience but the difference between having a Higher Level specialist and having nobody.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Short distances made slow by congestion and parking. A tutor arriving at 5pm has typically spent 45 minutes travelling, and the family pays for it. Removing the journey makes a 45-minute clinic economically sensible rather than absurd.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Villa communities where in-home arrangements come with two-hour minimum blocks because of travel. Online sessions can be the length the pupil can actually concentrate for, which after a full school day is rarely two hours.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Mirdif
regions.note: Better served by resident tutors, so the online advantage here is subject depth rather than logistics. Diploma Higher Level specialists are scarce locally even though general tutors are plentiful.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: Apartment living with difficult visitor access and paid parking, all of which a tutor prices in. Pupils here often return from school late, so a 7pm or 8pm session is common and is straightforward online.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Central and well supplied with experienced tutors, so families here are genuinely choosing rather than defaulting. The deciding factor is usually whether the subject needed is a Higher Level science or a minority option.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: A long drive from most of the emirate's residential tutoring pool, and close to universities whose students tutor locally. The split between those two facts is why subject level matters more than price in this cluster.

regions.name: Al Khawaneej and Mushrif
regions.note: Low-density areas at the edge of most tutors' practical range, where availability rather than cost is the binding constraint. A specialist reachable by video is a different proposition from a generalist reachable by car.

schoolClusters.city: Schools whose Diploma candidates we support online
schoolClusters.note: Candidates from these cohorts most often need technique work on specific papers and criterion-level feedback on coursework, both of which suit a shared board and a retained record.

schoolClusters.city: Schools where the subject simply is not timetabled
schoolClusters.note: Smaller or newer Diploma cohorts that cannot staff every Higher Level option. For these candidates a national specialist pool reachable by video is the only available answer.

dubai/ib-online-tutor.modesIntro: Length and frequency should follow what the session is for. These three shapes cover almost all Dubai Diploma requests, and the shortest is often the most effective.

modes.title: Forty-five minute technique clinic
modes.description: A short, single-purpose session: one paper type, one command term, one convention. Impossible to buy from a tutor who has driven across the emirate, and the right length for a teenager at 6pm after a full school day plus transport. Three of these in a fortnight clears most convention faults.

No travel, so the length matches the attention span

modes.title: Sixty-minute weekly slot
modes.description: The standard shape: ten minutes on the pupil's latest work, thirty on the fault, fifteen of independent work watched live, five to set the next task and write the note. The same specialist each week, so corrections compound rather than restarting.

modes.title: Ninety-minute coursework session
modes.description: Reserved for sustained drafting work on an investigation, exploration or essay, where stopping at sixty minutes breaks the thread. Used a handful of times per subject per year rather than weekly, because ninety minutes of concentration is a genuine cost to a pupil's evening.

sections.heading: What an IB online tutor in Dubai does for sixty minutes
paragraphs: A Diploma session has four blocks and they are not negotiable in order, because each one depends on the previous. What follows is the actual structure, with what exists at the end of each block.

The first ten minutes are the pupil's most recent marked work on the shared board. Not a conversation about how school is going, which is pleasant and uses the most valuable minutes of the hour. The tutor and the pupil read the lost marks together and the tutor names the fault out loud, in the pupil's hearing, in specific terms: this answer scored two out of five because the explanation stops before the cause. A pupil who can name their own fault is already most of the way to fixing it.

The next thirty minutes work that fault, and the sequence matters. The tutor builds two or three worked examples live on the board, narrating the decision at each step rather than presenting a finished solution. Then the pupil takes the pen. The tutor's job during that stretch is to watch the method appear line by line and intervene at the step where it breaks, not after the wrong answer arrives. This is the part of teaching that a shared board does better than a sheet of paper, because both people see the same large, saved surface.

The final twenty minutes split in two. Fifteen are the pupil working independently on a question they have not seen, under something resembling exam conditions, while the tutor stays silent and watches. Five are for setting what the pupil will produce before the next session and writing the note that records the component, the criterion and what changed. The note takes two minutes and it is the artefact a parent will actually use.

sections.heading: The tools, and the job each one does
paragraphs: Online tutoring is often sold on its platform, which is the wrong emphasis. The tools matter only in so far as each replaces something a tutor in a room would do, and four of them do almost all the work.

The shared annotation board replaces the sheet of paper between two people at a desk, and improves on it in two respects: it is large enough for both to write without crowding, and it is saved. The screen share replaces looking over a shoulder, which is how a tutor watches a pupil use a graphing calculator, a spreadsheet or a development environment. Document upload replaces the folder of marked work in a school bag, with the difference that the tutor can read it before the session rather than during it.

The video window itself does the least work and gets the most attention. Its job is to carry tone and to let the tutor see whether a pupil is lost, which it does imperfectly. Most of a session's real attention is on the board, exactly as it would be at a desk, and a tutor who spends the hour looking at the pupil's face rather than at their working is doing the wrong thing in either format.

What should be ignored is the long tail of features that sound impressive. Recorded lessons are occasionally useful and mostly unwatched. Gamified progress dashboards measure attendance. Artificial intelligence assistants that generate practice questions produce material not written to the specification, which is worse than no material. The useful technology list is short, which is why nobody markets it.

sections.heading: Connection, bandwidth and the things that genuinely go wrong
paragraphs: Dubai's domestic connectivity is good, and the failures that affect sessions are rarely about raw bandwidth. They are about the household, the device and the room, and all three are fixable in advance by a family that knows to look.

The commonest failure is the device. A pupil joining on a phone cannot write on a shared board usefully and cannot see a mark scheme and their own answer at once, so the session degrades into a conversation. A tablet with a stylus is good. A laptop with a mouse is workable. A laptop with a cheap graphics tablet is better than either for mathematics and chemistry. A phone is not a solution for Diploma work, and a provider who says it is fine is managing you rather than teaching.

The second is the room. A pupil sitting in a living room with a television on will not sustain fifteen minutes of independent timed work, and the tutor will see the attention go without being able to do much about it. A door that closes matters more than a fast connection. The third is scheduling collisions with the household: a session at 7pm in a flat where dinner happens at 7pm fails for reasons nobody will mention.

Genuine technical failure happens occasionally and should have a stated answer rather than an apology. The practical arrangement is that a session dropping in the first ten minutes is rescheduled at no cost, a session lost mid-way is continued or credited, and the tutor keeps a phone number to confirm what is happening rather than leaving a parent watching a frozen screen. Ask any provider what their answer is before you need it.

sections.heading: How a science practical works when the tutor is not in the laboratory
paragraphs: This is the fair question about online science teaching, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a reassurance. A tutor over video cannot supervise a titration or stand beside a pupil adjusting an oscilloscope, and nobody should pretend otherwise.

What matters is that the practical work in a Diploma science is done in the pupil's school laboratory under their teacher's supervision, because it has to be. The assessed individual investigation is carried out there, with the school's equipment and the school's risk assessment. Private tutoring is not where practical work happens in any delivery format, including in-home: a tutor at a kitchen table in Dubai Marina is not running a laboratory either.

Where tutoring genuinely contributes is before and after the bench. Before: interrogating the research question until it has a controllable independent variable, planning a method that will produce enough data points, and anticipating which variables will need controlling. After: processing the data, propagating uncertainties, drawing a conclusion the data actually supports, and evaluating the method honestly. Those are the parts the criteria reward most heavily, and they are entirely screen-based work.

The same logic applies to examined practical skills. Paper 2 data-based questions and the data analysis section of the Higher Level paper test processing and interpretation of unfamiliar data, not manual dexterity. Those sections respond extremely well to a shared board loaded with real datasets, and they are the parts of the subject that classroom time most often runs out before reaching.

sections.heading: Scheduling against the Dubai week
paragraphs: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, which sounds trivial and is not. A family being offered slots by a UK agency is being offered a tutor's afternoon, which is a Dubai pupil's late evening, and the arrangement either produces a tired pupil or quietly collapses after a month.

The real constraints in a Dubai week are school transport, co-curricular commitments and the household. Bus routes can return a pupil as late as 4.30pm, which makes a 4pm slot impossible regardless of intention. CAS commitments, sports fixtures and music lessons occupy fixed evenings. Dinner is a real appointment. A slot chosen without mapping those three things is a slot that will be cancelled, and repeated cancellation is how arrangements end.

The UAE calendar adds two things no competitor page in this market mentions. School timings shorten during Ramadan and the working day changes, which redistributes when a pupil can concentrate: post-Iftar sessions often work better that month than a tired shortened afternoon. Eid holidays fall on a lunar calendar and move each year relative to the exam season, so the number of usable weeks before a deadline changes from year to year.

The practical benefit of video delivery here is flexibility that in-home arrangements cannot match. A post-Iftar session at 9pm is straightforward when nobody is driving across the emirate to reach it. So is a 7am weekend slot in the final weeks before the May session, which some candidates genuinely prefer and which no visiting tutor would offer.

sections.heading: The record an online session leaves behind
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement that cannot be audited cannot be judged, and the audit material is the main structural difference between a video session and a visit. This is not a claim about teaching quality; it is a claim about what exists on a hard drive in April.

After a visit, a family has whatever was written on paper and a verbal summary at the door. After a session on a shared board, a family has the annotated script, the worked examples the tutor built, the pupil's own attempts with the corrections in place, the timed attempt from the independent block, and a dated note naming the component and the criterion addressed. Across twenty sessions that is a diagnostic history and a revision archive at the same time.

The revision use is the one families notice late. In the final ten weeks before the May session, a candidate revising from their own annotated attempts is revising their own faults, in their own handwriting, with the correction already beside the error. That is more useful than any published revision guide, and it costs nothing extra because it was produced as a by-product of the teaching.

The audit use matters earlier. A four-week review that can point to the week-one fault statement, five session notes and a school-marked assessment is a judgement on evidence. A review that consists of a conversation about how things seem to be going is not, and the difference becomes visible at the mock, which is the most expensive moment to discover an arrangement was not working.

sections.heading: Attention, and the honest cost of a camera
paragraphs: A page arguing for online delivery should state what it loses, or it is advertising. Three things are genuinely worse over video, and a family for whom any of them is decisive should hire locally and pay the in-home premium without hesitation.

The first is reading the pupil. A tutor in a room notices a shoulder drop, a pen hovering, the particular stillness that means a pupil has stopped following and will not say so. A camera flattens all of that. Experienced online tutors compensate by asking the pupil to work visibly rather than to listen, which is why the independent block exists, but compensation is not equivalence.

The second is younger children. Physical presence helps with attention in a way nothing on a screen fully replaces, and the younger the pupil the more true that is. For a Year 3 pupil, a shorter session and a parent nearby makes online workable. For a Year 1 pupil it is often simply the wrong format, and saying so costs us a booking.

The third is specific access needs. A pupil who requires physical prompting, who has significant attention differences, or who uses assistive arrangements that depend on being in the room, may be better served by in-person support. IB Gram does not offer in-home visiting in the UAE in any case, so a family in that position should hire locally, with the permit and subject-level questions in hand. For a Diploma candidate working on written, specification-bound material, the balance generally runs the other way, because the scarce thing is a specialist in the exact subject rather than a person who can park.

sections.heading: Live video against a tutor crossing Dubai
paragraphs: With the losses stated, here is the comparison on the factors that actually decide a Diploma outcome. IB Gram offers no in-home service in the UAE, so this is the reasoning behind the model rather than a comparison between two things we sell.

On the specialist question, which is the binding constraint in this emirate, video wins decisively. A family in Dubai South choosing from tutors who can reach them is choosing from a handful of people; choosing from a national pool for Higher Level Chemistry is a different exercise entirely. Dubai runs 227 private schools across 17 curricula, and the Diploma is a minority programme within that, so local Higher Level supply is structurally thin everywhere in the emirate.

On session length, video wins because there is no travel to amortise. A 45-minute clinic is sensible rather than uneconomic, and a teenager at 6pm after a full school day plus transport concentrates better for 45 focused minutes than for a two-hour block bought because the tutor drove forty minutes to get there.

On record, video wins by construction, as set out above. On reading the pupil in the room, presence wins. On cost, published in-home rates run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to AED 450 or above for a specialist, which means the in-home floor sits roughly where the online specialist band tops out. A family can weigh all five and reach a different conclusion for a nine-year-old than for a Diploma candidate, which is the right outcome.

sections.heading: Does online tutoring work for IB candidates? The useful version of the question
paragraphs: Asked generally, the question cannot be answered, and the confident answers available online are marketing in both directions. Asked specifically, it resolves quickly, because the real variables are the pupil's age, the kind of work being done, and whether the alternative is a specialist or a generalist.

For written, specification-bound Diploma work with a candidate of sixteen or seventeen, live video is at least as effective as a visit and frequently better, for the structural reasons above: a larger shared writing surface, a retained record, no travel cost in the hour, and access to someone who has actually taught the level. The honest caveat is that this depends on the session being run properly. A video session consisting of a tutor talking at a pupil is worse than a visit consisting of the same thing, because the camera makes passivity easier.

For a primary pupil, presence helps, and the younger the child the more it helps. For a pupil with specific access needs, the answer is individual and should be decided with the people who know them. For practical laboratory work the answer is that it belongs in the school laboratory in every format.

The question families should actually ask is narrower and more answerable: for this subject, at this level, for this pupil, is the best available person reachable by car. In Dubai, for a Higher Level science or a minority Diploma option, the answer is usually no, and that is what settles it. For primary numeracy in Al Barsha, the answer is often yes, and a local tutor at budget-band rates is a sensible purchase.

process.title: Check the device before anything else
process.description: A tablet with a stylus, or a laptop with a cheap graphics tablet, changes a Diploma session more than any choice of platform. A phone will not support writing on a shared board or holding a mark scheme beside an answer, and a session on a phone degrades into a conversation.

process.title: Pick a slot that survives the Dubai week
process.description: Map school transport, co-curricular evenings and the household's dinner time before choosing. A slot that collides with any of the three gets cancelled repeatedly, and repeated cancellation is how tutoring arrangements quietly end.

process.title: Send a marked script in advance
process.description: Uploaded before the session rather than produced during it, so the tutor reads it beforehand and the first ten minutes are diagnosis rather than discovery. This single habit recovers more useful time across a term than any other change.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session with the proposed specialist at no cost and with no card required. Watch for two things: whether the board is in use within the first few minutes, and whether the pupil spends fifteen minutes working rather than listening.

process.title: Agree the failure rules in advance
process.description: What happens if a connection drops in minute five, in minute thirty, or if a pupil misses a session. Ask before you need to know. A provider with a clear answer has thought about it; one who improvises will improvise in your favour or not depending on the month.

whyPoints.title: The hour described, not advertised
whyPoints.description: Four blocks, with what exists at the end of each: an annotated script, saved worked examples, the pupil's own corrected attempts, a timed attempt and a dated note. A parent can check whether that happened, which is the point of describing it.

whyPoints.title: Fifteen minutes of the pupil working alone
whyPoints.description: The independent block is where a session is actually diagnostic, because the tutor watches the method appear and intervenes at the step where it breaks. It is also the part a passive online session leaves out, which is why it is worth asking about.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject, not on driving radius
whyPoints.description: Dubai runs 227 private schools across 17 curricula and the Diploma is a minority programme inside that, so local Higher Level supply is thin in every community. A national specialist pool is the practical answer rather than a selling point.

whyPoints.title: Gulf Standard Time, and the UAE calendar
whyPoints.description: Slots scheduled on local time rather than on a tutor's afternoon, with post-Iftar and early weekend sessions available because nobody is driving. Ramadan timings and moving Eid dates change how many usable weeks sit before a deadline, and the plan accounts for that.

whyPoints.title: An archive that becomes revision material
whyPoints.description: In the final weeks before the May session a candidate revises from their own annotated attempts, with each correction beside the error that produced it. That is more useful than a generic revision guide and it costs nothing extra, having been produced as a by-product.

whyPoints.title: The limits stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Reading a pupil in the room is genuinely better in person, younger children benefit from presence, and practical laboratory work belongs in the school laboratory in every format. A family for whom any of those is decisive should hire locally, and we say so.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the first ten minutes of an online IB session?
faqs.answer: The pupil's most recent marked script goes on the shared board and the lost marks are read together, with the tutor naming the fault aloud in specific terms: this answer scored two of five because the explanation stops before the cause. No introductions, no discussion of how school is going. A pupil who can name their own fault is most of the way to fixing it, and these are the most valuable minutes in the hour. If a session opens with conversation instead, the tutor has not read the work beforehand.

faqs.question: Does my child need a particular device for online IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Something they can write on. A tablet with a stylus is ideal, a laptop with an inexpensive graphics tablet is excellent for mathematics and chemistry, and a laptop with a mouse is workable. A phone is not adequate for Diploma work: the pupil cannot write usefully on a shared board and cannot hold a mark scheme and their own answer on screen at once, so the session collapses into a conversation. A wired headset solves most audio problems and costs very little.

faqs.question: How does a tutor watch my child work if they are not in the room?
faqs.answer: Through the shared board, which is arguably better than looking over a shoulder. The pupil writes their working line by line on a large surface both people see, and the tutor intervenes at the step where the method breaks rather than after a wrong answer arrives. Roughly half of a sixty-minute Diploma session is the pupil writing rather than listening, including fifteen minutes of timed independent work with the tutor silent. If that is not happening, the format is not being used properly.

faqs.question: How are IB science practicals handled if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: They happen in the school laboratory, under the school's supervision, which is where they happen in every delivery format including in-home tutoring. No private tutor runs a laboratory. What tutoring contributes is the work either side of the bench: interrogating the research question until it has a controllable variable, planning a method that produces enough data points, then processing data, propagating uncertainties and evaluating the method. Those parts carry most of the criteria marks and are entirely screen-based, which is why they suit video particularly well.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops mid-session?
faqs.answer: Ask for the rule in writing before you need it, from any provider. A workable arrangement is that a session lost in the first ten minutes is rescheduled at no cost, a session interrupted part way through is either continued or credited for the unused portion, and the tutor has a phone number to confirm what is happening rather than leaving a parent watching a frozen screen. Genuine technical failure is uncommon in Dubai and the household-side causes, device, room and timing, account for most problems.

faqs.question: Why does it matter that sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time?
faqs.answer: Because a tutor's convenient afternoon is a Dubai pupil's late evening, and arrangements built that way collapse within a month. Scheduling locally also means working around the things that actually bind in this emirate: school transport that can return a pupil at 4.30pm, fixed co-curricular evenings, and the household's dinner. A slot that collides with any of those gets cancelled repeatedly. Sessions over video also make post-Iftar and early weekend times practical, which no visiting tutor would offer.

faqs.question: Can online sessions move to post-Iftar timings during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one of the clearer practical advantages of video delivery. School timings shorten during Ramadan and the working day changes, which redistributes when a pupil can actually concentrate: many candidates work better after Iftar than in a tired shortened afternoon. A 9pm session is straightforward when nobody has to drive across the emirate for it. Worth doing at the same time: counting the genuinely usable weeks to each deadline, since Eid dates move each year relative to the exam season.

faqs.question: What do I have at the end of twenty online sessions that I would not have otherwise?
faqs.answer: Five things, all dated and in one place: the annotated marked scripts, the worked examples the tutor built, the pupil's own attempts with corrections in position, one timed independent attempt per session, and short written notes naming the component and criterion addressed. After a visiting tutor, a family typically has whatever was written on paper and a doorstep summary. The archive has two uses: the four-week review becomes a judgement on evidence, and in the final weeks it is revision material specific to that pupil's faults.

faqs.question: Is anything genuinely worse about learning over video?
faqs.answer: Yes, three things, and a provider who denies it is advertising. Reading a pupil's body language is worse: a camera flattens the shoulder drop and the particular stillness that means someone has stopped following. Younger children benefit from physical presence, and the younger the child the more that is true. And a pupil with specific access needs may genuinely be better served in person. For written, specification-bound Diploma work with a sixteen-year-old, the balance usually runs the other way, because the scarce thing is subject expertise rather than proximity.

faqs.question: Can a 45-minute online clinic achieve anything on a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: For one specific fault, yes, and it is often the better purchase. A single-purpose clinic on one paper type, one command term or one convention fits what a teenager can concentrate on at 6pm after a full school day and transport. Three of those in a fortnight clears most convention faults. The reason this length barely exists in the in-home market is economic rather than pedagogical: nobody drives forty minutes across Dubai for 45 minutes of teaching, so two-hour minimums appear instead.

faqs.question: Do recorded lessons and progress dashboards actually help?
faqs.answer: Much less than they are marketed. Recordings are occasionally useful for a missed concept and mostly go unwatched. Progress dashboards generally measure attendance, which is not evidence of anything. Practice questions generated automatically are usually not written to the specification, which makes them worse than no material because they teach the wrong answer shape. The short list of tools that genuinely matter is a shared writing board, screen sharing, document upload and a written session note, which is why nobody advertises it.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor help with the pre-released Business Management case study?
faqs.answer: By building one annotated document with the candidate across several sessions, starting months before the paper. The case study is released well in advance, which makes it the most predictable preparation window in the Diploma and the most commonly wasted. Each session adds analysis of a different part of the stimulus with a tool applied to it rather than described. The document persists and the candidate keeps it, which is the practical point: a shared file grows across a year in a way a pile of handwritten notes does not.

faqs.question: Can oral components for languages be rehearsed over video?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the format is closer to the assessment than a conversation across a table. The individual oral is a prepared analysis delivered to a listener, which is structurally what a video session already is. Practice can be recorded and reviewed with the candidate for the thing the marking actually rewards, which is range used accurately rather than range attempted. A candidate who hears themselves attempt eight complex structures and control four usually narrows their repertoire voluntarily, which is the correct outcome.

faqs.question: What should I watch for in a trial online lesson to judge quality?
faqs.answer: Two things, both visible within ten minutes. First, is the shared board in use almost immediately, with the pupil's own marked work on it, or is the tutor talking. Second, does the pupil spend a substantial part of the hour writing rather than listening, including a stretch of timed independent work with the tutor silent. A session where a tutor explains well for sixty minutes is pleasant and diagnoses nothing. Ask also what the written note after the session will say, and check whether it names a criterion.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram offer in-person lessons as an alternative in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Teaching for every UAE family is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. A family who specifically wants someone physically present, and for a young child or a pupil with particular access needs that can be the right judgement, should hire locally. Two questions make that safer: whether the individual holds a current private tuition work permit, and one subject-specific question only someone who has taught the level can answer.

dubai/ib-online-tutor.closingHeading: Watch one session before deciding anything
dubai/ib-online-tutor.closingBody: The useful way to judge an IB online tutor in Dubai is to watch an hour of one. Send the subject, the level and one recent marked script, and the trial session will open on that script rather than on introductions. Watch for the board being used in the first few minutes, for the pupil writing rather than listening, and for fifteen minutes of timed independent work with the tutor silent. It costs nothing, no card is required and there is nothing to cancel. Afterwards you will have an annotated script, a written fault statement and a note naming what the first four weeks would target.

intro.heading: The papers are not the expensive part
paragraphs: Almost every Dubai family searching for IB past paper practice assumes the hard part is getting the papers. It is not. The hard part is that an unmarked paper teaches a student very little. Sitting a Higher Level paper takes two hours; marking it honestly against the published markscheme takes most of another hour, question by question, with the markscheme's accepted alternatives beside each answer. A student who sits ten papers and marks none of them properly has spent twenty hours learning that the papers are hard.

So the sensible unit of cost here is not an hour of tutoring. It is one complete marked attempt: the paper sat under timing, marked to the scheme, and then reworked question by question with the lost marks named. On published Dubai rates of AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB specialist, one properly marked Higher Level paper with a rework session is a real sum, and it is worth knowing that before buying a package quoted in hours.

There is a second cost most pages never mention. IB past papers and markschemes are copyright material. They are not ours to send you, and they are not the free commodity the aggregator sites imply. Schools access them through the IB's own resource channels, the IB sells past paper packs through its store, and subject guides contain specimen material. A tutoring site that emails you a folder of papers is distributing someone else's copyright, and the student is the one left relying on files that may be the wrong syllabus version.

What a tutor adds, then, is not access. It is the markscheme discipline: knowing what the scheme pays for, recognising the command term the question actually used, spotting that an answer is correct and unawardable because it is written at the wrong assessment objective. That is the service, and it is the thing worth paying AED 250 an hour for. Access to a PDF is not.

Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video with the paper and the markscheme on a shared screen. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, as that is an India-only service, and for paper work the online format is the practical one: the student's own script is on screen, annotated live, and the annotations stay in the file for the next session.

The rest of this page covers where the papers legitimately come from and what each source costs, how command terms decide marks, how the paper structures differ by subject family, the three-pass method that makes a marked paper worth sitting, and what the whole plan costs in Dubai with every figure attributed to whoever published it.

dubai/ib-past-papers-practice.programmesIntro: Past paper practice means different things at each stage, and buying the wrong version is a common waste. The three stages below are the ones Dubai IB families are working with, and each has a different honest answer on papers.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: There is no bank of MYP past papers to work through, because most MYP assessment is internal and criterion-based. The external on-screen examinations at the end of year five are task-based and built on unfamiliar stimulus, so useful practice is teacher-set tasks and specimen material rather than a historical paper archive.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai MYP families regularly ask for MYP past papers and are sold something that does not exist in the form they imagine. The honest substitute is criterion-marked tasks from the school plus any specimen material the coordinator can share, and a tutor who says so is saving you money rather than losing a sale.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: Papers are useful in DP1 only topic by topic, because the syllabus is incomplete. The right practice is extracting single questions on taught topics and marking them to the scheme, which trains command-term accuracy early. Whole papers sat in DP1 mostly demonstrate that the untaught half is untaught.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools run DP1 internal examinations towards the end of the year, and that is the first realistic point for a part-paper under timing. Before then, the better spend is on the Internal Assessment and on building the habit of checking an answer against a markscheme rather than against a textbook.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: The year whole papers earn their cost. A DP2 student is revising six subjects plus the core, so the scarce resource is time rather than papers. Practice has to be prioritised by where marks are actually lost, which is why the first marked paper in each subject matters more than the tenth.
programmes.countryNote: The May session is the one most Dubai schools sit, with mock examinations typically falling in the second term. Specific IB examination and results dates are set by the IB and are not published here, because none has been verified from an official source for this page; your Diploma coordinator holds the confirmed dates for your school.

dubai/ib-past-papers-practice.subjectsIntro: Paper structures differ sharply by subject, and so does what past paper practice should target. The grid below names the component where marks are most often recoverable in each subject rather than restating the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without technology and Paper 2 with it, and students who practise only with a calculator to hand are unprepared for the first. HL adds a Paper 3 of extended investigative questions, where marks go on explaining a method rather than reaching an answer.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is permitted across the papers, which misleads students into treating questions as button sequences. Marks are lost on interpreting results in context and on stating assumptions. HL Paper 3 is a long data investigation and rewards structured commentary.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data-based questions are where the recoverable marks sit, because they test reading a graph or table precisely rather than recall. Practice should be weighted towards those and towards extended response structure, with terminology checked against the markscheme's accepted wording.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation questions carry method marks that students lose by not writing steps, and organic mechanism questions carry marks for arrows and intermediates that a correct product does not earn. Both are visible on a marked script and fixable within a few papers.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Units, significant figures and the explicit statement of a physical principle are where scripts bleed marks. A student can reach the right number and score below half on the question. Marked papers expose this faster than any amount of worked-example reading.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy with correct labels and a stated direction of change earns marks independently of the prose. Evaluation at the end of extended responses is the most commonly missing element, and it is the difference between a competent answer and a high one.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source papers are mechanical once the structure is learned: value and limitations tied to origin, purpose and content rather than to generic comment. Essay questions reward a line of argument held across paragraphs rather than a sequence of accurate facts.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis of an unseen text and a comparative essay. Practice value comes from writing to the clock and from comparing two of the student's own attempts, because the improvement is structural and visible between drafts.

subjects.name: Language B: French, Spanish, Arabic
subjects.description: Reading and listening components reward exam technique as much as language: locating the answer, respecting the word limit, matching the register the task asks for. Writing tasks lose marks on text type conventions rather than on grammar.

dubai/ib-past-papers-practice.regionsIntro: Whole papers need an uninterrupted two hours, which is a scheduling problem rather than a geographic one. These notes are about when a Dubai household can realistically find that block.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and Dubai Hills
regions.note: Villa communities feeding full-continuum IB schools, so DP2 cohorts here are large and mock timetables cluster. Weekend mornings are the realistic slot for a timed Higher Level paper, and they book out early in the second term.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Barsha Heights
regions.note: Short commutes make a 16:30 start possible, which is unusual in Dubai and useful for a two-hour paper on a weekday. Worth taking if your child's school is in this cluster rather than defaulting to the weekend.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Mixed British and IB households, which means IGCSE mock papers and Diploma mocks in the same term. Two timed papers in one weekend is too much for most students; splitting them across a fortnight works better.

regions.name: Mirdif and Dubai Festival City
regions.note: A long eastern commute, so weekday timed papers rarely survive. Families here tend to run the sitting at home on a Saturday morning and the rework session on a weekday evening, which is a sensible split.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown
regions.note: Apartments with limited quiet space, where a two-hour silent sitting is harder to arrange than the tutoring. A paper split into two timed halves, clearly logged as such, is better than a sitting interrupted halfway through.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: University-belt families, often with strong Higher Level maths and science cohorts. Demand here concentrates on Paper 3 practice, which is short, specific and often the highest-return paper to mark.

schoolClusters.city: Western Dubai Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Large DP2 cohorts with internal mock timetables that drive demand for marked papers in a narrow window. Booking the marking capacity before the mock season rather than during it is the single practical advantage available to a family here.

schoolClusters.city: Central and eastern Dubai Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: A mix of continuum IB schools and schools where the Diploma sits alongside other curricula. Students here often arrive in DP1 from IGCSE and have never seen a markscheme, which makes the first marked paper unusually informative.

sections.heading: Where IB past papers legitimately come from, and what each source costs
paragraphs: IB past papers, markschemes and subject guides are copyright material belonging to the International Baccalaureate. That is not a technicality that only lawyers care about: it determines which copies are current, which have been altered, and whether a student is practising the syllabus they are actually sitting. A tutoring site that hands you a shared drive of papers is distributing someone else's material and giving you no way to know which syllabus version you have.

The legitimate routes are short to list. Your child's school holds access to IB resources through the IB's own channels and teachers can set past paper material from them, which makes the Diploma coordinator the first and cheapest place to ask. The IB sells past paper packs through its own store, which gives you clean, current files for a known price. Subject guides contain specimen papers and markschemes. Any of these is a better basis for practice than a free aggregator.

The aggregator sites deserve a specific warning rather than a general one. Beyond the copyright position, the practical risks are that the paper belongs to a superseded syllabus, that the markscheme has been retyped with errors, and that the file set is incomplete in exactly the way that matters, such as a missing data booklet. A student whose first experience of a markscheme is a retyped one learns the wrong accepted wording, which is the opposite of the point.

The table sets the sources against each other. Note what is absent from every row: IB Gram. We reference and link official sources and we do not distribute papers or markschemes, because they are not ours to give and because the version control matters more than the convenience.

sections.heading: Command terms are what the markscheme actually pays for
paragraphs: Every IB subject guide publishes a list of command terms and ties them to assessment objectives. State, outline, describe, explain, discuss, evaluate, justify, compare and contrast, deduce, determine: each one names a different depth of response, and the markscheme is written for that depth. An answer written at the wrong depth can be entirely correct and earn nothing, which is the single most frustrating experience in IB marking and the easiest to fix.

The pattern is consistent across subjects. Low-objective terms such as state and define want a short, exact response and are over-answered by able students who write a paragraph where a line was wanted, wasting time they later need. High-objective terms such as discuss and evaluate want a judgement supported both ways and are under-answered by students who describe accurately and never judge. Both errors are habits rather than knowledge gaps.

Working from a marked script is what breaks the habit, because the student sees their own correct sentence next to a markscheme that did not pay for it. In practice two or three papers is enough for a student to start reading the command term before the stem, which is the behaviour you are paying for. After that, the same student gains marks across every subject that shares the term list.

The table below pairs common command terms with what the scheme expects and the loss each one invites. Print it and keep it beside the student while they mark their own script; self-marking with the term list visible is the cheapest version of this intervention and it works.

sections.heading: Paper structures differ, so practice has to differ too
paragraphs: A student revising six subjects cannot practise all of them the same way, and the schedule most families write treats every paper as interchangeable. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches sits Paper 1 without technology and Paper 2 with it, so a student who always has a calculator to hand is systematically under-practised on half the subject. Applications and Interpretation permits technology throughout, which produces the opposite problem: fluent button use and weak interpretation.

Higher Level Paper 3 in maths is a separate discipline again. It is short, investigative, and awards marks for setting out a method and justifying steps rather than for a final answer. Students routinely skip it in revision because there are fewer past versions available, which is exactly why marking two of them properly has an unusually high return per hour.

In the sciences, data-based questions are the most recoverable component, because they test precise reading of a graph or table rather than memory. In history, source questions are mechanical once the structure is internalised: origin, purpose and content, then value and limitations that follow from them. In the language subjects, the loss is in text type conventions and word limits rather than in vocabulary.

The table maps the subject families to the practice that pays. Use it to allocate a fixed number of marked papers rather than to extend the schedule, because the constraint in the final Diploma year is hours in the week and not availability of papers. Confirm the current component pattern for each of your child's subjects against the subject guide the school is teaching from, since several guides have been revised in recent years and a paper from an older session may not match the structure your child will actually sit.

sections.heading: The three-pass method that makes a marked paper worth sitting
paragraphs: Most students sit a paper, see a mark, feel briefly bad about it and move on. That cycle costs two hours and teaches almost nothing. The method that extracts value has three passes over the same script, and the second and third are where the marks come from. It is simple enough that a student can run it alone once they have been shown it twice, which is the honest goal of paid support here.

The first pass is the sitting itself, under real timing, with no notes and no pausing. The timing is not a detail: a paper done over three evenings with a textbook open measures something other than the examination. The second pass is self-marking against the markscheme before anybody else sees it, which forces the student to read what the scheme actually pays for and is the single highest-return twenty minutes in the process.

The third pass is the tutor's. The script is re-marked independently, the two marks are compared, and every discrepancy is discussed, because a discrepancy means the student misread either the question or the scheme. Each lost mark is then classified as content not known, command term misread, method not shown, or time ran out. Those four categories drive completely different responses, and lumping them together as revise more is why plans stall.

The output is an error log the student maintains: paper reference, question, category of loss, and the fix. Over three papers the log shows a pattern, and the pattern is usually narrower than anyone expected. Students discover that half their losses in chemistry are method marks and none are content, which turns a vague fear of the subject into a specific habit to change.

sections.heading: What a past paper plan costs in Dubai, priced per marked paper
paragraphs: Three questions let a parent verify any quote in this market. How long is the session. Is marking of work outside the session included. And how many complete marked papers will exist at the end of the block. A provider who answers all three in writing is quoting something comparable; a provider who answers in hours and subjects is not, and the difference is usually the marking.

The published Dubai bands give the arithmetic. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 an hour. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for an IB specialist. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED's premium named tier reaches AED 650. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate, with independent tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in.

Translate that into marked papers. A Higher Level paper needs roughly forty to fifty minutes of marking plus a sixty-minute rework session, so call it two chargeable hours per marked paper with a specialist. At the mid band that is AED 300 to 600 per marked paper; at the specialist band, AED 400 to 900. A term of one paper a fortnight in two subjects is therefore a substantial commitment, and seeing it stated that way is more useful than a monthly figure that hides the volume.

What that reframing changes is the decision. Families often buy weekly hours in six subjects and end the term with no complete marked paper in any of them. Buying four marked papers in the two weakest subjects costs less and produces evidence. Every figure in this section belongs to the provider that published it; IB Gram quotes its own rate after the free trial lesson, stating the session length and whether marking is included.
