sections.heading: Why a good school report and a bad past paper score live together
paragraphs: This combination arrives in nearly every first conversation. The student is doing well in school assessments and scoring two or three grades lower on past papers, and the family reasonably suspects the school, the tutor or the student. Usually it is none of them. School assessments are often set on the topic just taught, with familiar question styles and a teacher who knows what was covered. A past paper samples the whole syllabus in the examiner's own wording.

Three specific gaps produce most of the drop. Breadth: a topic taught eight months ago has decayed and nothing in school has required it since. Wording: the paper uses the command term list rather than the teacher's phrasing. And endurance: a two-hour paper at the end of a school day measures something a forty-minute class test does not, and students lose marks in the final third at a rate that has nothing to do with knowledge.

Each of those has a different fix, and naming which one is operating is the whole value of the first marked paper. A decay problem needs interleaved review of old topics. A wording problem needs command term work and costs very little. An endurance problem needs full-length sittings and sleep, which no tutor can sell you and should say so.

What this also means is that the first past paper score is not a prediction. It is a measurement taken before any of the examination-specific work has happened, and treating it as a forecast is both inaccurate and demoralising. The number that matters is the gap between the first and third marked papers in the same subject, sat under the same conditions.

sections.heading: Marking honestly: what a tutor can and cannot claim
paragraphs: A tutor marks to the published markscheme. That is a real skill and a limited claim, and the limit matters. A markscheme lists accepted answers and allowed alternatives; applying it consistently to a student's own wording takes practice and judgement. What it does not give anybody is access to grade boundaries for a future session, to unreleased material, or to how a particular examiner would behave on a borderline response.

Grade boundaries move session by session, which is why no boundary is quoted on this page as a fixed figure. A raw mark converted using last session's boundaries is an estimate, and it should be presented as one. A tutoring site that tells you a raw mark equals a grade 6 is adding a precision that does not exist, and a family making a university decision on that number is being misled.

IB Gram also does not describe tutors as IB examiners. Examiner status is a specific appointment, it changes, and it is not evidence we can show you for every tutor on a platform. Where a tutor's examining experience is current and evidenced it can be stated on their own profile; it will not appear as a blanket claim on a landing page, and it would never imply access to marking decisions or paper content.

The honest offer, then, is narrower and more useful than the usual one. A tutor will mark a whole paper to the published scheme, show you the marked script, record the raw mark with the paper reference and the date, give an estimate band with the caveat attached, and name the four categories your child's lost marks fall into. Everything on this page is designed so you can check that offer rather than take it on trust.

process.title: Ask the school for the paper first
process.description: The Diploma coordinator and subject teachers hold legitimate access to current IB material, and that is the cheapest and most reliable source. Ask which papers the school will set and when. Coming to a tutor with a school-set paper already in hand removes any question about syllabus version and any question about copyright.

process.title: Sit one whole paper under timing at home
process.description: No notes, no pausing, full duration, in one sitting. Then self-mark against the markscheme before anyone else sees it. That self-marking is unpleasant and is the highest-return twenty minutes in the whole process, because it forces the student to read what the scheme actually pays for.

process.title: A free trial lesson spent on that script
process.description: The trial is a real session with the tutor who would continue, with no card details taken beforehand, and it is spent on the student's own marked script rather than on introductions. By the end you should have the four categories of loss named and a proposed number of sessions with an end date.

process.title: A paper a fortnight, with the marks logged
process.description: Comparable papers at intervals, each sat under the same conditions, each raw mark recorded with the paper reference and date. The interim sessions work the topics the last script exposed. The measure of progress is the gap between the first and third marked papers, not the tutor's impression.

process.title: Hand the method back to the student
process.description: Once a student can self-mark accurately and maintain an error log, the paid part should shrink. A tutor who has shown the method twice and then audits it monthly costs a fraction of weekly sessions and produces a student who can revise without supervision, which is the outcome worth aiming at.

whyPoints.title: Priced per marked paper
whyPoints.description: The quote states how many complete marked papers will exist at the end of the block. That is a number you can hold somebody to, unlike a weekly hour in six subjects which can run a whole term without producing a single full marked script.

whyPoints.title: We link the official sources and distribute nothing
whyPoints.description: IB papers, markschemes and guides are the IB's copyright and are not ours to send. The school and the IB's own store are the routes, and saying so protects you from practising a superseded syllabus from a retyped file.

whyPoints.title: Lost marks classified, not just counted
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark is sorted into content not known, command term misread, method not shown, or time ran out. Those four need different responses, and separating them is what turns a disappointing score into a short list of specific habits to change.

whyPoints.title: Estimates carry their caveat
whyPoints.description: Grade boundaries move by session, so a raw mark converted to a grade is an estimate and is labelled as one. No boundary is published here as fixed, and no tutor is described as an IB examiner without evidence that could be shown.

whyPoints.title: Online, with the script on the screen
whyPoints.description: Sessions run over live video with the student's own marked script shared and annotated live, and the annotations stay in the file. No home visits are offered anywhere in the UAE, which removes the travel premium in every published Dubai rate table.

faqs.question: Where can we legally get IB past papers in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Three routes. Your child's school holds legitimate access to IB material and the Diploma coordinator or subject teacher can set past paper work from it, which is the cheapest and most reliable source. The IB sells past paper packs through its own store, giving you current files for a known price. Subject guides contain specimen papers and markschemes. Any of those is better than a free aggregator, where the common problems are superseded syllabus versions, retyped markschemes with errors, and missing supporting material such as a data booklet.

faqs.question: Why will you not just send us a folder of papers and markschemes?
faqs.answer: Because they are not ours to send. IB past papers, markschemes and subject guides are the International Baccalaureate's copyright, and distributing them is a breach regardless of how commonly it is done. There is also a practical reason that matters more to your child: files passed around privately are frequently the wrong syllabus version or retyped with errors, and a student who learns a markscheme's accepted wording from a flawed copy has learned the wrong thing. We reference and link the official sources instead.

faqs.question: How many IB past papers should my child actually do?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most revision plans assume, marked far more carefully. Three complete marked papers in a subject, each self-marked then independently re-marked and reworked, usually reveal the full pattern of where marks are being lost. A fourth and fifth add confirmation rather than information. The common failure is ten papers sat and none marked properly, which costs twenty hours and teaches that the papers are hard. Prioritise two subjects, complete the cycle in both, then decide where the next hours go.

faqs.question: What does it cost to have a full IB paper marked in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Work it out from the published hourly bands rather than from a package price. Marking a Higher Level paper against the scheme takes roughly forty to fifty minutes, and the rework session that recovers the marks takes an hour, so budget about two chargeable hours per marked paper. At Dubai's published rates of AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor and AED 200 to 450 for an IB specialist, that is roughly AED 300 to 900 per marked paper. Ask any provider how many marked papers their block produces.

faqs.question: Are the free IB past paper websites safe to use?
faqs.answer: They carry two risks, and the copyright one is not the risk to your child. The practical dangers are a paper from a superseded syllabus, a markscheme retyped with errors, and an incomplete file set missing the data booklet or formula sheet the real paper assumes. A student practising from any of those is calibrating against the wrong standard. If the file came from a site rather than from the school or the IB, check the session and syllabus version before your child spends two hours on it.

faqs.question: Do IB grade boundaries stay the same from one session to the next?
faqs.answer: No. Boundaries are set per session and move, which is why no boundary figure is published on this page as fixed. A raw mark converted using a previous session's boundaries is an estimate and should always be labelled as one. This matters for real decisions: a family choosing a university offer on the basis of a converted mock mark is acting on a number with error bars that nobody states. Ask for the raw mark and the paper reference, and treat the implied grade as indicative.

faqs.question: Should my child practise by topic or sit whole papers under timing?
faqs.answer: Both, in that order, and the stage decides the mix. In the first Diploma year the syllabus is incomplete, so topic questions marked to the scheme are the right purchase and whole papers mostly demonstrate that the untaught half is untaught. In the final year whole papers earn their cost, because breadth, wording and endurance are what separate a school test result from an examination result. A reasonable rhythm in the final year is one full paper a fortnight with topic work between them.

faqs.question: What is a command term and why does it decide the mark?
faqs.answer: Every IB subject guide publishes a list of command terms tied to assessment objectives, and the markscheme is written for the depth the term demands. State wants one exact point. Explain wants a mechanism. Evaluate wants a judgement supported both ways. An answer written at the wrong depth can be completely correct and earn nothing, which is the most common recoverable loss on a marked script. Two or three marked papers is usually enough for a student to start reading the command term before the question stem.

faqs.question: Which IB mathematics papers allow a calculator?
faqs.answer: In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without technology and Paper 2 with it, so a student who always revises with a calculator to hand is under-practised on half the subject. In Applications and Interpretation technology is permitted across the papers, which produces the opposite weakness: fluent button use and thin interpretation of what the output means. Higher Level students in both courses also sit Paper 3, which rewards setting out and justifying a method rather than reaching a final answer, and is often the highest-return paper to mark.

faqs.question: My child does well in school tests and badly on past papers. Why?
faqs.answer: Three causes account for most of it. Breadth, because a school test samples the topic just taught while a paper samples the whole syllabus including material last seen eight months ago. Wording, because the paper uses the published command terms rather than the teacher's phrasing. And endurance, because marks fall away in the final third of a two-hour paper for reasons unrelated to knowledge. Each needs a different response, and naming which one is operating is the main value of the first properly marked paper.

faqs.question: Do you run in-person past-paper sessions at our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, because that is an India-only service, and every session is delivered online over live video. For paper work this is the practical format rather than a compromise. The student's own script is shared on screen and annotated live, the annotations stay in the file for the next session, and the raw marks accumulate in one place. It also removes the travel premium that sits between the published online and in-home rate bands in this market.

faqs.question: When should past paper practice start in the final Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Early enough that the first marked paper is a diagnosis rather than a verdict, which in practice means well before the school's mock window. Sitting the first paper a fortnight before mocks leaves no time to act on what it shows. Sitting it at the start of the second term gives space for three cycles in the weakest two subjects. Ask the school when its mocks fall, then work backwards, and book marking capacity before the mock season rather than during it, when every tutor in the city is full.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's paper the way an examiner would?
faqs.answer: A tutor marks to the published markscheme, consistently and with the accepted alternatives applied, and that is a real and useful skill. It is not the same as being an examiner, and IB Gram does not describe tutors as IB examiners on a landing page, because examiner status is a specific appointment that changes and that we could not evidence for every tutor. Where it is current and evidenced it belongs on an individual profile. Nobody has access to future boundaries or unreleased material, whatever a site claims.

faqs.question: How do we keep an error log, and does it actually change anything?
faqs.answer: Four columns are enough: paper reference, question number, category of loss, and the fix. The categories are content not known, command term misread, method not shown, and time ran out. The log works because it turns a vague sense of weakness into a pattern, and the pattern is almost always narrower than the student feared. A typical finding is that most chemistry losses are method marks and none are content, which changes the revision plan from reread the topic to write the steps down.

faqs.question: Is it worth buying specimen papers or past paper packs from the IB store?
faqs.answer: Often yes, particularly where the school cannot supply much and the subject has recently changed guides. The value is version certainty: you know the paper matches the syllabus your child is sitting and the markscheme has not been retyped. Specimens show format rather than the breadth of a real session, so they are better used early to learn the paper's shape than late to simulate the examination. Check with the coordinator first, because the school may already hold what you are about to buy.

dubai/ib-past-papers-practice.closingHeading: One paper, marked properly, before anything else
dubai/ib-past-papers-practice.closingBody: If you do one thing after reading this, make it this: ask the school for a current paper in your child's weakest subject, have them sit it under real timing in one go, and have them self-mark it against the markscheme before anybody else sees it. Then book the free trial lesson and spend it on that script. By the end of the session you should know which of the four categories your child's lost marks fall into, and you should have a proposed number of sessions with an end date and a count of marked papers. That is a quote you can check, which is the point of every figure on this page.

dubai/ib-physics-ia-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors below supervise Physics investigations specifically. Each has read drafts against the four criteria, works comfortably with uncertainty propagation and linearisation, and will say in the first session whether a proposed experiment can produce data good enough to analyse.

intro.heading: A Physics investigation is marked on what the data can support
paragraphs: Every Diploma Physics student, standard or higher level, submits one scientific investigation of up to about 3,000 words. It is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The school teacher marks it and the IB moderates a sample. It is worth roughly a fifth of the Physics grade, and in a subject where the papers are unforgiving, that fifth is the most controllable part of the course.

What distinguishes Physics from the other two sciences in this task is uncertainty. A Biology investigation lives or dies on statistical treatment; a Chemistry investigation on control of chemically significant variables; a Physics investigation on whether the numbers the student reports are supported by the precision of the instruments they used. Dubai school laboratories are generally well equipped, so students collect good raw data, write instrument uncertainties correctly into the table, and then compute a gradient as though those uncertainties had disappeared.

That single fault cascades through three of the four criteria. Data analysis loses marks because the processing is incomplete without propagated uncertainty. The conclusion loses marks because a result quoted to four significant figures from data supporting two is a claim the evidence does not justify. Evaluation loses marks because the limitations discussion has no quantitative handle on what each weakness did to the answer. One missing step, three criteria affected, and it is a step that can be taught in a single session.

The second pattern is linearisation. A great many Physics investigations examine a relationship that is not linear, and the analysis that earns marks plots a transformed pair of variables so the relationship becomes a straight line whose gradient means something physical. Students who plot the raw variables and fit a curve by eye have produced a graph that looks like data and supports no quantitative conclusion. Deciding what to plot against what belongs in the planning stage, before the laboratory session, not afterwards.

Our role is narrow and technical. We check a proposed investigation will yield analysable data, teach uncertainty propagation and linearisation, read the student's own draft once per criterion and state the band each sits in, and name the next job. The student performs the experiment, processes the data and writes the report. Nothing is calculated for them and no passage is written for them, because the investigation carries an academic honesty declaration that the student signs.

Sessions run online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared screen. A Physics IA session is a spreadsheet, a graph with error bars and a propagation calculation on the same screen, annotated live, with the file staying with the student. It also means a family in Dubai gets a tutor who has supervised Physics investigations rather than whichever science tutor can reach their community by seven in the evening.

Roughly a fifth of the Physics grade at both levels
Uncertainty must be propagated into the gradient and the result
Linearisation should be decided before the laboratory session
Evaluation needs the effect of each limitation, not a list of them
About 3,000 words, teacher-marked and externally moderated

dubai/ib-physics-ia-help.programmesIntro: Physics is assessed differently at each stage of the IB continuum, and Dubai students arrive at the Diploma investigation from several different starting points. Here is what each stage asks for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics at standard or higher level, with the same scientific investigation required at both. The four criteria are identical across Physics, Chemistry and Biology, which means a family with two children in different sciences is dealing with one mark scheme. Higher level adds syllabus content and additional paper material rather than a different investigation.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Physics higher level groups are often small, sometimes four or five students, and may be taught alongside standard level for part of the timetable. The practical consequence is limited peer benchmarking on what a strong investigation looks like, and limited laboratory technician time for individual experimental setups.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria including inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating, which rehearse the Diploma investigation closely. A student who has written MYP science investigations already understands variables, controls and the idea that an evaluation must say something specific.
programmes.countryNote: Continuum schools in Dubai give students five years of criterion-marked science investigations before the Diploma, and it shows. Students arriving at Year 12 from an IGCSE Physics course have usually done practical work assessed by an examination paper rather than by writing, and the gap is in reporting rather than in physics.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students taking Diploma Physics submit the same scientific investigation against the same four criteria. The difference is in the core, where a reflective project replaces TOK and the Extended Essay, and in the career-related study that sits alongside the subject courses.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is a minority route in Dubai and Physics is not a common component of CP packages. Families considering it should confirm with the school which science courses are available and at which level, because the internally assessed requirement does not reduce.

dubai/ib-physics-ia-help.subjectsIntro: Investigation topics come from the syllabus, and some areas produce analysable data far more reliably than others in a school laboratory. These are the areas Dubai Physics students use most, with what each delivers.

subjects.name: Simple harmonic motion
subjects.description: Pendulums and mass-spring systems give clean, repeatable timing data and a relationship that linearises neatly. The risk is that the experiment is so standard that research design marks depend entirely on the quality of the student's own refinements.

subjects.name: Resistivity and electrical circuits
subjects.description: Reliable data from accessible equipment, with instrument uncertainties that are easy to state and propagate. Students lose marks by ignoring heating effects, which change the quantity being measured during the measurement.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and specific heat capacity
subjects.description: Accessible but leaky: heat losses dominate and must be quantified rather than mentioned. An investigation that models the loss, or measures it separately, moves from a mid band to a strong one on evaluation.

subjects.name: Projectile and rotational motion
subjects.description: Video analysis makes this far more tractable than it once was, and frame-rate uncertainty becomes the interesting measurement problem. Needs care because repeated launches are rarely identical and that variability has to be reported honestly.

subjects.name: Optics, refraction and diffraction
subjects.description: Angle measurements carry large percentage uncertainties at small angles, which makes propagation genuinely consequential. A student who understands why their uncertainty blows up near zero has material for a strong evaluation.

subjects.name: Waves on strings and in air columns
subjects.description: Resonance experiments produce a linear relationship once the right variables are chosen, and end corrections provide a real systematic error to identify. Strong topic for demonstrating a systematic rather than random limitation.

subjects.name: Magnetism and induction
subjects.description: Good higher level ground with equipment most Dubai schools hold. Data tends to be noisy, which is useful: noisy data handled with proper repeats and error bars evidences better practice than clean data handled casually.

subjects.name: Fluid viscosity and terminal velocity
subjects.description: Sphere-drop experiments are cheap to run and give strongly non-linear relationships that reward correct linearisation. Temperature control is the hidden variable and is where control-of-variables marks are won.

subjects.name: Radioactivity and inverse square behaviour
subjects.description: Depends entirely on school equipment and source permissions, which vary across Dubai schools. Where available, counting statistics give a genuine reason to discuss random uncertainty quantitatively rather than qualitatively.

subjects.name: Solar and photovoltaic output
subjects.description: Locally relevant and well suited to Dubai conditions, with irradiance, temperature and angle all available as variables. The challenge is isolating one variable in an outdoor environment where several change at once.

dubai/ib-physics-ia-help.regionsIntro: Physics IA support is booked from across Dubai, and the limiting factor is usually laboratory access and higher level group size rather than the neighbourhood. These are the areas we hear from.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Sufouh

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Established IB provision alongside British schools. Transition students from IGCSE Physics are common, and their need is learning to report an experiment rather than to perform one.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba and Meydan

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Newer Diploma cohorts and newer laboratories. Equipment is often good and the exemplar base is thin, so topic choice tends to come from online lists rather than from previous cohorts.

sections.heading: The four criteria and what each six marks is for
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is marked out of twenty-four, split evenly across four criteria. That even split is informative: a student cannot compensate for a weak conclusion with an excellent method, because each criterion is capped at six. The strategic reading is that the cheapest marks are wherever the current draft is weakest, and for Physics that is almost always data analysis or evaluation rather than research design.

Research design rewards a focused question with a justified methodology, a sensible range for the independent variable, enough repeats to estimate random uncertainty, and controls over the variables that physically matter. Data analysis rewards processing that is correct, complete and carries uncertainty. Conclusion rewards an interpretation the data supports, compared against theory or an accepted value. Evaluation rewards limitations with their actual effects and improvements that address the dominant source of error.

The word that recurs across the top bands is specific. A specific range justified by the physics rather than by convenience. A specific propagated uncertainty rather than a note that uncertainties exist. A specific comparison with a published value including percentage difference. A specific statement that heat loss reduced the measured capacity by roughly a stated proportion, rather than an observation that heat was lost.

Treat the structure below as the planning frame and confirm the current criteria and mark allocations in the Physics subject guide your child's teacher is working from. The IB publishes the authoritative version and revises it on a cycle, and where this page differs from the guide, the guide governs.

sections.heading: Propagating uncertainty so the final answer means something
paragraphs: This is the single most valuable technical session in Physics IA work and the one Dubai drafts most often need. The sequence is mechanical once learnt. Record each instrument's uncertainty, usually half the smallest division or the manufacturer's stated figure. Convert to percentage where the calculation involves products, quotients or powers. Combine percentages by addition for products and quotients, multiplying by the power where a quantity is raised. Convert back to an absolute uncertainty on the final answer. Then round the answer so its last digit sits where the uncertainty does.

The step students skip is the gradient. Most Physics investigations extract a physical quantity from the slope of a graph, and that gradient carries an uncertainty derived from the spread of the data, conventionally by drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines through the error bars and taking half their difference. A gradient quoted without that uncertainty cannot support a comparison with an accepted value, which is exactly what the conclusion criterion asks for.

Once the propagation is in place, three criteria improve at once. Data analysis becomes complete. The conclusion can state whether the accepted value lies inside the experimental range, which is a far stronger statement than noting that the two numbers are close. Evaluation gains a quantitative basis, because the student can say which measurement dominated the uncertainty and therefore which improvement would actually matter.

The table below sets out the common Physics measurements, their typical uncertainty sources and what propagation does to them. It is a working reference rather than a substitute for the subject guide or the school's own practical guidance.

sections.heading: Linearising: deciding what to plot before the laboratory session
paragraphs: Physics relationships are often not linear, and a curve fitted by eye supports no quantitative claim. The move that earns marks is to transform the variables so the relationship becomes a straight line, then extract the physical quantity from the gradient or the intercept. A student who decides this in the planning stage collects the right data; a student who decides it afterwards frequently discovers they measured over the wrong range or took too few points to resolve the line.

The decision is usually simple algebra. If theory predicts that a period depends on the square root of a length, plot the period squared against the length and the gradient carries the constant of interest. If a relationship is an inverse square, plot against the reciprocal of the squared distance. If the dependence is exponential, plot a logarithm and the gradient gives the exponent. Each of these turns an unconvincing curve into a line whose gradient can be compared with a theoretical prediction.

Linearising also improves evaluation, because a straight-line plot makes systematic error visible. A non-zero intercept where theory predicts the origin is direct evidence of a systematic offset, such as an end correction in a resonance tube or a zero error on an instrument. A student who can point at the intercept and name the physical cause has written a specific evaluation rather than a general one.

Students sometimes resist on the grounds that the raw graph looks more natural. Both can appear: the raw relationship as evidence of the shape, the linearised plot as the basis of the analysis. What cannot appear is a curved plot with a hand-drawn trend and a conclusion that depends on it.

columns: What the gradient or intercept gives
rows: Gradient relates to local gravitational field strength
Gradient relates to source output; intercept exposes background
Gradient gives resistivity divided by cross-sectional area
Gradient gives the decay constant directly
Intercept reveals the end correction as a systematic error
Gradient relates to viscosity of the fluid

sections.heading: Conclusion and evaluation: the two criteria that need the same arithmetic
paragraphs: A conclusion earns marks by stating what the data shows, comparing it with theory or an accepted value, and being honest about the agreement. The sentence that scores is the one that says the gradient gives a value of a stated quantity with a stated uncertainty, that the accepted value does or does not lie within that range, and what the percentage difference is. The sentence that does not score is the one that says the results support the hypothesis.

Evaluation then builds on exactly that arithmetic. If propagation has shown that one measurement contributed most of the uncertainty, the evaluation has a dominant limitation to discuss and a targeted improvement to propose. If the intercept was non-zero where theory predicted the origin, there is a systematic error to name. If the repeats scattered widely, there is a random contribution to quantify. Without the arithmetic, evaluation collapses into a list of things that could have gone better, which is the single most common weak section in Dubai Physics drafts.

Two distinctions matter and are frequently blurred. Random uncertainty shows up as scatter and is reduced by more repeats; systematic error shifts every reading in the same direction and is not reduced by repeating anything. A student who proposes more repeats as the fix for a systematic offset has misdiagnosed the problem, and the band descriptors notice. The second distinction is between a limitation and a mistake: a procedural error the student made is not a limitation of the method, and claiming it as one costs credibility.

The best evaluations are short and quantitative. Three limitations, each with an estimated magnitude and a direction of effect, and one improvement that addresses the largest, outperform a page listing eight weaknesses with no numbers. Length is not what the criterion rewards.
bullets: State the measured value with its propagated uncertainty
Say whether the accepted value falls inside that range
Give a percentage difference rather than a verbal impression
Separate random scatter from systematic offset explicitly
Three quantified limitations beat eight unquantified ones

sections.heading: Where Dubai Physics candidates lose marks
paragraphs: Uncertainty abandonment is first and largest, for the reasons set out above. It is also the easiest to spot: a results table with a column headed uncertainty, and a conclusion with a bare number. Any family can check for that in two minutes without understanding the physics, and if it is present, the draft is leaking marks in three of the four criteria simultaneously.

Second is a research design where the controlled variables are listed but not justified. Writing that temperature was kept constant earns little; writing that temperature was kept constant because resistivity varies measurably with temperature over the range used, and stating how it was held, earns the band. Dubai laboratories are air-conditioned to a reasonably stable temperature, which is worth stating as part of the control rather than assuming.

Third is too narrow a range or too few points. Five points across a narrow span cannot establish a relationship, and no amount of careful analysis repairs that. Eight to ten well-spread values with three repeats each is the usual working minimum for a Physics investigation, and that is a design decision, made before the laboratory booking, not something to be regretted afterwards.

Fourth, and specific to this market, is topic imitation driven by thin exemplar bases. Small higher level sets and young Diploma departments mean students look online for topics, and the same four experiments recirculate. The physics is fine; the problem is that research design marks reward the student's own refinements, and a standard experiment copied wholesale gives them nothing to refine. Keeping the standard experiment and adding one genuine methodological improvement is the cheapest fix available.
bullets: Uncertainties recorded in the table and missing from the result
Controlled variables listed without physical justification
Too few data points over too narrow a range
A standard experiment copied with no refinement of the student's own
Evaluation written as a list rather than as quantified effects

sections.heading: When the school laboratory cannot support the experiment
paragraphs: This is a real constraint in Dubai and it is rarely discussed honestly. Laboratory time for individual investigations competes with timetabled practicals, technician availability varies, and specialist apparatus such as radioactive sources or precision optics is held by some schools and not others. A student whose chosen investigation needs equipment the school does not have will discover it late unless somebody asks early.

The productive response is to design around what is available rather than to abandon rigour. Video analysis of motion requires only a phone and free software and produces data with genuinely interesting frame-rate uncertainty. Thermal experiments need no specialist kit and provide a real systematic error to model. Electrical investigations use standard laboratory supplies. Solar output work suits Dubai conditions and needs an irradiance proxy and a multimeter. None of these is a compromise in criterion terms, because the criteria reward the quality of the design and the analysis rather than the sophistication of the apparatus.

Where measurements are taken at home rather than in a school laboratory, the honest reporting of conditions becomes part of research design. Ambient temperature, surface, lighting and the exact instrument used all belong in the method. A student who reports those carefully is demonstrating better practice than one who implies laboratory conditions that did not exist.

Ask the Physics teacher two questions early in the planning: what apparatus can be booked for individual investigation work, and how many laboratory sessions a student can expect. The answers shape the topic more than interest does, and getting them in writing at the start saves a wasted month.

sections.heading: What Physics IA support costs in Dubai, and why it runs online
paragraphs: Published Dubai market rates, read in October 2026, begin at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik at the budget online end, rise through Unitors at AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's AED 200-450 and above for specialist IB and IGCSE support, reaching AED 650 at BartyED for premium examiner-branded provision. Bestimate puts in-home visits at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. These are the market's figures rather than an IB Gram price list.

Physics investigation support sits at the specialist end of that range for a specific reason: the pool of tutors who can propagate uncertainty into a gradient and judge whether an evaluation is quantitative is much smaller than the pool who can teach the Physics syllabus. Scarcity prices everywhere, and this is a genuinely scarce skill rather than a marketing distinction.

The shape of the spend is a project rather than a subscription. Four to six sessions covers most investigations: one on design and feasibility, one on uncertainty and processing, one or two criterion reviews of the student's own draft, and one evaluation rebuild. Against Bestimate's AED 1,000-2,000 a month for specialist exam-year weekly tutoring, that is a smaller and more defined commitment, and it buys marks in the component the student controls most.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For this task the online format is the better one on its merits. The work is a spreadsheet, a graph and a propagation calculation on a shared screen, and the annotated file stays with the student for revision. It also removes the constraint that matters most in a small higher level Physics set, which is that the person who can supervise the investigation properly may not live anywhere near your community.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty is taught once and fixes three criteria
whyPoints.description: Propagation from instrument to gradient to final answer improves data analysis, makes the conclusion defensible and gives evaluation a quantitative basis. One session on the arithmetic does more for a Physics IA mark than three on the physics.

whyPoints.title: Linearisation is planned, not improvised
whyPoints.description: Deciding what to plot against what before the laboratory session determines whether the right data gets collected. Students who leave it until after discover they measured over the wrong range, and that is not repairable in the write-up.

whyPoints.title: We design around the laboratory that exists
whyPoints.description: Dubai schools differ in apparatus and in technician time. We will ask what can actually be booked and steer towards investigations that produce analysable data with available equipment rather than towards impressive ones that stall.

whyPoints.title: Evaluation gets rebuilt, not lengthened
whyPoints.description: Six marks reward limitations with magnitudes and directions. Three quantified limitations with one targeted improvement beats a page of unquantified weaknesses, and we will cut rather than add.

faqs.question: How long should the IB Physics investigation be?
faqs.answer: The upper limit is about 3,000 words, and strong investigations are frequently shorter. Tables, graphs, captions and calculations carry much of the content, and a report that reaches the limit through extended prose has usually padded the introduction or the evaluation. The useful discipline is to write the method, processing and evaluation as tightly as possible and let the data occupy the space. Confirm the current limit in the Physics subject guide your child's teacher is working from, since guides are revised on a cycle.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Physics IA need uncertainties propagated?
faqs.answer: Because three of the four criteria depend on it. Data analysis is incomplete without it, the conclusion cannot honestly compare a measured value with an accepted one without a range, and evaluation has no quantitative basis for ranking limitations. The sequence is mechanical: record instrument uncertainties, convert to percentages where quantities multiply or divide, combine them, find the gradient uncertainty from maximum and minimum gradient lines, and round the answer so its last digit matches the uncertainty.

faqs.question: What does linearising a graph mean in a Physics IA?
faqs.answer: It means transforming the variables so a non-linear relationship becomes a straight line, then extracting the physical quantity from the gradient or intercept. If a period depends on the square root of a length, plot period squared against length. If intensity falls as an inverse square, plot against one over distance squared. Decide this before collecting data, because it determines the range and the number of points needed. A hand-drawn curve through raw points supports no quantitative conclusion.

faqs.question: How many data points and repeats does a Physics investigation need?
faqs.answer: As a working minimum, eight to ten well-spread values of the independent variable with three repeats at each. Fewer points cannot establish a relationship convincingly, and without repeats there is no basis for estimating random uncertainty, which costs marks in data analysis. The range matters as much as the count: points clustered over a narrow span produce a gradient with a large uncertainty regardless of how carefully each measurement was made. These are design decisions, taken before the laboratory booking.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a systematic error and a random uncertainty?
faqs.answer: Random uncertainty shows up as scatter between repeats and is reduced by taking more repeats. Systematic error shifts every reading in the same direction, from a zero error, an end correction or a consistently mis-set instrument, and is not reduced by repeating anything. The practical consequence for the write-up is that proposing more repeats as the fix for a systematic offset misdiagnoses the problem, and band descriptors reward the student who separates the two and names the physical cause of the systematic part.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with their Physics IA without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach uncertainty propagation and linearisation, discuss whether a proposed design will produce analysable data, flag that a calculation contains an error for the student to find, explain what each criterion rewards, and report where a draft sits against the bands. A tutor may not perform the calculations, process the data, produce the graphs or write any part of the report. The student signs an academic honesty declaration and it must be accurate.

faqs.question: What if my child's school laboratory does not have the right equipment?
faqs.answer: Design around what is available, which costs nothing in criterion terms because the criteria reward design and analysis rather than apparatus. Video analysis of motion needs only a phone and free software and produces interesting frame-rate uncertainty. Thermal experiments need no specialist kit and supply a real systematic error. Electrical work uses standard supplies. Ask the Physics teacher early what can be booked for individual investigations and how many sessions are realistic, because the answer shapes the topic more than interest does.

faqs.question: Which Physics topics make the strongest investigations?
faqs.answer: Topics where the relationship is known from theory, the data is repeatable, and the uncertainties are large enough to be interesting but small enough to permit a conclusion. Simple harmonic motion, resistivity, thermal capacity with heat loss modelled, resonance in air columns and sphere-drop viscosity all meet those tests with ordinary equipment. Topics to be careful with are those needing apparatus the school may not hold, and those where several variables change at once outdoors unless the student can genuinely isolate one.

faqs.question: How much does the Physics IA count towards the final grade?
faqs.answer: Roughly a fifth of the Physics grade at both standard and higher level. It is marked out of twenty-four by the school teacher across four criteria of six marks each, and the IB moderates a sample of each school's marking, so the mark needs to be defensible against the band descriptors rather than simply generous. Confirm the exact weighting in the current subject guide, since the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle and the guide your child's teacher uses is the authority.

faqs.question: Why did a careful Physics investigation score in the middle?
faqs.answer: Most often because the uncertainties stopped at the results table. A report can describe a meticulous method, present clean data and still lose marks in data analysis, conclusion and evaluation simultaneously if nothing is propagated through to the final answer. The second common reason is an evaluation written as a list of weaknesses with no magnitudes attached, which the band descriptors cannot credit. Both are fixable in one or two sessions and neither reflects the quality of the practical work.

faqs.question: Should my child compare their result with an accepted value?
faqs.answer: Where one exists, yes, and the comparison should be quantitative. State the measured value with its propagated uncertainty, say whether the accepted value lies within that range, and give the percentage difference. That is a far stronger conclusion than observing that the values are similar. Where no accepted value exists, compare against the theoretical form instead: does the gradient have the sign and order of magnitude theory predicts, and does the intercept sit where theory says it should?

faqs.question: When should a Dubai Physics student start their investigation?
faqs.answer: Design work should begin at least five to seven months before the school's internal deadline, because laboratory access has to be booked and repeat data collection cannot be compressed. In practice that means starting in the first Diploma year for most Dubai schools. The long summer break is a particular hazard: school laboratories are generally unavailable, so any experiment needing school apparatus has to finish its practical work before term ends. Ask the teacher for the internal deadline list early.

faqs.question: What does Physics IA coaching cost for a family in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 run from about AED 33-65 an hour at budget online platforms to AED 650 for premium examiner-branded providers, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate putting specialist IB and IGCSE support at AED 200-450 and above. Physics investigation work sits at the specialist end because the ability to propagate uncertainty into a gradient is genuinely scarce. Four to six sessions is the usual block, so budget it as a project rather than monthly.

faqs.question: Can my child use data collected at home rather than in the laboratory?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the conditions are reported honestly and completely. Ambient temperature, the exact instrument used, the surface, the lighting and anything else that could affect the measurement belong in the method. A student who documents home conditions carefully demonstrates better scientific practice than one who implies laboratory conditions that did not apply. What is not acceptable is presenting home-collected data as though it came from controlled laboratory apparatus, which is a misrepresentation rather than a limitation.

dubai/ib-physics-ia-help.closingBody: For a Physics investigation the fastest useful diagnosis comes from the data rather than the prose. Send the results table and any graph, and the first session will say whether the uncertainties can be propagated to a defensible answer, whether the relationship needs linearising, and where each of the four criteria currently sits. If no data has been collected yet, that session is better still: design decisions made before the laboratory booking are the ones that determine what the write-up can claim. Sessions run over live video on Gulf Standard Time and the student keeps the annotated file.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Physics to Dubai students on live video at Standard and Higher Level. Each can state which guide they teach to, mark a structured question against the published scheme in front of you, and name the investigation criteria without looking them up. Those are the three things worth testing.

intro.heading: Pay the physics rate, then check you got it
paragraphs: Physics sits at the scarce end of the Dubai Diploma market, which means it prices at the top of the qualified band and frequently into the specialist band. Published figures in this emirate, read in October 2026: Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200 an hour, TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work, and the Bestimate rate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above. Premium named listings reach AED 650. A Dubai family paying at those bands is entitled to know what distinguishes the hour they are buying from an hour at AED 50, and almost no page in this market will tell them.

The distinction is checkable, which is the useful part. A physics tutor worth a specialist rate can say which subject guide they teach to and what changed in it. They can mark a structured question against the published scheme while you watch, and explain why a mark was withheld rather than saying the answer was nearly right. They can name the four assessment criteria of the scientific investigation and what each is worth. And they can tell you, after one diagnostic, whether a student's problem is physics or algebra, because in Dubai scripts it is usually algebra.

That last point is the single most useful thing on this page. A large share of lost marks in Diploma physics has no physics in it. Rearranging an equation with the unknown in a denominator, handling powers of ten, converting units before substituting, linearising a relationship so a graph gradient means something: these are mathematical operations, and a student who cannot do them quickly will score below their physical understanding on every paper. Diagnosing that costs one session and changes what the next twenty are spent on.

The components are where the money should be aimed. Physics is assessed through two written papers and an internally assessed scientific investigation carrying 20 per cent of the grade, with a 3,000-word ceiling, around ten hours of class time and 24 marks across four criteria. A fifth of the grade awarded for work done without time pressure is the most recoverable part of the course, and it is also the part most commonly left until the term when every other Diploma deadline lands.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The cost argument runs in the family's favour: the Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one in Dubai at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. For physics there is a second argument, which is that the tutor pool for Higher Level physics in this emirate is small enough that restricting it to driving distance is the one decision guaranteed to reduce quality.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor.programmesIntro: Physics arrives in a Dubai student's timetable by several routes, and what they bring from each determines what their Diploma physics support should cost and contain.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: Integrated or separate sciences assessed against criteria covering knowledge, inquiry and design, processing and evaluating, and reflection on the impacts of science. Students arrive at Diploma physics well prepared for the scientific investigation and often underprepared for the mathematical density of the written papers.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai's full-continuum IB World Schools this route feeds directly into Diploma physics, and the usual first-term surprise is the quantity of algebra. MYP science assessment does not require sustained symbolic manipulation under time, so the gap is real and it is not a physics gap.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics into Diploma physics
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Edexcel 4PH1 leaves a student fluent at structured written questions and, in the Cambridge case, practised at an alternative-to-practical paper. What transfers less well is independent experimental design, since IGCSE practical questions supply the method rather than asking the student to construct one.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai enrolment, so a substantial share of Diploma physics students arrive from IGCSE. Those who took Additional Mathematics 0606 arrive with the algebraic fluency Diploma physics assumes; those who took only 0580 Extended frequently do not.

programmes.name: IB Physics Standard Level
programmes.description: Two written papers plus the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. Paper 1 combines multiple-choice with a data-based section; Paper 2 is extended response. The right level for a student who needs physics for breadth or for a course that specifies the subject without specifying Higher Level, and it is not a soft option.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run Standard Level physics alongside Higher Level in the same room for part of the course, which means Standard Level students sometimes meet Higher Level content and conclude they are failing. Checking which content is actually assessed at their level is a five-minute fix with a real effect on confidence.

programmes.name: IB Physics Higher Level
programmes.description: The same component structure with substantially more content and longer papers. Required or strongly preferred by many engineering, physics and some medical and architecture courses. The mathematical demand is the differentiator rather than the conceptual difficulty, which is why the Higher Level diagnostic always includes algebra.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level physics is among the scarcest tutoring subjects in this emirate, which is why it prices at the specialist band and why availability rather than rate is often the binding constraint in the spring term. Booking in September costs less and comes with a choice of tutor.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics support is bought by component and by topic, and the price of an hour is the same whichever is addressed. These are the units a plan is built from, with what each actually costs a Dubai student in marks.

subjects.name: Mechanics and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum and energy. Conceptually the most accessible topic and the one where algebraic errors do the most damage, because almost every question is a multi-step substitution. Marks go to sign conventions and to unit conversion performed after substitution rather than before.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and gases
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat and the gas laws. The arithmetic involves powers of ten and large or small quantities, so calculator discipline and significant figures decide the mark more often than understanding does.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Wave behaviour, superposition, standing waves and simple harmonic motion. The topic where trigonometric fluency becomes load-bearing, and where Standard Level students frequently lose marks describing a phenomenon correctly without producing the required calculation.

subjects.name: Electricity and magnetism
subjects.levels: SL and HL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Circuits, fields, induction and capacitance at Higher Level. The most commonly reported weakness in Dubai physics enquiries, and in most cases the obstacle is circuit analysis as simultaneous equations rather than the physics of the circuit itself.

subjects.name: Fields, gravitation and orbits
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, potential, and orbital motion. Higher Level content requiring comfort with inverse-square relationships and with sketching field and potential graphs. Students who cannot sketch from an equation struggle here regardless of their conceptual grasp.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy and quantum phenomena. Exponential decay is the mathematical gate, and logarithm handling is what separates students who can complete a half-life question from those who can describe one.

subjects.name: Paper 1
subjects.description: Multiple-choice questions plus a data-based section. The data section is the discriminator: reading a graph gradient, identifying an uncertainty, recognising which quantity a plotted line actually represents. Pure multiple-choice practice does not prepare a student for it.

subjects.name: Paper 2
subjects.description: Extended-response questions across the syllabus, including experimental contexts. The largest single component in the course and the one where command-term discipline costs the most: describe, explain, deduce and justify each buy something different.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL · 20 per cent · 24 marks
subjects.description: An individual investigation with a 3,000-word ceiling and around ten hours of class time, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Six marks per criterion, and the usual failure is a research question that cannot produce enough varied quantitative data.

subjects.name: Mathematical technique inside physics
subjects.levels: Not a syllabus topic, and the most common real gap
subjects.description: Rearrangement with the unknown in a denominator, powers of ten, unit conversion, linearising a relationship so a gradient has meaning, and solving simultaneous equations from a circuit. None of this is physics, and all of it decides physics marks.

sections.heading: What an IB physics tutor in Dubai costs, and what the band buys
paragraphs: A qualified one-to-one online physics tutor in this emirate is advertised at AED 150-300 an hour, with IB-specific listings starting at AED 200 at Unitors and specialist work quoted at AED 270 by TutorChase. The Bestimate rate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium named listings reach AED 650 at BartyED. Below the qualified band, budget online provision starts at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik. Every figure here belongs to the provider or survey that published it, read in October 2026.

Physics prices toward the top because supply is thin. Higher Level physics requires a tutor comfortable with the mathematics as well as the content, and in a market where most tutoring supply is general rather than specialist, that combination is scarce. Scarcity also concentrates: demand across the emirate spikes in the same weeks of the final year, which is why a family looking in February meets the top of the band and a family looking in September meets the middle of it with a choice of tutor.

What the band should buy is specific and testable. At the qualified band and above, a physics hour should include marking to the published scheme rather than impression, feedback that names the command term and the mark withheld, and the ability to work on the investigation against its four criteria. At the budget band the realistic product is content review and worked examples, which is a legitimate purchase for mathematical drilling and is not the same thing as criterion-referenced marking.

What is published instead is the market benchmark above and the hour counts in the table below, so a quote can be held against both. The free 30-minute trial lesson, one per family and with no card details taken, is where the plan and the figure are discussed together.

sections.heading: The physics assessment structure, and where the weight sits
paragraphs: Physics is assessed through two written papers and an internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 combines multiple-choice questions with a data-based section and carries 36 per cent. Paper 2 is extended response and carries 44 per cent, making it the largest single component in the course. The investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent. Papers are longer at Higher Level than at Standard Level, reflecting the additional content rather than a different structure.

Most Dubai physics revision is organised by topic, and that is the wrong axis for the final term. Paper 2 at 44 per cent is where the grade is decided, and Paper 2 rewards command-term discipline and multi-step calculation under time. The data-based section of Paper 1 is the second priority and the most commonly neglected: reading a gradient, identifying an uncertainty, recognising which quantity a plotted line represents. Students who revise by drilling multiple-choice questions never touch it.

The investigation deserves disproportionate attention because of what it is. A fifth of the grade, 24 marks across four criteria, 3,000 words, around ten hours of class time, and no time pressure at all. A student who secures 20 of 24 on the investigation has banked a fifth of their grade before an examination hall is involved. A student who secures 10 has given away marks that were available for process rather than performance, which is the most frustrating way to lose a grade.

Command terms are worth naming explicitly because they transfer. State wants a fact. Describe wants observable detail. Explain wants a causal chain. Deduce wants a conclusion reached from given information. Justify wants the reasoning shown. A student who answers everything as a description loses marks across both papers simultaneously, and the correction is a habit change enforced through marking rather than a topic to be learned.

sections.heading: Most Dubai physics problems are not physics problems
paragraphs: Set a Dubai Diploma physics student twenty short algebraic manipulations with no physical context, time them, and count. Rearranging for a variable in a denominator. Multiplying and dividing powers of ten. Converting a unit before substituting rather than after. Taking logarithms of both sides of an exponential relationship. Solving two simultaneous equations from a circuit. A student who is slow and inaccurate across those items is not losing marks on physics content, and teaching them more physics will not help.

This is the most common diagnostic finding in this subject and it is also the cheapest to act on. The intervention is thirty-minute sessions two or three times a week for a few weeks, with no physics in them at all, measured by timed sets of twenty items counted week to week. Because the content is not Diploma-specific, it can be delivered at the lower end of the market rate, which makes it the best value purchase available in physics.

The second non-physics problem is graph behaviour. Diploma physics asks students to sketch relationships from equations, to linearise a non-linear relationship so a gradient carries meaning, and to extract a physical quantity from that gradient with its units. Students who have only ever read graphs produced by software cannot do this, and the Paper 1 data section finds them out immediately. It is a teachable skill and it transfers to chemistry and biology data questions as well.

The third is uncertainty. Diploma physics expects a student to state uncertainties, propagate them through a calculation, and discuss their effect on a conclusion. This matters doubly because it is examined in the papers and assessed in the investigation, where the data analysis and evaluation criteria both depend on it. A student who treats uncertainty as a sentence added at the end of a report is losing marks in two places for the same reason.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks, four criteria
paragraphs: The investigation is an individual piece of experimental work with a 3,000-word ceiling, around ten hours of class time, and 24 marks split evenly across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion, and evaluation. Six marks each. Those names and weights should be visible to the student before a research question is chosen, because they describe the task far better than the instruction to find something interesting.

The dominant failure in Dubai investigations is a research question that cannot generate the data the criteria require. Research design rewards a question with a clearly identified and genuinely variable independent quantity, a measurable dependent quantity, and controlled variables that are actually controlled. A question with two possible values of the independent variable cannot produce a graph, and without a graph the data analysis criterion has little to assess. Testing that before any apparatus is touched is the single highest-value session in the process.

Evaluation is the criterion students most often treat as padding. It asks for a reasoned assessment of the method's limitations and of the reliability of the conclusion, which is a different thing from a list of improvements beginning with the words 'use better equipment'. A good evaluation identifies which specific source of uncertainty dominated and explains how it propagated into the final result, which requires the uncertainty work to have been done properly during data collection rather than reconstructed afterwards.

The boundary is firm and worth stating before the first session. A tutor may teach experimental design, question whether a research question can produce usable data, teach uncertainty treatment, name the criteria and their mark allocations, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the experiment, supply data, or write any part of the report. Work that is not the student's own carries a malpractice finding against the student. One UAE-facing site advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and what is sold there is a risk to the Diploma.

sections.heading: Eight questions to ask a Dubai physics tutor before paying
paragraphs: A specialist rate should survive questioning, and these eight questions take about ten minutes. Which subject guide do you teach to, and what changed in it? What are the four criteria of the scientific investigation and what is each worth? Mark this structured question in front of me and tell me why the third mark was withheld. How would you tell whether this student's problem is physics or algebra?

The second four are about process. How will I see what happened in each session? What do you set between sessions and when is it marked? What will you not do with my child's investigation? And what happens if, three sessions in, you conclude that we are buying the wrong thing? A tutor who can answer that last one honestly is worth more than one who cannot, because the answer that costs them money is the answer that tells you they are competent.

Two things are worth refusing regardless of the answers. Any offer to supply, write or complete an investigation, at any price, because the consequence falls on the student as malpractice. And any promise of a specific grade or points total, because grade boundaries are determined after a session on the basis of candidate performance and no honest provider can commit to one in advance. A page that offers both is telling you what it is.

One more item belongs on the list in this market. If a tutor is described as an examiner at a premium rate, ask for evidence of current status, and note that examiner experience provides no access to marking in progress, grade boundaries or unseen paper content. What it does provide is calibration against the published criteria, and that is available well below the premium band in this emirate.

sections.heading: Higher and Standard Level physics: what the extra actually is
paragraphs: Both levels share the same component structure and the same four investigation criteria. Higher Level carries substantially more content and longer papers. The extension is concentrated in fields and gravitation, in electromagnetic induction and capacitance, and in the depth of quantum and nuclear material, and all of those additions lean harder on mathematics than the shared content does.

That is why the level conversation in Dubai should be settled from a marked paper rather than from enthusiasm. A student scoring low at Higher Level whose losses concentrate in two named topics has a content problem that teaching addresses across eighteen months. A student whose losses are spread evenly across every topic and question type is being told that the mathematical demand of the level is the issue, and that is not something tutoring reliably converts into a top grade in the time available.

The university requirement is the other input, and it is published by the universities themselves. Many engineering and physics courses expect Higher Level physics; some accept Standard Level with a Higher Level in mathematics; architecture and some medical routes vary considerably. Reading the actual requirement for the actual courses on a student's list is an afternoon's work and it removes most of the uncertainty from the decision.

Where a Dubai school teaches both levels in the same room for part of the course, there is a practical and cheap intervention available: confirm which content is assessed at the student's own level. Standard Level students who have sat through Higher Level material and concluded they are failing physics are more common than they should be, and the fix is a syllabus comparison rather than a term of tutoring.

sections.heading: Dubai's school and regulatory context for physics
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects annually against six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. The sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, and seven new private schools were approved for the 2026-27 intake, three of them International Baccalaureate, adding 16,846 places. KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27.

Laboratory provision is the physics-specific variable across that landscape. A well-equipped school laboratory makes the investigation a design problem; a thinly equipped one makes it a logistics problem, and the research question has to be chosen accordingly. This is worth establishing in the first investigation session, because a question that requires apparatus the school does not hold will fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the student's physics.

The mandatory-subject requirement affects the hours available. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral studies are taught in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with KHDA advising no such lesson falls below 25 minutes. A physics plan has to fit the week a student actually has.

Two points of record. For the mandatory subjects, the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, and teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold the relevant approval from KHDA. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education or the International Baccalaureate, operates no UAE office or centre, and does not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; those are referenced and linked at ibo.org instead.

process.title: Say the level and the component
process.description: The useful opening message names Standard or Higher Level, the topic or paper that is failing, and whether the investigation is in scope. Those three facts set the tutor, the hour count and the quote. An enquiry that says only 'physics help' has to be unpacked before anything can be priced.

process.description: Live video with the matched tutor, no card details taken and no obligation. Use it to run the verification questions: ask which guide, ask for the investigation criteria, and watch one structured question marked against the published scheme with the withheld mark explained.

process.title: The algebra diagnostic first
process.description: Twenty timed manipulation items with no physical context, counted. If the result is slow and inaccurate, the plan starts with short high-frequency drilling at the lower market band rather than with Diploma content at the specialist band. That sequencing is usually the difference between a plan that moves marks and one that does not.

process.title: A written plan with an hour count
process.description: The plan states the components, the number of sessions on each and the total, so it can be held against the published market bands on this page. It also states what is being left alone. An open-ended monthly figure cannot be compared against anything, which is why most of this market prefers one.

process.title: Investigation feasibility before data collection
process.description: Where the investigation is in scope, the first session tests whether the research question can generate enough varied quantitative data with apparatus the school actually holds. Changing a question early is cheap. Discovering the limitation after ten hours of class time is not.

process.description: The evidence is re-read at the halfway point. Where the algebra has come good and Paper 2 marks have moved, the frequency drops. The purpose of an hour count rather than a subscription is that it can be reduced as readily as extended.
