whyPoints.description: Completed investigations, grade promises, unevidenced examiner claims and self-asserted star ratings all carry prices in this market. Naming them is more useful to a family comparing quotes than another paragraph about teaching philosophy.

faqs.question: How much does an IB physics tutor in Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market, read in October 2026, put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work. The Bestimate survey places IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium named listings reach AED 650 at BartyED. Budget online provision starts at AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik. Physics prices toward the upper end because Higher Level supply is thin in this emirate, and demand concentrates in the same weeks each year.

faqs.question: How do I check an IB physics tutor is worth a specialist rate?
faqs.answer: Ask four content questions and four process questions, which takes about ten minutes. Which subject guide do you teach to and what changed in it? What are the four criteria of the scientific investigation and what is each worth? Mark this structured question in front of me and explain the withheld mark. How would you tell whether this student's problem is physics or algebra? Then: how will I see each session, what gets set and marked between them, what will you not do with the investigation, and what if you conclude we are buying the wrong thing?

faqs.question: Why does my child understand physics but still lose marks in IB papers?
faqs.answer: Usually because the lost marks are not physics marks. Rearranging an equation with the unknown in a denominator, handling powers of ten, converting units before substituting rather than after, linearising a relationship so a gradient carries meaning, and solving simultaneous equations from a circuit are all mathematical operations, and a student slow or inaccurate on them scores below their physical understanding on every paper. Twenty timed manipulation items with no physical context diagnose it in one session. The fix is short high-frequency drilling with no physics in it, which is the cheapest useful purchase in the subject.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria of the IB physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying six marks for a total of 24, with the component worth 20 per cent of the subject grade. The report has a 3,000-word ceiling and around ten hours of class time is allocated to it. Research design rewards a focused question with a genuinely variable independent quantity and properly controlled variables. Data analysis rewards correct processing, graphing and uncertainty treatment. Conclusion rewards a reading of the results related to accepted physics. Evaluation rewards identifying which source of uncertainty actually dominated, not a generic list of improvements.

faqs.question: What makes a physics investigation research question fail?
faqs.answer: Most commonly, an independent variable with too few usable values. A question that permits two or three settings cannot produce a graph, and without a graph the data analysis criterion has little to assess, which caps the piece regardless of how well it is written. The second failure is apparatus: a question requiring equipment the school does not hold fails for reasons unconnected to the student's physics. Both are detectable in a single session before any data is collected, which is why feasibility work is the highest-value hour in the whole process.

faqs.question: What extra content does IB Physics Higher Level actually add?
faqs.answer: It carries substantially more content and longer papers, and the extension is concentrated in fields and gravitation, electromagnetic induction and capacitance, and the depth of quantum and nuclear material. All of those lean harder on mathematics than the shared content does, which is why the mathematical demand rather than conceptual difficulty is the real differentiator. Decide the level from a marked paper: losses concentrated in named topics indicate a content problem that teaching addresses, while losses spread evenly across every topic and question type usually indicate that the level is the issue.

faqs.question: Which IB physics component should a Dubai student prioritise?
faqs.answer: Paper 2 first, at 44 per cent, because it is the largest single component and because the marks lost there are usually to command-term misreading and multi-step slips rather than to unknown content, both of which respond quickly to marking. The data-based section of Paper 1 is second and the most commonly neglected: gradients, uncertainties and recognising which quantity a plotted line represents. Students who revise by drilling multiple-choice questions never touch it. The investigation sits alongside both as a fifth of the grade available without time pressure.

faqs.question: Do IB physics tutors in Dubai cover both Standard and Higher Level content?
faqs.answer: Ask rather than assume, and ask about Higher Level specifically. The additional Higher Level material in fields, induction, capacitance and quantum physics is where tutoring supply in this emirate thins out, and a tutor comfortable with Standard Level may be working at the edge of their range on Higher Level fields questions. A useful test is to put a Higher Level question on a shared screen during the trial and watch it worked aloud. The answer should be fluent rather than reconstructed, and the difference is visible within a minute.

faqs.question: How many physics tutoring hours does a Dubai Diploma student need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the diagnostic shows, and the honest answer is usually a small number aimed precisely. An algebra gap is ten to twelve short sessions of drilling at the lower band. Investigation feasibility and draft review is three or four sessions. Paper 2 command-term discipline is six to eight sessions of marking-led work. A genuine content gap across several Higher Level topics is a term of weekly sessions. Buying a year of undifferentiated weekly content review before the diagnostic is how a family spends at the specialist band and sees no mark movement.

faqs.question: Is online physics tuition a problem when the subject has practical work?
faqs.answer: The practical work happens in the school laboratory either way, so the question is what support the practical work needs. Investigation coaching is design, uncertainty treatment and draft review, all of which happen on documents and graphs rather than at a bench, and all of which work better on a shared screen where annotations are saved. What online delivery cannot do is stand next to a student while they take a reading. What it can do is make sure the reading they plan to take will produce data the criteria can reward.

faqs.question: Is a home physics tutor in Dubai better value than online?
faqs.answer: The published numbers run one way. The Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online, and the premium rises with distance from the central tutoring clusters. The premium pays for a commute. For Higher Level physics there is a second consideration: the specialist pool in this emirate is small, and restricting it to driving distance reduces it further. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line on physics investigation support in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary that should be agreed before the first session. A tutor may teach experimental design, question whether a research question can generate usable data, teach uncertainty treatment and propagation, name the four criteria and their six marks each, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the experiment, supply data, or write any part of the report. Work that is not the student's own produces a malpractice finding against the student rather than the provider. One UAE-facing site advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750.

faqs.question: What did my child miss by coming to IB physics from IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Independent experimental design, mostly. IGCSE physics builds fluency at structured written questions and, in the Cambridge 0625 case, experience of an alternative-to-practical paper where the method is supplied and the student interprets it. Diploma physics asks the student to construct the method themselves, choose the variables, plan the uncertainty treatment and defend the design. Edexcel 4PH1 students arrive with practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than separately, which is a different starting point again. Either way the gap is design rather than content, and it shows up first in the investigation.

faqs.question: Do physics tutors working with Dubai students need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because the permit is free, no provider can justify a charge on the basis of licensing costs. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level physics specialist is free when we need one in Dubai?
faqs.answer: You should be told that plainly, with the options named rather than a general science tutor quietly substituted. Higher Level physics is among the scarcest subjects in this emirate and demand concentrates in the same weeks of the final year. The honest choices are a wait with a date attached, a tutor based outside the UAE delivering on the same live video platform and on Gulf Standard Time, or a referral elsewhere. A specialist rate charged for someone who has not taught Higher Level fields or induction is the thing to refuse. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor.closingHeading: Test the hour before you buy forty of them
dubai/ib-physics-tutor.closingBody: Physics prices at the top of the Dubai market because Higher Level supply is thin, and a family paying at that band should be able to verify what they are getting. Run the eight questions. Watch a structured question marked with the withheld mark explained. Run the twenty-item algebra diagnostic, because that one result often changes the whole plan and its cost. Send the level, the component and whether the investigation is in scope, take the free 30-minute trial lesson, and ask for a plan with a stated hour count so you can hold it against the published bands above.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-barari.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering IB Physics for Al Barari and the surrounding Dubailand communities. Each teaches the course at a named level and has worked with the scientific investigation, which is the component most Dubai students leave too late.

intro.heading: Physics is two separate problems wearing one name
paragraphs: Almost every IB physics difficulty is one of two things, and they need completely different tutoring. The first is mathematical: a student who cannot rearrange confidently, who loses track of units, or who treats a formula as a recipe rather than a relationship. The second is linguistic: a student who understands the physics perfectly and writes an answer that describes what happens instead of explaining why, and therefore scores two marks out of four.

The second problem is the more common one in Dubai and the less often diagnosed. Explanation questions in IB Physics carry a large share of the available marks and they are marked against reasoning, not against knowledge. A candidate who writes that the current increases has described the graph. A candidate who writes that the resistance falls because the temperature rise increases charge-carrier density, so for a fixed potential difference the current rises, has explained it. The physics is identical; the marks are not.

This matters in Al Barari for a practical reason. There is no school inside the community, so pupils commute out to the Dubailand and Nad Al Sheba belt, west towards Motor City and the Arabian Ranches, or across to Al Barsha South. Physics at Higher Level is taught in a minority of those schools, and the number of people in Dubai who teach it to examination standard and have an unused weekday evening within driving distance of a villa community off Al Ain Road is realistically zero. The scarcity is emirate-wide, not local.

The third thing worth establishing before you hire is the investigation. The scientific investigation is worth 20% of the physics grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria. It is also the component students begin latest and the one a tutor can most usefully influence, because the decisions that determine the mark are made before any data exists: what is being varied, what is being controlled, and whether the measurement is actually precise enough to show the effect.

So this page sets out the paper structure and weightings, breaks the investigation down criterion by criterion with its marks, explains honestly how practical work is handled when lessons are online, and shows where explanation marks are lost topic by topic. It also compares Al Barari with the communities around it, because a proximity search is how most families start.

One fact stated plainly. IB Gram delivers physics tuition to Al Barari as live one-to-one lessons over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Physics teaching is a shared screen, a worked problem, a marked explanation question and a conversation about an investigation design, none of which requires anyone to be in the room.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-barari.subjectsIntro: These are the physics topics Al Barari families ask about, with where the explanation marks actually go. Content is rarely the whole problem; the reasoning attached to it usually is.

subjects.name: Mechanics and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum and energy. The dominant loss is treating a graph as the answer: students report that velocity increases rather than reasoning from the resultant force. Momentum questions reward stating conservation explicitly before any calculation.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance and circuit analysis. The reliable weak point in every cohort, because circuit reasoning requires holding three relationships together rather than recalling one. Internal resistance questions are where Higher Level candidates separate.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields and the analogies between them. Higher Level treatment of potential and potential energy is the single most common reason a strong student requests help, because the sign conventions are unforgiving and the concepts are abstract.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Wave behaviour, superposition, standing waves and simple harmonic motion. Phase relationships are where marks go, and the fix is drawing the displacement against time before attempting a verbal answer. Diffraction questions reward naming the condition rather than describing the pattern.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Internal energy, specific heat capacity, latent heat and the ideal gas treatment. Students lose marks by conflating heat and temperature in written answers, which is a vocabulary problem with a mark consequence rather than a physics gap.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, mass defect and the photoelectric effect. Binding-energy calculations compound errors across several steps, so one early rounding decision survives to the final answer. The photoelectric effect rewards a precise statement of the threshold condition.

subjects.name: Energy production
subjects.description: Energy sources, efficiency and the physics of generation and transfer. Often under-revised because it feels descriptive, and it is a reliable source of accessible marks for a student who learns the efficiency arguments properly rather than in general terms.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error analysis
subjects.levels: HL and SL, examined and assessed internally
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and error bars on graphs. Examined in the papers and central to the investigation, and almost always under-taught. A few sessions here pays twice over.

subjects.name: Graph work and data analysis
subjects.description: Linearising relationships, gradients with meaning, intercepts and best-fit judgement. Students plot competently and then fail to state what the gradient physically represents, which is where the marks sit. Also the most transferable skill into the investigation.

subjects.name: Explanation and command terms
subjects.levels: HL and SL, across every topic
subjects.description: 'State', 'describe', 'explain', 'deduce' and 'discuss' carry different mark expectations. The highest-yield intervention available in IB physics is teaching a student to answer the verb, because it recovers marks in every topic at once rather than one topic at a time.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The mark is largely determined before any data exists, by whether the variable chosen can actually be measured precisely enough to show the effect being studied.

subjects.name: Mathematical technique for physics
subjects.description: Rearranging, indices, standard form, trigonometry in resolving vectors and, at Higher Level, the beginnings of calculus reasoning. A physics problem is frequently a mathematics problem in disguise, which is why a physics diagnostic has to test the algebra separately.

sections.heading: The papers, the weightings and where the time should go
paragraphs: The current IB Physics guide sets two written papers at each level plus the internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 combines multiple-choice questions with a data-analysis section. Paper 2 is extended response. The investigation carries 20% of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level. Confirm the exact weightings and durations for your child's cohort with their teacher or Diploma coordinator, because the IB revises subject guides and the current guide is the authority.

The structural point that matters for planning is where the marks are concentrated. The extended-response paper carries the largest single share, and it is where explanation marks live. That means the highest-value tutoring in physics is usually not more content teaching but deliberate practice at writing reasoning, because a student who scores poorly on extended response is losing marks in every topic simultaneously rather than in one.

The data-analysis section of Paper 1 is the second underrated area. It examines uncertainty, graph work, gradients with physical meaning and best-fit judgement — the same skills the investigation requires. A student who learns uncertainty propagation properly gains marks twice: once in the paper and once in the 20% component. Very few Dubai students arrive having been taught it systematically, because it tends to be covered alongside practicals rather than as a topic.

Higher Level differs from Standard Level by extension rather than addition in most topics. That has a specific consequence: you cannot prepare for Higher Level by learning the Standard Level course and then adding extra material at the end. The extension is woven through, which is why a Higher Level student who is behind needs more total hours than the same gap at Standard Level, usually about half again.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single investigation criterion or its mark allocation, which is remarkable given the component is worth a fifth of the grade. In the current science guides the individual scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria, each carrying 6 marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Confirm these with your child's teacher, since the IB revises its guides.

Research design carries 6 marks and is decided before any apparatus is touched. It rewards a clear research question, a methodology that can actually answer it, and explicit treatment of the independent, dependent and controlled variables. The commonest failure in Dubai schools is a question that cannot be answered with school equipment: the effect being studied is smaller than the measurement uncertainty, so the data shows nothing and no amount of later writing recovers it. That is why the viability conversation is the single most valuable hour a physics tutor spends.

Data analysis carries 6 marks and rewards correct processing, appropriate graphing and genuine treatment of uncertainty — error bars, propagation, and a statement of how uncertainty affects the conclusion. Conclusion carries 6 and rewards an answer to the stated research question, justified by the data and compared with accepted physics where relevant. Evaluation carries 6 and rewards identifying specific methodological weaknesses and proposing realistic improvements, not generic ones about human error.

Two practical conclusions. First, the two criteria students neglect, conclusion and evaluation, together carry 12 of the 24 marks and are the cheapest to improve, because they reward thinking rather than apparatus. Second, the whole thing is decided by the design. A student who starts in September with a measurable question has a straightforward route to a strong mark; a student who starts in February with an interesting question that cannot be measured has a problem no tutor can solve.

sections.heading: Practical physics when the tutor is on a screen
paragraphs: This deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. Practical work in IB Physics happens at school. Your child's school has the apparatus, runs the laboratory sessions, and supervises the investigation. A tutor, in any delivery format, is not running experiments for a student, and an in-home tutor arriving at an Al Barari villa with a trolley and a light gate is not what in-home tutoring looks like either.

What a tutor genuinely contributes to practical physics divides into three things, all of which work on a screen. The first is design: whether the proposed variable can be measured well enough, what the controls should be, how many values are needed and over what range. That is a conversation, and it is the part that determines the research design mark. The second is uncertainty and data treatment: propagating uncertainties, plotting with error bars, deciding what a gradient means physically, judging best fit. That is worked on shared data, which is better on a screen than over a dining table because both parties see the same spreadsheet and the same graph.

The third is the writing. The investigation is a written document assessed against four criteria, and the difference between 14 and 20 out of 24 is almost entirely in how the conclusion and evaluation are argued. A tutor reads the student's own draft, says what is not working and why, and the student rewrites. That is identical work in any format.

Where a screen genuinely loses something is in exam-board practical skills questions that assume laboratory familiarity, and in the intuition a student builds from handling apparatus. The honest answer is that the school provides that and a tutor cannot substitute for it. What a tutor can do is make sure the student knows what to look for before the laboratory session, which is more useful than it sounds, because most students arrive at a practical with no plan and spend the session following instructions.

sections.heading: Where physics marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Mark a physics paper rather than asking the student and the same patterns appear in almost every cohort. Four of them account for a large share of the lost marks, and three can be fixed in weeks.

The first is answering the wrong verb. 'State' wants a sentence, 'describe' wants what happens, 'explain' wants why, and 'deduce' wants a conclusion drawn from given information. Students who write everything they know satisfy none of them, and they lose marks in every topic rather than one. Teaching the command terms explicitly is the highest-yield intervention available in this subject, which is why it appears as a tutoring mode on this page rather than as an afterthought.

The second is unit and significant-figure discipline, which bleeds a mark at a time across an entire paper and concentrates in the compound-unit topics: fields, thermal physics, nuclear binding energy. The third is unshown method in multi-step calculation. Mark schemes award credit for steps, so a correct final figure with nothing written scores below a wrong figure with sound working, and the students most affected are the fastest ones.

The fourth is genuinely conceptual and takes longer: the gap between being able to use an equation and understanding the relationship it expresses. A student who can calculate a field strength but cannot say why the potential is negative has a conceptual gap, and it shows up as inconsistency — strong on calculation questions, weak on the explanation questions that carry the larger share of the extended-response paper. That is a term of work rather than a fortnight, and identifying it early is why a diagnostic session separates calculation questions from explanation questions deliberately.

sections.heading: Physics tutor supply here against the communities next door
paragraphs: A proximity search is how most families begin, so here is what it returns in this part of Dubai. For Middle Years sciences, local supply across the Dubailand communities is reasonable. For Diploma physics at Standard Level it is thinner. For Higher Level physics, and particularly for investigation coaching and uncertainty treatment, it is close to non-existent in any of these communities — not because Al Barari is poorly served but because the specialism is narrow and the total number of such teachers in Dubai is small.

Physics is more affected by this than mathematics. A competent mathematician can teach most IGCSE and Standard Level Diploma mathematics. A competent scientist cannot necessarily teach Higher Level physics fields and quantum topics to examination standard, because the content is specific and the explanation conventions are learned from marking. Add a distance filter and a fixed evening slot and the pool empties.

What differs between these communities is the clock rather than the supply. A Nad Al Sheba pupil can begin at half past four; an Al Barari or Mudon pupil realistically begins at five or later after a commute. Physics is particularly badly suited to a late, tired slot, because explanation writing is concentration work rather than repetition. A student who can do physics at ten in the morning may genuinely be unable to do it at seven in the evening, and that is a scheduling problem families routinely mistake for a comprehension problem.

In-home rates rise with distance from the centre while the available pool does not improve, so the further out you live the worse the value of a proximity search. Market in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The premium buys presence, and in physics presence is the component least needed, because the work is a shared screen, a marked answer and a spreadsheet.

Monthly estimates run AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

The more useful way to read those numbers in physics is per component, because the components reward tutoring very unevenly. Investigation coaching is the best-value block available: the component is 20% of the grade, the mark is largely set by design decisions, and six to eight sessions spread across a term can move it substantially. At the specialist band that is a few thousand dirhams against a fifth of a subject grade.

Explanation-writing blocks are the second best value, because the gain applies across every topic at once. Four to six sessions aimed at command terms, with answers marked and rewritten in the session, changes how a student writes for the rest of the course. Content teaching is the least efficient per hour, not because it does not work but because it addresses one topic at a time and there are many topics.

IB Gram publishes no hourly rate on this page, because the right figure depends on level, how many weeks remain and whether the work is content, investigation or technique. What we publish is the market band so any quote can be checked, and the first lesson is free so you can test whether the tutor actually knows the course before any money moves. Ask them to name the four investigation criteria and their marks; that question sorts this market quickly.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and what we will not supply
paragraphs: The investigation is individual assessed work, and there are providers in this region selling completed internal assessments at a published price. Submitting one is academic misconduct and the consequence falls on the student. So the boundary is worth stating before anyone asks, and we state it to the student rather than only to the parent.

A tutor may teach any physics the investigation requires, test whether a design is viable, explain each criterion and what its descriptors mean, teach uncertainty treatment, and read the student's own draft and say what is not working. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply the data, choose the research question outright, or edit a draft into something the student did not produce. Where a draft needs changing, the tutor names the problem and the student rewrites. That is slower and it is the only version that is both lawful and effective, because the conclusion and evaluation criteria reward thinking the student actually did.

On materials: syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. A tutor works from legitimately obtained material and teaches the student to read the assessment criteria themselves. We also do not describe tutors as IB examiners where current status cannot be evidenced, and examiner experience in any case gives no access to marking, boundaries or unseen paper content.

On regulation: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so distrust quoted amounts. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by the IB, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education, and nobody should claim such a thing without a permit number.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand physics but score badly on explanation questions?
faqs.answer: Because explanation questions are marked on reasoning rather than knowledge, and the two are separable. 'The current increases' describes a graph. 'The resistance falls because the temperature rise increases charge-carrier density, so for a fixed potential difference the current rises' explains it. The physics is identical and the marks are not. Students who write everything they know satisfy no command term at all. Teaching the verbs explicitly is the highest-yield intervention in this subject, because it recovers marks in every topic at once rather than one topic at a time.

faqs.question: How much is the IB physics investigation worth and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent of the grade at both Higher and Standard Level, marked out of 24 across four criteria carrying six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Confirm the current allocations with your child's teacher, since the IB revises its guides. The practical point is that research design is decided before any apparatus is touched, and the commonest failure is a question where the effect being studied is smaller than the measurement uncertainty, so the data shows nothing that later writing can recover.

faqs.question: Can physics practical work be taught over video?
faqs.answer: Practical work itself happens at school, with the school's apparatus and supervision, and no tutor in any format substitutes for that. What a tutor contributes divides into three things that all work on a screen: testing whether an investigation design can actually be measured, teaching uncertainty propagation and graph interpretation on shared data, and giving feedback on the student's own written draft. Where a screen genuinely loses something is laboratory intuition from handling apparatus, and we say so rather than pretending otherwise.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to an Al Barari villa?
faqs.answer: No. All UAE tuition is delivered live and one-to-one over video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run only in India and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. For physics the cost of that is minimal, because the work is a shared screen, a worked problem, a marked explanation answer and a spreadsheet of uncertainties. The gain is a shortlist of people who actually teach the course at your child's level, which in Higher Level physics is a small group across the whole emirate.

faqs.question: Which physics topics cause most trouble for Dubai Diploma students?
faqs.answer: Electricity and circuits in every cohort, because circuit reasoning requires holding current, potential difference and resistance together rather than recalling one formula. At Higher Level, fields are the usual request: potential and potential energy have unforgiving sign conventions and abstract concepts. Nuclear binding energy compounds rounding errors across several steps. Underneath all of them sits uncertainty treatment, which is examined in the data-analysis section and central to the investigation, and which almost nobody arrives having been taught systematically.

faqs.question: How many extra hours does Higher Level physics need over Standard Level?
faqs.answer: It is harder in a specific way: it extends the treatment of most topics rather than adding separate ones at the end. That has a practical consequence families should know before choosing. You cannot prepare for Higher Level by learning the Standard Level course and bolting extra material on, because the extension is woven through the whole syllabus. A Higher Level student who is behind therefore needs roughly half again the total hours that the same gap would need at Standard Level, and the sooner that is recognised the cheaper it is.

faqs.question: When should my child start the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Early in the first Diploma year if the school allows it, and at the latest as soon as a topic can be chosen. The reason is that research design carries six of the 24 marks and determines whether the other eighteen are reachable. A student who starts with a measurable question has a straightforward route to a strong mark; one who starts late with an interesting question that school apparatus cannot measure precisely enough has a problem no tutor can fix afterwards. The viability conversation takes an hour and saves a term.

faqs.question: What does IB physics tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget and student tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for qualified subject tutors online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or above for IB specialists, with in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 500 including travel. Monthly, at one session a week, that is roughly AED 240 to AED 600, AED 600 to AED 1,200, or AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above. Those are published market numbers, not IB Gram prices; the first lesson is free.

faqs.question: Which tutoring gives the best value in physics?
faqs.answer: Investigation coaching, because the component is 20% of the grade and the mark is largely set by design decisions that six to eight sessions across a term can genuinely influence. Second is an explanation-writing block of four to six sessions, since the gain applies across every topic at once. Third is two or three sessions on uncertainty and data analysis, which pays twice over: once in the data section of Paper 1 and once in the investigation. Single-topic content teaching works but addresses one topic at a time.

faqs.question: My child is strong at the maths and weak at the physics. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is one of the two standard profiles and it means something specific. A student who calculates confidently and explains poorly usually has a conceptual gap rather than a knowledge gap: they can use an equation without understanding the relationship it expresses. That shows up as inconsistency, strong on calculation questions and weak on extended response. It takes a term rather than a fortnight, and it is why a physics diagnostic should work calculation and explanation questions separately rather than producing a single score.

faqs.question: How does a Middle Years Programme student fare in Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: Differently from an IGCSE student, and the difference is worth knowing. Middle Years sciences assess inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating, so those students usually arrive comfortable with investigation design and weaker on algebraic execution. IGCSE students arrive with solid content coverage and a habit of short answers, so they struggle with extended explanation but handle the manipulation. Knowing which route your child came through tells a tutor where to look in the first session instead of discovering it in week four.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help design my child's investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can test whether a proposed design is viable, which is the most valuable hour available on this component, and can explain what each criterion rewards. What a tutor cannot do is choose the research question outright, supply the data, or write any part of the document, because conclusion and evaluation together carry twelve of the twenty-four marks and reward thinking the student actually did. Where a draft needs changing, the tutor names the problem and the student rewrites it themselves.

faqs.question: Is a weekend morning really better for physics than a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and more so than in other subjects. Explanation writing is concentration work rather than repetition, and a student who reasons well at ten in the morning may genuinely be unable to at seven in the evening after a commute, a full school day and other homework. From Al Barari the realistic weekday start is five o'clock. Families who can manage a weekend morning for the explanation and paper work, with a shorter weekday slot for content, generally get more from the same number of hours.

faqs.question: Do physics tutors in the UAE need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of quoted amounts. Ask to see the permit rather than accepting a verbal assurance, and ask any agency the same question.

faqs.question: Should a Higher Level physics student also be tutored in maths?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the diagnostic should answer it rather than guesswork. Higher Level physics assumes confident rearranging, indices, standard form, vector resolution and the beginnings of calculus reasoning, and where those are shaky the physics sessions spend their time on algebra at specialist rates. If that is the picture, a short mathematics block is cheaper and faster. If the algebra is secure and the explanation is weak, mathematics tutoring will not help and the hours belong in command-term practice instead.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-barari.closingHeading: Two questions that sort this market
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-barari.closingBody: Ask any physics tutor, including ours, to name the four investigation criteria and their mark allocations, and to mark one of your child's explanation answers rather than correct it. A genuine specialist does both without hesitation; much of this market can do neither. Then establish where the investigation stands, because the earlier it is in the process the more a tutor can affect the twenty per cent it carries. From there the work is unglamorous: explanation answers written, marked and rewritten, uncertainty taught once and properly, and full papers under timing. Al Barari sessions run live and one-to-one over video at Gulf Standard Time. Practical work stays at school, we make no home visits in the UAE, and we promise no grades.

intro.heading: Physics help is time-sensitive, and most plans ignore the date
paragraphs: The single most common mistake in IB physics tutoring is buying the wrong intervention for the time of year. A family arrives in March asking for help with a predicted 4 and is sold a weekly content programme that starts at the beginning of the course, which in March is the one thing that cannot work. Another family arrives in the autumn of DP1 and is sold past-paper practice on material the student has not been taught. Both are competently delivered. Both are badly timed, and timing in a two-year programme with a fixed external assessment window is not a detail.

So this page is organised by date rather than by topic. It sets out what each term of the Diploma should achieve in physics, then counts the final eight weeks backwards with a measurable target for each one. The reason eight weeks is the unit is simple: it is roughly the longest period over which a specific, honest plan can be held, and it is roughly the point at which a family notices a problem and starts looking for help.

The assessment structure is what makes the calendar work. In the current Diploma physics guide, Paper 1 carries 36% and includes a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, Paper 2 carries 44% and is the extended-response paper, and the Internal Assessment - a single scientific investigation marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6 - carries 20%. Each of those three blocks has a different last useful moment. The Internal Assessment closes when the school's deadline closes. Paper 2 technique improves until the final fortnight. Learning Theme D fields from nothing stops being viable several weeks out.

On dates specifically, this page publishes none. UAE schools sit the May session, and ibo.org or your school's IB coordinator are the only places to confirm a session window, a results date or an upload deadline. Several pages in this market quote IB dates confidently from secondary sources, and a date a parent plans around is not something to approximate. What this page does instead is count backwards in weeks from whatever your actual dates are, which stays correct every year.

On delivery: IB Gram teaches Al Barsha students one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer in India only. For physics the practical consequence is useful - Paper 2 working, graph analysis and an Internal Assessment draft all annotate better on a shared screen - and the specialist pool for Higher Level physics across this city is small enough that removing the travel requirement is often what makes a match possible at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria each marked out of 8. The Sciences criteria - inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating - map closely onto the Diploma's scientific investigation, which makes MYP science technique a genuine predictor of Internal Assessment performance.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Barsha campuses run the MYP into the Diploma. A student arriving in DP1 Physics from a strong MYP Sciences profile has usually met controlled variables, uncertainty and evaluation before, and finds the Internal Assessment familiar in shape rather than alien.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics, Years 10-11
programmes.description: The other common route in, with Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 the usual specifications. Cambridge 0625 carries a practical component worth 20% of the grade, which is good preparation for Diploma practical work; Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers.

That is a DP1 autumn problem and it is cheap to fix at that point.

programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route, offered by several schools in this cluster. Deeper in physics and narrower overall than the Diploma, with no Theory of Knowledge or Extended Essay competing for evenings.

An A Level physics student has fewer competing deadlines than a Diploma student, so a weekly arrangement is easier to sustain. dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-barsha.subjectsIntro: The physics content below is organised by where it costs marks rather than by syllabus order, because in a calendar-driven plan the order of work is set by mark allocation and time remaining.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, and at Higher Level rotational and relativistic extensions. The losses are rarely conceptual: they are in resolving vectors consistently, in sign conventions for momentum, and in failing to state the system being considered before applying conservation.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws, current electricity and circuits. Circuit questions with two unknowns and internal resistance are the reliable Higher Level loss, usually because the student writes equations without first labelling the circuit and defining the loop.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, wave model, superposition, standing waves and at Higher Level simple harmonic motion in full. Phase relationships and path difference arguments are where marks go, because they require a diagram the student did not draw.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential, and electromagnetic induction. The hardest theme at Higher Level and the one most often reached last in the course, which is exactly why it dominates an eight-week plan when a student is behind.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear energy levels, fission and fusion, and at Higher Level quantum and nuclear structure extensions. Content-light relative to fields and heavily rewarded for precise definitions, which makes it good value late in a plan.

subjects.name: Paper 1A: multiple choice
subjects.description: Part of the 36% Paper 1 weighting. Rewards rapid elimination and unit reasoning rather than full calculation, and improves measurably with timed practice on past questions in the final weeks. The one component where speed is itself the skill.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: data analysis
subjects.description: The data-based section of Paper 1, testing graph interpretation, gradients, uncertainty and whether a conclusion is supported. Improves faster than any other physics component because the skills are rule-governed, and it is routinely never revised separately.

subjects.name: Paper 2: extended response
subjects.description: The 44% paper, where a chain of reasoning must be written out rather than implied. Students who know the physics lose marks by stating a conclusion without the intermediate steps that earn the marks, and by omitting units or directions.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: A single independent investigation marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The most recoverable marks in the subject while the school's deadline is open, and unrecoverable once it closes.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error analysis
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, error bars and lines of maximum and minimum gradient. Examined in Paper 1B and required in the investigation, and the single most transferable physics skill a tutor can teach.

subjects.name: Mathematical technique for physics
subjects.description: Rearrangement, logarithms, small-angle approximations, gradients of non-linear data and linearising relationships. Many apparent physics failures at Higher Level are mathematics failures wearing a physics question, and they are faster to fix than the physics.

subjects.name: Definitions and command terms
subjects.description: State, outline, explain, deduce, show that and determine each demand a different answer shape, and several physics definitions are awarded marks only in precise wording. Cheap marks, learnable late, and almost never deliberately revised.

sections.heading: Where you are in the physics year, and what that changes
paragraphs: An IB physics tutor in Al Barsha should ask what week it is before asking anything about physics. Three blocks make up the grade and each has a different closing date. The Internal Assessment - the scientific investigation, 20% of the grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6 - is recoverable until the school's deadline and then not at all. Paper 2, at 44%, is the extended-response paper and its technique improves right up to the final fortnight. Paper 1, at 36%, splits into a multiple-choice section where speed is the skill and a data-analysis section where the skills are rule-governed and move faster than anything else in the subject.

That produces a simple decision rule. If the school's investigation deadline is still open, the first conversation is about the investigation, whatever the parent came to discuss, because it is the largest block of marks still fully within the student's control. If the deadline has passed, the first conversation is about which paper the marked mock says is losing marks, and the answer is usually Paper 2 reasoning rather than physics knowledge.

The seasonal mistakes follow from ignoring this. In October of DP1, families buy past-paper practice on material not yet taught, which produces discouragement rather than information. In February of DP2, families buy a content programme starting from Theme A, which spends the available weeks on the part of the course the student already knows. In the week an investigation draft is due, families buy an extra session, which adds pressure to the week that had least capacity for it. Each of these is an ordinary, well-intentioned decision made without reference to the calendar.

This page does not publish IB session or results dates. UAE schools sit the May session; ibo.org and your school's IB coordinator hold the specifics, and the internal deadlines your coordinator sets matter more day to day than the external ones. Ask for the full internal deadline list at the start of DP1 - investigation drafts, Extended Essay milestones, mock weeks, predicted grades - and build everything, including tutoring, around that list.

sections.heading: The eight weeks counted backwards, with a measurable target each week
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the window in which a specific plan can honestly be held, and it is when most families start looking. The table below is a worked plan for a student with a marked mock, a passed investigation deadline and two themes they have never properly learned. It is deliberately ordered by return per week rather than by syllabus sequence.

The ordering logic has three parts. Paper 1B data analysis comes first because its skills - gradients, uncertainty, error bars, whether a conclusion is supported - are rule-governed, transfer to Paper 2, and typically move within two weeks. Definitions and command terms come early for the same reason: they are cheap, finite and never revised deliberately. Then the unlearned content, taken strictly in order of marks available rather than in the order the textbook presents it, which in practice usually means Theme D fields before anything else because fields is both heavily examined and the theme most often reached last.

Timed full papers come last, in the final fortnight, and not before. Practising under time pressure while technique is insecure teaches a student to make the same errors faster and produces a demoralising score that informs nobody. Pacing - knowing when to leave a question - is a genuine skill worth several marks, and it is the only thing a timed paper teaches that an untimed one does not.

The important column in the table is the last one. A plan without a weekly measure is a wish. If week three's target was to score the uncertainty questions on two past Paper 1B sections and the student cannot, the plan changes in week four rather than at the end. That is the whole value of counting backwards: it converts eight weeks of anxiety into eight checkable statements.

sections.heading: Paper 1 and Paper 2: different papers, different problems
paragraphs: In the current Diploma physics guide Paper 1 carries 36% and Paper 2 carries 44%, and treating them as one revision task is why students plateau. They test different things and fail for different reasons, so a plan that improves one may do nothing for the other.

Paper 1 splits in two. The multiple-choice section rewards elimination, unit reasoning and order-of-magnitude judgement, and the skill is partly speed: a student who calculates every option fully will not finish. The data-analysis section tests graph interpretation, gradient extraction, uncertainty handling and whether a stated conclusion is supported by the data shown. That second part is the most improvable component in the whole subject, because the marks go to specific conventions rather than to insight, and it is the component most often never revised separately from the physics.

Paper 2 is where the physics knowledge of a capable student goes unrewarded. The paper asks for extended responses, and the marks sit on the intermediate steps of a reasoning chain. A student who understands that increasing the separation reduces the field strength, writes that conclusion, and omits the relationship it depends on will score a fraction of the available marks. Units, directions and the system under consideration all carry marks. This is a writing problem attached to physics, and it responds to being marked against a scheme rather than to being re-taught.

The practical instruction for a student in the final weeks: revise Paper 1B as a separate skill, drill definitions and command terms as a separate task, and practise writing six-mark Paper 2 answers in full before worrying about whether the physics is complete. A student who can write a complete reasoning chain on the physics they do know will outscore a student with broader knowledge and no structure, reliably, every session.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks, four criteria, one deadline
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment in Diploma physics is a single independent scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is the largest block of marks a student fully controls, and it closes permanently when the school's deadline closes. Both halves of that sentence should drive the calendar.

Where the marks go is predictable. Research design loses marks when the question is too broad, when the methodology does not justify its choices, and when the controlled variables are listed without explaining why they matter. Data analysis loses marks on uncertainty propagation, on graphs without error bars where they are warranted, and on processing that is correct but not explained. Conclusion loses marks when it states a result without comparing it to accepted values or established theory. Evaluation loses the most marks of all, because students list limitations instead of judging their impact on the result and proposing realistic, specific improvements.

What a tutor may legitimately do here is substantial and worth paying for. Teach the four criteria in the IB's own terms. Interrogate the research question before weeks are spent on it. Explain uncertainty propagation and graphing conventions. Read a draft and say which criterion it currently falls short of and why. Ask the questions the supervisor will ask. What a tutor may not do is write, draft, restructure or edit any part of the investigation, or design it for the student. The work is submitted under the student's name with their supervisor's authentication, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student.

The timing point for an Al Barsha family: the useful window opens before data collection, not after. A tutor reading a finished draft can improve the evaluation and the write-up. A tutor consulted before the design is fixed can prevent the entire investigation from being built on a question that cannot produce analysable data - which is the single most expensive failure available in this component, because it cannot be repaired by better writing.

table.caption: THE SCIENTIFIC INVESTIGATION - FOUR CRITERIA OF 6, AND WHERE THE MARKS GO
rows: A focused question with justified methodology

No error bars; propagation omitted; processing unexplained
A result compared against theory or accepted values
A statement of findings with no comparison
Limitations listed, impact not judged, improvements vague
A coherent investigation, not four separate sections
Sections that do not refer to each other

sections.heading: Term by term through DP1 and DP2
paragraphs: The eight-week plan is for people who are already late. The cheaper version of this page is the term-by-term one, and it starts in the autumn of DP1 with something that is not physics: mathematics. Higher Level physics assumes algebraic rearrangement, logarithms, small-angle approximations and the ability to linearise a non-linear relationship, and a student arriving from IGCSE Physics has usually not needed any of it. Several apparent physics failures in DP1 are mathematics failures wearing a physics question, and they are faster and cheaper to fix in October than in March.

The second DP1 priority is uncertainty, taught as a working habit rather than as an examinable topic. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, error bars and lines of maximum and minimum gradient appear in Paper 1B and are required in the investigation. A student who treats uncertainty as something to learn later will do the investigation twice: once without it and once properly.

Spring of DP1 is where the investigation question should be forming, and where a short tutoring intervention has disproportionate value. Summer and the start of DP2 are when the content load peaks and when Theme D fields usually arrives - the hardest theme and the one students most often meet while also writing an Extended Essay. Autumn of DP2 is the investigation deadline and the mock season, which together consume the term. The final months are papers and technique only.

The practical scheduling consequence in Al Barsha is to place tuition where the calendar has room rather than where the anxiety is loudest. Autumn DP1 and spring DP1 have genuine capacity. Autumn DP2 does not, and adding a weekly session to the term that contains both the investigation deadline and mocks frequently makes the term worse. A plan that front-loads is cheaper, calmer and more effective than one that back-loads, which is the opposite of how most families buy.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs, and when in the year to buy it
paragraphs: Cost in physics is as much about timing as about rate, which is why this section sits inside a calendar page. The same hour bought in October of DP1 and in March of DP2 does different amounts of work, and the March hour costs the same or more. Published Dubai rates run from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik in the budget band, through AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one with travel runs AED 180-500, Bestimate quoting AED 180-350. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650.

For Higher Level physics the specialist band is often simply what the subject costs, because the pool of people who can teach fields and uncertainty properly at that level is small across the whole emirate. That is a genuine difference from, say, IGCSE mathematics, where the mid band is usually sufficient. It is also the reason the cheapest total cost comes from buying early: a smaller number of specialist hours in DP1 does more than a larger number in DP2, and the DP2 hours are the ones most likely to be unavailable because every other family wants them in the same eight weeks.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. The exam-year band is the relevant one for most DP2 physics requests, and seeing it written down is usually what prompts a family to ask whether all of those hours are needed. Frequently they are not: an investigation block plus a Paper 1B block plus an eight-week plan is a smaller total than a weekly arrangement running from September.

All figures above are other providers' published rates, read during the October 2026 research round, quoted as market context rather than as an IB Gram price list. For household context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private-school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. School fees are capped by policy; tuition is not, and in a Diploma year it is the line that grows fastest. Before committing, ask for the rate per 60 minutes, whether VAT is included, the cancellation terms, and the tutor's position on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Barsha, and what eight weeks cannot do
paragraphs: Send four things: the level, the current predicted grade, where the scientific investigation stands, and the most recent marked mock. Add the school's internal deadline list if you have it. From those we can write the plan in one message - whether the first block is the investigation, Paper 1B, unlearned content in mark order, or nothing. Then we match a tutor who teaches physics at that level, you take a full-length trial lesson at no cost on your child's own paper, and you decide.

Sessions run weekly in Gulf Standard Time. For Al Barsha the honest start is 5:00pm for a local gate and 5:15pm for a commute from Al Sufouh, Jumeirah Village or Emirates Hills, since Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road take the whole corridor's traffic at release. A sports fixture in Al Quoz removes that evening entirely. Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing. Weekend mornings suit timed papers and investigation work, which need more than an hour.

What eight weeks cannot do, said plainly. It cannot teach two years of physics. It cannot reopen a closed investigation deadline, which is why the investigation question is asked first in every enquiry. It cannot make a student who has not learned fields competitive on a paper that examines fields heavily - it can only ensure they score everything available elsewhere. And it cannot produce a grade promise, from us or from anybody; a provider offering one in the final weeks is selling reassurance to a worried parent.

The fixed limits. No home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. No claimed approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson - the IB authorises schools rather than tutors and IB Gram holds nothing from any of them. No writing, drafting, restructuring or editing of a scientific investigation, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed work. No supplied or reproduced past papers, mark schemes or subject guides; we reference the official sources and work from your school's own copies. No IB dates published without confirmation on ibo.org. And no statistics about our own results, because we cannot publish the sample, date and method that would make them meaningful.
