process.title: Say where you are in the year
process.description: The level, the predicted grade, whether the scientific investigation deadline is open or closed, and the date of the next mock. Those four facts determine the whole plan, and the investigation question is the one that changes it most.

process.title: Send the marked mock
process.description: A marked paper with the examiner or teacher marks visible shows whether losses sit in Paper 1A speed, Paper 1B data technique, Paper 2 reasoning structure or unlearned content. Those four need completely different plans in completely different orders.

process.title: Agree the weekly targets in writing
process.description: For a defined block, each week gets a focus and a measure - full marks on two data-analysis sections, definitions recited precisely, past questions on one theme scored unaided. A plan without weekly measures cannot be corrected mid-course.

process.title: Take the free trial on your own paper
process.description: A full-length one-to-one lesson at no cost on your child's marked mock. Judge it on whether the tutor names components and weightings, states the investigation boundary unprompted, and orders the work by marks available rather than by syllabus.

process.title: Review weekly against the measure, not the mood
process.description: Each week either hit its target or it did not, and the plan changes in the following week rather than at the end. In a final-term block that weekly correction is the whole mechanism; in DP1 a six-to-eight-week review is enough.

whyPoints.title: The date is asked before the physics
whyPoints.description: Three blocks make up a physics grade and each has a different closing date. Buying a content programme in March or past papers in October is competently delivered and badly timed, and timing is the most common avoidable error in this subject.

whyPoints.title: The investigation is raised first, every time
whyPoints.description: It is 20% of the grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6, and it closes permanently at the school's deadline. Asking about it in the first message is not a sales step; it is the only part of the plan that has an expiry date.

whyPoints.title: Work ordered by marks available
whyPoints.description: In a limited window, topics are taken in order of marks rather than syllabus sequence, and Paper 1B data technique comes before content because it moves fastest and transfers to Paper 2. That ordering is the difference between triage and a tour.

whyPoints.title: Weekly measures, not weekly sessions
whyPoints.description: Each week of a defined block carries a target you can check. If week three's target is missed, week four changes. Without that, eight weeks of sessions produce a feeling of progress and no information about whether there was any.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates we have not verified
whyPoints.description: ibo.org blocks automated access, so this page publishes no session or results dates and points you to your coordinator instead. Several pages in this market quote dates they have not confirmed, and a date a parent plans around deserves better.

whyPoints.title: Early beats late, and we say so
whyPoints.description: Mathematical technique and uncertainty bought in the autumn of DP1 do more than twice the hours bought in March, and specialist physics hours in the final eight weeks are the hardest in the market to get. Saying this costs us the panic season.

faqs.question: We are eight weeks from the physics papers. What is actually achievable?
faqs.answer: Technique and triage, not coverage. In eight weeks a student can learn Paper 1B data analysis properly, drill definitions and command terms, learn the two or three highest-mark topics they never covered, and fix Paper 2 reasoning structure so the physics they do know scores fully. What cannot happen is learning two years of content. Order matters: data analysis first because it is rule-governed and moves fastest, definitions next because they are cheap and finite, then unlearned content strictly in order of marks available, then timed papers in the final fortnight only.

faqs.question: Is the scientific investigation still worth working on at this stage?
faqs.answer: Only if the school's deadline is open, and that is the first question to answer. The investigation is worth 20% of the physics grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria of 6 - research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation - which makes it the largest block of marks a student fully controls. Once the school's deadline passes it is closed permanently. If it is still open, work on it before anything else, because evaluation and data analysis marks are often recoverable in a few sessions. If it has closed, the whole plan moves to the papers.

faqs.question: Which physics component improves fastest?
faqs.answer: The data-analysis section of Paper 1. Its marks go to specific conventions - extracting a gradient correctly, propagating uncertainty, drawing error bars, drawing lines of maximum and minimum gradient, and stating only conclusions the data supports - and conventions can be learned in two weeks. It also transfers: the same skills are required in the scientific investigation and show up in Paper 2 questions on experimental data. Despite that, it is the component students most often never revise separately, because it feels like a part of the physics rather than a skill of its own.

faqs.question: My child knows the physics but scores badly on Paper 2. Why?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 2 marks sit on the intermediate steps of a reasoning chain, not on the conclusion. A student who understands that increasing separation reduces field strength, writes that conclusion, and omits the relationship it rests on will score a fraction of the available marks. Units, directions and a statement of the system under consideration all carry marks too. This is a writing problem attached to physics and it responds to being marked against a scheme rather than to being re-taught. Two to four weeks of writing full six-mark answers usually moves it.

faqs.question: What should a DP1 physics student work on in the autumn term?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and uncertainty, which is not what families expect to buy. Higher Level physics assumes algebraic rearrangement, logarithms, small-angle approximations and the ability to linearise a non-linear relationship, none of which IGCSE Physics required. Several apparent physics failures in DP1 are mathematics failures wearing a physics question. Alongside that, uncertainty should be taught as a working habit rather than as an examinable topic, because it appears in Paper 1B and is required throughout the investigation. Both are far cheaper to fix in October than in March, and both prevent problems rather than repairing them.

faqs.question: When do IB physics exams happen and when do results come out?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session, and this page deliberately publishes no specific session or results dates. ibo.org is the authoritative source and your school's IB coordinator holds the internal deadlines that matter more day to day - investigation drafts, Extended Essay milestones, upload dates, mock weeks and the predicted-grade point. Several pages in this market state IB dates confidently from secondary sources, and a date a family plans around should be confirmed rather than inherited. Ask the coordinator for the full internal list at the start of DP1 and build everything around that.

faqs.question: Which theme should an Al Barsha student tackle first with six weeks left?
faqs.answer: Fields - gravitational, electric and magnetic, potential, and electromagnetic induction. It is conceptually the hardest, it is heavily examined, and it usually arrives late in the course, often while the student is also writing an Extended Essay. That combination means a student behind on fields is behind on a large share of available marks with little time left. In an eight-week plan it is normally the first content block, ahead of anything else, because the marks per hour available there exceed anything in the earlier themes the student has already covered.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do on the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Teach the four criteria in the IB's own terms, interrogate the research question before weeks are spent on it, explain uncertainty propagation and graphing conventions, read a draft and say which criterion it falls short of and why, and ask the questions the supervisor will ask. A tutor may not write, draft, restructure or edit any part of it, nor design the investigation for the student. The work is submitted under your child's name with their supervisor's authentication, so the malpractice consequence is theirs. Agree the boundary explicitly before any session on the investigation.

faqs.question: Is it better to consult a tutor before or after collecting investigation data?
faqs.answer: Before, decisively. A tutor reading a finished draft can improve the write-up, the conclusion and the evaluation. A tutor consulted before the design is fixed can prevent an investigation built on a question that cannot produce analysable data - which is the most expensive failure available in this component, because no amount of good writing repairs it. One session on the research question, early, is worth several sessions on the draft later. Almost nobody books that session, because at that stage nothing appears to be wrong.

faqs.question: What do Al Barsha families pay per hour for Diploma physics support?
faqs.answer: Published specialist rates sit at AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's guidance putting IB specialists at AED 200-450 or more, while a qualified subject tutor working online runs AED 150-300 and Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. For Higher Level physics the specialist band is often simply what the subject costs, because the pool able to teach fields and uncertainty properly is small across the emirate. Monthly estimates for specialist exam-year support run AED 1,000-2,000 or more. Buying fewer hours earlier beats buying more hours in the final term.

faqs.question: When should timed physics papers start?
faqs.answer: The final fortnight, and not before. Timed practice while technique is still insecure trains a student to make the same errors faster and produces a score that discourages without informing. The correct order is content, then mark-scheme technique, then the clock. What a timed paper teaches that nothing else does is pacing - when to abandon a question and return to it - and that is worth several marks on a long paper. Two timed papers with proper reviews in the last two weeks does more than six timed papers spread across a term.

faqs.question: Our child has a service commitment and sport. How do we fit physics in?
faqs.answer: Plan around three usable weekday evenings rather than five, and put the tutored session on the best of them. In this corridor a fixture in Al Quoz or Al Barsha removes a whole evening because of the double journey, not just the hours of the activity. Keep weekend mornings for the work that needs more than an hour - a timed full paper, an investigation session - because an hour squeezed into a tired weekday evening is not where extended work belongs. A plan that assumes five free evenings will be abandoned by October.

faqs.question: What time can an Al Barsha physics session realistically start?
faqs.answer: 5:00pm for a student at a local Al Barsha gate and 5:15pm if the commute runs out to Al Sufouh, Jumeirah Village or Emirates Hills. Secondary release across this cluster is tightly bunched between roughly 2:45pm and 3:15pm, and Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road take the corridor's traffic simultaneously, so arrival is usually between 3:40pm and 4:35pm. Allow for changing and food. Online delivery keeps that window intact, because nothing in the arrangement depends on how either road happens to be moving at the time.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle physics and maths together?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma student this is one of the genuinely sensible pairings, because the overlap is real. Higher Level physics assumes rearrangement, logarithms, small-angle approximations and linearising relationships, and a tutor working across both can teach the mathematics inside the physics question where the student will actually meet it. That is often more effective than separate sessions, and cheaper. Beyond adjacent pairings the claim gets thin: a tutor offering four Higher Level subjects is claiming something improbable, and matching should still be done on level as strictly as on subject.

faqs.question: What would make you say the eight-week plan is not worth buying?
faqs.answer: If the marked mock shows the student is losing marks almost entirely to content never taught across several themes, eight weeks of specialist tuition will not change the grade materially, and the honest plan is a cheaper, narrower one: secure Paper 1B, the definitions and one high-mark theme, and accept the rest. If the investigation has closed at a low band and the papers are already strong, there may be nothing worth buying at all. And if the student is not doing work between sessions, more sessions is the wrong purchase - that is a supervision problem, not a physics one.

intro.heading: Al Barsha South, Dubai Marina, Al Barsha 1 — the same Physics paper in all three
paragraphs: An IB Physics tutor in Al Barsha South is a different search from an IB Physics tutor in Dubai Marina only in one respect: the traffic. The syllabus is identical. A student at a school off Hessa Street and a student in a tower on the Marina walk sit the same Paper 1, the same Paper 2, and submit a scientific investigation marked against the same four criteria out of the same 24 marks. If your child is losing marks on uncertainty propagation, the postcode has nothing to do with it and moving to a tutor two districts over will not fix it.

What the postcode does change is which tutors can physically reach you, and that is exactly the constraint worth removing. Al Barsha South sits behind Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, bounded by Dubai Science Park, Arjan and the Jumeirah Village communities. A tutor driving in from Mirdif at 4.30pm on a Tuesday is making a forty-minute trip each way, and you pay for that in the hourly rate whether the invoice itemises it or not. The pool of Physics specialists who will make that drive is small, and it is smaller again if you need Physics HL rather than SL.

Delivered online, the pool stops being a map problem. A family in Al Barsha South 2 can work with a specialist who has taught the fields and nuclear content at HL for years, instead of whoever is free within a twenty-minute radius. That is the whole argument, and it is the same argument a Marina family or an Arjan family would get: the comparison between districts collapses once distance stops being a filter. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India, and saying so plainly is more useful to you than a promise we would not keep.

This page is written for the comparison you are actually running. It sets Al Barsha South against the neighbourhoods either side of it on the things that genuinely differ — school end times, commute windows, which schools each cluster feeds, what the in-home market quotes for a visit — and then shows where those differences stop mattering. It also does the part the competing pages skip: the actual assessment structure, the themes, the places Physics marks disappear, what the Dubai market charges in AED with the source attached, and where the line sits between coaching an investigation and interfering with it.

One thing to settle before you read further. Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. Individuals giving private lessons need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which u.ae states is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone offering to teach your child in Al Barsha South without one is operating outside that framework, and the official application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Ask. It is a reasonable question and a tutor who cannot answer it has told you something.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-barsha-sout.programmesIntro: Physics does not begin in DP1. The students who find themes A and B manageable are usually the ones who met forces, energy and particle models properly in MYP Sciences or IGCSE. These are the programme stages we teach into, and what each one needs from a Physics tutor working with a family in Al Barsha South.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Physics SL and HL share five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. HL adds further content inside each theme rather than bolting on a sixth. Assessment is Paper 1, Paper 2 and the scientific investigation. Paper 1 splits into multiple-choice and a data-analysis section, which is where students who have only practised calculation questions get caught.
programmes.countryNote: Al Barsha South students mostly reach DP Physics through one of two routes: a British-curriculum IGCSE at a school in Al Barsha South or Al Barsha 1, or MYP Sciences at an IB continuum school. The two routes arrive with different gaps. IGCSE students are fluent in recall and weak on uncertainties; MYP students are comfortable with investigation design and short on algebraic fluency. The first two lessons establish which of those you have.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed on four criteria rather than papers, and Physics content sits inside an integrated sciences course for most of the programme. MYP 4 and 5 are where Physics separates out in many schools. Criterion B and C work — inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating — is the direct ancestor of the DP investigation, so a student who has been coasting on criterion A knowledge drops sharply in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Barsha South and Al Barsha 1 families are at IB continuum schools and will choose between Physics SL, Physics HL and a non-Physics science at the end of MYP 5. We treat that choice as a real one with evidence behind it: how the student handled rearranging equations, whether they could design a fair test without a template, and what the MYP 5 criterion scores actually say rather than what the predicted grade feels like.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the pre-DP route
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 are the two syllabuses most British-curriculum schools in this part of Dubai run. Both split into core and extended or tiered papers, and both carry an assessment of practical skills. The content overlap with DP themes A, B and C is substantial, which is why a weak IGCSE Physics grade is a reliable predictor of a difficult DP1.
programmes.countryNote: A family in Al Barsha South choosing between A Level and IB Diploma at 16 is usually also choosing between two schools in different districts. Physics is the subject where that choice bites hardest, because the IB route keeps the investigation and the data-analysis paper while the A Level route weights the written papers more heavily. We will say which suits a given student rather than which is better in the abstract.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme science components
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines DP courses with a career-related study, and students taking a DP Physics course inside CP sit exactly the same Physics assessment as a full Diploma candidate. The difference is the surrounding load: fewer DP subjects, a reflective project, and a service-learning requirement that competes for the same evenings a Physics investigation needs.
programmes.countryNote: CP is offered at a small number of Dubai schools and is rare in the Al Barsha South cluster, so most families here will not meet it. We list it because the Physics component is identical and because parents comparing schools across districts occasionally find it and assume the Physics is lighter. It is not. The papers and the investigation weightings do not change.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-barsha-sout.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely the only pressure point. These are the subjects most often taught alongside it for students in Al Barsha South and the neighbouring communities, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks go missing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E, with HL extension inside each. Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44%, investigation at 20%. The recurring HL failure is fields: students handle gravitational and electric fields separately and never see the shared structure, so transfer questions between them collapse.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual partner subject for Physics HL. Calculus fluency is what makes kinematics and rates of change in Physics feel easy or impossible. AA HL students who are secure on differentiation rarely struggle with Physics theme A; the ones who are not, do.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI SL alongside Physics SL is a common Al Barsha South combination and it works, with one caveat: AI spends less time on algebraic rearrangement, so Physics becomes the place where that weakness appears. We drill rearrangement inside Physics rather than pretending it is a maths problem.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the four investigation criteria and the same uncertainty conventions as Physics, so the skills transfer directly. Students doing both sciences often write two investigations in the same term; sequencing those so they do not collide is half the support we give in DP1.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The data-analysis half of Paper 1 rewards the same habits in Biology as in Physics: read the axes, check the units, say what the gradient physically means. Biology students who have been taught to describe rather than interpret lose marks in exactly the same places.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paired with Physics HL by students heading for engineering. The overlap is logic and systems thinking rather than content, but the internal assessment load is heavy and runs on the same calendar as the Physics investigation, which matters for planning.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: The design cycle shares its evaluation habits with the Physics investigation, and students doing both get a genuine advantage in criterion D. The risk is the opposite one: a Physics investigation written as a design project loses marks for having no measurable research question.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Mechanics content overlaps with Physics theme A more than most students expect, particularly around forces, moments and energy transfer. Where a student is taking it instead of Physics, we teach the mechanics directly rather than treating it as applied biology.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Energy flow, efficiency and thermodynamics appear here in a form Physics students recognise immediately. ESS is often chosen as the second science by a Physics HL student, and the quantitative sections are where a Physics tutor is useful to an ESS grade.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The natural sciences area of knowledge is far easier to write about with a worked Physics example in hand than from the textbook treatment. We use the student's own investigation as the case study, which is legitimate and makes the TOK exhibition specific rather than abstract.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB Physics tutor in Al Barsha South is actually asking
paragraphs: A parent in Al Barsha South typing this phrase is asking two questions at once, and only one of them is about Physics. The first is whether a competent DP Physics specialist can be found who will work with their child. The second, usually unspoken, is whether living in Al Barsha South rather than Al Barsha 1, Dubai Marina or Emirates Hills puts them at a disadvantage. The answer to the first is yes. The answer to the second is that it did, until delivery stopped being geographic.

Here is the concrete version of that. The in-home tutoring market in Dubai works on a radius. A tutor advertising DP Physics HL will cover the districts they can reach inside roughly half an hour, because an hour of unpaid driving around a 60-minute lesson makes the economics impossible otherwise. Al Barsha South sits behind a motorway interchange and the inbound traffic at 5pm is the worst part of the day. The practical result is a thinner list of people willing to come, and a higher quoted rate from the ones who are.

Online delivery removes the radius entirely, and that is a bigger change than it sounds for a subject as specialised as Physics. The constraint on Physics tutoring is not supply of tutors in general; it is supply of tutors who have taught theme D at HL often enough to know where students lose the marks. That person might be anywhere. Matching on syllabus experience rather than driving distance is the single most useful thing this format does, and it applies identically to a family in Al Barsha South 2 and a family in JLT.

So the honest framing of this page is not that Al Barsha South is special. It is that the comparison between Al Barsha South and the district next door, which is the comparison most parents here are running, stops being a factor once the lesson happens over video. What remains worth comparing is school end times, which school each pocket feeds, and when a session can realistically start. Those are real differences and the next section sets them out.

Set side by side, Al Barsha South, Al Barsha Heights and the Emirates Hills cluster differ on commute, school pool and when an evening session can start. They do not differ on syllabus, assessment, grade boundaries or anything else that determines a Physics grade.

Read the last column first. Every row ends in the same place: it changes the scheduling conversation and nothing about the teaching. A student in Al Barsha South 4 who cannot start before 5.15pm needs a later slot than a student in Al Barsha Heights who walks home. Both need the same work on uncertainty propagation and the same number of timed Paper 1 sets before May.

The one row worth dwelling on is tutor pool. In-home coverage genuinely varies between these districts, and it varies most for the narrowest subjects. A family wanting general maths support will find someone locally in any of them. A family wanting Physics HL with real theme D experience will find the list short in all three, and shortest in whichever district is furthest from where tutors actually live. That asymmetry is the one the online format erases, which is why the comparison ends in a draw.

If you are weighing a school move between these clusters, weigh it on the school: Physics HL availability, how many students the department runs, whether the investigation is scheduled early or late in DP1, and what KHDA's current inspection report says. Those are the differences that reach the grade. Driving time to a tutor is not one of them any more.

sections.heading: IB Physics assessment structure, and what each component actually rewards
paragraphs: Most pages selling Physics tutoring describe the subject as challenging and stop there. The useful version names the components, their weightings and what each one tests, because a student losing marks in Paper 1 needs completely different work from a student losing them in the investigation. Physics at both levels is assessed by Paper 1, Paper 2 and the scientific investigation, weighted 36%, 44% and 20%.

Paper 1 is the component families underestimate. It divides into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, and those two halves reward opposite habits. Multiple-choice punishes slow, full working; data analysis punishes fast, pattern-matched answers. A student who has only practised Paper 2-style extended questions arrives at Paper 1 able to do the physics and unable to do the paper. That is a technique problem and it is fixable in weeks.

Paper 2 is where the five themes are tested in extended response, and where command terms decide the mark. Explain, deduce, determine, suggest and state ask for structurally different answers, and the mark scheme awards the structure as much as the content. A student who writes a correct paragraph in answer to determine has not answered the question. This is the most reliable source of recoverable marks we see in DP2.

The investigation carries a fifth of the grade on a report capped at 3,000 words and marked on four criteria of six marks each. It is the only component where a student controls the conditions entirely, and the only one where a careless research question limits the ceiling before a single measurement is taken. Treating it as coursework to be completed rather than a designed experiment is the single most expensive mistake available in DP Physics.

sections.heading: Where IB Physics marks are lost, theme by theme
paragraphs: Physics marks do not leak evenly. They cluster, and they cluster in the same places across every school in Dubai we have worked with. Knowing the cluster matters because it converts a vague instinct that a child is struggling with Physics into a short list of fixable things, which is what a first diagnostic lesson is for.

In theme A, the loss is almost always vectors treated as numbers. A student who can quote that momentum is conserved but cannot handle a two-dimensional collision has a vector problem, not a momentum problem. In theme B, it is the difference between heat and temperature, and the sign conventions in the first law. Students who can recite the equations lose marks because they cannot say which way energy moved.

Theme C punishes imprecision about phase and path difference, and standing waves are where that becomes visible. Theme D, fields, is the reliable HL killer: gravitational and electric fields are taught weeks apart, learned as separate formula sets, and never connected, so any question that transfers between them finds the gap. Theme E loses marks on decay and binding energy because students work with mass numbers instead of mass defect.

Across all five, two habits cost more than any content gap. The first is omitting units and direction, which the mark scheme penalises without mercy. The second is answering the command term the student wishes had been asked. Both are trainable, both are fast to train, and both are why a student who understands the physics can still sit at a 4. We start there because it is the quickest honest gain available.
bullets: Theme A: vectors handled as scalars; relative motion; energy accounting with no system defined
Theme B: heat versus temperature; sign conventions; ideal gas assumptions applied where they fail
Theme C: phase and path difference; standing-wave boundary conditions; superposition sketched not reasoned
Theme D: gravitational and electric fields learned as unrelated topics, so transfer questions fail
Theme E: mass defect versus mass number; half-life questions attempted arithmetically rather than exponentially
Everywhere: missing units, missing direction, and the wrong command term answered confidently

A university-student tutor working online is advertised in Dubai from around AED 45 to AED 65 an hour by EdFlik, and Tutopiya's published rates start lower again at roughly AED 33 to AED 52. At that level you are buying homework supervision. For DP Physics HL specifically, that is not what is needed, and families who try it usually pay twice.

Move up one tier and the figures change shape. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 and IB tutoring from AED 200 an hour, which is the honest band for a qualified subject tutor working online. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level support at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and BartyED sits at the top of the visible market at AED 650 for premium named tutors. Three of the six best-ranking pages in this search publish no price at all.

The in-home column is the one worth reading carefully, because it is where the travel premium becomes visible. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. The gap between the online and in-home band for the same tutor quality is not a quality difference. It is the drive to Al Barsha South, priced in. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

None of those are IB Gram's prices and none of them are quoted as ours. They are the market, cited so you can check them yourself against the same pages we read. What a parent should take from the table is the shape rather than any single number: the jump from budget to qualified is large and worth paying, the jump from qualified to premium is smaller and much more dependent on the individual, and the in-home premium buys travel rather than teaching.

sections.heading: Online against a tutor driving to Al Barsha South, compared honestly
paragraphs: A fair comparison has to concede what in-home tutoring genuinely does better. A tutor in the room can see a student's page without asking, can hand them a paper and watch them start, and removes any argument about whether the camera is on. For a younger child who needs a physical presence to stay on task, that is a real advantage and no amount of video quality replaces it. Saying otherwise would be dishonest.

What it costs is visible in the previous table. The in-home band sits AED 100 to AED 200 above the online band for comparable experience, and Al Barsha South is on the expensive side of that spread because of the interchange traffic. Beyond the rate, the hidden cost is cancellation: a tutor stuck on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road at 5pm loses the session, not half of it, and in DP2 a lost week before the May session is not recoverable by doubling up later.

The decisive factor for Physics specifically is the tutor pool. In-home restricts you to specialists within driving range of Al Barsha South who happen to have a free slot at 5pm. For Physics HL with real theme D depth, that list is short in every Dubai district, and short lists mean you take availability over fit. Online, the filter is syllabus experience, which is the filter that actually predicts whether a student's uncertainty work improves.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so this is not a comparison we are pretending to be neutral about, and you should read it knowing that. Our home-visiting service operates only in India. sections.heading: The Physics investigation: what a tutor may do, and what would be malpractice
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is worth a fifth of the Physics grade and it is the component where outside help goes wrong most often. The IB's academic-honesty rules make the student the author of the work, and a breach is an expulsion risk for the student rather than an inconvenience for the tutor. So the boundary needs stating in plain terms before any investigation support begins, not after.

What a tutor can legitimately do is teach. That means teaching how a research question becomes measurable, teaching uncertainty propagation properly rather than as a formula to be recalled, explaining how the four criteria are awarded and what the six marks inside each are actually for, reviewing the student's own draft and giving feedback that names the criterion. All of that is teaching and all of it is normal practice between a student and any teacher.

What a tutor must not do is author. A tutor does not supply the research question, does not generate or adjust data, does not rewrite the student's prose into their own, and does not produce any part of the report. One competitor in this search sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring; it is the thing that gets a diploma withheld, and no page on this site will offer it.

The practical test we apply is simple and you can apply it too. If the tutor's contribution can be described to the school's IB coordinator without anyone being embarrassed, it was teaching. We keep a written record of what was advised in each investigation session for exactly that reason. Ask any tutor you are considering what their record-keeping looks like; the answer tells you where they think the line is.
bullets: Legitimate: teaching research design, uncertainty treatment, criterion structure, graphing conventions
Legitimate: feedback on the student's own draft, naming which criterion is weak and why
Not legitimate: supplying the research question or the data set
Not legitimate: rewriting, editing to completion, or producing any section of the report
Ask for the session record - a tutor who keeps one has already thought about this line

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects sitting alongside Physics
paragraphs: A Physics-focused page has to mention something that no competitor page in this search does: your child's Diploma is not the whole timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's own guidance states its requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those lessons take hours out of the same week Physics needs.

The organisational rules are specific, and they explain timetable decisions parents often find puzzling. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language.

KHDA also sets the instructional time, calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met and with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. It further requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. That is a credential question you are entitled to ask your school directly.

Why this belongs on a Physics page: when a DP1 student is drowning, the first instinct is to add Physics hours. Often the actual problem is that Arabic and Social Studies homework is eating the two evenings Physics needed, and the fix is sequencing rather than more tuition. We would rather say that than sell you a second weekly slot. One more constraint worth knowing: for the mandatory UAE subjects, use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so these are not subjects where a tutor can substitute their own material.

sections.heading: KHDA, your school's inspection report, and what it tells a Physics parent
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. For a family in Al Barsha South, KHDA is the only one that matters, and its inspection reports are public.

An inspection report is more useful to a Physics parent than a school's own marketing, because it reports on teaching and assessment at each phase rather than on the school overall. A school can carry a strong headline band while the secondary science provision is the weakest thing in the report. Read the phase-level judgements and the section on students' attainment and progress in science specifically, then read what the inspectors said should improve.

The scale and context are worth knowing too. Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, and the enrolment split by curriculum ran UK 37%, Indian 26%, US 14% and International Baccalaureate 7%. That last figure explains something families in Al Barsha South notice: IB Diploma provision is a minority of a very large market, which is why Physics HL groups can be small and why specialist availability inside one district is unreliable.

Two further pieces of context for anyone budgeting. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. And the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More IB places in the pipeline is good news for this area.

sections.heading: If no Physics specialist is free: the honest version of availability
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this search implies unlimited instant availability. None of them discloses what happens when a specific subject at a specific level is not covered, which is the moment a parent most needs to be told the truth. Physics HL is one of the narrower requests in the UAE market, and a week in which no suitable specialist has a 5pm slot is a normal week, not a failure.

What we do in that case is say so and offer the alternatives. Sometimes the answer is a different slot, including a weekend morning, which for Physics is often better than a tired weekday evening anyway. Sometimes it is a tutor whose primary subject is Maths AA HL with strong Physics coverage, which is a genuine fit for theme A and mechanics work and an honest mismatch for theme E. Sometimes it is a wait of a week or two, with the school's own department clinics in the meantime.

What we will not do is put a general science tutor in front of a Physics HL student and let you find out in a month. The cost of that is not the wasted fees; it is the month. In DP2 a month is a measurable fraction of what is left before the May session, and recovering it means doubling session frequency at exactly the point a student has least capacity. Disclosing a gap up front is cheaper for everyone.

This is also why the free trial exists in the shape it does. One lesson, no card details, and the tutor tells you afterwards what they found and whether they are the right person. A tutor saying they are not the right fit for a particular student is useful information, and a platform that never produces that answer is not screening anybody.

The mark breakdown is the one that matters. A 4 built on a strong Paper 2 and a collapsed Paper 1 needs different work from a 4 built the other way round.

Vague feedback about confidence is not a diagnosis. If the tutor cannot name the problem in syllabus language, that is a signal about the tutor.

For DP2 that means counting backwards from the May session and deciding how many timed Paper 1 sets have to be marked before it.

process.description: Each lesson ends with notes naming what was fixed and what is next, so you are not relying on your child's summary. Every six to eight weeks there is a deliberate review: is this working, should the frequency change, is the same tutor still the right fit. Changing tutor at that point is a normal outcome, not a complaint.

For Physics HL that usually means asking directly about theme D and the HL extension material, because those are the places a generalist runs out of depth and an online match is what makes the question answerable.

faqs.question: Is it harder to find an IB Physics tutor in Al Barsha South than in Dubai Marina?
faqs.answer: For in-home tutoring, slightly, and for one reason: Al Barsha South sits behind a motorway interchange that is slow inbound at 5pm, so fewer tutors will make the trip and those who do price it in. The pool is thin for Physics HL in both districts, because theme-level specialists are scarce across Dubai rather than concentrated anywhere. Online, the difference disappears entirely, since the match is made on syllabus experience rather than driving range. If you are comparing the two districts for a school move, compare the schools' Physics HL provision instead.

faqs.question: My child is at a British-curriculum school in Al Barsha South and moving into IB Physics. What breaks first?
faqs.answer: Three things, predictably. Algebraic rearrangement under time pressure, because IGCSE Physics rewards recall more heavily than DP does. Uncertainties, which IGCSE touches and DP treats as a habit running through every piece of practical work. And the gap between describe and explain, because DP command terms are enforced in the mark scheme in a way IGCSE ones often are not. A bridge block over the summer that drills rearrangement, graph interpretation and the four investigation criteria before the first real one is set removes most of that first-term shock.

faqs.question: How much of the IB Physics grade is the scientific investigation, and can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: The investigation is 20% of the grade at both SL and HL, reported in up to 3,000 words and marked on four criteria of six marks each. A tutor can teach research design, uncertainty propagation and how the criteria are awarded, and can give feedback on your child's own draft naming which criterion is weak. A tutor cannot supply the research question, generate the data, or produce any part of the report. That boundary is set by the IB's academic-honesty rules and breaching it puts the student's diploma at risk, not the tutor's business.

faqs.question: What do Physics tutors charge per hour in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai market spreads widely. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52 at the budget end. Unitors lists IB tutoring from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes about AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 table puts specialist support at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED sits at AED 650. In-home visits are quoted AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the rate. Those are other companies' published figures, not ours; check them at source.

faqs.question: Why is Physics HL theme D such a common problem for Dubai students?
faqs.answer: Because gravitational fields and electric fields are usually taught weeks apart, learned as two separate formula sets, and never explicitly connected. The syllabus treats fields as one idea with different sources; students treat them as two chapters. Any exam question that transfers reasoning from one to the other then finds the gap instantly, and because theme D sits late in most schemes of work it gets taught under time pressure in DP2. The fix is one or two sessions building the shared structure deliberately, before past-paper work rather than after it.

faqs.question: Can my child start Physics tutoring eight weeks before the May session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the shape of it should be different from year-round support. Eight weeks is not enough to re-teach five themes, so the work becomes triage: find the two themes carrying the most recoverable marks, fix command-term technique across Paper 2, and run timed Paper 1 sets with the data-analysis section practised separately from the multiple choice. Expect two sessions a week rather than one. What we will not do is tell you a grade this produces, because nobody honest can, and anyone offering a figure is selling something else.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to homes in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Our tutoring for UAE families is delivered one-to-one online over live video, and we do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Independent tutors and local agencies in Dubai do offer it, quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate. If your child genuinely needs somebody in the room to stay on task, that is a real need and hiring locally is the right answer. For DP Physics, where theme-level fit matters more, we think online wins on merit.

faqs.question: What time can a weekday session realistically start if we live in Al Barsha South 4?
faqs.answer: Around 4.15pm at the earliest, and often 4.45pm once the bus run from schools in Al Barsha 1 or Al Sufouh is counted. South 4 and 5 sit closer to Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, so inbound traffic at 5pm is the main variable. Many families here settle on a 6pm or 7pm slot instead, and for Physics that is usually better: uncertainty work and extended-response practice are poor use of a tired student. Weekend mornings are the other option and they are the most productive slots we schedule.

faqs.question: Does my child need a permit-holding tutor, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. According to u.ae it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, is the official route. Ask any tutor directly. Operating without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Barsha South would a Physics student typically attend?
faqs.answer: Inside or beside Al Barsha South the schools are mostly British curriculum, including Nord Anglia International School Dubai, GEMS Founders School - Al Barsha South, Safa Community School, Dubai Heights Academy and Kings' School Al Barsha. The IB Diploma provision this area feeds into sits largely in Al Barsha 1 and Al Sufouh, at schools such as Dubai American Academy and GEMS World Academy - Dubai. We name these as market context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with or endorsement from any of them, and curriculum offerings change, so check with the school.

faqs.question: Is online Physics tutoring actually workable for practical and data skills?
faqs.answer: For data skills, yes, and arguably better: the entire Paper 1B skill set is reading an unseen data set, plotting it correctly, and interpreting gradient and intercept, which is screen work. Uncertainty propagation is the same. What online cannot do is replace the student's own hands-on practical sessions at school, and it should not try. The tutor's job around the investigation is design, treatment of uncertainty and criterion-level feedback on the student's own write-up. The measurements stay the student's, taken in their school laboratory under their teacher's supervision.

faqs.question: How many Physics sessions a week do Al Barsha South families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One, almost always, and that is the right number for DP1. A single 60 or 90-minute weekly slot keeps the current theme solid without becoming a parallel course that competes with school homework and the mandatory Arabic and Social Studies lessons. Frequency goes up in two situations: an investigation in progress, where a short block of extra sessions is better than a permanently higher rate, and the final eight to twelve weeks before the May session. We review frequency every six to eight weeks rather than leaving it to drift.

faqs.question: What should I read in my school's KHDA inspection report if I care about Physics?
faqs.answer: Skip the headline band and go to the phase-level judgements for secondary and post-16, then find the attainment and progress judgements for science specifically. A school can hold a strong overall band while secondary science is the weakest area in the report. Read the recommendations section too, because that is where inspectors name what the school was told to fix. KHDA publishes these, and u.ae describes KHDA as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. It is free and more candid than any prospectus.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education lessons really affect how much Physics tutoring we need?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum licensed, with KHDA requiring implementation from the start of the 2025-26 academic year and setting instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. That is real homework in real evenings. When a DP1 student is overloaded, the fix is often sequencing the week rather than adding Physics hours, and we would rather tell you that than sell a second slot.

faqs.question: What happens if the first Physics tutor is not the right match?
faqs.answer: You say so and we change them, and the review point every six to eight weeks exists partly to make that conversation routine rather than awkward. A tutor who reports after a trial that they are not the right person for a particular student is doing their job, not failing it. The mismatch that matters most in Physics is level and theme depth: somebody strong at SL mechanics can be genuinely out of their depth on HL nuclear and quantum content, and finding that out in week two costs you a week rather than a term.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Physics and Maths AA for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and when it works it works well, because the calculus in AA HL is what makes rates of change in Physics theme A feel natural. The combination to be careful about is the reverse: a Maths specialist covering Physics HL will usually be solid through themes A and B and thinner on D and E. We will name that mismatch rather than let it surface in April. If the student needs both subjects at HL, two specialists is normally the better arrangement, scheduled on different evenings.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-barsha-sout.closingHeading: Start with one lesson and a real diagnosis
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-barsha-sout.closingBody: If your child is sitting IB Physics at a school this part of Dubai feeds, the next useful step is small: send the most recent mark breakdown by paper and book a free trial lesson. No card details are taken to arrange it. A Physics specialist teaches a full session online at a time that fits the Al Barsha South school run, then writes you a short note naming what is actually wrong in syllabus terms rather than in generalities about confidence. If the diagnosis is that school science clinics would fix it, we will say so. If it is theme D and command terms, you will know that within a week instead of in April.

intro.heading: The syllabus a physics tutor needs to be teaching
paragraphs: Physics is the Diploma subject where an out-of-date tutor is hardest to spot. The content looks familiar from any era of physics teaching, so a tutor who learned the previous syllabus can talk confidently through mechanics and electricity while missing the structure the current course is built on. IB Physics is organised into five themes, and the assessment splits Paper 1 into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section that is effectively a separate skill.

The second thing a parent needs to know is where the marks are. The Scientific Investigation, the internally assessed report, carries twenty per cent of the final grade on its own, with a word limit of three thousand words. A student can know the physics well and lose a fifth of the grade on a report written in a fortnight. Across a cohort, that single component moves more grades than any topic.

The third is that physics marks are lost mathematically rather than conceptually. Uncertainty propagation, gradient interpretation, unit handling and logarithmic treatment of data account for more lost marks than any individual theme. These are teachable in a handful of sessions and they appear in every paper, which makes them the highest-return work available in the subject and the work most often skipped in favour of revisiting topics that feel difficult.

Al Furjan complicates the supply side. The community is residential, sitting between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Yalayis Road, and Dubai's Diploma physics teachers work near the schools that run the programme. In the Jebel Ali and Dubai South corridor those schools are fewer than in Al Barsha, Al Khail or Jumeirah, so the pool of people who will drive into the villa districts for a 17:00 session is small, and Physics Higher Level narrows it further.

IB Gram removes the drive. Every UAE lesson runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30, and no tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. For a subject where the required specialism is this narrow, that trade favours the wider pool heavily: a Masakin family gets a Higher Level physics specialist rather than whoever is twenty minutes away.

On dates: UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session. We do not publish specific IB exam or results dates anywhere on this site, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date in front of a parent who acts on it is worse than no date. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal deadlines, including the Scientific Investigation submission, and that calendar is the one to ask for in September. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own timetables and those are used elsewhere on this site with sources attached, which is the difference between a date we can stand behind and one we cannot.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-furjan.programmesIntro: Physics arrives in stages, and the handovers are where confidence breaks. These are the stages an Al Furjan family passes through on the way to the Diploma.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Sciences are assessed against criteria A to D on an eight-point scale, with criterion D on reflecting on the impacts of science and criterion C on processing and evaluating being the two that consistently cost marks. Physics content at this stage is thin compared with what the Diploma expects, so the preparation that matters is graph work, uncertainty language and writing a method with controlled variables named.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students in Al Furjan are home between 15:40 and 16:30 depending on the route, so a 17:00 session fits. The useful work at this stage is not more physics content but the processing skills the Diploma assumes: plotting properly, reading gradients from a line rather than from points, and stating uncertainty. Those skills transfer to every science the student later takes.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Five themes covering motion, the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour, fields, and nuclear and quantum physics, with Higher Level going deeper across all of them rather than adding separate topics. Assessment is Paper 1, split into multiple choice and data-based sections, Paper 2 with short and extended response, and the Scientific Investigation at twenty per cent.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students from Al Furjan travel to the Al Barsha or Al Khail corridor for school, so they are home closer to 17:00 and book 18:00 or 19:00 physics sessions. Higher Level Physics is one of the scarcer specialisms in this part of Dubai, which is the main practical reason families here end up with a tutor one level below the one their child sits.

programmes.name: The Scientific Investigation
programmes.description: A single independent investigation reported in up to three thousand words, assessed against four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is worth twenty per cent of the grade at both levels. The research question and the quality of the data collected decide most of the mark, and both are fixed long before the report is written.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Al Furjan families most often ask for help late. A weak research question cannot be rescued by good writing, so the highest-value session is the earliest one. Tutors read the criteria with the student, question the design, teach the uncertainty and graphing treatment the data needs, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. No part of the report is written by the tutor.

programmes.name: From IGCSE Physics into the Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE Physics builds recall and single-step calculation. Diploma Physics expects algebraic rearrangement under pressure, uncertainty propagation, logarithmic data treatment and extended written explanation. The gap is mathematical and procedural rather than conceptual, which means it closes quickly with targeted work and slowly with general revision.
programmes.countryNote: Families in this corridor usually change schools for the Diploma, since full Diploma provision nearby is limited. Arriving with the mathematics already fluent removes one of the three things a student is otherwise juggling in the first term. Four to six summer sessions on rearrangement, graphs and uncertainty is the normal size of this block and the best value in the sequence.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-furjan.subjectsIntro: Physics shares its demands with several other Diploma subjects, and families in this corridor often need more than one covered. These are the components and neighbouring subjects we are asked about most.

subjects.name: Physics HL
subjects.description: The five themes at greater depth, with the additional demand being sustained quantitative reasoning rather than extra topics. Extended response questions in Paper 2 reward explanation built from a named principle, and students who describe what happens without naming the physics that causes it score consistently below their understanding.

subjects.name: Physics SL
subjects.description: The same five themes with reduced depth and the same Scientific Investigation at twenty per cent. The commonest problem at Standard Level is treating it as a lighter subject: the data-based and uncertainty demands are identical in kind, and they are where most Standard Level marks are lost.

subjects.name: Paper 1A: multiple choice
subjects.description: Rewards speed and recognition, and punishes a student who works every question algebraically. The skill is knowing which questions to reason through and which to eliminate, and that is practised by doing timed sets rather than by learning more content.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: data-based questions
subjects.description: Effectively a separate examination of experimental skill: reading instruments, processing data, plotting, interpreting gradients and intercepts, and handling uncertainty. Students revise themes and neglect this section, which is why it is the most reliably recoverable set of marks in the subject.

subjects.name: Paper 2: short and extended response
subjects.description: Carries the larger share of the written marks and rewards structured explanation. Command terms decide the shape of the answer: describe, explain, outline and discuss each require something different, and a well-informed answer to the wrong command earns little.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation
subjects.description: Up to three thousand words, twenty per cent of the grade, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The research question and the data decide the mark. Evaluation is the criterion students treat as a list of apologies rather than a critical assessment of the method's limits.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error analysis
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and uncertainty bars on graphs. It appears in Paper 1B, in Paper 2 and throughout the investigation, which makes it the single highest-return topic in the subject and one many students never systematically learn.

subjects.name: Graph and gradient work
subjects.description: Linearising a relationship, choosing axes that make a gradient meaningful, reading gradients from a line of best fit rather than from plotted points, and interpreting intercepts physically. Taught properly in two sessions and worth marks in every component.

subjects.name: Mathematics for Physics
subjects.description: Rearrangement, indices, logarithms, small-angle approximations and trigonometry. Students who understand physics but are slow algebraically often need mathematics support rather than more physics, and diagnosing which of the two is the actual problem takes one session with a marked paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside Physics and sharing the same investigation structure and uncertainty demands. Families often arrange both, and where one tutor genuinely covers both to the level needed that is efficient; where they do not, two specialists beat one generalist.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised independent research. Physics essays fail on feasibility more than on ambition: a question requiring equipment the student cannot access produces a literature review rather than an investigation. That is diagnosable in one early session.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the natural sciences
subjects.description: Students taking Higher Level Physics are often asked to write about scientific knowledge, and generic claims about the scientific method score poorly. A physics tutor's useful contribution is supplying real examples from the course that can carry a knowledge argument.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what Higher Level actually adds
paragraphs: The current IB Physics syllabus is organised into five themes rather than a numbered topic list, and the organisation matters because it changes how the course is taught and revised. The themes cover space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. A tutor who talks about topic numbers from an older guide is working from a structure the school no longer uses, which makes their revision planning unreliable.

Higher Level does not bolt on a separate list of extra topics. It goes deeper within the same five themes, and the additional demand is sustained quantitative reasoning: longer chains of algebra, more unfamiliar contexts, and extended written explanations that have to be built from a named principle rather than described. That is why a Standard Level specialist stretched to Higher Level often teaches the content adequately and the assessment poorly.

The practical consequence for revision is that cross-theme skills matter more than theme coverage. Energy appears in every theme. Field concepts recur. Graphical relationships and proportionality run throughout. A revision plan built theme by theme in isolation produces a student who can answer a question about waves and cannot answer a question that uses wave behaviour inside a different context, which is what the papers actually do.

A useful test of a physics tutor is to ask them to name the themes and then ask what Higher Level adds. Someone teaching the current course answers immediately and talks about depth rather than extra content. Someone working from memory of a previous syllabus will describe additional higher-level topics, which is the wrong shape for this course.

sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2 are three different examinations
paragraphs: Physics revision usually treats the written papers as one thing with a shared body of knowledge. The assessment does not work that way. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, and those two sections test entirely different competencies. Paper 2 then tests structured written explanation. A student can be strong in one and weak in another, and a plan that does not separate them cannot address that.

The multiple-choice section rewards speed and recognition. A student who works every question through algebraically runs out of time, and the fix is practice in timed sets with explicit attention to elimination and estimation. It is also the section where a reliably strong student can lose marks to carelessness rather than ignorance, which is a different intervention from learning more physics.

The data-based section is, in effect, a written practical examination. It asks for instrument reading, data processing, plotting, gradient and intercept interpretation, and uncertainty handling. Students revise the five themes and leave this section to chance, which is why it is the most recoverable set of marks in the subject. Four sessions of pure data work typically moves more marks than four sessions on any theme.

Paper 2 is where command terms decide the outcome. Describe, explain, outline, discuss and compare each require a different answer shape, and a knowledgeable answer to the wrong command earns little. The practical remedy is writing answers and having them marked against the command used, which is slower work than going through content and the reason many tutors avoid it.

sections.heading: Uncertainties and graphs: the marks almost nobody drills
paragraphs: If a family in Al Furjan could buy only four physics sessions, uncertainties and graph work would be the right purchase. The reasoning is straightforward: these skills are examined in the data-based section, reappear in Paper 2, and carry a substantial share of the Scientific Investigation's analysis and evaluation marks. No individual theme has that reach, and no individual theme is as quickly fixable.

The specific competencies are narrow. Distinguishing absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty. Propagating uncertainty through addition, multiplication and powers. Deciding how many significant figures a result can honestly carry. Drawing uncertainty bars and using them to judge whether a relationship is supported. Each of those is a rule with a worked example behind it, not a concept requiring insight.

Graph work is similar. Choosing axes that linearise a relationship so a gradient means something. Reading a gradient from a line of best fit rather than from two plotted points, which is the single most common graph error across every science. Interpreting an intercept physically rather than as a number. Recognising when a log plot is the honest way to display data. All teachable, all examined, all frequently skipped.

Why it gets skipped is worth saying. These skills do not feel like physics to a student, and they do not produce the satisfying sensation of understanding a hard topic. A tutor who works from a marked paper rather than from the student's sense of difficulty will prioritise them, which is one of the clearest differences between a specialist and a generalist in this subject.

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation is a single report of up to three thousand words, worth twenty per cent of the Physics grade at both levels, assessed against four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Its share of the grade is larger than most families realise and its outcome is decided earlier than most students realise, because the research question and the quality of the data collected constrain everything that follows.

Research design is where marks are won or lost before any writing. The question needs a measurable dependent variable, a controllable independent variable, a realistic range of values, and enough repeats to say something. Questions that fail are usually too broad, or depend on equipment the student cannot access, or produce data with so much scatter that no relationship can be claimed. One early session on the design prevents all three.

Data analysis is where the uncertainty and graph work from the previous section pays for itself directly. Processing raw data correctly, propagating uncertainty, plotting with uncertainty bars, and extracting a gradient that answers the research question is the whole of this criterion. Conclusion then asks for an answer to the question, justified by the data and compared with accepted physics, which is a different task from restating the results.

Evaluation is the criterion students treat as a confession. A list of apologies about imprecise equipment scores poorly. What the criterion asks for is a critical assessment of the method's limitations, with specific improvements that would address specific weaknesses, and an honest statement of what the data can and cannot support. That shift in framing is worth several marks and takes one session to explain.

sections.heading: How much of a physics problem is actually a maths problem
paragraphs: A regular diagnosis in this subject is that the student understands the physics and cannot execute the mathematics fast enough. Rearranging a relationship with the unknown in the denominator, handling indices and standard form under time pressure, using logarithms to linearise, applying small-angle approximations, and manipulating trigonometric expressions are all routine demands in Diploma Physics, and all of them are mathematics rather than physics.

Distinguishing the two takes one session with a marked paper. If the student can explain what is happening physically and then stalls on the algebra, the intervention is mathematical. If the algebra is fluent and the explanation is vague, the intervention is conceptual. Treating a mathematical problem with more physics teaching is a common and expensive error, because the student keeps being taught things they already understand.

This is where the IB mathematics course choice interacts with physics. Students taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches meet the algebraic and calculus demands in their maths lessons and arrive at physics with the fluency assumed. Students taking Applications and Interpretation may be excellent mathematicians in a different register and need the manipulation practised separately. Neither is wrong; they are different support needs.

The practical answer for an Al Furjan family is to ask which problem they are buying help for. Where one tutor genuinely covers both physics and the required mathematics to the level needed, that is efficient and we will say so. Where they do not, two specialists outperform one generalist, and pretending otherwise to keep a single booking would be dishonest.

sections.heading: Is there a Higher Level physics specialist near Al Furjan?
paragraphs: The honest answer is that there may be and you should not plan around it. Al Furjan is residential, and Dubai's Diploma physics teachers work near the schools that run the programme, which in the Jebel Ali and Dubai South corridor are fewer than further north. Add the requirement of Higher Level specifically, in a fixed evening slot, within a reasonable drive, and the pool reduces to a handful of people who are generally already committed.

What happens next is predictable. A family takes the nearest competent science tutor and hopes the level difference does not matter. At Standard Level it sometimes does not. At Higher Level it shows within two sessions, usually on extended response marking or on uncertainty propagation, because teaching those well requires having taught them before to this assessment rather than knowing the physics.

Online matching replaces the map with a calendar, and that is the entire argument on a page like this one. IB Gram matches by subject and level and delivers one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address, since home visiting is an India-only service. For a specialism this narrow, the wider pool wins by a distance.

Where we cannot cover a request we say so. Physics at both levels is reasonably well covered across the UAE set and usually matched within a few days, though availability tightens in January and February when every Diploma 2 family in Dubai is looking for the same evening slots. The free trial is the test: bring a marked Paper 2 and ask what pattern connects the lost marks.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a subject with an internally assessed report
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the Physics grade sits in a document the student produces at home, which makes the boundary on help more than a formality. At least one provider in this market advertises completed internal assessments at a fixed price. If a student submits a report they did not produce, the IB treats it as malpractice and the Diploma is what is at risk, not the seller's revenue. That asymmetry is the reason to be explicit.

The legitimate territory is wide and worth using. A tutor may read the four criteria with the student and explain what each rewards, question the research question and the method design until they are workable, teach the uncertainty and graphical techniques the data requires, show how a published paper structures an analysis, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts against each criterion. Most of the recoverable marks are inside that list.

What a tutor may not do is write or rewrite the report, process the student's data for them, supply the analysis, or outline the document for the student to fill in. IB Gram tutors state that boundary at the first session of any investigation block and give feedback in writing, so a school asking what support was received gets an answer that stands up. Parents should expect that from any tutor in this subject.

Two related limits. We do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; they are cited and linked, and sessions work from what the school has issued. And we do not describe tutors as IB examiners without evidence of current status, nor use examiner status to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because it gives no such access.
