faqs.question: How is IB Physics organised now, and why does it matter for choosing a tutor?
faqs.answer: The current syllabus runs on five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level goes deeper within those themes rather than adding a separate topic list. It matters because a tutor working from an older guide plans revision against a structure the school no longer uses. Ask a tutor to name the themes and say what Higher Level adds. Someone teaching the current course answers immediately and talks about depth rather than extra content.

faqs.question: What is Paper 1B and why do students lose marks on it?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, and the data-based section is effectively a written practical examination. It asks for instrument reading, data processing, plotting, gradient and intercept interpretation, and uncertainty handling. Students lose marks there because they revise the five themes and leave experimental skill to chance. That makes it the most recoverable set of marks in the subject: four sessions of pure data work usually moves more marks than four sessions on any single theme.

faqs.question: How much is the IB Physics Scientific Investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level, reported in up to three thousand words and assessed against four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Its outcome is largely settled before the writing starts, because the research question and the quality of the data constrain every criterion that follows. A question that is too broad, or that needs equipment the student cannot access, cannot be rescued by good prose in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: What does the Evaluation criterion actually want?
faqs.answer: A critical assessment of the method's limitations, with specific improvements addressing specific weaknesses, and an honest statement of what the data can and cannot support. What students write instead is a list of apologies about imprecise equipment, which scores poorly because it identifies problems without analysing their effect or proposing a real fix. Reframing it from confession to critique is worth several marks and takes about one session to explain properly, which is why it belongs early in an investigation block.

faqs.question: If we could only buy four physics sessions, what should they cover?
faqs.answer: Uncertainties and graph work. Those skills are examined in the data-based section, reappear in Paper 2, and carry a substantial share of the investigation's analysis and evaluation marks, so their reach is wider than any single theme. The specific competencies are narrow and rule-based: absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, significant figures justified by the uncertainty, uncertainty bars, and reading a gradient from the line of best fit rather than from two plotted points.

faqs.question: Is my child's problem physics or maths?
faqs.answer: One session with a marked paper will tell you. If they can explain what is happening physically and then stall on rearranging the relationship, the problem is mathematical: indices, standard form, logarithms, trigonometry and algebra under time pressure are routine demands in this course. If the algebra is fluent and the explanations are vague, the problem is conceptual. Treating a mathematical difficulty with more physics teaching is common and expensive, because the student keeps being retaught things they already understand.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose Paper 2 marks when the physics is right?
faqs.answer: Because command terms set the shape of the answer and a knowledgeable answer to the wrong command earns little. Describe, explain, outline, discuss and compare each require something different, and the commonest loss is describing what happens without naming the principle that causes it. The remedy is writing answers and having them marked against the command term used, then rewriting once. It is slower work than going through content, which is why many tutors avoid it and why it moves grades.

faqs.question: How hard is Physics Higher Level compared with Standard Level?
faqs.answer: The difference is sustained quantitative reasoning rather than extra topics, since Higher Level deepens the same five themes. Longer chains of algebra, more unfamiliar contexts, and extended explanations built from a named principle are the added demands. A Standard Level specialist stretched to Higher Level often teaches the content adequately and the assessment poorly, and the gap shows within two sessions, usually on extended response marking or on uncertainty propagation rather than on any particular theme.

faqs.question: What should an Al Furjan student do in the summer before Diploma Physics?
faqs.answer: Close the mathematical and procedural gap, not the content gap. IGCSE Physics builds recall and single-step calculation; the Diploma expects rearrangement under pressure, uncertainty propagation, linearising a relationship and extended written explanation. Four to six sessions on those removes one of the three things a student is otherwise juggling in the first term. That matters here because families in this corridor usually change schools for the Diploma, so a new school and a new teaching style arrive at the same time.

faqs.question: Who decides the research question if a tutor is involved in the investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can question the design, which is different from producing it. The legitimate work is reading the four criteria with the student, interrogating the research question until it is measurable and feasible, teaching the uncertainty and graphical techniques the data will need, showing how published work structures an analysis, and giving written feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write the report, process the data, supply the analysis or outline it for the student to complete. That boundary is stated at the first session.

faqs.question: Which physics topics cause the most trouble in Dubai cohorts?
faqs.answer: Fields and wave behaviour, for different reasons. In fields, potential and field strength get used interchangeably, which is a definitional problem rather than a conceptual one and responds to careful definitional work before any problems. In waves, phase difference and path difference are confused, and diagram-first explanations fix it faster than more formulae. Nuclear and quantum physics is usually recalled confidently and handled weakly quantitatively, so it needs calculation practice with exponentials rather than more reading.

faqs.question: When can a physics session start for a Diploma student living in Al Furjan?
faqs.answer: Usually 18:00, and 19:00 on a day with a sports fixture or a CAS commitment. Diploma students from this community mostly travel to the Al Barsha or Al Khail corridor for school, so they are not home before 16:30 and often later. Children at Dubai Investments Park or Green Community schools are home by 15:40 and can start at 15:50, which suits Middle Years science work. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time, and a missed session moves to the next evening rather than the next week.

faqs.question: Are the IB physics exam dates listed anywhere on this site?
faqs.answer: No, and that is deliberate. UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session and we write about that session, but we do not publish specific IB exam or results dates because the IB's own site blocks automated checking, and an unverified date in front of a parent who acts on it is worse than no date at all. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal calendar, including the Scientific Investigation deadline, and that is the document to ask for in September.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor cover physics and chemistry for a Higher Level student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. The two subjects share an investigation structure and the same uncertainty and graphing demands, so a tutor strong in experimental skill transfers usefully between them. What does not transfer is subject-specific assessment experience: marking a chemistry energetics answer and marking a physics fields answer are different skills. Where one tutor genuinely covers both to the level needed we will say so, and where they do not, two specialists beat one generalist.

faqs.question: My child says physics revision is not working. What is usually wrong?
faqs.answer: The plan is almost always built theme by theme, which produces a student who can answer a question about waves and cannot answer a question that uses wave behaviour inside another context. The papers do the latter. A better plan works across themes on the recurring ideas, energy, proportionality and graphical relationships, and treats Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2 as three separate preparations. A tutor working from the marked mock rather than from a syllabus checklist will usually spot this in the first session.

faqs.question: Can you promise my child a 7 in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: No. We do not predict or guarantee grades in any subject, and a provider who does is selling confidence rather than teaching. What can be stated is where the marks sit and how they are typically lost: command-term errors on Paper 2, unpractised data skills on Paper 1B, uncertainty treatment missing throughout, and an investigation worth twenty per cent decided by a research question fixed too late. Working through that list on the evidence of marked work is what actually moves a physics grade.

intro.heading: The real question is not proximity, it is whether anyone nearby can teach HL physics
paragraphs: Al Garhoud is a small neighbourhood. A few hundred metres of low-rise villas and apartment blocks between Garhoud Bridge, Al Rebat Street and the airport fence. Search for an IB physics tutor in Al Garhoud and the results will mostly be agencies in other parts of the city that list the area name because listing area names is cheap. The question a parent is actually asking gets lost in that: not who is nearby, but who can sit down with a Diploma physics student and know what the mark scheme wants.

Those are different questions because Diploma physics at Higher Level is a narrow specialism. A general science tutor can teach IGCSE physics competently. Diploma Higher Level asks for something else: fluency across the whole guide, comfort with the data booklet, the ability to look at a six-mark extended-response answer and say precisely which marking point is missing, and enough experience of the Scientific Investigation to coach a student through designing their own without ever touching the writing. Physics also carries more mathematical load than any other Diploma science, so a tutor who cannot handle calculus-adjacent manipulation will stall on the mechanics and the fields topics.

Count the pool honestly. Dubai's private sector reported 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with the IB accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment. Diploma physics is taken by a minority of that minority, Higher Level by a fraction again, and the teachers qualified to teach it are overwhelmingly employed full time by the schools running the programme. Restrict the search to people willing to drive to Al Garhoud at 17:00 and the pool shrinks to something close to chance. Several of the most visible agency pages in this search quote a US dollar rate, publish no area detail at all, and route UAE parents to a non-UAE phone number. That is what the local supply problem looks like from the outside.

So the structure of this page is a verification exercise rather than a sales pitch. It sets out what a Diploma physics specialist has to be able to do, how to test for it inside a single free trial lesson, what the Dubai market charges across each provider model, and what IB Gram will tell you if no specialist is free for the slot you want. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For a subject this narrow, that is the mechanism that widens the pool rather than a compromise on it. One further point before the detail. The cost of getting this wrong in physics is not measured in dirhams but in terms. A Diploma student who spends DP1 with a tutor who re-teaches content the student already understands arrives in DP2 with the original problem and one year fewer in which to fix it. Diagnosis is the expensive skill and the one worth testing for, which is why the first two sections of this page are a checklist rather than a description of a service.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences into Diploma Physics
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed on criteria rather than on content coverage, which means a student can arrive in DP1 with strong investigative skills and thin mechanics. The gap is usually quantitative: rearranging formulae, handling units and prefixes, and working with graphs where the gradient means something physical. This is the route that creates the specialist scarcity. The tutoring need is diagnostic: a student who understands the physics but writes answers that miss marking points needs mark-scheme work, not re-teaching, and the two are easy to confuse.

Checking the departmental requirement in writing before the subject choice is locked is the cheapest piece of advice on this page.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-garhoud.subjectsIntro: Diploma physics is one subject with a small number of well-known failure points. Tutoring is efficient when it attacks those and wasteful when it marches through the guide from the first page.

subjects.name: Kinematics and dynamics
subjects.description: Suvat equations are rarely the problem. Free-body diagrams drawn wrongly are, and every subsequent line of working inherits the error. Students also lose marks by treating a deceleration as a positive quantity and by failing to state the direction they have taken as positive.

subjects.name: Work, energy and momentum
subjects.description: Conservation arguments are worth easy marks and are often skipped in favour of a longer force-based method. The common error is applying conservation of mechanical energy to a collision that is not elastic, which the question usually signals clearly.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and gas laws
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity and latent heat calculations are mechanical once set out, but students mix units of mass and forget that the temperature change in kelvin equals the change in degrees Celsius. Ideal gas questions punish careless pressure units.

subjects.name: Waves, superposition and resonance
subjects.description: Path difference and phase difference are routinely conflated. Standing wave questions need a diagram, and single-slit and double-slit distinctions are tested more precisely than most students expect from classwork alone.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The most common loss point across the whole course. Potential dividers, internal resistance and non-ohmic components appear in questions requiring the student to reason about a circuit rather than recall a formula. Half the marks go to explanation, not calculation.

subjects.name: Fields: gravitational and electric
subjects.description: Sign conventions for potential and potential energy cause more errors than the physics does. HL extends into field and potential gradients and the mathematical treatment, which is where the mathematical load becomes the limiting factor for many students.

subjects.name: Magnetism and electromagnetic induction
subjects.description: Determining the direction of an induced current requires two rules applied in sequence and students apply one. HL questions on induction and alternating current demand confident algebra as much as confident physics.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Binding energy per nucleon questions are reliable marks if the mass defect is handled carefully with the data booklet. The qualitative quantum content is where exam answers become vague, and vague answers earn nothing in a mark scheme written around specific statements.

subjects.name: Using the data booklet
subjects.description: A skill, not a reference habit. Students waste minutes hunting for an equation they half-remember, or use a formula whose symbols mean something different from what they assumed. Twenty minutes of deliberate data booklet practice pays for itself in a paper.

subjects.name: Extended-response technique
subjects.description: The longer questions are marked against specific points. Writing more does not help; writing the named physical reason does. This is the single most teachable thing on the list and the one most often left untouched by general science tutors.

subjects.name: Uncertainties, error bars and graph analysis
subjects.description: Percentage uncertainty propagation, drawing a line of best fit through error bars, and deciding what a gradient physically represents. These skills carry marks on the papers and underpin the Scientific Investigation, so work here counts twice.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation, as process coaching
subjects.description: Assessed internally on four criteria totalling 24 marks. A tutor may teach the criteria, question a research design, explain what good analysis looks like and comment on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the investigation or write any part of it.

sections.heading: What a Diploma physics specialist has to be able to do
paragraphs: Before you can judge whether a tutor knows the syllabus, you need a list of what knowing it means. The list is shorter than it sounds and almost none of it is about qualifications on paper. It is about four capabilities, each of which can be tested in a conversation.

The first is mark-scheme literacy. Given a six-mark extended-response question and a student's answer, a specialist will tell you which specific marking points are present and which are missing, in under a minute. A general science tutor will tell you the answer is good or needs more detail. The difference is the whole value of the hour, because almost all preventable loss in Diploma physics happens between understanding the physics and writing something a mark scheme recognises.

The second is data booklet fluency. The booklet is provided in the examination and students who have not practised with it lose minutes they cannot afford and misuse symbols whose meaning differs from their classroom notation. A specialist will open it without hesitation and know which formulations sit where. The third is mathematical confidence at the level the Higher Level fields and induction content demands; physics is the most mathematical of the Diploma sciences and a tutor who stalls on algebraic rearrangement will stall on the course.

The fourth is experimental and uncertainty literacy, which carries marks in the papers and underpins the Scientific Investigation. Propagating a percentage uncertainty, deciding whether a gradient has physical meaning, and judging whether a research design controls what it claims to control are not optional extras. A tutor who treats the investigation as a writing exercise rather than a design exercise is the wrong tutor, and also the kind most likely to drift across the academic-honesty line.

sections.heading: How to verify a physics tutor in one free trial lesson
paragraphs: A free trial is only worth anything if you use it as an assessment rather than an introduction. Forty minutes is enough, and you do not need to understand physics to run it. What you are watching for is specificity: a specialist talks about named topics, named question types and named marking points, and a generalist talks about confidence, foundations and building up slowly.

Start by handing over the problem rather than describing it. Send the tutor a photograph of a recent marked physics test or past-paper attempt before the lesson, and ask them to come with a view. By the end of the lesson they should be able to say something like: the physics on the mechanics question was right but the free-body diagram omitted the normal reaction, the circuit question lost two marks because the explanation did not mention internal resistance, and the uncertainty in part c was propagated as an absolute rather than a percentage. Three statements of that kind mean the diagnosis is real.

Then ask the three questions parents most often skip. Which parts of the guide do you teach most weeks? How do you handle the Scientific Investigation, and what will you not do? What would you do differently if my child were targeting a 7 rather than a 5? The third question separates tutors who have a method from tutors who have a manner. A specialist will answer it in terms of extended-response technique and past-paper volume, not in terms of motivation.

Finally, watch your child rather than the tutor for the last ten minutes. A Diploma physics student who is being taught well starts talking. If your child is nodding and the tutor is explaining, the lesson is a lecture, and a lecture is available free on the internet. The behaviour you are paying for is the tutor asking a question your child cannot immediately answer and then waiting.

sections.heading: Availability for Higher Level physics, and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this search implies unlimited availability, because stating a limit looks like weakness. It is more useful to state it. Higher Level Diploma physics is the tightest coverage in the whole subject list, for the obvious reason that the people who can teach it well are mostly teaching it full time somewhere. Standard Level physics, IGCSE physics and MYP sciences are comfortably covered. Specific combinations, such as HL physics plus HL Mathematics Analysis and Approaches with the same tutor, are harder again.

What that means in practice for an Al Garhoud family is that the slot and the specialist sometimes compete. A 17:00 Tuesday slot with a general science tutor is available immediately. A 17:00 Tuesday slot with an HL physics specialist might be two weeks away, or might require moving to 18:30, or to Thursday. The right answer depends on how close the examination session is and whether the problem is content or technique, and it is a conversation worth having explicitly rather than discovering by drift.

The fallback matters too. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for a niche requirement, the tutor may be based elsewhere and teaching into Gulf Standard Time. That is disclosed rather than hidden, which is more than can be said for parts of this market: two of the most visible agency pages serving UAE parents route enquiries to a non-UAE telephone number without saying where the teaching happens, and one shows a Dubai footer address on a page written for Abu Dhabi.

sections.heading: Where the extra Higher Level content actually sits
paragraphs: Parents often assume Higher Level physics is a different course from Standard Level. It is not. It is the same course with extensions, and knowing where those extensions sit tells you where tutoring hours have to go. The common content is taught to both levels; the Higher Level additions concentrate in the more mathematical areas, chiefly fields and potential, electromagnetic induction and alternating current, rotational motion, and the quantum and nuclear material.

That distribution has a practical consequence. A Higher Level student struggling with the common core has a content problem that affects everything, and the fix is sequential: secure the core first, because the extensions build on it. A Higher Level student who is comfortable in the core and losing marks only in the extension areas has a mathematical problem dressed up as a physics problem, and the fix is algebraic fluency plus practice on the specific question styles those topics use.

Distinguishing between those two situations is the first job of a trial lesson, and it changes the whole plan. It also changes the hours. A student in the first situation needs weekly work across DP1 and DP2. A student in the second can often be fixed in a block of eight to ten sessions concentrated on three topics, which is a materially different bill.

Confirm the current structure of the course and its assessment on ibo.org or with your child's IB coordinator before planning around any of it. The Diploma physics guide has been revised, assessment components have changed with it, and ibo.org is the only authority worth citing on what the current papers are. No IB examination or results date appears on this page for the same reason: those dates belong to the IB and to your school's coordinator, not to a tutoring site.

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: Diploma physics includes an internally assessed Scientific Investigation, assessed against four criteria totalling 24 marks. It is the part of the course where families are most often offered help they should refuse, and the part where the distinction between teaching and producing is sharpest.

What a tutor may legitimately do: explain each criterion and its mark allocation, so the student knows what is being judged; question a research question until the student can defend it; ask whether the variable control does what the student claims; explain what good uncertainty treatment and good evaluation look like, using a different investigation as the example; and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. All of that is teaching, and all of it moves marks.

What a tutor may not do: design the investigation, supply the research question, write any section, or redraft the student's text to completion. The work submitted must be the student's own. A breach is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student's award rather than on the tutor. This search results set includes an operator selling completed Internal Assessments outright at a fixed price, which is exactly the offer to walk away from however convenient it looks in a difficult term.

The timing is worth planning as deliberately as the content. Investigation deadlines are set internally by the school, usually months before the examination session, and they collide with mock examinations in most Diploma timetables. Three to five coaching sessions placed around the school's own deadline are worth more than the same sessions placed wherever the calendar happened to be free, and they take pressure off the mock period rather than adding to it.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the rest of your child's week
paragraphs: Physics does not exist in isolation on a Dubai timetable, and the other demands on the week are part of why a physics plan fails. Private schools in Dubai are regulated by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Inspection reports are published on the regulator's own site and are the right place to read about a school rather than a tutoring page's summary of it.

KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirement to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

The practical effect for a Diploma physics student in Al Garhoud is that the timetable carries mandatory subjects on top of six Diploma courses, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and creativity, activity and service. Physics is competing for attention with all of it. A tutoring plan that assumes the student has unlimited evening hours is a plan that collapses in week four, which is why the weekly slot on this page is one lesson rather than three outside the examination run-in.

Dubai's sector is also still expanding: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. More Diploma places means more Diploma physics students competing for the same thin pool of specialists, which is the structural reason the availability conversation earlier on this page is not going to get easier.

sections.heading: Permits, credentials and the claims to be sceptical about
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists the route as private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so disregard any page quoting an amount.

Beyond the permit, two claims in this market deserve scepticism. The first is regulator approval. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises; it is a specific thing with a specific process, and a tutor or platform without it is not approved by anybody. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises, and claims no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any page describing its tutors as approved by one of those bodies is describing something that does not exist.

The second is examiner status. Describing a tutor as an IB examiner is only meaningful if the status is current and evidenced, and it should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because it confers none of those. A physics tutor's usefulness is demonstrated in the trial lesson by reading a mark scheme accurately, which is a test anyone can run, rather than by a title on a profile that nobody can check.

Review claims are the third thing to discount. Competitor pages in this set publish self-asserted star ratings, including two different ratings on the same page, and one shows a rating from twenty reviews next to a claim about a far larger student body. Self-serving review markup is against Google's structured data policy and tells you nothing about whether a tutor can teach Higher Level fields. The verification checklist is more work than reading a rating and it is the only method that actually answers the question.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB physics tutor near Al Garhoud who knows the Diploma syllabus?
faqs.answer: Within walking distance, almost certainly not. Al Garhoud is a small, low-rise neighbourhood, and Higher Level Diploma physics is a narrow specialism whose practitioners are mostly teaching it full time in schools. That is why lessons here are delivered one-to-one over live video rather than in person: the search becomes for a Diploma physics specialist rather than for a science graduate within a twenty-minute drive of the airport perimeter. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is an India-only service, and for a subject this narrow that widens the available pool rather than narrowing it.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a physics tutor really understands the Diploma mark schemes?
faqs.answer: Send a marked script before the trial lesson and ask them to come with a view on it. A specialist will tell you which specific marking points are missing from a six-mark extended response, usually in under a minute. A generalist will say the answer needs more detail or better structure. Ask them which booklet entry applies to a named question, and ask what they would do differently if your child were targeting a 7 rather than a 5. The answer should be about extended-response technique and past-paper volume, not about confidence and motivation.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Higher and Standard Level Diploma physics in practice?
faqs.answer: Higher Level is the same course with extensions rather than a separate one. The common content is taught to both levels, and the Higher Level additions cluster in the more mathematical areas: fields and potential, electromagnetic induction and alternating current, rotational motion, and the quantum and nuclear material. That matters for planning. A student weak in the common core needs sequential weekly work, because the extensions build on it. A student comfortable in the core but losing marks only in the extension topics usually has an algebra problem rather than a physics one, and that can be fixed in a focused block.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand physics in class but lose marks in tests?
faqs.answer: Because understanding and answering are different skills, and the Diploma papers mark the second one. Extended-response questions are assessed against specific named points, so an answer that is conceptually right but does not state the required physical reason earns nothing. Add the common mechanical losses, free-body diagrams with a force omitted, uncertainties propagated as absolute rather than percentage, circuit explanations that never mention internal resistance, and most of a grade can sit in execution rather than knowledge. This is the most teachable gap in the subject and the one a general science tutor is least likely to target.

faqs.question: How quickly can you find a Higher Level physics tutor for a slot after school?
faqs.answer: For Standard Level, usually within a week. For Higher Level in a peak 16:30 to 17:30 slot, often one to two weeks, and sometimes the honest answer is that the slot and the specialist compete. A later start at 18:30, or a Thursday when the school week is ending anyway, is normally available sooner. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a niche combination, the tutor may be based elsewhere and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed rather than hidden. Ask about availability before planning a term around a particular hour.

faqs.question: What does the Scientific Investigation count for, and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: It is internally assessed against four criteria totalling 24 marks and it forms part of the final Diploma physics grade. Because it is coursework, the honesty rules bite hardest here. A tutor may explain each criterion and its mark allocation, question a research question until the student can defend it, challenge whether the variable control does what the student claims, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not design the investigation, supply the question, or write any part of it. Confirm the current criteria and weighting with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look over my son's physics investigation before he submits it?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read a draft your son has written and tell him what a criterion is asking for that his draft does not yet deliver. That is feedback, and it is legitimate and useful. What a tutor must not do is rewrite sections, supply analysis, or edit the text to completion, because the submission has to be the student's own work. The distinction is not a formality: academic malpractice under IB rules puts the student's whole award at risk, and the consequence falls on him rather than on the tutor. Operators in this market selling finished assessments are selling that risk.

faqs.question: How much does a Diploma physics specialist cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above: TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table shows AED 200 to 450 or more. Below that, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Budget online tutoring runs from about AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65, which is often adequate for IGCSE physics but rarely for Higher Level. Premium named tutors go higher, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Those are market rates, not IB Gram's price.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying specialist rates when cheaper physics tutoring is available?
faqs.answer: For MYP sciences or an IGCSE physics catch-up, often not. For Higher Level Diploma physics, usually yes, and the reason is arithmetic rather than snobbery. A tutor who cannot read a mark scheme will spend twenty weeks re-teaching content your child already understands, and at the end of it the written answers still miss the marking points. You have then spent the specialist budget in hours instead of in dirhams and arrived at the paper with the original problem. The waste in this subject is almost never the hourly rate; it is hours spent on the wrong activity.

faqs.question: Which physics topics do Dubai Diploma students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Electricity and circuits is the most common across the whole course, because the questions require reasoning about potential dividers, internal resistance and non-ohmic components rather than formula recall, and roughly half the marks go to explanation. After that: fields and potential, where sign conventions cause more errors than the physics does; electromagnetic induction, where the direction of an induced current needs two rules applied in sequence; and uncertainty and graph analysis, which carries marks on the papers and underpins the investigation. The qualitative quantum material is where answers go vague, and vague answers score nothing.

faqs.question: Should my child take Higher Level physics if they want to study engineering?
faqs.answer: Most engineering and physical-science departments that UAE students apply to expect Higher Level physics alongside Mathematics Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation. Check the specific departmental requirement in writing before the Diploma subject choice is locked, because changing route in DP2 is difficult. Tutoring cannot substitute for the prerequisite, and no page should imply that tuition is required for admission, which is a false claim about an admissions process. What tutoring can do is make Higher Level physics survivable alongside the rest of a Diploma timetable.

faqs.question: Do physics tutors working with Al Garhoud families need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists the application as private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the app, website or e-services. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so ignore any figure quoted on a tutoring site.

faqs.question: What should I make of a tutor advertised as an IB physics examiner?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a claim to verify rather than a credential to rely on. Examiner status is only meaningful if it is current and evidenced, and it should never be taken to imply access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or paper content, because it confers none of those. The practical test is better: hand over a marked script and see whether the tutor can name the missing marking points. That tells you what you actually need to know, it takes a minute, and anyone can run it. The same scepticism applies to self-asserted star ratings, which several pages in this search publish.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Dubai school teach Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Because KHDA requires it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with implementation required by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For tutoring planning the point is simply that the week is fuller than six Diploma subjects suggests.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week does a Diploma student in Al Garhoud need?
faqs.answer: One 60 or 90-minute lesson a week through DP1 and DP2 is the usual pattern, rising to two or three a week for six to ten weeks before the examination session. More than that rarely helps, because the limiting factor becomes independent past-paper work rather than teaching time. A student who sits one timed paper a fortnight and reviews it against the mark scheme will improve faster on a single weekly lesson than one taking three lessons and doing nothing between them. The week is also already full of mandatory subjects, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge.

faqs.question: What time can a physics lesson start for a student living in Al Garhoud?
faqs.answer: On most weekdays, 16:30 at the earliest and more often 17:00 or 17:30. Secondary schools in and around Al Garhoud, Festival City and Oud Metha finish between 14:00 and 15:00, activity clubs extend two or three afternoons to about 16:00, and a bus loop through Garhoud, Al Rigga or Al Mamzar adds twenty-five to fifty minutes. Thursday suits a longer 90-minute session because Friday mornings start later at most schools. Saturday morning is the only window where a full timed paper plus a proper review fits without rushing either half.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-habtoor-cit.tutorsIntro: The physics tutors here have taught the Diploma course through to examination and marked to a published scheme. They work from the student's own script rather than from a revision guide, because an IB physics mark is decided by command-term discipline and uncertainty handling long before it is decided by content recall.

intro.heading: Physics at Diploma level is a language problem before it is a content problem
paragraphs: Most students who struggle with IB Physics understand the physics. What they lose marks on is the instruction. An IB physics paper asks a student to state, to outline, to explain, to deduce, to determine, to sketch and to draw, and each of those verbs has an agreed meaning that the mark scheme enforces. A student who explains when the paper said state wastes time; a student who states when the paper said explain loses the mark entirely. That gap between knowing and scoring is where a tutor earns their fee, and it is diagnosable in a single marked question.

The second recurring issue is uncertainty. The current physics guide treats experimental skills as examinable in the written papers, not merely in the laboratory, so absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, error bars, lines of best and worst fit, and the number of significant figures a result is entitled to all appear on the data-based section. Students arriving from IGCSE or MYP science have usually never had to carry an uncertainty through two steps of arithmetic, and the first time they meet it in a Diploma paper it costs them several marks.

The third is the scientific investigation, which carries twenty per cent of the final grade under the current guide and is the single largest block of marks a student controls directly. It is also the part of the course where families most often ask for the wrong kind of help. A tutor can teach a student how a research question is narrowed, how a variable is controlled, how uncertainty is estimated and how a conclusion is tied back to evidence. A tutor cannot write it, draft it, or edit it into something the student did not produce. We say that plainly on every page, because this market contains providers who sell finished work and that is a malpractice risk for your child rather than a service.

Al Habtoor City is a tower community on the Sheikh Zayed Road side of the Dubai Water Canal with no school inside it, so the Diploma students who live here attend schools spread across Al Safa, Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim, Al Barsha and Nad Al Sheba. HL Physics is a smaller cohort than HL Biology or HL Chemistry in most of those schools, which has a practical consequence: the pool of tutors who have actually taught the HL-only material to examination is thinner than the pool who will say they can. Online removes that constraint, because the match is made on who has taught the course rather than on who can reach a tower in the evening.

IB Gram delivers physics support to UAE families online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not run home visits anywhere in the Emirates; that is an India-only service. For physics the screen is an advantage rather than a concession: graphs are annotated live, a simulation can be shared mid-explanation, the student's own marked script sits on screen beside the mark scheme, and the session is recorded so a derivation can be re-watched at the third attempt rather than half-remembered.

programmes.description: The two-year course assessed by written papers plus the scientific investigation. Content runs across themes A to E, and HL carries additional material within each theme rather than a separate topic list. Tutoring divides into three strands: content, command-term technique and experimental reasoning. Most students need all three, in different proportions, and the proportions change between the first and second year of the course.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai schools, HL Physics is often a smaller set than HL Chemistry or HL Biology, which means a student can be the only person in their class stuck on a particular HL derivation. That isolation is the most common reason an Al Habtoor City family looks outside the school for help, and it is the reason the tutor's own teaching history with HL material matters more than their general physics background.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, heading into Diploma Physics
programmes.description: MYP sciences assess against criteria A to D, which rewards investigative process and scientific communication rather than the mathematical fluency the Diploma assumes. Students can score well in MYP and still arrive in Year 12 unable to rearrange a formula with confidence or interpret a gradient. Bridging work in the summer between the two is short, cheap and disproportionately effective.
programmes.countryNote: Al Habtoor City families whose children attend IB-continuum schools in Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim or Al Barsha often ask for this bridge in July or August. Six to eight short sessions on algebraic rearrangement, standard form, graph interpretation and uncertainty basics will remove most of the September shock, and it costs far less than repairing the same gap in the second term of Year 12.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics, as the route into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are the usual pre-Diploma routes for students in British-curriculum schools near Al Safa. Both reward recall and formula use more than reasoning about uncertainty, so a strong IGCSE grade is not a reliable predictor of a comfortable Diploma start. The transferable skills are algebraic fluency, graph work and confidence with standard form.
programmes.countryNote: A student moving from Extended 0625 into Diploma Physics typically meets three new demands at once: uncertainty arithmetic, command-term precision and the expectation that a conclusion is argued from data rather than stated. Naming those three in advance turns a frightening transition into a short list of fixable items.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-habtoor-cit.subjectsIntro: Physics rarely arrives alone from this postcode. These are the subjects most often requested alongside it, and the reason the pairing makes sense rather than the fact that it happens.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E, two written papers and the scientific investigation. The marks that move fastest are command-term discipline, uncertainty handling and the data-based section, not additional content revision.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The natural partner. Differentiation, trigonometric manipulation and logarithmic graph work all appear inside physics questions, and a student weak in one usually looks weak in both for the same underlying reason.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by students who still take Physics, and the pairing needs care: the algebraic fluency physics assumes is not the main emphasis of this route, so the gap has to be closed deliberately rather than hoped away.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the data-processing and uncertainty demands, and the same students sit both investigations in the same term. Coordinating the two internal assessment timelines saves more stress than extra content teaching does.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A frequent third science choice for engineering-bound students. Logic and algorithmic thinking transfer in both directions, and the modelling questions in physics become noticeably easier.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Overlaps with physics on materials, forces and testing. Students often use the same practical instincts in both courses, and the investigation skills are closely related.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Physics supplies some of the most usable material in the course - measurement, models, what counts as evidence. Tutoring here is structural: how an argument is built and how a counterclaim is handled.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A supervised four-thousand-word research piece. A tutor helps the student narrow a question, read critically and plan, and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor does not write any part of it.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: The pre-Diploma course for British-curriculum students near Al Safa. Formula recall and graph work dominate, and the algebra built here is what Diploma physics will later assume.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Criterion-based assessment that rewards investigative process. The gap into Diploma physics is mathematical rather than conceptual, and it is cheapest to close in a holiday block.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-habtoor-cit.modesIntro: Physics support takes three shapes depending on what the marked evidence says is wrong. Each runs online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time.

modes.title: Theme-by-theme teaching
modes.description: For students whose content is genuinely incomplete, usually in fields, nuclear and quantum physics, or the HL extensions within a theme. The work is sequential and builds on a written map of what has and has not been covered, so a parent can see progress as coverage rather than as effort. This is the slowest mode and the only one that fixes a real content gap.

modes.title: Script clinics on command terms and uncertainty
modes.description: The highest-return mode for a student who understands the physics and still loses marks. The student sits past-paper questions, the tutor marks them against the published scheme, and the session is spent only on the gap between what was written and what the scheme wanted. Most students recover several marks a paper within four sessions, because the errors repeat.

modes.title: Investigation coaching, inside the honesty rules
modes.description: Support on the scientific investigation that stays on the correct side of the line: narrowing a research question, choosing and controlling variables, estimating uncertainty, structuring an evaluation, and reading a draft the student wrote to tell them what an examiner would ask next. The student writes every word. We will not draft, complete or edit the work into something they did not produce.

modes.title: Pre-examination paper blocks
modes.description: A fixed run of sessions in the final term, built around whole papers sat under time. No new content is introduced in the last fortnight by design. The purpose is pacing, question selection order and the elimination of repeated errors, which is almost always worth more at that stage than another pass through a theme.

sections.heading: What an IB physics tutor in Al Habtoor City is actually asked to fix
paragraphs: The request that arrives from these towers is rarely teach my child physics. It is more often that a predicted grade has dropped, that the data-based questions are going badly, or that an investigation has stalled with a research question too broad to measure. Each of those is a different job. Treating all three as content revision is the most common way tutoring money gets wasted in this subject, because content revision does nothing for a student who already knows the physics and is losing marks to the mark scheme.

The first diagnostic is always a marked script. Give a tutor a recent paper with the marks on it and the pattern is visible within twenty minutes: whether the losses sit in multiple choice, in the data-based section, in the extended response, or scattered across all three in the form of missing units and wrong significant figures. Those four pictures lead to four different plans, and a tutor who starts teaching before seeing a script is working blind.

The second is the student's own written working. Physics answers fail in specific ways: a free-body diagram drawn without the forces labelled, a vector treated as a magnitude, a gradient quoted without units, a conclusion asserted rather than argued from the data. Watching the student write is how those habits are caught, and it is the reason a physics session has to be interactive rather than a lecture with the camera on.

The third thing being asked, usually unspoken, is for an honest view of whether the target grade is reachable. That answer should come from marked papers at week one and week four, not from encouragement. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone in this market who offers one should be asked to publish the terms. What can be committed to is a named diagnosis, work set and marked every week, and a straight answer when the evidence changes.
bullets: Bring a marked script to the first session; it is worth more than a syllabus list
Multiple-choice losses, data-based losses and extended-response losses need different plans
Units, significant figures and labelled diagrams are marks, not presentation
An honest week-four review based on a second marked paper

sections.heading: The five themes, and where HL students actually feel the difference
paragraphs: The current IB physics guide organises content into five themes rather than the older numbered topic list: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. HL students study the same five themes with additional material inside each, which is a structural point worth understanding. There is no separate HL topic block to leave until last. The HL content is interleaved, so a student who falls behind at SL level in a theme is simultaneously behind on the HL extension of it.

In practice the difficulty is unevenly distributed, and the distribution is predictable. Space, time and motion is where weak algebra shows up first, because it is the theme that demands the most rearrangement and the most careful attention to vector signs. The particulate nature of matter is conceptually comfortable and arithmetically fiddly, with unit conversions doing most of the damage. Wave behaviour is where diagrams carry marks and where students who cannot draw accurately lose them. Fields is the theme most often named as the hardest, because it is abstract and because the HL extension is substantial. Nuclear and quantum physics tends to arrive late in the course, which means it is frequently the least rehearsed theme in the examination.

The table below is the map we build a teaching plan from. It is a guide to where tutoring hours usually go rather than a statement about any individual student, and the balance should always be set by a marked script rather than by a general expectation. Where a school has taught the themes in an unusual order, that order matters more than the guide's sequence, and it is worth asking the physics teacher for the department's scheme of work.

One practical consequence of the interleaved HL structure: revision planning has to be done theme by theme with the HL material explicitly listed, or it gets quietly skipped. The most common HL-only gap we are asked to repair is not a difficult idea but an unpractised one, left undone because it sat at the end of a theme the class had already moved on from.

sections.heading: Paper 1, Paper 2 and the investigation: what each component rewards
paragraphs: The assessment has three parts under the current guide: a first paper containing multiple-choice questions and a data-based section, a second paper of short and extended response questions, and the scientific investigation completed in school and marked internally against published criteria. The investigation carries twenty per cent of the final grade. The precise duration and percentage split of the written papers differs between SL and HL and has changed with recent guide revisions, so confirm your own cohort's figures with the school's IB coordinator rather than trusting any summary, including this one.

Each component rewards a different habit, which is why a single revision strategy underperforms. The multiple-choice section rewards speed and the ability to eliminate; it punishes students who work every question fully. The data-based section rewards uncertainty discipline, graph accuracy and the willingness to quote a gradient with its units. The extended-response paper rewards command-term precision and structured argument, where a six-mark answer needs a plan rather than a paragraph. The investigation rewards a narrow question, controlled variables and an evaluation that engages honestly with the limitations of what the student actually did.

The most useful consequence for a parent is that the weakest component is identifiable from any recent marked paper, and the plan should follow the evidence. A student losing marks mostly in multiple choice needs timed practice and elimination technique, which is cheap and fast. A student losing marks in the data-based section needs uncertainty arithmetic, which takes four to six sessions. A student losing marks in extended response needs command-term work and answer planning, which shows up quickest of all because the errors are so repetitive.

The table sets out what each component is testing and the failure mode we see most often. Read the right-hand column as a diagnostic list: if two of those describe your child, that is the plan for the next month.

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that decides whether an answer scores
paragraphs: IB command terms are defined in the subject guide and applied literally by examiners. A student who treats them as synonyms will write good physics and score badly. This is the single most teachable thing in the subject, and it is also the thing most often left untaught because it looks like exam technique rather than physics. In marked scripts, command-term errors are among the largest recoverable categories, and they recur in the same student across papers until someone names the pattern.

The practical method is narrow and repetitive. Take the student's own answers, put the mark scheme beside them, and identify what the scheme wanted that the answer did not supply. Within three or four sessions a student can usually predict the required answer length from the verb and the mark allocation alone, which is the skill that transfers to every question in every paper. It is unglamorous work and it moves grades faster than another pass through fields.

Two related habits travel with it. The first is matching answer length to marks: a two-mark question wants two scoring points, and a paragraph that contains both plus three others may still score two while costing time elsewhere. The second is reading the stem for the quantity actually requested. A question that asks for a change in energy and receives an energy is wrong, and a question that asks for a magnitude and receives a vector with a sign may be too.

The table lists the terms that cause the most trouble in physics specifically, with what the examiner is looking for. It is deliberately short: four or five terms account for most of the losses, and drilling five terms properly beats skimming twenty.

sections.heading: Uncertainties, significant figures and the data-based section
paragraphs: Uncertainty is the part of IB Physics that students arriving from IGCSE or MYP have genuinely never done. At IGCSE a measurement is a number. In the Diploma it is a number with a range, and that range has to survive being squared, divided and plotted. Absolute and percentage uncertainty, combining uncertainties through a calculation, drawing error bars, fitting a line of best fit and a line of worst fit to extract an uncertainty in a gradient: none of that is conceptually hard, and all of it is unfamiliar enough to cost marks on first contact.

The significant-figure rule is the cheapest mark in the paper and the most frequently dropped. A result is entitled to the precision its least precise input allows, and a student who copies ten digits off a calculator display is announcing that they do not know this. The habit takes about two weeks to establish and then holds for the rest of the course, which makes it one of the few genuinely free improvements available in the subject.

Graph work is the other half of this section, and it is manual. Choosing a scale that uses the grid, plotting accurately, drawing a line rather than joining points, reading a gradient from the line and not from two data points, and quoting that gradient with units. Each of those is a mark somewhere, and each is practised rather than understood. Students who do this work on screen with a tutor watching improve faster than students who do it alone, because the errors are invisible to the person making them.

For a tower household in Al Habtoor City the practical requirement is modest: squared paper, a sharp pencil, a ruler and a calculator that is not a phone. The tutor needs to see the page, so the camera gets angled at the desk rather than the face. That is the whole equipment list, and it works better than any application.
bullets: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, then propagation through a calculation
Error bars, best-fit and worst-fit lines, and the uncertainty in a gradient

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: what a tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: The investigation is the largest single block of marks a student controls, and it is assessed against published criteria. It is also the place where the academic-honesty line is most likely to be crossed, usually by a provider rather than by a student. The line itself is clear. A tutor may teach the student how to narrow a research question, how to identify and control variables, how to estimate and propagate uncertainty, how to structure an analysis, and how an evaluation engages with real limitations. A tutor may read a draft the student wrote and respond with the questions an examiner would ask.

A tutor may not write the investigation, draft any section of it, rewrite the student's text into something better than they produced, supply data, or hand over a previous student's work as a model to be adapted. Providers in this market sell completed internal assessments; one advertises them openly. Buying that is an academic-malpractice trigger for your child, with consequences that sit with the student and not the seller. We will not do it, and the reason we state it on the page is that saying it out loud is one of the few reliable ways to tell providers apart.

What good support actually looks like is narrower and more useful than most families expect. The most common single failure in a physics investigation is a research question that cannot be measured with the equipment available in a school laboratory. Fixing that in week one saves the whole project. The second most common is a data set too thin to support any conclusion, which is a planning failure rather than a writing failure. The third is an evaluation that lists apologies instead of identifying which limitation actually mattered and how it would be addressed.

Timelines matter as much as content. Schools set internal deadlines for the investigation that sit well before the external ones, and those internal dates are the ones that govern a student's term. We map the plan against the school's timeline rather than the board's, and we schedule the heavy weeks away from the mock series where that is possible.
bullets: We coach the design, the uncertainty treatment and the evaluation argument
We never write, draft, rewrite or supply the work or its data
A research question that cannot be measured is the most common fatal error
Feedback arrives as examiner questions, not as improved text
The school's internal deadline is the one the plan is built around

sections.heading: Past-paper work that actually moves a physics grade
paragraphs: Most students do past papers wrong. They work through questions untimed, check the answers, mark themselves generously, and feel better without improving. The version that works is specific and slightly unpleasant: whole sections under time, marked against the published scheme by someone who will not be generous, with every lost mark categorised rather than merely counted. The category list is short - content gap, command term, unit or significant figure, arithmetic, graph accuracy, timing - and a tally across three papers tells you exactly what the next month should contain.

Marking honestly is the part a student cannot do alone, and not because they lack integrity. A student who has just written an answer cannot see what is missing from it; they see what they meant. A tutor reading the same answer against the scheme sees that the reasoning chain has two steps where the scheme wanted three. That is the whole value of the exercise, and it is why a marking clinic often beats a teaching session for a student who is already working hard.

Sequencing matters too. Early in the course, questions should be used by theme, immediately after the theme is taught, so the content is reinforced while it is fresh. In the final term, whole papers under time replace topic sets, because the skill being trained has changed from recall to allocation of time. In the final fortnight, no new content: the only work with a positive return is eliminating the errors that the tally says are recurring.

One caution about materials. We reference and link the official syllabus, specimen and timetable documents rather than reproducing them, and we do not supply board-owned papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Your child's school has legitimate access through its own subscriptions, and the board's own site is the correct source for everything else.
bullets: Whole sections under time, marked to the published scheme
Every lost mark categorised, then tallied across three papers
Topic sets early in the course, whole papers in the final term
