sections.heading: Tower logistics, tutor supply and what the online format changes for physics
paragraphs: Al Habtoor City sits on Sheikh Zayed Road between Business Bay and Al Safa, a cluster of residential towers and hotels along the Dubai Water Canal. There is no school in the development, so the Diploma students who live here travel out each morning to Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa or Nad Al Sheba. The return journey lands most students home between 15:45 and 16:45, which in practice means a physics session starting before 17:30 is a session that will eventually be cancelled by traffic.

In-home arrangements in Dubai are priced with that journey included: market quotes for a home visit run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, with published monthly packages of about AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. The premium does not buy better physics. It buys a car on Sheikh Zayed Road at the worst hour of the day, and it restricts the choice of tutor to those who live near enough to make the trip worthwhile.

For HL Physics specifically, that restriction is the real cost. HL Physics sets in Dubai schools are often small, and the tutors who have actually taught the HL-only material to examination are correspondingly few. A family selecting from those who can reach a tower in the evening peak is selecting from a thin list. A family selecting online is selecting from everyone. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - that is an India-only service - and for this subject the online format is the stronger option on its own merits rather than a fallback.

The screen also suits the subject. A graph can be annotated live while the student watches, a simulation shared mid-explanation, the mark scheme placed beside the student's own script, and a derivation recorded so it can be re-watched when it is needed rather than when it was taught. Those are not substitutes for a room. For physics they are better, and the Al Habtoor City evening that does not include a second car journey is a straightforward gain.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a wish list
process.description: The fastest start is a recent marked paper, the level your child takes, and the school's name. From those three we can usually tell whether the problem is content, command terms, uncertainty or timing, and which of those is worth paying for first. A syllabus list tells us far less than twenty minutes with a marked script does.

process.title: Free trial lesson spent on a question, not a conversation
process.description: The first session is free and runs on real past-paper questions chosen from the script you sent. The tutor watches the working appear and the diagnosis follows from that. Afterwards you get a short written note naming what is costing marks and what order to fix it in, and that note is yours whether or not you continue.

process.title: Fix a slot that survives the school run
process.description: We set a weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, deliberately after the return to the towers rather than during it. For Al Habtoor City that is usually 17:30 or later. Sessions booked optimistically early are the ones that get rescheduled, and a rescheduled session is a lost week in a subject that builds.

process.title: Work the strand the evidence named
process.description: Content gaps get theme-by-theme teaching with a written coverage map. Command-term and uncertainty losses get script clinics with the mark scheme open. An investigation gets design coaching inside the honesty rules. Most students need two of the three in sequence rather than all three at once.

process.title: Re-mark at week four and say what has changed
process.description: A second paper is sat and marked at week four, and the error tally is compared with week one. If the pattern has not moved, we change the approach or the tutor rather than defending either. If the target needs a different plan for the second year of the course, that is said then, while there is time to act on it.

whyPoints.title: Matched on who has taught HL Physics, not on who lives nearby
whyPoints.description: HL Physics is a small cohort in most Dubai schools, so the honest tutor pool for HL-only material is narrow. Online matching ignores geography and selects on teaching history, which for this subject is the difference between a tutor who can explain a field derivation and one who can only recite it.

whyPoints.title: The mark scheme is open on screen
whyPoints.description: Sessions work from the student's own script with the published scheme beside it, so progress is measured in marks recovered on named question types. That also makes the week-four review meaningful: two error tallies can be compared, while two impressions cannot.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty and significant figures are taught as rules
whyPoints.description: The data-based section is where IGCSE and MYP students arrive least prepared, and it is also where the fastest recoverable marks sit. We drill propagation, error bars and precision on the student's own calculations until the habit holds without prompting.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit on investigation support
whyPoints.description: We coach the research question, the variable control, the uncertainty treatment and the evaluation argument, and we respond to the student's drafts with the questions an examiner would ask. We do not write, rewrite or supply work. In a market where completed internal assessments are openly sold, the limit is the point.

whyPoints.title: No approvals claimed that we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education, and no office in the UAE. Where a page names a regulator it is to explain what that body does, never to imply it endorses us.

whyPoints.title: Calendar planning around the May session
whyPoints.description: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and the school's internal investigation deadlines usually bite harder on a student's term than the external window does. We plan blocks around both, and around Ramadan, rather than discovering the clash in the week it happens.

faqs.question: What does an IB physics tutor cost for a student living in Al Habtoor City?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with IB and IGCSE specialists quoted from about AED 200 to 450 or more; one premium provider publishes AED 650. In-home visits are quoted higher, roughly AED 180-500 an hour, because the fee carries the journey. Monthly estimates from the Bestimate Dubai rate table run about AED 600-1,200 for mid-band weekly support and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work. Those are market figures with their sources, not an IB Gram price list. We quote after the free trial lesson, once we know which strand of work your child actually needs.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our apartment in Al Habtoor City for physics lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is something we do only in India. Physics sessions for Al Habtoor City students run one-to-one online over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the online format is genuinely the stronger choice: HL Physics sets in Dubai schools are small, so the number of tutors who have taught the HL-only material to examination is limited, and selecting from those who could drive to Sheikh Zayed Road in the evening peak narrows that list further. On screen, graphs are annotated live and the session can be re-watched.

faqs.question: How are the five physics themes different from the old numbered topics?
faqs.answer: The current guide groups content into themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. The important structural change is that HL material sits inside each theme rather than in a separate block at the end. A student who is behind at SL level in a theme is therefore behind on its HL extension at the same time, and revision plans have to list the HL content explicitly or it gets skipped. Ask your child's teacher for the department's scheme of work, because the order themes are taught in varies between schools and that order matters more than the guide's sequence.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in physics when they understand the topic?
faqs.answer: Usually command terms, units, significant figures or answer length rather than content. IB command terms are defined in the guide and applied literally: state wants a fact, outline wants brief key points, explain wants a chain of reasoning, and determine wants working followed by a value with units. An answer that explains when the paper said state wastes time; one that states when the paper said explain scores nothing. Add gradients quoted without units and calculator displays copied to ten digits, and a capable student can lose several marks a paper without a single gap in knowledge. Script clinics fix this faster than more teaching does.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the physics scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach your child how to narrow a research question until it is measurable with school equipment, how to identify and control variables, how to estimate and propagate uncertainty, how to structure the analysis, and how an evaluation engages with the limitations that actually mattered. A tutor can read a draft your child wrote and respond with the questions an examiner would ask. A tutor cannot write it, draft a section, rewrite the text or supply data. Providers who sell completed internal assessments exist in this market, and buying one is an academic-malpractice risk that lands on the student.

faqs.question: How much harder is HL Physics than SL for a Dubai Diploma student?
faqs.answer: The HL course covers the same five themes with additional material inside each, so the difference is depth and volume rather than a separate syllabus. In marked work the HL-only material is where most HL marks are lost, and fields is the theme that causes the most difficulty, both because it is abstract and because its HL extension is substantial. The practical risk in Dubai schools is isolation: HL Physics sets are often small, so a student stuck on an HL derivation may have nobody in the class to work through it with. That is the single most common reason families here look for outside support.

faqs.question: My child came from IGCSE physics and is struggling in Year 12. Why?
faqs.answer: Three new demands usually arrive at once. Uncertainty arithmetic, which IGCSE barely touches, suddenly has to survive being carried through a calculation. Command-term precision starts being marked literally, where IGCSE was more forgiving about answer length. And conclusions have to be argued from data rather than stated. None of the three is conceptually difficult, and all three are unfamiliar, which is why a strong Extended 0625 or 4PH1 grade does not predict a comfortable Diploma start. Six to eight focused sessions on those three items closes most of the gap, and doing it early in Year 12 is far cheaper than repairing it later.

faqs.question: Which maths course should a physics student in Dubai take alongside it?
faqs.answer: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is the more natural partner, because the differentiation, trigonometric manipulation and logarithmic graph work it emphasises appear inside physics questions. Applications and Interpretation can work, but the algebraic fluency physics assumes is not that route's main emphasis, so the gap has to be closed deliberately rather than hoped away. Check the published entry requirements of the universities your child is aiming at, since engineering and physical-science courses often specify the maths route. Make the decision with the school's coordinator rather than from a corridor rumour, and make it while the option block can still be changed.

faqs.question: When should an Al Habtoor City family start physics support in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The cheapest point is the summer before Year 12, closing the uncertainty, algebra and command-term gaps before the course assumes them. The next cheapest is early in the first year, working weekly alongside school teaching so themes are reinforced while they are fresh. The most common actual starting point is after the first serious internal assessment in Year 12, which still leaves plenty of room. Starting in the final term is possible and the work changes shape: no new content, whole papers under time, and error-pattern elimination. The honest answer in that situation comes from a marked paper rather than from optimism.

faqs.question: What time do physics sessions start for students in these towers?
faqs.answer: Usually 17:30 or later. A Diploma student living in Al Habtoor City travels out to Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Umm Suqeim or Nad Al Sheba each morning and returns across or along Sheikh Zayed Road in the afternoon, typically arriving home between 15:45 and 16:45. Add the lift, food and a change of clothes, and the first slot that survives a bad traffic day is around 17:30. Families who book earlier in optimism tend to rebook by the third week. Because sessions are online there is no second journey, which is the main reason this timing holds through a whole term.

faqs.question: Do you teach physics to students sitting A Level rather than the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, although this page is written for the Diploma. Students in British-curriculum schools near Al Safa and Umm Suqeim often take A Level Physics instead, and the work overlaps substantially: the same algebraic fluency, the same graph and uncertainty discipline, the same need for command-term precision under a different name. The differences are in assessment structure and practical endorsement arrangements. Tell us the board and specification code when you enquire, because the past papers and the mark-scheme conventions differ, and revising on the wrong board's material is the most common avoidable waste of a student's time.

faqs.question: How do online physics sessions handle diagrams and derivations?
faqs.answer: The student writes, the tutor watches. Working goes on squared paper or a tablet with the camera angled at the page rather than the face, so a dropped vector sign or an unlabelled free-body diagram is caught as it happens. A shared digital whiteboard carries anything the tutor needs to demonstrate, and a simulation can be shared mid-explanation when a field or a wave is easier seen than described. Sessions are recorded, which matters for derivations: a student can re-watch the step they lost at the moment they need it rather than trying to reconstruct it from notes. Setup takes about ten minutes before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Which session do IB candidates in the UAE sit, and how should we plan around it?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. We deliberately do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages, because the International Baccalaureate's own site is the authoritative source and should be checked directly or through the school's IB coordinator. For planning purposes the dates that matter more to a student's term are internal: the school's own deadlines for the scientific investigation and for the Extended Essay, which typically fall well before anything the board sets. Build the tutoring plan around those internal dates, keep the mock series clear of the heaviest coursework weeks, and confirm every external date with the school.

faqs.question: What if no HL Physics specialist is free in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than placing a generalist. SL Physics matching is usually quick. HL requests, especially where the gap is in the HL extension of fields or in nuclear and quantum physics, draw on a smaller group, and the honest options are a different time slot, a short wait for the right tutor, or a script-marking clinic in the meantime so no time is wasted. We will also tell you where a tutor is based before you book. Filling a specialist slot with whoever is available is how families end up paying for sessions that confirm what they already knew.

paragraphs: A parent in Al Jaddaf searching for an IB Physics tutor is usually three or four weeks into a problem. A mock paper came back at a 4. The school's subject teacher has thirty students and a Paper 3 option to finish. Somebody in a building WhatsApp group recommended a tutor at AED 300 an hour, and somebody else said their nephew charges AED 90. Neither number came with an explanation, and that is the real difficulty: the Dubai tutoring market publishes almost no prices, so families negotiate blind.

What the figures do is let you work out, before you commit, whether a quote you have been given is cheap, normal or steep for the thing being sold.

The second half of the money question is harder and nobody writes about it: where does the spend actually get wasted? In DP Physics the answer is specific. It is wasted on general science tutors re-teaching mechanics that the student already follows. It is wasted on hours spent on Topic 1 and Topic 2 while the Paper 3 option sits untouched until April. It is wasted on sessions with no past-paper marking, because a student who can explain an idea verbally and still writes a two-mark answer for a four-mark question has a technique problem that only marked scripts expose.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.programmesIntro: Physics appears in three different shapes across an IB school career, and the cost of support differs sharply between them. Below is what each stage asks of a student in Dubai, and what tutoring at that stage is realistically buying.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Two years, taken at Higher or Standard Level. The current course is organised around themes covering space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Assessment is Paper 1 split into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, Paper 2 of extended response questions, and the scientific investigation that all DP sciences now share. HL adds additional higher level content within each theme rather than a separate bolt-on syllabus.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Jaddaf the DP Physics cohort is small at most schools, often a single teaching group covering both HL and SL in the same room. That has a direct cost consequence: HL-only content gets compressed, and families end up buying tutoring to cover material the timetable never reached rather than material the student failed to understand. Ask the subject teacher which HL sections are scheduled for the summer term before booking hours.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Physics sits inside integrated or discrete MYP Sciences, assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Each criterion is marked out of eight. The habits that decide DP Physics grades are built here, particularly the processing and evaluating criterion, which is where uncertainty, graphing and error analysis first appear in a formal mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Physics support is the cheapest intervention available to an Al Jaddaf family and the one most often skipped. A Year 10 student who cannot draw a line of best fit with error bars will lose the same marks in DP two years later, at three times the hourly rate, under exam pressure. Buying four MYP sessions on graphing is a smaller spend than buying twelve DP sessions on data analysis in Year 13.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the DP entry route
programmes.description: Many students in this part of Dubai arrive at DP Physics from Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 rather than from MYP. Both cover mechanics, thermal physics, waves, electricity, magnetism and radioactivity, and both stop well short of the calculus-adjacent reasoning the Diploma expects. The gap is not content coverage; it is the move from recall and substitution to multi-step derivation and justification.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE-to-DP Physics transition is the single most predictable place an Al Jaddaf family spends money badly. A student with an A* at 0625 is often told no support is needed, then meets uncertainty propagation in the first term and loses confidence. Six targeted sessions in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, on algebraic rearrangement and uncertainty handling, cost less than a term of rescue work in November.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-jaddaf.subjectsIntro: DP Physics is one course, but the hours a tutor spends are allocated by theme, and some themes cost more to fix than others. Below is what each area assesses and where the marks drain away.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, circular motion and, at HL, rotational dynamics and special relativity. Marks are lost on sign conventions in momentum problems and on candidates who resolve forces correctly then forget that the component along the slope is the one doing work.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal concepts, the ideal gas law, kinetic theory and current electricity. The common failure is numeric rather than conceptual: temperatures entered in degrees Celsius into a relationship that demands kelvin, and specific heat capacity questions where the mass of the container is quietly ignored.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave characteristics, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect. Standing-wave questions reward a candidate who can sketch the harmonic before calculating; those who go straight to a formula routinely use the wrong fraction of a wavelength for a pipe closed at one end.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential, orbital motion and electromagnetic induction. HL extends into field and potential gradients. The recurring loss is direction: Lenz's law questions where the induced current sign is stated without reference to the change in flux that caused it.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and, at HL, quantum tunnelling and the Rutherford scattering treatment. Binding-energy-per-nucleon questions are a reliable marks source once a student stops confusing mass defect with total mass.

subjects.name: Measurement and uncertainty
subjects.description: Not a theme in its own right but assessed in every paper and in the investigation. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through products and powers, significant figures and error bars. More Paper 1B marks turn on this than on any single topic in the guide.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: The internally assessed report, worth 20 per cent at both levels and marked out of 24. Criteria cover research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The most expensive mistake is a research question too broad to produce a gradient worth analysing, which no amount of later editing repairs.

subjects.name: Experimental and data skills
subjects.description: Reading apparatus diagrams, identifying control variables, choosing sensible axes and spotting systematic versus random error. Paper 1B presents unfamiliar apparatus and asks for judgement, so a student drilled only on recall will stall even with strong theory.

subjects.name: Mathematics for Physics
subjects.description: Logarithms for decay curves, trigonometric resolution, gradient and area interpretation, and rearrangement under time pressure. Students taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation often need this scaffolding explicitly; those on Analysis and Approaches usually need it only for log-linearisation.

subjects.name: Paper 3 option content
subjects.description: Where the older course structure still shapes school planning, option material is taught last and revised least. Whichever option a school runs, it is the block most likely to be unfinished in March, which makes it the highest-value tutoring hour of the whole two years.

sections.heading: Which assessment components justify which hours
paragraphs: Spending decisions in DP Physics get much easier once the weightings are on the table. The external assessment is split across Paper 1 and Paper 2, and the internally assessed scientific investigation carries 20 per cent at both Higher and Standard Level. That last figure is the one families consistently under-rate. A fifth of the grade is decided by a report written over several months, on the student's own schedule, with no exam-hall pressure. Hours spent there are the cheapest marks available in the whole course.

Paper 1 is worth looking at in two halves because they fail for different reasons. Section A is multiple choice across the syllabus, and it rewards breadth plus fast elimination. Section B is the data-based section: unfamiliar apparatus, a table of readings, and questions about uncertainty, gradient and systematic error. A student can be strong on theory and weak on Section B, and no amount of re-teaching mechanics will move it. That is a technique block, usually four to six sessions, and it is the highest-return repair work in the subject.

Paper 2 is extended response and it is where command terms decide the mark. Describe, explain, deduce, justify and comment all ask for different amounts of writing, and candidates who write one sentence for a four-mark 'explain' lose two marks they understood perfectly. This is why a tutoring arrangement without marked scripts is a poor purchase: the gap is invisible in conversation and obvious on paper. Ask any prospective tutor how many past-paper questions they will mark per month, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

The practical consequence for a budget is a sequencing rule. Pay for investigation support early, pay for Section B technique in the middle, and pay for timed Paper 2 practice last. Families who reverse that order spend more and gain less, because the investigation deadline passes while the money is still going on content revision.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks and strict limits on help
paragraphs: A fifth of the DP Physics grade comes from the scientific investigation, marked out of 24 against criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is the only part of the course where a student controls the conditions completely, and it is the part most often left until the deadline is close enough to cause panic. For a family managing a budget, it is also the best value block of tutoring in the two years, because the work happens in calm weeks rather than exam weeks.

The failures are predictable and nearly all of them are design failures rather than writing failures. A research question that cannot produce a measurable gradient will not recover at the analysis stage. Too few values of the independent variable leaves a graph that cannot support a conclusion. Repeats omitted means no random uncertainty to report, which hollows out the data-analysis criterion. A tutor who reads the proposal in week one is worth more than one who reads the draft in week ten, and costs the same per hour.

There are firm limits on what a tutor may do here, and they are not negotiable. Under IB academic-honesty rules the investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach uncertainty propagation, question whether a control variable is really controlled, explain what the evaluation criterion rewards, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any part of the report, generate the data, or edit the text into its final form. Any provider offering to supply a finished investigation is offering the student a malpractice finding.

That boundary is worth stating to any tutor before you hire them. The answer tells you a great deal. A tutor who explains where the line sits and how they work inside it is a tutor who has supervised real IB students. One who promises a polished report has told you they have not, or that they do not care what happens to your child's diploma.

sections.heading: Where Al Jaddaf families waste money on Physics tutoring
paragraphs: Four spending mistakes account for most of the wasted money we see in this corridor, and all four are avoidable with one conversation before the first session. The first is hiring a general science tutor for DP Physics. Someone who teaches IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics competently may still have never marked a DP Paper 2 to criteria. At AED 150 an hour that is not a bargain; it is a slower route to the same place, paid for by the hour.

The second is buying hours without diagnosis. A parent reports that their child is struggling with physics, and twelve sessions of general revision follow. Had anyone read the marked mock first, the pattern might have been obvious: full marks on the recall questions, consistent losses on anything involving uncertainty or a gradient. That is a four-session fix, not a twelve-session one. The diagnosis costs nothing and routinely saves four figures in AED.

The third is leaving the Paper 3 option content to the school's timetable and hoping. Option material is taught last, revised least and examined fully. If a school is behind in March, the option is what is behind, and the student who has never seen half of it walks into a paper carrying marks they could have had. Asking in January which sections remain unscheduled is the single highest-value question a parent can put to a subject teacher.

The fourth is paying a premium rate for a scarce named tutor when the problem is routine. If a student cannot rearrange an equation under time pressure, that is not a problem requiring the most expensive person available. It needs a competent tutor and six weeks of drilled practice. Save the specialist rate for the problems that genuinely need a specialist: HL option depth, borderline-7 refinement, and investigation design in an unusual context.

sections.heading: Sequencing two years of DP Physics spend
paragraphs: Total cost falls sharply when support is sequenced rather than bought in response to crises. The shape that works for most Al Jaddaf families is light in the first term, concentrated around the investigation in the middle, and intense for a defined final stretch. Reactive spending inverts that: nothing happens until a mock grade arrives, then a large block is purchased in the most expensive weeks of the course, when every good tutor in the city is already fully booked.

In the first DP term the useful spend is small and diagnostic. Two or three sessions establishing whether the student can handle uncertainty, logarithms and multi-step rearrangement will tell you what the next twenty months need. If those are sound, weekly tutoring may genuinely not be necessary yet, and a parent who hears that from a tutor has found a tutor worth keeping. If they are not sound, fixing them in term one is a fraction of the cost of fixing them in term five.

The middle of the course belongs to the investigation and to Paper 1 Section B technique. Both are calm-weather work, both are cheap relative to their mark value, and both are nearly impossible to do well in the final term. A family that books a six-session investigation block and a six-session data-skills block across DP Year 1 has spent perhaps a third of a crisis budget and removed the two largest sources of lost marks.

The final stretch is for timed practice and marked scripts, and it is worth paying for properly. This is where command-term discipline, time allocation across Paper 2, and the habit of reading the mark allocation before writing all get built. Book it early in the academic year rather than when revision starts, because specialist availability in the weeks before the May session is the scarcest thing in the Dubai market and the one that prices accordingly.

sections.heading: KHDA, the permit, and what your fee is paying for
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the published report for your child's school is worth reading before you buy tutoring, because it often names the subject departments where attainment lags. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate provision accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment.

Private tutoring itself is governed federally rather than by KHDA. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure you see circulating should be treated with caution. What matters practically is that the permit is free and quick, which means a tutor who has not obtained one has chosen not to. Asking is reasonable, and the answer is informative either way.

One further point, because it affects who you should and should not hire. Abu Dhabi's ADEK rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, MoE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, approval or partnership, and does not claim any. We are an independent tutor-matching platform, and our fee buys teaching hours and matching, nothing more.

sections.heading: Booking, trialling and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the level, the school, what the last marked paper looked like and how many weeks are left. We propose a tutor whose DP Physics coverage matches that specifically, including the option topic where it is relevant. A free trial lesson runs before any payment, on a real piece of work rather than a sales call. If the match is wrong, you say so and we propose another, and nothing has been spent.

What happens when no specialist is available is a question competitors in this market avoid answering, so here is ours plainly. DP Physics at Higher Level with a particular option is a narrow specialism, and in a busy term the right tutor may not have a free slot in the Gulf Standard Time evening window. When that happens we say so rather than substituting a general science tutor at the same rate. Usually we can offer a different slot, a tutor in a different time zone whose availability overlaps the UAE evening, or a start date a fortnight out. Occasionally the honest answer is that we cannot help this term.

The practical reason to ask early is scarcity, not sales pressure. Availability for DP sciences tightens from the new year onward and is at its worst in the final weeks before the May session, which is precisely when demand peaks. A family that arranges a weekly slot in the autumn pays the same hourly rate as one that arranges it in the spring, but gets a materially better choice of tutor. That is the clearest case in this whole market where acting early is worth money.

Lead forms on this site collect a parent's name, a contact address, the student's year group, subject and level, and nothing else. That information exists to match a tutor and to arrange the trial lesson. It is not sold on, and you can ask for it to be deleted at any time; the privacy notice linked from every page sets out how. We do not ask for a child's photograph, school report or grades to arrange a trial.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for an IB Physics tutor in Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates span AED 45 to 650 an hour, and the tier matters more than the area. Budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Specialist IB rates run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutoring reaches AED 650 at BartyED. For DP Physics with a Paper 3 option, the AED 200 to 300 band is where most Al Jaddaf families find a genuine subject specialist.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying extra for a tutor who will travel to Al Jaddaf?
faqs.answer: The premium is real and it buys travel rather than teaching. Bestimate records in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online. A tutor driving to the creek for a 17:00 session loses three hours of their day for one paid hour, and the rate reflects that. The bigger cost is choice: you are selecting from whoever will make the trip, not from everyone who teaches your child's option. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE and delivers lessons online.

faqs.question: My son gets the theory but keeps losing marks on the data questions. What is that?
faqs.answer: That is Paper 1 Section B, and it is a technique problem rather than a knowledge one. Section B gives unfamiliar apparatus, a table of readings and questions about uncertainty, gradient and systematic error. A student can know every theme in the guide and still stall there, because the skill being tested is judgement about measurement. It usually takes four to six focused sessions on absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through products and powers, error bars and log-linearisation. Re-teaching mechanics will not move it, which is why a marked script is the first thing a tutor should ask for.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the DP Physics scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within firm limits. A tutor may help narrow a research question until it produces a measurable gradient, teach uncertainty propagation, challenge whether a control variable is genuinely controlled, explain what each criterion rewards, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not write any section, generate or adjust data, or edit the report into final form. The investigation carries 20 per cent of the grade at both levels and is marked out of 24, and it must be the student's own work under IB academic-honesty rules. Any provider offering a finished report is offering a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: How many sessions does DP Physics usually take to turn around?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the marked paper shows. A single diagnosable technique gap, such as uncertainty handling or command-term discipline, is often a four to six session block with re-marked evidence at the end. Unfinished option content takes longer, roughly one session per syllabus section plus practice. A student two grades below target across every component usually needs weekly support across a full year rather than a block. Anyone quoting a session count before reading a marked script is guessing, and that guess is how families end up paying for twelve sessions when four would have done.

faqs.question: Why does the Paper 3 option content matter so much to the budget?
faqs.answer: Option material is taught last, revised least and examined fully, which makes it the most reliably unfinished part of a DP Physics course. If a school is running behind in the spring, the option is what is behind. A student who meets half of it for the first time in revision is leaving marks on the table that cost nothing to secure earlier. Asking the subject teacher in January which sections remain unscheduled costs nothing and often redirects a tutoring budget from general revision, where the returns are modest, to option teaching, where they are large and immediate.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and can I ask about it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is governed by the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The u.ae guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Is online Physics teaching really equivalent for a practical subject?
faqs.answer: For the assessed parts of DP Physics, yes, and in one respect it is better. Nothing in Paper 1, Paper 2 or the investigation requires the tutor to be in the room. Screen-sharing a past-paper diagram, annotating a graph together and working through uncertainty line by line is often clearer on a shared screen than over a kitchen table. What online delivery changes is the pool: an Al Jaddaf family can work with the tutor who actually teaches their option topic rather than the one who will drive to the creek at 17:00. Practical work itself happens at school, where the apparatus is.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful thing I can buy right now?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis. Send the most recent marked Physics paper and have a tutor read it before buying any hours. In many cases the pattern is immediately clear: full marks on recall, consistent losses on anything with a gradient or an uncertainty, or correct physics written too briefly for the mark allocation. That turns an open-ended arrangement into a defined four to six session block with a measurable end point. The second cheapest useful purchase is investigation design support early in DP Year 1, because 20 per cent of the grade is decided in calm weeks rather than exam weeks.

faqs.question: Which exam series do Physics students in Dubai actually sit?
faqs.answer: IB Diploma candidates in the UAE sit the May session, with a November session available as an alternative or resit route. For Cambridge qualifications the UAE sits the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai parent given February dates has been given the wrong country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and in November. We do not publish specific IB exam or results dates on these pages, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than none. Confirm with your school's IB coordinator.

faqs.question: Does my child need a different tutor if they take Maths AI rather than AA?
faqs.answer: Not a different tutor, but the tutor needs to know. Students on Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation generally meet less algebraic manipulation and less work with logarithms than those on Analysis and Approaches, and DP Physics assumes a fair amount of both. The practical effect is that log-linearising a decay curve, or rearranging a three-variable relationship under time pressure, needs explicit scaffolding rather than a passing reminder. Tell the tutor at matching, not in week six. It changes the order in which the first few sessions are built and saves repeated backtracking later.

faqs.question: Should I buy a monthly package or pay by the hour?
faqs.answer: Packages in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, which is a discount to the hourly rate in exchange for commitment. That is good value when the need is established and the tutor is proven, and poor value before a trial lesson has happened. The sensible order is a free trial, then a short block with a stated end point and marked evidence, then a longer commitment if the evidence supports it. Committing to a term before anyone has seen the student work is how tutoring budgets get stranded.

faqs.question: How early should an Al Jaddaf family book for the exam run?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, and for a reason that has nothing to do with sales pressure. The hourly rate does not rise as exams approach, but availability collapses. DP Physics at Higher Level with a specific option is a narrow specialism, and the evening slots in Gulf Standard Time are the ones every UAE family wants. A parent who fixes a weekly slot in the autumn pays the same as one who fixes it in the spring but chooses from a far better set of tutors. If you already know an exam-run block is coming, reserve it while there is still a choice to make.

faqs.question: What happens if no DP Physics specialist is available for us?
faqs.answer: We say so. Competitors in this market rarely disclose a coverage limit, and the usual substitute is a general science tutor at a specialist rate, which wastes a term and the money. When no suitable tutor has a slot in the UAE evening window, we will normally offer a different time, a tutor in another time zone whose availability overlaps the Gulf evening, or a start date a fortnight or so out. Occasionally the honest answer is that we cannot cover it this term. That is a better outcome for a family than a confident match that turns out not to teach the course.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-khail-gate.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Physics at a named level and diagnose which of the three underlying skills is failing before teaching any content. Each works from the student's own script and the published data booklet.

intro.heading: Three skills stacked, and only one of them is physics
paragraphs: IB Physics asks a student to do three things at once and most struggling students are failing at exactly one of them. The first is physics: understanding the model, knowing which principle applies, choosing conservation of energy over kinematics because the question gives you heights and not times. The second is mathematics: rearranging, substituting, handling powers of ten, reading a gradient, and doing all of it under time pressure. The third is measurement: uncertainties, significant figures, error bars, and reasoning about how good a result actually is.

A student who understands the physics and cannot rearrange confidently will look like a physics failure in every paper. A student who can do both and has never been taught uncertainty propagation loses a consistent block of marks in the data-analysis questions and in their investigation. A student fluent in all three and slow at arithmetic loses the final questions on a paper to the clock. Those are four different problems and one report comment, and the comment is usually about working harder.

Separating them takes one script read properly. The physics failures show as the wrong principle chosen or a conceptual error stated in words. The mathematics failures show as a correct starting equation followed by an incorrect rearrangement. The measurement failures cluster in the data questions and in anything asking about precision, accuracy or reliability. The timing failures show as blank space at the end rather than wrong answers anywhere.

There is a fourth skill that sits underneath all of it and is almost never taught explicitly: using the data booklet. Every IB physics examination supplies one, and a student who knows what is in it stops memorising relationships and starts spending their revision on when to use them. Students who have never deliberately worked through the booklet waste time hunting for an equation that is on a page they have not looked at properly.

Then there is the internally assessed scientific investigation, which carries a published share of the grade and is the part of physics most under-planned. Its ceiling is set at the design stage: a research question that cannot generate data with a measurable trend cannot be analysed well, and no quality of write-up repairs that. Uncertainty treatment in the investigation is also where the strongest and weakest work separate most visibly.

The rest of this page works through those pieces: the mathematics physics assumes, graph linearisation, uncertainty propagation, data booklet technique, the investigation, and the Higher Level extension content where Standard Level habits break down. All of it is diagnosable from a marked paper, which is why the first session should be a working session. A parent can start that process without us: find the script, look for questions where a correct relationship is followed by a wrong line, and count them. That number alone usually settles what kind of help is needed.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Available at Higher and Standard Level, with Higher carrying additional content and a greater paper load. Assessment combines external papers, including data-analysis questions, with an internally assessed scientific investigation. A data booklet is supplied in the examinations, so the emphasis is on selection and application rather than recall of relationships.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, where International Baccalaureate students are about seven per cent of private enrolment, Physics Higher Level cohorts are often small. That means limited individual attention inside the class and, for a student with a specific gap in the Higher Level extension content, little chance of it being noticed and addressed in lesson time.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria, including inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating, which map more directly onto the Diploma investigation than onto its papers. Students from MYP often design better investigations and write weaker timed answers in the first Diploma term.
programmes.countryNote: In the Dubailand belt most schools run IGCSE rather than MYP, so a Diploma physics class here usually mixes both entry routes. The MYP-entry student needs timed writing practice; the IGCSE-entry student needs independent investigation skills. Naming which applies takes one conversation.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the prerequisite
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 Extended or Pearson 4PH1 is the realistic preparation for Diploma Physics. The Extended content includes the quantitative treatment of forces, electricity and waves that the Diploma builds on; a Core entry omits several topics the Diploma assumes as prior knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE in the June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only. Most UAE school centres enter candidates for the Alternative to Practical paper, which is a written paper about experimental work rather than a laboratory assessment.

programmes.name: A Level Physics as the alternative
programmes.description: The other post-16 physics route in this belt, narrower and deeper, usually taken alongside mathematics. Both routes are accepted widely for engineering and physical sciences, and the practical difference is breadth of the rest of the timetable rather than physics content.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, plus five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 or better, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-khail-gate.subjectsIntro: These are the physics skills and topic areas that generate the most requests, described by the specific failure rather than by syllabus heading.

subjects.name: Rearranging and substituting
subjects.description: The commonest hidden cause of low physics marks. A student who can state the right relationship and cannot isolate the required variable confidently loses the question, and the loss looks like a physics error on a report. Fixing it is algebra practice inside physics contexts rather than a separate maths course.

subjects.name: Powers of ten and unit prefixes
subjects.description: Nanometres, megajoules, kilowatt-hours and scientific notation in calculations with several steps. Errors here produce answers wrong by a factor of a thousand, which the student often spots as implausible and cannot locate, costing time as well as marks.

subjects.name: Graphs and linearisation
subjects.description: Turning a non-linear relationship into a straight line by plotting the right quantities, then extracting a physical constant from the gradient or intercept. Explicitly taught in good classrooms and absent from many, and it appears in both the papers and the investigation.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error propagation
subjects.description: Absolute and fractional uncertainty, propagation through products, quotients and powers, error bars and uncertainty in a gradient. A consistent block of marks in data-analysis questions and the single clearest differentiator in investigation scores.

subjects.name: Mechanics and energy
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum and energy conservation. The marks turn on choosing the right approach: energy methods where times are absent, momentum where a collision is involved. Students who default to kinematics everywhere make hard work of easy questions.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.levels: HL and SL, deeper at HL
subjects.description: Wave behaviour, superposition, standing waves and at Higher Level simple harmonic motion treated quantitatively. Phase relationships and boundary conditions on standing waves are where diagrams are drawn wrongly and marks follow.

subjects.name: Fields and circuits
subjects.levels: HL and SL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, and electrical circuits. Potential and potential energy are routinely conflated, and circuit questions are lost on reading a series arrangement as parallel rather than on any analysis error.

sections.heading: The mathematics physics assumes and does not teach
paragraphs: Diploma Physics is built on a set of mathematical skills it treats as prior knowledge. Rearranging an equation where the required variable sits inside a bracket or on a denominator. Working confidently with indices and powers of ten across several multiplication steps. Handling unit prefixes without converting twice or not at all. Reading a gradient from a graph with awkward axis scales. Using radians where a question is set in radians. None of those is taught in a physics lesson, and all of them are tested in every paper.

The diagnostic signature is distinctive once you look for it. A script where the correct relationship is written at the top of a question and the next line is algebraically wrong is a mathematics problem. A script where no relationship appears at all, or the wrong one appears, is a physics problem. The two look identical in a grade and call for completely different work, and the first is much faster to fix.

The fix is algebra practice inside physics contexts rather than a general mathematics course. Taking twenty past-paper questions, writing only the rearrangement step for each and checking it, builds the specific fluency the subject needs in a couple of sessions. A student who does that stops losing marks on questions they understood, which is the most frustrating category of loss and the most common.

The related trap is mental arithmetic with powers of ten. An answer wrong by a factor of a thousand is usually recognised as implausible by the student, who then spends two minutes hunting for the slip and loses time as well as the mark. Writing every quantity in scientific notation before substituting looks laborious and removes an entire class of error, which on a paper with several multi-step calculations is worth more than it costs.

sections.heading: Linearisation: the graph skill that separates grades
paragraphs: A great deal of physics assessment asks a student to extract a physical constant from experimental data, and the reliable route is to plot a straight line. If the relationship is a power law or an inverse relationship, plotting the raw quantities gives a curve from which nothing precise can be read. Plotting the right transformed quantities gives a straight line whose gradient or intercept is the constant you want.

The skill has three parts. First, rearranging the physical relationship into the form of a straight line, deciding what should go on each axis so that the gradient has physical meaning. Second, plotting accurately with a sensible scale, which carries marks in itself. Third, reading the gradient from the line of best fit rather than from two data points, which is the error almost every untrained student makes because using points feels more precise and is not.

This appears in the written papers in data-analysis questions and it appears again in the investigation, where a graph that linearises the relationship is usually the difference between an analysis that supports a conclusion and one that gestures at a trend. It is also one of the clearest cases where a short taught technique produces a visible mark improvement, because the student was not failing to understand anything, only failing to know the method.

Teaching it works best on the student's own data or on a real data-analysis question rather than in the abstract. Rearranging the relationship, choosing axes, plotting, drawing the line, reading the gradient with units, and then asking what the intercept means physically: that sequence, done three or four times across different relationships, is usually enough for it to become automatic.
bullets: Rearrange the relationship into straight-line form before plotting anything
Choose axes so the gradient has a physical meaning
Read the gradient from the line of best fit, never from two data points
Ask what the intercept means physically; it often carries a mark

sections.heading: Uncertainties, properly
paragraphs: Uncertainty treatment is the part of physics that distinguishes a strong script from a competent one, and it is routinely taught as a set of recipes to memorise. It works far better understood. An absolute uncertainty is the range within which a measurement plausibly lies, taken from the instrument's resolution or from the spread of repeated readings. A fractional or percentage uncertainty expresses that range relative to the measurement, which is what matters when quantities are combined.

The propagation rules follow from that and are short. Adding or subtracting quantities adds their absolute uncertainties. Multiplying or dividing adds their fractional uncertainties. Raising to a power multiplies the fractional uncertainty by that power, which is why a quantity that appears squared dominates the uncertainty in a result and is the first thing to measure more carefully. A student who understands that last point can say something intelligent in an evaluation instead of a generic comment about human error.

Graphically, uncertainties appear as error bars, and the examinable skill is drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines through the bars to obtain an uncertainty in the gradient. That is a procedure with a fixed method and it is worth practising to reliability, because it appears in data-analysis questions and because it is the standard way an investigation quantifies the uncertainty in its result.

There is also a vocabulary problem worth fixing at the same time. Precision, accuracy, reliability and validity mean different things and the published expectations use them exactly. A result can be precise and inaccurate, which is what a systematic error produces. A method can be reliable and invalid, which is what measuring the wrong thing consistently produces. Students who use these words loosely lose evaluation marks they could have had for free.

sections.heading: Using the data booklet as a technique
paragraphs: Every IB physics examination supplies a data booklet containing the relationships and constants a candidate needs. That changes what revision should consist of, and most students never adjust. Instead of memorising relationships, the useful work is knowing what is in the booklet, where it is, and which relationship applies to which situation. The subject stops being a recall test and becomes a selection test.

The practical exercise is to work through the booklet deliberately, page by page, with the syllabus beside it, and annotate which topic each section serves. Half an hour spent doing that once removes the commonest time loss in a physics paper, which is a student turning pages looking for something while the clock runs. It also reveals relationships the student did not know were provided, which they had been memorising unnecessarily.

The second half of the technique is selection practice. Given a question, which of several plausible relationships applies, and why. A question giving heights and asking for a speed wants energy conservation; a question giving a time wants kinematics; a question involving a collision wants momentum. Students who default to one approach regardless make hard work of straightforward questions and run out of time.

What the booklet does not contain is the physics reasoning, the command-term discipline or the unit handling. A student who treats it as a crutch, hunting for an equation before thinking about the situation, uses it badly. The order that works is to decide what physics applies, then find the relationship that expresses it, then substitute. That sequence also produces the written working the mark scheme pays for.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation in physics specifically
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation carries a published share of the physics grade and its ceiling is set early. A research question that cannot produce a measurable trend across an achievable range makes good analysis impossible, and the single commonest failure is choosing a question where the dependent variable barely changes. Testing the design with a quick preliminary run before committing is worth more than any amount of careful write-up afterwards.

Physics investigations live or die on uncertainty. Every instrument used needs an estimated uncertainty recorded at the point of measurement, every repeated reading needs recording rather than averaging on the spot, and the final result needs an uncertainty derived by propagation or from a graph. An investigation reporting a value with no uncertainty cannot reach the top of the evaluation criteria, however well the experiment was executed.

The evaluation section is where most of the recoverable marks sit and where students write the least. The published expectations reward identifying which measurement contributed most to the uncertainty in the result, explaining why, and proposing a specific improvement that would reduce it. That is a different piece of writing from a general list of things that went wrong, and it follows directly from understanding that a squared quantity dominates a propagated uncertainty.

The honesty boundary is firm and worth stating plainly. A tutor can teach the physics, question whether the design can produce a trend, explain each published criterion, discuss how to estimate an instrument's uncertainty, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor cannot design it for them, process their data, write any section or edit it to completion. Operations selling completed Internal Assessments exist in the Gulf market, and the malpractice consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

A curve with no quantified uncertainty
A generic list of things that went wrong
At writing, but follows from design

sections.heading: Higher Level extension content, and where Standard Level habits break
paragraphs: Higher Level Physics adds content the Standard Level course does not examine, and it adds a greater paper load. The extension material arrives later in the two years and is taught faster, because the shared content had to come first. That produces a familiar pattern: a student who coped through Year 12 and started struggling in Year 13 usually has a specific gap in the extension topics rather than a general weakness.

The habits that break are specific. At Standard Level a student can often reason qualitatively about fields and oscillations; at Higher Level the treatment becomes quantitative and the algebra gets harder. Circular motion and gravitation demand confident manipulation of relationships with several variables. Oscillations treated quantitatively require comfort with phase and with differential relationships. Students who got through the shared content on physical intuition find intuition insufficient.

Diagnosing this needs the syllabus rather than guesswork. List the Higher Level extension topics, have the student attempt one question on each under time, and the gaps appear immediately. They are usually one or two topics, not five, and a block aimed at those specifically is far more efficient than open-ended revision that spends most of its hours on secure material.

There is an honest exception. A Higher Level student weak across the shared content as well as the extensions is carrying a load heavier than the course assumes, often alongside two other demanding Higher Level subjects. The useful conversation there is about level rather than topic, and it belongs in term one of Year 12 while the school can still act, not in the spring of Year 13 when it cannot.

sections.heading: What physics tutoring costs, and which band is worth it
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates divide into bands, and for physics the choice between them depends on which of the three underlying skills is failing. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises online tutoring from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at around AED 270, and BartyED charges AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 500 with travel included.

For an algebra-inside-physics problem, the mid band is usually sufficient: the work is practice on a narrow skill and does not require deep familiarity with the Diploma's assessment. For an uncertainty and data-analysis problem, the specialist band earns its premium, because the published expectations are precise and a tutor who has not marked against them tends to teach uncertainty as recipes rather than as reasoning. For investigation design coaching, the same applies.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages circulating in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. All of those are the providers' own published figures rather than ours.

The shape that works for physics specifically is a short data-analysis and uncertainty block early, because it pays in both the papers and the investigation, then investigation coaching at the design stage, then weekly paper work in the final year. That is front-loaded compared with how most families buy, and it is cheaper overall because the uncertainty work done once keeps paying.

sections.heading: Teaching a laboratory subject over video
paragraphs: Physics raises the reasonable question of whether a laboratory subject can be taught remotely. The answer depends on what is actually being assessed. The written papers test physics reasoning, mathematics and data analysis, none of which requires apparatus. The investigation requires apparatus, and the student has access to it at school; what they usually lack is help with the design decisions and the uncertainty treatment, both of which are conversations rather than procedures.

In practice an online session suits physics well. The working is visible line by line on a shared surface, graphs can be plotted and read together, a data set can be annotated on screen, and the data booklet is open in front of both parties. For data-analysis work it is at least as good as sitting side by side, and for uncertainty propagation it is better, because the derivation stays on screen rather than being rubbed out.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Al Khail Gate or anywhere else in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. The published in-home band in Dubai is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 online, and the difference largely reflects the journey.

The selection point matters particularly here. Physics Higher Level cohorts in Dubai are small, and a student with a specific gap in a Higher Level extension topic needs somebody who teaches that content regularly. Within a short drive of Al Khail Gate that person may not exist; online they teach it weekly. For long sessions, full timed papers and investigation work, weekend mornings are the realistic slot given the Al Khail corridor commute.

faqs.question: My son understands physics but his marks are low. What is actually wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three things that all look like a physics problem on a report. Algebra: he writes the right relationship and the next line is wrong, which is a rearrangement failure. Measurement: he loses a consistent block of marks in data-analysis questions because uncertainty handling was never taught properly. Timing: the last questions are blank rather than wrong. A marked script distinguishes them in about forty minutes, and two of the three are considerably faster to fix than teaching content again.

faqs.question: What is linearisation and why does it matter in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: It is rearranging a physical relationship so that plotting the right transformed quantities gives a straight line, whose gradient or intercept is the constant you want. A power law plotted raw gives a curve from which nothing precise can be read. The skill has three parts: deciding what goes on each axis, plotting accurately with a sensible scale, and reading the gradient from the line of best fit rather than from two data points. It appears in the papers and again in the investigation.

faqs.question: How do uncertainties propagate in physics calculations?
faqs.answer: Adding or subtracting quantities adds their absolute uncertainties, which is why designs resting on a small difference between two large measurements are fragile. Multiplying or dividing adds their fractional uncertainties, so the worst-measured quantity dominates. Raising to a power multiplies the fractional uncertainty by that power, which means a quantity appearing squared dominates the uncertainty in the result. Understanding that last point lets a student write a real evaluation identifying which measurement to improve, rather than a generic comment.

faqs.question: Does my child need to memorise physics equations for the IB?
faqs.answer: Far fewer than most students assume, because every IB physics examination supplies a data booklet with the relationships and constants. The useful revision is knowing what is in it, where it sits, and which relationship applies to which situation. Half an hour spent annotating the booklet against the syllabus removes the commonest time loss in a paper, a student turning pages while the clock runs, and usually reveals relationships they had been memorising unnecessarily.

faqs.question: What makes a good research question for a physics investigation?
faqs.answer: One where the dependent variable changes measurably across a range the student can actually achieve with school apparatus. The commonest failure is a question where the measured quantity barely moves, which makes meaningful analysis impossible however carefully the data are collected. A quick preliminary run before committing is worth more than any amount of careful write-up afterwards. The second requirement is that every instrument's uncertainty can be estimated, because a result without an uncertainty cannot reach the top evaluation criteria.

faqs.question: Why did my daughter lose evaluation marks when her experiment worked?
faqs.answer: Because the evaluation criteria reward something more specific than a list of things that went wrong. The published expectations want the student to identify which measurement contributed most to the uncertainty in the final result, explain why it dominated, and propose a specific improvement that would reduce it. That follows from understanding propagation: a quantity appearing squared dominates. A generic paragraph about human error and more repeats scores in the lower bands even after a well-executed experiment.

faqs.question: How can a physics practical be supported if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The apparatus is at school and the student has access to it; what they usually lack is help with the design decisions and the uncertainty treatment, and both are conversations rather than procedures. An online session suits that well: the data set is annotated on screen, graphs are plotted and read together, and the uncertainty derivation stays visible rather than being rubbed out. The written papers test reasoning, mathematics and data analysis, none of which needs apparatus at all.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a physics tutor to Al Khail Gate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address anywhere in the Emirates. All UAE lessons are one-to-one and live over video on Gulf Standard Time. For physics the online pool matters because Higher Level cohorts in Dubai are small: a tutor teaching the Higher Level extension content weekly may not exist within a short drive of this community.

faqs.question: My son was fine in Year 12 physics and is struggling now. Why?
faqs.answer: Most likely a gap in the Higher Level extension content, which arrives later in the two years and is taught faster because the shared material came first. The habits that break are specific: qualitative reasoning that worked for the shared content is insufficient once fields, circular motion and oscillations are treated quantitatively with multi-variable algebra. The diagnosis takes one session: list the extension topics from the syllabus and have him attempt one timed question on each.

faqs.question: Is Physics Higher Level necessary for engineering?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and it should be checked against actual entry requirements rather than assumed. Many engineering and physical sciences programmes expect Physics and Mathematics at Higher Level, often Mathematics Analysis and Approaches specifically. Read the requirements of several plausible universities in term one of Year 12, while a level change is still administratively possible. A student carrying three demanding Higher Levels who is struggling in all of them has a load problem rather than a physics problem, and that is a different conversation.

faqs.question: How much should we pay for IB Physics tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends which problem you are buying help for. For rearrangement practice or graph technique the qualified band is sufficient, published at AED 150 to 300 an hour with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. For uncertainty, data analysis and investigation coaching the specialist band earns its premium, at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase around AED 270. Budget providers advertise from around AED 33 to 65. In-home is AED 180 to 500 with travel included. All published by the providers themselves.

faqs.question: What should a physics tutoring plan look like across two years?
faqs.answer: Front-loaded, which is the opposite of how most families buy. A short uncertainty and data-analysis block in Year 12, because it pays in both the papers and the investigation. Investigation design coaching before data collection, when the ceiling is still open. Then weekly paper work through Year 13 on whichever of the three skills the scripts say is failing. That sequence costs less in total than a Year 13 scramble and includes the two interventions a scramble cannot deliver.

faqs.question: Does the calculator matter in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: Less than in mathematics and more than students expect. The IB specifies permitted graphical display calculator models, and the recurring loss in physics is the angle mode: a calculator left in degrees for a question set in radians produces a wrong answer from a correct method. The other issue is speed with scientific notation across multi-step calculations. An hour of model-specific practice removes both, and almost nobody schedules it deliberately.

faqs.question: When do Dubai IB students sit physics exams?
faqs.answer: UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and we publish no specific examination or results dates on these pages. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family plans around has to be right. Confirm the window and the results dates with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge qualifications sat alongside, UAE centres sit the June and November series.

faqs.question: Our only free evening is Wednesday. What happens if nobody covers HL physics then?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a generalist. Higher Level physics is a narrow specialism and demand peaks across the city in the same weeks before a session, so a specific level at a specific hour does occasionally come up empty. The options are a different time, a different tutor with a handover of the diagnostic notes, or a wait with a date attached. A tutor unfamiliar with what Higher Level examines will teach the shared content well and miss the extension gap that is actually causing the problem.
