intro.heading: Does anybody near here know the Physics course my child is actually taking?
paragraphs: That is the real question behind a search for a Physics tutor in Al Khawaneej, and it has an unusually specific answer in this subject. Diploma Physics has been revised: the content is organised into themes rather than the older topic-and-option arrangement, experimental technique, technology and mathematics are treated as assessed tools running through the course, and the examination components are not structured as they once were. A tutor who learned the previous version will teach correct physics against a map that no longer matches your child's.

This is not a minor administrative difference. It changes which material belongs together, what a paper expects, and in some cases whether a component a tutor remembers preparing candidates for still exists in the same form. A student can spend a term being well taught and still be surprised by the shape of the examination, which is the most dispiriting way to lose marks that exists.

The second part of the problem is supply, and it is worse in Physics than in almost any other subject. A Dubai secondary school running the Diploma typically has one or two staff able to teach Physics confidently at Higher Level, because the group is small and the content demands it, and those people are employed full time. Al Khawaneej itself holds primary provision and a Dubai Schools campus; its secondary students travel out. The number of people living within a short drive of this community who teach the current Physics course is, realistically, very small. Ask the school how many staff teach it at Higher Level and the local picture becomes clear in one reply.

Put the two together and a local search in this catchment tends to produce approximate matches: a competent science teacher who does not specialise in Physics, a Physics teacher who learned the older course, or an undergraduate who sat the subject recently and has never read a mark scheme as a marker. None of those is dishonest. They are what a distance filter leaves behind, and the only move that genuinely widens the set is removing the distance filter.

That is what IB Gram does: matching on the subject, the level and the current guide, with teaching delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. The rest of this page is the syllabus detail you need in order to judge any tutor, including ours, and the questions that reveal in a few minutes whether somebody knows this course or an older one. None of it requires you to understand the physics; it requires you to know which questions produce a revealing answer.

sections.heading: The tutor who learned the old course
paragraphs: This is the specific risk in Physics, and it is invisible for several weeks. The Diploma Physics guide has been revised, and the revision was not cosmetic: content is now organised into themes rather than the older arrangement of numbered topics plus an option, the assessment components are structured differently, and experimental technique, technology use and mathematical skill are treated as tools running through the whole course rather than as separate add-ons.

A tutor who prepared candidates under the previous guide and has not taught the subject since knows the physics perfectly well. What they do not know is where it now sits, which material is examined together, what a given paper asks for, and whether a component they remember still exists in the same form. The teaching will be good and the preparation will be aimed at a target that has moved. Students notice this first in mock papers, by which point a term has gone.

The remedy is a question rather than a judgement. Ask any prospective tutor when they last prepared a candidate for Diploma Physics and how the course is organised now. A specialist will describe the themes and the tools without hesitation and will refer you to the school's current subject guide as the authority. Somebody working from older material will describe numbered topics and an option. Neither answer is shameful; only one of them is a match for your child. The table below gives the questions and what the answers tell you.

sections.heading: The themes, and what each one actually demands
paragraphs: Organising Physics by theme rather than by numbered topic is not merely a relabelling. It groups material that shares an underlying idea, which means a student who understands the idea travels well across the theme and a student who has memorised examples does not. The practical consequence for tutoring is that the diagnosis has to find the idea that is missing rather than the lesson that was absent.

Motion and space-time demands confident handling of vectors and of rate, and it is where the gap between understanding a graph and extracting a value from it first shows. The particulate nature of matter demands moving fluently between the microscopic picture and the measurable quantity. Wave behaviour demands holding a geometric picture and an algebraic relationship at once. Fields demands reasoning about something with no visible cause, which is where recitation fails most visibly. Nuclear and quantum physics demands accepting a probabilistic account and reasoning inside it rather than looking for a mechanical analogy.

The table pairs each theme with the misconception that most often sits underneath a lost mark, and with what a session should actually do about it. The reason this is more useful than a list of topics is that the misconceptions are durable: a student who believes a field is a force rather than a property of space will keep producing the same class of wrong answer across several themes until somebody names it. That naming is what a Physics specialist does and what a general science tutor usually cannot.

sections.heading: The papers do different jobs, and a revision plan should notice
paragraphs: Confirm the current component structure and weightings with your child's Diploma coordinator, because the school's own documentation is the authority and these arrangements have changed. What is stable, and what families consistently miss, is that the written components reward different behaviours and that revising for one does not prepare a student for the others.

A multiple-choice section rewards speed and the fast elimination of a wrong option, and it punishes a student who spends four minutes on the hardest item and then rushes eight easy ones. A data-based section rewards careful reading of a graph or table and the ability to write a conclusion that names a relationship and attaches an uncertainty to it. An extended-response component rewards a visible chain of reasoning in which the physics is made explicit rather than assumed. Those are three different skills, and a student who has only revised content has practised none of them.

There is a practical test a parent can run without knowing any physics. Ask your child how long they should spend on a single multiple-choice item, and what they do if they are still stuck after that long. A student with an answer has been taught to sit the paper. A student without one has been taught the content and left to work out the examination for themselves, which is the most common gap in otherwise well-taught Physics candidates in this catchment. Fixing it costs a session, and it is not a content problem at all.
bullets: Confirm current component structure with the Diploma coordinator

sections.heading: Three things a Physics specialist sees in a marked script
paragraphs: Hand the same marked Physics paper to a general science tutor and to a Physics specialist and you get two different readings. The general tutor explains the correct physics for each wrong answer. The specialist reads the pattern, and there are three things they look for first, none of which is about content knowledge.

The first is precision that the instrument could not support. An answer quoted to five figures from a measurement made with a metre rule tells an examiner that the candidate does not understand what their apparatus can know, and it loses marks in a question the student otherwise answered. The second is the order in which graph work was done: error bars added after the line of best fit rather than before it, which inverts the logic of the whole exercise and shows up again in every gradient and conclusion that follows. The third is explanation questions answered descriptively, where the student has stated what happened and never accounted for why.

All three are mechanical, all three are independent of theme, and all three are fixable within a handful of sessions. That is why a specialist usually starts there rather than with whichever theme the student named. It also explains why a family can buy months of competent content teaching and see the grade barely move: the content was never the binding constraint. For an Al Khawaneej family with limited evening hours, finding the binding constraint quickly is the whole point of paying for a specialist rather than a generalist.
bullets: Impossible precision: the instrument limits the answer, not the calculator
Error bars drawn before the line, never after it
Explanation questions that describe rather than account for a result
All three are theme-independent and fixable in a few sessions

sections.heading: The assessed tools: technique, technology and mathematics
paragraphs: One of the clearer improvements in the current Physics course is that experimental technique, the use of technology and mathematical skill are treated as things the course teaches and assesses rather than as background competences a student is assumed to arrive with. For tutoring this is useful, because it makes explicit what good teachers always knew: a large share of Physics marks are lost in these three areas rather than in the physics.

Experimental technique means knowing how to choose an instrument, read it to an appropriate precision, identify what will vary and what must be controlled, and judge whether enough repeats have been taken. These skills are assessed in written questions about experiments the candidate did not perform, which makes them learnable without a laboratory and highly responsive to deliberate practice.

Technology means handling data and representations competently, including producing and interpreting graphs and using software or a calculator efficiently under time pressure. Mathematics means the algebra, trigonometry, logarithms and proportional reasoning that sit inside Physics questions. Most Physics difficulty that families describe as conceptual turns out, on inspection of a script, to be one of these three. Twenty minutes a week of pure rearrangement practice with no physics context remains the single highest-return intervention available in the subject, and it improves Chemistry calculations at no extra cost. The practical instruction for a family with limited evening time is to attack the tools before the themes, because the tools are assessed in every theme and the themes are assessed only when they appear.

sections.heading: Fields and quantum physics: where recitation stops working
paragraphs: Two themes expose memorisation more ruthlessly than the others, and they are the ones Higher Level candidates in this catchment most often name when asked what they find hard. Fields asks a student to reason about a property of space with no visible cause. Quantum and nuclear physics asks them to reason inside a probabilistic account rather than to find a mechanical picture that behaves the way they expect.

A student who has memorised relationships will answer confidently on familiar configurations and collapse on anything rephrased. The classic diagnostic is a question with no numbers in it: why is the field inside a hollow conductor zero, what happens to the potential as you move between two like charges, why does a particular decay produce the spectrum it does. A candidate holding the underlying idea can reason towards an answer. A candidate holding memorised results has nothing to deploy.

This is slow work and it does not respond to cramming, which is the argument for addressing it in the first year rather than the revision term. In a session it looks like being asked to predict before any equation appears, and then to justify the prediction. Students find it uncomfortable for a few weeks because it exposes precisely where the understanding stops, and that exposure is the point. It is also something a small Higher Level class cannot safely do to one student in front of their peers, which is one of the better arguments for one-to-one teaching in this subject.

sections.heading: The investigation, and what a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Every Diploma Physics candidate produces an independent scientific investigation, assessed against published criteria, and it must be the student's own work. Stating the boundary in both directions is more useful than asserting integrity in general terms, so here it is. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards. A tutor may ask whether a research question can be measured with the apparatus the school actually has. A tutor may point out that a plan produces too few data points to show a trend, that the uncertainty treatment is thin, or that an evaluation lists limitations without ranking them.

A tutor may not write the investigation or any section of it, rewrite the student's sentences into their own voice, supply the data, or hand over a method the student then adopts without understanding. There are operators in this market selling completed Internal Assessments outright. A student who submits one risks their whole Diploma, and that risk does not expire when the document is accepted. IB Gram will not produce assessed work at any price, and the same line applies to the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay.

Most investigation marks are lost at the start rather than in the writing, which is why coaching early is worth several times coaching late. An ambitious question that yields four data points cannot be rescued by careful prose. A narrow question with one clearly measurable independent variable and enough repeats to show a trend can be written up by an average writer and score well. Narrowing the question is the single most valuable hour in the whole project, and it is the hour students resist hardest because narrowing feels like abandoning the interesting version.

sections.heading: Starting, and the availability we disclose in advance
paragraphs: Send three things. The most recent marked Physics paper with the teacher's comments intact. The level your child sits and the theme the class is currently covering. And the realistic weekday time your child is genuinely able to work, which for a student travelling home to Al Khawaneej from Mirdif, Al Warqa or Al Qusais is later than families expect.

Then a free trial lesson, one-to-one over live video. Use the questions from this page during it: how the course is organised now, when they last prepared a candidate, what the assessed tools are. Then ask them to read the marked script and say what the pattern is. If the answer names measurement discipline, graph order or descriptive explanation rather than listing topics to revise, you have found a specialist. If the hour is spent on their background, you have learned something about the provider instead.

The disclosure, stated before you ask for it. Higher Level Physics specialists are among the scarcest teaching commodities in this emirate, and there are genuinely weeks when no UAE-based specialist holds an evening slot that fits an Al Khawaneej timetable. Where that is the case you will be told, and offered a specialist based elsewhere teaching the same course on the current guide over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time. What will not happen is a general science tutor being presented as a Physics specialist because a slot needed filling. No competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: How do I know whether a Physics tutor knows the current IB course?
faqs.answer: Ask how the course is organised now and when they last prepared a candidate. A current specialist describes the content as themes with experimental technique, technology and mathematics as assessed tools running through them, and points you to your school's own subject guide as the authority. Somebody working from older material describes numbered topics plus a chosen option. Neither answer is shameful, but only one matches the course your child is taking, and the mismatch stays invisible until mock papers.

faqs.question: Why is a Higher Level Physics tutor so hard to find near Al Khawaneej?
faqs.answer: Arithmetic rather than bad luck. A Dubai secondary school running the Diploma usually has one or two staff able to teach Physics confidently at Higher Level, because the group is small and the content requires it, and those people are employed full time. Al Khawaneej holds primary provision and a Dubai Schools campus rather than a large secondary Physics cohort. Add a requirement for weekday evening availability and proximity, and the set of candidates is frequently one person or none.

faqs.question: What does a Physics specialist notice that a general science tutor misses?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is content. Answers quoted to a precision the instrument could not support, which loses marks on otherwise correct work. Graph questions where the error bars were added after the line of best fit rather than before it, inverting the logic and affecting every gradient and conclusion that follows. And explanation questions answered descriptively, stating what happened without accounting for why. All three are theme-independent, all three are mechanical, and all three are fixable in a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: Which Physics theme causes the most difficulty?
faqs.answer: Fields, usually, because it asks a student to reason about a property of space with no visible cause, and memorised relationships collapse the moment a configuration is rephrased. Quantum and nuclear physics is a close second for the same reason: students look for a mechanical analogy that behaves the way they expect, and there is not one. The best diagnostic in both is a question with no numbers in it, which reveals immediately whether the student holds the idea or a set of results.

faqs.question: What are the assessed tools in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: Experimental technique, the use of technology, and mathematical skill. The current course treats them as things it teaches and assesses rather than as competences a student is assumed to arrive with, which is a genuine improvement because it names where most marks are actually lost. Technique covers instrument choice, precision, variable control and judging repeats. Technology covers data handling and representation. Mathematics covers the algebra and trigonometry inside Physics questions, which is where most apparently conceptual difficulty turns out to live.

faqs.question: How should my child prepare for the multiple-choice section?
faqs.answer: By practising the behaviour rather than the content. The section rewards pace and fast elimination of wrong options, and punishes a candidate who spends four minutes on the hardest item and then rushes eight easy ones. The practical test a parent can run is to ask your child how long they should spend on a single item and what they do if still stuck. A student with an answer has been taught to sit the paper. A student without one has been taught the content and left to work out the exam alone.

faqs.question: Can a tutor coach the Physics investigation legitimately?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a line worth stating in both directions. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, ask whether a research question can be measured with the school's actual apparatus, say that a plan yields too few data points, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any section, rewrite the student's sentences, supply the data, or provide a method the student does not understand. Operators selling completed Internal Assessments exist, and submitting one risks the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: When should the investigation work start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most students begin, because the marks are lost at the start rather than in the writing. An ambitious question producing four data points cannot be rescued by careful prose, while a narrow question with one clearly measurable variable and enough repeats to show a trend can be written up by an average writer and score well. Narrowing the question is the single most valuable hour in the project and the one students resist hardest, since narrowing feels like abandoning the interesting version of the idea.

faqs.question: My child is strong in maths and weak in Physics. Why?
faqs.answer: Two patterns produce that combination. The first is measurement discipline: a student can solve the algebra flawlessly and lose marks for quoting an impossible precision or omitting an uncertainty, which is a Physics-specific habit rather than a mathematical one. The second is explanation: Physics asks for a chain of reasoning in words, and strong mathematicians often give the calculation and stop. Both are diagnosable from one marked script and both respond quickly, which makes this a cheaper problem to fix than it first appears.

faqs.question: Does my child need Physics at Higher Level for engineering?
faqs.answer: Check the specific programme at the specific institution, because requirements vary and change. Engineering faculties commonly expect Physics and a mathematics subject at Higher Level, and some name Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation. Read the admissions page for the exact degree, note what it names, and plan the Diploma choices backwards from that. A tutor can help with the Physics; the entry requirement itself should come from the university rather than from any tutoring provider.

faqs.question: Is online teaching workable for a subject with practical work?
faqs.answer: For the written assessment of experimental skills, yes, and arguably better than the alternative. The questions ask about experiments the candidate did not perform, testing variable identification, precision, anomaly explanation and method improvement, all of which are learnable without apparatus and respond strongly to deliberate practice. A shared whiteboard with the student's own script and graphs on screen covers the working methods the subject needs. The school supplies the laboratory work; tutoring supplies the discipline around interpreting and writing about it.

faqs.question: How many Physics sessions a week does a Higher Level student here need?
faqs.answer: One, placed well, plus practice between sessions that actually happens. Two short sessions on separate evenings beat a single long block for Physics, because the subject needs repeated practice at starting questions rather than extended explanation. For a student travelling home to Al Khawaneej from Al Qusais or Al Warqa, the binding constraint is attention rather than hours, so a weekend morning generally outperforms a second tired weekday evening by a clear margin.

faqs.question: Where should we get Physics past papers and the current subject guide?
faqs.answer: From your child's school, which holds the current guide and the material it is entitled to use, and from the board's own published pages. Files circulating in parent groups are frequently from the previous version of the course, and an outdated guide is worse than none because it looks authoritative and quietly misplaces whole sections of content. IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables.

faqs.question: What should an Al Khawaneej family send before a first Physics session?
faqs.answer: Three things. The most recent marked Physics paper with the teacher's comments left on, which is where any real diagnosis comes from. The level sat and the theme the class is currently covering, so the session connects to this week rather than to a generic syllabus order. intro.heading: Knowing physics and knowing this physics course are different things
paragraphs: A parent in Al Mamzar searching for a physics tutor will find people who know physics. That is not the scarce thing. The scarce thing is someone who knows the specific Diploma course your child is entered for, which was restructured and is now organised into five themes rather than the longer topic list older tutors trained on. The themes are space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. A tutor who still talks about mechanics, thermal physics and waves as separate units is describing a guide that is no longer the one being examined.

The assessment has changed with it. Paper 1 is now split into two parts sat together: Paper 1A is multiple choice, and Paper 1B is a data-analysis section built around experimental results. Paper 2 carries short and extended response questions. The internal component is a single scientific investigation rather than several practical write-ups, worth a fifth of the grade and marked on four criteria. Each of those is a distinct skill, and a student can be strong at two and weak at the others while a report simply says "physics: 4".

Al Mamzar's geography makes the matching problem worse rather than better. The neighbourhood is residential, the nearest schools offering the Diploma are in the Al Garhoud cluster, and Higher Level physics is a minority entry even there. The pool of people within a short drive who have taught the current Higher Level course to examinations is, realistically, close to empty. Choosing a tutor by distance in this situation means choosing by availability of a car rather than by knowledge of a syllabus.

IB Gram does not place tutors at addresses in Al Mamzar or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are offered only in India. Physics is taught live, one-to-one, over video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own marked work on screen, and data sets worked through together. For a subject whose hardest marks sit in graph interpretation and uncertainty propagation, a shared screen is arguably better than a kitchen table, because both parties are looking at the same axes at the same time.

What follows is the detail a parent needs to interview a physics tutor properly: the structure of the current course, how the papers are weighted, what the investigation is marked on, the specific places Diploma students lose physics marks, how the year counts backwards, and what Dubai tutors charge in AED. Every claim here is checkable against the school, the published guide or the named source, and a parent who takes nothing else away should at least leave able to ask a tutor which themes they have taught and how they mark an extended response.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what changed from the course parents remember
paragraphs: The current Diploma physics guide is organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level students cover additional material within those same themes rather than a separate list of options. Anyone being considered as a tutor should be able to name them without prompting.

The reorganisation matters because it changed emphasis, not just labels. Treating fields as a single theme, for instance, pushes gravitational, electric and magnetic fields together and invites questions that move between them inside one extended response. A student taught the older separate-topic structure will have the content but not the habit of connecting it, and the extended-response marks sit exactly in that connection. Similarly, putting the particulate nature of matter into one theme ties thermal behaviour to gas laws and to the structure of matter in a way the earlier arrangement did not.

The second change is the internal assessment. Instead of several practical write-ups accumulated over two years, there is one scientific investigation, which the student designs and carries out, worth a fifth of the final grade. That concentrates risk: a poorly chosen research question is no longer diluted by other work. It also concentrates opportunity, because a student with months to work on a single piece has more control over that fifth of their grade than over any paper.

For a parent interviewing tutors in Al Mamzar, the practical test is simple. Ask which themes the student has covered so far and listen to whether the tutor uses the theme names fluently or translates them back into older topic headings. The second answer is not disqualifying - good physicists adapt - but it tells you how recently that person has taught this course, which is the thing you are actually trying to find out.

sections.heading: How the physics papers are weighted, and why Paper 1B is the one nobody practises
paragraphs: Diploma physics is assessed by two external papers plus the internal investigation. Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade, Paper 2 carries 44%, and the scientific investigation carries the remaining 20% at both Standard and Higher Level. Paper 1 is sat in two parts in one sitting: Paper 1A is multiple choice across the whole course, and Paper 1B is a data-analysis section built on experimental results. Higher Level papers are longer and carry more extended-response weight within Paper 2.

Paper 1B is the component students meet least and lose most on. It asks for the things nobody practises in a normal homework cycle: identifying the independent and dependent variables in someone else's experiment, deciding what to plot to get a straight line, reading a gradient and saying what it physically represents, propagating an uncertainty, and judging whether a conclusion is supported by the spread of the data. A student can know every equation in the course and score poorly here.

Paper 1A rewards a different skill again: speed and elimination. Students lose marks by doing full algebra on questions designed to be answered by inspecting units or spotting a proportionality. Practising multiple choice as a timed skill, with a rule about when to abandon a question and come back, is worth more in the final weeks than another pass through the content.

Paper 2 is where the marks are concentrated and where command terms decide the outcome. "State" wants one line. "Describe" wants what happens. "Explain" wants why, in terms of physics, and an answer that describes without explaining loses the explain marks even when every fact in it is correct. Marking a student's own answers against the published command-term definitions, rather than against a model answer, is the fastest route to those marks.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria and where a tutor must stop
paragraphs: The investigation is marked on four criteria - research design, data analysis, conclusion, and evaluation - each worth six marks, giving twenty-four in total. It is worth a fifth of the physics grade and is capped in length, so it rewards precision rather than volume. Students who understand the criteria write a different report from students who do not, and most students have never read them.

Research design is where the grade is usually decided, because it is where a project becomes answerable or does not. A research question that names the independent variable, the dependent variable and the controlled variables explicitly is already most of the way to the marks. One that asks a broad question about a phenomenon invites a report that measures something interesting and concludes nothing specific. Data analysis then rewards correct uncertainty treatment, sensible processing, and graphs that are actually readable - labelled axes, units, error bars where they belong.

Conclusion and evaluation are the two most under-written sections in every cohort. A conclusion has to state what the data shows, compare it to the accepted physics where that is possible, and address whether the relationship found is the one expected. Evaluation has to identify specific weaknesses with their effect on the result, not a list of generic improvements. "More repeats would improve reliability" earns little; naming the dominant source of uncertainty and explaining how it skewed the gradient earns more.

The boundary on help is firm. A tutor may teach any physics the student needs, discuss whether a design will produce usable data, explain uncertainty propagation, point at a criterion by name, and give feedback on a draft. A tutor never writes the report, never supplies data, and never edits the prose to completion. Under IB academic-honesty rules the consequence of crossing that line falls on the student, which is a far worse outcome than a mediocre mark.

sections.heading: Where Diploma physics students in Deira schools actually lose marks
paragraphs: The pattern across the cohorts near Al Mamzar is consistent and it is mostly procedural rather than conceptual. Students understand the physics and lose the marks in the writing of it.

Uncertainties lead the list. Absolute and percentage uncertainty, how they combine through a multiplication and through a power, and how many significant figures a final answer may legitimately carry. Students who have never been taught this properly lose marks in Paper 1B and again in the investigation, which is a double cost. Units follow close behind: a numerically correct answer with a missing or wrong unit is a lost mark, and in a paper with twenty such answers that adds up quickly.

Then come graph skills. Deciding what to plot so that a relationship becomes linear, drawing a line of best fit by judgement rather than through the first and last points, and interpreting a gradient and an intercept as physical quantities rather than as numbers. Fourth, command terms in extended responses, where "explain" answers that describe lose marks the student had the knowledge to earn. Fifth, algebraic rearranging under time pressure, which is a mathematics gap presenting as a physics problem - students on Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation are more exposed to it.

A first diagnostic session should produce a written list naming which of those this particular student loses marks to. The list then drives the hours. Without it, tuition becomes a pleasant second explanation of whatever the school taught that week, which is the most common way for a physics hour to feel useful and change nothing.

sections.heading: Al Mamzar's supply problem, stated honestly
paragraphs: There is no large pool of current-syllabus Diploma physics specialists living in Al Mamzar, and a parent restricting the search to a short driving radius is choosing from a handful of people. That is the honest answer to "is there a physics tutor near me", and it is why IB Gram teaches every UAE booking live over video instead of sending anybody to an address.

The arithmetic behind it is straightforward. Dubai has 227 private schools across seventeen curricula, and the International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7% of private-school enrolment in the emirate. Only a minority of the schools near Al Mamzar offer the Diploma at all. Within those, physics is a smaller cohort than mathematics or English, and Higher Level physics smaller again. Multiply those filters and the number of people within fifteen minutes of the Corniche who have taught the current Higher Level course to final examinations is not a pool, it is a coincidence.

Distance also buys less than parents expect. The properties that move a physics grade are knowing the current guide, marking against command terms, and being able to teach uncertainty propagation clearly. None of them correlate with where a tutor lives. What distance does buy is presence in the room, and the market charges for it: in-home visits in Dubai are quoted at AED 180-500 an hour including travel, against online specialist bands starting lower for equivalent expertise.

The remaining constraint is the hour itself. In this neighbourhood that usually means after 4.15pm on a school day, and later where a parent is driving back through the Sharjah-bound traffic. Online delivery makes the hour the only constraint, which is the point. We do not offer home visits in the UAE at all; that service exists only in India.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs in this part of Dubai, in AED
paragraphs: Looking at the cheapest band first makes the market easier to read. Tutopiya advertises online tuition from around AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both at the university-student end. That band is genuinely useful for homework supervision and is the wrong place to look for Higher Level physics with a data-analysis component. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour, TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work, and Bestimate's Dubai research puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200-450 and above. BartyED advertises AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Packages observed in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. The second figure buys the same number of hours for roughly double, and the difference is travel across Dubai at the worst time of day.

Where physics money is most often wasted: paying a specialist rate for content a cheaper tutor could cover, buying a block of hours before anyone has diagnosed what the student is losing marks to, and starting investigation support after the school's internal deadline has already passed. The third is the most expensive, because the investigation is a fifth of the grade and the only component where months of lead time exist.

These are market figures from the named sources, read in October 2026, and not IB Gram's price list. Our own arrangement begins with a free trial lesson and a written diagnosis, and the number of hours recommended afterwards is whatever the diagnosis supports rather than whatever a package contains.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators, and the questions worth asking before you pay
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is permitted rather than unregulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private lessons without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so a specific amount quoted to you is unverified. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, completed through its app, website or e-services.

Schools themselves sit under a different authority. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued specifically to training institutes with premises. IB Gram holds no such permit, has no UAE centre, and claims no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA or the IB.

There is also a rule worth knowing about teachers. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics requirements, as reported in the press, bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that restricts the same thing. That is reported rather than quoted here, and worth verifying against the current policy document, but the direction is clear: your child's own physics teacher is not the right person to engage privately.

Four questions then settle most of a physics booking. Which level and which themes have you taught to final examinations? How do you mark an extended response, and will I see where the explain marks went? How do you teach uncertainty propagation? And what will you refuse to do with the scientific investigation? A tutor who answers the fourth crisply, without being pushed, is usually the one to book.

faqs.answer: Four criteria - research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation - each worth six marks, twenty-four in total, making up a fifth of the final grade. Research design usually decides the outcome, because a question with the independent, dependent and controlled variables named is answerable and a broad one is not. Conclusion and evaluation are the most under-written sections in every cohort: a conclusion must compare the result to accepted physics, and an evaluation must name a specific weakness and its effect rather than ask for more repeats.

faqs.question: How much harder is IB Physics at Higher Level than at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level covers the same five themes with additional material inside each, longer papers and more extended-response weight, so the difference is depth and stamina rather than a separate syllabus. The skills that trouble students - uncertainty, graph interpretation, command terms - are identical at both levels because the data-analysis section and the investigation are common. A student struggling at Standard Level will not be rescued by dropping down if the problem is those shared skills, and that is worth diagnosing before any level change is discussed with the school.

faqs.question: My son keeps losing physics marks on uncertainties. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most reliably recoverable losses in the subject. The content is small: absolute and percentage uncertainty, how uncertainties combine through multiplication, division and powers, and how many significant figures a final answer may legitimately carry. Taught as one deliberate block with a dozen worked examples, most students have it within two or three sessions. The payoff is doubled, because it earns marks in the data-analysis section of Paper 1 and again in the data-analysis criterion of the scientific investigation.

faqs.question: Does IB Physics Higher Level require Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Not formally, and students do take Higher Level physics alongside Applications and Interpretation. The practical issue is that physics assumes confident algebraic rearranging rather than teaching it, so a student whose mathematics course drills modelling and statistics instead of manipulation can lose physics marks for mathematical reasons. Where that combination is in place, the sensible fix is explicit algebra practice inside the physics hour rather than extra physics content. Check the specific prerequisites of any degree course you have in mind, since departments differ.

faqs.question: Can my child do the physics practical work if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The practical work belongs to the school, and that is where the equipment and the supervision are. A tutor's role is the thinking around it: whether a research question is answerable with the apparatus available, how to plan the data collection, how to treat uncertainty, how to plot for a linear relationship, and what the gradient means. All of that is better done on a shared screen than at a table, because both people are looking at the same axes. The student collects their own data and writes their own report.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 'explain' and 'describe' in an IB Physics answer?
faqs.answer: "Describe" asks what happens; "explain" asks why, in terms of physics. An answer that correctly narrates a process in response to an explain command loses the explanation marks even though every statement in it is true, which is why students who know the content still lose marks on Paper 2. The remedy is mechanical: mark the student's own answers against the published command-term definitions rather than against a model answer, so they see exactly which clause was missing. Most students fix it within a few marked questions.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Mamzar actually offer IB Physics at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: The nearest Diploma provision is in the Al Garhoud and airport-side cluster, which includes schools such as Deira International School, Universal American School Dubai, Dubai English Speaking College and St Mary's Catholic High School. Whether Higher Level physics runs in a given year depends on how many students opt for it, and in smaller cohorts it sometimes does not. Ask the Diploma coordinator directly how many students are in the Higher Level physics group, because a group of four is a different teaching experience from a group of eighteen.

faqs.question: How many hours of physics tuition does a Higher Level student usually need?
faqs.answer: One hour a week is the normal starting point, and it is enough for a student who follows the lesson in class but cannot reproduce it under examination conditions. Two hours is justified where the student has moved curriculum recently, where mathematics is the underlying weakness, or in the final term when Paper 1B and Paper 2 technique are being built in parallel. A short additional block around the scientific investigation is usually better value than permanently increasing the weekly hours, because the investigation has a fixed deadline and a fixed weighting.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics needed for an engineering degree in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Many engineering programmes list physics among their preferred or required subjects, often at Higher Level, but requirements differ between universities and between departments within one university. Read the department's own published entry requirements and confirm them with the admissions office rather than relying on a school summary or a tutoring page. Where physics is required, the mathematics prerequisite usually sits beside it, and the combination of Higher Level physics with Analysis and Approaches is the one most engineering admissions pages recognise immediately.

faqs.question: What do IB Physics tutors charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Rates read in October 2026 split into bands. Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase quotes about AED 270, and Bestimate puts specialist exam-year work at AED 200-450 and above. BartyED advertises AED 650 for a premium named tutor. In-home visits including travel run AED 180-500. Those are market figures from the sources named, not IB Gram's own prices, which begin with a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: My daughter is strong at maths but weak at physics. Why does that happen?
faqs.answer: Usually because physics marks are awarded for explanation rather than for calculation. A student who can manipulate equations fluently may still answer an "explain" question by describing, omit units, read a gradient without saying what it represents, or treat uncertainty as an afterthought. None of those is a mathematics weakness. The fix is not more physics content but deliberate work on how physics answers are constructed and marked, which is why a first diagnostic session should include one extended-response question marked in front of the student.

intro.heading: The afternoon is the constraint, not the physics
paragraphs: Al Manara is a small villa district wedged between Al Wasl Road and Sheikh Zayed Road, with Umm Suqeim on one side and Al Safa on the other. It has no IB school inside its own boundary. Every Diploma student living here travels, and the direction of that travel decides what time a physics session can start. Families who look coastward send children to Raffles World Academy or Kings' School Dubai in Umm Suqeim, or to Jumeirah Baccalaureate School in Al Safa. Families who look inland cross Sheikh Zayed Road towards Dubai American Academy and GEMS Wellington International School. Those two journeys are nothing alike at 3pm, and a tutoring plan that ignores the difference gets cancelled by the third week.

A coastward run is short in distance and awkward in timing. Umm Suqeim is four to six kilometres from most of Al Manara, but the roundabouts on Al Wasl and Jumeirah Beach Road absorb that distance in queues, and a bus that leaves school at 3:05pm can still be dropping at 3:45pm. The inland run is the opposite shape: a longer drive, but on Sheikh Zayed Road and the Al Barsha interchanges, where a bus route with six stops regularly turns a twelve-minute journey into forty. Diploma students on that route are rarely in the door before 4:15pm, and some are closer to 4:40pm.

That matters for physics specifically. Physics is the subject where a tired student produces work that looks like understanding and is not. A Paper 1 multiple-choice set finished at 9:30pm after four hours of other homework tells a tutor almost nothing, because the errors are fatigue errors rather than conceptual ones. Diagnosing where a Higher Level student is actually losing marks needs an hour when they are still able to reason, and in Al Manara that hour is usually 4:45pm to 6:15pm on a coastward schedule and 5:15pm to 6:45pm on an inland one.

Online delivery exists in this plan for a practical reason, not a philosophical one. IB Gram matches physics by component: a tutor who has taught Paper 3 Section B on the optional topic your child's school has chosen, who can mark an uncertainty treatment the way the published criteria mark it. The number of such teachers living within a twenty-minute drive of Al Manara is small, and if the search is restricted to that radius you end up choosing between availability and expertise. Delivered over live video, the radius stops mattering and the finish-time arithmetic becomes the only real constraint. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India.

The rest of this page is written in that order. First the school run and the slots it leaves. Then the Diploma physics course as the school week actually delivers it, the components and their weightings, and the places Al Manara students lose marks most often. Then what the Dubai market charges, what the travel premium buys, and where the scientific investigation ends and academic malpractice begins. Finally the practical mechanics: what to send before the first session, what a KHDA inspection band does and does not tell you, and what happens when the slot you need is not free.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-manara.programmesIntro: An Al Manara family's physics question is nearly always a Diploma question, but the subject starts earlier than DP1 and the schools in both commute directions run different approaches to it. These are the programmes in play for a student living here, and what each means for physics specifically.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is taught as an integrated subject in Years 7 to 9 and usually splits into separate physics, chemistry and biology teaching in Years 10 and 11. Assessment is against four criteria rather than a percentage, which is why a student can carry a 6 in MYP Science and still arrive in DP1 Physics unable to rearrange an equation under time pressure. The criteria reward investigation design and reflection, and those are real skills, but they are not the same skills Paper 1 tests.
programmes.countryNote: Al Manara families usually meet MYP at Raffles World Academy in Umm Suqeim or at Jumeirah Baccalaureate School in Al Safa, both inside the coastward run. Because MYP finishes earlier in the day than the Diploma timetable at the same schools, a Year 10 student from Al Manara is frequently home by 3:30pm, which opens a 4pm slot that no Diploma student in the same household can use.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Diploma Physics is sat at Standard or Higher Level. Both levels share a common core and both are assessed by three written papers plus the scientific investigation, with Higher Level adding additional depth across the themes and a longer Paper 2. Higher Level is a two-year commitment with roughly 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and that difference shows up most in the quantitative work: more algebra, more multi-step problems, less scaffolding in the question stems.
programmes.countryNote: Students from Al Manara sit the Diploma at six or seven schools across the two commute directions, and the schools do not all choose the same Paper 3 optional material. Before any session is booked it is worth asking your child's physics teacher which option the cohort is following, because a tutor matched on the wrong one will be useful for two papers out of three.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools within reach of Al Manara run IGCSE Physics as Cambridge 0625 or Pearson Edexcel 4PH1 before students choose between A Level and the Diploma. The two syllabuses cover similar ground and assess it differently: Cambridge tiers into Core and Extended with an alternative-to-practical option, Pearson examines on two papers with no tiering. Students arriving in DP1 from either route have usually met waves and electricity but not uncertainty propagation.
programmes.countryNote: The inland schools from Al Manara are the IGCSE-heavy ones, and a Year 11 student there sitting 0625 in the June series has a different autumn from a DP1 student at the same address. If both children are in the same house, the IGCSE timetable collapses in April and May while the Diploma one collapses in March, which is useful when booking two slots.

programmes.name: The alternative routes
programmes.description: Several schools in both commute directions offer A Level Physics alongside or instead of the Diploma. A Level is modular in content and assessed entirely externally, with practical endorsement rather than a graded internal task. Families comparing the two for a physics-leaning child should look at what the university target actually asks for: a UK engineering offer will specify A Level grades or Diploma points, and the two are not interchangeable in the way prospectus wording suggests.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence for an Al Manara household is scheduling. A Level Physics students sit papers in a single window and can revise in long blocks; Diploma students carry the scientific investigation through DP1 and into DP2 alongside five other subjects, so their tutoring need is spread thin across eighteen months rather than concentrated in one term.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-manara.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely the only subject in question. A Diploma student from Al Manara who needs physics support usually needs it because of the mathematics underneath it, and the sciences share enough method that one tutor can often cover two. These are the subjects most often requested alongside IB physics in this part of Jumeirah.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Three written papers plus the scientific investigation. Marks go missing in uncertainty treatment, in the extended-response questions on Paper 2 where command terms are ignored, and in the optional topic on Paper 3 that schools teach last and revise least.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual hidden cause of a physics problem. Calculus, logarithms and the manipulation of algebraic expressions appear inside physics questions without warning, and a student weak on AA content loses physics marks that look like physics errors.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics and modelling content maps directly onto the data analysis in the scientific investigation. AI students taking Physics HL need deliberate work on the algebraic side, which their own course does not drill to the same depth.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the quantitative method and the uncertainty rules with physics, which makes a combined booking efficient. Energetics and kinetics in particular use the same graph-reading and gradient skills as mechanics.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Chosen alongside physics by students aiming at biomedical engineering or medicine. The statistical treatment in the biology investigation is more demanding than most students expect, and that is where tutoring hours convert fastest.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Overlaps with physics in materials, structures and energy. Students taking both can usually reuse their understanding of stress, strain and efficiency across the two courses if someone points out the connection.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Logic gates, binary representation and the computational thinking topics sit close to the digital content in physics. HL computer science students taking physics tend to be strong on method and weak on written explanation.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Biomechanics draws on the same force and momentum analysis as DP physics. Students who switch from physics to this subject mid-DP1 need the transition handled carefully, because the assessment structure is not equivalent.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: The four-criterion model rewards investigation design and reflection. Preparing a Year 11 student for DP1 physics means adding the quantitative fluency the criteria do not test: unit conversion, rearrangement and significant figures under time pressure.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Six topic areas across two theory papers plus a practical component. Extended candidates lose most marks on electromagnetic induction and on the longer calculations in Paper 4, where working is required and rarely shown.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two papers, no tiering, with the content split across forces and motion, electricity, waves, energy, magnetism, radioactivity and astrophysics. The astrophysics and radioactivity sections are routinely under-taught and are cheap marks to recover.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Physics students often find the TOK essay harder than the physics. The exhibition and essay reward precise use of knowledge claims, and a science-leaning student usually needs help converting a good instinct into the structure the assessment rewards.

sections.heading: What time a physics session can actually start in Al Manara
paragraphs: A physics session in Al Manara can start at 4:45pm if the school run is coastward and at 5:15pm if it crosses Sheikh Zayed Road. That is the whole answer, and it is the single most useful fact on this page, because almost every tutoring arrangement that collapses in this neighbourhood collapses on timing rather than on teaching.

The arithmetic is simple and nobody does it. School ends between 2:50pm and 3:20pm depending on the school and the year group. A bus with multiple stops adds twenty to forty minutes, and a parent collection adds whatever the Al Wasl Road or Al Barsha interchange queue is doing that afternoon. Then there is the genuinely necessary gap: a Diploma student who walks in at 4:25pm and sits down for physics at 4:30pm will spend the first twenty minutes of a paid hour being tired in front of a stranger.

The table below is built from the two commute directions rather than from an average, because the average is useless here. A coastward family and an inland family living two streets apart have completely different evenings. The right-hand column is the earliest slot that has a reasonable chance of surviving a full term, not the earliest slot that is technically possible.

One further adjustment matters during the winter sports season. Several of the schools in both clusters run after-school activities until 4:30pm or 5pm two days a week, which removes those days from the physics window entirely. It is better to book one reliable session a week than two that are each cancelled monthly.

sections.heading: Diploma physics as the school week actually delivers it
paragraphs: Diploma Physics is assessed by three written papers and one internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 is multiple choice plus data analysis, Paper 2 is structured and extended response, and Paper 3 covers the optional material the school has selected. The internal task carries a fixed share of the final grade at both levels, which means a student can lose a grade boundary on a piece of work submitted months before the papers are sat.

What the published course outline does not show is the order a school delivers it in, and that order is what creates most tutoring problems. Mechanics is taught first, in DP1, when students are still adjusting to the Diploma workload. Electricity and magnetism arrive in the second and third terms. The optional topic is usually taught last, often in the final term of DP2, compressed into a few weeks because the calendar has run out. The result is predictable: the material students know best is the material they met when they were least able to learn it, and the material they met most recently is the material they have practised least.

For a student from Al Manara this has a scheduling consequence. The useful time to work on mechanics and uncertainties is DP1, when the content is live in class and there is room in the week. The useful time to work on the optional topic is the term it is taught, not the revision window, because by then everything is competing with everything. Families who start physics support in DP2 are usually paying to rebuild DP1 foundations while DP2 content arrives on top, and that is twice the work for the same grade movement.

Higher Level adds depth rather than new themes, and the extra teaching hours go mostly into harder quantitative treatment. A Standard Level student who can rearrange an equation and read a gradient is in reasonable shape. A Higher Level student needs to do that under time pressure, across multi-step problems, while tracking units and significant figures, and the gap between those two states is where most of the Higher Level tutoring hours in this neighbourhood go.
bullets: Paper 1: multiple choice and data analysis, no extended writing
Paper 2: structured and extended response, where command terms decide marks
Paper 3: the optional topic, taught last and revised least
The scientific investigation is submitted long before the papers are sat

sections.heading: Where Al Manara physics students lose marks, topic by topic
paragraphs: Three patterns account for most of the lost marks in Diploma physics scripts from this part of Dubai, and none of them is 'not understanding physics'. The first is uncertainty treatment. Students can quote the rules for propagating absolute and percentage uncertainties and still not apply them to their own data, because the rules were taught as a procedure and never as a judgement about how much a measurement can be trusted. In the scientific investigation this costs marks directly. On Paper 1 data-analysis questions it costs marks quietly.

The second is command terms on Paper 2. 'State', 'describe', 'explain', 'discuss' and 'justify' each carry a different expectation about how much reasoning has to be written down, and students who answer every one of them in the same register lose marks on half. An explanation that stops at the correct physical quantity, without the causal step connecting it to the observed effect, reads as complete to the student and incomplete to the mark scheme. This is the single most recoverable category of loss in the subject, and it is recoverable in weeks rather than months.

The third is the optional topic on Paper 3. Because it is taught late and quickly, students arrive at the paper with a shallow version of the material and no bank of worked problems. A Higher Level student who has done ten past-paper questions on the option is in a very different position from one who has read the textbook chapter twice. The fix is unglamorous: timed questions on the option, marked properly, from the term it is taught rather than from April.

Underneath all three sits a mathematics problem that presents as a physics problem. Logarithmic scales, exponential decay, small-angle approximations and the manipulation of compound fractions appear inside physics questions and are assumed knowledge. A student taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation alongside Physics HL meets several of these in physics before meeting them in maths. Naming that out loud usually changes a parent's view of what the tutoring is for.

sections.heading: Standard Level against Higher Level, component by component
paragraphs: Parents in Al Manara ask about the level choice more often than about any single topic, usually in DP1 when a 4 appears on a Higher Level report. The honest answer is that the decision should be made on the university target and on the student's quantitative fluency, not on the current grade, because the current grade in the first term of DP1 reflects adjustment as much as ability.

The practical differences are set out below. Both levels sit three papers and the scientific investigation, and the core content overlaps heavily. What changes is depth, time, and the proportion of questions that require more than one step. Higher Level questions more often ask a student to combine two relationships they were taught separately, which is a different skill from knowing each relationship well.

The university angle is worth checking properly rather than assuming. An engineering or physical-sciences offer from a UK or North American university frequently specifies Higher Level physics or an equivalent, and dropping to Standard Level in DP2 can close a route that looked open in DP1. Medicine is the opposite case: chemistry and biology usually matter more, and Standard Level physics is often sufficient. Ministry of Education equivalency for UAE universities is a separate process again, described further down, and no published IB points threshold for it should be taken on trust from a tutoring website, including this one.

sections.heading: The hour that has to come from somewhere: homework arithmetic
paragraphs: A Diploma student from Al Manara has a finite evening, and adding a physics session to it means something else moves. Pretending otherwise is how a good tutoring plan turns into a tired child. It is worth doing the arithmetic once, openly, before the first booking.

Take an inland commute. Door time 4:25pm. A reasonable restart is 5:15pm after food and a break. Six Diploma subjects generate homework, and in DP2 the scientific investigation, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge generate more. Two to three hours of work is a normal weekday load at this stage, which takes the evening to around 8:15pm with no physics session in it. Insert a sixty-minute session and either the evening runs to 9:15pm or an hour of homework does not happen.

The resolution most Al Manara families land on is to let the session replace homework rather than sit on top of it, and to be explicit with the tutor about that. If the week's physics homework is a problem set, the session works through it and the student finishes the remainder independently. If the week's physics homework is reading, the session replaces it entirely and the reading is caught up at the weekend. This only works if the tutor knows what the school has actually set, which is why the session notes go both ways.

The other resolution is to use the weekend properly. Friday and Saturday allow a ninety-minute session with a timed paper inside it, which is worth more than two weekday hours for exam technique. Families on the inland run in particular find that one weekend session and one short weekday check-in survives a term better than two weekday hours ever does.

sections.heading: What physics support costs in this market, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most families start and it is where the money is most often wasted. A university student tutoring online advertises from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour: EdFlik publishes rates from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to AED 52. At that price a tutor can supervise homework competently. What they generally cannot do is mark a Higher Level Paper 2 extended response against the published criteria and explain why a correct-sounding answer scored two out of four, which is the specific thing a stuck physics grade needs.

A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to AED 300 band; Unitors quotes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Subject specialists in IB, IGCSE and A Level run from roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table showing AED 200 to AED 450 and above. A named or examiner-branded tutor at the top of the market reaches AED 500 to AED 650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Those figures are the providers' own published rates, not IB Gram's, and they were read in October 2026.

The interesting number is the in-home band, because it is the one an Al Manara parent is implicitly comparing against. Visiting one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to AED 500. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visiting sessions. The gap between those two monthly figures is roughly the cost of a car crossing Sheikh Zayed Road twice a week. It buys travel, not teaching, and it narrows the tutor pool to whoever is willing to make the journey at 5pm.

What a parent can verify independently is worth more than any of this. Ask for the rate in AED per sixty minutes, ask whether marking time is inside or outside that hour, ask what happens to a session cancelled with four hours' notice, and ask to see one piece of marked work before paying for a term. Those four questions separate the bands faster than any price list, and they cost nothing.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The internally assessed scientific investigation is the student's own work, and that is not a formality. IB academic-honesty rules treat work that is not a student's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the tutor who helped. Any provider offering to supply a finished investigation is selling an expulsion risk. One agency found in the research for these pages sells completed internal assessments outright; that is the clearest possible signal to walk away.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. They can interrogate a research question until it is narrow enough to be answerable with the equipment available. They can point out that a proposed method will generate five data points when the criteria reward a range wide enough to show a trend. They can teach uncertainty propagation on a worked example that is not the student's own experiment. They can read a draft and say that the evaluation section describes limitations without explaining their effect on the conclusion. They can mark against the published criteria and explain the gap between a mark and the one above it.

What they must not do is write a sentence of it, choose the research question for the student, process the data, or edit the text into its final form. The practical test an Al Manara parent can apply at home is ownership: can your child explain, without notes, why that research question, why that method, and what the uncertainty on the key measurement actually means? If the answer is no, the work has been done to them rather than with them, regardless of what the mark looks like.

The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay if it is being written in physics, and to the Theory of Knowledge essay. Process coaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own draft are all legitimate and all useful. Supplying content is not. Every session on an internally assessed task under this arrangement ends with the student holding the next action, in writing, and the tutor holding none of it.
bullets: Research question narrowed by questioning, never chosen for the student
Uncertainty analysis taught on a different experiment, then applied by the student
Drafts read and marked against the criteria, never edited to completion
The ownership test: can your child explain the method without notes?

sections.heading: The year as a physics student in Al Manara experiences it
paragraphs: The Diploma year has a shape, and tutoring that ignores it wastes money in predictable places. Autumn term in DP1 is the cheapest time to buy physics help and the time families are least likely to buy it, because no grade has gone wrong yet. Mechanics and the measurement-and-uncertainty material are both live in class, and fixing them while they are live costs a fraction of rebuilding them in DP2.

The winter of DP1 brings the first serious internal assessments and, at most of the schools in both Al Manara clusters, the first report that uses predicted-grade language. That report is a weak diagnostic on its own: a 4 in physics tells you the grade and not the cause, and the cause is usually one of the three loss patterns described above. A single diagnostic session on a marked script is more informative than a term of general support.

Spring and early summer of DP1 is scientific investigation season at most schools, running into DP2 for some. This is the block where process coaching earns its keep, and it is also the block where the honesty boundary matters most. Ramadan falls inside this window in the current years, and session timing shifts with it: post-Iftar slots work well for older students and badly for anyone who has to be up for a 7am school bus, so it is worth agreeing the Ramadan pattern in advance rather than cancelling four weeks of sessions.

DP2 runs towards the May session that UAE schools sit, and the autumn and winter terms before it are when option-topic work and timed paper practice have to happen. For IGCSE siblings in the same household the rhythm is different: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May or June and again in November, with the November 2026 timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and results reaching students in January. Always check the live official timetable rather than a restated date, including the one in this sentence. No specific IB session or results date is published on this page, because the IB's own site could not be verified directly for it.

sections.heading: KHDA, the permit, and who is actually marking your child's work
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, and the authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

An inspection band is a whole-school judgement, and reading it as a physics judgement is a mistake Al Manara parents make regularly. A school rated Outstanding can have a physics department running on supply cover for a term; a school rated Good can have a long-serving Higher Level teacher with a deep bank of option resources. The report text beneath the band is where the subject-level detail sits, and it is published. Reading the science paragraphs of your own school's most recent report is a better use of twenty minutes than comparing two bands.

On the tutor side, the position is clearer than most websites make it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you. The application route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

A separate rule matters in Abu Dhabi and is worth knowing even from Dubai, because families move: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. The marketing line 'your child's own teacher, privately' is one to decline. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, MoHRE, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge accreditation, approval or partnership, and any provider claiming otherwise should be asked for the permit or centre number.
