sections.heading: Starting, and what happens when the slot you need is full
paragraphs: The useful first step is not a booking, it is a marked script. Send the most recent marked physics paper, the school's assessment calendar for the term, and the name of the Paper 3 optional topic the cohort is following. Those three items let a tutor say something specific in the first session instead of spending it on introductions, and they are the difference between a diagnostic hour and a pleasant one.

Then the trial lesson. One lesson, before any payment, with no card details taken and one per family. The point of it is not to be impressed. The point is to see whether the tutor can look at your child's marked script and name the loss pattern, and whether your child will talk to them. A tutor who spends the trial describing their own experience has used it badly.

Availability is where most providers stop being honest, so here is the real position. Physics specialists who can mark a Higher Level script properly are not evenly spread across the clock. The 5pm to 6:30pm Gulf Standard Time window is the most requested hour in the UAE, and for a specific optional topic at Higher Level the match may take several days rather than an afternoon. When no specialist is free in the slot an Al Manara family needs, there are three honest options: take a different slot, take a weekend session instead of a weekday one, or wait for the right match. Being handed a general science tutor to fill the gap is the outcome worth refusing, and it is the one that quietly happens elsewhere.

If the match is wrong, say so after the second session rather than the eighth. The useful signal is not whether your child liked the hour; it is whether the work coming back is specific. Session notes that name a topic, a command term and a next action are working. Notes that say the session went well are not. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, so what you are buying is the teaching and the evidence it produces, delivered over live video into an Al Manara afternoon that already has enough traffic in it.
bullets: Send a marked script, the term calendar, and the Paper 3 option before the trial
Judge the trial on whether the loss pattern gets named

process.title: Send the evidence first
process.description: A marked physics script, the school's assessment dates for the term, and the Paper 3 optional topic the cohort is following. Three items, five minutes, and they convert the first session from an introduction into a diagnosis. A photograph of the marked paper is enough; the examiner comments matter more than the total.

process.title: Agree the slot against the real door time
process.description: Tell us the school and whether the run is coastward or inland, and the slot is set from that rather than from a round hour. A coastward family usually lands on 4:45pm, an inland one on 5:15pm or later. Activity afternoons are taken out of the pattern before anything is booked.

process.title: Match on the component, not the subject
process.description: Physics is matched by what your child is actually losing marks on: uncertainty treatment, Paper 2 extended response, or a specific Paper 3 option. The match takes longer than a general science booking and is the reason the first session has something to say.

process.title: Take the trial lesson
process.description: One lesson, no payment, no card details, one per family. Watch for two things: whether the tutor can name the loss pattern from the marked script, and whether your child talks. If either is missing, the match is wrong and saying so costs nothing at that stage.

process.title: Hold the slot and read the notes
process.description: The session runs weekly at the same time, with notes the same evening naming the topic covered, the error pattern seen and the next action for the student. Those notes are the measurement. If they stop being specific, the arrangement has drifted and is worth resetting.

whyPoints.title: The slot is built from your commute, not ours
whyPoints.description: Al Manara has two school-run directions with forty-five minutes between their door times. Sessions are scheduled from your child's actual arrival time, which is why the booking survives past the third week instead of becoming the thing that gets cancelled during assessment season.

whyPoints.title: Physics matched by paper and option
whyPoints.description: The Paper 3 optional topic differs between schools in the same cluster. Matching on it means a tutor who has taught and marked that material rather than one who will read the chapter alongside your child. It takes longer to arrange and it is the whole point.

whyPoints.title: Marked scripts with the reasoning written out
whyPoints.description: Work comes back marked against the published criteria with the gap between the awarded mark and the one above explained in words. A grade on its own is information your child already had. The explanation is what changes the next attempt.

whyPoints.title: AED figures attributed, never invented
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is a provider's own published figure with the provider named and the reading date stated. IB Gram does not publish a rate card here, and no statistic appears on this page without its source, its date and what it counts.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: On the scientific investigation, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, the tutor questions, reviews and marks. The student writes, chooses and submits. That boundary is written down because the consequence of crossing it falls on your child.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: If no Higher Level physics specialist is free in the slot you need, you are told that and offered a different slot, a weekend session or a wait. A general science tutor is not quietly substituted to fill the gap.

faqs.question: What time can an IB physics session realistically start for an Al Manara family?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which direction the school run goes. If your child is at Raffles World Academy, Kings' School Dubai or Jumeirah Baccalaureate School, the day ends around 3pm and the door time in Al Manara is 3:30pm to 4pm, so a 4:30pm or 4:45pm start works across a full term. If the run crosses Sheikh Zayed Road to Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, door time is 4:15pm to 4:40pm and the earliest slot that survives is 5:15pm or later. Booking the inland family into a 4:30pm slot is the most common reason a physics arrangement collapses by week three.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Manara students actually travel to for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Al Manara has no IB school within its own boundary, so every Diploma student commutes. The coastward cluster is Raffles World Academy and Kings' School Dubai in Umm Suqeim, Jumeirah Baccalaureate School in Al Safa, and Horizon International School on the Umm Al Sheif edge. The inland cluster, across Sheikh Zayed Road, includes Dubai American Academy and Dubai International Academy in Al Barsha and GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh. These schools are named as context for the commute; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them and none endorses this page.

faqs.question: Does it matter which Paper 3 optional topic my child's school teaches?
faqs.answer: It matters more than almost anything else in the match. Paper 3 examines the optional material a school selects, and schools in the same Dubai cluster do not all choose the same one. A tutor matched on subject alone can help with Paper 1 and Paper 2 and will be reading the option chapter at the same pace as your child. Ask the physics teacher which option the cohort is following before the first session is booked. It is one email and it changes who the right tutor is.

faqs.question: My daughter is in DP1 and came home with a 4 in Higher Level physics. Is that a level problem?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the first-term DP1 report is a poor basis for the decision. A 4 at that stage most often reflects adjustment to Diploma workload plus one of three specific loss patterns: uncertainty treatment applied as a procedure, command terms answered in a single register, or a mathematics gap presenting as a physics gap. A diagnostic session on the marked script will name which one. Decide the level question on the university target and on quantitative fluency, in the second term, with a marked paper in front of you rather than a grade.

faqs.question: Is there any point in physics tutoring over video when so much of the course is practical?
faqs.answer: The practical skills the Diploma assesses are mostly analytical rather than manual. The scientific investigation is marked on the quality of the research question, the method's ability to generate meaningful data, the handling of uncertainty and the evaluation, and all four can be taught and reviewed over a shared screen. What video cannot do is hand your child a micrometer, and it does not need to: the school provides the laboratory. Screen sharing on a marked script and a spreadsheet of the student's own data is the format most of this work actually needs.

faqs.question: How much does an IB physics tutor cost in Dubai, and what should we expect to pay?
faqs.answer: Published market rates, read in October 2026, run from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for a student tutor online, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for an IB specialist, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Visiting one-to-one tuition in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500. Those are the providers' own figures, not IB Gram's. Ask for a rate per sixty minutes and whether marking is billed inside the hour.

faqs.question: What does the extra cost of a visiting tutor in this area actually buy?
faqs.answer: Travel, and a smaller pool to choose from. Monthly packages in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visiting sessions, and the difference is a car crossing Al Wasl Road or Sheikh Zayed Road twice a week at 5pm. It does not buy better physics teaching, and it narrows the choice to whoever will make the journey. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India.

faqs.question: Can a physics tutor help with the scientific investigation without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can question a research question until it is answerable, point out that a method will produce too few data points, teach uncertainty propagation on a different worked example, read a draft and mark it against the published criteria, and explain the gap to the next mark. A tutor cannot choose the question, process the data, write any part of it or edit it to completion. The test at home is ownership: your child should be able to explain the question, the method and the key uncertainty without notes.

faqs.question: We are starting in DP2. Is it too late for physics support to change anything?
faqs.answer: It is not too late, but the work is different and more expensive in hours. DP2 support usually has to rebuild DP1 foundations, chiefly rearrangement fluency and uncertainty handling, while DP2 content and the option arrive on top. The fastest returns in that position come from Paper 2 command-term technique and from timed questions on the Paper 3 option, both of which move marks in weeks. What DP2 cannot recover cheaply is a weak scientific investigation already submitted, because that mark is fixed before the papers are sat.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week should an Al Manara student have?
faqs.answer: One, held reliably, beats two that get cancelled. The evening arithmetic in this neighbourhood is tight: an inland commute leaves roughly three usable hours between 5:15pm and bedtime, and six Diploma subjects already fill them. One weekly session that absorbs the week's physics homework rather than adding to it is sustainable across two years. Where a student needs more, a ninety-minute weekend session with a timed paper inside it is worth more for exam technique than a second rushed weekday hour.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover physics and mathematics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is frequently the right arrangement. A large share of lost physics marks in Diploma scripts come from mathematics: logarithmic scales, exponential decay, small-angle approximations and compound algebra appear inside physics questions as assumed knowledge. A tutor who teaches both can fix the cause rather than the symptom, which matters particularly for a student taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation alongside Physics at Higher Level, since several of those tools arrive in physics before they arrive in maths.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and how do we check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount with suspicion. Applications go through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service. Ask a tutor directly whether they hold a current permit.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA Outstanding rating tell us about the physics teaching at a school?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band from Outstanding to Very Weak, but that band is a whole-school judgement covering leadership, provision and outcomes across every subject and phase. A school rated Outstanding can have a physics department on supply cover; a school rated Good can have a long-serving Higher Level specialist. The subject-level detail sits in the report text beneath the band, which KHDA publishes. Reading the science paragraphs of your own school's latest report is more useful than comparing two bands.

faqs.question: Can physics sessions move during Ramadan or the school run changes mid-year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better to agree the pattern in advance than to cancel four weeks. Post-Iftar slots work well for older Diploma students and badly for anyone catching an early school bus, so the sensible Ramadan pattern is usually a shorter session earlier in the afternoon, or a shift to the weekend. Mid-year changes to the school run matter too: a bus route change or a move from the coastward to the inland cluster shifts the door time by up to forty-five minutes, and the slot should move with it.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level physics specialist is free in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: You are told. The 5pm to 6:30pm Gulf Standard Time window is the most requested hour across the UAE, and for a specific Paper 3 option at Higher Level a match can take several days rather than an afternoon. The honest options are a different weekday slot, a weekend session, or waiting for the right person. What should not happen is a general science tutor substituted quietly to fill the gap, which is the outcome worth refusing wherever it is offered.

faqs.question: Does an IB physics grade matter for Ministry of Education equivalency in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a separate process from school assessment, run by the Ministry of Education rather than by a school or a tutor. For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold should be published without being read on the Ministry's own site, and this page does not state one. Check the official channel directly.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-manara.closingBody: An IB physics tutor in Al Manara is useful in proportion to how specific the first session is, and specificity comes from two things: a marked paper with the examiner's comments on it, and an honest answer about what time your child actually walks in the door. Send those, plus the Paper 3 optional topic the school is following, and the trial lesson can start with a diagnosis instead of an introduction. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time, from whichever slot your commute direction leaves open. If no specialist is free in that slot, you will be told so rather than offered a substitute.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-mankhool.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Diploma Physics at Higher and Standard Level for students at the Diploma schools reachable from Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai. Work is scoped from where the student is in the two-year sequence and from the dates their own school controls, including the laboratory timetable.

intro.heading: The physics year has a date in it that nobody controls at home
paragraphs: Most Diploma subjects can be rescued at home. A student behind in Economics can read, write and be taught at a desk, in an evening, at any point in the two years. Physics has a component that cannot be done that way. The scientific investigation requires the student to collect their own data with real apparatus, and that apparatus sits in a school laboratory whose time is allocated by a timetable the family has no part in writing.

That single fact reorders everything. The date that matters is not the internal deadline for submitting the investigation; it is the last point at which laboratory access can realistically be obtained, which is earlier and much less visible. A student who settles on a research question two weeks before the deadline has not left themselves two weeks of work. They have left themselves no viable route to data at all, and the investigation they submit will be built on whatever they can measure without equipment.

The second structural feature is that Diploma Physics accumulates. Mechanics underpins energy; energy and algebraic handling underpin fields; fields and induction underpin a great deal of the second year, particularly at Higher Level. A student who passed through year one on intuition rather than on secure method does not discover the consequence immediately - they discover it twelve months later, in a term where there is no space to go back. In a subject like this, revision is not something that happens at the end. It is a maintenance schedule that runs through both years.

Families in Al Mankhool and Bur Dubai have an extra blind spot. The schools in this district mostly run to sixteen, so Diploma Physics students have usually moved campus, often recently. The household has no history with how that school sequences physics topics, how it schedules laboratory time, when its internal deadlines fall or how hard its mock papers are marked. A parent can genuinely not tell whether their child is behind the class, behind the syllabus, or simply being taught in an unfamiliar order.

So this page is organised around the dates rather than the topics. The laboratory calendar first, because it is the one with no flexibility. Then the dependency chain, so you can see which gaps block which later work. Then a maintenance schedule for revisiting topics across two years rather than cramming them in one term. Then the mock audit, the level-change decision and its school-set deadline, and what a late block in this subject can honestly reach. No IB examination or results date appears on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so none has been verified at source, and we will not publish a date a family would reorganise a year around.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-mankhool.programmesIntro: Where a student sits on the IB continuum changes which dates bind and what a block of sessions can be used for. Physics in particular behaves differently at each stage because the practical requirement changes.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Taken at Higher or Standard Level, assessed through written papers plus an internally assessed scientific investigation that the student designs, runs and writes. Higher Level adds content and an additional paper, and the second year leans heavily on the first. The investigation's internal deadline is set by the school, and the laboratory time it requires is allocated by the school too.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision near Al Mankhool sits outward from the district - Al Jaddaf, across the creek and toward Nad Al Sheba - so students from here commute, and their laboratory access is at a campus the family does not know well. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools, creating 16,846 places.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Science taught as an integrated group and assessed against four criteria on a 1-8 scale rather than by terminal papers. Criterion B inquiring and designing and Criterion C processing and evaluating are the direct ancestors of the Diploma investigation, which makes this the cheapest place to learn investigation discipline properly.
programmes.countryNote: There is no external deadline at this stage, which makes the planning problem entirely different. A block here is pre-emptive: investigation habits and algebraic handling built in Year 10 remove the two things that most often go wrong in Diploma year one, and they cost a fraction of what repairing them later costs.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics
programmes.description: Tiered Core and Extended, with practical skills assessed either through a practical examination or through the alternative-to-practical written paper depending on the centre's entry. Cambridge runs the exams in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones.
programmes.countryNote: What a student took here predicts their first Diploma Physics term more reliably than any report comment. A student arriving from Core tier has a genuine content gap; one arriving from Extended with secure algebra usually copes. The summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is the only window in the whole sequence with no competing deadline.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics
programmes.description: The other pre-sixteen route sat in Dubai, with its own paper structure and question style. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Because schools in this belt split entries between boards, two Diploma Physics students starting Year 12 together may have had meaningfully different preparation and different practical-assessment routes. Establishing which, in the first session, saves a term of teaching aimed at the wrong starting point.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-mankhool.subjectsIntro: Diploma Physics topics are not independent, which is what makes the calendar matter. Below are the main areas, with what each one blocks if it is not secure and roughly when it has to be solid.

subjects.name: Measurement and uncertainty
subjects.description: Taught early, treated as administrative, and then required in every data question and throughout the investigation. A student who never learned to propagate uncertainty properly loses marks in the investigation and in the papers, and the repair is short if it happens early.

subjects.name: Mechanics and kinematics
subjects.description: The foundation, and the usual site of an undetected gap because early confidence hides weak method. Blocks energy, momentum and anything involving resolved components. Must be secure by the end of the first year or the second year becomes repair work.

subjects.name: Energy, work and power
subjects.description: Depends on mechanics and on algebraic rearrangement. Students treat energy conservation as a formula rather than as a constraint on the whole situation, which is why they can state it correctly and still not know what to do with it in an unfamiliar context.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Reasonably self-contained, which makes it a viable late target when other ground is lost. Marks go on precise definitions and on distinguishing temperature from thermal energy in explanations, both of which are writing discipline as much as physics.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Conceptually approachable and mathematically unforgiving. Phase, path difference and superposition questions punish approximate reasoning, and students strong elsewhere often find their long-answer marks drop here without warning.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Where marks disappear in volume. Students recite relationships and cannot reason about what happens to the rest of a circuit when one component changes. That reasoning is trainable with targeted questions and does not improve by re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Fields, induction and electromagnetism
subjects.description: Second-year content that assumes mechanics, algebra and trigonometric handling. It separates a comfortable Higher Level student from a struggling one, and it is the clearest case of why a year-one gap surfaces a year late.

subjects.name: Atomic, nuclear and particle physics
subjects.description: Mostly self-contained and therefore a sensible late block. Exponential behaviour in decay questions trips students whose mathematics course has not reached logarithmic handling, which is a mathematics gap rather than a physics one.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: The component with a school-set deadline and a school-controlled laboratory requirement. Marks are lost on design and on uncertainty evaluation rather than on the experiment, and both require explaining choices rather than reporting results.

subjects.name: Mathematical handling for physics
subjects.description: Rearrangement with squared terms, resolving components, gradients and areas as physical quantities, proportional reasoning and exponentials. Not physics, frequently the real gap, and best fixed in a short narrow block rather than inside a physics hour.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-mankhool.regionsTitle: Which calendar each neighbourhood is on

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-mankhool.modesIntro: Three blocks matched to the three things that actually go wrong in a Diploma Physics calendar. Each is aimed at a date rather than at a general sense that more physics would help.

modes.title: Investigation planning block
modes.description: A short run of sessions timed well before the school's internal deadline, aimed at the only part of the investigation that can be fixed cheaply: whether the research question can actually be answered with the apparatus the school can make available, and when that apparatus can be booked.

modes.title: Maintenance hour across both years
modes.description: A weekly or fortnightly hour whose job is partly current content and partly keeping earlier topics alive, because the second year of this subject assumes the first. Students resist the revisiting because it feels like going backwards, and it is the reason Higher Level grades hold in year two.
bullets: Part current topic, part scheduled revisit of an earlier one
Diagram before algebra, every session, without exception

An end-of-year-one audit against what year two assumes

modes.title: Final-term paper block
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week in the closing weeks, built on full timed papers and the audit of them. No new content unless an audit demands it. This is what converts a student who understands the physics into one who earns the marks for understanding it.
bullets: Full papers under exam conditions at the correct level
Every lost mark assigned to content, method, misreading or the clock

sections.heading: The laboratory is the immovable date
paragraphs: Work backwards from apparatus, not from the deadline. The scientific investigation requires the student to collect their own data, the apparatus lives in a school laboratory, and laboratory time is allocated by a timetable written around taught lessons rather than around individual coursework. That means there is a last viable date for data collection which sits well before the submission deadline, and it is the date almost nobody asks about.

The sequence has a lead time at every stage. Reading and thinking produces a candidate research question. The question has to be checked against what can actually be measured with available equipment, which often kills the first idea - and killing it early is cheap. Then the method has to be designed well enough that the laboratory session is productive, because a student who arrives with a vague plan burns their access and may not get another slot. Then the data is collected, then processed, then written up against the criteria.

Compress that and specific failures follow, all of them predictable. A question that cannot be answered with the apparatus available. A single data run with no repeats, so uncertainty cannot be evaluated properly. A range too narrow to show a relationship. A method that could not be refined because there was no second session. None of those is a knowledge failure and all of them cap the mark.

The table sets out the stages with who controls each date. Ask your child's school for the investigation deadline and the laboratory arrangement in the same conversation, at the start of the year, because the two together are the plan.

sections.heading: The dependency chain, and when each link has to hold
paragraphs: Diploma Physics is not a list of topics; it is a chain. Mechanics underpins energy. Energy and algebraic rearrangement underpin a great deal of the rest. Trigonometric handling and resolved components underpin fields. Fields underpin induction and electromagnetism, which is where Higher Level separates. A weak link does not announce itself where it sits - it announces itself in whatever topic comes next and needs it.

This is why a student can work steadily through year one, receive acceptable reports, and then fall away in year two. Nothing changed about their effort. The content changed to material that assumes fluency they never built, and by then the timetable has no space for going back. It is also why the end of year one is the highest-value audit point in the whole course: an afternoon spent testing whether the foundational handling is actually secure prevents the most common second-year collapse.

For a family deciding when to buy help, the chain gives a rule. Gaps in the early links are urgent regardless of how comfortable the current topic feels, because they compound. Gaps in self-contained topics - thermal, nuclear, parts of atomic physics - are not urgent and can be addressed late, which makes them good targets when weeks are short. Knowing which category a gap falls into is more useful than knowing how large it is.
The table maps the links. Use it to work out whether a reported weakness needs attention now or can wait, and take the actual teaching order from your child's school, which varies.

sections.heading: A maintenance schedule beats a final-term crammed revision
paragraphs: In a subject that accumulates across two years, leaving revision to the final term is a structural error rather than a matter of discipline. By the time the last term arrives there is too much material and too little time, and the student is also finishing an investigation, sitting mocks in five other subjects and completing Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay requirements. The capacity simply is not there.

The alternative is unglamorous and it works: a schedule of revisits running through both years. Part of each session, or every second session, spent re-testing an earlier topic under time rather than re-explaining it. The distinction matters. Re-explaining produces recognition, which feels like knowledge and disappears. Re-testing produces retrieval, which is what an examination requires and what survives.

Students dislike this intensely because it has no sense of forward motion, and it is the single practice that most reliably protects a Higher Level grade in year two. A topic touched three times across eighteen months at widening intervals is held; a topic taught once in year one and revised once at the end is not, however well it was taught the first time.

There is a practical version of this that costs nothing extra. Before each new topic, spend the first ten minutes of the session on a short retrieval test of whatever earlier topic the new one depends on. It takes a tenth of the hour, it tells the tutor immediately whether the new content has a foundation to stand on, and it stops the common pattern where a student is taught fields on top of mechanics they can no longer use. Over a year that amounts to several hours of maintenance that nobody had to schedule separately.
The table gives a workable rhythm. Fit it to your child's school's actual teaching order, which varies, and treat the intervals as a guide rather than a prescription.

sections.heading: The mock script, read the physics way
paragraphs: Mocks are the only marked timed scripts a Diploma Physics student sees before the real papers, and in this subject they are especially informative because the failure modes are so distinguishable. Spend one session auditing rather than discussing the grade, and the remaining weeks organise themselves.

The four causes are the same as in any subject - content not known, method not shown, question misread, time ran out - but each looks particular in physics. Content not known usually appears as a blank or an abandoned question in a topic the student cannot enter. Method not shown appears as a correct final answer with no working, or as a numerical answer with no unit, both of which forfeit marks that were earned. Question misread appears most often as a description written where the command verb asked for an explanation. Time ran out appears as unattempted questions at the end of a paper the student could have answered.

The long-answer pattern deserves separate attention because it accounts for so much. A student who knows the physics writes a set of true statements, and the mark scheme awards credit for a linked chain: this happens, which causes this, which means this. Unlinked truth scores poorly. Students need to see this marked against the real scheme two or three times before they accept that writing less, in order, scores more.

Then there is the diagram. Physics questions involving geometry - inclines, fields, forces in two dimensions - are routinely failed by students who attempt the algebra without drawing first. Making a diagram non-optional is one instruction, it takes a single session to establish, and it converts a reliable category of lost marks into earned ones for the rest of the course.
bullets: Audit the script into four causes before anybody discusses the grade
A correct answer with no working or no unit forfeits marks already earned
Descriptions written where the verb asked for an explanation are the commonest misread

Making the diagram non-optional removes a whole category of losses

sections.heading: Dropping from Higher to Standard: a decision with a school deadline
paragraphs: Some of the families who arrive asking for physics help are in a different conversation. The student was placed in Higher Level on the strength of an IGCSE grade rather than on demonstrated algebraic fluency, the content is cumulative, and they are working hard and falling behind anyway. No quantity of tuition fixes a structural mismatch in a subject that builds on itself.

Whether a move to Standard Level is available, and until when, is set entirely by the school. Some permit it during the first term of year one and not afterwards; some have an earlier cut-off tied to their own internal deadlines. The date is rarely advertised and is almost always earlier than a struggling family would like. Asking about it costs nothing, commits to nothing, and is far better done in the autumn than in the spring.

A short diagnostic block is the right way to generate evidence for that conversation. Two or three sessions with a specialist, working through questions at the current level, will distinguish a fixable gap from a genuine mismatch - and crucially will say which. That finding is more useful in a meeting with a coordinator than a parent's impression, and it is a small purchase relative to a term of the wrong plan.

If a change is not available, say so and reset the goal honestly. A mismatched Higher Level student can still gain substantially through method marks, long-answer structure, diagram discipline and paper timing, without ever becoming comfortable with the hardest second-year content. That is a legitimate target. What is not legitimate is selling a term of work on the implication that the gap will close when it will not.

sections.heading: The mathematics underneath, and when to fix it
paragraphs: A large share of Diploma Physics students who need help do not have a physics problem. They explain the mechanism correctly, name the right relationship, and then stop. The failure is in the mathematical handling, and because the timetable says physics, that is what the family buys. Understanding improves, the grade does not move.

The diagnostic takes minutes. Give the student a problem they have described correctly and watch where the pencil stops. Stopping at rearranging a relationship to make a different quantity the subject is an algebra gap. Stopping at reading a gradient or an area off a graph is a graphical one. Stopping at splitting a vector into components is trigonometry. Stopping at decay or attenuation is exponential and logarithmic handling. None of those is taught by teaching physics.

The awkward part is ownership. A student taking Physics Higher Level alongside Mathematics Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is in a genuine gap: the physics assumes handling that mathematics course does not teach, the physics teacher assumes the mathematics course covers it, and nobody is responsible. It is nobody's fault and it is entirely fixable, usually in a narrow block of three or four sessions rather than a term.

On timing, this is urgent rather than deferrable, because the handling is needed across every subsequent topic. A mathematics gap identified in year one and closed in four sessions costs almost nothing. The same gap carried into fields and induction in year two makes a demanding topic impossible and consumes a term that was needed elsewhere.

sections.heading: Term block or spot block: how to buy this subject
paragraphs: Physics support divides naturally into two purchases, and conflating them is how budgets go wrong. A term block is a weekly or fortnightly maintenance hour running alongside the course, doing current content and scheduled revisits. A spot block is three to five sessions aimed at one identified thing: the mathematical handling, the investigation plan, the long-answer structure, one self-contained topic. The first is a commitment; the second is a repair.

Most families default to the term block because it is the familiar shape, and a good proportion of them needed a spot block. A student whose only real problem is that they do not draw diagrams, or do not write units, or cannot rearrange, needs two or three sessions and a habit, not thirty weeks. Conversely, a Higher Level student in a cumulative subject with a genuine foundation gap needs the term block, and a spot block will not hold.

For reference, the published bands, each attributed to the provider that published it and read in October 2026. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts qualified online tuition at AED 150 to 300 and specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level provision at AED 200 to 450 or more, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270. In-home one-to-one including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500, and BartyED publishes AED 650. None is an IB Gram price. Monthly, one Dubai provider publishes AED 799 for eight online sessions, near AED 100 an hour; in-home monthly packages are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Diploma Physics sessions for Al Mankhool students run one-to-one over live video, which for this subject carries a practical benefit beyond the rate: diagrams, graphs and worked algebra sit on a shared annotated screen rather than on a notebook turned sideways at the edge of a table.

sections.heading: Regulators, the permit and the periods inside the school day
paragraphs: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes inspection reports on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. For a physics family that is directly useful, because the report comments on science provision. If science teaching is named as a strength, the laboratory and taught side is in capable hands and a private hour belongs on theory, mathematical handling and the investigation plan. If science is flagged as an area for improvement, the balance shifts.

Across the country, ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates it there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project.

On tutors, the position is checkable. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time. Operating without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation, no KHDA institute permit and no UAE office.

Finally, the periods that squeeze the physics week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year or April 2026 where the year begins in April. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Those periods sit inside the day alongside six Diploma subjects, a laboratory requirement, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which is why the available study time is always less than a timetable suggests. Ramadan compresses it further: school hours shorten, the day changes shape, and the sensible move is to agree in advance that the physics hour shifts to a post-Iftar slot for that period and returns afterwards.

process.title: Ask the school two things at once
process.description: The internal deadline for the scientific investigation and how laboratory access is allocated. Those two together are the real calendar for this subject, and the second one is the question almost no family thinks to ask until data collection has become impossible.

process.title: Send the level and the maths route
process.description: Physics Higher or Standard Level plus the Mathematics course and level taken alongside it. That combination predicts most of what will go wrong, and a Higher Level physics student on Applications and Interpretation Standard Level needs a specific gap closed early.

process.title: Free trial lesson on a problem already attempted
process.description: A full session at no charge, built around a question the student has already tried. Watching where the pencil stops distinguishes a physics gap from a mathematics gap from a long-answer writing gap, which are three different plans for the same money.

process.title: Decide term block or spot block, explicitly
process.description: A weekly maintenance hour with scheduled revisits, or three to five sessions aimed at one identified thing. Most families default to the first and a good proportion needed the second, and we would rather name that than sell the larger commitment.

process.title: Audit, then re-audit
process.description: Progress is measured on marked scripts audited into content, method, misreading and the clock, and on whether the investigation is on schedule against the laboratory calendar. If neither moves across a block, the plan or the tutor changes.

whyPoints.title: Planned from laboratory access backwards
whyPoints.description: The investigation's binding date is the last viable data-collection slot, not the submission deadline, and it is set by the school's laboratory timetable. We plan from that, because a question settled too late has no route to data regardless of how hard anybody then works.

whyPoints.title: Dependencies named, not discovered late
whyPoints.description: Mechanics, uncertainty and algebraic handling block most of year two. We treat gaps in those as urgent whatever the current topic feels like, and self-contained topics such as thermal and nuclear physics as the sensible late targets.

whyPoints.title: Revisits scheduled across both years
whyPoints.description: In an accumulating subject, re-testing earlier topics under time through both years protects a Higher Level grade far better than a crammed final term. Students resist it because it has no forward motion, which is precisely why it needs scheduling.

whyPoints.title: The mathematics gap diagnosed separately
whyPoints.description: Many physics students who need help have an algebra, graph, trigonometry or logarithm problem wearing a physics badge. Physics Higher Level with Applications and Interpretation Standard Level is the standard case. We fix it in a narrow block rather than selling physics hours.

whyPoints.title: Honest about a level mismatch
whyPoints.description: Where a student is genuinely mismatched to Higher Level, a diagnostic block produces evidence for a conversation with the school while a change is still possible - and if it is not, we reset the goal to what method, structure and timing can realistically reach.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be shown
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no UAE office, no grade guarantees, no IB dates we have not verified at source, no board documents supplied, and every dirham figure attributed to the provider that published it with the month read.

faqs.question: What is the real deadline for the IB Physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Not the submission date - the last point at which laboratory access can realistically be obtained, which sits well before it and is set by the school's laboratory timetable. A student who settles on a research question a fortnight before submission has no viable route to data, and the investigation ends up built on whatever can be measured without equipment. Ask the school for the internal deadline and the laboratory arrangement in the same conversation, at the start of the year. The second question is the one families forget to ask.

faqs.question: What goes wrong when investigation data collection is rushed?
faqs.answer: Four things, all predictable and all capping the mark. A research question that cannot actually be answered with the apparatus available. A single data run with no repeats, so uncertainty cannot be evaluated properly. A range too narrow to show the relationship the question claims. And a method that could not be refined because there was no second laboratory slot. None of those is a knowledge failure. All of them are consequences of compressing a sequence that needs weeks of lead time at the feasibility and booking stages.

faqs.question: Why do Higher Level physics grades sometimes fall in the second year?
faqs.answer: Because the subject accumulates and year two assumes year one was secured rather than merely covered. Mechanics underpins energy; algebra and resolved components underpin fields; fields underpin induction and electromagnetism, where Higher Level separates. A student who passed through year one on intuition meets the consequence twelve months later, in a term with no space to go back. The prevention is an audit at the end of year one - one diagnostic paper, honestly marked, against what year two will assume.

faqs.question: Which physics topics are urgent to fix and which can wait?
faqs.answer: Urgent: measurement and uncertainty, algebraic rearrangement, mechanics and resolving components, because each blocks a large amount of later work and gaps there compound. Can wait: thermal physics and much of atomic and nuclear physics, which are largely self-contained and therefore good late targets when weeks are short. Knowing which category a reported weakness falls into is more useful than knowing how large it is, because it tells you whether the hours are needed now or can be scheduled.

faqs.question: Is it better to revise physics throughout the course or in the final term?
faqs.answer: Throughout, and in an accumulating subject that is a structural point rather than a discipline one. By the final term there is too much material and too little capacity, with an investigation finishing, mocks in five other subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay all competing. The alternative is a revisit rhythm: part of each session re-testing an earlier topic under time rather than re-explaining it. Re-explaining produces recognition, which fades. Re-testing produces retrieval, which is what the papers require.

faqs.question: My child explains the physics correctly and still loses marks. What is wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually the mathematical handling. Give them a problem they have described correctly and watch where the pencil stops: rearranging a relationship is an algebra gap, reading a gradient or area off a graph is graphical, splitting a vector is trigonometry, decay questions are exponentials and logarithms. None of those is fixed by teaching physics, which is why a term of physics tuition can improve understanding without moving the grade. A narrow block of three or four sessions on the specific skill usually does more.

faqs.question: Can Physics Higher Level work alongside Maths Applications and Interpretation SL?
faqs.answer: It can, provided somebody explicitly teaches the handling the physics assumes and that mathematics course does not cover - rearrangement with squared terms, resolved components, gradients and areas as physical quantities, proportional reasoning, exponential behaviour. The problem is ownership: the physics teacher assumes the maths course covers it, the maths course has a different syllabus, and nobody is responsible. Identify it in year one and close it in four sessions; carried into fields and induction in year two it makes a demanding topic impossible.

faqs.question: How should we read my child's mock physics script?
faqs.answer: Audit it into four causes before discussing the grade: content not known, method not shown, question misread, time ran out. In physics each has a signature. Content appears as abandoned questions in a topic the student cannot enter. Method appears as a correct answer with no working or no unit, forfeiting marks already earned. Misreading appears as a description where the verb asked for an explanation. The clock appears as unattempted questions the student could have answered. Count them, then build the plan from the count.

faqs.question: Why do long-answer physics questions score so badly for students who know the topic?
faqs.answer: Because the mark scheme rewards a linked causal chain rather than a quantity of true statements. A student writes eight correct sentences about a phenomenon and scores about half, while three sentences connected properly - this happens, which causes this, which means this - score well. Explicit connective language earns the links. Students find this counterintuitive because the fix means writing less, and they need to see it marked against the real scheme two or three times before they trust it. It then transfers across every topic.

faqs.question: Could my child be in the wrong level for physics altogether?
faqs.answer: It happens, usually when a Higher Level placement was made on an overall IGCSE grade rather than on demonstrated algebraic fluency. In a cumulative subject that mismatch cannot be out-worked. Whether a move to Standard Level is available is set by the school, often only within the first term of year one, and the date is rarely advertised. Two or three diagnostic sessions on current-level questions will distinguish a fixable gap from a genuine mismatch, and that finding is far more useful in a meeting than an impression.

faqs.question: How big is the step from IGCSE Physics to Diploma Physics?
faqs.answer: Larger in mathematical demand than in content, and much larger from the Core tier than from Extended. A student arriving from 0625 Extended or 4PH1 with secure algebra usually copes; one arriving from Core has a real content gap that surfaces in the October of Diploma year one. The investigation is the other unfamiliar element, particularly for students who came through an alternative-to-practical route. The summer before Year 12 is the only window in the sequence with no competing deadline, which makes it the cheapest place to act.

faqs.question: Should we buy a weekly hour or a short block for physics?
faqs.answer: Depends on what is actually wrong, and the two are different purchases. A student whose problem is that they do not draw diagrams, do not write units, or cannot rearrange needs three sessions and a habit, not thirty weeks. A Higher Level student with a genuine foundation gap in a cumulative subject needs the weekly maintenance hour with scheduled revisits, and a short block will not hold. Most families default to the weekly hour and a good proportion needed the short one, which is worth establishing in the first session.

faqs.question: What does Diploma Physics support cost around Al Mankhool?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end - Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 - AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tuition on Bestimate's 2026 table, AED 200 upward from Unitors for IB, AED 200 to 450 or more for specialist provision, AED 270 from TutorChase and AED 650 from BartyED. In-home including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500. Monthly, one provider publishes AED 799 for eight online sessions. All read October 2026, all theirs rather than ours.

faqs.question: Does the school's inspection report help us decide what to buy?
faqs.answer: More than usual in a science subject. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the reports free, and they comment on science provision specifically. If science teaching is named as a strength, the taught and laboratory side is in capable hands and a private hour belongs on theory, mathematical handling and the investigation plan. If science is flagged for improvement, a weekly maintenance hour is doing more structural work and is worth more.

faqs.question: How do we keep physics going through Ramadan and term breaks?
faqs.answer: By deciding in advance rather than improvising. School hours shorten during Ramadan, the day changes shape and productive energy moves to after Iftar, so a slot that works in a normal term will not survive unchanged - agree beforehand that the hour shifts to a post-Iftar time and returns afterwards. For term breaks, count them out of any block before it is agreed: a notional eight-week plan in the UAE academic year routinely delivers six, and the plan should be built for the real number.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a Higher Level physics tutor here?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than putting a general science tutor in the slot. Diploma Physics at Higher Level is a narrower specialism than Chemistry or Mathematics and the pool is smaller, so the honest options are to wait for the right person, to begin with a related specialist on a clearly stated interim basis, or not to book. Because delivery is online rather than by somebody driving across Dubai, the pool is every Higher Level Physics specialist available rather than the few who would travel into Al Mankhool.

intro.heading: Al Mizhar against the communities next door, and why the Physics answer is identical
paragraphs: An Al Mizhar family looking for Physics help tends to run the same mental comparison. Mirdif has the schools, so perhaps Mirdif has the tutors. Al Warqa has the biggest cohorts, so perhaps the supply is better there. Al Khawaneej is quieter, so perhaps rates are lower. Nad Al Hamar is closer to the Ras Al Khor road, so perhaps a tutor driving from Deira gets there faster. Every one of those comparisons is about geography, and Higher Level Physics is the subject where geography matters least.

Here is the arithmetic that collapses the question. A Dubai secondary school running the Diploma Programme will typically have one or two teachers qualified to take Physics at Higher Level, because the cohort for it is small. Spread that across the eastern suburbs and the total number of people within a twenty-minute drive of Al Mizhar who can confidently teach the Higher Level additional topics is tiny, and all of them are already employed full time by a school. The pool you are actually choosing from is not your neighbourhood's pool. It is whoever is free on a Tuesday evening and willing to drive.

That is the comparison worth making instead: not Al Mizhar against Mirdif, but a local generalist against a Physics specialist who is not local. A tutor who teaches Physics as their subject knows that the data-based questions reward a candidate who draws the error bars before the line of best fit, and that the standard trap in the fields topic is a student who can quote the inverse-square relationship but cannot explain why the field inside a hollow conductor is zero. A capable maths teacher helping out with Physics will not reliably know those things, however near your villa they live.

IB Gram resolves the comparison by removing distance from it. Lessons for every UAE family are taught one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own script on screen. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. What that buys an Al Mizhar family is the Physics specialist rather than the nearest available adult, and it buys the half-hour of commuting back as revision time.

The rest of this page is written as a set of comparisons, because that is the question Al Mizhar parents arrive with. What the surrounding communities actually differ on. What the Dubai market charges and what each price band buys. How the Physics components differ from one another in what they reward. Where the marks go in each one. And what to do about the one genuine local variable, which is what time your child gets home and how much usable attention is left when they do.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-mizhar.programmesIntro: Physics sits inside a programme, and the programme decides what the subject is for. Al Mizhar families send children into IB continuum schools in Mirdif and into British-curriculum schools that switch to the Diploma at sixteen, so both routes into Physics appear in this catchment.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma, where Physics is chosen at Higher or Standard Level alongside five other subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Physics at Higher Level carries additional topics and a heavier problem-solving load, and the Internal Assessment is a single independent scientific investigation written by the student. This is where most Physics tutoring demand in the eastern suburbs sits.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma is one of seventeen licensed curricula, and International Baccalaureate schools accounted for seven per cent of private enrolment in 2024-25 according to the Dubai Media Office. For an Al Mizhar family that means a smaller Physics cohort than a British-curriculum A Level group, and therefore fewer teachers to go round.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five years before the Diploma, where science is assessed against four criteria rather than by paper marks. Students are judged on knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student who scores well here but has never been asked to carry an uncertainty through a calculation will feel the Diploma Physics jump sharply in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Uptown International School in Mirdif runs the continuum, so a proportion of Al Mizhar students arrive at Diploma Physics straight from the Middle Years Programme rather than from IGCSE. The gap those students most often need closing is algebraic fluency and formal uncertainty treatment, not conceptual physics.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The inquiry-led primary programme, taught through transdisciplinary units rather than separate subjects. There is no Physics as such, but the habits that later decide a Physics grade begin here: measuring carefully, recording what was actually observed rather than what was expected, and explaining a result to someone else. Primary support in this catchment is usually about numeracy and written explanation.
programmes.countryNote: Eastern Dubai has primary provision closer to home than secondary provision, including a Dubai Schools campus at Al Khawaneej, so younger children in Al Mizhar generally travel less than their older siblings. Tutoring demand at this stage is lighter and tends to be about keeping pace rather than closing a gap.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-mizhar.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely tutored alone. The subjects below are the ones Al Mizhar families most often pair with it, usually because the same student is fighting the same algebra in two places at once.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The page's subject. Mechanics, waves, electricity and magnetism, nuclear and quantum physics, with Higher Level adding depth across the same themes. Marks are lost in uncertainty treatment, in graph work, and in explanation questions where a student describes a result instead of accounting for it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual partner subject for a Physics student. Calculus, trigonometric identities and algebraic manipulation are the tools Physics assumes you already have. A student failing Physics questions on kinematics is often failing the differentiation inside them rather than the physics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics-heavier maths route, taken by some Physics students whose degree plans do not demand Analysis and Approaches. Regression and modelling transfer usefully into the Internal Assessment, but the lighter algebra means Physics problem-solving needs separate attention.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside Physics by students aiming at engineering or medicine. Energetics, kinetics and equilibrium reward the same unit-tracking discipline as Physics calculations, so the two subjects can be revised with one shared habit rather than two.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The third science in many eastern-suburbs timetables. Its demands are different from Physics: volume of recall, precise command-term response, and statistical treatment of data. Students who carry a Physics approach into Biology essays tend to under-write the explanation.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Chosen by Physics students who want a second technical subject. The internal assessment is a developed solution with documentation, which is a different kind of project discipline from a scientific investigation and often needs separate planning support.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Overlaps with Physics in materials, structures and energy. The design cycle and the extended written components reward students who can justify a decision rather than describe it, which is the same skill Physics explanation questions test.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: A science option that uses mechanics in an applied setting, including force, work and power in human movement. Students often find the quantitative sections easier after Physics tutoring has fixed their handling of units and rearrangement.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: A transdisciplinary option covering energy, systems and sustainability. Energy-flow calculations and data interpretation are the sections where a Physics-trained student has an immediate advantage, and where other students most often need help.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Compulsory across the Diploma. For a Physics student the useful ground is how experimental evidence becomes accepted knowledge, and what counts as proof in a natural science. Support here is about structuring an argument, never about producing the assessed essay.

Those are market figures published by those providers and read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices, and they are quoted here so an Al Mizhar family can see the shape of the market before anyone quotes them anything. sections.heading: The Physics components compared: what each one is really testing
paragraphs: A parent who knows the subject is assessed by papers and an investigation still rarely knows that the papers reward different things. Treating them as one undifferentiated exam is the commonest reason a student revises for forty hours and moves by two marks. The multiple-choice section rewards speed and the elimination of a wrong option; the data-based section rewards careful reading of a graph and a sentence that names a relationship; the extended-response paper rewards a worked line of reasoning with the physics made explicit.

The table lays those differences out next to where Al Mizhar students most often lose the marks. Confirm the current weightings against your child's own subject guide or their Diploma coordinator before you plan around them, because the Physics guide has been revised and the numbers below are the broad shape rather than a quotation from the IB. The point of the table is not the percentages. It is that a revision plan which drills content but never times a multiple-choice section, or never writes a conclusion that states a relationship with its uncertainty, has left two of the three papers untouched.

The investigation sits apart from all of it and is worth about a fifth of the grade in most current arrangements. It is marked on criteria a student can read, and the marks are lost early, in the choice of question, long before the writing starts. A question with one independent variable that can be measured enough times to show a trend is worth more than an ambitious question that produces four data points. A tutor's job here is to make the student's own question workable and to explain what the criteria reward; the investigation is written by the student and nobody else.

sections.heading: Uncertainties and graphs: the two things that separate a 5 from a 7
paragraphs: If a Physics student in the eastern suburbs is stuck in the middle of the grade range, the cause is usually not the physics. It is the handling of measurement. A student who can derive the equation but writes an answer to five significant figures from a ruler reading has told the examiner they do not understand what the instrument could possibly know. Uncertainty is not an administrative add-on to a Physics answer; it is part of the claim being made, and it is marked as such.

Graph work fails in a similarly mechanical way. The sequence that earns marks is fixed: plot the raw data, draw the uncertainty bars, then draw the best line that passes through them, then take the gradient from two widely separated points on that line rather than from two data points. Students who draw the line first and the bars afterwards have inverted the logic of the whole exercise, and it shows in every subsequent answer. Maximum and minimum gradients for an uncertainty in the gradient follow from the same construction, and they are quick marks once the construction is a habit.

Both skills are fixable in a handful of sessions, which is why they are worth attacking first. They are also independent of topic, so an hour spent on them pays back in mechanics, in electricity and in the investigation at the same time. This is the specific reason a Physics specialist beats a nearby generalist: a generalist helps the student get the right answer, and a specialist notices that the right answer was quoted to an impossible precision and that the marks were lost anyway.

sections.heading: The one local factor that is real: arrival time and usable attention
paragraphs: Having argued that geography does not decide tutor quality, it is worth being precise about the thing geography does decide. A student in Al Mizhar on a long bus route to Al Warqa or Al Qusais can arrive home in the late afternoon, hot, hungry and with the day's attention mostly spent. Book Physics at that moment and the hour buys you a tired student transcribing worked solutions. Book it ninety minutes later and the same hour buys attention.

The practical rule in the eastern suburbs is to put Physics after a break and a meal, and to keep the session to a length the student can hold. Sixty focused minutes beats ninety drifting ones, and two sessions of forty-five minutes on separate evenings beats a single ninety-minute block for a subject that needs problem practice rather than exposition. Online delivery helps here in a dull but genuine way: a video lesson can start at the time that suits the household, and it does not need a half-hour margin for somebody else's drive from Deira.

There is a second local factor worth planning around, which is the shape of the UAE week. The weekend falls on Saturday and Sunday, with a short Friday. A Saturday or Sunday morning slot gets a rested student and is the single most underused hour in most families' timetables. Midweek, the realistic window is one session, and starting it on a Tuesday or Wednesday gives the student time to act on the feedback before the school week ends. During Ramadan, sessions can move after Iftar and keep running rather than pausing for a month.

sections.heading: Verifying a Physics tutor in the UAE: permits and what you may ask
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences follow for an Al Mizhar parent comparing options. First, a tutor who tells you no permit is needed is wrong: individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted as unverified. Second, the permit is free, so a provider adding a licensing fee to your bill should be asked what exactly the fee covers.

There is a separate point about school staff. Press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff there are barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording with the relevant authority before relying on it. The practical reading for a Dubai family is simple enough: do not arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately for money, however convenient it looks. Note also that an operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a different thing from an individual's permit. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and does not describe itself as KHDA approved.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the Physics investigation, stated plainly
paragraphs: The independent investigation has to be the student's own work, and the boundary between teaching and malpractice is not vague. A tutor may explain what the assessment criteria ask for. A tutor may discuss whether a research question can be measured with the equipment available. A tutor may read a draft and say that the uncertainty treatment is thin, that the graph is plotted against the wrong variable, or that the evaluation lists limitations without ranking them. All of that is teaching.

A tutor may not write the investigation, draft a section of it, rewrite the student's sentences into their own, supply the data, or produce a method the student then adopts without understanding it. Some operators in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student's whole Diploma at risk, and it is not a service IB Gram will provide at any price. The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay.

The practical version for a parent is a test you can apply yourself. Ask your child to explain, without notes, why their method controls the variable it claims to control. If they can, the work is theirs and the tutoring has done its job. If they cannot, something has gone wrong regardless of how good the document looks. The same test works on any piece of coursework in any subject, and it is more useful than any assurance a provider gives you.

sections.heading: Starting: the trial, the match, and the coverage limit we will tell you about
paragraphs: The first step is a short consultation about the actual problem, which is rarely the one stated. A parent says Physics; the diagnostic conversation and a look at a marked script often show algebra, or uncertainty handling, or a student who understands the lesson and cannot start a question alone. Getting that right before booking matters more than the choice of tutor, because it decides what the first eight sessions are for.

Then a free trial lesson with the proposed tutor, one-to-one over live video. Treat it as a diagnostic rather than a demonstration: send the last marked Physics paper beforehand and ask the tutor to work through where the marks went. A tutor who can tell you which component is bleeding marks and why, inside an hour, is worth booking. One who spends the hour describing their experience is not. If the match is wrong, say so and ask for a different one; that is normal and early is the cheapest time to do it.

Here is the coverage limit, stated before you ask. Higher Level Physics specialists are scarce, and there are weeks when no UAE-based specialist has a free evening slot that suits an Al Mizhar schedule. Where that happens, IB Gram will say so and offer a specialist based elsewhere, teaching the same course over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time, rather than quietly substituting a general science tutor. You will be told which it is before you book. Across the eastern suburbs, that transparency is the whole of the argument: you are choosing the right Physics teacher, not the nearest one.

process.description: We look for someone who teaches Diploma Physics as their own subject at the level your child sits, with experience of the component you named. Because lessons are online, the search covers Physics specialists rather than whoever can reach Al Mizhar by seven in the evening.

process.description: One hour, one-to-one over live video, before any commitment. Ask the tutor to work through a marked paper and tell you where the marks went. You should finish the hour knowing what the first block of sessions will target and roughly how long it will take.

process.description: A weekly time chosen for when your child is actually capable of concentrating, after arrival and a break. Weekend mornings are available and are usually the most productive hour in the week. Ramadan timings move after Iftar rather than pausing.

process.description: Four sessions in, look at a marked piece of work rather than at a feeling. Has the uncertainty treatment changed? Are graph marks being picked up? If the evidence has not moved, we change the plan or the tutor instead of adding hours.

whyPoints.description: Sessions target the component that is losing marks rather than the subject in general. Uncertainty treatment and graph construction are the fastest gains in Physics, and both are independent of topic, so the work pays back across the whole course.
