whyPoints.description: Slots are set around when a child on a long bus route can actually think, and the UAE weekend is treated as the resource it is. Nobody needs a half-hour margin for a drive from Deira, so the hour starts when your household is ready.

faqs.question: Is it easier to find an IB Physics tutor in Mirdif than in Al Mizhar?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is structural rather than local. A Dubai secondary school running the Diploma usually has one or two teachers qualified to take Physics at Higher Level, because the cohort is small, and those people are employed full time by the school. That is true of schools in Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Khawaneej equally. Living nearer the school gate shortens your child's bus ride; it does not add Physics specialists to your neighbourhood. The choice that actually improves the teaching is a Physics specialist taught one-to-one over live video rather than the nearest available adult.

faqs.question: Why would I pay the same for an online Physics lesson as for a tutor who drives to Al Mizhar?
faqs.answer: You would not, and that is the point of the rate table above. Published Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor teaching online, and monthly in-home packages circulate at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against around AED 799 online. The gap is travel, not teaching quality. Spend the in-home premium on a Physics specialist instead of on an hour of somebody's driving and the subject expertise rises while the cost stays flat.

faqs.question: Does my child need Higher Level Physics for engineering at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Check the specific programme, because requirements vary by university and by course and they change. Engineering faculties commonly expect Physics and a mathematics subject at Higher Level, and some specify Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation. The reliable method is to read the admissions page for the exact degree your child wants, note the subject and level required, and plan the Diploma choices backwards from that. A tutor can help with the Physics; the entry requirement itself should come from the university, not from any tutoring provider.

faqs.question: How many Physics sessions a week does a Higher Level student in the eastern suburbs need?
faqs.answer: One well-placed session a week is the normal starting point, with a second added only for a specific reason such as a component that is badly behind or a term with an investigation deadline inside it. Two sessions on separate evenings beat one long block for Physics, because the subject needs problem practice between explanations rather than more exposition. For a student on a long bus route, the practical limit is attention rather than time, which is why a weekend morning slot often outperforms a second weekday evening.

faqs.question: My child understands Physics in class but freezes on the paper. What is going on?
faqs.answer: That pattern is almost always a problem with starting a question rather than with understanding the content. Following a worked solution uses recognition; starting cold requires choosing which relationship applies before any numbers appear. The fix is mechanical: practise identifying what is conserved, what is constant and what is being asked, on questions the student does not then complete. Ten openings in twenty minutes trains the skill that is missing far faster than three full solutions. It is one of the quickest changes a specialist Physics tutor can make.

faqs.question: What are error bars for, and why do they cost my child marks?
faqs.answer: Error bars show how precisely each point was measured, and they are drawn before the line of best fit because the line has to pass through them. Students who draw the line first and add bars afterwards have inverted the logic, and the error shows up again in every gradient and conclusion that follows. Marks are also lost when a conclusion states a relationship without attaching any uncertainty to it. This is learnable in a few sessions, applies to every topic, and is one of the clearest separations between a mid-range and a top Physics script.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Physics investigation without crossing an IB rule?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth stating plainly. A tutor may explain what the assessment criteria reward, discuss whether a research question can be measured with available equipment, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite the student's sentences, supply data or hand over a method the student does not understand. Operators selling completed Internal Assessments exist in this market; using one risks the entire Diploma. IB Gram does not provide that at any price.

faqs.question: What time should a Physics session start for a student travelling home to Al Mizhar?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume. A student arriving home in the late afternoon from Al Warqa or Al Qusais has spent most of the day's attention on the journey and the school day. Allow a break and a meal, then start. Ninety minutes after arrival is a reasonable default, and sixty focused minutes beats ninety drifting ones. Because lessons are online, the slot can be set around your household rather than around a tutor's drive across Dubai, which in practice means an earlier finish and a student who sleeps on time.

faqs.question: Does a Physics tutor teaching an Al Mizhar family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE requires a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure quoted to you as unverified.

faqs.question: Is a university student at Academic City a reasonable Physics tutor for a Higher Level candidate?
faqs.answer: For a younger student needing structure and company while working, often yes, and the published budget rates of roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour reflect that honestly. For a Higher Level candidate close to a paper, usually not. The gains at that stage come from someone who can mark a script against the scheme, name the component losing marks and explain why an explanation answer scored two out of four. That is a different skill from having passed the course recently, and it is what the specialist bands are charging for.

faqs.question: Which Physics topic should we start with if there is time for only one?
faqs.answer: Not a topic at all. Start with uncertainty treatment and graph work, because they are assessed everywhere and they are independent of content. A student who plots raw data properly, draws bars before the line, takes a gradient from the line and writes a conclusion with an uncertainty attached picks up marks in mechanics, in electricity, in the option content and in the investigation at once. Topic revision afterwards then lands on a student who can actually record what they have worked out.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor take Physics and Maths: Analysis and Approaches together?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a great deal of Physics difficulty is really algebra and calculus difficulty. A tutor who teaches both can fix the rearrangement inside the Physics question rather than treating it as someone else's problem. Where a single person cannot cover both at the level required, two specialists working to one plan is better than one generalist covering both badly. The decision should be made on the diagnostic, not on the convenience of a single invoice.

faqs.question: Does the Al Mizhar school mix change which Physics route my child takes?
faqs.answer: It changes the entry point rather than the destination. Students coming through the continuum at Uptown International School reach Diploma Physics from the Middle Years Programme, where science is assessed against criteria rather than by paper marks, so the first gap is usually formal uncertainty treatment and algebraic fluency. Students arriving from a British-curriculum school have met calculation-heavy papers but not criterion-based investigation work. Both arrive at the same Diploma course, and knowing which route your child took tells a tutor what to check in week one.

faqs.question: What should I send before a first Physics session for an Al Mizhar student?
faqs.answer: Four things, and they take ten minutes to gather. The most recent marked Physics paper or test, with the examiner's or teacher's comments left on it. The school's current topic and the next assessment date. The level sat, Higher or Standard, and the other subjects in the Diploma. And the realistic time your child walks through the door on a weekday. The first three let the tutor plan a diagnostic instead of a getting-to-know-you hour. The fourth decides whether the slot you book is one your child can actually use.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-muteena.tutorsIntro: The physics tutors below work from the student's own marked papers and the school's position in the two-year course. Each teaches to the current syllabus structure rather than an older one, which matters because the themes, the paper split and the IA criteria were all rebuilt in the most recent revision.

intro.heading: What an IB physics tutor should be working on in Al Muteena
paragraphs: Physics at IB Diploma level fails students in a small number of specific places, and an Al Muteena parent looking for help is usually describing one of them without knowing its name. The child understands the lesson but cannot start a Paper 2 question. The marks are fine on mechanics and collapse on fields. The Internal Assessment has been drafted three times and the teacher keeps saying the methodology is not sufficiently justified. These are different problems with different fixes, and lumping them together as weak at physics is why a generic tutor often achieves nothing.

The current Diploma Programme physics syllabus is organised into five themes: Space, time and motion; The particulate nature of matter; Wave behaviour; Fields; and Nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level studies the same themes with additional content and additional depth rather than a separate list of topics, which is a structural change from older versions of the course and the reason a tutor working from out-of-date material gives misleading advice about what is examinable.

Assessment is two written papers plus the Internal Assessment. Paper 1 is split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, and together Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade. Paper 2 carries 44% and is where extended response, unfamiliar context and multi-step reasoning are tested. The Scientific Investigation carries the remaining 20%, marked out of 24 across four criteria, with a 3,000-word limit on the report. Those proportions decide where tutoring time should go, and a student losing marks in Paper 2 is losing them from the largest single component.

Al Muteena sits in the older part of Dubai, close to Deira, with most of the cluster's IB Diploma provision a short bus ride away in Al Garhoud. That geography is the reason the in-home physics market here is thin and expensive: a DP physics specialist is a narrow profession in any city, and asking one to drive into Deira on a weekday evening narrows it further. Market rates for in-home one-to-one visits in Dubai run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against roughly AED 200 to AED 450 for an IB specialist teaching online.

IB Gram teaches Al Muteena students one-to-one over live video, with the student's own paper and marked IA draft shared on screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For a subject this narrow, the format is the substance of the offer: the question stops being who is nearby and becomes who teaches Paper 2 extended response and who has supervised a scientific investigation through all four criteria.

A final point on what this page is for. It names syllabus structures, mark allocations and published rates with their sources so that an Al Muteena parent can check a prospective tutor against something concrete rather than against adjectives. Ask which theme is weakest and why. Ask which component the first month is aimed at. Ask what the four IA criteria are worth. A physics teacher will answer all three in a sentence each.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-muteena.programmesIntro: Physics tutoring requests in this cluster come from three stages of a student's school career, and each needs a different starting point. The DP course is the one most Al Muteena enquiries are about, but the two routes into it matter as much.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Two years across five themes, assessed by Paper 1, Paper 2 and the Scientific Investigation. Higher Level adds content and depth inside the same themes and sits longer papers. The practical programme runs alongside the theory, and the investigation that becomes the IA is usually started in DP1 and submitted in DP2.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools examine in the May session, so an Al Muteena DP2 student is working to a spring examination window with the IA due to the school well before it. The internal deadline set by the school is the one that governs a student's workload, and it is usually several months earlier than any external date.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences into DP Physics
programmes.description: MYP sciences are marked against four criteria out of eight each, with inquiry and reflection weighted heavily. DP physics replaces that with mathematical modelling, algebraic rearrangement and precise use of defined terms. Students who were strong in MYP often find the first term of DP1 harsher than expected, and the gap is usually mathematics rather than physics.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Al Garhoud and Deira cluster run MYP through to Year 11 before the Diploma, so this transition is common locally. Six weeks of work on algebraic rearrangement, units and significant figures before DP1 starts does more for a physics grade than anything else available at that point.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics into DP Physics
programmes.description: An IGCSE physics course, whether Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1, covers much of the same territory at lower mathematical demand. The step up into DP is about treating equations as models rather than formulas to substitute into, and about writing answers that explain rather than state. Students arriving from Extended or Higher tier adapt faster than those from the lower tier.
programmes.countryNote: Because Old Dubai has both British and IB secondaries within a few kilometres, a student may sit IGCSE at one school and the Diploma at another. Where that happens, the summer between is the single most useful tutoring window in the whole two-year plan, and it is almost always unused.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-muteena.subjectsIntro: These are the physics areas Al Muteena students most often bring to a first session, written in terms of what the examination actually asks rather than as a topic list.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, with circular motion and the HL extension into rotational dynamics and relativity-adjacent content depending on the route. Marks are usually lost to sign conventions and to treating momentum problems as energy problems.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, internal energy and the kinetic model. The reliable mark loss here is in explanation questions that ask why a quantity changes, where students describe the change instead of explaining the mechanism.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave characteristics, superposition, standing waves, diffraction and interference. Diagram labelling carries real marks, and phase relationships are the single most misread part of the theme.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields treated as one idea with three contexts. Field and potential are confused constantly, and the HL extension into field strength calculations and electromagnetic induction is where Higher Level candidates separate.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and atomic spectra. Calculations here are usually straightforward; the lost marks are in definitions used imprecisely, which examiners mark strictly.

subjects.name: Paper 1B data analysis
subjects.description: Graph plotting, gradient interpretation, uncertainty propagation and significant figures on unfamiliar data. This section is a skill rather than a topic, it can be trained in a handful of sessions, and students rarely practise it separately from the multiple-choice half of Paper 1.

subjects.name: Paper 2 extended response
subjects.description: Multi-part questions in unfamiliar contexts carrying the largest share of the grade. The teachable skill is reading the command term, planning two lines before writing, and answering the question asked rather than the topic recognised.

subjects.name: Practical skills and uncertainties
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, error bars, and the difference between random and systematic error. This underpins both Paper 1B and the Internal Assessment, and it is the most common single weakness in an IA draft.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation
subjects.description: One independent investigation reported in up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A tutor coaches the process, questions the method and gives feedback on the student's own writing, and does not write any part of it.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what Higher Level adds to each
paragraphs: The current DP physics syllabus is built on five themes rather than a core plus options, and Higher Level extends the same themes instead of adding separate ones. That structure is worth understanding before buying tutoring, because it changes what a Standard Level student can safely skip. Under this arrangement there is no option topic to abandon: depth is distributed across all five themes, so a student who has written off fields cannot compensate by over-preparing mechanics.

The practical consequence for an Al Muteena student is that diagnosis has to be theme-level and specific. Marks lost in Space, time and motion usually come from sign conventions and from solving momentum problems with energy methods. Marks lost in Fields come from the confusion between field strength and potential, which is a conceptual repair rather than a practice problem. Marks lost in Nuclear and quantum physics are rarely calculation errors; they are definitions stated loosely, and examiners mark definitions strictly.

Higher Level candidates meet additional content within each theme and sit longer papers, which changes the pacing problem as well as the content problem. A Higher Level student who can do every question but not in the time available needs a different intervention from one who cannot do the questions. Those two students look identical on a mock result and need opposite plans, which is the argument for a diagnostic session before any package is agreed.

sections.heading: Paper 1, Paper 2 and the Investigation: the weightings that set the plan
paragraphs: Tutoring time should follow the marks. Paper 2 carries 44% of the physics grade, Paper 1 carries 36% across its multiple-choice and data-analysis sections, and the Scientific Investigation carries 20%. A family paying for weekly sessions should be able to say which of those three the current block is aimed at, and a tutor who cannot answer that question is teaching physics in general rather than preparing for this examination.

The structure also explains a common pattern. Students who revise by reading notes tend to improve on Paper 1 multiple choice and not at all on Paper 2, because the second paper tests whether unfamiliar context can be decoded rather than whether content is remembered. The fix is doing Paper 2 questions under time, marking them against the published scheme, and reading what the scheme rewarded. Most students have never read a mark scheme for their own answer, and the first time they do is usually the most useful hour of the term.

Paper 1B, the data-analysis section, is the most neglected part of the examination and the most trainable. It asks for graph work, gradient interpretation, uncertainty propagation and sensible significant figures on data the student has not seen before. None of that requires new physics, which is why a student eight weeks from the papers can still gain real marks there when the theory ship has largely sailed.

Higher Level and Standard Level candidates sit papers of different length on the same structure. The table sets out the components and what each one actually rewards, so a parent can ask for a plan expressed in those terms rather than in topics covered.

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment is the one part of the physics grade where a student has months of control and almost no external pressure, and it is where capable students most often leave marks behind. It is a single independent investigation reported in up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying six marks. No competitor page in this market names a single criterion, let alone its mark allocation.

The failures are predictable. Research design loses marks when the research question is too broad to be answered by the data collected, or when variables are listed without a justified method of control. Data analysis loses marks when uncertainties are mentioned rather than propagated, and when a graph is plotted without error bars or a considered line. Conclusion loses marks when the student restates the result instead of interpreting it against accepted physics. Evaluation loses marks when weaknesses are listed generically rather than tied to the specific data obtained.

The word limit is a genuine trap. A report over 3,000 words is not rewarded for the extra length, and students routinely spend their effort on background theory that earns nothing while compressing the evaluation that carries six marks. Reading the criteria before writing, rather than after, is the single highest-return piece of advice available on an IA.

What a tutor does here is bounded. The investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor asks whether the research question is measurable, challenges the control of variables, points to uncertainty treatment that will not survive marking, and gives written feedback on the student's draft. A tutor does not write, redraft to completion or produce any section of the report, and any provider offering to do so is proposing something that puts the student's diploma at risk.

sections.heading: Where physics marks go missing in a mock paper
paragraphs: A marked mock paper is the most informative document a parent can hand a tutor, and it almost always shows the same handful of patterns. The marks are not usually lost where the student felt uncertain. They are lost in places the student thought they had answered correctly, which is why self-assessment without a mark scheme is unreliable.

Command terms come first. State, describe, explain, outline, deduce and discuss each have a defined expectation, and an explanation offered where a description was asked for wastes time without gaining marks, while a description offered where an explanation was required gains almost nothing. Second is units and significant figures, which quietly remove marks across an entire paper rather than in one place. Third is the unit-less final answer after three lines of correct physics.

Fourth is the habit of starting to write before reading the whole question. Paper 2 questions build, and part (c) often tells you what part (a) was for. Fifth is time management: a Higher Level paper does not reward a perfect answer to question one followed by blank space. All five are behaviours, not knowledge gaps, which is why six weeks of focused work can move a physics grade even when the content is still imperfect.

The practical first step with a new student is to go through one marked paper line by line against the published scheme and count where the marks actually went. That produces a list of three or four named habits, and the first month of tutoring then has an agenda a parent can check.

sections.heading: What specialist physics tuition costs in Dubai, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Physics at Diploma level is a narrow specialism, and narrow specialisms are priced accordingly. Published market rates in Dubai put IB and IGCSE specialist tuition at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 or more an hour, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and BartyED publishing AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Qualified subject tutors teaching online are quoted from around AED 150 by Unitors for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to AED 52, which buys a general tutor rather than a DP physics teacher.

The interesting figure is the gap between in-home and online, because that gap is the only part of a tutoring invoice that buys no teaching. In-home one-to-one in Dubai is published at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with the Bestimate survey putting the ordinary band at AED 180 to AED 350. For a subject taught by a small number of people in the city, the travel premium also narrows the shortlist: the tutor has to be both a physics specialist and willing to drive into Deira in the evening, and those two conditions rarely coincide.

What the premium genuinely buys is physical presence, which matters for some students and not for others. What it does not buy is a better physicist. For an Al Muteena DP2 student whose problem is Paper 2 extended response and an IA evaluation, the useful variable is who has marked that paper and supervised that investigation, not who is nearby. Set against KHDA's confirmation on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, tutoring is the part of an education budget still moving.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly table on this page. The arrangement is a free trial lesson, a written diagnosis, then a plan sized to what the diagnosis shows, because a student repairing fields in DP1 and a student six weeks from the papers need different numbers of hours. Every figure above is attributed to the provider or survey that published it so a parent can verify it before relying on it.

sections.heading: Online physics for a practical subject: the honest comparison
paragraphs: Physics involves apparatus, so the question of whether it can be taught over video is a fair one. The answer depends on which part of the course is in question. The practical programme itself belongs to the school, which runs the laboratory work and supervises the investigation; a tutor's role in practical work is to interrogate design, uncertainty and analysis, all of which happen on paper and on screen rather than at a bench.

For theory, data analysis and examination technique, video delivery is at least as good as a kitchen table. The screen is shared, the student's own marked paper is on it, and the tutor watches the working appear in real time instead of reading a finished answer. Graph work and uncertainty propagation are better on a shared digital surface than on paper, because the tutor can annotate the same object the student is looking at. Sessions are recorded, so a derivation can be rewatched later in the week.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; that service is offered only in India. Lessons for Al Muteena families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. This is stated plainly because the alternative is a parent discovering it after payment, which is what happens on pages that route UAE families to a non-UAE telephone number without saying where the tutor is.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a physics tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: This section exists because one of the pages competing for these queries sells completed Internal Assessments. That is not a grey area. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, and submitting work produced by someone else is malpractice with consequences that fall on the student rather than on the provider who sold it.

The boundary is workable and clear in practice. A tutor may teach the physics, explain the criteria, question a research question until it becomes measurable, challenge a method, point out that an uncertainty treatment will not survive marking, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may discuss what the evaluation criterion rewards and ask the questions that make a student notice their own gap.

A tutor may not write any part of the report, redraft the student's text into something else, supply a method to copy, or produce the analysis. The practical test a parent can apply is whether the words in the document were typed by their child. If a tutor has made that question difficult to answer, something has gone wrong regardless of what the grade looks like.

There is also a sourcing boundary worth naming. Official syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, and reproducing or distributing them is not something a tutoring provider should do. The right approach is to reference them and point to the official source, which is also why this page links out rather than offering downloads.

sections.heading: The May session and the school deadlines that come first
paragraphs: Dubai IB schools examine in the May session, and an Al Muteena DP2 family planning tutoring should work backwards from that. The dates a student actually feels, though, are the school's internal ones: the IA draft deadline, the final IA submission to the teacher, the mock window and the point at which predicted grades are set. Those sit months before any external examination and they are set by the school, not the board.

This project does not publish specific IB examination or results dates, for a defensible reason: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no date here has been confirmed against the source. Any page that states an IB results date without naming where it read it is asking a parent to trust an unverified number. The correct instruction is to confirm the session dates with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, and to treat the school's internal calendar as the operational one.

For families with a child sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications alongside or before the Diploma, those calendars are published and sourced. Cambridge runs June and November series, and the February/March series is offered to India only, so it is not a route available in Dubai. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026.

The useful planning rule for physics is simple. Count backwards from the school's IA deadline first, because that is 20% of the grade with a fixed date and no second attempt, then plan paper technique into the window that remains. Families who do it the other way round usually find themselves supervising an investigation in the same fortnight as the mocks.

faqs.question: What should an IB physics tutor diagnose in the first session?
faqs.answer: Which component is leaking marks. Paper 2 carries 44% of the grade, Paper 1 carries 36% across multiple choice and data analysis, and the Scientific Investigation carries 20%. A student weak on Paper 2 extended response and a student weak on Paper 1B data analysis look similar on a mock percentage and need opposite plans. A first session should work through a marked paper against the published mark scheme and produce three or four named habits to attack, rather than starting a syllabus sweep from theme A.

faqs.question: How is the current DP physics course organised into themes?
faqs.answer: Five themes: Space, time and motion; The particulate nature of matter; Wave behaviour; Fields; and Nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level studies the same five with additional content and depth rather than separate option topics. That matters practically because there is no option to drop, so a student who has written off fields cannot compensate elsewhere. It also matters when choosing a tutor, since anyone working from older course structures will give misleading advice about what is examinable and how the depth is distributed.

faqs.question: How many marks is the physics Internal Assessment worth and how is it split?
faqs.answer: The Scientific Investigation carries 20% of the subject grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The report has a 3,000-word limit. Most lost marks come from a research question too broad for the data collected, uncertainties mentioned but never propagated, a conclusion that restates the graph rather than interpreting it, and generic limitations in the evaluation. Reading the criteria before writing rather than afterwards is the highest-return single piece of advice on an IA.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line between IA coaching and IB malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the physics, explain what each criterion rewards, question the research question until it is measurable, challenge the control of variables, flag an uncertainty treatment that will not survive marking, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, redraft or produce any section of the report, nor supply a method to copy. The test a parent can apply is whether their child typed the words. Providers selling completed investigations put the student's diploma at risk, not their own.

faqs.question: Is Paper 1B data analysis worth practising separately?
faqs.answer: It is the most neglected and most trainable part of the examination. The section gives unfamiliar data and asks for graph work, gradient interpretation, uncertainty propagation and sensible significant figures. None of that requires new content knowledge, which is why a student eight weeks from the papers can still gain real marks there when learning fresh theory has stopped being realistic. Most students practise Paper 1 as a single block of multiple choice and never work the data section on its own, which leaves the easiest available improvement untouched.

faqs.question: My son understands every lesson but freezes on Paper 2. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the two measure different things. Classwork rewards understanding the material in the context it was taught. Paper 2 presents unfamiliar contexts and multi-step reasoning, and asks the student to decide what physics applies before applying it. Students who revise by rereading notes improve on recall and not at all on this. The repair is doing Paper 2 questions under time, marking them against the published scheme, then reading what the scheme rewarded. Most students have never read a mark scheme for their own answer, and the first time is usually the most useful hour of the term.

faqs.question: Does online delivery work for a subject with laboratory work?
faqs.answer: For theory, data analysis and examination technique, yes, and in some respects better than a kitchen table: the student's own marked paper is on a shared screen, graph work can be annotated jointly, and the tutor watches working appear rather than reading a finished answer. The practical programme itself belongs to the school, which runs the laboratory and supervises the investigation. A tutor's contribution to practical work is design, uncertainty and analysis, all of which happen on paper. What video does not give is physical presence, which some students genuinely need.

faqs.question: Will someone come to our building in Al Muteena to teach physics?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits exist only in India. Lessons here are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In-home physics tutoring in Al Muteena is available from independent tutors and agencies at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, and choosing it is reasonable. The hidden cost is the shortlist: the tutor must be both a DP physics specialist and willing to drive into Deira in the evening, and those two conditions rarely overlap.

faqs.question: How much does a DP physics specialist charge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put IB and IGCSE specialist tuition at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 or more an hour. TutorChase quotes AED 270; BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor; Unitors advertises IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. At the lower end EdFlik lists from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to AED 52, which buys general academic help rather than DP physics depth. Those are market rates with named sources, not an IB Gram price list, and should be checked on the provider's current page.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost the most marks in physics papers?
faqs.answer: Explain and deduce, because both are commonly answered as describe. State, describe, explain, outline, deduce and discuss each carry a defined expectation, and answering at the wrong depth either wastes time or earns nothing. An explanation given where a description was asked for costs minutes and gains no extra credit; a description given where an explanation was required gains almost nothing at all. Working through one marked paper and counting the command terms that were misread usually produces a shorter and more actionable list than any revision guide.

faqs.question: When should a DP1 student start physics tutoring rather than waiting?
faqs.answer: The two highest-value windows are the term in which fields and thermal physics are taught, because both are conceptual repairs that compound if left, and the months in which the investigation is designed. Waiting until DP2 mocks means arriving with a conceptual gap and a submitted IA, neither of which can be fixed quickly. A DP1 student with one weak theme and an open investigation is in the best possible position to use tutoring, and usually needs fewer total hours than a DP2 student with the same underlying problem.

faqs.question: Do you publish the IB exam dates for this year's May session?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been verified against the source, and publishing an unverified date a parent might act on is worse than publishing none. Confirm the session with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. Cambridge and Pearson dates are different: those are sourced, so this page states that Cambridge runs June and November series and that Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor cover physics and the maths it depends on?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is worth asking during matching rather than assuming either way. A DP physics specialist usually teaches Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches competently, and the algebraic rearrangement, graph work and uncertainty handling overlap genuinely. Where a student needs Higher Level maths at depth as well as physics at depth, two specialists normally beat one person covering both. The deciding factor is the specific tutor's subject depth at the level required, which is established during matching rather than promised in advance on a web page.

faqs.question: What happens if no physics specialist is free at the time we need?
faqs.answer: You are told that, with a realistic date, rather than offered whoever is available. DP physics is a narrower pool than mathematics, and a specific constraint such as an early-morning slot before school can take longer to fill. Substituting a general science tutor for a Higher Level physics request wastes a family's money and a student's term, so it is not done. If the request cannot be matched well, the honest answer is a waiting date or a recommendation to look elsewhere, and that is what no competitor page in this market discloses.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-nahda.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB physics to Al Nahda students one at a time over live video, at a slot that survives a normal school week. Each works from the current guide's themes and the paper structure your child will actually sit, Standard Level or Higher.

intro.heading: Physics has to fit a Tuesday that is already full
paragraphs: Most physics tutoring fails on scheduling rather than on teaching. A family books an ambitious slot, the slot collides with the real shape of the week, sessions get moved, moved sessions get crammed, and crammed sessions are the least productive hours anybody pays for. In Al Nahda that collision is sharper than in most Dubai neighbourhoods, because of where the neighbourhood sits and what the week already contains.

Al Nahda lies on the Dubai side of the Sharjah boundary, with Al Nahda Street and Al Ittihad Road carrying cross-emirate commuter traffic through the same late-afternoon window that families want for tuition. A Diploma student from Al Nahda is usually already travelling, because the IB Diploma provision this neighbourhood uses sits in Garhoud, Mamzar and Festival City rather than inside Al Nahda itself. School finishes, the return leg takes longer than the outbound one, and the usable evening starts later than a timetable on paper suggests.

The week also carries fixed load that families arriving from elsewhere do not expect. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA calculates the instructional time for those subjects on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. That time is already allocated before a physics tutor asks for an hour.

On top of that sit the Diploma's own pressure points: internal assessment deadlines set by the school, a mock fortnight roughly a term before the written papers, and the laboratory work that feeds the scientific investigation. A physics tutor who treats all weeks as equivalent will be asking for an hour during the fortnight the student has three drafts due, and the hour will be bought and wasted.

IB Gram works around this by removing the one variable nobody can fix, which is the journey. Al Nahda physics lessons are one-to-one over live video, screen-shared, on Gulf Standard Time, which means a session can begin the moment the student is at a desk rather than when a tutor has finished crossing Al Ittihad Road. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. A family who specifically wants somebody physically present should hire locally, and the published Dubai band for that is AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is included.

The rest of this page is built on that week. It sets out when a physics session realistically fits, how the papers divide the grade, what the scientific investigation demands and when it has to start, how much mathematics physics quietly assumes, how practical and data skills are taught over video, and which topics are worth a holiday block instead of a weekly hour.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-nahda.programmesIntro: Al Nahda students reach IB physics by several routes, and the route decides how much of the first term is spent catching up rather than moving forward. These are the programmes that feed into it locally.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Standard or Higher Level across five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Assessment is Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the internal scientific investigation at 20%. Higher Level adds depth inside every theme rather than bolting on separate options, which is why the Higher Level jump is felt as pace rather than as new territory.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma physics places used by Al Nahda families sit mainly in Garhoud, Mamzar and Festival City, so a physics student from this neighbourhood is commuting daily. That journey is the reason an evening online slot outperforms an afternoon in-home one here: the student is home and at a desk before any visiting tutor could have arrived.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Criterion-marked sciences on a 0-8 scale rather than examined against a content list, with physics taught inside an integrated sciences course for much of the programme. Students arrive in Diploma physics having met the ideas and rarely having met a timed paper that demands algebraic rearrangement under pressure.
programmes.countryNote: Several Deira and Garhoud schools run MYP continuously into the Diploma, which makes this the most common entry route for Al Nahda physics students. The gap to close in the first term is assessment technique and mathematical fluency, not physics content.

programmes.name: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 Physics
programmes.description: The other main entry route. Core and Extended on Cambridge, with practical skills assessed through either Paper 5, a timed practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative-to-practical written paper. Students who sat Paper 6 arrive in Diploma physics with less apparatus handling than those who sat Paper 5, which shows up in the investigation rather than in the written papers.
programmes.countryNote: Al Nahda's British-curriculum feeder schools run IGCSE at 16 before splitting towards A Level or the Diploma. Students moving from Extended physics into Standard Level usually cope; those moving into Higher Level with weak algebra find the first term unexpectedly hard.

programmes.name: AS and A Level Physics
programmes.description: The alternative senior route, three or four subjects in depth with separate practical endorsement arrangements depending on the board. Tutoring demand is concentrated differently: fewer subjects, more hours each, and a heavier mathematical load earlier than in Diploma Standard Level physics.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Al Nahda choosing A Level over the Diploma often do it to drop a subject count that a cross-emirate commute makes unmanageable. That is a reasonable logistical decision and it changes the tutoring shape rather than the amount.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-nahda.subjectsIntro: Physics is one subject and a dozen separate difficulties. These are the parts of the current guide where Al Nahda students most often need a tutor, with what actually goes wrong in each.

subjects.name: Theme A: space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, work, energy, momentum and circular motion, with rigid-body mechanics and relativity at Higher Level. Students lose marks on sign conventions and on problems where two conservation laws apply at once, because they choose a law before deciding what the system is.

subjects.name: Theme B: the particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, the ideal gas model and current electricity. Specific heat capacity and latent heat questions fail on unit handling rather than on physics, and circuit questions fail on reasoning about what the circuit does when a component changes.

subjects.name: Theme C: wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave models, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with diffraction and resolution extended at Higher Level. Phase relationships are the usual fault line: students can describe a standing wave and cannot say what two points on it are doing relative to each other.

subjects.name: Theme D: fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, induction and motional emf, with orbital motion and field potential developed further at Higher Level. This theme is where Higher Level students lose the most marks, because the mathematics and the conceptual load rise together.

subjects.name: Theme E: nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear binding energy, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and matter waves. Taught late in most schools and therefore the theme most likely to be met in a rush, which makes it a strong candidate for a holiday block rather than a weekly hour.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: A single student-designed investigation written up within the published word limit, marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The commonest loss is a conclusion that restates the data instead of comparing it to accepted physics with a stated uncertainty.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error analysis
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and uncertainty bars with a worst-acceptable-line gradient. Carries marks in Paper 1B and heavily in the investigation, and is the single most reliably under-taught skill in school physics courses.

subjects.name: Graph work and linearisation
subjects.description: Choosing what to plot so that a relationship becomes a straight line, then extracting a physical quantity from the gradient or intercept. Students who can plot and cannot linearise lose marks in both the written papers and the investigation.

subjects.name: Algebraic rearrangement in physics
subjects.description: Not a physics topic, but the most frequent hidden cause of lost physics marks. Students who hesitate over rearranging a formula under time pressure run out of paper time rather than running out of understanding, and the fix sits outside the physics syllabus entirely.

subjects.name: Command terms and paper discipline
subjects.description: Deduce, outline, explain, justify, suggest and determine each demand a different structure and length of answer. Marks are lost routinely by students who know the physics and answer a different command than the one printed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches support
subjects.description: Physics assumes competence with logarithms, small-angle approximations, trigonometric identities and basic calculus reasoning. Students taking Applications and Interpretation alongside Higher Level physics often need these supported deliberately rather than assumed.

subjects.name: Chemistry crossover for physics students
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws and nuclear content overlap with Diploma chemistry. Students taking both can be taught the shared mathematics once, which saves hours and makes the overlap an advantage rather than a duplication.

sections.heading: When a physics session actually fits an Al Nahda week
paragraphs: The honest answer is later than families plan for. A Dubai school day ends in the early-to-mid afternoon, the return journey from Garhoud or Mamzar into Al Nahda runs against the heaviest cross-emirate flow of the day, and a 16-year-old who has just spent that time in a car is not ready to reason about momentum conservation for sixty minutes. Allow for arrival, food and twenty minutes of nothing, and the first genuinely productive weekday slot is early evening.

This is where the delivery format earns its place rather than being a compromise. An online session starts when the student sits down. A visiting tutor's session starts when the tutor arrives, and the arrival window in Al Nahda between 4pm and 7pm is wide enough that families routinely lose the first ten minutes of an hour they paid for. Over a two-year Diploma course that difference compounds into a meaningful number of lost sessions.

Three recurring pressures then decide which weeks are usable at all. School assessment fortnights come round two or three times a year and are the wrong weeks to add an hour, because the student's time is already committed to work that counts. Internal assessment deadlines set by the school cluster unevenly and will swallow an evening whether or not a tutor is booked. Ramadan moves the usable evening entirely, and shifting a session to a post-Iftar slot is an ordinary accommodation rather than an exception.

The workable pattern is therefore one protected weekday evening hour with a problem set due before it, a longer weekend session when investigation work is live, and an agreed policy for assessment fortnights and travel. Agreeing that policy at the start is worth more over two years than a small reduction in the hourly rate, because it determines how many of the hours you paid for actually took place.

sections.heading: How the physics grade is actually divided
paragraphs: Families budget revision time by subject and almost never by component, which means most physics revision is distributed roughly opposite to where the marks sit. The current guide divides the grade three ways and the proportions are published, so there is no reason to guess.

Paper 1 carries 36%. It comes in two parts: Paper 1A is multiple choice, and Paper 1B is a set of data-based and experimental questions. That second part is the one schools under-prepare, because it tests uncertainty handling, graph interpretation and experimental reasoning rather than recall, and those skills are usually taught incidentally during practical work rather than deliberately. A student who treats Paper 1 as a recall test is leaving the easier marks of the two halves on the table.

Paper 2 carries 44% and is the extended-response paper, with Standard Level sitting ninety minutes and Higher Level sitting two and a half hours. Length changes the skill: a Higher Level student has to pace across a longer paper and hold quality through the final questions, which is a stamina problem that only timed full papers reveal. Standard Level students more often lose marks to command-term mismatches than to running out of time.

The internal scientific investigation carries the remaining 20%, which is a fifth of the grade awarded for a single piece of work the student designs and writes themselves. It is also the only component where a family has months of advance warning and complete control over the timetable. Treating it as a fifth of the revision budget rather than as a piece of homework is the single clearest planning decision available in Diploma physics.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, counted backwards from the deadline
paragraphs: A fifth of the physics grade rests on one investigation, and the deadline is set by the school rather than the board, which means it lands earlier than students expect and in the same weeks as other subjects' internal deadlines. Counting backwards from it is the only reliable way to keep it from being written in a weekend.

The marking is criterion-based, covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Each criterion fails in a characteristic way. Research design fails when the variables are not genuinely controllable or the method cannot produce enough data to show a relationship. Data analysis fails when uncertainties are quoted without being propagated, or when the graph plotted is not the graph that linearises the relationship. Conclusion fails when it restates the trend rather than comparing a measured value to accepted physics with a stated uncertainty. Evaluation fails when weaknesses are listed generically instead of being tied to the specific data obtained.

The order of useful help is therefore the reverse of what students ask for. By the time a draft exists, the design is fixed and most of the available marks are already decided. The high-value conversation happens before data collection: is this relationship measurable with this apparatus, will the range give enough points, what is the dominant uncertainty, and what will be plotted against what. An hour spent there is worth several hours spent polishing a write-up built on a method that could not have worked.

What a tutor may do here is bounded and worth stating plainly. A tutor may explain the criteria, question the design, ask what a graph shows, point at a conclusion that does not follow from its own data, and mark practice work. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a section, or edit a draft into a finished state. The deliverable from a good investigation session is the student knowing what to change, with the changes still unmade. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequences fall on the student, not the seller.
bullets: Research design: controllable variables, adequate range, enough data points
Data analysis: uncertainties propagated, and the graph that linearises the relationship
Conclusion: a measured value compared to accepted physics, with uncertainty stated
Evaluation: weaknesses tied to the actual data, not a generic list
The useful conversation happens before data collection, not after the first draft

sections.heading: How much mathematics physics quietly assumes
paragraphs: A large share of lost physics marks are not physics mistakes. They are rearrangement, logarithm and trigonometry mistakes made under time pressure by students who understand the physics perfectly well. Diagnosing this correctly saves a family money, because the fix sits outside the physics syllabus and takes a fraction of the time that re-teaching physics would.

The standing assumptions are specific. Rearranging multi-variable formulae fluently, including when the unknown appears twice. Handling indices and standard form without a calculator prompt. Using logarithms to linearise exponential relationships, which appears in radioactive decay and in capacitor discharge. Small-angle approximations in wave and oscillation work. Trigonometric resolution of vectors in two dimensions, with sign conventions kept straight. Gradients and areas under graphs read as physical quantities rather than as geometry.

The mismatch shows up most clearly in students taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation alongside Higher Level physics. That is a legitimate and common combination, but the two courses emphasise different skills, and the algebraic manipulation physics leans on is developed more directly in Analysis and Approaches. Those students need the specific techniques supported deliberately rather than assumed, and the support is cheap because the list is short.

Testing for this takes one session. Give the student a set of physics questions where the physics is easy and the algebra is not, and watch where the time goes. If they hesitate for ten seconds before every rearrangement, the problem is not fields or thermodynamics. It is the thing underneath, and three targeted sessions on it will do more for the grade than a term of theme revision.

sections.heading: Teaching practical and data skills over live video
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online physics is the laboratory, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. A video link cannot put a student's hands on a travelling microscope. What it can do, and in practice does better than a crowded school laboratory, is teach the reasoning that the practical marks actually reward.

Start with where those marks live. Paper 1B is data-based and experimental, and the investigation is assessed on design, analysis, conclusion and evaluation. None of those four is a manual-dexterity assessment. They are judgements about whether a method can answer a question, whether uncertainty has been handled honestly, and whether a conclusion follows from the data. All of that is taught better with a shared screen, a real data set and a tutor asking why, than standing at a bench with twenty other students and forty minutes.

The mechanics are straightforward. The student's own raw data goes on screen. Uncertainty columns get built together. Graphs are plotted, and then re-plotted differently when the first attempt fails to linearise. A worst-acceptable line is drawn and a gradient uncertainty extracted from it. The student explains what the intercept means physically and discovers, out loud, whether they believe their own result. Published simulations stand in where a phenomenon needs to be seen rather than handled.

The school still owns the apparatus work, and that is the right division. Your child's physics teacher runs the practical programme and supervises the investigation. A tutor's job is the reasoning around it: interrogating a method before data is collected, and interrogating the data afterwards. For a Cambridge IGCSE student who sat Paper 6, the alternative to practical, rather than Paper 5, this reasoning gap is usually wider on arrival in the Diploma than anybody has noticed.
bullets: Paper 1B rewards experimental reasoning, not apparatus handling
Uncertainty propagation and linearisation are screen-shared skills by nature
Worst-acceptable-line gradients teach uncertainty better than any explanation

sections.heading: Which topics deserve a holiday block rather than a weekly hour
paragraphs: Not all physics content responds to the same schedule. Some topics are cumulative and suit a weekly hour that tracks the course. Others are coherent wholes that fall apart when delivered in sixty-minute slices a week apart, and those are the ones to buy as a block during a school holiday.

Fields is the clearest example. Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields share a structure, and the point of the theme is that the structure repeats. Taught across six separate weekly hours interrupted by school assessment fortnights, students learn three unconnected topics and miss the analogy that makes the theme manageable. Taught in four consecutive sessions over a holiday week, the analogy does the work and the content halves in difficulty.

Nuclear and quantum physics is the second. It is covered last in most school courses, which means it arrives when revision has already started and gets compressed. Learning it properly in a holiday block before the course reaches it inverts that problem: the student meets school lessons as revision rather than as first contact, which is a materially better experience in the exam year.

Against that, the topics that suit a weekly hour are the cumulative skills: uncertainty handling, graph work, algebraic fluency and command-term discipline. Those improve through repeated small doses with marked work in between, and a holiday intensive on them produces a short-lived spike. The sensible plan uses both shapes deliberately, which also spreads the cost across the year rather than concentrating it in the exam term when hours are least able to add content.

sections.heading: What physics support costs in this market
paragraphs: Rates belong on this page because a schedule is only realistic if it is affordable. What follows is the market's published pricing, read in October 2026, attributed to whoever published it. None of it is an IB Gram price list; IB Gram's cost is discussed after the free trial, once a tutor has seen the student's work.

The lowest published tier is budget online support, with Tutopiya advertising from roughly AED 33 to AED 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. That tier can supervise homework and drill recall. For Higher Level fields or an investigation evaluation it is the wrong purchase, because the work needs somebody who can mark against the published criteria.

The tier most Diploma physics families use is a qualified subject tutor working online, where Unitors publishes an IB entry rate from AED 200 an hour and TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. In-home delivery is published at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to AED 500 by independent home tutors, the difference being the journey rather than the teaching.

Translated into a year, a single protected weekly hour at the specialist band is roughly AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 a month on Bestimate's own monthly estimates for exam-year support. A plan that uses a weekly hour through the first year, two holiday blocks, and a concentrated final term costs less in total than two hours a week for two years and does more, because the hours land where the content and the deadlines actually are.
