sections.heading: Who may teach, and what nobody may promise
paragraphs: Two rules shape any tutoring arrangement in Dubai and both are worth checking before the first session. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The u.ae guidance states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so nobody should quote you an amount.

The second is who may be asked. Abu Dhabi's ADEK professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Asking your child's own physics teacher to tutor them privately is therefore the wrong request, however practical it sounds when a deadline is close.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity again, requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps. Holding either permit does not make anybody KHDA approved as a tutor, and IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

Alongside that sits what nobody can honestly promise. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a points total or a university place, and a provider implying otherwise is describing something outside anybody's control. No statistic should appear without the number it is drawn from, the date and the method. Nor should a tutor be described as a current IB examiner without evidence, and examiner status must never be presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content.

process.title: Measure your own week first
process.description: Time the gap between the school bell and your child sitting at a desk ready to work, on three normal days. That number, not an idealised afternoon, is what the physics slot has to fit around, and it is usually forty minutes later than families assume.

process.title: Send the level, the themes covered and the deadline dates
process.description: Standard or Higher Level, which of the five themes the school has reached, and the school's own internal assessment deadlines. Those three facts let a first session work on what is live rather than on what a generic physics course would cover in month four.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session on real material, no payment and no commitment, ending in a written view of where the marks are going. Often that view identifies algebraic fluency rather than physics content, which changes what the following term should cost.

process.title: Fix one protected slot and the exception policy
process.description: Agree the weekday evening hour on Gulf Standard Time, plus what happens during school assessment fortnights, Ramadan, Eid and travel. Over two years that policy protects more paid hours than any discount on the rate.

process.title: Book the investigation sessions before the data is collected
process.description: Put two longer weekend sessions in the calendar at the design stage and the first-draft stage. Help before collection is worth several times help afterwards, because by the time a draft exists the design is fixed and most of the marks are already decided.

process.title: Use holidays for the themes taught last
process.description: Block the fields theme and the nuclear and quantum theme into consecutive holiday sessions ahead of the school reaching them. School lessons then act as revision instead of first contact, which is a materially easier exam year.

whyPoints.title: Built around a commuting week
whyPoints.description: Al Nahda Diploma students mostly travel to Garhoud, Mamzar or Festival City and come home through the slowest hour of the day. Sessions are placed after that journey rather than inside it, and an online lesson starts at the desk rather than at the door.

whyPoints.title: Weighted the way the grade is weighted
whyPoints.description: Paper 1 is 36%, Paper 2 is 44% and the investigation is 20%. Preparation is divided accordingly, including deliberate work on Paper 1B's data and experimental questions, which school courses most often teach incidentally.

whyPoints.title: The investigation treated as a fifth of the grade
whyPoints.description: Help is scheduled before data collection, where it changes the available marks, rather than after a draft exists. Feedback comes as questions on the student's own work; no text is ever supplied, rewritten or edited to completion.

whyPoints.title: Algebra diagnosed, not assumed
whyPoints.description: A large share of lost physics marks are rearrangement and logarithm errors under time pressure. Finding that in session one is cheaper for a family than discovering it in April, and it is a short fix rather than a long one.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online and stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Al Nahda physics lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is an India-only service, and the published local rates for that route appear on this page.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, no unsourced numbers
whyPoints.description: No promised grade or points total, no claimed success rate, no self-asserted rating. Every AED figure here names its publisher and the month it was read, and the regulators discussed are explained rather than claimed as endorsements.

faqs.question: When does a weekday IB physics session realistically start in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: Later than most families plan. A Dubai school day ends in the early-to-mid afternoon, and the drive back into Al Nahda from Garhoud, Mamzar or Festival City runs against the heaviest cross-emirate traffic of the day. Add arrival, a meal and twenty minutes of decompression, and the first genuinely productive weekday slot is early evening. The useful exercise is to time the gap between the school bell and your child actually sitting at a desk on three normal days, then place the session after that number rather than before it.

faqs.question: Does crossing into Sharjah traffic rule out a 5pm physics lesson?
faqs.answer: It rules out a reliable one with a visiting tutor, and it does not affect an online one. Al Nahda sits against the Sharjah boundary with Al Nahda Street and Al Ittihad Road both carrying cross-emirate commuter flow through the late afternoon. A tutor who agrees to arrive at five is committing to an unpredictable journey, which is why families report losing the first ten minutes of hours they paid for. A video lesson begins when the student sits down, so the question becomes whether the student is ready rather than whether the roads cooperated.

faqs.question: How long should an IB physics session run on a school night?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes, with rare exceptions. A Diploma student who has travelled home through peak traffic has limited high-quality attention left, and the last twenty minutes of a ninety-minute weekday session are usually worth less than the paper they are written on. Two-hour blocks exist in this market because in-home packages have to amortise a journey over more teaching, and that logic does not apply online. Longer sessions belong at weekends, where they are genuinely useful for investigation work that needs quiet, continuous time.

faqs.question: Is a Friday afternoon physics slot better than a weekday one?
faqs.answer: For some things, yes. Weekend time is the right place for the scientific investigation, because interrogating a method, building uncertainty columns and re-plotting a graph that failed to linearise all need continuous quiet rather than a squeezed hour. It is also better for holiday-style blocks on a whole theme. For the cumulative skills, uncertainty handling, algebraic fluency and command-term discipline, a weekday slot with marked work due before it works better, because those improve by frequency rather than by length.

faqs.question: How do the physics papers split their marks at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% and runs two hours at Higher Level, combining Paper 1A multiple choice with Paper 1B data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 carries 44% and runs two and a half hours as the extended-response paper. The internal scientific investigation carries the remaining 20%. The practical consequence is that a fifth of the grade comes from one piece of work the student designs and controls, and that Paper 1B rewards experimental reasoning rather than recall, which is the half of Paper 1 school courses most often under-prepare.

faqs.question: What is in Paper 1A and Paper 1B of IB physics?
faqs.answer: They sit within the same paper and test different things. Paper 1A is multiple choice across the five themes, where marks are usually lost to a well-constructed distractor rather than to missing physics. Paper 1B is a set of data-based and experimental questions, testing uncertainty handling, graph interpretation, gradient extraction and judgements about method. Because 1B skills are often picked up incidentally during school practical work rather than taught deliberately, preparing the two halves separately is one of the clearest gains available in physics revision.

faqs.question: How much maths does IB physics assume a student already has?
faqs.answer: More than the physics guide spells out. Fluent rearrangement of multi-variable formulae, including when the unknown appears twice. Indices and standard form without prompting. Logarithms for linearising exponential relationships, which appear in radioactive decay. Small-angle approximations in oscillation and wave work. Vector resolution with sign conventions held straight. Gradients and areas under graphs read as physical quantities. Students taking Applications and Interpretation alongside Higher Level physics often need these supported deliberately, and that support is short and cheap compared with re-teaching physics content.

faqs.question: Can physics practical skills be taught without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: The reasoning can, and the reasoning is where the marks are. Paper 1B and the investigation assess research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, none of which is a test of apparatus handling. With the student's own raw data on a shared screen you can build uncertainty columns, plot and re-plot until a relationship linearises, draw a worst-acceptable line and extract a gradient uncertainty from it. The school keeps the apparatus work and supervises the investigation, which is the correct division of labour rather than a workaround.

faqs.question: When in the two years should physics tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Earlier and lighter beats later and heavier. A weekly hour through the first year, aimed at uncertainty handling, algebraic fluency and the themes as they arrive, costs the same per hour as exam-term support and does considerably more, because content can still be learned and consolidated. The exam year then needs a concentrated final term rather than a rescue operation. Families who reverse that order buy more hours in total and get less from them, because the last fortnight before the papers cannot add content that was never covered.

faqs.question: Do physics sessions move after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be agreed before the month starts rather than negotiated during it. Ramadan changes the usable evening entirely for most families, and a post-Iftar slot is an ordinary accommodation rather than a special arrangement. Because lessons are delivered over live video there is no journey to replan, so a seasonal change of slot is straightforward. The thing worth deciding in advance is whether the frequency drops for the month as well as the timing, which depends on where the school's own deadlines sit.

faqs.question: What happens to our physics slot during the school's mock fortnight?
faqs.answer: The sensible answer is that it changes purpose rather than continuing unchanged. During the school's own assessment weeks the student's time is committed to work that counts, so adding new content is the wrong use of the hour. Either pause and bank the sessions, or convert them into marked past-paper work that doubles as mock preparation. The fortnight immediately after mocks is the single most valuable window in the year for a diagnostic session, because a marked mock script is free evidence the school has already produced.

faqs.question: How many physics hours fit around Arabic and Islamic Education lessons?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the school day's length suggests. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA calculates that instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, permits schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. That time is allocated before any tutor asks for an hour, which is why one protected weekly physics hour with marked work between sessions usually outperforms attempting two or three.

faqs.question: Does an IB physics tutor need to follow my child's school scheme of work?
faqs.answer: Partly, and following it exclusively is a trap. Knowing which of the five themes the school has reached stops a tutor teaching fields in October when the class is still on kinematics. Following the scheme week by week, though, means re-teaching Tuesday's lesson every Wednesday and never touching the uncertainty handling or algebraic fluency underneath, which is what the papers probe. The workable arrangement is a tutor who tracks the school's position and the school's deadlines while running their own diagnosis of what is actually costing marks.

faqs.question: Which physics topics are worth a holiday block rather than a weekly hour?
faqs.answer: Fields first. Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields share a structure, and the analogy that makes the theme manageable is invisible when the content arrives in sixty-minute slices a week apart. Four consecutive sessions over a holiday week make it one topic instead of three. Nuclear and quantum physics is second, because it is covered last in most school courses and otherwise met during revision. Cumulative skills work the other way: uncertainty, algebra and command terms improve through small weekly doses with marked work between them.

faqs.question: Is a 30-minute physics session ever worth booking?
faqs.answer: For a narrow job, yes. Half an hour is enough to work through one marked question set, settle one specific confusion, or review a single criterion of an investigation draft. It is not enough to teach a theme or to attempt a timed paper. The useful pattern is a short session inserted between regular hours during a heavy fortnight, which keeps continuity without adding load. What it should not be is a cheaper substitute for a proper hour, because setup and recall consume a disproportionate share of a short slot.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to a building in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one teaching to UAE families over live video, screen-shared and scheduled on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are offered only in India. For physics specifically this is an advantage rather than a compromise, because the constraint on a visiting tutor is who holds Higher Level physics depth and can cross Al Ittihad Road by five o'clock, and that pool is small. A family who wants a person in the room should hire locally, where the published Dubai band runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-nahda.closingHeading: Place the slot where the week actually has room
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-nahda.closingBody: Before choosing a tutor, time three school days from the bell to your child sitting at a desk ready to work. Then ask the school for the current theme and the internal assessment deadline dates. Those two pieces of information decide more about whether physics tutoring works than any comparison of hourly rates, because an hour that happens beats an hour that was booked. Take the free trial lesson, agree one protected evening slot and an exception policy for assessment fortnights and Ramadan, and keep the longer sessions for the investigation.

intro.heading: Understanding the physics is not the same as being paid for it
paragraphs: The characteristic IB Physics problem is not ignorance. It is a student who can explain a phenomenon correctly in conversation, writes something true in the examination, and scores two marks out of five. Parents read the grade as a knowledge gap and buy content teaching. The marked script usually says something else entirely: the answer described rather than explained, the gradient was used without units, the uncertainty was ignored, or the named law that the question was testing never appeared.

That is why this page is built around the mark scheme rather than around the topic list. You will find the syllabus themes with what each is actually tested on, the demands of each paper, a table of the specific traps that recur in marked Al Quoz scripts with what the scheme wanted instead, a proper treatment of uncertainty and graph work, and the internal investigation criteria with an honest account of what a tutor may do with a draft.

Physics also has an unusually sharp divide between Standard and Higher Level, and it is not simply more content. Higher Level questions require longer chains of reasoning held together under time pressure, and a student who copes at Standard Level by answering each part independently finds that strategy fails. The fix is not more topics; it is practice at sustaining an argument across a multi-part question, which is a trainable skill nobody teaches explicitly.

Confirm specifics against the subject guide your child's school holds. The IB revises its guides, the current Physics course differs from its predecessor in how practical and data work is assessed, and we do not reproduce or supply IB documents because they are the organisation's copyright. What this page gives you is the shape of the assessment and the failures that recur within it, both of which outlast any particular revision.

The district holds its housing in Al Quoz 1, 2 and 3 between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, with the rest given over to warehouses, workshops, showrooms and the Alserkal Avenue arts spaces. Children travel outwards to school in several directions, so a weekday session realistically starts between 5pm and 5.30pm. That is long enough for one full data question and the marking of it, which is the natural unit of a physics session.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-quoz.subjectsIntro: Physics is best organised by what is assessed rather than by chapter. Below are the content areas and components Al Quoz students most often need, each with the specific failure that recurs in marked work.

subjects.name: Motion, forces and momentum
subjects.description: Kinematics, Newton's laws, momentum and impulse. The recurring failure is an answer that states what happens to an object rather than naming the law that makes it happen, which forfeits the explanation marks even when the physics is understood.

subjects.name: Work, energy and power
subjects.description: Energy transfer, efficiency and power calculations. Students lose marks by writing an energy statement without specifying which store the energy moved from and to, and by treating efficiency as a ratio without stating what was wasted.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat and the gas laws. Characteristic errors are temperature units left in Celsius where kelvin is required, and heat and temperature used interchangeably in written answers, which the scheme treats as a physics error rather than a wording one.

subjects.name: Waves, oscillations and resonance
subjects.levels: SL and HL, deeper at HL
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, superposition, standing waves and resonance. Phase relationships are where marks go, together with diagrams that are drawn without the labelled features the question specified.

subjects.name: Electricity and magnetism
subjects.description: Circuits, fields, induction and electromagnetic effects. This is the area Al Quoz students most often name as the problem, and the underlying issue is usually circuit reasoning rather than formula recall: an inability to say what happens to current and potential difference when one component changes.

subjects.name: Fields and gravitation
subjects.levels: SL and HL, substantially extended at HL
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, potential and energy. Higher Level demands longer derivations, and the marks are lost in the middle of them, where a student who knows the start and the end omits the two steps that were being tested.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear energy and quantum phenomena. Answers go wrong on conservation statements written loosely, and on explanations that assert a result without reference to the quantisation that makes it necessary.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainties
subjects.levels: SL and HL, assessed in a written paper
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainties, propagation, error bars, lines of best and worst fit and gradient interpretation. Marks here are the most reliably recoverable in the whole subject because the technique is finite and almost always taught in a hurry.

subjects.name: Extended response technique
subjects.description: Holding a chain of reasoning across four or five marks without losing the thread. This is the Higher Level discriminator and it is trainable: the student learns to answer the question asked, in sequence, with each step justified rather than assumed.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: Internally assessed individual work marked against lettered criteria and moderated. The commonest structural failure is a research question whose variables cannot be controlled or measured precisely enough with school equipment, which caps the analysis before any data is collected.

sections.heading: What an IB physics tutor in Al Quoz should establish in the first hour
paragraphs: An IB physics tutor in Al Quoz means one-to-one Diploma physics teaching at home on a weekday evening. IB Gram delivers that as a live online session into Al Quoz homes on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen. No tutor is sent to a UAE address, because in-person home visits are a service we run only in India.

The first hour should not be teaching. It should be reading two marked scripts and separating four possibilities, because they produce the same grade and need completely different plans. One: the student does not know the content. Two: the student knows it and answers the wrong command term. Three: the student knows it and loses the data marks on uncertainty and gradients. Four: the student knows it and cannot sustain reasoning across a five-mark question.

Only the first of those is a content problem, and in practice it is the least common among Al Quoz students who were strong at IGCSE. The other three are technique, they are finite, and they are the reason a student can revise diligently for six weeks and move half a grade. A tutor who starts by re-teaching topics without reading the scripts is treating the most likely diagnosis as the least likely one.

The second thing to establish is the level, because the Higher Level failure mode is specific: reasoning that is correct for two steps and then stops. That is not solved by content and it is not solved by more practice questions attempted in parts. It is solved by attempting long questions whole, writing the chain out in full, and then compressing it.

sections.heading: The syllabus as it is actually assessed
paragraphs: Physics content lists are easy to find and not very useful, because they say what is covered and not what is tested. The table below reorganises the same material around the second question: for each area, what is the examiner actually looking for, and what does a student typically write instead.

Two patterns run through the whole table. The first is that explanation marks require a named principle. An answer that says the object slows down is a description; an answer that says the resultant force opposes the motion, so by Newton's second law the acceleration is negative, is an explanation. Students who are confident in physics often write the first kind because the second feels laboured, and the scheme pays only for the second.

The second pattern is units and specification. Gradients reported without units, temperatures left in Celsius where kelvin is required, energy statements that do not say which store the energy left, diagrams drawn without the features the question named. Each is a single mark. Across a paper they add up to more than any topic.

The IB revises its science guides, and the current Physics course differs from the previous one in how practical and data work is assessed. We do not reproduce or supply those documents because they are the IB's copyright, so the subject teacher remains the authority on what this year's cohort sits.

sections.heading: The papers, and what each one rewards
paragraphs: The written assessment separates two quite different skills, and students who are good at one are frequently weak at the other without realising the distinction exists. One paper tests breadth and speed: recognition, quick application and a data-analysis section built on an unfamiliar experiment. The other tests depth: structured questions and extended response work where a chain of reasoning has to hold.

The data-analysis work deserves naming separately because it is the most recoverable block of marks in the subject. It is finite: absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, error bars, lines of best and worst fit, gradient with units, and an interpretation sentence. That list is short enough to be taught properly in three or four sessions, and it is almost always taught in a rush because it sits alongside everything else.

Extended response is the opposite: not finite, and only improvable by practice with marking. The method that works is unglamorous. Attempt the whole question, write the reasoning out in full including the steps that feel obvious, mark it against the scheme, then rewrite it compressed. Students resist the full write-out because it feels slow, and it is the only thing that reliably stops the two-step collapse.

There is one more distinction worth drawing, because it changes how a block is planned. The multiple-choice work is improved by volume and an error log; the extended response work is improved by depth and rewriting. A student given more multiple choice because it is easy to set will get faster at something they were already adequate at, while the component actually costing them marks goes untouched. Match the practice to the failure rather than to convenience.

Confirm the current paper structure, durations and weightings with your child's subject teacher, since the structure of IB science assessment changed with the recent guide revision and the school holds the authoritative version for this cohort.

sections.heading: The mark-scheme traps, named
paragraphs: These are the specific failures that appear again and again in marked physics scripts from Dubai schools. None of them is a gap in physics. Every one of them is a gap between what the student wrote and what the scheme required, which means every one of them can be closed without learning any new content.

The most expensive is describe offered where explain was asked. The command terms are not stylistic; they define the mark allocation. Describe asks what happens, explain asks why, determine asks for a value with working, and deduce asks for a conclusion reached from given information. A student who answers the wrong one can write a paragraph of correct physics and score nothing, which feels so unjust that students argue with it instead of adapting, and the argument costs them the next paper too.

The second most expensive is a gradient or intercept used without units or without saying what it represents physically. A graph question frequently carries marks for the gradient value, the units and the physical interpretation as three separate things, and students routinely collect one of the three. The fix is a habit rather than a lesson: every gradient gets a value, a unit and a sentence.

The rest are listed in the table. Work through them with marked scripts rather than in the abstract, because the point is not to recognise the trap in a list but to see where your own child walked into it last month.

sections.heading: Uncertainties and graphs, done properly
paragraphs: This is the most recoverable block of marks in IB Physics and the one most often left to accident. The technique is finite, which is unusual and extremely useful: there is a list, the list is short, and a student who can execute the list reliably stops losing those marks entirely.

The list runs roughly as follows. Distinguish absolute from percentage uncertainty and convert between them without hesitating. Propagate correctly through addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and powers. Decide how many significant figures the data actually supports. Plot with error bars that reflect the uncertainty rather than decorating the graph. Draw lines of best and worst fit and use the difference to estimate the uncertainty in the gradient. Report the gradient with its unit and say what it represents physically.

That is three or four sessions of work for most students, and it transfers directly to the internal investigation, where the same skills are assessed against the criteria and carry a share of 20 per cent of the grade. A student who learns uncertainty properly in DP1 collects those marks twice, in the investigation and in every data question thereafter.

The reason it goes untaught is structural rather than anyone's fault. It sits alongside the content in a crowded two-year course, it feels like arithmetic rather than physics, and students who are confident in physics find it tedious. That combination is exactly why it is reliably available as a source of recovered marks for anyone willing to spend three sessions on it.

sections.heading: The internal investigation, and what a tutor may touch
paragraphs: The internal scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the physics grade, is marked by the school against lettered criteria and is moderated by the IB. Across the competitor pages researched for Dubai IB queries, not one names a single criterion, which is a remarkable omission for a fifth of a grade.

The structural failure is almost always in the research question rather than in the execution. A question whose variables cannot be controlled or measured precisely enough with the equipment actually available in a school laboratory caps the analysis and evaluation criteria before any data exists. This is fixable in an afternoon at the design stage and unfixable three weeks later, which is why the first session on an investigation should be interrogation rather than encouragement.

The second common failure is uncertainty planned after the fact. A student who collects a single run per condition cannot subsequently produce an uncertainty analysis, and no amount of writing rescues it. The uncertainty plan belongs in the method, before the laboratory session, and that single piece of sequencing is worth more than any later polishing.

On the boundary: a tutor may teach what each criterion rewards, press on the research question until it is measurable, demonstrate uncertainty technique on unrelated practice data, read the student's own draft and say which criterion it currently fails and why, and teach the skill the draft reveals is missing. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of the investigation. One operator researched for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that is an academic honesty breach and the consequence falls on the student. The test after any session is whether your child could explain and defend every change in their own words.

sections.heading: Past-paper work that actually produces marks
paragraphs: Most students do past papers and most students do them in a way that produces very little. They attempt a paper, check the answers, feel reassured by the questions they got right, and move on. That process tells them what they already knew and does not change anything.

The method that works has four steps and students dislike all of them. Attempt the question whole and under time. Mark it yourself against the scheme's own wording, not against your memory of the physics. Log the failure by category, not by topic, so that describe-for-explain across eight questions registers as one pattern rather than eight unrelated slips. Then rewrite two of the failed answers to scheme wording from scratch.

The logging step is the one that matters and the one that gets skipped. A student logging by topic concludes they are weak at waves and circuits. The same student logging by category discovers they lose marks whenever a question says explain, in every topic, which is a four-session fix rather than two months of content revision. The category log is also what makes progress visible to a parent.

On materials: we do not publish or supply IB past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables or subject guides as downloads, because they are the IB's copyright and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure. We reference them, cite the official source and work from what your child's school legitimately provides. A provider advertising those files as a feature is distributing someone else's property.

sections.heading: What physics support costs, and what to refuse to pay for
paragraphs: The market figures first, attributed and dated October 2026, because a parent should be able to judge any quote against something. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table. Budget online provision starts at Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

What is worth paying a specialist rate for is diagnosis and technique. Reading two marked scripts and identifying that a student loses marks on command terms rather than on content is worth more than twenty hours of content revision, and only someone who knows the scheme can do it. Uncertainty technique, extended response structure and investigation design are the other three places where expertise changes the outcome rather than the atmosphere.

What to refuse is equally clear. General weekly physics support bought with no diagnosis, because it has no target. Content re-teaching of topics the marked script shows the student already knows. Any offer to help with the investigation beyond teaching and feedback. Any provider quoting in a currency you do not pay in, or claiming approval from KHDA, ADEK, the IB or Cambridge, since an independent tutoring platform holds none and we hold none either.

For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year. Tutoring is the variable line in an education budget, which is the argument for buying defined blocks with review dates rather than an open arrangement that nobody examines until the session has happened.

paragraphs: Send four things: the level, the school, and the last two marked physics scripts or the current investigation draft. A specialist reading those will usually name the failing category in a sentence, and the free trial lesson exists to produce that diagnosis before any payment is made.

What will not be claimed on the call. No grade promise, because nobody can honestly make one. No suggestion that tutoring is required for equivalency, university admission or school progression, which would be a false claim about a regulatory process. No regulator or board approval: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office or centre. No satisfaction statistics, because a figure without its sample, date and method is decoration.

The disclosed limit matters more in physics than in most subjects. Higher Level physics is the hardest specialism to cover at a specific early-evening hour, and in the weeks before the May session those slots fill first across the whole corridor around Al Quoz. When nothing is available you are told, offered the nearest workable alternative and given a realistic view of when the slot opens. Nobody general is substituted for a specialist you asked for.

One last fact worth carrying into any conversation with any provider. Individuals offering private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here or anywhere else on this site.

process.title: Send marked scripts, not a grade
process.description: Content gaps, command term errors, data technique and reasoning collapse all produce the same grade and need four different plans of four different lengths. Two marked scripts usually separate them within the first session, and photographs are entirely adequate.

process.description: The first session reads the scripts and categorises the losses: content, command term, uncertainty and graphs, or sustained reasoning. Three of those four are finite technique problems that respond to three or four sessions without any new physics being taught.

process.description: Physics sessions often need an unbroken hour for a data question or a derivation. Al Quoz families usually hold a 5pm to 5.30pm weekday slot, adding a weekend morning when a Higher Level block needs two sessions and the evenings cannot take them.

whyPoints.description: Most IB physics marks are lost between what a student knows and what the scheme pays for. Naming that gap by category, then closing it, usually moves a grade faster than any amount of content revision does.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty treated as a finite teachable list
whyPoints.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation, significant figures, error bars, best and worst fit lines, gradient with units and interpretation. Three or four sessions, and the marks transfer straight into the internal investigation.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level reasoning trained deliberately
whyPoints.description: The two-step collapse on a five-mark question is the Higher Level discriminator, and it responds to whole questions written out in full and then compressed. Attempting long questions part by part reinforces exactly the habit that causes it.

whyPoints.title: Investigation design interrogated before data
whyPoints.description: A research question that cannot be measured with school equipment caps the analysis criteria before a single reading is taken. That is fixable in one session at the design stage and not fixable afterwards, which is why the sequencing matters more than the polishing.

faqs.question: My child understands physics but scores badly. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three technique failures rather than a content gap. Describe offered where the question said explain, which can score nothing on a correct paragraph of physics. A gradient reported without its unit or physical meaning, where three separate marks were available. Or uncertainty ignored in a data question. All three are visible in a marked script within minutes and all three are three or four session fixes, which is why the first hour should be reading scripts rather than re-teaching topics.

faqs.question: Does an IB physics tutor come to our Al Quoz home?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Physics is taught one-to-one into Al Quoz homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. For physics specifically the shared screen helps, because a data question with a graph and three columns of uncertainties is far easier to work through when both people can annotate the same thing at once.

faqs.question: What is the physics internal investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent of the subject grade, marked by the school against lettered criteria and moderated by the IB. The marks are concentrated in design, data processing, analysis and evaluation rather than in presentation, which is why the research question decides the ceiling. A question whose variables cannot be controlled or measured precisely with school equipment caps the analysis before any data exists, and that is fixable at the design stage and essentially unfixable afterwards.

faqs.question: How is IB physics different from IGCSE physics?
faqs.answer: The content gap is modest and the assessment gap is large. IGCSE rewards a correct statement and a correct substitution. The Diploma rewards application of a named principle, justification of each step, and quantified uncertainty. A student who was comfortable at IGCSE arrives in DP1 with a strategy that quietly stops paying, and the grade falls before anyone identifies the cause. Four to six sessions in the summer between Year 11 and DP1 on command terms and uncertainty prevents most of that fall.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on graph questions?
faqs.answer: Because a graph question typically carries separate marks for the gradient value, its units and its physical meaning, and most students collect one of the three. Error bars are a second source: bars drawn decoratively rather than from the actual measurement uncertainty, with no best and worst fit lines and therefore no gradient uncertainty. It is the most recoverable block of marks in the subject, because the technique list is short and finite, and three sessions usually closes it.

faqs.question: At what stage of the investigation is a tutor actually useful?
faqs.answer: Almost entirely at the start, before any data is collected. A tutor may interrogate the research question until it is measurable with the equipment actually available, teach what each criterion rewards, demonstrate uncertainty technique on unrelated practice data, and read the student's own draft and say which criterion it fails and why. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of it. After a session your child should be able to explain and defend every change in their own words.

faqs.question: Is electricity really the hardest topic, or does it just feel that way?
faqs.answer: It is genuinely the one Al Quoz students name most, and the underlying difficulty is usually reasoning rather than recall. Circuit questions ask what happens to current and potential difference when one component changes, which requires holding the whole circuit in mind rather than applying a formula. Students who have memorised the relationships can still fail that question. The fix is structured circuit reasoning practice, not more formulae, and it generally takes three or four sessions to become reliable.

faqs.question: What is the two-step collapse in Higher Level answers?
faqs.answer: A student starts a five-mark question correctly, completes two steps, and then stops, having lost the thread of the argument. It is the characteristic Higher Level failure and it is invisible in short-answer practice, which is why students who drill short questions keep meeting it. The remedy is to attempt long questions whole, write the reasoning out in full including the steps that feel obvious, mark against the scheme, then rewrite it compressed. Six to eight sessions of this changes the pattern.

faqs.question: How should my child be using past papers?
faqs.answer: Not the way most students do. Attempt the question whole and under time, mark it yourself against the scheme's own wording rather than against your memory of the physics, then log the failure by category rather than by topic. That last step is the one that matters: logging by topic produces the conclusion that waves and circuits are weak, while logging by category reveals that explain questions lose marks in every topic, which is a four-session fix rather than months of revision.

faqs.question: Do you provide IB past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be cautious about any provider that offers them as a feature. IB past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables and subject guides are the organisation's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. We reference them, cite the official source, link to it, and work from what your child's school legitimately provides. The school holds proper access and the subject teacher is the authority on what this cohort actually sits.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level physics worth tutoring if it is a sixth subject?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and usually only briefly. The common Al Quoz pattern is a Standard Level physics student carrying two heavier Higher Levels who gives physics the least preparation time and then loses points on technique rather than content. Four sessions on command terms and data technique typically moves it further than a term of content revision would, because the content was never the problem. The question is whether those points matter to the offer being chased.

faqs.question: What does physics support cost in Dubai at the moment?
faqs.answer: The market, attributed and dated October 2026: a qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour, with specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. Budget online provision starts at AED 33 to 65, which suits practice supervision rather than diagnosis. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel. Ours is set after the free trial, because the block length depends entirely on what the marked scripts show.

faqs.question: How far ahead should we book Higher Level physics support?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, because this is the hardest specialism to cover at a specific hour. In the weeks before the May session the early-evening Higher Level physics slots fill first across the whole corridor around Al Quoz, since every DP2 household wants the same time. If you know a block is coming after mocks, agreeing the pattern in advance costs nothing and secures the slot. When nothing is available we say so and give a realistic date rather than substituting someone general.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor take physics and maths?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the overlap is genuine, because algebraic fluency pays in both and a student who cannot rearrange an equation under pressure struggles twice. The test is still component-level competence in each subject separately, including the physics investigation and the mathematics exploration, which are different pieces of work with different criteria. If a tutor is strong on Analysis and Approaches but vague about physics uncertainty conventions, two specialists serve your child better than one diary.

intro.heading: Why a Physics specialist beats a nearby tutor for Al Quoz 4 families
paragraphs: Al Quoz 4 is a residential pocket inside a district most people associate with warehouses, galleries and car workshops. Families here live close to Al Safa and Al Manara, a short run from Umm Al Sheif, and within reach of the Al Khail Road corridor that feeds Al Barsha South and Dubai Hills Estate. What the neighbourhood does not have is a dense cluster of DP Physics teachers waiting for the phone to ring. Search for a tutor by distance and you get whoever lives nearby. That person may be excellent at GCSE-level mechanics and still be unable to tell you why your child's Theme D answer on gravitational potential scored two marks out of five.

Physics at Diploma level is not general science taught harder. It is a specific syllabus with five themes, a defined set of tools, and an assessment model that rewards a particular kind of written answer. A student can understand electromagnetic induction perfectly well in conversation and still lose marks because the question said 'explain' and the answer only described. That gap is a teaching problem, not an intelligence problem, and it is the single most common reason a bright Al Quoz 4 student sits at a 4 while believing they understand the material.

The honest position on location is this. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address — home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for Al Quoz 4 families run live over video, one-to-one, with a shared whiteboard and a document camera on the student's working. That constraint turns out to be an advantage for Physics specifically, because the subject lives in diagrams, graphs and worked algebra, all of which travel better over a screen than they do over a dining table with a tired tutor who has just driven in from Mirdif.

It also widens the pool enormously. Instead of choosing from the handful of DP Physics teachers who happen to live within driving distance of Al Quoz 4, a family chooses from specialists who have taught the themes their child is struggling with. If the problem is Theme A kinematics and the graph work underneath it, that is one kind of tutor. If the problem is a scientific investigation with no measurable independent variable three weeks before the school deadline, that is a different one. Distance would never have surfaced either.

Parents here tend to arrive with a specific trigger: a mock paper that came back lower than the predicted grade, a Theme E topic test on nuclear decay that went badly, or a school comment that the investigation plan is not viable. The first session is diagnostic rather than remedial. A tutor reads the actual script, finds whether marks were lost on physics, on mathematics, on command-term reading or on timing, and then builds a plan against that. Guessing which of the four it is wastes the first month of tuition, and that is the money most families regret spending.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-quoz-4.programmesIntro: Physics sits at the end of a longer route. programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Five themes: A space, time and motion; B the particulate nature of matter; C wave behaviour; D fields; E nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level adds additional sub-topics within the same themes rather than a separate option. Assessment is Paper 1 (section A multiple choice, section B data and experimental), Paper 2 short and extended response, and the internally assessed scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade.

Schools near this neighbourhood set that internal deadline at noticeably different points, so a tutor working with two students from two schools is working to two calendars.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Sciences in MYP is assessed against four criteria — knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, reflecting on the impacts of science. Students work on a 1 to 8 scale per criterion. The physics content is lighter than IGCSE, but the investigation skills are heavier, which is why MYP students often arrive in DP strong on method and thin on algebra.
programmes.countryNote: Several continuum schools serving the eastern and central parts of Dubai run MYP straight into DP without an IGCSE year. For an Al Quoz 4 family on that route, the gap to close before DP1 is almost always mathematical: rearranging formulae, handling indices, and reading gradients off a graph confidently.

programmes.name: Mathematics alongside Physics
programmes.description: Physics HL leans on Analysis and Approaches content: trigonometric functions for wave behaviour, logarithms for radioactive decay, and calculus intuition for rates of change in Theme A. Students taking Applications and Interpretation alongside Physics HL are not blocked, but they carry more mathematical load inside the Physics lessons themselves, and that changes how a tutoring plan is built.
programmes.countryNote: University admissions teams at institutions in the UAE and abroad differ on whether they accept Applications and Interpretation for engineering entry. An Al Quoz 4 family choosing in Year 11 should check the specific course page rather than relying on general advice, and should treat Physics HL plus Analysis and Approaches as the lower-risk combination for engineering.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the entry route
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 both feed DP Physics. The Extended tier of 0625 covers the mathematical treatment DP assumes; the Core tier does not. A student entering DP Physics from Core, or from a school that taught combined science, starts with a content gap rather than an ability gap, and it is a closable one if it is identified early.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate private enrolment in Dubai, so a large share of DP Physics students in and around Al Quoz 4 come through IGCSE rather than MYP. The practical difference shows in Paper 1B: IGCSE candidates handle uncertainty and data better, MYP candidates handle investigation design better.

sections.heading: What 'IB physics tutor in Al Quoz 4' actually returns, and what it should
paragraphs: The literal answer: an IB physics tutor in Al Quoz 4 is almost always found online rather than down the road, because DP Physics specialists are thin on the ground in any single Dubai sub-community and Al Quoz 4 is a small residential pocket inside a largely commercial district. Searching by distance filters on the wrong variable. Searching by theme and level filters on the right one.

Type the phrase into Google and most results are area-named blog posts written to catch the query rather than answer it. Several name no school, no syllabus theme and no price. The thing proximity genuinely buys is nothing in this subject. A Physics lesson is a diagram, a graph, a page of algebra and a conversation. All four work over video. sections.heading: The DP Physics syllabus your child is sitting, theme by theme
paragraphs: Current DP Physics is organised into five themes rather than a core plus options. Theme A covers space, time and motion: kinematics, forces, work and energy, momentum, and at Higher Level the rotational and relativistic extensions. Theme B is the particulate nature of matter, which carries thermal physics, the gas laws, current electricity and the circuit work students usually meet first. Theme C is wave behaviour, from simple harmonic motion through superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect.

Theme D is fields, and it is where Higher Level candidates most often stall. Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields are taught as one idea expressed three ways, and the syllabus expects a student to move between them fluently. The difficulty is rarely the equations. It is that a question about gravitational potential and a question about electric potential look different on the page and are the same physics underneath, and a student who memorised them separately has twice the work and half the confidence.

Theme E is nuclear and quantum physics: radioactive decay, binding energy, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and at Higher Level matter waves and the quantum model. It arrives late in the course, often in the same term as the investigation deadline, and it is routinely the theme with the weakest school coverage simply because the calendar ran out. For an Al Quoz 4 student, Theme E support in the second term of Year 13 is one of the highest-value interventions available.

Running underneath all five themes are the tools: experimental technique, technology and mathematics. These are not a separate unit to revise. They are what Paper 1B tests directly and what the investigation is marked on, and a student who can state Theme C perfectly while being unable to draw a line of best fit with an uncertainty estimate will lose marks in both places.

sections.heading: Where Al Quoz 4 students actually lose Physics marks
paragraphs: Mark loss in DP Physics is diagnosable, and it falls into four buckets that need four different responses. The first is physics: the student does not know the content. This is the easiest to fix and the least common in the students who come through this page, because a family paying for tuition has usually already noticed their child works hard.

The second is mathematics. A Theme C question on standing waves is solvable by a student who is comfortable with wavelength relationships and unsolvable by one who stalls on rearranging to find the unknown. In practice a meaningful share of Physics mark loss at Standard Level is arithmetic and algebra wearing a physics costume. The tutoring response is to fix the mathematics inside the physics question rather than sending the student off to do unrelated algebra drills.

The third is command terms, and this is the one schools flag least often. State, describe, explain, outline, deduce, discuss and determine each require a different shape of answer. 'Explain' wants a causal chain. 'Describe' wants the observation without the mechanism. A student who writes a beautiful explanation where the question asked for a description has done more work than required and scored less than they could. Drilling this takes a fortnight and is often worth a grade band.

The fourth is timing. Paper 1B runs slower per mark than Paper 1A because every question requires reading a table or a graph before any physics happens. Students who treat the whole paper as one undifferentiated clock routinely leave section B half finished. Splitting the paper mentally into two papers with two budgets is a technique, not a talent, and it is taught in a single session.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks, four criteria, one report
paragraphs: The internal assessment in DP Physics is a single scientific investigation worth 20% of the final grade at both levels. It is marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The report runs to a maximum of 3,000 words. That structure matters more than most students realise, because six marks for evaluation means the paragraph a student writes last, usually at midnight, carries the same weight as the whole experimental design.

The most common failure is upstream of the writing. A student picks a research question that sounds interesting and produces three data points clustered in a narrow range. No amount of good writing rescues an investigation that cannot generate enough variation to analyse. A feasibility conversation before the method is fixed is the highest-value hour a Physics tutor spends, and it is the hour schools have least time for because a supervisor is managing a whole cohort.

The second common failure is treating data analysis as a graph. The criterion wants processing that is appropriate to the data, uncertainty carried through the processing, and a graph that shows the relationship being claimed rather than a scatter with a line forced through it. Students who learned to propagate uncertainty for Paper 1B tend to score well here; students who met uncertainty only as a rule to quote tend not to.

The boundary matters and it is firm. A tutor may teach experimental design, question whether a method will work, explain uncertainty, review a draft the student has written and give feedback on it. A tutor may not write, draft, restructure or produce the investigation, or any part of an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay. The work must be the student's own, and the IB treats breaches of that as malpractice with consequences that fall on the student.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Dubai schools running the IB Diploma sit the May session, and a Physics plan that starts from the exam date and works backwards is a different plan from one that starts in September and hopes. The fixed points a family in Al Quoz 4 should put on a wall chart are the school's internal investigation deadline, the school mock window, the final weeks of Theme E teaching and the start of study leave. Confirm each with the school's IB coordinator, because they vary by school and the IB's own published dates should be checked against ibo.org rather than taken from a tutoring page.

Counting backwards, the investigation is the item with the least slack. Most schools set an internal deadline in the first or second term of Year 13, and the data collection has to happen before that, which means the research question has to be settled weeks earlier still. A student who reaches the school deadline with unusable data has no route to recover 20% of the grade. This is why investigation coaching is scheduled in the first term, not the last.

Mocks are the second fixed point and the most useful diagnostic a family will get for free. A mock script tells a tutor whether the problem is content, mathematics, command terms or timing, and it does so with real evidence rather than a parent's impression. Bringing the marked script to a first session is worth more than any amount of describing the problem in advance.

For families whose child sits Cambridge or Pearson qualifications alongside or before the Diploma, the series are different and so are the deadlines. Cambridge International runs June and November series for UAE candidates — the February and March series is offered to India only, so it should not appear in any UAE plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, which is why a resit decision made after results is often already late for the next available window.

sections.heading: KHDA, the school report, and what it tells you about Physics teaching
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the reports are published. For a family in Al Quoz 4 choosing between schools, or trying to understand why a child's Physics experience differs from a cousin's across the city, these reports are the only public evidence available.

What an overall band does not tell you is anything specific about Physics. A school rated Very Good overall can have a small, thinly staffed Diploma science department, and a school rated Good can have a long-serving Physics teacher whose cohorts do well. The useful part of a report is the subject-level commentary and the section on teaching and assessment, not the headline. Read those and the picture of what your child is actually getting becomes clearer.

Dubai's private sector is large and still growing. KHDA figures for 2024-25 put enrolment at 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37%, Indian at 26%, US at 14% and the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment. That last figure explains the thin Physics specialist market directly: IB is a minority curriculum here, DP Physics HL is a minority choice within it, and the pool of people who teach it well in any one neighbourhood is correspondingly small.

KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Useful context when a family is weighing tuition spend: the school bill is flat this year, which for some households is what makes a weekly Physics session affordable. None of this means IB Gram holds any status with KHDA. It does not, and no tutoring platform should imply otherwise.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and the questions worth asking a tutor
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, which grants it free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure a parent reads should be treated with suspicion.

There is a related point that matters in Abu Dhabi and is good practice everywhere: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. A parent who is offered 'your child's own teacher, privately' is being offered something the rules do not contemplate.

The questions worth asking any Physics tutor are short. Which themes have you taught at Higher Level? Can you talk me through how you would check whether my child's investigation design will produce usable data? What exactly will you do with a draft, and what will you refuse to do? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition permit? A tutor who answers all four clearly is a different proposition from one who answers with a testimonial.

On our side, the honest version includes what happens when the match is hard. Some Physics requests are narrow — a specific Higher Level theme, an unusual timetable, an investigation three weeks from a deadline. If no specialist is free for the slot a family in Al Quoz 4 needs, we say so and offer the nearest workable alternative rather than filling the slot with a generalist. A free trial lesson exists precisely so that judgement sits with the parent after seeing a tutor teach, not before.

faqs.answer: Theme D fields and Theme E nuclear and quantum physics, for different reasons. Theme E tends to arrive late in the course, often alongside the investigation deadline, and is the theme schools most often teach in a rush. In practice it means one report, written largely in one term of Year 13, carries more weight than any single examination paper section, which is why feasibility work on the research question is time well spent.

Students taking Applications and Interpretation can and do succeed, but they carry more mathematical work inside the Physics lessons themselves, and a tutoring plan has to allow for it. intro.heading: Physics homework is not homework, and that changes the timetable
paragraphs: A maths problem set can be broken into ten-minute pieces. A physics task usually cannot. A data-analysis exercise with uncertainties propagated through three stages, a graph that has to be linearised before the gradient means anything, or a write-up of a practical done on Tuesday in a school lab near Al Garhoud - each of those needs a single unbroken run at it. Al Qusais families discover this in Year 12 when a child who manages maths homework between 16:00 and 17:00 sits down to physics at 20:30 and is still there at 22:15.

That is why the school run matters more on this page than on any other subject page for this neighbourhood. Private schools across Al Qusais, Al Nahda, Al Mamzar and Al Garhoud finish the academic day between roughly 14:30 and 15:15, and bus loops along Damascus Street and Al Nahda Road put most students home between 15:00 and 15:45. The mandatory UAE subjects - Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies, required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum - take their share of the evening. What is left on a school night is one short window and one long one, and physics needs the long one.

There is a second timing pattern specific to the subject. Lab work is timetabled, so practical write-ups cluster. In most schools around Al Qusais the physics practical falls mid-week and the write-up is due within a few days, which means Wednesday and Thursday evenings carry a different kind of work from Monday's problem set. A tutoring slot pinned to Monday at 16:00 because that was the first thing available will spend a term handling the wrong task on the wrong night.

The content underneath all this changed recently, and it matters for who you hire. The current IB physics guide organises the course into five themes - space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; nuclear and quantum physics - rather than into the older numbered topics, and the assessment shifted to two papers with the data-based questions moved into Paper 1. A tutor working from pre-2023 material will teach competent physics against the wrong assessment map, which costs marks in a way that is almost invisible until a mock paper arrives.

IB Gram delivers physics to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For physics specifically the online format has a practical advantage beyond the obvious one: a shared screen handles a spreadsheet of raw readings, an uncertainty calculation and a linearised graph far better than two people sharing one exercise book, and a ninety-minute block costs nothing in travel at either end of it.

If HL Physics is the plan for a Dubai university application or an engineering route abroad, confirm with the IB coordinator before Year 11 choices close that the course will actually be timetabled for your child's cohort.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, the preparation that decides Year 12
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria out of eight each: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion C, processing and evaluating, is the direct ancestor of the Diploma scientific investigation, and a student who sat in the 3-4 band on it in Year 10 will struggle with the Diploma version without specific help.
programmes.countryNote: MYP science criterion scores are the most useful thing an Al Qusais parent can hand a physics tutor, and the least often sent. The overall 1-7 hides which of the four criteria is weak, and a student weak on C needs a different term of work from one weak on A.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the route in
programmes.description: Most students entering Diploma Physics around Al Qusais arrive from Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 rather than from MYP. Both cover mechanics, waves, electricity and radioactivity to a level the Diploma assumes, and neither prepares a student for the uncertainty treatment, graph linearisation and extended written reasoning the Diploma expects from the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge 0625 students in Dubai sit either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper depending on the centre's arrangements. Which one your child sat tells a tutor a great deal about how much hands-on data handling they have actually done, so it is worth checking the paper numbers on the timetable.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-qusais.subjectsIntro: Families search for an IB physics tutor in Al Qusais and then describe one of a small number of specific problems. These are the ones that come up most, and the session length each one genuinely needs.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, with circular motion and gravitation extending at Higher Level. The usual failure is not the physics but the vector work: components taken on the wrong axis, or a free-body diagram drawn with a force that does not exist. Fixable in a few focused sessions and worth marks across every paper.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, internal energy and entropy, with greater depth at Higher Level. Students lose marks by treating temperature and heat as interchangeable and by quoting relationships without stating the conditions under which they hold. A ninety-minute block is enough to repair both habits.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave characteristics, superposition, standing waves, the Doppler effect and diffraction, with additional depth at Higher Level. The phase relationships are where understanding either forms or does not, and they are far easier to teach on a shared screen with an animated graph than on paper.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields treated together, with potential and field strength at Higher Level. The conceptual trap is sign conventions, and the mathematical trap is inverse-square reasoning applied to the wrong quantity. Both show up as consistent, diagnosable mark losses in Paper 2.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear binding, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and matter waves, extended considerably at Higher Level. This theme is often taught last and revised least, which makes it one of the more reliable places to recover marks in the final term.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: data-based questions
subjects.description: Reading a table of raw data, identifying the uncertainty, choosing what to plot, linearising, drawing a best-fit line and extracting a physical quantity from the gradient. A separate skill from the physics content and the single most trainable component on the course. It deserves its own sessions rather than a corner of somebody else's.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: One investigation worth a fifth of the grade, marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A tutor may teach the criteria, question a method, point out that an uncertainty has not been propagated and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not design it, write it or produce the data.

subjects.name: Mathematics for physics
subjects.description: Rearranging multi-variable relationships, logarithms for exponential decay, small-angle approximations, trigonometry in resolving, and gradients that carry units. Students taking Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches often need this stream explicitly, and it is usually the fastest route to a better Paper 2.

sections.heading: The physics week in Al Qusais: which night carries which kind of work
paragraphs: Pin the tutoring slot to the subject's rhythm rather than to the first gap in a calendar. In most schools around this part of Dubai the physics practical is timetabled once a week or once a fortnight, and the write-up is due within a few days of it. That creates a predictable shape: a problem set early in the week, a practical mid-week, a write-up due late in the week, and a weekend that is either the best study block of the seven days or a complete loss depending on whether anybody planned it.

Against that, the household constraints are fixed. School ends between roughly 14:30 and 15:15, buses reach Al Qusais between 15:00 and 15:45, and the mandatory UAE subjects set work of their own. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time using a 40-minute lesson unit and permits schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, which in practice means the evening is fuller than parents expect. Realistically there is one short weekday window around 15:45 to 17:00 and one evening window around 19:30 to 21:15.

Physics does not fit the short window well. Ninety minutes is the unit in which an uncertainty-propagated data set, a linearised graph and an interpretation of the gradient can be completed in one run. Forty-five minutes produces half a graph and a note to continue, and the continuation never has the same momentum. So the sensible arrangement for most Al Qusais families is one long block at the weekend or in a late evening slot, plus a short correction slot pinned to the night the school actually sets physics.

An in-home tutor can do none of this flexibly. A ninety-minute evening block means a tutor driving into Al Qusais at 19:15 and leaving at 21:30, and the published Dubai in-home range of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel reflects exactly that. Online delivery makes the long block cheap to schedule and cheap to move, which is the whole practical argument for it on a physics page rather than a general one.
