sections.heading: The current physics guide: five themes and two papers, mapped
paragraphs: The course your child sits is organised differently from the one most online notes describe, and that gap is the single most common reason a competent tutor underperforms in physics. The current guide, whose first examinations fell in 2025, runs five themes rather than a numbered topic list: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level adds depth inside each theme rather than appending separate options at the end.

The assessment changed with it. There are two written papers. Paper 1 carries multiple-choice questions and a data-based section, bringing data analysis into a timed written paper rather than leaving it to the practical scheme. Paper 2 carries short-answer and extended-response questions and is the heavier of the two by weighting. The internal assessment is a single scientific investigation worth a fifth of the final grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation.

For a tutoring plan, the practical consequence is that data handling is no longer optional. A student who has been taught the content well and has never practised reading a table of raw values, deciding what to plot, linearising a relationship and extracting a quantity from a gradient will lose a consistent block of marks in Paper 1 with no obvious content weakness to blame. That pattern is diagnosable from one marked paper and repairable in a handful of targeted sessions.

Verify the specifics against your child's own course outline and the IB's published guide rather than against any restatement, including this one. Schools confirm which guide a cohort is sitting and the IB coordinator is the right person to ask. We do not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables - those are the board's copyright and should be reached through the school or the IB's own site.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion, and the line a tutor holds
paragraphs: A fifth of the physics grade comes from one investigation the student designs, runs and writes. It is marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each, and knowing which is which changes how a Year 12 spends their time. Research design asks for a focused research question, an identified independent and dependent variable, controlled variables and a method capable of producing data that answers the question. Data analysis asks for raw data recorded properly, uncertainties stated and propagated, and processing that is correct and clearly presented.

Conclusion asks for an answer to the research question justified by the processed data and compared against accepted physics. Evaluation asks for the method's real limitations and realistic improvements - not a list of generic apologies about human error, which is the most common way students lose marks on this criterion. Across the drafts we see from Dubai schools, data analysis and evaluation are where marks are most often left behind, and both are teachable without touching the student's own work.

The most expensive mistake is upstream of all four criteria: a research question that cannot produce usable data. If the independent variable cannot be varied over a meaningful range with the equipment available, or the dependent variable cannot be measured with an uncertainty small enough to show the relationship, no amount of good writing recovers it. Screening the question in one session at the start of the process is the highest-value hour on the whole component.

The boundary is firm. Under IB academic-honesty rules the investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate a research question, point out that an uncertainty has not been propagated, explain why a graph should be linearised, mark a draft against the descriptors and say plainly that a section is below standard. A tutor may not design the investigation, write any part of it, supply data or redraft it to completion. This search result contains sellers who offer finished Internal Assessments; buying one puts the student's diploma at risk, and we will not do it.

sections.heading: The maths a physics student needs, and when the maths course causes trouble
paragraphs: Physics marks are lost to mathematics more often than to physics. The specific skills are few and identifiable: rearranging a multi-variable relationship without error, using logarithms to handle exponential decay, applying small-angle approximations where the syllabus permits them, resolving vectors with trigonometry, and reading a gradient that carries units rather than a bare number. None of that is advanced. All of it has to be automatic under time pressure, and for many students it is not.

The Diploma maths course a student takes changes the risk. Analysis and Approaches builds the algebraic fluency physics assumes, with calculus at its centre and a non-calculator paper that forces manipulation to be secure. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led, with a calculator available throughout, and a student taking AI alongside Physics HL frequently needs a deliberate maths-for-physics stream rather than hoping the overlap covers it.

This matters for Al Qusais families in a concrete way, because subject blocks are set by the school and a student may not have had a free choice. If your child is taking Physics HL with AI SL, that combination is workable and it needs the maths gap named rather than discovered in February. Three or four sessions on rearrangement, logarithms and gradient interpretation early in Year 12 is cheaper than a term of physics tutoring that keeps stalling on algebra.

The same applies on the way in. Students arriving into Diploma physics from Cambridge IGCSE 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 have met mechanics, waves, electricity and radioactivity, but not uncertainty propagation or graph linearisation at Diploma depth. That is a bridging job best done in the summer before Year 12, when there is a long uninterrupted block and nothing competing for it - the single most wasted window in the whole two-year programme.

sections.heading: What physics tutoring costs around Al Qusais, and why the long block changes the sum
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates are the right starting point because they are checkable, and the useful comparison on a physics page is per block rather than per hour. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted across the Dubai market at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. Named IB specialists sit higher: TutorChase published AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table puts specialist exam-year support at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with BartyED at AED 650 for premium named tutors.

At the budget end, platforms staffed largely by university students advertise from the low double digits - Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both read in October 2026. For physics that band carries a particular risk: the content can be explained competently by someone who has never marked an investigation against the four criteria or practised a Paper 1B data set under time. Those are the two things that most reliably move a physics grade, and they are not general tutoring skills.

In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors asking AED 200 to 500. Translate that into the ninety-minute block physics actually needs and the arithmetic becomes stark: a single long in-home session reaches the upper hundreds before any discussion of quality, and the published monthly packages - around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits against about AED 799 for eight online sessions - tell the same story from the other direction.

None of these are IB Gram prices. They are other providers' published figures, attributed and read in October 2026, and we quote against the level, the component and the weeks remaining rather than from a table. The free trial lesson is one lesson with the matched tutor, with the fee discussed afterwards - and for physics we would use that trial on a real data-based question rather than on a conversation, because that is where you learn whether the tutor can teach the subject or only describe it.

sections.heading: KHDA, the regulator map, and what a school report does not tell you about physics
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects on a published six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the rating applies to the school rather than to a department inside it. For a parent in Al Qusais choosing between two schools on the strength of physics specifically, a more useful question is whether Physics is actually timetabled at Higher Level for the coming cohort, and how many students took it last year.

The regulator map is worth knowing because this catchment touches a border. Dubai sits with KHDA; Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which u.ae states regulates private education in the emirate and which, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. A family in Al Nahda can cross systems by crossing a street.

Two KHDA requirements shape the week a physics plan has to fit into. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited due to different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, the IB, Cambridge, Pearson or any other body named on this page, and nothing here should be read as implying one. We describe what these organisations do because a parent weighing a tutoring decision in Dubai needs that context and almost no competing page provides it. Confirm anything that affects a real decision with the school, the regulator's own site, or the IB coordinator.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what we say when no HL physics specialist is free
paragraphs: The first message should contain five things: the school, the level - Physics HL or SL - the year group, the most recent grade or MYP criterion scores, and the night of the week the school actually sets physics. That last item is the one nobody sends and the one that decides whether the slot survives the term. Add which Diploma maths course your child takes, because that changes whether a maths-for-physics stream is needed alongside.

We match on the level and the component rather than on the subject name. A student whose problem is Paper 1B data handling needs a different tutor hour from one whose problem is theme D conceptual depth, and both are different again from a student three weeks from an investigation deadline. The first lesson is a free trial with the matched tutor - one lesson, one tutor, fee discussed afterwards - and for physics we would spend it on a real data-based question rather than on introductions.

Availability is where most providers go quiet, so here is the position stated plainly. Higher Level physics specialists are the scarcest match in this subject and demand concentrates in the same two evening hours across the Gulf. Before mocks and in the weeks around investigation deadlines, those hours fill. If nobody suitable is free in your window, you are told at the match stage, with the options: a different slot with the right specialist, an adjacent-expertise tutor now, or a wait with a date against it. We will not put an SL generalist in front of an HL student and let a family find out in February.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, for every family in the UAE. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the Emirates and no tutor is sent to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. Private tutoring here is permit-regulated - the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years - so ask any tutor you consider, including ours, whether they hold it.

faqs.answer: Ninety minutes for the main weekly session, with a shorter slot mid-week if the budget allows. In most schools within reach of Al Qusais the practical is timetabled mid-week and the write-up is due a few days later, so Monday carries a problem set and Wednesday or Thursday carries a write-up. faqs.question: What changed in IB physics, and does it affect which tutor we need?

faqs.question: What are the four criteria on the IB physics investigation worth, mark by mark?

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with the physics investigation without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach the four criteria, interrogate the research question before any data is taken, explain why a relationship should be linearised, point out an uncertainty that has not been propagated, mark a draft against the descriptors and state that a section is below standard. A tutor may not design the investigation, write any part of it, supply data or rewrite it to completion. The work must be the student's own under IB academic-honesty rules, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student, not the seller.

faqs.question: My child takes Physics HL with Maths Applications and Interpretation. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is workable and it needs the maths gap named early rather than discovered in February. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led with a calculator available throughout, so a student may not have the automatic algebraic rearrangement, logarithm handling and gradient interpretation that Physics HL assumes. Three or four focused sessions on those specific skills in the first term of Year 12 costs far less than a term of physics tutoring that keeps stalling on algebra. Say which maths course your child takes in your first message.

faqs.question: We came from Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625. What is the gap into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Content coverage is mostly fine - mechanics, waves, electricity and radioactivity are all there. The gap is in treatment. Diploma physics expects uncertainty stated and propagated, graphs linearised before a gradient is interpreted, and extended written reasoning that justifies rather than asserts. IGCSE rarely demands any of those at Diploma depth. It is a bridging job of perhaps eight to twelve hours, best done in the summer before Year 12 when there is a long uninterrupted block, which is the most wasted window in the whole two-year programme.

faqs.question: What does physics tutoring cost around Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates, read in October 2026: a qualified subject tutor online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IB specialists run roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour inclusive of travel. Those belong to the providers that published them; we quote against the level, the component and the weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 1B worth separate practice?
faqs.answer: Because it tests a different skill from the rest of the course and almost nobody practises it deliberately. The data-based section gives raw values and asks a student to identify the uncertainty, decide what to plot, linearise where necessary, draw a best-fit line and extract a physical quantity with units from the gradient. A student strong on content and untrained on this loses a consistent block of marks with no obvious topic to blame. It is diagnosable from one marked paper and repairable in a handful of targeted sessions.

faqs.question: Is online physics tutoring workable when so much of the subject is practical?
faqs.answer: The practical work itself happens in the school lab and always will. What a tutor does with it is handle the data, the uncertainty, the graph and the write-up structure, and all of that transfers better to a shared screen than to two people over one exercise book. A spreadsheet of raw readings, a linearised plot and an annotated draft are easier to work on jointly online than in person. What online cannot do is run the experiment, which is why we ask what the school's practical scheme covers before planning.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Qusais actually run Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: The Diploma cohorts closest to this neighbourhood sit mainly in Al Mamzar, Al Garhoud and Festival City, at schools such as Al Ittihad Private School Al Mamzar, Deira International School and Universal American School. Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Oud Metha are dominated by Indian-curriculum and British-track schools running IGCSE sciences at sixteen, so many Diploma physics students from here commute each morning. Confirm current programmes with the school directly and against KHDA's own school listing; we name these schools as neighbourhood context and claim no affiliation.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week does a Higher Level student need?
faqs.answer: One long block a week is the sensible default for a student who is coping and wants to move up a grade, provided the problem sets between sessions are actually attempted. Two - one long, one short - suits a student with a diagnosed content gap, a Paper 1B weakness or an investigation running behind the school's internal deadline. Three is an intensive block before mocks rather than a steady arrangement. The more useful question is how many days pass between the lesson and the work it was meant to fix.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level physics specialist is free in our time slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you at the match stage rather than after a payment. Higher Level physics is the scarcest match in this subject, demand concentrates in the same two Gulf evening hours, and before mocks and around investigation deadlines those hours fill. The options are then stated plainly: a different slot with the right specialist, a tutor with adjacent expertise starting now, or a wait with a date attached to it. What we will not do is place a Standard Level generalist with a Higher Level student and hope nobody notices.

faqs.question: Do you send a physics tutor to our home in Al Qusais?
faqs.answer: No. Every UAE lesson we arrange runs one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we operate only in India. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the Emirates. The Dubai market does supply in-home physics tutors, quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the fee, and for a ninety-minute physics block that arithmetic gets expensive quickly. If you choose that route, ask the tutor about the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-qusais.closingHeading: Book the long block, and tell us which night physics lands
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-qusais.closingBody: Two pieces of information make a physics plan work for an Al Qusais family: the level your child sits and the night of the week the school actually sets physics work. With those, the shape is straightforward - a ninety-minute block at the weekend or from 19:45 for data, graphs and Paper 2 work, plus a shorter correction slot pinned to the night the homework lands. Send the level, the school, the latest grade and your two workable windows, and the first lesson is a free trial with the matched tutor: one lesson, fee discussed afterwards, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.
